title: P0: AnnounceTrustStore Debug derive leaks sealing seed
description: announce_store.rs derives Debug on AnnounceTrustStore, whose sealing_seed is Option<Zeroizing<[u8;32]>>. zeroize 1.9.0's Zeroizing has #[derive(Debug)] on a transparent tuple struct (zeroize-1.9.0/src/lib.rs:602-604), so any {:?}/dbg!/trace of the store prints all 32 seed bytes. With the seed an attacker forges/validates every seal, defeating tamper/rollback fail-closed protection; if callers pass node identity material it is a root secret leak. Fix: manual redacted Debug impl (print only whether a seed is present). Note: GatewayOscoreSenderStore/GatewayOscoreRecipientStore in lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs share the same pattern — file a follow-up there or fix in same pass. Found by security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-12zy.
close_reason: wave-10

title: checkin_resource: PUT /config/checkin, POST /checkin, POST /rollcall missing OSCORE/local-admin gate
description: Root cause: checkin_resource.c was written against lichen_coap_respond only and skipped the coap_oscore_unprotect_resource_request + is_protected/lichen_coap_is_local_admin gate every sibling resource uses (coap_server.c:191, coap_msg.c:1946, coap_config.c:752, coap_location.c:1298). (P0) PUT /config/checkin (checkin_resource.c:224-254): any mesh node can rewrite scheduled check-in config - set target to attacker addr with include_location=true (periodic location exfiltration per 18.6.4), disable safety check-ins, or set interval_s=1 (radio flood). Fix: unprotect with COAP_METHOD_PUT, add is_protected||local_admin gate, respond via coap_oscore_respond_resource, read oscore.payload. (P1) POST /rollcall (145-174): unauthenticated 4-packet 7-day table squat (capacity default 4, timeout up to 604800) and id-reset wipes responded/missing lists - require OSCORE and/or restrict id-reset to creating identity. (P2) POST /checkin (90-117): forged/overwritten presence - any peer can overwrite a genuine help check-in keyed on self-asserted node text; gate POST and verify node matches authenticated source IID; make documented decision on unauthenticated GET /checkin exposure.
close_reason: Fixed all three endpoints in checkin_resource.c: unprotect via coap_oscore_unprotect_resource_request (POST/POST/PUT), gate is_protected||lichen_coap_is_local_admin -> 4.01, respond via coap_oscore_respond_resource, read oscore.payload (house pattern per coap_config.c config_put / coap_msg.c msg_ack). (b) rollcall: gate added; id-reset — creator identity is NOT recorded in the oracle-matched service layer (struct lichen_rollcall has no creator field), so identity-conditioned reset is not derivable here; restricted re-POST of a known id to capacity semantics by restoring responded/missing counts after lichen_rollcall_post wipes them (started/timeout_s still update). Local-admin fallback kept per house convention (all cited siblings use is_protected||local_admin); strict OSCORE-only for rollcall would need a decision if wanted. (c) checkin: gated; authenticated source identity IS available post-unprotect (ctx lookup keys on the source-address IID, so AEAD success binds the source address) -> node-vs-source enforced, 4.03 on mismatch. Residual risk: the local-admin path may post on behalf of any node (trusted on-device client, by design). GET exposure left as-is (public read); decision filed as follow-up. Verification: twister lichen.checkin_resource on qemu_x86_64 8/8 test cases passed incl. new regressions (unauthenticated_writes_rejected, oscore_checkin_node_binding, rollcall_repost_preserves_lists); host suite lichen/tests/checkin_rollcall 1/1 green; cppcheck clean. Note: native_sim/qemu_x86(32) cannot run locally (twister 4.1 filters native platforms on macOS; no i686 SDK toolchain; ZEPHYR_EXTRA_MODULES triggers the known zcbor Kconfig loop) — ran the suite without the module flag, which this suite does not need.

title: CRITICAL: provisioning carve-out lets any peer forge inviter==local-node_id invitation and read group master_secret
description: File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_invite.py:63-90 + groups_collection.py join_key :643-695. render_post has NO auth gate; pubkey lookup miss + inviter==node_id branch performs ZERO verification, records attacker-chosen role (admin), then join_key serves {master_secret,master_salt,key_epoch} over attacker's own pairwise context. CONFIRMED via live read-only harness replica of shipped test wiring (CHANGED returned, role=admin stored, 32-byte secret leaked). Exploit chain: POST invite {group_id,inviter:<local node id>,role:'admin',expires:<future>,signature:junk} -> record_invitation -> GET/POST key -> secret + admins[] membership. Fix: carve-out MUST require locally-trusted origin (LCI loopback OR pairwise identity==node_id) and/or pin node's own pubkey so even local docs verify. No OSCORE-free path may reach verification skip.
close_reason: Fixed: inviter==node_id provisioning carve-out now requires locally trusted origin only (_origin_locally_trusted: LCI loopback admin OR pairwise OSCORE identity==node_id, shared helper in groups_collection.py mirroring messaging._peer_is_local_admin firmware semantics). Wire deliveries claiming inviter==node_id must pin node's own pubkey via new node_pubkey registry param and pass schnorr48 verification exactly like foreign inviters; unpinned+untrusted+unsigned => 4.03. Legit LOCAL provisioning kept end-to-end (vector test via [::1] LCI client). Live-harness replica: forged invite -> 4.03/131, ledger empty, attacker join_key -> 4.03 with zero bytes of master_secret disclosed. tests/coap groups: 87 passed.

title: join_key returns group OSCORE keys in plaintext
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_collection.py

GroupsItemResource._join_key (approx lines 274-302) returns master_secret and master_salt as a CBOR CoAP payload. There is no check for pairwise OSCORE (request.opt.oscore / oscore_protected / object_security). Encrypted POST /groups in GroupsCollectionResource._create (lines 137-143) also returns master_secret on the same unauthenticated path.

spec/12-apps.md 18.8.2 Key Distribution: the join_key exchange MUST be OSCORE-protected with the pairwise context from EDHOC. Quote: Never sent in plaintext.

Any mesh peer who knows or guesses a group id can POST /groups/{id}/key and receive the current group OSCORE master secret. That is full compromise of group confidentiality.

Related planned work exists as l1qw.10.11.3.2 (pairwise OSCORE key distribution); this bead tracks the defect in the code that already ships join_key.
acceptance_criteria: Reject join_key (and encrypted create if mesh-reachable) unless the request was unprotected only after a successful pairwise OSCORE unprotect. Do not put master_secret or master_salt on a plaintext CoAP response. Tests must cover unprotected join_key -> 4.01 and protected join_key still returning key material.
close_reason: join_key and encrypted POST /groups require a pairwise OSCORE identity bound after successful unprotect (oscore_context/oscore_context_id on request or remote). Spoofed CoAP OSCORE option, oscore_protected flag, empty identity, and group OSCORE contexts return RFC 7252 4.01 with no master_secret/master_salt and no membership mutation. OSCORE-bound join_key still returns spec 18.8.2 key material (32-byte secret, 8-byte salt, AES-CCM-16-64-128). pytest tests/coap/test_groups_{item,collection,rekey}.py passed.

title: [review] project-LICHEN-6mij.2.4: use-after-return in coap_oscore_auth_mutating (stack pointer dangles)
description:
P0 correctness bug. coap_oscore_auth_mutating at coap_oscore.c:249 allocates uint8_t plain[CONFIG_LICHEN_OSCORE_PLAINTEXT_MAX] on its own stack, stores result->payload = plain at line 283. After return, plain is reclaimed. Callers (deaddrop_post, msg_inbox_post) dereference auth.payload after return — UB.

Fix: Move plain buffer into struct coap_oscore_auth_result as inline array, or pass buffer from caller.

Affected: coap_oscore.c:249,283 | coap_oscore.h:124-130 | coap_dtn.c:123,152,172 | coap_server.c:341,345
notes: Fix implemented in working tree: deleted orphaned coap_oscore_auth_mutating() (coap_oscore.c) - zero callers repo-wide, struct type removed in 6mij.2.4 refactor, sizeof(*result) on incomplete type made TU uncompilable. Behavior replicated at handlers via coap_oscore_unprotect_resource_request + inline local-admin guards. native_sim build verification deferred (EC2 paused by user); deletion-only change, zero references verified by grep.
close_reason: Fix VERIFIED in committed + working-tree state. (1) The dangling-pointer helper is gone: commit 0de6a9383a 'fix(oscore): drop orphaned auth_mutating helper' removed coap_oscore_auth_mutating(); repo-wide rg for coap_oscore_auth_mutating|coap_oscore_auth_result (excluding .beads and docs) returns zero matches (rg exit 1); coap_oscore.h declares only existing functions. (2) The replacement result path is structurally immune to this UAR class: coap_oscore_unprotect_resource_request() stores plaintext in result->plainbuf[] EMBEDDED in struct coap_oscore_unprotect_result (coap_oscore.h:52), so result->payload points either into the caller-owned struct or into the caller-owned request packet - never at helper stack memory. (3) deaddrop_post and confessions_post now consume requests through exactly that helper (coap_dtn.c:107-121, 226-241), eliminating the last inline unprotect logic in the file; the keys put/delete inline pattern keeps plain[] handler-local so no pointer escapes its frame. (4) cppcheck (warning,style,performance,portability) passes on coap_dtn.c. Remaining gap: no in-repo build compiles coap_dtn.c (CONFIG_LICHEN_COAP_DEADDROP enabled nowhere), so the deferred native_sim compile verification stays deferred - now tracked as project-LICHEN-worker6-qj3l instead of silent debt.

comments.author: Mark Atwood
comments.text:
DECISION NEEDED: relay signer identity binding for link frames (decomposed from project-LICHEN-2auf.44.9.8). The wire-format choice is Mark's.

== CURRENT STATE (evidence, as of 2026-08-28 tree) ==
The premise "link frame omits a signer identifier" is STALE: the closed Schnorr-48 wire migration (project-LICHEN-2auf.35) added a mandatory 8-byte Signer Identifier (SIID) to every signed frame.
- spec/02-physical-link.md 4.1-4.2: SIID (0/8B) after Dst Addr; LLSec SI bit 7; signed frames MUST set S+SI; transcript "LICHEN-LINK-v1"||0x00||LENGTH||LLSec||Epoch||SeqNum||DST_LEN||DstAddr||SIID||Payload binds the exact 8 SIID octets; "the selected trust-store public key, rather than SIID by itself, establishes the authenticated sender identity".
- Re-sign call sites: rust/lichen-link/src/relay.rs:83 relay_verified_frame (verify inbound against pinned upstream key, then re-sign with own key/own SIID/own counter); C lichen/subsys/lichen/link/lichen_link_tx.c:235 lichen_link_relay_raw and :348 lichen_link_relay_frame (same pattern).
- Key resolution today: Rust indexed lookup peers.get(&signer_iid) (link_layer.rs:1117); Python pinned-key cache keyed by canonical IID (link_layer.py); C uses O(N) constant-time trial-verify over the provisioned peer table (l2/lichen_l2_peer.c:118 peer_try_all_pubkeys) with TOFU pinning (lichen_l2_peer.c:306) and post-match SIID<->canonical-EUI64 binding (lichen_link_rx.c:196-203). No implementation derives the key from the preserved IPv6 source.
- Vectors: test/vectors/wire_format_v2.json already covers SI+S normal / relay-resigned / malformed frames and hop re-signing inputs.
RESIDUAL GAP: spec leaves key-SELECTION policy open (SIID is "routing hint only until the signature verifies"); C's selection is correct and fail-closed but is whole-table trial verification (CPU cost on STM32WL-class: up to CONFIG_LICHEN_LINK_MAX_NEIGHBORS Schnorr-48 verifies per frame) rather than SIID-indexed lookup, and relay-neighbor TOFU cache semantics (populate/evict) are not normative.

== BYTE BUDGET (spec/02 4.1; rust frame.rs MAX_FRAME_LEN=255, MAX_FRAME_BODY=254) ==
Signed-frame fixed overhead: LLSec(1)+Epoch(1)+SeqNum(2)+SIID(8)+Sig(48) = 60B, plus DstAddr(0/2/8). Payload budget = 254-60-dst_len = 194B broadcast / 192B short / 186B extended. Length field: 1B, body 4-254B, LoRa total cap 255B.
(a) 0B if SIID stays 8B (status quo); shrinking SIID to 4B truncation saves 4B (payload 190/198) but is a breaking transcript change (SI flag implies exactly 8 on-wire octets today).
(b) 0B wire change.
(c) +8B if signer identity duplicated inside payload (or 0B reusing transcript SIID); adds a second signature verify per hop.

== OPTIONS ==
(a) Explicit truncated signer ID in frame (4-8B of relay IID/key hash).
  Wire cost: 4B saved only if SIID shrinks 8->4B; no saving if added alongside.
  Security: SIID remains an untrusted hint (signature still binds the trust-store key), but 32-bit truncation invites SIID-space collisions -> wrong-candidate lookups -> verify fails (DoS/confusion, not forgery). 8B form is strictly stronger and already shipped.
  Cross-impl churn: HIGH. Transcript definition change; C/Rust/Python parsers+signers; flag-day upgrade semantics per spec 4.1 ("MUST NOT accept both transcripts for the same frame").
  Vector impact: full regeneration of link_frame.json, link_frame_signed_modes.json, wire_format_v2.json, link-edge-fuzz.json, frame_length_boundaries.json.
(b) Deterministic lookup: verifier resolves the key from the TOFU key cache keyed by the frame's link-layer signer address (SIID -> canonical EUI-64 -> pinned key); no wire change.
  Wire cost: 0B. wire_format_v2 stays valid.
  Security: claimant without the pinned key fails transcript verify (key substitution rejected); SIID never allocates state pre-verify (spec 4.2 already mandates); replay stays keyed by (pubkey, key-generation). Relay spoofing fails closed. Cache semantics must be normative: pin on first VERIFIED contact, reject key mismatch for a pinned SIID (TOFU violation), eviction only per trust-store policy.
  Cross-impl churn: LOW-MEDIUM. Rust/Python already indexed; C replaces/augments peer_try_all_pubkeys with SIID-indexed lookup (keep constant-time properties or document trade), adds relay TOFU population. Spec gains one normative paragraph.
  Vector impact: none for wire bytes; add cross-impl cache-behavior and 3-node A->B->C relay-chain vectors (C's cache pins B, not A).
(c) Signer identity inside signed payload + two-hop verification chains.
  Wire cost: ~0-8B; verifier must validate relay sig AND origin sig.
  Security: adds end-to-end origin attribution at link layer, but origin cannot predict per-hop mutations (Hop Limit, RFC 6554 SRH address swaps), so origin-sig scope is ill-defined; doubles Schnorr-48 verifies per hop (constrained MCU cost); doubles replay state; duplicates the existing DAO Origin Signature profile (lichen/subsys/lichen/link/sos_origin.c, application-layer, domain-separated per draft-lichen-schnorr-00 8).
  Cross-impl churn: VERY HIGH (spec 8.4 hop-by-hop model rewrite + all impls).
  Vector impact: full regeneration + new chain vectors.

== RECOMMENDATION ==
Option (b). The wire already carries the strongest form of (a) - a full 8-byte transcript-bound SIID - so truncation buys 4B at breaking-transcript cost, and (c) duplicates the SOS/DAO origin signature with 2x verify cost and ill-defined scope across SRH mutations. The open problem is key-selection policy: make SIID-indexed TOFU trust-store lookup normative in spec 02 (4.1/4.2) and align C to Rust/Python behavior. Child implementation beads are filed, gated on this decision.

comments.author: Mark Atwood
comments.text:
ASSESSMENT (2026-08-28): DECOMPOSED. Spec answers the policy (spec/05-routing.md 8.7/8.7.1/8.7.2); implementations are uneven, and the Rust authorization core exists only as UNCOMMITTED in-flight work by another session. No human escalation needed: the spec pins /0, foreign host routes, and delegation semantics.

== WHAT EXISTS ==
1. DAO origin authenticity (8.6) is real in all impls:
   - Rust: DaoOriginValidator (rust/lichen-rpl/src/dao_origin.rs:194) = pinned key + IID binding + Schnorr48; root ingest DaoManager::process_signature_verified_inner (rust/lichen-rpl/src/routing.rs:489) orders admission -> replay classification -> has_exact_origin_target -> sender_is_authorized -> staged apply -> replay-floor commit (routing.rs:573). Rejects land BEFORE route and floor mutation.
   - Python: validate_and_process_dao_wire_at -> target_mismatch / multiple_target (python/src/lichen/rpl/dao_manager.py:869-886).
   - C: sos_origin.c parse/transcript/verify exists (lichen/subsys/lichen/link/sos_origin.c) but is NOT wired into the RPL root path (see gap 3).
2. Wire-profile rejection of non-/128 Targets: Rust envelope parser rejects Target data length != 18 (rust/lichen-rpl/src/message.rs:470-476) -> /0 and broad prefixes die during verify, pre-everything; C semantic parser rejects prefix_len != 128 (lichen/subsys/lichen/rpl/rpl_dao_process.c:145-148) and E=1 (:184).
3. Foreign host routes: Rust rejects at the policy gate (has_exact_origin_target, routing.rs:633-650: exactly one Target, prefix_len==128, prefix==origin). Python rejects (dao_manager.py:875). C does NOT (gap 3).

== GAPS (children filed) ==
1. C root DAO ingest is FAIL-OPEN: lichen_rpl_dao_manager_process_dao_ex hardcodes authenticated=true (rpl_dao_process.c:735); process_dao never receives the DAO source address (rpl_dao_process.c:583-608), so a foreign /128 host route (target != origin) is accepted and installed. Fix requires API change (thread origin + authenticated through lichen/rpl_routing.h:655,671) and profile-aware rewrite of lichen/tests/rpl_routing/src/main.c fixtures (install_one/process_one at :150-165 advertise foreign targets). Child: project-LICHEN-worker6-d1oh
2. Rust delegation gate is UNCOMMITTED in-flight work in the working tree (routing.rs +137 lines: UnauthorizedPrefixReason, PrefixAuthorizationError, PrefixDelegations keyed by pubkey, MAX_PREFIX_DELEGATIONS=64) and does not compile (E0502 borrow conflict routing.rs:219-224); it is not yet wired into process_signature_verified_inner. Child: project-LICHEN-worker6-d1oi
3. Python has an unwired COSE_Sign1 delegation primitive (python/src/lichen/crypto/delegation_tokens.py, spec 18.8.6: create/verify/scope) and no delegation cache in dao_manager. Child: project-LICHEN-worker6-d1oj
4. Delegation delivery (CoAP POST .well-known/prefix-delegation, COSE_Sign1, delegation_seq, expiry per spec 8.7.2) exists nowhere. Child: project-LICHEN-worker6-d1ok
5. Vectors: no cross-impl allow/deny matrix for DAO prefix authorization. Child: project-LICHEN-worker6-d1ol

== LANDED IN THIS UNIT ==
rust/lichen-rpl/tests/dao_prefix_authorization.rs (new standalone target, fmt+clippy clean): literal 4-row allow/deny matrix at the authed root ingest boundary, validated against HEAD 439c12e041 in a clean worktree (1 passed):
  - self_host_route_allowed -> Ok(Applied), route installed, replay floor committed
  - foreign_host_route_rejected -> Err(RouteRejected), NO route, NO floor (proves pre-mutation ordering)

title: Enforce atomic OSCORE reservations
description: Complete Rust OSCORE crash/concurrency safety with storage-mediated compare-and-swap or an exclusive context-owner lease. Every sequence-consuming public protect path must require a reservation token obtained by atomically advancing persisted state before encryption; Context::new must not let reused key material self-assert freshness; restored ordinary-response one-shot state must be persisted or no-PIV responses prohibited. Remove SecureStack plaintext/mutable-stack bypasses.
design: Reservation storage owns CAS(expected,next) or an exclusive lease. In-memory Context state alone cannot coordinate multiple processes or prove key material is fresh.
acceptance_criteria: Two simulated processes restoring the same expected sequence race and exactly one reserves/transmits; all public request/fresh-PIV response paths require reservation capability; blind-write callbacks reject; crashes after reserve cause gaps not reuse; ordinary response state is persisted or disabled; SecureStack cannot bypass OSCORE through mutable plaintext stack; no_std tests and three security reviews pass.
notes: Completed atomic context-bound CAS reservations, explicit fresh registration versus restore-only loading, crash-safe sequence gaps, transactional ordinary response replay commits, strict RFC option/KID/context handling, authenticated secure ingress, CoAP correlation/ACK handling, and C.4-C.8 vectors. title: tunnel_auth check_time never advances last_now on the Ok path: rollback detection lags real time on a quiet gateway
description: Found by security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-k8ix (P1). rust/lichen-gateway/src/tunnel_auth.rs check_time:419-430 updates self.last_now only on the fully-successful tails (accept_post:361, authorize_decapsulation:415), so the watermark is the time of the last SUCCESSFUL operation, not the last OBSERVED time. Python's mirror _observe_time (tunnel_auth.py:413) sets _last_now = now on EVERY non-rollback observation, including requests that later fail. On a low-traffic LoRa border router the watermark can lag real time unboundedly (and failing requests at real time never move it in Rust, while they would in Python); if the clock then rolls back to T with last_now <= T, the rollback is undetected and any entry that expired in real time but was not yet opportunistically purged authorizes decapsulation again - the captured-grant-cannot-rearm guarantee is void exactly when the gateway is quiet. Fix: set self.last_now = Some(now) on the Ok path of check_time (the tail assignments become redundant but harmless); keep the rollback path NOT updating last_now (retain the high-water).
close_reason: Fixed: check_time's Ok path now sets self.last_now = Some(now) on every non-rollback observation (tunnel_auth.rs), matching Python's _observe_time which sets _last_now on every observation. Watermark = last observed time, not last successful operation; rollback detection can no longer lag real time on a quiet gateway. Rollback path still retains (does not advance) the high-water. Verified: full gateway lib suite 221/221 (one pre-existing test rejected_wrong_authentication_signature_egress_expiry_and_replay_atomically used non-monotonic now values - 1 then 10_000 then 1 - which under correct semantics hits ClockRollback; reordered its asserts replay-before-expiry so time is monotonic, all original assertions preserved, none weakened); clippy clean; fmt applied.

title: 6 C host suites red at HEAD: schc_rule{1..6}_compress fail test_profile_limit/rule constraints (pre-existing, baseline-reproducible)
description: Found by robustness codereview pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-wrxl (P1, pre-existing on the branch, NOT caused by the wrxl delta - reviewer verified identical failures from a git archive HEAD baseline). On heft (clang 20, -std=c23, ASan+UBSan per test_common.cmake): lichen/tests/schc_rule1_compress through schc_rule6_compress (6 suites) fail test_profile_limit (e.g. rule1 main.c:149-150 profile-limit assertion) and test_rule_constraints_and_checksum (:167/:197 SCHC_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT). Everything else green: schc, schc_ack_processing, schc_fragment_generation, schc_mqtt_sn, schc_parity (57/57), schc_reassembly, rule*_decompress. Likely SCHC_FRAGMENT_MAX_PACKET_SIZE/profile-limit or rule-constraint drift from recent SCHC work (hahk/wrxl-era changes to lichen_schc_compress gating or fragment sizing). Needs triage: run each suite, diff expectations vs current constants, fix code or tests per spec (spec/03-adaptation.md fragmentation/profile limits), do NOT weaken assertions without a spec basis.
close_reason: Root cause of the 6 red suites: lichen_schc_compress capped RAW input at SCHC_FRAGMENT_MAX_PACKET_SIZE (22554), but compressible packets legitimately have raw > compressed - the rule1-6 profile-limit tests build raw up to MAX+15 expecting encoded output == MAX (Rust has no raw-input cap; the ceiling applies to the ENCODED SCHC packet, codec.rs:1123). Fix: removed the raw-input cap; enforced the ceiling on encoded output instead - fallback branches (pre-IPv6 in the wrapper, version-6 generic dispatcher in subsys/schc/schc.c, mirroring Rust encode_rule255 needed > profile_limit) and the rule compressors' own existing caps. rule5/6 also pinned a stale error code (INVALID_ARGUMENT) for the corrupt-checksum case; updated to the committed gate contract NO_MATCHING_RULE (rule1's agnostic <0 and Python/Rust rejection semantics unchanged; atomicity assertions retained). New pin: tests/schc test_rule255_fallback_profile_ceiling (raw 22553 -> 22554 OK; 22554 -> BUFFER_TOO_SMALL, atomic) - the exact C/Rust divergence the review probe found. Verified on heft: all 18 C host suites green (clang+ASan/UBSan; schc 16/16 incl. new test), cppcheck clean. 3x codereview (correctness/security/robustness, reviewer-model passes): converged on the generic-dispatcher fallback ceiling gap, fixed in this commit; resource-exhaustion/int-overflow/remote-DoS re-checks all PASS (u16 declared lengths bound IPv6 input at 65575, INT_MAX guard retained, no VLAs, all writes out_len-bounded); pre-existing finding filed as 1dft (C generic decompress RX ceiling).

title: Python decode_rule255 applies endpoint address policy on receipt, violating spec 03 TX/RX split; diverges from Rust RX
description: P1, found by worker5 probe during project-LICHEN-worker6-1jbb verification. spec/03-adaptation.md:426-429 (canonical TX/RX split, landed faed8ccfb5): 'Rule 255 DECODING is byte-preserving and MUST validate structure and checksums only: a decoder MUST NOT apply the endpoint address policy on receipt, because a structurally valid packet already on the link is preserved verbatim rather than dropped as malformed. This split keeps the two implementation families interoperable: a packet one implementation cannot originate is still delivered intact by the other.' Python python/src/lichen/schc/headers.py decode_rule255 -> validate_full_ipv6 still runs _validate_ipv6_addresses (rejects unspecified src, multicast src, unspecified dst) AND UdpDatagram.from_bytes(payload, src) re-checks malformed sources (python/src/lichen/ipv6/udp.py:96-97) on the RX path. Rust RX decode_rule255 -> validate_full_ipv6_structure (codec.rs:1464) applies NO address checks (spec-compliant). Probe (valid UDP checksum, independent RFC 1071 oracle): src=:: / src=ff02::1 / dst=:: -> Python decode_rule255 REJECTS (invalid IPv6 source/destination address), Rust ACCEPTS byte-preserving - identical on-air bytes, opposite verdicts, same class as the k0r2 break for the loopback/v4mapped/scope classes wlts fixed. Also inflates RuleVersionFailureTracker misbehaving-peer notifications on Python nodes. wlts close incorrectly recorded 'Python verified aligned: decode_rule255:212 runs structural validation only' - the split was only verified for the 5 loopback/v4mapped/scope classes; the 3 unspecified/multicast-source classes still hit _validate_ipv6_addresses first. Fix: split decode from the full validator on the Python side the way Rust did (decode_rule255 must call a structure+checksums-only validator: version/length/next-header/chain/UDP length/checksum over RFC 2460 s8.1 dst, NO _validate_ipv6_addresses, NO UdpDatagram.from_bytes malformed-source check, keep UdpDatagram length/zero-checksum structure checks), keep validate_full_ipv6 (TX) enforcing the full emission policy; then add the 3 missing corpus rows (source ::, source ff02::1, destination ::) to schc_adaptation.json rule255_endpoint_policy with expect_valid=false (they currently cannot be committed: python false-branch asserts decode byte-preservation and would fail), and rerun parity + adaptation suites in both impls.
close_reason: Fixed: Python decode_rule255 is now byte-preserving per spec/03-adaptation.md canonical TX/RX split, matching Rust. Changes: (1) new _validate_ipv6_structure (headers.py:138) enforces version/length/ext-header chain/UDP length/zero-checksum refusal/checksum over RFC 2460 s8.1 upper-layer dst - NO _validate_ipv6_addresses, NO UdpDatagram malformed-source check (from_bytes called WITHOUT src so the endpoint check never fires; length/zero-checksum structure checks kept); (2) decode_rule255 calls it and returns data[1:] verbatim; (3) validate_full_ipv6 = structure + _validate_ipv6_addresses, TX semantics unchanged (the old from_bytes(payload, src) malformed-source check was redundant on TX - _validate_ipv6_addresses rejected the same classes first, so no behavior delta); (4) unspecified-dst TX message aligned to canonical 'invalid IPv6 destination address <addr>' (was 'invalid unspecified IPv6 destination address', headers.py:87, matching Rust codec.rs:255 and the vector mapping); (5) 3 corpus rows added to schc_adaptation.json rule255_endpoint_policy (rx_byte_preserving unspecified source / multicast source / unspecified destination, expect_valid=false, expect_error codes mapped in both impls) with expected_counts 8->11. Verification on heft: python adaptation 67/67 (3 new rows green), full test_vectors 770/770, python/tests/schc 1377/1377; ruff check+format clean; RUST adaptation_vectors.rs consumed the same JSON green (2/2, count equality assert 11==11 at :1468) and all 14 lichen-schc integration targets green under their feature sets. 3x delegated codereview: correctness PASS (TX union preserved - both validate_full_ipv6 call sites followed by emission check; zero stale old-text references; counts/coverage consistent), security PASS (checksum + RH3 structure intact; downstream DIO-ingest screening question filed as separate P3), edge PASS (bytearray/type behavior identical, boundary handling moved not altered, no return-value reliance).

title: Rust decode_rule255 must not apply endpoint address policy (spec 03 Rule255 canonical TX/RX split)
description: Child of project-LICHEN-worker6-k0r2; keystone spec work already landed (spec/03-adaptation.md 'Endpoint address policy (canonical TX/RX split)': emission policy applies to every transmitted packet incl. Rule255 ENCODE; DECODING is byte-preserving, MUST validate structure+checksums only, MUST NOT apply the endpoint address policy, so 'a packet one implementation cannot originate is still delivered intact by the other'). Python verified aligned: headers.py encode_rule255:188-189 and compression fallback :860-861 run _validate_rule255_emission_endpoints; decode_rule255:212 runs structural validation only. Rust violates the RX half: rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs decode_rule255 (:1444 area) routes through validate_full_ipv6 (:279) -> validate_address_policy (:241-263) and returns Err(InvalidPacket) on loopback/IPv4-mapped/bad-scope endpoints (k0r2 trigger bytes: src ::1, src ::ffff:192.0.2.1, dst ::1, dst ff01::1 scope 1, dst ff0f::1 scope 15) - identical on-air bytes decode in Python and fatal in Rust, and inflate RuleVersionFailureTracker via decompress_authenticated_frame_tracked (:1470-1482). Fix: decode_rule255 (and any RX-side full-packet validation reachable from it) must validate version/length/next-header/UDP length/checksum structure but NOT the endpoint policy; keep the TX paths (compress gate :2140, encode_rule255 :1414) enforcing validate_address_policy. Prefer an explicit split (e.g. structural validator used by decode vs TX validator) over a bool flag if it reads cleaner; keep public API churn minimal and document the RX/TX split in the doc comments. Pin with unit tests: decode_rule255 ACCEPTS the five k0r2 trigger classes; encode_rule255 still REJECTS them.
close_reason: Both halves of the k0r2 divergence were already implemented at HEAD (spec canonical TX/RX split landed in faed8ccfb5; Rust codec.rs already split validate_full_ipv6_structure (RX, policy-free) from validate_full_ipv6 (TX, structure+policy); Python already enforces _validate_rule255_emission_endpoints on encode+fallback and decodes emission-free). What was actually broken: (a) Python validate_rule7_addresses still raised stale 'invalid Rule 7 ...' texts from 95d85c3747 while the shared-vector test (faed8ccfb5) pins canonical 'invalid IPv6 ...' texts matching Rust - 10 rule7_*_rejected vectors failed fleet-wide on main; fixed the 3 message texts; python/tests/test_vectors.py 767/767. (b) Rust codec.rs endpoint-policy tests never compiled (Ipv6Addr::from_str without FromStr in scope); added use core::str::FromStr as _; in tests mod; cargo test -p lichen-schc --features std green (81 lib + all suites, incl. rule255_emission_rejects_policy_invalid_endpoints and rule255_decode_is_byte_preserving_despite_emission_policy); no_std lib build verified clean. 3x codereview (correctness/security/robustness, reviewer-model passes): all PASS, no new P0-P3 (one P3 env note duplicates the already-filed rust-oscore/Attic-paths blocker). Remaining k0r2 work tracked by child 1jbb (shared Rule255 endpoint-policy vectors consistency check + parity script rerun + close parent).

title: oscore observe notifications have no effective replay window: PIV check reads response_window but commit writes replay_window
description: Found by 3x codereview of the rust-oscore observe port (9liz unblock work; two reviewers converged independently, one with an empirical scratch test). In /home/mark/crates/oscore/src/lib.rs (machine-local clone, captured in patches/rust-oscore-local.patch): begin_unprotect_response_inner checks the response/notification PIV with is_response_reuse (~lib.rs:1308), which reads response_seq/response_window — but that window is only ever written by mark_response_used from the SERVER-side no-PIV branch of protect_response (~lib.rs:1111). PendingResponse::commit writes the PIV into the inbound REQUEST replay window via update_replay_window (lib.rs:259-261). Check window != commit window, so on a client the checked window is never initialized and is_response_reuse is always false: a captured notification (or explicit-PIV response) replays indefinitely at the OSCORE layer (AEAD intact). The doc comment on begin_unprotect_observe_response claims 'freshness is enforced by the response Partial IV replay window' — that enforcement does not exist. Ordinary responses are masked by the request-PIV one-shot guard; observe deliberately skips it (by design), leaving notifications as the one unprotected class. In-tree impact contained: lichen-node commits unconditionally but lichen-coap ObserveClient::process rejects Duplicate/Stale via the authenticated Class-E Observe sequence (lichen-coap/src/observe.rs:678-697). Fix direction: check the notification/response PIV with is_replay (the recipient window commit already writes — self-consistent, since response PIVs and request PIVs share the peer sender-seq space per RFC 8613; mirrors the pre-port unprotect.rs:199 design), or commit into response_window via mark_response_used. Must fix in the local clone + regenerate patches/rust-oscore-local.patch + add a notification-replay test; upstream push of the crate needs Mark's authorization.

title: Rust tunnel_auth evicts replay/revocation floors under capacity pressure; Python fail-closes with CAPACITY (P-R divergence)
description: Found by 3x codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-0rep (two reviewers converged, P1/P2 family). rust/lichen-gateway/src/tunnel_auth.rs floors are bounded at N with silent LRU eviction: accept_post floor_index fallback :339-348 evicts min-used floor, revoke() :247-256 does the same on unknown-key revoke with full floors (returns Ok). A revoked floor's used is never refreshed after revoke() (its entry was deleted; authorize_decapsulation refresh :408-414 only touches floors matching an ACCEPTED claim), so a revoked floor is always the first eviction candidate. If evicted, replaying the captured revoked POST (claim still unexpired) finds no floor and no entry -> accept_post re-accepts it and re-arms the data plane. Python mirror python/src/lichen/gateway/tunnel_auth.py never evicts floors: floors capped at _max_history (4x max_entries, :388), receive_post denies CAPACITY when full (:484-485), revoke() raises 'authorization replay history is full' and mutates nothing (:503-505); _revoked persists until genuine re-arm (:491) or root change (:435). Same inputs: Rust accepts, Python denies. Exploitability is low (forcing eviction of the target key needs N distinct newly-accepted keys, which requires fresh root-signed grants, not replays) but it is a semantic weakening plus a hard cross-impl divergence. Fix: mirror Python - give floors their own bounded history that fail-closes with a Capacity/TunnelAuthError variant when full (accept_post and revoke), never silently evict; align capacity constant with Python's 4x; add unit tests for accept-on-full and revoke-on-full; add shared vector post_cases if the corpus schema can express capacity denials.
close_reason: Fixed: tunnel_auth replay floors are no longer silently LRU-evicted. (1) replay_floors is now [[Option<ReplayFloor>; 4]; N] (FLOOR_SLOTS_PER_ENTRY=4, mirroring Python _max_history = 4 * max_entries; stable-Rust nested array since N*4 const arithmetic is unsupported); (2) accept_post of a NEW key with no free floor slot returns Err(TunnelAuthError::Capacity) instead of evicting the min-used floor - the old behavior let an attacker whose 5th grant evicted a REVOKED floor replay the captured revoked POST and re-arm the data plane; (3) revoke of an unknown key on a full history returns Err(Capacity) (Python raises 'authorization replay history is full') and, per review, now resolves the slot BEFORE any mutation so a refused revoke leaves the table untouched (struct invariant 'validation before mutation' restored); (4) existing keys reusing their own floor slot are never capacity-gated (Python parity); (5) Capacity maps through the uniform COAP_FORBIDDEN_CODE fail-closed policy; (6) struct doc updated. New test floor_capacity_fails_closed_and_retains_revoked_floor pins: 4 distinct keys fill the history, 5th accept -> Capacity, revoke-on-full -> Capacity, replay of the REVOKED A's captured post -> Revoked (the exploit pin), existing-key floor advance still accepted. Shared vector rows NOT added: the tunnel_authorization corpus schema expresses single-post cases only and cannot encode the table-full precondition; also generator drift on that file is tracked by wtxl (macOS canonical regeneration required) - noted rather than forced. Verification on heft: gateway lib 222/222 (new test + all prior), clippy clean, fmt applied. 3x delegated codereview: correctness found revoke-premutation (fixed) + stale doc (fixed); security PASS (capacity check order after auth/expiry/replay - no occupancy oracle for unauthenticated peers; fill-by-valid-grants is Python-parity, not divergence); edge PASS (N=0, equal-path_seq, flattened index boundaries exact, capacity boundary genuine with no mutation on refusal).

title: Rust tunnel_auth check_time rollback wipes replay/revocation floors; Python retains them (P-R divergence)
description: Found by 3x codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-0rep (two reviewers converged, P1). rust/lichen-gateway/src/tunnel_auth.rs:419-425 check_time() calls self.clear() on clock rollback, wiping entries AND replay_floors and resetting last_now=None (clear():213-218). title: C compress gate lacks IPv6 address policy; emits Rule255 that Python peers fatal on
description: P1, found by correctness+security codereview passes of project-LICHEN-worker6-hahk (both independent reviewers converged with probe evidence). lichen/subsys/lichen/schc/schc.c:557 gates compress via validate_ipv6_transport_lengths only, which performs zero address checks. Rules 0-7 reject these (scope checks, rule7 via validate_rule7_addresses) so emission is via the fallback path. title: announce_store accept(): failed floor write leaves stale cache entry that can regress the durable state
description: Found by correctness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-t8ox. rust/lichen-node/src/announce_store.rs:394-403: on the durable path, write(iid,false,next) commits the new state record, then write(iid,true,next)? at line 401 early-returns Err(Io) on failure, skipping remember(iid,next) at line 403. For an existing pin, load(iid) at line 378 cached the OLD state, so after the failed accept: cache=old, durable state=new, durable floor=old. Every subsequent load() takes the cache fast path (308-311) and returns the old state despite the durable record holding the new one, and a subsequent accept() validates against the stale cached state, so a replayed/held announce with old.seq < seq < new.seq (RFC 1982) passes the seq_gt check at 383 and is written over the newer durable state record - the sealed state regresses and an already-seen announce is re-accepted. The header's state-then-floor crash analysis (lines 10-13) assumes a crash destroys the cache; a non-fatal floor-write error (ENOSPC/EIO on the floor root) violates that while the cache survives. Fix: on the floor-write error path, self.records.remove(iid) before returning Err so the next load() rebuilds from disk (state=new, floor=old lag heals forward to new). Removal is the fail-safe option; caching next also works since durable state is next, but removal is simpler.
close_reason: Fixed in 64bdfc03bc: accept() evicts the IID cache entry when the floor witness write fails after the state commit (removes the stale pre-accept state that could otherwise re-validate a replayed intermediate sequence over the newer sealed state); module doc extended to cover the non-crash failure case; regression test failed_floor_write_evicts_stale_cache_and_load_rebuilds added (detaches floor_storage to drive the exact Err(Io) path, asserts durable state advanced on disk via raw record bytes, same-store load rebuilds to the durable state, replay of seq 150 rejected after heal, floor advances, restart serves seq 201). Verified: cargo test -p lichen-node --lib announce 52/52 green on heft; clippy -D warnings clean.

title: Rust and Python routers deliver in-transit RH3 packets locally on outer-dst match; C router forwards per RFC 6554
description: Confirmed empirically by the security codereview pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-njdx (live Router.route probe). In-transit source-routed packets (Routing header with segments_left != 0, outer dst = this node, UDP checksum validly over the RFC 2460 s8.1 final destination) are LOCALLY DELIVERED by Rust (lichen-node/src/stack.rs:562-566 delivers when ipv6_destination_is_local_or_multicast, which reads only bytes 24..40 with no segments-left check; lichen-schc/src/link.rs:184-193 admits on L2 destination alone) and Python (lichen/routing/router.py:474-476 returns DELIVER_LOCAL on outer-dst match; node.py:978-982 hands it to the app). C honors forwarding precedence: lichen/subsys/lichen/routing/router.c:504-522 forwards and never delivers while segments_left != 0, and additionally rejects at router level what the P/R gates admit: RH3 final address equal to outer dst (router.c:400-402), misaligned address grids, and multiple Routing headers (saw_routing) — Rust/Python have no router-level SRH validation at all (RFC 8200 s4.4 processes only the first Routing header; P/R gates accept a second one and derive checksum scope last-wins). Attack: an authenticated neighbor unicasts outer-dst=victim + RH3 SL=1 to any final -> the victim Rust/Python node consumes the datagram C would only relay; same wire bytes, opposite fate; downward RPL source-routed traffic silently terminates at the first Rust/Python relay. Fix direction: before local delivery, reject/deliver-local only when no Routing header has segments_left != 0 (mirror router.c), add router-level SRH validation (final != outer dst when SL!=0, single RH3, aligned address grid) to Rust and Python, and pin with cross-impl admission vectors. Related gate-level context: the SCHC-gate last-wins multi-RH acceptance is consistent P<->R (no gate-level bypass), recorded here for the router fix.
close_reason: Fixed and pinned. (1) Rust survey_routing_headers and Python survey_source_route now mirror C parse_ipv6_dispatch: in-transit RH3 (SL!=0) has forwarding precedence and is never delivered locally; envelope checks (hop_limit==0, unspecified/multicast source), HBH first+unique, terminal UDP>=8/ICMPv6>=4 min lengths, bounded extension chain (max 3 exts, C -E2BIG parity incl. the smuggled-5th-header hole), RH3 type-3-only, aligned grid, RFC 6554 4.2 reserved policy (Cmpr/Pad zero, rest ignored), MAX_ROUTE_HOPS=8, grid content checks (unspecified/multicast/dup/src/dst), SL<hop_limit. (2) Python node.py: RPL-DIO classification requires ICMPv6 immediately after IPv6 header (no ext headers) so RH3-bearing datagrams fall through to survey; _relay_source_routed gated on outer-dst-is-self; PacketError caught. (3) Cross-impl admission corpus test/vectors/srh_admission.json (34 cases, fixed verdict literals, stdlib-only generator generate_srh_admission.py with --check, JSON schema) consumed by Rust unit test srh_admission_vectors_match_c_router_policy and python tests/rpl/test_srh_admission_vectors.py. (4) Fixed malformed test packets that the aligned policy correctly rejects: rust rfc6554_route_crosses test (NH59+payload -> real UDP header) and three python test_node.py packets. Validation: cargo test -p lichen-node all green (341 incl. vectors); python pytest full suite green except pre-existing unrelated vector-generator drift (filed project-LICHEN-worker6-wtxl); ruff/rustfmt clean on touched files; delta re-review clean. Review follow-ups filed: nuz5 (gateway ingress bypass), nd1h (secure_transport divergence), j2st (own-source forward check).

title: C SCHC compress gate skips all UDP validation for ext-header packets and never verifies UDP checksums on the Rule255 fallback path
description: Confirmed empirically by 3x codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-njdx (three independent reviewers converged; ASan/UBSan-clean C probe). lichen/subsys/lichen/schc/schc_helpers.c validate_ipv6_transport_lengths:451 tests the OUTER next header (packet[6]) so any HBH(0)/Routing(43)/DSTOPT(60)-led packet returns SCHC_OK before the UDP length check, and no UDP checksum verification exists anywhere on the C compress path (checksum is computed only inside rule compressors over the outer dst, which ext-header packets can never match; schc_compress.c:104/180/406 are compute sites). lichen_schc_compress then emits verbatim Rule255 (subsys/schc/schc.c:122-131) and lichen_link_tx.c:134 transmits. Trigger bytes (src fe80::1, dst fe80::2, RH3 [17,2,3,1,0,0,0,0]+fe80::a, UDP 5000->5001 'ping'): (1) in-transit RH3 with checksum over the OUTER dst 0xfcef -> Python/Rust REJECT (RFC 2460 s8.1 requires final-dst scope), C ACCEPTS and re-emits ff+packet; (2) UDP length field says 8 with 12 bytes present -> P/R REJECT, C ACCEPTS; (3) wire checksum 0x0000 -> P/R REJECT, C ACCEPTS; (4) HBH-terminated UDP with garbage checksum 0xdead -> P/R REJECT, C ACCEPTS. Same root cause makes the njdx in-transit checksum-scope vector vacuous under C. Related pre-existing instance of the identical gap (same bead fix): plain UDP to non-5683/non-10883 ports with wrong (0x1234) or zero checksum is accepted by the C Rule255 fallback while Python/Rust reject (rules only verify checksums for CoAP/MQTT-SN/ICMPv6 shapes). Impact: C nodes inject Rule255 datagrams every Rust/Python node fatals on at ingress decode_rule255 -> validate_full_ipv6 (blackhole/partition on mixed fleets). Fix: track the chain-final offset and upper-layer destination in the C walk (mirroring Rust codec.rs:281-348), verify UDP length + nonzero valid checksum over the RFC 2460 s8.1 destination there, and apply the same checks to the direct-UDP fallback path; add shared malformed vectors for each class.
close_reason: Re-close: this close was lost in a beads-store merge (live store resurrected pre-close in_progress state with no close reason; the work itself was already complete and committed before the close). Fixed and pinned. title: sx12xx modem-hold semantics break TX once async RX is armed; L2 needs driver-level arbitration contract
description: Found by 3x codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-sb0b (all three reviewers converged, P0). Upstream sx12xx (v3.7.0, incl. patches/zephyr-v3.7.0-local.patch which does not touch modem semantics): sx12xx_lora_recv_async() takes modem_acquire() and holds modem_usage=BUSY for the entire armed lifetime; sx12xx_ev_rx_done() auto-re-arms Radio.Rx(0) and never releases. Consequences once L2 arms async RX (sb0b): every lora_send() fails -EBUSY at the driver's modem_acquire (all TX dead on Heltec/T-Deck/nRF SX12xx boards); L2-level modem_mutex/tx_pending arbitration does not help because the driver never consults them. Note the driver ALSO silently overwrites the callback on double-arm (opposite of loopback's -EBUSY). Fix options: (a) L2 wraps TX with explicit disarm (recv_async(dev,NULL)) + re-arm under its existing modem_mutex, or (b) drivers release the modem between async frames and L2 keeps one-shot re-arm, or (c) driver-level arbitration with a written contract in lora_l2.h. Coordinate with the TX-side async refactor (child of project-LICHEN-worker6-9hfe) before choosing. Also verify modem_release clears async_rx_cb (suspected pre-existing leak). Test-only loopback half of this was fixed inside sb0b (one-shot delivery).

title: Routing-header divergence: Rust enforces RPL SRH type-3 + checksum over final destination, Python accepts any Routing type and checksums over outer destination
description: Confirmed empirically by 2 independent codereview passes (discovered-from project-LICHEN-worker6-xuc8). Rust validate_full_ipv6 (rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs:297-317) requires Routing type 3 (RPL RH3), rejects ext_len<24/flags!=0/segments_left>address_count, and when segments_left==0 verifies the UDP checksum over the FINAL destination per RFC 2460 s8.1 (codec.rs:314-316,345). Python validate_full_ipv6 (python/src/lichen/schc/headers.py:125-133 + python/src/lichen/ipv6/packet.py:237-248) walks ANY Routing header via generic TLV with no type/segments validation and always checksums over the outer destination. Diverges in BOTH directions with concrete trigger bytes: (A) valid RH3+UDP checksummed over final dst -> Rust Rule255 Ok, Python fatal 'invalid Rule 255 IPv6 UDP checksum' (Rust-encoded in-transit datagram fatally rejected by Python); (B) Routing type 0 (forbidden class, RFC 5095) with segments_left=1 and outer-dst checksum -> Python Rule255 accepted and forwarded, Rust fatal 'unsupported RPL source-routing header'. Same wire bytes get opposite verdicts on both encode and decode. Fix needs one canonical policy (RH3-only + RFC 2460 s8.1 checksum scope is the standards-correct candidate), aligned Python+Rust, plus shared SRH fallback/malformed vectors. Related but distinct: project-LICHEN-worker6-prld (Rule255 laxness generally), project-LICHEN-worker6-0t11 (Rule 1/6 prefix divergence).
close_reason: Fixed and pinned. Canonical policy = RH3-only routing headers (RFC 6554: type 3, CmprI/CmprE/Pad octets zero, full 128-bit addresses, segments_left <= address_count; RFC 5095 type 0 rejected) + RFC 2460 s8.1 UDP checksum scope (final RH3 address while segments_left != 0, else outer dst). Changes: (1) Python validate_full_ipv6 gains _validate_routing_headers (headers.py) mirroring Rust codec.rs:281-328 exactly (index mapping, 24-byte floor, address_count floor-division, last-address slice, last-RH3-wins, Fragment rejection via parser, checksum over returned upper-layer dst). (2) C validate_ipv6_header_chain added in schc_helpers.c + IPV6_NH_*/IPV6_ROUTING_TYPE_RPL_SRH constants in schc_internal.h, called from validate_ipv6_transport_lengths — required so the shared vectors hold C parity. (3) Rust production code unchanged (was already canonical); added tests srh_packet/routing_header_policy_matches_rfc6554_and_rfc2460/fragment_header_is_unsupported. (4) 4 shared vectors in schc_compression.json after rpl_dao_no_dodagid_nonmatch: srh3_in_transit_udp_fallback (fallback), routing_type0_malformed, srh3_segments_left_overflow_malformed, ipv6_fragment_header_malformed — hex built with an independent RFC 1071 checksum oracle (no lichen code), then byte-verified by a reviewer's own implementation. Gates: python tests/schc + test_vectors + relay vectors 2170 passed (incl 5 new header tests), vector tooling 57 passed; rust lib 78 passed, shared_vectors 3 passed (44 vectors); C parity scripts/check-schc-compression-parity.py PASS across Python+Rust+C (ASan/UBSan); ruff, mypy, clippy, cppcheck, cargo fmt clean. 3x codereview (correctness/security/robustness, all empirical) found no defect in the changed Python/C/Rust logic or vectors; all confirmed findings are adjacent pre-existing gaps filed as new beads discovered-from this one: worker6-hahk (P1 C compress gate skips UDP checks for ext-header packets + no checksum on Rule255 fallback), worker6-lqgt (P2 C Rule255 decompress validates nothing), worker6-xyix (P1 Rust/Python routers deliver in-transit RH3 locally where C forwards per RFC 6554), worker6-nyx7 (P3 C latent OOB read guard). The Python-vs-Rust address-policy laxness already tracked as worker6-k0r2 (no duplicate filed). Note: C checksum non-enforcement is NOT a regression of this bead's Python<->Rust alignment; it is the pre-existing broader C-gate gap in worker6-hahk.

title: Rule255 gate address-policy divergence: Python accepts loopback IPv4-mapped bad-scope-multicast, Rust fatals same bytes
description: Confirmed empirically by 3x codereview (discovered-from project-LICHEN-worker6-xuc8). Python validate_full_ipv6 -> _validate_ipv6_addresses (python/src/lichen/schc/headers.py:83-87) rejects only unspecified/multicast source and unspecified destination; Rule 255 encode (headers.py:145,816) and decode (headers.py:168) accept loopback endpoints, IPv4-mapped endpoints, and multicast destinations of ANY scope. Rust validate_address_policy (rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs:241-263, called from validate_full_ipv6:279 gating compress:2140, encode_rule255:1414, decode_rule255:1444) additionally rejects loopback, IPv4-mapped, and multicast scope outside 2..=14. Trigger bytes (port 10883, valid checksum, TC=FL=0 or TC=0x10): src=::1, src=::ffff:192.0.2.1, dst=::1, dst=ff01::1 (scope 1), dst=ff0f::1 (scope 15): Python emits byte-preserving Rule255 and round-trips; Rust returns Err(InvalidPacket) on compress AND on decompress of the Python-emitted bytes — identical on-air bytes decode in one implementation and not the other (hard interop break; also inflates RuleVersionFailureTracker misbehaving-peer notifications via decompress_authenticated_frame_tracked codec.rs:1470-1482). Spec is ambiguous: spec/03-adaptation.md:170-177 scopes address policy to Rule 7 selection, :183-186 mandates Rule255 fallback for packets failing only a matching requirement, :415-417 defines Rule255 payload validity without address policy (favors Python), but :177 invalidates interface-local scope 1 on a transmitted link (favors Rust). Fix needs a spec-level canonicalization of validate_full_ipv6 endpoint policy, aligned in both implementations, plus shared fallback vectors for loopback/IPv4-mapped/scope-0-1-15 endpoints. Distinct from project-LICHEN-worker6-prld (which covers Rule255 accepting structurally malformed data; this is opposite-verdict divergence on structurally valid data).
close_reason: Closed: last child 1jbb complete. Final state of the k0r2 divergence: the 5 trigger classes (loopback src, IPv4-mapped src, loopback dst, scope-1 dst, scope-15 dst) are pinned by shared corpus rows with encode-REJECT + byte-preserving-decode-ACCEPT asserted in BOTH implementations (rust RX split landed faed8ccfb5/wlts; python emission enforcement landed 8b07985284); python rule7 message texts canonicalized ef4eb8de22 (767->769 tests green fleet-side); rust test compile fixed same commit. Remaining endpoint-policy work tracked by: 29bu (P1: python RX still applies _validate_ipv6_addresses on the 3 unspecified/multicast-source classes - spec 03 TX/RX split violation found by probe during this round, independently corroborated by reviewer-model security pass; adds the 3 remaining corpus rows when fixed) and wrxl (P1: C compress gate lacks the emission policy entirely). title: Announce store capacity policy: cache-counted gate allows durable overflow and bricks pinned peers
description: announce_store.rs capacity checks count self.records (volatile cache, resets on restart), not durable records. Trace: accept 40 originators, restart, accept 40 new ones (gate passes on empty cache) -> 80 durable records; after next restart the first 64 load()s fill the cache and the remaining durably-pinned peers get Err(Full) from load()/accept() for the process lifetime. Separately an attacker can saturate the store with 64 self-minted TOFU identities, blocking new legitimate pins until restart, then re-fill after each restart. Fix: load() must return valid durable state even at full cache (skip the cache insert — cache is an optimization); accept's cap applies only to IIDs with no durable record; LRU-evict cache entries on capacity (durable floors persist). Test store_capacity_is_bounded only covers the ephemeral store. Found by correctness+security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-12zy.

title: First-accept crash window permanently bricks an originator
description: announce_store.rs accept() writes state then floor. The doc invariant (crash between writes leaves floor lagging, healed forward) only holds when a floor already exists. On the FIRST-ever accept for an IID, a crash or transient IO error on the floor write leaves (Some(state), None): load() returns Err(Corrupt) forever, accept() propagates it via self.load(iid)?, and there is deliberately no removal API — the originator is bricked short of manual file deletion. Fix: heal (Some, None) on first contact by writing floor := state — safe because the sealed state record is unforgeable under the seal threat model and a deleted floor cannot lower trust below it — or add a guarded recovery/tombstone API. Found by correctness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-12zy.
close_reason: Fixed: load() now heals (Some(state), None) by rewriting floor := sealed state (announce_store.rs:270-275), unbricking the first-accept crash window; (None, Some(_)) stays fail-closed. New regression test store_heals_first_accept_crash_window_instead_of_bricking covers un-brick, durable heal, held-seq refusal, and continued advance; mirror-half test updated to assert heal. title: [bug] tunnel_auth: revoked-post resubmission returns Revoked but regression test expects Replay
description: lichen-gateway/src/tunnel_auth.rs test revocation_root_change_expiry_and_lru_fail_closed (tunnel_auth.rs:921-975) fails deterministically on current main at :954-957: after table.revoke(second_claim...) succeeds, re-accepting the identical root post (accept_post(second.body..., own, 3)) returns Err(TunnelAuthError::Revoked) while the regression test asserts Err(TunnelAuthError::Replay). Repro: cargo test -p lichen-gateway --lib tunnel_auth::tests::revocation_root_change_expiry_and_lru_fail_closed (2/2 runs failed; 211 other lib tests pass). Root cause to adjudicate: accept_post() check ordering now classifies the revoked-then-replayed post as Revoked (revocation check precedes replay-window check), but the test (and possibly spec/06 tunnel-auth text) treats replay as the expected failure class for an identical resubmitted post. Decide the canonical classification: if Revoked-first ordering is deliberate (fail-closed on revocation before anti-replay), update the test assertion and any spec text; if replay-first is canonical, fix accept_post ordering and re-run the full revocation/expiry/LRU matrix. Discovered while validating bead 5rx2 (unrelated subsystem; no code was changed).
close_reason: Adjudicated: Revoked is the canonical classification; fixed the regression test's expectation (tunnel_auth.rs:954-961). Basis: revoke() deletes the accepted entry but retains a revoked floor (tunnel_auth.rs:257-267), so after revocation accept_post cannot distinguish a byte-identical replay from a stale-seq post — the design keeps no post-revocation entry cache. The floor check therefore deliberately classifies every equal/stale-seq post against a revoked floor as Revoked via the explicit retained.revoked branch (tunnel_auth.rs:316-320), which is strictly more informative than Replay and equally fail-closed. The test expectation required a distinction the design does not maintain and was committed red alongside its own implementation (both arrived in 660b9bf3bf; never green). Non-revoked replay still reports Replay (unchanged, asserted elsewhere). Spec is silent on the ordering. Verification: cargo test -p lichen-gateway all suites pass (212 lib + 3 integration), clippy clean, fmt clean.

title: GroupMobility._update_jitter redraw loop hangs on giant dt with tiny jitter_update_us
description: Found in 3x codereview of uory fix (mobility.py ~:398). _update_jitter's 'while self._jitter_elapsed_us >= self.jitter_update_us' loop is NOT covered by the step() iteration cap: with jitter_m>0, jitter_update_us=1, dt_us=10**18 it performs ~dt/jitter_update_us redraw iterations (RNG+trig per member per pass) - the exact hang class uory fixed for the movement loops. Fix: cap redraws per call (or compute redraw count arithmetically: elapsed = (elapsed + dt) % jitter_update_us, redraws = total // jitter_update_us, drawing only the last few targets that matter). Test: jitter_m>0 + jitter_update_us=1 + giant dt terminates (giant-dt test file test_mobility_giant_dt.py currently only covers jitter_m=0).
acceptance_criteria: giant-dt regression test with jitter_m>0/jitter_update_us=1 passes; no other behavior change for normal configs
close_reason: Fixed: _update_jitter redraw loop now capped at _MAX_STEP_ITERATIONS per step() call (same bounded-work policy as the movement loops); elapsed zeroed on break. Behavior identical for all configs drawing <= 100k target sets; giant-dt configs bounded (~100k redraws). New regression test test_group_mobility_giant_dt_tiny_jitter_update_terminates. Suite 1645 passed, mypy+ruff clean.

title: Implement lora_recv_async in LICHEN LoRa drivers (prereq for L2 async RX)
description: Bead sb0b's premise 'driver async API already exists' is false: lr1110.c:627, lora_sim.c:433, lora_renode.c:279 all return -ENOTSUP, and lora_loopback.c (ping_l2 RX source) has no recv_async vtable slot at all (NULL fp call). Wiring lichen L2 to lora_recv_async without this work makes every driver deaf - a hardware RX regression (rx_thread polling works today on LR1110). Implement recv_async: LR1110 DIO1 RX_DONE IRQ + RX-continuous re-arm per SX126x/LR1110 datasheet; loopback driver delivers queued packets via registered cb (work-item context); sim/renode at minimum must not silently -ENOTSUP once L2 depends on it. Discovered from sb0b during claim check.
acceptance_criteria: lora_recv_async on each driver delivers frames (loopback: ping_l2 RX path; lr1110: DIO1 IRQ path per datasheet); L2 async tests pass; no NULL recv_async vtable slots remain
close_reason: Implemented lora_recv_async on all four drivers (loopback, sim, renode, lr1110). Loopback: work-item delivery of queued packets; sim: dedicated RX thread speaking the push protocol (RX_ENTER/RX_PACKET/RX_TIMEOUT_PUSH, same as lichen-hal/lichen-embassy Rust clients) with thread-owned modem release; renode: self-rescheduling 10ms delayable-work poller; lr1110: DIO9 IRQ path re-enabled while armed with RX-continuous re-arm per datasheet, fail-stop disarm on SPI failure. All four use upstream sx12xx semantics: CAS modem lock, -EBUSY on conflict, cancel via cb=NULL (-EINVAL if idle). Fixed 3-review findings: failed-acquire counter leak (atomic_cas), sim cancel/recv-thread socket cross-consumption (thread releases modem on park, self-disarm after 10 consecutive exchange failures), lr1110 NULL-cb race (cb_lock + single snapshot), lr1110 rearm storm (fail-stop), drain_exact signed-length regression, renode mid-run cancel race (cancel_delayable_sync + pre-register re-check), loopback sync-recv steal (-EBUSY when armed), unbounded drain cap, k_thread_create under spinlock, sim stack default 4096. Validated on AWS Zephyr v3.7.0 builder (worktree 1m92-validate): loopback+sim compile native_sim/native/64, renode compiles nucleo_wl55jc, lr1110 compiles t1000_e/nrf52840; new ztest test_loopback_recv_async_delivers_frames passes (arm, -EBUSY double-arm, delivery with correct len/RSSI/SNR, cancel 0, -EINVAL double cancel); full hal suite passes both configs; cppcheck clean. Pre-existing (not this bead): coap_status.c static-assert/switch-enum failures break puck app + ping_l2 builds against v3.7.0 - filed separately.

title: test_tofu_capacity_rejects_active_session_saturation fails on HEAD: receive returns CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED, test expects REPLAY

Likely test expectation or pin-budget precheck ordering drifted in the 660b9bf3bf link-layer security commit. NOT caused by project-LICHEN-worker6-jqa9 fix (verified via stash). title: [review] spec/02-physical-link.md 4.5 still mandates FNV-1a32 for short-address DAD; contradicts CRC32-IEEE resolution everywhere else
description: P1, wave-7 review. spec/02-physical-link.md:435-500 (also :67) says 'Short-address DAD uses FNV-1a32 ... Implementations MUST match test/vectors/short_addr_dad.json' but the vector files (short_addr_dad.json:3, dad_hash_clarification.json:8-13), Python (short_addr.py), and Rust (short_addr.rs) now mandate CRC32-IEEE (init 0x4348454E, xorout 0xFFFFFFFF, poly 0xEDB88320); 04-network.md:250 already specifies crc32_ieee. A spec-literal implementation today fails the vectors and vice versa - recreates the duplicated-pseudocode ambiguity bo37 was filed to eliminate. Fix: spec-only edit - replace 4.5 FNV pseudocode + line 67 with the crc32_ieee form or cross-ref 04-network.md 12.3; keep FNV only for CCP channel/SF selection. Reviewer independently verified all corrected vector values (0x5dd5056e etc.) with a hand-rolled CRC oracle - the values are right, only the spec text is stale.
close_reason: spec/02-physical-link.md 4.5 rewritten: FNV-1a32 pseudocode replaced with CRC-32/IEEE (reflected, poly 0xEDB88320, init 0x4348454E = ASCII LICHEN, xorout 0xFFFFFFFF - zlib/binascii convention), matching short_addr.py (python/src/lichen/link/short_addr.py:98-139) and short_addr.rs + the vector corpus. derive_short_addr / derive_short_addr_with_seed now crc32_ieee-based; seed mixing kept (LE, mixed[4..8]). Line 67 SF-assignment fallback updated: hash_32/FNV-1a32 retained for CCP channel+SF selection only, DAD cross-ref updated. Pseudocode transcription independently verified: binascii.crc32(0011223344556677, 0x4348454E) = 0x5dd5056e == pinned vectors[0].full_crc32.

title: Python root DIO verifier accepts impersonated DODAGID (no derivation binding check)
description: Found wiring test/vectors/root_dio_signature.json into python/tests/crypto/test_orphan_vector_consumers.py. Vector root_dio_signature_impersonation pins expected={signature_valid:true, dodagid_binding_valid:false, overall_valid:false, error:dodagid_mismatch} ('Attacker pubkey does not derive to claimed DODAGID'). Python verify_root_dio_signature (python/src/lichen/crypto/root_dio_signature.py:291) only cross-checks payload.dodag_id against a supplied dio_dodag_id; it never checks that dodag_id derives from the signer pubkey/root_iid. Calling verify_root_dio_signature(sig, attacker_pubkey, current_time=0, dio_dodag_id=claimed_dodag_id) returns (True, None): the attacker-signed DIO claiming the victim DODAGID is ACCEPTED. Spec 8.10.1 binding requires dodag_id to embed/derive from the root identity (dodag_id = 0220 || root_iid || root_iid[:6]-pattern in vectors). Fix: add derivation check (reject DODAG_ID_MISMATCH when dodag_id does not bind to root_iid/pubkey), then tighten the consumer test which currently documents the gap with an assertion that fails when the fix lands. Cross-check C/Zephyr and Rust verifiers for the same gap.
close_reason: Added unconditional DODAGID-to-signer-key binding check in verify_root_dio_signature (python/src/lichen/crypto/root_dio_signature.py): after the kid/IID check, payload.dodag_id must equal yggdrasil_address(pubkey).packed (0x02 || SHA512(pubkey)[0:7] || masked-IID, per spec 06-security.md key-binding invariant and the vector oracle 'DODAGID must equal AddrForKey(root_pubkey)'); else reject DODAG_ID_MISMATCH. Check runs even when dio_dodag_id cross-check is omitted, and after IID_MISMATCH so kid_mismatch precedence is preserved. Tightened test_orphan_vector_consumers.py impersonation case: removed the (True, None) ratchet, now strictly asserts vector pins (False, DODAG_ID_MISMATCH) both with and without the cross-check param. Vector file unchanged (rule derived from existing fields). Rust counterpart: no root-DIO COSE verifier exists in rust/ (lichen-rpl verify.rs DAO envelope verify already binds origin == ygg_addr_from_pubkey), so no Rust gap to file. Evidence: pytest test_orphan_vector_consumers.py 39 passed/5 skipped; -k root_dio 45 passed/5 skipped; full python/tests/crypto 702 passed/5 skipped/0 failed; ruff clean.

title: Refactor Zephyr L2 to use async LoRa API (interrupt-driven RX/TX)
description:
Replace polling rx_thread with lora_recv_async() callback. Replace blocking lora_send() with lora_send_async(). Wire CAD to CadDone interrupt.

## Current (bad)
- rx_thread loops calling blocking lora_recv() with 10ms yield sleeps
- TX blocks in lora_send()
- Retries use k_sleep() delays

## Target (good)
- lora_recv_async() registers callback, fires on DIO1 RX_DONE IRQ
- lora_send_async() with TX_DONE callback
- CAD_DONE IRQ drives CSMA state machine directly
- No polling, no sleeps, no retries - just state + interrupts

## Files
- lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/lora_l2_rx.c (rx_thread -> async callback)
- lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/lora_l2_tx.c (blocking send -> async)
- lichen/subsys/lichen/link/csma.c (wire to CAD IRQ)

## Verification
- Existing tests pass
- No k_sleep in hot paths
- Radio state machine matches SX126x datasheet section 13
notes:
Scope: Zephyr C only (Rust Embassy and Python asyncio already event-driven).

Why P1:
- Power: CPU sleeps between interrupts vs spinning in poll loops. Critical for battery nodes.
- Responsiveness: UI/shell not blocked waiting on radio timeouts. 
- Correctness: No timing assumptions. Hardware tells you when it's ready.
- Debuggability: State machine with clear transitions vs "add another sleep."
close_reason: Decomposed into 4 P1 children (async driver API already exists in all 3 drivers, so no driver-exposure child needed; L2 refactor is ~1450 lines across rx/tx/cad + lifecycle, well over 50-line implement threshold): project-LICHEN-worker6-sb0b (RX async: rx_thread->lora_recv_async, immediately ready), project-LICHEN-worker6-0lm8 (TX async: lora_send->lora_send_async + TX_DONE completion, blocked by sb0b), project-LICHEN-worker6-uwip (CAD: blocking lichen_lora_cad_run -> CadDone IRQ driving csma.c state machine, blocked by 0lm8), project-LICHEN-worker6-rx2w (integration sweep: no k_sleep hot paths, SX126x datasheet 13 conformance, full test run, blocked by sb0b+0lm8+uwip).

title: [review] lichen-node forwarder drops DAOs carrying generalized Targets (wave-6 wire-profile widening broke multi-hop)
description: P1, wave-6 review. message.rs:481 now admits generalized Target bodies, but lichen-node/src/routing/router.rs:1148 dao_parents_for_source parses each target with RplTarget::from_bytes which still requires exactly 18 bytes + prefix_len==128 + flags==0 (message.rs:706-720), and ok()? aborts the whole function on the first non-conforming option; node.rs:597-601 treats None as drop-not-forward. Net: the legitimate grouped DAO (self-/128 + delegated-/64) proven by the new end-to-end test is silently dropped at the first non-root hop - delegated prefixes only propagate when the advertiser is adjacent to the root. Fails closed, no security exposure, but breaks the feature's multi-hop story. Fix: teach dao_parents_for_source the 8.7.1 generalized body shape (or skip-and-continue per-option instead of aborting) + multi-hop forwarding test with a delegated-/64 DAO. title: Port prefix-authorization gate to C DAO processing
description: lichen/subsys/lichen/rpl/rpl_dao_process.c process_dao() checks channel authentication, RPL instance/DODAG scope, and sequence freshness, but has NO per-origin prefix authorization: any authenticated sender can advertise any target (no self-/128 binding, no delegation table, no /0 denial). The Rust reference implementation now has this gate (DaoManager::authorize_dao_prefixes + PrefixDelegations in rust/lichen-rpl/src/routing.rs, spec/05-routing.md section 8.7.1-8.7.2). Port the gate to rpl_dao_process.c with literal allow/deny parity tests (self /128 allowed, delegated allowed, foreign denied, /0 denied, no state mutation on denial). Delegation bootstrap/persistence is a separate concern per the Rust design.
close_reason: C DAO prefix-authorization gate ported with sub-/128 generalized semantics (resolution (b), cross-ref l327). DESIGN: (1) Delegation table in rpl_dao_process.c implements the free-function API already declared in rpl_routing.h (lichen_rpl_prefix_delegate/revoke/delegation_authorizes/delegations_reset, CONFIG_LICHEN_RPL_MAX_PREFIX_DELEGATIONS=64): static file-scope storage, no malloc, operator-seeded process-lifetime state, canonicalizing + idempotent delegate, exact-match authorizes (no sub/aggregate inheritance), fail-closed on NULL//0/>128 (ERR_INVALID) and capacity (ERR_FULL). Gate reads the table under the DAO manager mutex; threading contract documented (mirrors Rust &mut exclusivity; Rust keys by pubkey, C by verified DAO Source Address per header note). (2) dao_targets_match_origin replaced by dao_targets_authorized: every Target canonicalized per spec/05-routing.md 8.7.1 (reserved flags + bits beyond Prefix Length ignored), self-/128 allowed, else exact delegation required; /0, truncated bodies, prefix_len>128, and targetless DAOs fail closed; runs in process_dao BEFORE extract/slot/sequence/graph/rebuild so denials are zero-mutation. (3) extract_updates Target parsing generalized to prefix_len 1..=128 with >=ceil(prefix_len/8) octets, canonicalized; /0 rejected. (4) WIRE LAYER: validate_dao_options in messages.c enforced the pre-generalized profile (Target data_len==18, flags==0) which rejected generalized bodies before the gate; relaxed to mirror Rust is_generalized_target_body (len>=2, plen<=128, len-2>=ceil(plen/8), flags ignored) - rpl_messages.h doc comments updated; lichen_rpl_target_parse left untouched (test-vector-pinned, no production caller after this change). PARITY with rust/lichen-rpl/tests/dao_prefix_authorization.rs: self-/128 allow+Applied, foreign /128 deny, unauth/absent-origin fail-closed (pre-existing matrix, now 4 rows counted as passes); foreign /64 + /0 gate-denied pre-mutation (memcmp of whole root_state incl. workspace); truncated /64, plen 129, 1-byte target body, targetless all rejected; delegation API fail-closed (/0, /129, exact-match /63+/72+/56, foreign-origin binding, non-canonical lookup denied, idempotent re-delegate, 64 capacity + 65th ERR_FULL + idempotent at capacity, revoke canonical + absent no-op, reset); delegated /64 end-to-end Applied with canonical snapshot (active, seq verified) and route installed, plus delegated foreign /128 Applied; non-canonical /64 body (extra 0xff host bytes) canonicalized end-to-end; reserved-flags /128 accepted (8.7.1 receivers-ignore); /127 boundary encoding (low bit ignored) installed as canonical /127; /63 vs /64 delegation denied pre-mutation. title: Zephyr C: NV-persisted per-gateway claim_seq replay gate (slot_claim_settings)
description:
NV-persisted per-gateway claim_seq high-water for the slot-claim replay gate (parent design D4). Spec basis: GCP-6.5 step 8 + persistence table (spec/08-gateway-coordination.md:193,210-220) as amended by the spec child (receiver-side MUST persist).

Template: lichen/subsys/lichen/link/replay_settings.c:1-76 — SETTINGS_STATIC_HANDLER_DEFINE with root "lichen/replay", dual-blob a/b wear-leveling, K_MUTEX, load/save ops. Mirror that pattern under root "lichen/slot_claim", one entry per gateway IID (settings name = 16 hex chars of IID, value = uint32 LE high-water).

Implementation:
1. New module lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/slot_claim_settings.c (+ Kconfig CONFIG_LICHEN_SLOT_CLAIM_REPLAY, default y when slot coord is on): API slot_claim_seq_load(iid, &seq) / slot_claim_seq_store(iid, seq); RAM cache table of CONFIG_LICHEN_SLOT_COORD_MAX_GATEWAYS {iid[8], seq, valid} guarded by mutex; lazy settings_load_subtree("lichen/slot_claim") at coord init.
2. Wire into lichen_slot_coord_process_claim (coap_slot_coord.c:290-341) after signature verify and expiry check, BEFORE conflict resolution (:341-365): if claim_seq <= cached -> new enum LICHEN_CLAIM_REJECT_REPLAY (coap_slot_coord.h:83-93, value 5) -> 4.03 Forbidden at the resource (:1013-1024 mapping). On accept path, store new high-water BEFORE registering the gateway (:367-376) — persist-first: a burned seq only forces the legitimate sender to increment (spec :219); apply-then-persist reopens the replay window on crash-between.
3. New result enum value mapped in the POST handler response-code selection; do not silent-discard replay (it is a validation failure per spec :198, not a signature failure).
4. Wear consideration: claims are infrequent (superframe-scale); note expected write rate in the Kconfig help text; dual-blob pattern from replay_settings.c keeps erase wear bounded.
5. Host test: simulate store/load cycles + reboot (re-open) in the lichen/tests/ CMake harness with a settings backend stub; assert reject <= cached, accept > cached, persistence survives re-init.

Acceptance criteria:
- Claim with claim_seq equal to or below the persisted high-water for that IID is rejected with LICHEN_CLAIM_REJECT_REPLAY -> 4.03; higher seq accepted and persisted.
- High-water survives simulated reboot (RAM cache rebuilt from NV).
- First-ever claim from an IID (no cached entry) accepted per spec :193.
- Store happens before slot-table mutation (unit test asserts ordering via hooks or state inspection).
- Host CMake test passes ASan/UBSan; cppcheck clean.
close_reason: Decomposed per >50-line rule: child 1 = slot_claim_settings.c NV settings module (discovered-from nwjl.4), child 2 = wiring into lichen_slot_coord_process_claim + LICHEN_CLAIM_REJECT_REPLAY + 4.03 mapping + replay test. Full template/spec refs preserved in child descriptions. Picking up smaller beads per one-bead loop.

title: Zephyr C: slot-claim COSE_Sign1 decode+verify+gating in coap_slot_coord.c
description:

Current defects (evidence):
