title: accept_authenticated_schc_packet admits overheard unicast SCHC
description:
File: rust/lichen-schc/src/link.rs accept_authenticated_schc_packet

lichen-link::LinkLayer::receive_frame authenticates known-peer frames with no destination admission (unlike Python LinkLayer.receive _wire_is_for_local, which returns NOT_FOR_US before a receipt exists). AuthenticatedFragmentReceiver::receive_frame in this crate already requires frame.is_unicast_for(link). accept_authenticated_schc_packet does not inspect destination_mode/destination at all.

On LoRa everyone hears the air. An Extended unicast SCHC data frame destined to Charlie, overheard by Bob who has Alice's DIO context, therefore decompresses: is_current_for and accepts_authenticated_frame pass, counter > DIO floor passes, peer.decompress runs. Callers that then route/deliver the IPv6 (node/stack) can locally process or relay a frame that was not addressed to them, duplicating Charlie's copy. Broadcast (AddrMode::None) must remain admissible, matching Python _wire_is_for_local.

Fix: before decompress, require the authenticated destination to be this receiver: Extended dest == link.local_eui64(), None/broadcast allowed, Short only if the link has that short address, Elided only when the inner IPv6 dest is local or multicast. Reject others as InvalidPacket/InvalidPeerEvidence. Do not require is_unicast_for (that would drop legitimate broadcast SCHC).
acceptance_criteria: accept_authenticated_schc_packet rejects an otherwise valid authenticated SCHC data frame whose Extended destination is another node's EUI-64. The same payload accepted when dest is the receiving link's EUI-64 still decompresses. AddrMode::None broadcast SCHC still accepts. Behavior matches Python receive NOT_FOR_US for overheard unicast and does not break broadcast. Test covers Extended-foreign, Extended-local, and broadcast on one admitted peer context.
notes: 2026-08-26 Phase-2 fix: reproduced Bob accepting Alice's authenticated SCHC frame addressed to Charlie (Ok(59)). accept_authenticated_schc_packet now rejects foreign Extended and all Short destinations before payload classification/decompression (LinkLayer has no installed local short-address state), admits local Extended and None broadcast, and validates Elided packets against the decoded inner IPv6 destination (local link-local, local native 0200::/8, or multicast only). Elided decode uses a bounded 1500-byte scratch buffer so rejected foreign traffic leaves caller output unchanged. Regression covers Extended foreign/local, broadcast, Short fail-closed, Elided link-local/native/multicast/foreign, one peer context, and output non-mutation. Green: focused regression; full lichen-schc --features std (71 unit, all integrations/vectors/docs); strict scoped Clippy std all-targets; no-default-features check; targeted rustfmt and diff check. Rust-only surface; no applicable C/Zephyr module and no Python changes (existing Python filtering was the oracle). No Phase-3 review.
close_reason: Reject overheard authenticated unicast SCHC before decompression; preserve broadcast and validated elided local/multicast admission with green Rust gates.

title: accept/compress keep superseded DIO SCHC policy live
description:
File: rust/lichen-schc/src/link.rs

compress_schc_for_peer and accept_authenticated_schc_packet gate only on peer.is_current_for(link) (DIO evidence still accepted by this LinkLayer: same receiver Arc, current key-generation Arc, still pinned). That is not 'latest DIO for this signer'.

PeerContextAuthority::issue_from_authenticated_dio and FragmentationPolicy::install_peer both reject authenticated_counter <= the stored floor and bump generation so an older capability fails is_current/accepts_entry. from_authenticated_dio_frame (the only constructor that sets evidence, which is_current_for requires) has no such registry. A later DIO for the same signer (higher seqnum, possibly incompatible Rule Set Version) leaves the earlier AuthenticatedPeerSchcContext fully usable:

- compress_schc_for_peer still encodes under the old remote_version (v3 compressed rules after a mismatch DIO, or the reverse)
- accept_authenticated_schc_packet still decompresses data with counter > the OLD floor under the old policy, even when a newer DIO admitted a stricter floor and different version

Python LinkLayer keeps one _schc_peer_contexts entry per signer and always looks that up (w0mm is the store-rollback dual). Std link.rs has no equivalent, so stale and current capabilities both work until unpin/rekey.

Fix: keep a per-signer latest DIO counter/version (PeerContextAuthority, FragmentationPolicy, or LinkLayer) and treat a context as current only when its authenticated_counter/generation is the live one. Reject superseded contexts as InvalidPeerEvidence. Do not use a capability whose remote_version no longer matches the latest admitted DIO.
acceptance_criteria: After two authenticated DIOs from the same signer on one LinkLayer (seqnum 10 then 20, same key generation), compress_schc_for_peer and accept_authenticated_schc_packet reject the seqnum-10 AuthenticatedPeerSchcContext with InvalidPeerEvidence. The seqnum-20 context still compresses/accepts. If the second DIO advertises an incompatible Rule Set Version, data is not decompressed with v3 compressed rules via the first context. FragmentationPolicy/PeerContextAuthority supersession behavior is unchanged. Regression covers same-version refresh vs version-changing DIO.
notes: 2026-08-26 Phase-2 fix: added bounded 32-entry AuthenticatedSchcPolicy owner for std link integration. compress_schc_for_peer and accept_authenticated_schc_packet now require the candidate context to match the registry's signer/counter/version/key-generation entry before output or policy use. DIO role is cryptographically parsed then retained in AuthenticatedPeerSchcContext, so callers cannot mislabel root vs peer. Same-signer refresh/version change supersedes older capabilities; <= counter and receipt-clock rollback reject; a different authenticated root becomes current while the old root high-water remains retained, preventing rollback when switching back. Regression encodes the prior seq10 context surviving seq20 failure mode and covers old/new acceptance+compression, same-version refresh, v3-to-incompatible fallback, root switch, rollback before/after switch, and output non-mutation. Existing 2tdl destination filtering preserved. Green: focused lifecycle test; full lichen-schc std suite (71 unit, all integrations/vectors/docs, 7 link integration); strict std all-target Clippy; no-default-features check; targeted rustfmt and diff checks. C/Zephyr audit found wire codecs and rule-version option parsing but no retained std peer-capability/free-function analog, so no west build was applicable. No Phase-3 review.
close_reason: Bound std SCHC compression/ingress to the latest authenticated signer/version/root policy with rollback-safe tests and green scoped gates.

title: handle_origin_validated_dao reconstructs option-252 EUI via U/L xor on 02xx origin
description:
File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs
Perspective: correctness / security

handle_origin_validated_dao() requires origin == ygg_addr_from_pubkey(pubkey) (02xx), then sets authenticated_eui64 = eui64_from_authenticated_origin(origin). That helper is NodeId::from_ipv6, which always does iid[0] ^= 0x02 (RFC 4291 inverse for link-local/ULA hardware EUI).

Consequences:
- Link-local origins, where that inverse actually recovers the hardware EUI-64 used by option 252 and short_addr_assignment.json (e.g. 0011223344556677), are rejected by the ygg_addr equality check.
- 02xx origins are accepted, but from_ipv6 then yields SHA-512(pubkey) IID with the U/L bit set. That value is neither the hardware EUI-64 in canonical assignment wires nor the pin-table IID used by DaoOriginValidator (origin[8..], U/L already cleared). Those 8-byte strings differ in bit 1 of byte 0 for every 02xx address.
- process() then fails closed with "assignment option EUI-64 does not match authenticated origin" for any DAO that carries the hardware EUI or the Announce IID. The only matching option EUI is the synthetic xor-ed hash, which the in-module test constructs on purpose.

This is not a refile of project-LICHEN-worker6-810t (missing origin binding). The binding exists and is the wrong identifier for 02xx. Fix: map authenticated origin/pubkey to the same EUI-64 option 252 uses (hardware NodeId from the pin/identity table, or the unmodified 02xx IID if that is the spec identity). Do not apply the RFC 4291 hardware inverse to a key-derived 02xx IID.
close_reason: Bound option-252 EUI derivation to the authenticated DAO public key and exact key-derived 02xx origin, then toggled the U/L bit once per the link profile. Removed handle_origin_validated_dao use of generic IPv6-to-NodeId inverse. Added non-native, raw-IID, mismatched-key, low-order substitution, and U/L-boundary regressions. Verified 207 lichen-rpl library tests, 13 address-assignment vector tests, Clippy with warnings denied, no-default-features check, and fmt.

title: PresenceResource local-admin rejects real UDP [::1]:port hostinfo
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/presence.py (_peer_is_local_admin, render_put)

The ixev write gate treats loopback as LCI admin. The helper only strips a port when hostinfo has exactly one colon (IPv4 host:port). IPv6 with a port is left intact, then strip("[]") turns "[::1]:54321" into "::1]:54321", which IPv6Address rejects, so the peer is untrusted.

aiocoap udp6 hostinfo is hostportjoin(plainaddress, sockaddr[1]) and omits the port only when it equals 5683. A loopback LCI client uses an ephemeral source port, so request.remote.hostinfo is "[::1]:<ephemeral>" on the real UDP path (bind_coap_udp defaults to ::1). LichenRemote.authority also emits "[host]:port" when the port is not 5683.

Impact:
- PUT /presence from a real loopback LCI client returns 4.01 unless allow_writes=True.
- Tests only use SimpleNamespace(hostinfo="[::1]") without a port, so they do not catch this.
- Fail-closed (not an auth bypass), but the documented LCI exception never matches production remotes.

Same parse mistake as open bead project-LICHEN-worker6-1v6y in messaging.py. confessions.py _host_from_hostinfo already parses bracketed IPv6 correctly. Do not refile 1v6y; this is the copy used by the presence write gate.
acceptance_criteria: PUT /presence from a loopback remote whose hostinfo is [::1]:<ephemeral> (and LichenRemote [::1]:non-5683) returns 2.04 without allow_writes. Mesh/global remotes still return 4.01. Tests cover the port-bearing IPv6 hostinfo form, not only [ ::1 ].
close_reason: Fixed strict aiocoap hostinfo parsing for bracketed IPv6 and IPv4 loopback peers with validated ports; added remote, scoped, malformed, and boundary regressions. Full CoAP suite, Ruff, and focused mypy are green.

title: rekey leaves removed admins on the admin roster
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_collection.py

spec/12-apps.md 18.8.2 Roles: Admins are always members. Removal by owner/admin plus rekey must drop the removed node from the authoritative roster.

rekey() (240-272) when removed_member is not the owner:
- filters item[\"members\"]
- pops item[\"invitations\"][removed_member]
- does not touch item[\"admins\"]

requester_role (378-389) checks owner, then admins, then members. A removed admin therefore still returns \"admin\".

Impact on this resource:
- _roster_view_authorized still treats them as affiliated
- GET /groups/{id} includes members/admins for that pairwise identity
- GET /groups/{id}/members returns 2.05 instead of 4.03

test_rekey_never_strips_owner covers owner only. test_rekey_on_member_removal uses a member, not an admin. join_key admin promotion (test_join_key_admin_invitation_promotes_admin) has no corresponding removal path.
acceptance_criteria: rekey(removed_member=X) where X is not the owner MUST drop X from members and admins and keep requester_role(X) is None. Owner is still never stripped. Tests: promote admin, rekey(removed_member=admin), admin pairwise GET /members is 4.03, admins list no longer contains them, owner remains a member.
close_reason: Rekey now atomically removes non-owner identities from current members, admins, and invitations while rotating keys; stale persisted admin-only entries fail closed. Rust parity preserves owners and removes admins. Added authorization, last-admin, entropy retry, concurrent epoch, persistence, and owner regressions; group/OSCORE tests, Ruff, focused mypy, Rust tests/clippy/package fmt passed.

title: POST /groups ignores creator identity and hands out group keys
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_collection.py

spec/12-apps.md 18.8.2 Group Creation: POST coap://[creator-node]/groups. Creator automatically becomes owner. Encrypted create returns master_secret only on that creation response.

_create (191-238):
- encrypted=True only checks _pairwise_oscore_identity(request) is not None
- unencrypted=True/default has no OSCORE check
- record[\"owner\"] and record[\"members\"] are always self.owner
- the authenticated peer is not recorded and is not compared to self.owner
- encrypted 2.01 still includes master_secret

test_encrypted_create_pairwise_oscore_returns_master_secret sets oscore_context_id to \"edhoc-pairwise\" while owner is \"0200::1111\" and still expects CREATED plus master_secret. test_groups_create_and_list POSTs unencrypted groups with no OSCORE from a mesh client.

Consequence: any EDHOC peer can mint an encrypted group attributed to this node and receive the group OSCORE master_secret without being a member. Any mesh peer can mint unencrypted groups under the victim owner identity (DoS/cap tracked separately as worker6-bfzz). a594 closed the plaintext-key case; this is the remaining creator-authorization hole.
acceptance_criteria: Encrypted POST /groups 2.01 only when the pairwise OSCORE identity is the collection owner (or a documented LCI principal). That identity becomes owner and is the only member at create. Any other pairwise peer gets 4.03 and no master_secret. Unencrypted POST is not mesh-open: same owner bind or 4.01. Tests: non-owner pairwise encrypted create has no key material and does not insert a group; owner pairwise still creates.
close_reason: POST /groups now requires one unambiguous live pairwise OSCORE identity matching the configured owner for encrypted and unencrypted creation. The authenticated creator is the sole initial member; non-owner, absent, spoofed, group, and conflicting contexts fail before mutation or key disclosure. Creation is serialized and entropy failures return 5.00 without state, permitting retry. Full group/OSCORE tests, Ruff, and focused mypy passed.

title: Group OSCORE roster auth is not bound to the group
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_collection.py

spec/12-apps.md 18.8.2 Membership Synchronization: GET /groups/{id}/members is OSCORE-protected with the group context for that group. Full membership is not broadcast.

_roster_view_authorized (410-415) returns True if _group_oscore_identity(request) is not None. _group_oscore_identity (73-85) returns the first bound value that _is_group_oscore_context accepts. That classifier (53-59) is only:
- value == \"group\", or
- external_aad_is_group, or
- is_signing

The returned identity is never compared to item[\"id\"], item[\"key_id\"], or an OSCORE id_context. Possessing any RFC 9203 group context (group A) authorizes GET /groups/{B} (full document with members/admins) and GET /groups/{B}/members.

Pairwise affiliation is correctly scoped via requester_role(item[\"id\"], peer). Group-mode is a boolean. test_groups_item.py group_ctx_request uses a generic _GroupOscoreContext and does not create a second group.

This is not worker6-yuvj (unprotected GET). Current code already gates on some group context; it does not gate on the right one.
acceptance_criteria: GET /groups/{id} roster fields and GET /groups/{id}/members MUST require a group OSCORE context for that group (id_context/key_id/group_id match) or a pairwise identity with requester_role for that id. A group context for group A against group B returns 4.03 with no members/admins. Tests cover two encrypted groups and a swapped group context.
close_reason: Roster disclosure now requires a live RFC 9203 context bound to the exact encrypted group and current key epoch via id_context, group_id plus key_epoch, or key_id; affiliated pairwise identities remain group-scoped. Cross-group, unbound, mixed, and stale contexts return 4.03 with no roster. Full group/OSCORE tests, Ruff, and focused mypy passed.

title: DeadDrop OSCORE identity ignores live security_context
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py
Perspective: correctness (security impact on POST gate and private ACL)

Spec 18.9: writes MUST be OSCORE-protected; rate limits and private/group ACL are per OSCORE context. _request_context_id() / _bound_oscore_identity() only accept request.oscore_context, request.oscore_context_id, and the same names on request.remote. Strings, non-empty bytes, or durable_context_id() count.

The live aiocoap stack does not set those attributes. After successful unprotect, request.remote is aiocoap.transports.oscore.OSCOREAddress(security_context, underlying_address). ConfessionsResource already reads recipient_id/kid on the context object.

Evidence:
- _request_context_id never reads remote.security_context or recipient_id (deaddrop.py ~59-98).
- python/tests/coap/test_deaddrop_resource.py _protected() sets request.oscore_context_id by hand. Stack tests only cover unprotected and spoofed option -> 4.01; there is no live unprotect POST that succeeds.
- lichen.crypto.oscore.MemorySecurityContext.durable_context_id() is _sender_context_id(), which hashes master_secret+salt+id_context+sender_id and omits recipient_id. If oscore_context were the live MemorySecurityContext, every pairwise peer would share one rate-limit and private-drop ACL.

This is not a refile of worker6-ex47 (spoofed option-as-auth, fixed). After that fix the gate still cannot see the identity the stack actually binds, so legitimate OSCORE POSTs return 4.01 oscore_required, and wiring durable_context_id() naively would collapse peers.

Impact:
- Python /deaddrop cannot accept real OSCORE writes on the live stack.
- Private/group ACL and 6/hour quota cannot be per-peer even if the attribute were later set to MemorySecurityContext.

Oracle: ConfessionsResource recipient_id/kid; aiocoap OSCOREAddress.security_context after unprotect.
acceptance_criteria: A request unprotected by the live stack (request.remote is aiocoap OSCOREAddress with security_context, or MemorySecurityContext) is accepted for POST, rate-limited per peer recipient_id, and used as the private/group ACL key. Two pairwise peers must not share a bucket. Spoofed opt.oscore still returns 4.01. Tests must drive a real post-unprotect remote, not only request.oscore_context_id.
close_reason: Bound DeadDrop authorization, private/group ACL, and per-peer quota state to the live post-unprotect remote.security_context recipient_id/KID, preferring authenticated peer identity over local sender/durable context IDs and failing closed when live peer identity is absent. Added live MemorySecurityContext regressions for peer role, durable-ID collision/per-peer buckets, reconstructed-context quota replay, spoof fallback, missing identity, and private ACL isolation. 140 focused DeadDrop/secure CoAP/OSCORE tests, Ruff lint/format, scoped strict mypy, and diff check pass.

title: Python coordinator RELEASE ignores DAOSequence
description: Dual-impl of project-LICHEN-worker6-m557. python/src/lichen/link/address_assignment.py ShortAddressCoordinator.process() uses _last_sequence_by_eui only on ALLOCATE. RELEASE deletes the live mapping with no RFC 6550 wrapping freshness check, so ALLOCATE seq=1, RELEASE seq=2, ALLOCATE seq=3, then retransmitted RELEASE seq=2 still drops the seq=3 assignment. Apply the same rule as rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs: same sequence = idempotent copy, newer = new request, older/incomparable = ignore before mutating. Keep last sequence after RELEASE so a later stale RELEASE cannot clobber a newer allocation. Tests should cover that scenario plus stale ALLOCATE not renewing a lease.
notes: Implemented Python RFC 6550 Section 7.2 DAOSequence freshness before allocation/release mutation. Same-sequence retries are idempotent only when operation matches current state; older/incomparable requests cannot release or renew. RELEASE retains/persists the last sequence using backward-compatible SAT3 state tombstones (SAT2/SAA1 remain readable), including release-on-unmapped updates, atomic save failure, restart, wrap/window and deterministic concurrency coverage. Rust state-machine freshness matches, but its SAT2 tombstone restart gap is already tracked by open project-LICHEN-worker6-emcr; no C/Zephyr short-address coordinator analogue was found (C lollipop helpers exist in RPL only). Gates: address-assignment 48 passed; full Python link 804 passed, 11 skipped; Ruff and mypy clean; git diff --check clean.
close_reason: Closed

title: MessagesStore POST stores caller map; from is spoofable
description:
File: rust/lichen-client/src/msg.rs (MessagesStore::post_inbox)

POST /msg/inbox keeps the decoded caller CBOR map (after canned expansion and id assign) as both the sent record and the inbox record. It does not build a server-authoritative receive document.

Spec 18.1.2 inbox items are {id, from, ts, body}. from is the sender identity. The Python oracle (python/src/lichen/coap/resources/messaging.py render_post) has a SECURITY comment and body.pop("from", None) so the client cannot spoof sender.

Rust never strips from, never stamps receiver time, and never allowlists keys. A mesh POST can:

1. Set from to an arbitrary IPv6 string (sender spoofing).
2. Set read to true so unread_count() (spec 18.1.2) skips the message.
3. Leak send-only keys (to, canned, ack, priority, text) into GET /msg/inbox.

Fix: strip or ignore untrusted keys; set from from the transport/peer, not the payload; persist only the spec receive fields (plus server id/ts). Match the Python from strip at minimum.

Perspectives: security, correctness.
close_reason: POST /msg/inbox strips payload from, rebinds from transport peer, and persists spec 18.1.2 receive fields only. Tests cover spoof, rebind, duplicate keys, read unread, send-key leak.

title: handle_dao trusts option EUI-64 with no origin or signer binding
description:
File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs
Perspective: security

handle_dao() parses AddressAssignmentRequest::from_dao_bytes() and process() keys the unique-address table on the EUI-64 carried inside option 252. There is no check against a DAO Origin Signature (spec/05-routing.md 8.6), a pinned Announce identity, the IPv6 source IID, or the link-layer signer SIID.

A mesh member that can emit a DAO can ALLOCATE or RELEASE for any other node's EUI-64: occupy their derived/preferred short address, or evict them with RELEASE. process() has no authenticated-identity parameter, so even a caller that verified origin has no API to bind the verified identity to the option EUI.

Client apply_dao_ack() likewise installs assigned_short from the option after only matching the claimed EUI and DAOSequence; it does not require a root-authenticated DAO-ACK.

Canonical vectors are unsigned, so this is the live mutating API as written, not a missing extra feature. Fix: reject assignment DAOs unless the option EUI-64 matches the authenticated origin/signer, and plumb that identity into handle_dao/process. rust/lichen-rpl/src/dao_origin.rs already exists for provenance.
close_reason: handle_dao/process now require authenticated origin EUI-64 and reject option-252 identity spoofing; apply_dao_ack requires root_authenticated. Tests green.

title: Confessions rate limit and sender keyed on spoofable SenML bn
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/confessions.py
Perspective: security (also robustness)

Spec 18.10.3 REQUIRED rate limit is 1 POST / 30s and 12 / hour per
node IID, to prevent spam. Rate limiting "uses per-node IID (not
OSCORE context)".

render_post gets source_iid from _extract_source_iid() (lines 62-69,
469-471): the SenML base name urn:dev:mac:<token>: is taken as the
node IID. There is no bind to CoAP source, OSCORE kid, or signature.
bn is attacker-controlled. The same token is stored as sender when
anonymous is false (lines 489, 530).

Evidence:
- 20 POSTs with distinct bn IIDs in one second all return 2.01
- anonymous=0 with bn of another node stores source=that IID and
  GET /confessions/{id} includes sender
- _request_times grows one list per spoofed IID and is only pruned
  when that key is seen again (_prune_old_requests)

Impact: the tightest LICHEN rate limit is honor-system; spam is
unlimited; the rate table is an unbounded RAM DoS; non-anonymous
posts impersonate any IID.

Acceptance: rate-limit key MUST be an authenticated identifier
(IPv6 source IID and/or OSCORE identity when present). Client
supplied sender/bn MUST NOT create a distinct quota bucket or a
displayed sender unless it matches that identity. Stale rate
buckets MUST be reaped without waiting for that key to return.
close_reason: Rate limits and displayed sender now key on authenticated IPv6 source IID (OSCORE identity if no IPv6). SenML bn/sender cannot mint quota or impersonate. Stale rate buckets reaped globally. Tests in test_confessions_resource.py and confessions_rate vector consumers pass.

title: DeadDrop after/expires use monotonic default clock
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py
Perspective: correctness

DeadDropResource.__init__ defaults time_func to time.monotonic().
Drop created timestamps, age_s, GET ?after, and SenML expires all
use that same clock.

Spec 18.9 GET query is ?after=17216... (unix). LCI 17.5.8 POST
example uses SenML n=expires as unix 1721736400. _extract_ttl does
remaining = expires - now. drops() filters
drop["created"] <= after.

With the default monotonic now (uptime seconds, ~1e6-1e7):
- unix after=1721650000 compares against created~uptime, so
  created <= after is true for every drop and the filter drops
  the whole collection
- unix expires - monotonic now is ~1.7e9 seconds, clamped to
  DEADDROP_MAX_TTL (7d) instead of remaining wall time
- expires in the past does not expire; _extract_ttl falls through
  to DEADDROP_DEFAULT_TTL (24h)

Tests pass because they inject _Clock() at unix-epoch values,
hiding the default-clock mismatch.

Acceptance: default construction honors unix after/expires as
specified; keep monotonic (or equivalent) only for the 6/hour
rate window.
close_reason: Default DeadDrop clock is unix time.time for created/age/after/expires (spec 18.9, LCI 17.5.8); monotonic only for the 6/hour rate window. ttl=0 past-expires prune immediately. Tests: TestDefaultClockUnixEpoch plus exact TTL boundary. 54 passed.

title: DeadDropResource does not speak RFC 8428 SenML+CBOR
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py
Perspective: correctness (security impact on privacy)

Spec 18.9 and get_link_description advertise Content-Format 112
(application/senml+cbor). RFC 8428 Table 4 uses integer labels
(0=n, 2=v, 3=vs, -2=bn, ...). lichen.senml.codec.pack() emits those
labels. ConfessionsResource correctly uses unpack().

DeadDrop POST uses _decode_single_cbor() plus _senml_text() /
_extract_ttl() which look up string keys "n", "vs", "v" on each
record. GET /deaddrop wraps metadata as string-key maps and labels
the body ct=112.

Evidence with pack() of privacy=private, ttl=3600, type=message:
- _senml_text(payload, "privacy") is None
- _extract_ttl returns 86400
- stored privacy is "public"
- unauthenticated GET lists the drop
- unpack() of the GET body returns SenmlRecord objects with all
  fields None (string labels without trailing _ are ignored)

Oracle tests hide this by cbor2.dumps()'ing Python dicts with
string keys, which is not RFC 8428 SenML+CBOR.

Impact: spec-compliant C/Rust/Python pack() peers cannot set TTL,
type, recipient, or privacy. "private"/"group" drops are stored
public (confidentiality failure). GET bodies are not SenML+CBOR
so cross-impl interop fails spec 18.9 "MUST produce identical
SenML output".

Acceptance: POST of lichen.senml.codec.pack() records honors ttl,
type, recipient, and privacy; private drops are omitted from public
GET and return 4.03 by id; GET collection unpack()s to records
with n/vs/v populated.
close_reason: DeadDrop POST/GET speak RFC 8428 integer-label SenML+CBOR via lichen.senml.codec (pack GET, SenmlRecord.from_cbor_map POST). pack() privacy/ttl/type/recipient honored; private omitted from public GET and 4.03 by id; collection GET unpacks with n/vs/v. Independent tests in test_deaddrop_resource.py (hand-built Table 4 maps + pack/unpack). 46 passed.

title: DeadDrop OSCORE POST gate treats option presence as auth
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py
Perspective: security (also correctness)

Spec 18.9: writes MUST be OSCORE-protected; unprotected POST returns 4.01
{"error":"oscore_required"}. DeadDropResource.render_post uses
_request_context_id() as that gate.

_request_context_id() (lines 57-71) reads request.oscore_context,
request.oscore_context_id, and request.oscore_protected. The live CoAP
stack never sets those attributes (only tests set oscore_context_id).
It then treats request.opt.oscore is not None as authenticated and
returns context id "default".

Evidence: POST with valid SenML and request.opt.oscore=b"\x00" (no
OSCORE unprotect) returns 2.01 Created and stores the drop under
"default". An empty OSCORE option also passes.

Impact:
- Unprotected clients satisfy the MUST-protect rule by attaching an
  OSCORE option to plaintext.
- All such writes share context "default", so they share the 6/hour
  bucket and can GET private/group drops stored under "default".
- Per-context rate limits and private-drop ACL cannot work on the
  live stack because real OSCORE identities are never bound.

Contrast: HandoffResource documents that object_security is set only
after successful unprotect.

Acceptance: unprotected POST with a spoofed OSCORE option still
returns 4.01; only a request that actually unprotected under a
distinct OSCORE context is allowed, rate-limited, and used as the
private/group ACL key.
close_reason: DeadDrop POST/GET OSCORE gate no longer treats opt.oscore or oscore_protected as auth. Only a non-empty identity bound after unprotect (request.oscore_context / oscore_context_id or the same on request.remote) is accepted as the rate-limit and private/group ACL key. Spoofed option (b'\x00' and empty), boolean flags, and empty ids return 4.01 oscore_required; tests in test_deaddrop_resource.py pass (42).

title: with_store freezes clock at 0 so persisted SAT2 leases never expire
description:
File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs
Perspective: correctness (dual-impl)

ShortAddressCoordinator::with_store() calls build(store, None, SHORT_POOL_SIZE, None, unix_zero). unix_zero always returns 0 and lease_seconds is None.

On load, decode_table_state() restores SAT2 expiries, then prune_expired() runs with now=0. Deadlines such as 160 are not <= 0, so expired rows stay in by_short/by_eui. Because lease_seconds is None, later process() never refreshes or honors those deadlines either.

Python ShortAddressCoordinator(store=store) defaults clock to time.time() and prunes persisted expiries on construct even when lease_seconds is None. Rust with_store is the obvious restart constructor and silently immortalizes leased assignments. Lease restart tests avoid this by using with_lease() plus an injected clock, so the divergence is untested.

Fix: with_store must take (or default to) a real clock and prune with current time; loading SAT2 with expiries must not depend on with_lease being used. Align with the Python constructor.
close_reason: with_store now prunes SAT2 expiries against unix_now (Python time.time default). unix_now fails closed on pre-epoch clocks instead of returning 0. Regression: canonical expiry 160 is kept by a frozen clock at 0 and dropped by with_store; cargo test -p lichen-rpl --features std --lib address_assignment:: (13 passed) and --test address_assignment_vectors (13 passed).

title: Coordinator RELEASE ignores DAOSequence; stale RELEASE drops a newer allocation
description:
File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs
Perspective: correctness

ShortAddressCoordinator::process() uses last_sequence_by_eui only on the ALLOCATE path. The RELEASE path (around the `AssignmentOperation::Release` branch) deletes the live mapping for request.eui64 with no check against the stored DAOSequence.

Consequence: ALLOCATE seq=1, RELEASE seq=2 (ACK lost or delayed), ALLOCATE seq=3 (new mapping installed), then a retransmitted RELEASE seq=2 still succeeds and removes the seq=3 assignment. The ALLOCATE path treats equal sequence as idempotent retransmission; RELEASE treats every sequence as authoritative.

A stale or replayed RELEASE is therefore destructive after re-acquisition. The same inequality test on ALLOCATE treats any sequence != last as a fresh request, so a stale ALLOCATE with a different sequence also renews the lease rather than being ignored as older.

Fix: apply RFC 6550 wrapping freshness (same sequence = idempotent copy, newer = new request, older = ignore) to both ALLOCATE and RELEASE before mutating the table. Dual-impl note: python/src/lichen/link/address_assignment.py has the same RELEASE gap; spec/vectors only require duplicate RELEASE of the current mapping to be idempotent, not clobbering a newer allocation.
close_reason: ShortAddressCoordinator::process now applies RFC 6550 Section 7.2 DAOSequence freshness to ALLOCATE and RELEASE before mutating. Same/older/incomparable sequences are ignored; last sequence is retained after RELEASE so a retransmitted RELEASE cannot drop a newer allocation. Tests cover the seq=1/2/3 replay, lease non-renewal, and 255->0 wrap. cargo test -p lichen-rpl --features std --lib address_assignment:: (12 passed) and --test address_assignment_vectors (11 passed).

title: to_ipv6 preserves scope_id so routing keys split
description:
## Problem

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py to_ipv6() returns IPv6Address as-is, including scope_id. make_link_local() and link_local_from_pubkey() now attach zone_id. Python treats these as unequal:

IPv6Address('fe80::1%eth0') != IPv6Address('fe80::1')

Both are used as OrderedDict keys in RouteCache, GradientTable, and RPL. Insert via a zoned link-local, lookup from a wire-derived unzoned address, miss.

## Why it matters

Zones are never on the wire (.packed omits them). After the zone_id work, the same 128-bit LCI/link-local can exist in zoned and unzoned form. Silent route miss, not an error.

## Where

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py:30-47 to_ipv6, 125-145 make_link_local
python/src/lichen/loadng/cache.py:73 _entries keyed by IPv6Address
python/src/lichen/gradient.py:118 same
design: Zone is local interface metadata (make_link_local docstring). Routing tables must key on the 128-bit address. Either strip scope in to_ipv6, or add an explicit packed-key helper and switch loadng/gradient/rpl to it. Do not drop zone from make_link_local return values used for local send.
acceptance_criteria: A zoned and unzoned form of the same 128-bit address must compare equal as routing keys, or to_ipv6/docs must stop being used as a dict key without packing. Add a test that lookup(fe80::1) finds an entry inserted as fe80::1%lci0 (or the chosen canonical form). Wire packed bytes still round-trip.
close_reason: routing_key canonicalizes on packed 128-bit bytes so fe80::1 and fe80::1%zone share RouteCache/GradientTable/RPL keys; to_ipv6 still preserves scope_id for local send; independent packed-oracle tests pass

title: to_ipv6 maps bool to loopback (::1/::)
description:
## Problem

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py to_ipv6() is the routing-table canonicalizer (loadng RouteCache, GradientTable, RPL paths, gateway handoff). It documents AddrError for any invalid input and accepts only IPv6Address, str, or 16 packed bytes.

Because ipaddress.IPv6Address treats bool as int:
- to_ipv6(True) -> ::1 (loopback)
- to_ipv6(False) -> ::

Verified with the stdlib constructor. Sibling helpers in the same file already reject bool via type(x) is int (unicast_prefix_based_mcast group_id, _normalize_zone_id).

## Why it matters

A JSON/CBOR boolean in an address field does not fail closed. Traffic or a route cache entry is bound to loopback instead of being rejected. That is silent misdelivery at a system boundary.

## Where

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py:30-47 (to_ipv6)
Callers: python/src/lichen/loadng/cache.py, python/src/lichen/gradient.py, python/src/lichen/rpl/routing.py, python/src/lichen/gateway/handoff.py
design: Reject bool explicitly (bool is an int subclass). Do not accept arbitrary ints unless the documented contract is expanded; the current docstring allows only IPv6Address, str, and 16-byte packed data.
acceptance_criteria: to_ipv6(True) and to_ipv6(False) raise AddrError. to_ipv6 still accepts IPv6Address, str, and 16-byte packed values. Tests cover the bool rejection without weakening existing vector checks. loadng/gradient/rpl call sites keep using to_ipv6 as the coercer.
close_reason: to_ipv6 rejects bool/int (stdlib maps True/False to ::1/::). Tests cover bool rejection plus documented IPv6Address/str/packed-bytes forms. loadng/gradient/rpl still coerce via to_ipv6.

title: inbox POST drops from, never rebinds peer
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/messaging.py

Correctness/security: render_post (lines 201-203) pops client-supplied 'from' (anti-spoof) but never writes sender identity from request.remote. The comment claims the transport layer sets sender identity; nothing in this module does.

Spec 18.1.1 requires from as sender IPv6. Stored inbox/sent maps therefore omit from. GET /msg/inbox and Observe notifications cannot attribute the sender. python/tests/coap/test_messages_resource.py::TestMessagesObserve.test_observe_notified_on_post asserts inbox[0]['from'] == _TO_A after POSTing _MSG2, which is inconsistent with the strip-and-forget path.

Confirmed: POST {from, to, body} yields inbox [{to, body, id}] with from absent.
acceptance_criteria: After POST /msg/inbox, stored inbox and sent records have from bound to the request peer identity (not the payload). Client-supplied from is still ignored. GET/Observe include that bound from. A unit test covers strip-plus-rebind without using the resource as its own oracle.
close_reason: render_post (messaging.py:249-252) strips client-supplied 'from' and rebinds it to request.remote.hostinfo, matching the request.remote.hostinfo peer-binding convention used by provisioning.py/edhoc.py/senml.py. Stored inbox (_inbox), sent (_sent) and detail records all carry the bound identity; GET /msg/inbox, GET /msg/sent, GET /msg/sent/{id} and Observe notifications expose it. Old test_observe_notified_on_post asserting inbox[0]['from'] == _TO_A encoded the bug (payload-trusted attribution); corrected to exact equality against the server-side constructed peer authority. Added strip-plus-rebind tests: full-transport rebind of _MSG2 spoofed 'from' to known peer '[::1]' across inbox/sent/detail/observe, plus render-level test proving OSCORE-bound non-loopback peer overrides payload spoof. 116 passed tests/coap/test_messages_resource.py; 141 passed broader -k messages subset (2 collection errors are pre-existing local missing optional deps jsonschema/defusedxml). ruff check+format clean.

title: msg POST lacks OSCORE-or-admin gate
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/messaging.py

Correctness/security: MessagesResource.render_post (line 191, mounted at /msg/inbox), LegacyMessagesAliasResource.render_post (line 400, /messages), and MessageReceiptsResource.render_post (line 344, /msg/ack) accept unauthenticated POSTs.

Impact: any CoAP peer can inject inbox and sent records, fire Observe, spoof /msg/ack receipts, persist read=True to hide from unread_count, and POST id=2^64-1 to pin _next_id and fail-close auto-id (5.03) for the process lifetime.

SentMessagesResource.render_post (line 277) is the only path that checks _peer_is_local_admin; inbox and ack do not.

Loopback and OSCORE-protected peers still succeed per coap_lci_auth.json. Match firmware: oscore.is_protected || is_local_admin.

title: PUT /presence has no local-admin or write gate
description:
Spec 18.5.2 treats PUT coap://[node]/presence as set-own-presence. Peer operations are GET/Observe. PresenceResource.render_put accepts any CoAP client with a valid CBOR map.

Impact:
- A mesh peer can overwrite another node's advertised status, msg, battery, and ts.
- A peer can PUT status=emergency without the SOS origin-signature path (spec 18.4.1).
- Observe subscribers are then fed attacker-chosen presence documents (amplification / false emergency).

Sibling resources already gate writes: ConfigResource defaults allow_writes=False (4.01), SentMessagesResource requires _peer_is_local_admin.

File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/presence.py render_put

This is not LCI access.py (out of scope); the resource itself needs a write gate (local-admin, allow_writes, or equivalent OSCORE-bound check).
acceptance_criteria: Unauthenticated/non-local PUT returns 4.01. Local-admin or explicitly enabled writes still return 2.04. GET/Observe from peers remain allowed.
close_reason: PUT /presence now rejects unauthenticated writes with 4.01 unless allow_writes=True or local-admin loopback; GET/Observe remain public. Tests cover both gates.

title: accept_authenticated_schc_packet ignores DIO admission counter floor
description:
File: rust/lichen-schc/src/link.rs

Python LinkLayer.accept_authenticated_schc_packet rejects ingress when logical_counter(epoch, seqnum) <= the DIO issuance admitted_counter (test_peer_policy_gates_unfragmented_ingress_and_egress, match 'predates'). AuthenticatedFragmentReceiver::receive_frame in this crate already rejects counter <= admission_floor.

accept_authenticated_schc_packet never compares the data frame counter to peer.authenticated_counter(). Link replay can still accept an in-window older seqnum that was not yet seen (DIO at N, delayed data at N-k). That packet is then decompressed under the newer peer SCHC policy.

Compute the frame counter the same way fragment.rs does ((epoch as u32) << 16) | seqnum and reject when counter <= peer.authenticated_counter() as InvalidPeerEvidence / invalid packet, matching Python.
acceptance_criteria: A replay-accepted SCHC data frame whose logical counter is less than or equal to the peer DIO authenticated_counter is rejected. A frame with a strictly greater counter still decompresses. Behavior matches Python predates-policy rejection and the fragment receiver admission floor. Test covers seqnum == floor and seqnum == floor+1 on the same admitted peer context.
close_reason: Reject unfragmented SCHC data when logical counter <= DIO authenticated_counter. Test covers seqnum == floor, in-window floor-1, and floor+1. cargo test -p lichen-schc --features std --test link_layer_integration 5 passed.

title: accept_authenticated_schc_packet does not bind peer context to receiving link
description:
File: rust/lichen-schc/src/link.rs

accept_authenticated_schc_packet admits SCHC data if link.accepts_authenticated_frame(data_frame) and data_frame.sender pubkey equals peer.signer_identity(). Decompress then only checks retained DIO evidence is_current() (retirement flags).

It does not call peer.is_current_for(link). That check is what compress_schc_for_peer uses, and it is the full live binding: same receiving LinkLayer instance, peer still in the table, matching key-generation Arc, still pinned.

Without it, a caller can decode on link B using a DIO-issued AuthenticatedPeerSchcContext from link A, or keep using a context after the peer is unpinned/removed as long as the retirement atomics are still live. Python stores peer contexts on the LinkLayer and cannot do this. FragmentSender::new / policy.accepts_current already fail closed on the same binding.

Fix: require peer.is_current_for(link) (and signer match against the live evidence) before decompress, matching compress_schc_for_peer.
acceptance_criteria: accept_authenticated_schc_packet returns InvalidPeerEvidence when the peer context was issued for a different LinkLayer instance, when the peer is no longer pinned or present, or when the DIO evidence is otherwise not accepted by the receiving link. compress_schc_for_peer and unfragmented accept use the same is_current_for gate. Regression test covers foreign-link and unpinned-peer contexts.
close_reason: accept_authenticated_schc_packet now requires peer.is_current_for(link) and live-evidence signer match before decompress, matching compress_schc_for_peer. Regression covers foreign-link and unpinned-peer contexts. cargo test -p lichen-schc --features std --test link_layer_integration 4 passed.

title: PUT /presence skips spec 18.5.3 automatic status
description:
PresenceResource.render_put stores the client document and only updates _last_interaction_at. It never calls _apply_auto, unlike note_gps/note_sos/note_battery/tick.

Consequences:
- While _sos_active is True, PUT can replace emergency with busy/available/offline. GET and Observe then advertise a non-emergency status until the next tick. Spec 18.5.3 says SOS active -> emergency.
- PUT with battery < 10 can omit low_battery. Spec 18.5.3 says add the flag when battery < 10%.
- note_sos(False) restores _pre_sos from SOS start, discarding any PUT that happened during SOS.

Files:
- python/src/lichen/coap/resources/presence.py render_put (approx lines 149-174)
- python/src/lichen/presence.py apply_automatic_status

Fix: after validating the PUT body, run the same automatic-status pass used by note_* (at least SOS and low_battery) before notifying observers.
acceptance_criteria: PUT cannot clear emergency while note_sos(True) is in effect. PUT with battery 9 yields low_battery true without waiting for tick. Tests cover SOS-active PUT and low-battery PUT.
close_reason: PUT /presence now runs apply_automatic_status after validation: SOS-active PUT cannot clear emergency, battery 9 sets low_battery without tick, PUT during SOS is restored on SOS clear. Tests in test_presence_resource.py.

title: rekey drops old keys so grace period is inert
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_collection.py

GroupsCollectionResource.rekey (150-170) and epoch_accepted (172-183).

spec/12-apps.md 18.8.2 Rekeying: increment key_epoch, distribute the new key, and reject the old key_epoch only after a 1 hour grace (REKEY_GRACE_S=3600). That requires keeping the retired master_secret/master_salt until grace expiry so old-epoch OSCORE can still be unwrapped.

rekey() overwrites item['master_secret'] and item['master_salt'] immediately. retired_epochs stores only {key_epoch, expires}, not the retired key material. epoch_accepted() can return True for the old epoch during grace, but join_key/GET /key can only return the new secret, and nothing can decrypt old-epoch traffic.

Also: if removed_member equals item['owner'], rekey() strips the owner from members. Spec 18.8.2: Owner is always a member.
acceptance_criteria: rekey() MUST retain retired (master_secret, master_salt, key_id, key_epoch) until expires. epoch_accepted True implies the retired key is still available for unprotect. After grace, retired material is dropped. rekey() MUST NOT remove the owner from members.
close_reason: rekey() now retains full retired key material (master_secret/master_salt/key_id/key_epoch) until REKEY_GRACE_S via _live_retired pruning; group_key_for_epoch() exposes unprotect-capable material; owner never stripped from members; removed member's invitation revoked. Verified by test_groups_rekey.py (grace retention/drop, vector-driven epoch acceptance, owner invariant).

title: Unauthenticated GET leaks group membership lists
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_collection.py

spec/12-apps.md 18.8.2 Membership Synchronization: Full membership list is NOT broadcast (privacy). Authoritative GET /groups/{id}/members is specified with OSCORE group context.

Current behavior:
- public_group_document (53-67) includes owner, admins, and members
- GroupsItemResource.render_get len==1 (204-210) returns that document to any client
- render_get len==2 rest[1]==members (222-232) returns the same lists with no OSCORE check

Anyone who can CoAP GET the node learns the full member and admin sets. GET /groups listing also exposes names and member counts (89-99) with no access control; that is weaker but still a roster oracle when combined with item GET.
acceptance_criteria: GET /groups/{id}/members requires OSCORE group (or pairwise owner/admin) context; unprotected GET returns 4.01/4.03. GET /groups/{id} MUST NOT include the full members/admins arrays unless the requester is authorized per 18.8.2.
close_reason: public_group_document no longer carries admins/members; item GET serves roster arrays only to authorized viewers (group OSCORE context or roster-affiliated pairwise peer); GET /groups/{id}/members requires OSCORE - bare request 4.01, authenticated-but-unaffiliated 4.03. /groups listing keeps the spec 18.8.4 member-count shape. Tests extended accordingly.

title: Group PUT/DELETE/join_key skip owner/admin roles
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_collection.py

spec/12-apps.md 18.8.2 Roles:
- Owner: delete group, invite/remove anyone
- Admin: invite/remove members (not owner/admins)
- Member: send/receive, view membership

The handlers ignore the requester:
- GroupsItemResource.render_put (235-257) lets any client rename any group
- GroupsItemResource.render_delete (259-266) lets any client drop the group record
- GroupsItemResource._join_key (288-293) appends body['node'] to members with no invitation check and no bind of 'node' to the CoAP/OSCORE peer

Unlike deaddrop.py and handoff.py, this resource never inspects OSCORE context or peer identity. join_key is therefore open enrollment plus key fetch. DELETE on the owner node destroys the authoritative group, not a local leave.
acceptance_criteria: Mutating /groups/{id} and /groups/{id}/key MUST authenticate the requester (pairwise OSCORE) and enforce the 18.8.2 role table. join_key MUST require a prior valid invitation and MUST bind body.node to the authenticated peer. Unauthorized PUT/DELETE/join_key return 4.01 or 4.03.
close_reason: PUT/DELETE require pairwise OSCORE and owner role (admin/member -> 4.03, plaintext -> 4.01). join_key requires pairwise OSCORE, a live invitation, and body.node bound to the peer; admin invitations promote to admins. pytest groups item/roles/rekey/collection 43 passed.

title: Reject unauthenticated generation-ahead key and DAO slots
description: SECURITY review: FileKeyStore._best_slot_locked and TwoSlotFilePersistence._validate_anchored_slot automatically advance the trusted external anchor when the selected attacker-writable slot is exactly anchor+1. Slot checksums are unkeyed, so an offline/local storage attacker can forge a valid generation-ahead seed or arbitrary DAO TX/RX floor and have load authenticate it into the independent anchor. Two-slot storage retains the anchor-matching committed slot; loads must select the slot exactly matching the external anchor and ignore/reject unanchored newer slots rather than advancing trust from file contents. Add forged +1 restart tests for key, DAO TX, and DAO RX.
close_reason: Verified: FileKeyStore._best_slot_locked and TwoSlotFilePersistence._get_anchored_slot require exact external-anchor match (no anchor+1 trust advancement); forged+1 restart tests present for key (test_unanchored_generation_ahead_seed_is_ignored_and_overwritten), DAO TX and DAO RX. 200/200 tests pass.

title: Detect complete deletion of authenticated DAO TX state
description: python/src/lichen/rpl/dao_persistence.py uses .dao_tx_initialized to detect slot deletion, but the marker lives beside the slots and is itself unauthenticated/unanchored. Deleting both dao_tx slots and the marker makes load_tx_state return None as if first boot; DaoManager with allow_tx_bootstrap=True can then reuse Origin Sequence 1 for the same key, contrary spec/05-routing.md lines 249-257. Store the initialized/high-water fact in an independent monotonic anchor or provisioned per-key floor that cannot disappear with the slots, and add a restart test deleting marker plus both slots.
close_reason: Verified implemented: code and bead-mandated adversarial tests present and passing (test_key_persistence.py, test_dao_persistence.py, test_trust.py: 200/200).

title: Make FileKeyStore identity state rollback-resistant
description: python/src/lichen/crypto/key_persistence.py FileKeyStore accepts rollback and ambiguous identity state. After a successful store, deleting both node_seed slots makes load_seed return None even with fail_closed=True, so callers can bootstrap a different node identity. Corrupting/deleting only the newest slot silently restores the older seed, and two valid equal-generation slots with different seeds silently select slot 0. The unanchored u32 generation/checksum cannot distinguish first boot, interrupted write, deletion, stale restore, or divergent slots. Add durable initialization plus an independent monotonic/authenticated rollback anchor (or an equivalent provisioned floor), reject complete deletion and stale restoration after initialization, reject equal-generation divergence, validate fail_closed as an exact bool, and add adversarial deletion/latest-slot/equal-generation/restart tests.
close_reason: Verified implemented: code and bead-mandated adversarial tests present and passing (test_key_persistence.py, test_dao_persistence.py, test_trust.py: 200/200).

title: Authenticate and anchor persisted TrustStore snapshots
description: python/src/lichen/crypto/key_persistence.py TrustStorePersistence calls itself tamper/fail-closed storage but trust_store.json contains only attacker-recomputable JSON and an in-file revision. Deleting the file returns None; restoring any older valid snapshot is accepted on restart; and a locally writable forged snapshot can choose arbitrary derived keys, trust levels, revocation flags, and rotation floors. This can erase TOFU pins/revocations or replay an old key-rotation authorization. Pair the snapshot with a local authentication key and independent monotonic revision/deletion anchor, fail closed after initialized-state deletion or rollback, bind all policy fields, and test deletion, byte-valid forgery, and old-snapshot restoration.
close_reason: Verified implemented: code and bead-mandated adversarial tests present and passing (test_key_persistence.py, test_dao_persistence.py, test_trust.py: 200/200).

title: Durably commit every persistent TrustStore security mutation
description: python/src/lichen/crypto/trust.py accepts a persistence backend but verify_or_pin, add_trust_anchor, revoke, and remove mutate memory and return success without saving; only rotate_key performs a transactional persistence commit. A crash after a first TOFU pin, anchor upgrade, or revocation therefore reopens first-contact trust or resurrects a revoked key, while the API has already reported success. When persistence is configured, make each security transition commit before exposure with full in-memory rollback on any BaseException; retain clearly named unsafe test-only in-memory helpers if needed. Add crash/failing-backend/CAS tests for every mutator.
close_reason: Verified implemented: code and bead-mandated adversarial tests present and passing (test_key_persistence.py, test_dao_persistence.py, test_trust.py: 200/200).

title: Make per-origin DAO RX replay floors deletion-resistant
description: python/src/lichen/rpl/dao_persistence.py load_rx_floor treats absence of both per-key slot files as a normal first DAO even after a floor was committed. Deleting both dao_rx_<pubkey> slots therefore resets that pinned key replay floor and permits an old signed DAO to be accepted as fresh, violating spec/05-routing.md lines 259-266 that missing receive state fails closed. Persist an authenticated/anchored catalog or per-key initialization floor tied to the Announce pin so previously initialized keys cannot become unseen through deletion or stale restore; test full deletion and rollback of both slots across root restart.
close_reason: FIXED: anchored RX floor catalog in TwoSlotFilePersistence (dao_rx_catalog.bin, checksummed, atomically written, anchored via StateRevisionAnchor). load_rx_floor fails closed when catalog records an initialized key but slot files are missing, rejects slots below/diverging from catalog high-water, heals catalog forward over slot-commit crash windows. 12 new tests (8 fail on pre-fix code); 91/91 dao_persistence, 1478 rpl+vectors pass; ruff+mypy strict clean. Files: python/src/lichen/rpl/dao_persistence.py, python/tests/rpl/test_dao_persistence.py (uncommitted per task constraints)

title: Restrict SCHC control-wire issuance to authenticated transitions
description: python/src/lichen/schc/fragment.py exposes SchcSessionManager.issue_control_wire as a generic authority mint. Any caller holding the manager can supply arbitrary canonical ACK, ACK-REQ, Sender-Abort, or Receiver-Abort bytes plus any 32-byte peer and object; the method does not prove an authenticated reassembly/sender transition or validate key_generation against current peer state. consume_fragment_wire then accepts the manager-issued token and does not inspect the stored key_generation, bypassing the intended one-use target-bound transition policy. Remove/restrict the generic issuer and issue controls only atomically inside receipt-bound reassembly or active-sender transitions; validate current generation at consume; add forged-direct-issuance tests for unknown/stale peers and every control form.
close_reason: Fixed: consume_fragment_wire now requires looked-up key_generation current AND non-None (closed None-is-None vacuity); _issue_control_wire_unlocked rejects None at mint (fail-closed). 33 new forged-issuance tests across all 5 control forms x unknown/stale peers. 1181 schc tests pass. Follow-up filed as worker6-sppu.

title: Trust rotation can commit on disk while reporting failure and rolling memory back
description: CORRECTNESS: TrustStore.rotate_key mutates the in-memory snapshot, calls TrustStorePersistence.save, and on any exception restores the old in-memory entry/revision. But TrustStorePersistence._write_json_locked performs os.replace before chmod and directory fsync. If either post-replace operation raises, save reports failure even though trust_store.json already contains the rotated key and advanced revision. rotate_key then restores old memory, so runtime and durable trust disagree; restart accepts a rotation the caller was told failed, and subsequent saves fail stale-revision CAS. Treat the post-replace state as an indeterminate/terminal persistence transition or redesign commit/reconciliation so an exception cannot produce a durable new snapshot with old live memory. Add injected chmod/directory-fsync failure tests around public rotation.
close_reason: Fix verified: indeterminate/terminal post-replace transition already committed in 95d85c3747 (_write_json_locked replaced-flag, TrustStorePersistenceIndeterminateError, save() revision/terminal handling, _commit_security_mutation durable_state_may_have_advanced honoring). Audit traced all paths: pre-replace failures roll back memory with disk untouched; post-replace chmod/open/fsync and post-write anchor failures keep memory==disk and poison the backend as terminal, so stale-CAS divergence is impossible. Added missing tests in python/tests/crypto/test_key_persistence.py: test_rotation_after_indeterminate_failure_is_terminal_not_stale (chmod+directory_fsync parametrized; subsequent rotate raises terminal TrustError not stale-CAS; memory/disk stay in agreement) and test_pre_replace_rotation_failure_keeps_disk_and_memory_old (os.replace injection; disk old + memory old; no staging leftovers; retry succeeds durably). Mutation-checked: reverting _commit_security_mutation to unconditional rollback makes all post-replace tests fail, so they bite. 124 passed in test_key_persistence.py + test_trust.py; ruff clean.

title: Make fresh simulator identity consistent with advertised node ID
description: rust/lichen-gateway/src/bin/lichend.rs creates a new random identity seed in a fresh ephemeral simulator state root, but Args::node_id defaults to fixed 0200000000000001 and startup aborts when the derived IID differs. Because the seed is created internally after argument parsing and discarded with the temp root, a normal fresh --sim invocation cannot know or reuse the required IID; the default invocation fails deterministically except with negligible random coincidence. Derive the simulator node ID from its generated identity by default, or expose deterministic seed/identity provisioning while preserving validation for explicitly supplied IDs.
close_reason: Verified fixed in commit 95d85c3747: Args::node_id is Option<String> (no fixed default), resolve_node_id(None, id.iid) derives advertised node ID from generated/persisted identity, explicit IDs still validated against identity IID. Unit test implicit_node_id_tracks_generated_identity_but_explicit_id_is_validated passes (9/9 lichend bin tests). Smoke run: default --sim --no-tun starts with derived IID and no abort; explicit mismatched --node-id aborts with 'configured root IID does not match persisted identity' (exit 1). No code changes required.

title: Allow authenticated propagation of newer DODAG versions across multiple hops
description: rust/lichen-node/src/routing/router.rs and rust/lichen-rpl/src/dodag.rs classify a DIO as root-authorized only when the immediate link signer derives to the DODAGID, then reject any version change from a peer. RPL DIOs are re-originated/relayed by non-root parents, so nodes more than one hop from the root can never adopt a root-triggered DODAGVersionNumber increment and global repair partitions the mesh. Add a separately verifiable root-owned version authorization that peers can propagate (or another spec-defined authenticated mechanism) while retaining rejection of unauthorized peer version changes.
close_reason: Root-signed DODAG version authorization (option 0x16, Schnorr48 over LICHEN-RPL-DODAG-VERSION-v1 transcript) verified and propagated by non-root parents; lollipop floor rejects stale/replayed authorizations. Added negative tests (garbage sig, non-root key, mismatch, duplicate, truncated, stale version, idempotent replay) using canonical vectors from test/vectors/dodag_version_authorization.json; fixed dao_parents_for_source transit-group flush regression and runtime.rs Ipv6Addr compile break. cargo test -p lichen-rpl (233/233 lib + 54 integration) and lichen-node (266/267 lib, sole failure pre-existing secure.rs blockwise owned elsewhere) pass; clippy/fmt clean.

title: Align Rust gateway key rotation with canonical replay-safe transcript
description: rust/lichen-gateway/src/trust.rs still signs and verifies legacy KEY_ROTATE: || new_pubkey messages. The canonical protocol requires LICHEN-KEY-ROTATION-v1 || 0x00 || old_pubkey || old_key_derived_iid || new_pubkey || rotation_sequence_be64, with a strictly increasing nonzero persisted rotation sequence. PinnedGateway and persistence currently carry no rotation sequence, so a previously valid rotation authorization can be replayed and Rust is not interoperable with the current spec/Python implementation. Update the API, transcript, durable state, and canonical vectors/tests together.
close_reason: Verified prior transcript/sequence work against Python oracle; closed remaining parity gaps: IID now derived internally in rotation transcript (spec 8.7), same-key rotation rejected (UnchangedRotationKey), v1->v2 migration test added. 43 trust tests pass; full gateway suite green except pre-existing bead-owned tunnel_auth failure.

title: Reject incomplete or concurrently changed atomic recovery reads
description: P1 robustness review: atomic JSON backup/journal/artifact readers issue one os.read but do not require the returned length to equal the fstat snapshot. A short read can publish a truncated rollback backup, while concurrent same-bound growth/shrink can make recovery operate on a non-snapshot. Require exact stable lengths (with max+1 growth detection) and add failure-injection tests.
close_reason: Fixed: announce/persistence.py _read_state now requires len(raw)==fstat snapshot AND post-read re-fstat unchanged. 4 failure-injection tests (short read, growth, growth-past-cap, shrink). 236 announce tests pass. Same-pattern in key_persistence/dao_persistence slots is mitigated downstream by checksum/HMAC+anchor validation and tracked for review.

title: Gateway default TUN route still narrows native profile to 0202::/16
description: rust/lichen-gateway/src/config.rs documents the exact canonical 0200::/8 native profile, and Gateway::is_local_mesh recognizes all 0x02 addresses, but default_ipv6_prefix() and Config::default_sim() still return 0202::/16. lichend passes this prefix directly to tun::configure, so a default deployment installs only a /16 route and fails to deliver the other 255/256 of valid key-derived native addresses. Change both defaults to 0200::/8 and add configuration/routing regression coverage.
close_reason: Verified: default_ipv6_prefix() and Config::default_sim() already return 0200::/8; no 0202 remains in the crate; tun::configure passes prefix through. Added missing regression coverage: byte-exact /8 prefix assertions and is_local_mesh 0201::1 acceptance test. Targeted tests pass. Test-strength follow-up filed (pre-state assertion).

title: Reject exhausted handoff sequences instead of saturating and reusing them
description: NodeRegistry::accept_handoff advances dao_sequence, path_sequence, and OSCORE sender_sequence with saturating_add(1). At the integer maximum this leaves the value unchanged, violating the documented mandatory increment and permitting DAO/path replay or OSCORE nonce reuse after transfer. Validate all transferred sequence counters before mutation and fail the handoff on exhaustion; add boundary tests proving MAX is rejected and MAX-1 advances exactly once.
close_reason: Verified: accept_handoff already validates via checked_add into locals before any mutation; exhaustion returns Err(SequenceExhausted) leaving registry untouched. Added the two mandated boundary tests: MAX rejected without mutation (all 3 counters), MAX-1 advances exactly once. handoff_vectors 17/17 pass.

title: Persist GCP slot semantic state atomically with replay high-water
description: GatewayCoordinator::handle_post_slots durably advances SlotClaimVerifier replay state, but peer_claims and the locally reallocated info.slot_map.owned are memory-only. After restart, the gateway retains a high-water that rejects the same authenticated claim while forgetting the accepted peer ownership and any slots it relinquished, recreating collisions until a peer emits a higher sequence. Persistence errors can similarly consume a claim without committing semantic state. Store replay high-water, peer claims, and local allocation as one restart-safe transaction, and test accepted/lost claims across restart and injected write failures.
close_reason: Fixed: we-win conflict branch upserts the verified peer claim into candidate_peer_claims before commit, so replay high-water + peer claims + owned move as one restart-safe transaction (validate_semantic_slot_state would otherwise CorruptState-lockout the peer). Test-first: new test fails pre-fix (0xa0), passes post-fix (0x45); existing tests cover restart survival and write-failure-does-not-consume-claim. Pre-existing floor-temp wedge filed separately.
