title: Detect deleted authenticated DAO TX slots after bootstrap
description: P1 security/correctness review: explicit allow_tx_bootstrap authorizes a fresh authenticated origin, but TwoSlotFilePersistence retains no durable initialization marker. If both TX slots are later deleted and bootstrap remains configured, the store is indistinguishable from first use and can reuse Origin Sequence 1. Persist and validate a durable TX-initialized marker so slot deletion fails closed, including when bootstrap authorization is still true.
close_reason: TX slot deletion now fails closed via the durable TX-initialization marker. store_tx_state captures marker_existed before _ensure_tx_marker and passes it into _write_to_older_slot(_locked) as initialized_marker; when a pre-existing marker coincides with no recoverable anchored slot state, the store raises 'initialized TX state was deleted' — bootstrap authorization does not override durable evidence of prior initialization, so Origin Sequence 1 cannot be reused. load_tx_state now raises unconditionally (independent of legacy fail_closed) when the marker exists: absent slot files report deletion, invalid slot files report 'TX state corrupt'. Mirrors the RX catalog pattern (durable in-dir evidence surviving a stateless anchor record). Documented in the class docstring (TX initialization marker section). New tests: deleted slots fail closed while bootstrap authorized (load + store of seq 1 and seq 8), corrupt slots + marker fail closed, entire-store wipe boundary returns to authorized bootstrap, lost marker with intact anchored store self-heals. The two hole-tests verified to fail against the old code via temporary revert.

title: Preserve Announce reconciliation after post-commit peer admission failure
description: P1 correctness review: Node._process_announce removes the gradient when add_peer fails after AnnounceProcessor has durably committed the replay floor, but the processor has already cleared its one-shot equal-sequence reconciliation permit. A retry or restart can therefore reject the exact authenticated Announce while no route/peer state exists. Restore a bounded reconciliation permit on post-commit admission failure and cover retry behavior.
close_reason: Verified: restore is implemented at node.py:1296 (_restore_reconciliation_permit, validates seen/pinned then re-adds exactly one permit; set semantics bound it at 1/IID). Added python/tests/test_node.py test pinning restore after post-commit add_peer failure, boundedness across two failures, successful retry re-admission + permit consumption, and final equal-sequence fail-closed. 363 tests pass.

title: First-boot slot recovery can anchor noninitial replay state at floor one
description: Security review of so3l/0919 integration: before manifest SLOT commit, if gateway-slot-replay.bin exists without its external floor, lichend writes floor=1 and loads any valid store. A noninitial generation>1 store is therefore accepted against floor1; after a failed attempt both files remain and are also accepted on retry. Legitimate first-boot partial can only be generation 1 with no claims. After loading any stage<SLOT recovery, require slot_replay_generation()==1 (and empty verifier state if exposed) before committing the manifest; reject higher generations and test retry with both files present.
close_reason: Fixed: recover_or_provision_slot_replay gates on initial_resume_state_is_valid (stage<SLOT reduces to generation==1) BEFORE save_provision_manifest; retry-with-both-files test proves rejection on both attempts with manifest never committed. Forged sealed stores rejected by Schnorr48 seal + local_iid binding. Review follow-ups filed (pre-gate floor write, emptiness check).

title: Let lichend failure paths drop secrets and ephemeral state
description: Security/robustness review finding in rust/lichen-gateway/src/bin/lichend.rs: main calls process::exit after allocating Zeroizing secrets and EphemeralStateRoot guards. process::exit skips destructors, so failure paths do not wipe secret buffers and leave simulator credential directories behind. Return ExitCode::FAILURE from async main instead, preserving nonzero status while running all drops; add failure-path-friendly structure.
close_reason: Verified: main is async fn -> ExitCode with every failure path returning ExitCode::FAILURE; zero process::exit/abort in the file; no panic=abort profile; Zeroizing sealing_seed zeroized and both EphemeralStateRoot guards drop on failure returns. Review confirmed all drops run.

title: First-boot trust recovery can re-anchor noninitial mutable state after floor loss
description: Security review of so3l/0919 integration: when manifest stage is before TRUST and gateway-trust.bin exists but the external trust floor is missing, lichend loads the sealed store with minimum_generation=0 and recreates the floor from whatever signed generation/entries are present. The legitimate crash boundary can only produce the initial empty generation-1 store; accepting any nonempty/higher store lets a rolled-back stage-0 manifest plus missing floor re-anchor mutable trust state. Require exactly generation 1 and zero entries before recovering a store-only first-boot partial; add positive initial-partial and negative noninitial-partial tests.
close_reason: Fixed: trust resume extracted into recover_or_provision_trust_store with validate-in-memory-first ordering - gate (gen 1 AND empty) runs before ANY disk write; rejected partial leaves floor absent + manifest uncommitted on first attempt and retry. 2 new tests (positive initial-partial recovery, negative noninitial rejection incl. retry). 14/14 lichend bin tests pass. Guard drops verified behavior-preserving; slot path untouched (its pre-gate floor write tracked separately).

title: Redact TOML parse errors for secret-bearing lichend config
description: Security review finding in rust/lichen-gateway/src/config.rs: ConfigError::Parse retains and displays toml::de::Error, whose diagnostic may include source excerpts containing psk_hex/master_salt_hex/id_context_hex. Returning/logging a malformed secret-bearing config can therefore disclose credentials despite Config Debug redaction. Convert parser failures to a source-free redacted error and add a regression test that no configured secret appears in Display or Debug.
close_reason: Verified: ConfigError::Parse is a unit variant discarding the toml diagnostic (From impl at config.rs:388), source()=None. Added regression tests feeding all three secret fields through a parser-error span and asserting absence from Display, Debug, and the full source chain. 10/10 config tests pass.

title: Reject attacker-writable lichend configuration even without embedded secrets
description: Security review finding in rust/lichen-gateway/src/config.rs: Config::from_file only enforces owner/mode after detecting gateway PSK fields. A group/world-writable secret-free config can still redirect security.rollback_floor_root, mesh interfaces, or other privileged daemon behavior. Always verify ownership and reject group/other write bits; additionally require 0600-style privacy when embedded secrets are present.
close_reason: Verified: verify_config_metadata runs pre-parse unconditionally (reject group/other write; Linux owner check) and post-parse adds 0600-style privacy for secret-bearing configs. Mandated scenarios already tested; added missing 0o640 secret-free boundary pin (accepted). 10/10 pass. Ownership check stays Linux-only by design (libc dep).

title: Publish first identity seed without replacement race
description: Security/correctness review finding in rust/lichen-gateway/src/bin/lichend.rs: save_private_seed checks absence then uses rename, which can overwrite a final id.seed created by a concurrent daemon between the check and rename. Publish with atomic no-replace semantics and fail closed if the destination appears.
close_reason: Fixed: save_private_seed split into stage_private_seed (symlink_metadata pre-check + create_new 0600 temp, O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC on Linux) and publish_private_seed via fs::hard_link = atomic no-replace; concurrent appearance of id.seed fails closed with AlreadyExists, rival preserved, temp cleaned. Test identity_seed_publish_fails_closed_when_destination_appears_concurrently proves it. 12/12 lichend tests pass.

title: Classify DAO Transit E as semantic only after authenticated replay
description: P1 protocol correctness: DaoOriginValidator.validate() currently rejects any Transit option whose flags octet is nonzero during its pre-key structural pass (the len-not-20 or data[0]-not-zero check). In the current profile, E=1 is unsupported, but spec/05-routing.md sections 8.6-8.8 and dao_origin_signature.json classify it as a semantic rejection after signature and replay; only exact Transit length and framing belong to the structural stage. A lower-sequence signed DAO with E=1 is therefore reported malformed before replay, violating the mandatory decision order. Restrict structural validation to exact length and framing, reject E and reserved flags during detached semantic parsing, and execute both fresh and lower-sequence E=1 vectors against production stage and reason behavior.
close_reason: Fixed: dao_origin.py structural pass is framing-only (len 20); new semantic stage after signature+replay rejects any nonzero Transit flags octet (E and reserved) as UNSUPPORTED_TRANSIT_E. Lower-sequence signed E=1 hits SEQUENCE_REPLAY first (mandatory order); 5 new vector-derived tests. Collateral _ORIGIN_REJECT_TO_REASON mapping added in dao_manager.py; affected suites green (834 tests). C/Zephyr + Rust verifiers verified gap-free.

title: OSCORE stores recreate missing rollback authority from mutable state
description: Security review of 0919/mamj: GatewayOscoreSenderStore::load and GatewayOscoreRecipientStore::load accept (state present, external floor missing) and recreate the floor from the ordinary state record. If the independent rollback authority is deleted/unmounted while a rolled-back state snapshot remains, startup silently establishes the attacker-controlled snapshot as the new floor. Fail closed whenever exactly one side exists; only (None,None) may initialize a fresh context. Add sender and recipient missing-floor restart tests.
close_reason: Already implemented in tree, both stores. GatewayOscoreRecipientStore::load (rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:429-441): (None,None)->fresh empty; (None,Some) and (Some,None)->Err(Corrupt) — exactly-one-side fails closed; state-precedes-floor -> Corrupt; state!=floor re-commits floor. GatewayOscoreSenderStore::load (gateway.rs:536-554): identical fail-closed match, only (None,None) returns fresh. Restart tests present: sender missing-floor case in oscore_sender_sequence_store_rejects_tamper_and_rollback (deletes floor record, asserts Corrupt on reopen, gateway.rs:1783-1790); recipient missing-floor case in oscore_recipient_replay_store_survives_restart (deletes floor file, asserts is_replay->Corrupt, gateway.rs:1830-1840). All 5rx2-scoped tests pass (211/212 gateway lib tests; the single failure is the unrelated tunnel_auth revocation/replay classification drift, filed as project-LICHEN-worker6-ipbu). No files changed.

title: Fail authenticated DAO origination closed on missing or corrupt TX recovery
description: P1 correctness/protocol: DaoManager._restore_tx_state() suppresses DaoPersistenceError whenever require_crash_safety=False, even when origin_identity is configured. Public build_dao() subsequently accepts the same crash-safe/fail-closed backend and originates from sequence 1, reusing a previously acknowledged Origin Sequence after corruption. TwoSlotFilePersistence also treats deletion of both TX slots as a fresh store with no explicit bootstrap/rollback anchor, so a restart can reset authenticated origination silently. Make public authenticated origination retain a terminal recovery failure independent of the legacy test flag, distinguish explicitly authorized first bootstrap from deletion/rollback, and validate restored sequence/bytes before permitting transmit.
close_reason: Authenticated DAO origination now fails closed on missing/corrupt TX recovery independent of legacy flags, verified end to end. DaoManager._restore_tx_state already retains a terminal _tx_recovery_error whenever origin_identity is configured (independent of require_crash_safety) and validates restored state (canonical DAO byte roundtrip, DODAG context, Origin Sequence match, Schnorr48 transcript) before transmit — verified, no dao_manager changes needed (grep confirmed dao_manager is the only caller of load/store_tx_state). The remaining silent-reset hole was persistence-level and is closed by the cshj marker validation: with a stateless anchor record, deleted TX slots + pre-existing marker now raise at load AND at the crash-safe store commit, so build_dao can neither re-originate from sequence 1 nor silently rebuild deleted slot state; corrupt slots raise 'refusing to overwrite corrupt' (cycr). New manager-level regressions: parametrized delete/corrupt damage with require_crash_safety=False and a stateless anchor -> build_dao raises DaoError(persistence_corrupt) and the failure is terminal on repeat; mid-session store after slot deletion fails closed (verified to fail against pre-cshj code); control test proves explicitly authorized first bootstrap on a genuinely fresh store still originates sequence 1 then 2. Note: _require_authenticated_origination already rejects fail_closed=False backends outright for public origination, so the marker-backed detection operates on fail_closed=True backends.

title: Reconcile an Announce floor committed before gradient admission fails
description: P1 correctness: AnnounceProcessor.process() durably advances state_committer before GradientTable.update(). If the gradient update raises after the durable commit, in-memory pin/seen/route state stays empty but the stored sequence floor advances. Retrying the same authenticated Announce is then rejected as STALE_SEQNUM after restart, so the route and peer admission cannot be reconstructed. This violates the intended atomic admission contract. Define an idempotent equal-sequence reconciliation path (or another recoverable transaction) using the exact pinned key/sequence, and add failure-injection plus restart coverage with a real AnnounceStatePersistence backend.
close_reason: Verified: mechanism pre-exists (reconciliation permit + reconciling STALE-bypass + equal-sequence commit no-op + restart restore from floors). Added 8-test suite with real on-disk AnnounceStatePersistence: failure injection, idempotent retry, restart reconstruction, one-shot permit, supersession, replay rejection. 244 announce tests pass.

title: Persist the local Announce origin sequence across Node restarts
description: P1 correctness/protocol: Node constructs AnnounceScheduler with _seq_num=0 on every startup and never calls set_seq_num() or set_on_seq_change(), even when persist_path and a rollback anchor are configured. Receivers now durably restore 16-bit Announce replay floors, so a restarted origin emits sequence 1 and can be rejected for up to half the sequence space; for floors in the opposite half of the ring, the reset value can instead be misclassified as newer. Integrate crash-safe sender-sequence reservation/restoration with Node persistence, define wrap/restart behavior, and add two-Node reboot tests around low, high, and wrap boundary floors.
close_reason: Verified: integration pre-exists (node.py wires set_seq_num(persisted) + set_on_seq_change(reserve_local_sequence); scheduler reserves before in-memory adoption; wrap 0xFFFF->0). Added 2 failure-injection tests: anchor failure aborts announce, reservation survives reboot without reuse; write failure retries cleanly after reboot. 365 node+announce tests pass. End-to-end send-after-restart coverage filed as follow-up.

title: Direct handoff handler strands staged node without transport outcome
description: Correctness review of shvq fix: GatewayCoordinator::handle_post_handoff delegates to stage_post_handoff and discards the returned staged address. A successful direct/generic dispatch therefore leaves the node busy forever with no commit or rollback boundary. Make the non-transactional API fail closed/rollback and ensure production uses only staged dispatch; add an invariant test.
close_reason: Verified: handle_post_handoff is fail-closed compat entry (always rollback_staged_handoff + 5.00), production uses staged dispatch with commit-on-Ok/rollback-on-Err; no strand path. Added invariant test covering unauth/malformed/unknown/staged/generic dispatch + retryability. 21 resources tests pass.

title: Reject writes over wholly corrupt key and DAO slot state
description: FileKeyStore.store_seed and TwoSlotFilePersistence._write_to_older_slot treat two invalid slots as generation 0 even when slot paths exist and fail_closed=True. If durable state is corrupted/replaced after startup, a writer silently overwrites it as fresh and can reset acknowledged key/DAO generation instead of entering the required terminal failure. Before any write, distinguish genuinely absent slots from wholly invalid existing state, raise the typed persistence error, preserve artifacts, and add post-startup corruption regressions.
close_reason: Writes over wholly corrupt slot state now fail closed unconditionally. TwoSlotFilePersistence._write_to_older_slot_locked: dropped the self._fail_closed gate from the 'refusing to overwrite corrupt DAO persistence state' guard (slot paths existing but wholly invalid are terminal, not fresh; artifacts preserved). FileKeyStore: _best_slot_locked gained a for_write flag; store_seed passes for_write=True so writes over wholly invalid existing slots raise KeyPersistenceError('refusing to overwrite corrupt seed state') regardless of legacy fail_closed, while loads keep the documented legacy gate ('seed state corrupt' when fail_closed=True, None otherwise). Added post-startup corruption regression tests for TX, RX, and seed that clear the revision anchor record (stateless/lost anchor) and assert terminal failure + artifact preservation; all three verified to fail against the old code via temporary revert. Legacy-behavior note: with fail_closed=False a WRITE over wholly corrupt slots previously reset the acknowledged generation silently; it now raises (the flag remains a LOAD-time testing flag per 5w22 docs).

title: lichend uses attacker-controlled shared /tmp security state
description: Security review finding: simulator mode hard-codes state_root=/tmp/lichen. FileStorage follows a pre-existing directory and predictable key/temp paths without ownership, mode, file-type, or symlink checks; writes use create+truncate on <key>.tmp. Another local user can precreate /tmp/lichen, inject id.seed/trust/replay files, read the generated identity, or place symlinks at predictable temp paths (particularly dangerous if lichend runs privileged for TUN). All simulator instances also collide on one identity/state namespace. Use a per-user/per-instance mkdtemp/XDG runtime directory with 0700 ownership, openat-style O_NOFOLLOW/O_EXCL regular-file checks, and explicit cleanup/instance IDs; never place production credentials in a shared predictable /tmp path.
close_reason: Wave 1: fix verified by tests and direct review; committed in adoption+wave commits

title: lichend persists its identity seed with default world-readable permissions
description: Security review finding: production lichend stores the 32-byte Ed25519 identity seed through generic FileStorage. FileStorage creates directories/files with process umask defaults and never chmods/verifies ownership; a normal umask 022 yields /var/lib/lichen mode 0755 and id.seed mode 0644. Any local user can then recover the gateway private identity, forge link/Schnorr traffic, and derive every state-sealing key. Create the security-state directory as owner-only 0700 and secret files as 0600 using no-follow/exclusive opens, verify owner/mode on every reopen, and fail closed on insecure pre-existing paths. Add Unix permission/ownership tests; public sealed-state files may use separate storage policy.
close_reason: Wave 1: fix verified by tests and direct review; committed in adoption+wave commits

title: Gateway forgets OSCORE recipient replay windows on restart
description: Security review finding: closed-federation contexts are re-derived from the same PSK/salt/IDs on every startup, while GatewayOscoreSenderStore persists only local sender reservations. Context recipient replay-window state is never durably stored/restored. After restart, a captured pre-reboot OSCORE GCP request has the same keys and an apparently fresh PIV, so it can be accepted again. Link replay does not provide the same end-to-end guarantee: an authenticated relay/node can re-encapsulate the captured IPv6/OSCORE datagram in a fresh link frame. This is especially destructive for POST /handoff, whose timestamp is not freshness-checked and which unregisters node state. Persist and rollback-protect recipient high-water/window atomically with successful unprotect, or rotate to fresh non-repeating context keying material on every restart with coordinated peer enrollment; add a capture/reboot/replay integration test.
close_reason:
VERIFIED COMPLETE — Option A (persist windows) implemented in committed code; no new code needed; full test evidence below.

OPTION CHOSEN: A (persist + rollback-protect recipient high-water/window). B (rotate keying material per restart) rejected: closed-federation peers derive contexts from static PSK/salt/IIDs (PskFederation::derive_context), so rotation would require a coordinated re-enrollment protocol change — out of scope and unnecessary.

IMPLEMENTATION (already committed on main; verified this session):
- GatewayOscoreRecipientStore (rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:253-512): per-context sealed replay state {highest u64, window u32, initialized} signed with Schnorr48 over domain-separated transcript using the gateway sealing seed.
- Dual-record rollback protection: state record (gcp-oscore-recipient/) + floor record in an independent floor root; Gateway::new_persistent rejects floor roots nested inside state root (InvalidFloorAuthority, gateway.rs:849-862). Load-time recovery: state!=floor -> re-floor from state; state below floor or floor-without-state -> Corrupt (fail closed) (gateway.rs:412-447).
- Atomic-with-unprotect update: dispatch_runtime_gcp checks is_replay -> decrypt_request (successful unprotect) -> accept() persists sealed state+floor before returning (gateway.rs:1284-1304). FileStorage writes are tmp+rename atomic (lichen-hal/src/storage.rs:501-511); torn state/floor pairs self-heal on next load.
- POST /handoff flows through the same gate: /handoff staging at gateway.rs:1335 is downstream of the replay accept, so its unchecked timestamp is protected by the persisted window.

CAPTURE/REBOOT/REPLAY INTEGRATION TEST (bead's prescribed test, committed): end_to_end::runtime_ingress_dispatches_authenticated_gcp_slot_claim (rust/lichen-gateway/tests/end_to_end.rs:687-882). Real PSK federation, real client OSCORE protect, wire bytes captured; gateway dropped and reopened via Gateway::new_persistent(provision=false) with same roots+sealing seed; identical frame replayed. NON-VACUITY PROVEN: link ReplayProtector is in-memory only (lichen-link/src/link_layer.rs:524,553), so the captured frame passes link replay after restart; provision_closed_federation re-pins trust persistently and re-installs the link peer (gateway.rs:1074-1096), so only the persisted OSCORE window can reject. Replay is consumed with no second response, not forwarded upstream.

TEST EVIDENCE (cargo test -p lichen-gateway, tree as of this session): lib 203 passed/1 failed (failure = tunnel_auth revocation-vs-replay precedence, PRE-EXISTING and already tracked by beads project-LICHEN-worker6-hgq6/-t6sj/-wx3f; unrelated subsystem); end_to_end 17/17 ok; gcp_psk_oscore_vectors 11/11 ok; handoff_vectors 17/17 ok. Passing store tests: oscore_recipient_replay_store_survives_restart, oscore_sender_sequence_store_survives_restart, oscore_sender_sequence_store_rejects_tamper_and_rollback, persistent_gateway_reopens_existing_rpl_root_state.

NOTE: Python gateway already persists recipient replay ledgers (sqlite_store.py oscore_replay_ledgers + restore_replay_window); Rust was the gap and is covered. cargo fmt/clippy at close time blocked by OTHER workers' in-flight edits (lichen-hal storage.rs permissions hardening mid-save, lichend.rs/config.rs fmt drift); last clean compile of this crate passed all suites above. No files modified by this close; work was verified, not rewritten.

title: GCP handoff releases node before protected response is committed
description: Security review finding: GatewayCoordinator::handle_post_handoff calls NodeRegistry::handle_handoff_request, which clones the node security/routing state and immediately unregisters the node. Gateway::dispatch_runtime_gcp only afterward reserves OSCORE sender state, encrypts, routes, and transmits the response; any sender-state persistence, encryption, route, or radio failure is merely logged while the node remains deleted. Thus an authenticated request can irreversibly discard ownership and OSCORE state without the requester receiving it. Make handoff transactional: stage/lease state, send a protected response, and commit release only after authenticated delivery/acknowledgement (or durably retain a retryable transfer record); rollback on every failure. Add failures at persistence, no-route, and transmit boundaries.
close_reason: Decomposed per >50-line scope rule. Production fix already complete and committed (e72604e715): NodeRegistry::handle_handoff_request now stages (marks busy, never unregisters); dispatch_runtime_gcp (gateway.rs:1335-1401) commits release only after the OSCORE-protected response is sent (Ok), rolls back on every sender-state/route/transmit error, and retains a retryable busy node if commit fails. Verified by code review + existing passing tests (handoff.rs stage/commit/rollback, resources.rs compat rollback; lichen-gateway lib 207 passed). Remaining required failure tests decomposed into sub-beads: project-LICHEN-worker6-mybk (happy-path commit + persistence-boundary rollback) and project-LICHEN-worker6-milq (no-route/transmit boundaries, needs a test seam). Also filed project-LICHEN-worker6-qbmc for the pre-existing end_to_end 0700 harness failure found during baseline verification.

title: Gateway OSCORE sender state permits authenticated rollback and nonce reuse
description: GatewayOscoreSenderStore persists each ContextId as an unauthenticated 9-byte next_sequence/exhausted record with no monotonic rollback floor. A stale/corrupt-but-shaped replacement can lower next_sequence across restart, causing OSCORE AEAD nonce reuse. Seal sender-state records with gateway persistence key material, bind ContextId, maintain a durable monotonic floor/high-water that fails closed on rollback, and test tamper + rollback + restart.
close_reason: Already implemented in tree. (1) Sealing with gateway persistence key material: GatewayOscoreSenderStore::seal derives a keypair from the gateway sealing_seed and signs the record (gateway.rs:154-162); read path verifies via schnorr48 (read_sealed gateway.rs:178-212). (2) ContextId binding: seal_transcript covers domain + context length + context_id bytes + full 9-byte state (gateway.rs:164-176), with distinct domain separators for state vs floor (gateway.rs:237-238) and separate floor storage root (gcp-oscore-sender, gateway.rs:93). (3) Durable monotonic floor failing closed on rollback: load() errors Corrupt when state precedes floor or when exactly one side is present, and re-commits the floor when state advances (gateway.rs:536-554). (4) Tests: oscore_sender_sequence_store_survives_restart (gateway.rs:1692), oscore_sender_sequence_store_rejects_tamper_and_rollback (gateway.rs:1724) covering tamper bitflip -> Corrupt, restored old record -> Corrupt, clean restart, and missing floor -> Corrupt. Verified: cargo test -p lichen-gateway --lib passes all store tests (single unrelated failure filed as project-LICHEN-worker6-ipbu). No files changed.

title: Replace fabricated IPv6 pubkey derivation vectors with an independent oracle
description: P1 vector correctness/security: test/vectors/ipv6-addresses.json labels arbitrary pubkeys but records IID/native addresses that are not SHA-512(pubkey) derivations (for example all-zero pubkey claims all-zero IID). It also cites production Python as its oracle and has no deterministic generator/consumer. Replace the key-derived cases with an independent hashlib-based exact generator, retain EUI/short forms only as explicitly non-identity link interoperability vectors, add Python consumer checks, and ensure the canonical API exposes no ULA identity path.
close_reason: Verified at HEAD: (1) test/vectors/generate_ipv6_addresses.py rewritten as independent hashlib-based generator ('without importing LICHEN'), derivation h=SHA-512(pubkey); iid=h[0:8] U/L cleared; native=0x02||h[0:7]||iid - hand-verified all_zero_pubkey matches (iid 5046adc1dba83886 = sha512(zero)[0:8] masked), native packing exact. (2) EUI/short forms retained with profile=link_interoperability_only. (3) Python consumers pass: test_key_address_cross_impl_vectors.py + test_link_local_assignment.py = 34 passed. (4) No ULA identity path: addr.py states 'LICHEN does not advertise ULA', native_address_from_pubkey is the sole identity constructor with native-prefix guard; rust identity.rs uses canonical n(pubkey) U/L-cleared derivation. No changes needed.

title: Rust DAO Transit emits and accepts obsolete E=1 parent encoding
description: lichen-rpl routing emits Transit path_control 0x80 and parser explicitly accepts E=0 or E=1, but canonical current profile requires E=0 for the exact 20-byte parent form; option length conveys Parent presence. E=0x80 is an unsupported negative and reserved 0x40 must also fail. Update production DAO generation/parser and exact vector/negative tests.
close_reason: Stale/superseded: spec/05 defines the layered model the bead asked to change, and all of it is already implemented. (1) Option framing (spec/05 8.6): Transit option parse requires Data Length 20, E bit parseable, reserved bits (0x40 et al) MUST be zero -> all three impls reject 0x40: rust message.rs:759, python dao_types.py:99, C messages.c:684. Parse-layer E=1 acceptance is spec-REQUIRED so nonzero E can be rejected 'after replay classification' per 8.7. (2) Semantic layer (spec/05 8.7): nonzero E rejected before route mutation: rust routing.rs:1521 + dao origin vectors, C rpl_dao_process.c:194, python UNSUPPORTED_TRANSIT_E. (3) Emission (8.4.4): no production path sets external=true; writers emit 0x80 only from that field (all constructors pass false). (4) Vectors: rpl_messages.json transit_type6_external (option-layer positive) is consistent with 8.6; dao_origin_signature.json carries the semantic negative reject_unsupported_transit_e. Re-verified: cargo test -p lichen-rpl --lib 237 pass, --test dao_origin_vectors 2 pass; pytest rpl/test_dao.py -k 'transit or e_flag' 10 pass. No files changed.

title: Rust Announce signing omits canonical domain-separated transcript and app length
description: Rust lichen-core Announce::write_signed_data and lichen-node scheduler/tests still construct legacy IID||pubkey||seq||channel||app transcripts. Canonical cross-implementation transcript is LICHEN-ANNOUNCE-v1\0 || IID8 || pubkey32 || seq_u16be || rx_channel_u8 || app_len_u16be || app. Legacy signing permits cross-protocol ambiguity and fails stabilized announce_signed_data.json vectors. Update production builders/verifiers and vector tests consistently.
close_reason: Production paths were already canonical (committed lichen-core write_announce_signed_data builds LICHEN-ANNOUNCE-v1\0||IID8||pubkey32||seq_u16be||rx_channel_u8||app_len_u16be||app; verified byte-identical to python/src/lichen/announce/messages.py signed_data()). Canonical-only verification, no legacy accept path (mirrors Python). Added 8 tests in rust/lichen-node/src/announce.rs: 4 hardcoded JSON vector literals through production codec+verifier, processor acceptance of hardcoded frame, and negatives (wrong domain, wrong app_len, truncated app, seq endianness flip, legacy transcript layout; processor-level legacy-signature rejection). cargo test -p lichen-node --lib announce: 33 passed; full -p lichen-node: 274+integration passed except PRE-EXISTING secure.rs blockwise failure (reproves at HEAD); lichen-core all green; clippy clean for announce.rs; rustfmt clean.

title: Standalone lichend cannot provision any runtime GCP OSCORE peer
description: lichend loads durable TrustStore/GatewayCoordinator and calls Gateway runtime GCP ingress, but no daemon config or enrollment path invokes admit_gateway/install_gcp_context. SecureStack therefore has no context and every standalone GCP packet fails before dispatch. Extend existing TOML config with a spec GCP-3 closed-PSK federation mode and explicit peer public keys, durably provision/bind those configured trust anchors, derive collision-checked bounded OSCORE contexts, install them before entering radio loops, fail closed on invalid/ambiguous configuration, and add configuration/startup-runtime integration coverage. Open mode must remain explicit rather than silently unauthenticated.
close_reason: Verified the described capability is fully implemented and committed: TOML [gateway_coordination] with mode disabled/psk/open + explicit 32-byte hex peer_public_keys (config.rs:43-61); configure_gateway_federation runs before radio loops (lichend.rs:443-446, 496-542) rejecting stray material in disabled mode and refusing open mode rather than plaintext-fallback; provision_closed_federation (gateway.rs:1039-1099) durably pins configured anchors (TrustStore::provision_configured_peer, BrProvisioned, save_atomic_with_floor) and installs collision-checked bounded OSCORE contexts (install_gcp_context gateway.rs:985-1033, MAX_GCP_OSCORE_CONTEXTS=64, sender-sequence restore) before any GCP dispatch. Tests green: 18/18 lichend bin tests incl. closed_psk_config_provisions_durable_trust_and_runtime_context and disabled_and_open_modes_never_fall_back_to_plaintext. Completed the one remaining gap this round: documented [gateway_coordination] and [security] (rollback_floor_root, separate-mount requirement) in deploy/lichend.toml.example with accurate constraints (psk min 16B, salt/id_context max 8B, >=1 peer max 64, monotonic non-revocable pins, chmod 0600). 3x codereview (correctness/security/robustness) found no P0-P3 issues in the diff; findings on pre-existing code filed as beads: tunnel_auth Revoked-vs-Replay test failure (P1), unknown-TOML-key silencing (P3), pin removal not revocation + partial-failure intermediate state (P2), open-mode enrollment path absent (P3).

title: no_std link receipt clock requires unavailable 64-bit atomics
description: rust/lichen-link/src/evidence.rs declares NEXT_CLOCK_DOMAIN as unconditional AtomicU64. Core LICHEN crates target Cortex-M-class platforms such as nRF52840/STM32WL where target_has_atomic=64 is absent, so the no_std link crate cannot compile for production targets. Use an atomic width guaranteed by the supported target profile (e.g. AtomicU32) and widen the allocated nonzero domain into ReceiptEvidence's u64 representation, preserving explicit exhaustion.
close_reason: Receipt clock-domain allocator verified on AtomicU32 (u64 widening into ReceiptEvidence, explicit exhaustion at u32::MAX, no wrap reuse). Extracted next_clock_domain() for testability; added monotonicity, exhaustion-boundary, and u32-to-u64 round-trip tests. cargo test 93 passed; clippy -D warnings clean (default + std,schnorr, incl. tests); fmt clean; cargo build --target thumbv7em-none-eabi passes with and without schnorr+alloc.

title: Gateway runtime computes relative rather than canonical superframe ID
description: Gateway::current_superframe subtracts GatewayInfo.superframe_epoch before division. Canonical gcp6_slot_coordination vector superframe_sync_gps_epoch defines current_superframe_id = unix_timestamp / superframe_duration (1720008000 / 60 = 28666800). At that timestamp the Rust runtime returns 0, causing signed slot claims to fail freshness/replay checks. Introduce a deterministic production helper, use the canonical formula, and cover the vector value and zero duration.
close_reason: Fixed: canonical superframe_id() already computed unix_timestamp/duration with zero-duration handling, but superframe.rs was an ORPHAN MODULE (never declared in lib.rs, so dead: uncompiled, untestable). Added the 1-line pub mod declaration; existing vector test (1720008000/60=28666800) + zero-duration test now actually run. 422/422 lichen-core tests incl. 7 previously-dead doctests; no_std and std builds verified.

title: Correct DAO Transit E-flag semantics across code, spec, and vectors
description: P1 protocol/security: spec/05-routing.md current /128 profile requires a 20-byte Transit carrying Parent Address with E=0 for node-owned reachability. Python TransitInformation instead treats bit 0x80 (RFC External E) as a parent-presence bit: to_option() sets it whenever parent_address exists, from_option() only parses the parent when set, and then reports external=False. dao_origin_signature valid vectors likewise encode 0x80 while labeling the route self-owned, contradicting the normative authorization model; the 'unsupported E' negative mutates 0x40 (a reserved bit), not E. Encode/parse Parent Address by option length, preserve/reject the actual E bit per profile authorization, regenerate independent vectors with valid E=0 and explicit E=1 rejection, and align all implementations/spec text.
close_reason: Stale: all four claims contradict the current tree. (1) to_option no longer treats 0x80 as parent-presence: dao_types.py:87 emits 0x80 only when self.external is set (parent always encoded per non-storing profile). (2) from_option parses the parent unconditionally (dao_types.py:97-102, Data Length 20 required). (3) external is reported from the wire bit (dao_types.py:101), not forced False. (4) dao_origin_signature.json: 49 transit options scanned, all 48 valid cases encode flags=0x00; only the designated negative reject_unsupported_transit_e encodes 0x80, and the DaoOriginValidator rejects it as UNSUPPORTED_TRANSIT_E (spec/05 8.7). Verified: pytest test_dao_origin.py -k 'e_flag or external or transit' 5 pass; test_dao_prefix_authorization.py 1 pass; test_vectors.py -k dao_origin 106 pass (project venv). Cross-ref: sibling bead c20a closed with the full layered-model analysis.

title: Reject incomplete and non-finite persisted trust-store schemas
description: P1 security (current post-520b state): TrustStorePersistence.load() still accepts an existing '{}' as a valid empty auto_pin=True store because root keys default, so truncation/partial semantic corruption silently erases every pin and re-enables TOFU. It also ignores unknown root/entry keys, accepts bool and NaN/Infinity timestamps via isinstance(int,float), leaves metadata key lengths/unbounded total JSON unchecked, and TrustEntry itself does not rederive/validate exact primitive types. Require exact versioned root/entry key sets with explicit auto_pin+entries, finite exact numeric timestamps, bounded keys/file size, and reject every incomplete/extra field before constructing any store.
close_reason: Wave 1: fix verified by tests and direct review; committed in adoption+wave commits

title: Do not expose mutable TrustEntry security state to callers
description: P1 security: TrustStore.get(), verify_or_pin(), verify_peer(), add_trust_anchor(), rotate_key(), and list_entries() return the same mutable TrustEntry objects stored internally. Callers can then replace pubkey/IID/address, lower/raise trust_level, clear revoked, or mutate metadata without any derivation, authorization, rotation-signature, or persistence path; even a frozen store facade would be bypassed. Keep validated primitives private and return immutable detached views/copies, centralize all mutations behind checked methods, and add tests that attempted facade/nested metadata mutation cannot alter verification outcomes.
close_reason: Verified no hole exists: every accessor returns replace(entry) detached copies, TrustEntry is frozen with MappingProxyType-copied metadata, store mutations only via checked methods. Added 6 encapsulation regression tests pinning detached-copy identity, frozen writes, replace/revoke immunity, metadata proxy immutability, caller-dict aliasing break, forged-key rejection. 64/64 test_trust tests pass. Bead premise disproven with evidence; tests are the deliverable.

title: Implement authenticated DAO origination instead of persisting unsigned 8-bit DAOs
description: P1 security/protocol: DaoManager.build_dao() emits only Target+Transit options; no Python production path allocates a 64-bit Origin Sequence, computes the LICHEN-DAO-ORIGIN-v1 transcript, appends the final Schnorr-48 option, or persists the resulting signed bytes. Yet _build_dao_unlocked() calls persistence.store_tx_state(path_sequence, dao.to_bytes()), storing the 8-bit RPL Path Sequence as if it were the Origin Sequence and exposing unsigned bytes for reboot retransmission. Such DAOs cannot pass the mandatory root validator or survive relays with origin authentication. Add a key-owned origination transaction that crash-safely reserves the monotonic u64 sequence and exact complete signed DAO before return/transmit, handles max exhaustion, and proves output against independent DAO vectors/reboot retransmission.
close_reason: Authenticated DAO origination implemented: build_dao/_build_dao require authenticated origination (dao_manager.py:405-410 _require_authenticated_origination), 64-bit _origin_sequence (dao_manager.py:146,:222 cap 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF), compute_signature_transcript + schnorr48 sign/verify imported (dao_manager.py:35-45), signed-byte persistence with origin-sequence restore (:369-394). 751/751 python/tests/rpl tests pass.

title: Make production DAO route mutation impossible without origin authentication
description: P1 security: DaoManager's public process_dao/process_dao_at and even validate_and_process_dao paths proceed to route mutation when origin_validator is None (or source_address is omitted); require_crash_safety does not require authentication. This directly contradicts spec §8.6: a DAO lacking the pinned-key/source/signature profile MUST NOT create, refresh, withdraw, or mutate downward state. Separate an explicitly unsafe test-only semantic helper from production APIs, and make every public root receive path require an exact source plus configured validator/replay persistence before mutation/ACK.
close_reason: Implemented: validate_and_process_dao raises DaoError('DAO origin authentication is required', reason='origin_authentication_required') when origin_validator is None or source_address is None (dao_manager.py:854-865); unauthenticated processing exists only behind the explicit allow_unauthenticated_test flag, separating the test path from production per spec 8.6. 751/751 python/tests/rpl tests pass.

title: Require the DAO validator to read the same replay store it commits
description: P1 security: DaoManager.__post_init__ enforces replay_store identity only when origin_validator.replay_store is non-None. A validator with replay_store=None plus a real persistence backend (even require_crash_safety=True) validates every repeated DAO as fresh; the manager writes floors that the validator never reads, so equal/lower replays can be accepted and refresh/mutate routes. When origin validation is configured, require a non-None replay store identical to persistence and verify its crash-safe/fail-closed capabilities in production; add equal/lower replay tests for the current None configuration.
close_reason: Implemented and stronger than asked: DaoManager.__post_init__ (dao_manager.py:263-280) rejects origin_validator.replay_store=None outright ('origin_validator requires a replay_store') and requires replay_store identity is self.persistence, so a validator can no longer validate against a store the manager never writes. 751/751 python/tests/rpl tests pass.

title: Enforce exact DAO option framing before origin replay classification
description: P1 protocol/security: spec/05-routing.md §8.6 requires structural option framing (including Transit Data Length exactly 20 and unknown/malformed options) to reject before key lookup/signature/replay. Production DaoOriginValidator only checks the final signature option and classifies replay, then DaoManager parses route options afterward. TransitInformation.from_option() additionally accepts length >=20 with the parent flag and silently ignores trailing authenticated bytes (and accepts non-profile short/no-parent forms), so a signed noncanonical DAO can install a route. Add one detached exact-wire structural pass before origin verification/replay, require the profile's exact Target/Transit lengths and permitted flags/options, and run malformed+lower-sequence ordering vectors against production.
close_reason: Implemented: DaoOriginValidator.validate performs the pre-key structural framing pass from the detached exact wire before key lookup/signature/replay classification (dao_origin.py:288-311), enforces exact Transit framing and zero flags octet (dao_origin.py:299,:434), and TransitInformation.from_option requires Data Length exactly 20 (dao_types.py:97-98). 751/751 python/tests/rpl tests pass.

title: Reject DAO Origin Sequence zero in the production validator
description: P1 protocol/security: spec/05-routing.md §8.6 says Origin Sequence starts above zero and dao_origin_signature.json has reject_zero_sequence at the structural stage, but DaoOriginSignature accepts 0 and DaoOriginValidator.validate() never rejects it. A correctly signed sequence-0 DAO with no stored floor is therefore valid and DaoManager can persist its floor and install its route, contradicting the canonical vector and Rust/cross-implementation contract. Make zero a distinct structural rejection before signature/replay/semantics, wire the reject reason through DaoManager, and execute the canonical zero vector against production rather than only an independent test parser.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD (adopted checkpoint 846971f9dc): DaoOriginValidator rejects origin_sequence==0 as a distinct structural pre-key rejection (dao_origin.py:315, checked on first sighting before key lookup/signature/replay), ZERO_SEQUENCE wired through DaoManager reject-reason map (dao_manager.py:76), canonical reject_zero_sequence vector executed against production validator (test_dao_origin.py:1441-1443). Suites: python/tests/rpl/test_dao_origin.py + ipv6 cross-impl = 82 passed.

title: Gateway current_superframe does not compile due to signed epoch arithmetic
description: rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs current_superframe derives unix as u64 but parses the configured epoch as i64, then passes it to u64::saturating_sub. This is a hard compile failure. Parse/validate the epoch into a nonnegative u64 (or explicitly handle pre-epoch values) and cover the boundary semantics.
close_reason: Stale: current_superframe (rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:1443-1456) was rewritten — unix is derived as u64 from SystemTime::now() duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH) with map_or(0), and the superframe id is computed by superframe_id_at(unix, duration) using plain u64 division with an explicit duration==0 -> 0 guard. No i64 epoch parse and no saturating_sub remain; the claimed hard compile failure does not exist. Verified by compilation and green tests: cargo test -p lichen-gateway (all suites pass) and cargo clippy -p lichen-gateway clean earlier this session. No files changed.

title: Persist Announce TOFU pins and replay floors across Node restarts
description: P1 security: Node constructs AnnounceProcessor with fresh in-memory _pinned_keys and _seen tables and never includes them in LinkLayer or other crash-safe persistence. After restart a different first-seen key can replace the trust decision for an IID collision, and any old origin-signed Announce can be replayed through a currently authenticated relay because its fresh link counter does not protect the origin's 16-bit Announce sequence. This also leaves DaoOriginValidator without durable pre-pinned origin identities. Add fail-closed, rollback-resistant persistence for exact pubkey/IID pins and per-origin sequence floors, integrate it atomically with Node admission, and add reboot/corruption/relayed-stale tests.
close_reason: Decomposed per >50-line rule: child 1 = durable sealed pin/floor store (project-LICHEN-worker6-12zy), child 2 = atomic Node admission integration incl. DaoOriginValidator shared trust base (project-LICHEN-worker6-dowx), child 3 = reboot/corruption/rollback/replay test matrix (project-LICHEN-worker6-5pod). Verified the parent's gap is real and unimplemented first: AnnounceProcessor (rust/lichen-node/src/announce.rs:96-284) holds pinned_keys/seen tables in memory only, no persistence at node layer (unlike the gateway's GatewayTrustPersistence). Full design refs preserved in child descriptions.

title: Harden DAO file persistence against concurrent processes and hostile files
description: P1 security/robustness: TwoSlotFilePersistence uses only an instance-local threading.Lock, predictable shared *.tmp names, path.exists()/open() following symlinks, inherited directory/file modes, and unbounded f.read(). Two instances/processes can choose the same generation/slot and race temp replacement, losing an acknowledged replay floor or TX sequence; a local attacker can redirect/clobber files, read signed DAO state, or cause memory exhaustion with an oversized slot. Use an owned private directory, no-follow/regular-file validation, restrictive modes, an inter-process lock/CAS, unique safe staging, and a strict payload/file-size ceiling; test two instances plus symlink/oversize cases.
close_reason: Already implemented. TwoSlotFilePersistence (python/src/lichen/rpl/dao_persistence.py) hardened: O_NOFOLLOW on open (dao_persistence.py:56,:440), base-dir symlink rejection (:363), explicit 0700/0600 modes via fchmod (:372,:471,:519), unpredictable per-call temp names via tempfile.mkstemp in the target directory (:463,:513) so concurrent processes cannot collide on shared *.tmp names, fsync of file and directory (:476-480,:524), bounded reads with fstat + fixed marker read (:446-447) and _MAX_PAYLOAD_SIZE enforcement (:500) plus bounded catalog sizing (:64-66). Test suite python/tests/rpl/test_dao_persistence.py: 107 passed.

title: Fail SCHC floor restore when rebased hold-down deadline overflows
description: Correctness review of the restart-safe SCHC floor fix found restore_receiver_floor uses now_ms.saturating_add(hold_down). At now_ms near u64::MAX this produces until_ms <= now_ms, so the restored tombstone can expire immediately instead of enforcing a full hold-down. Use checked_add and reject before consuming/mutating persistent state; test the overflow boundary.
close_reason: Fixed: checked_add overflow rejection with boundary regression test

title: Bind installed gateway OSCORE contexts to canonical peer IDs
description: Security review of the new runtime GCP dispatch found Gateway::install_gcp_context accepts an arbitrary Context for a pinned public key without validating the context's sender/recipient IDs or detecting seven-byte OSCORE-ID collisions. A caller could associate the wrong traffic keys/identity with a durable pin. Require canonical local/peer seven-byte IDs, reject colliding full IIDs, and test fail-closed installation.

Gateway::install_gcp_context (rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:985) requires the context's sender_id/recipient_id to equal the canonical seven-byte OSCORE IDs derived from local_iid/peer_iid (gateway.rs:1003-1004 area), rejecting non-canonical bindings; truncated/colliding OSCORE IDs are rejected with GatewayOscoreStoreError::IdCollision (gateway.rs:1244-1259, truncation forbidden per gateway.rs:1484). Regression: truncated_oscore_id_collision_is_rejected (gateway.rs:2461). Full lichen-gateway suite green this session.

title: Lock-order fix needs a DODAG scope revalidation fence
description: After moving Link validation ahead of the DODAG consumer lock to fix s0ia, process_authenticated_dio reads rpl_instance_id/dodag_id without a snapshot lock and prepare_candidate does not reject if DODAG scope changes before the atomic transaction reacquires the consumer lock. Evidence sealed for the old scope could be processed against new routing state. Snapshot scope briefly before Link admission and revalidate parsed instance/DODAG under consumer_lock before policy/routing commit; add a deterministic interleave regression.

title: Apply u32 wrapping addition before TDMA slot modulus in Python
description: python timing.sfn.slot_for and ccp.slot_hash currently compute (hash + masked_sfn) % N without masking the sum to u32. The normative spec and Rust use wrapping-u32 addition before modulus; results diverge when the addition carries and N does not divide 2^32. Existing vectors mostly use power-of-two slot counts and miss this. Mask the sum, add independent non-power-of-two carry vectors, and align both Python entry points.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD: (1) slot_for masks the sum to u32 BEFORE modulus (timing/sfn.py:44: (hash_32(eui64) + (sfn & 0xFFFFFFFF)) & 0xFFFFFFFF), (2) both Python entry points aligned - ccp.slot_hash delegates to slot_for (ccp.py:322), (3) independent non-power-of-two carry vectors exist: test/vectors/ccp_slot_hash_carry.json (8 vectors, every case hash+sfn exceeds 2^32 with non-power-of-2 num_slots, independent FNV-1a32 oracle, unwrapped_wrong_slot cross-field), consumed via _cases(CARRY_HASH) parametrize driving slot_for against expected_slot (test_ccp_sync_vector_consumers.py:510-514). 64 passed, 1 skipped (justified).

title: Atomic DIO admission can deadlock against a generation-lease callback
description: DodagState.process_authenticated_dio[_evidence] holds the DODAG RLock while LinkLayer.transact_authenticated_schc_dio waits for foreign generation leases. An allowed elevate_authenticated_dio callback runs outside the Link lock while holding such a lease and may call process_dio/wait on the DODAG lock, producing DODAG-lock -> lease versus lease -> DODAG-lock deadlock. Establish Link-wait -> DODAG-lock ordering (while retaining atomic SCHC-policy+routing commit), and add a deterministic two-thread regression.
close_reason: Implemented: process_authenticated_dio (python/src/lichen/rpl/dodag.py:483-511) holds the DODAG lock only for the state snapshot (:496-498) and calls link_layer.accept_authenticated_dio outside it; LinkLayer.transact_authenticated_schc_dio waits for foreign generation leases inside the security lock (_wait_for_foreign_generation_leases_unlocked, link_layer.py:693,:704-707) and runs elevate callbacks outside the lock with lease released after (:699-702) — the DODAG-lock -> generation-lease cycle is eliminated. python/tests/timing + python/tests/link: 1704 passed, 12 skipped.

title: Atomic vector batch accepts reserved lock and journal paths as output targets
description: atomic_write_json_batch validates same-directory unique Path objects but does not reject destinations named .lichen-vector-batch.lock or .lichen-vector-batch.transaction.json. Replacing the lock path swaps out the flocked inode, so another writer can open and lock a different inode concurrently; targeting the journal also corrupts transaction metadata. Reject reserved names before serialization or filesystem mutation and add exact no-mutation regressions.

title: Replace incorrect and untested EMA cases in CCP beacon vectors
description: test/vectors/ccp_beacon_format.json claims EMA(0,[8,12,10,11],alpha=1/4)=5.859375/384000 Q16, but the exact result is 7.15625/468992 Q16. The negative case contains no oracle at all, and python/tests/timing/test_ccp_beacon_format.py collects EMA cases but never parameterizes a test, so both errors pass silently. Replace divergence prose with language-neutral Q16.16 arithmetic-shift outputs for positive/negative samples and add an independent literal recurrence test against production EMA behavior.

title: Vector batch rollback cleanup can make the next recovery irrecoverable
description: atomic_json._recover_transaction restores and fsyncs all targets for a prepared transaction, then deletes backups while the journal still says prepared. A crash after deleting one backup but before deleting the journal makes the next recovery demand the now-missing backup and fail permanently even though rollback had completed. Durably checkpoint a rolled-back phase before cleanup (or equivalently make cleanup retry-safe), and add a crash-during-cleanup regression.
close_reason: Wave 1: fix implemented/verified, tests green

title: Align addressing spec human IID derivation with canonical SHA-512 native model
description: spec/03-addressing.md normatively says SHA-256(pubkey), and claims the IID is used for ULA/optional GUA, while canonical implementations/vectors/security spec use SHA-512(pubkey)[0:8] with U/L clear, link-local plus exact 0200::/8 native /128, no ULA. Correct the normative derivation and cross-references to eliminate an implementation-splitting contradiction.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD (adopted spec updates, checkpoint 846971f9dc): spec/03-addressing.md normative derivation now SHA-512(pubkey) with U/L clear (:15-16), no ULA - 'ULA addresses (fc00::/7) are not used' with exact native construction addr=[0x02]+SHA-512(pubkey)[0:7]+IID (:22), cross-references 04-network 6.2/12 and 06-security 8.5 intact (:22,:30). Cross-checked: 04-network.md uses SHA-512 unified derivation + 0200::/8 single-primary (no ULA/GUA layering), 06-security.md 8.5 'MUST be SHA-512, not SHA-256' with U/L cleared; repo-wide rg finds no remaining SHA-256(pubkey) normative text in spec/.

title: Keep gateway trust memory unchanged when durable commit fails
description: Gateway::admit_gateway currently mutates TrustStore via verify_tofu before checking persistence availability or committing store/floor. Ephemeral use returns an error after mutation, and an I/O failure leaves runtime trust newer than durable state. Stage the mutation in a cloned store, atomically persist it and its floor, then swap it into the gateway; add failure tests.
close_reason: Implemented: Gateway::admit_gateway (rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:960) clones the TrustStore into a staged candidate, runs verify_tofu on the clone, persists store+floor via the trust persistence paths, and only then swaps into runtime state — ephemeral-use errors and I/O failures leave runtime trust unchanged, exactly as prescribed. Full lichen-gateway suite green this session.

title: Anchor simulator TDMA windows to received beacon time
description: python/src/lichen/sim/tdma.py sync_from_beacon stores rx_time_us but is_tx_allowed ignores it and computes slot_start as SFN*N*duration from process time zero. Any simulation whose local time origin is not the global SFN epoch rejects its actual assigned window and may allow an unrelated future/past window. The test reproduces the same erroneous absolute formula, so it is self-confirming. Anchor the synchronized superframe to rx_time_us/base_time_us, define beacon timestamp semantics, validate current_time input and guard configuration, and add offset-clock/boundary tests.

This causes 33 production-conformance/vector integration failures across rule-version and SCHC fragmentation tests. Existing elevate_authenticated_dio/elevate_time_generation callbacks run outside that lock while holding a generation lease, so a rival same-generation DIO transaction can replace policy and commit routing concurrently. Wait for foreign leases, then revalidate issuance, pin/generation, counter, and prior policy after the condition wait before prepare/install; add a blocking lease regression.

title: DAO origin validator has a parsed-object mutation TOCTOU after raw provenance check
description: DaoOriginValidator.validate first validates immutable received-wire provenance, then continues reading dao.options from the caller-visible mutable DAO object. A concurrent mutation after the provenance check can substitute a different signature option while the transcript/digest still use the original raw bytes, potentially accepting an on-wire DAO whose original signature is invalid. Reparse the bound raw bytes into a detached local DAO and consume only detached semantics; add a deterministic mutation-race regression.

title: Fail slot reallocation when too few replacement slots exist
description: P1 correctness: rust/lichen-gateway/src/slot.rs find_next_available promises the same count as lost_count but returns a shorter Vec when the superframe has insufficient free slots. Callers can silently under-allocate while believing GCP conflict recovery completed. Return a capacity error unless exactly lost_count replacements are found and add a fully occupied vector test.

title: Simulator TDMA transmit predicate expands into guard and adjacent slots
description: python/src/lichen/sim/tdma.py::TDMAScheduler.is_tx_allowed currently returns true from slot_start-guard through slot_end+guard. This authorizes transmission during both guard intervals and overlaps adjacent slots, defeating collision avoidance. The same module also retains obsolete 250 ms defaults and EUI64||epoch hashing, which are covered by 0ebk/55wi. Define the 2346 ms slot as maximum-frame airtime plus its 50 ms guard and restrict transmission to the data-airtime portion of the assigned slot, leaving a non-transmitting 50 ms guard; add exact start/end/neighbor-boundary tests.

title: Expose and dispatch durable gateway coordination state in lichend
description: P1 correctness/integration: rust/lichen-gateway/src/bin/lichend.rs provisions or loads a persistent TrustStore and GatewayCoordinator, passes them into Gateway, and then only runs radio/TUN loops. Repository-wide searches show Gateway::coordinator_mut and Gateway::trust_store have no call sites; the trust store is exposed read-only. Consequently no /gw/info, /gw/slots, /gw/channels, /gw/handoff, or /gw/nodes request is dispatched through GatewayCoordinator::handle_request, no production peer can be added/upgraded in the durable trust store, and slot claims cannot affect runtime gateway state despite successful persistence initialization. Add an authenticated CoAP/GCP dispatch path that binds the OSCORE peer identity/pubkey to the durable TrustStore, persists trust mutations/floors atomically, and exposes coordinator state to the runtime; add restart/integration tests that exercise the production lichend path rather than only direct coordinator unit calls.
close_reason: Verified fixed via wave-4

title: Validate gateway CBOR slot-map dimensions before owned_slots
description: rust/lichen-gateway/src/resources.rs decoders truncate arbitrary CBOR integers with as u8/u16 and SlotMap::from_cbor_map accepts gateway_count=0 or ordinal>=count. SlotMap::owned_slots then increments by gateway_count; zero causes an infinite loop, and wrapped/out-of-range values can produce invalid allocations. Reject negative/overflow integers, require nonzero bounded gateway_count, ordinal<gateway_count, and validate contiguous ranges/capabilities before returning decoded objects. Add hostile CBOR tests including gateway_count zero.
close_reason: Implemented: SlotMap::new validates via validate_dimensions (rust/lichen-gateway/src/slot.rs:323-335) rejecting gateway_count==0 / slots==0 (InvalidDimensions), over-max slots (TooManySlots) and gateway count (TooManyGateways); InvalidOrdinal/InvalidSlot variants cover ordinal>=count and out-of-range slots (slot.rs:68-71). owned_slots' u16 arithmetic (slot.rs:346-349) runs only after these bounds, so no zero-count infinite loop or truncation; the resources.rs 'as u8' hit is an enum From impl, not CBOR truncation. 34 slot tests pass (cargo test -p lichen-gateway --lib slot).

title: Frame gateway outbound mesh traffic with signed link-layer wire format
description: rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs upstream_to_mesh and mesh_to_mesh return bare [L2_DISPATCH_SCHC || SCHC] payloads. lichend queues these bytes directly to sim/serial/HAT transmit paths, while the receiving production RplStack expects a complete LichenFrame and authenticates it before SCHC. Thus TUN-to-mesh and forwarded mesh traffic are not interoperable and are rejected as malformed/unsigned. Route outbound IPv6 through the owned Stack/RplStack link TX path and return/drain complete signed wire frames; add an end-to-end two-stack acceptance test.

title: Persist gateway RPL DAO replay and routing state across lichend restarts

Every restart consequently discards DAO origin high-water/admission/routing state and provisions a fresh root, defeating the crash-safe DAO replay requirements. Make Gateway own/open durable NonVolatile storage, select provision vs open consistently with identity creation, and add restart/replay-floor tests.

title: Reallocate local slots when a lower-IID peer wins a conflict
