No outcome or callback tells any caller to reallocate/re-claim, so both gateways continue transmitting in overlapping slots contrary to GCP-6.3's loser MUST select next available slot and re-claim. Implement the local loser transition (or return a mandatory typed action) and test the full conflict/reclaim state change.
close_reason: Implemented: handle_post_slots (rust/lichen-gateway/src/resources.rs:1938) tracks reallocated_slots (:1981), sets the retained local allocation (:2078) when a lower-IID peer wins, and publishes the outcome to callers (:2102); regression lower_iid_peer_forces_complete_local_reallocation (resources.rs:2530) covers the lower-IID conflict path. Slot lib tests green (34 passed).

title: Derive PSK federation keys from the complete configured PSK
description: rust/lichen-gateway/src/trust.rs accepts PSKs longer than 16 bytes and federation_identifier hashes the complete PSK, but derive_context passes only self.psk[..16] to OSCORE. Two configurations with identical first 16 bytes and different suffixes therefore produce identical traffic keys while is_isolated_from reports them isolated. Either enforce an exact 16-byte PSK or KDF the complete PSK into the 16-byte OSCORE master secret, and add a suffix-difference key/isolation test.
close_reason: Fixed: complete-PSK KDF into OSCORE master secret + suffix-difference regression

title: Persist SCHC tombstone duration in a restart-safe clock domain
description: rust/lichen-schc/src/fragment.rs serializes TerminalTombstone.until_ms as an absolute process-monotonic timestamp and restore_receiver_floor installs it unchanged after restart. Monotonic epochs are not comparable across processes: a new uptime already above the old value expires the replay hold-down immediately, while a reset-to-zero clock can extend it arbitrarily. Persist a restart-independent expiry or conservatively reconstruct a full hold-down from restore time, bind the representation into the sealed floor record, and add restart tests with lower and higher new clock values.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-3

title: Native address routing and identity specs contradict canonical 0200::/8 SHA-512 derivation
description: Final correctness review found incompatible definitions of the key-derived native address space and IID algorithm. Canonical Python yggdrasil_address() fixes addr[0]=0x02 and derives the IID from SHA-512; SCHC Rules 1/6, spec/03-adaptation.md, the SCHC draft, generators, and vectors therefore match only 0200::/8. But python/src/lichen/node.py configures Router with IPv6Network('0200::/7'), python/src/lichen/schc/headers.py::_is_global admits first bytes 0x02 and 0x03, and spec/01-architecture.md, 04-network.md, 05-routing.md, 06-security.md plus vector descriptions call the space 0200::/7 or 02xx::/7. Consequently the router can classify 0300::/8 destinations as native mesh even though no canonical key derivation creates them and SCHC Rules 1/6 reject them. In addition, spec/04-network.md section 6.2 shows IID=SHA-256(pubkey)[0:8], contradicting its own references, spec/06-security, Python, and exact vectors that require SHA-512. Establish the canonical 0200::/8 + SHA-512 definition everywhere, narrow routing/global classification accordingly, update stale vector prose, and add negative coverage proving 03xx addresses are not native-profile addresses.
notes: Decision: Full Yggdrasil compat. Implement exact AddrForKey algorithm from yggdrasil-go: invert pubkey, count leading 1s, embed in address per upstream spec. This is a BREAKING CHANGE - all existing addresses will change. Address space becomes 0200::/7 (not /8). SHA-512 hash approach is abandoned.
close_reason: Decision made: full Yggdrasil compat. Implementation beads filed: worker6-yjg6 (Python), worker6-4tji (Rust), worker6-4bju (C), worker6-lqzm (specs). Breaking change accepted.

title: Default TOFU mesh bootstrap cannot authenticate an unknown Announce
description: LinkLayer.receive requires _find_sender to locate a pre-existing peer key before it can verify any link signature. _find_sender only checks self, rekeyed peers, peer_lookup, and peer_lookup_all; Node supplies only its existing peer_db. Yet the offline baseline requires learning an unknown peer's public key from its signed Announce and Node._process_announce adds that peer only after LinkLayer.receive succeeds. Starting with the default empty peer_db therefore rejects every discovery Announce as BAD_SIGNATURE and can never form a TOFU mesh. Add a bounded, structurally parsed Announce bootstrap candidate path that derives/checks SIID, verifies the link signature and inner Announce signature before pinning, without admitting arbitrary payload keys; add empty-node mutual discovery and malformed-candidate regressions.
close_reason: Verified fixed via wave-4

title: Receipt-clock callback failure is recoverable and can extend stale authority
description: python/src/lichen/link/link_layer.py::_receipt_now permanently disables the receipt clock and clears receipts only for regression/reentry. If the bound MonotonicClock callback raises or returns an invalid value, the exception escapes without setting _receipt_clock_failed or revoking _verified_receipts/_authenticated_dio_issuances. After an arbitrarily long outage the callback may return a barely advanced value, allowing an actually stale one-use receipt or DIO issuance to remain usable; Node's receive loop catches non-LinkSecurityClockError exceptions and continues. Treat any callback/capability/validation failure as terminal LinkSecurityClockError, revoke all time-bound authorities, and regress raise/NaN/awaitable then recovery attempts.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-3

title: Authenticated DIO issuance omits signer/source and root key binding
description: python/src/lichen/rpl/authenticated_dio.py::_issue_authenticated_dio_from_ipv6 seals AuthenticatedDio after checksum/instance/DODAG/MOP/role checks but does not require the decompressed IPv6 source to be fe80:: plus the authenticated signer's IID, nor (for expected_role=root) require DODAGID == AddrForKey(signer). Those checks exist only in DodagState's routing consumer. DioTimeVerifier and LinkLayer.accept_authenticated_schc_dio trust the sealed object directly, so an authorized link signer can obtain time/SCHC-policy evidence for a DIO asserting another source (and a root can assert a DODAG not derived from its key). The packets-timing wrong-signer test explicitly short-circuits before calling production admission, so it does not regress this. Enforce both identity bindings at sealed issuance for unfragmented and fragmented DIOs, then make routing/time/SCHC consumers share the same rejection vectors.
close_reason: wave-6

title: TDMA guard and slot-duration requirements contradict the 2346 ms canonical minimum
description: Final correctness review: spec/09-packets-timing.md §14.8, python timing constants, Rust constants, and packets-timing.json require one 50 ms guard and a minimum 2346 ms slot for a maximum 255-byte SF10/125 kHz frame. spec/02a-coordinated-capacity.md still encodes guard default 100 ms and says max_airtime(current_SF)+100 ms; spec/02a-tdma.md presents a 60-byte typical packet plus 50 ms as a 250 ms slot and even says GPS may reduce the guard. These normative statements permit incompatible schedules and slots too short for the profile maximum. Align beacon field defaults, minimum-slot calculation, examples, and any guard-reduction language with the canonical maximum-frame rule and exact airtime vector.
acceptance_criteria: All normative TDMA documents and vectors require the same guard and maximum-frame-derived slot minimum at each configured data rate.
close_reason: wave-5

title: Normative TDMA specs define incompatible SFN slot-hash formulas
description: Final Python/spec correctness review: spec/09-packets-timing.md §14.7 and python/src/lichen/timing/sfn.py/test/vectors/ccp_sfn_wrap_slot_hash.json define slot=(FNV1a32(EUI64)+u32(SFN)) mod N. spec/02a-coordinated-capacity.md §2a.2 instead declares FNV1a32(EUI64 XOR SFN) mod N as the one true interop algorithm, while spec/02a-tdma.md declares FNV1a32(EUI64 || SFN little-endian) mod N. These produce different slots and the §14.7 cross-reference claims 02a is authoritative, so conforming implementations can never interoperate. Choose one canonical preimage/formula, update every normative spec/example/vector description and executable Python/Rust consumer, and add cross-document fixed vectors at SFN 0, 1, 0xffffffff, and wrap.
acceptance_criteria: One unambiguous formula and byte order is normative everywhere; Python and Rust execute the same independent vectors including wrap.
close_reason: Specs already aligned on option 1: (fnv1a32(EUI64) + u32(SFN)) mod N. Line 76 of 02a-coordinated-capacity.md, line 38 of 02a-tdma.md, line 566 of 09-packets-timing.md all match. No changes needed.

title: Rule 7 decoder accepts overlong compressed residue at profile boundary
description: python/src/lichen/schc/headers.py reconstructs a MAX_PACKET_SIZE MQTT-SN Rule 7 packet from an encoded residue and accepts one extra trailing residue byte because only the reconstructed packet length is bounded after decoding. python/tests/schc/test_headers.py::test_mqtt_sn_rule7_profile_size_boundary now fails: compress_packet(max_size_raw) + 0x00 does not raise SchcError. Preserve the j2yt MAX_PACKET_SIZE uncompressed boundary while rejecting encoded residues whose complete consumption/reconstruction is non-canonical or exceeds the Rule 7 encoded bound. Add focused exact-boundary regressions, then run SCHC tests, Ruff, mypy, and 3x review convergence.
notes: Investigation showed the production decoder was correct under j2yt/spec: 22,554 is the encoded SCHC ceiling, and an extra MQTT-SN payload byte below that ceiling is indistinguishable from legitimate payload. The stale test incorrectly bounded reconstructed IPv6. Fix updates link-local and full-address regressions to construct exactly 22,554 encoded bytes and reject encoded max+1; no production limit change. Full python/tests/schc: 346 passed.
close_reason: Wave 1: fix implemented and validated (tests green)

title: Persist Rust SCHC generation-scoped tombstone and admission floors
description: spec/03-adaptation.md §5.6 and draft-lichen-schc-lora-00 require bounded tombstones/floors/hold-down records to persist with authenticated trust/replay state. Rust FragmentationPolicy currently retains receiver tombstones only in RefCell memory; recreating the policy loses terminal high-water and can admit a delayed prior fragment after restart under the same key generation. Add a bounded opaque-generation-bound persistent record/import-export transaction boundary, fail closed on corrupt/colliding/rollback state, and test restart restoration plus retired-generation invalidation.
notes: Implemented signed durable persistence: LICHEN-LINK-TRUST-v1 record serializes local/remote keys, owner-derived durable generation+serial, next serial, replay epoch/window, exact SCHC floor commitment, and anti-rollback revision. Restore creates fresh runtime token after full validation and capacity checks. LICHEN-SCHC-FLOOR-v1 record preserves exact generation/rule/tombstone/outcome/floor, blocks admission if missing, rejects corruption/rollback/revision mismatch, and restores only against committed trust state. Restart/reinstall tests and full gates pass.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-1

title: Node stays RUNNING after terminal receive task failure
description: python/src/lichen/node.py _receive_loop correctly re-raises LinkPersistenceError/LinkSecurityClockError, but Node only probes _receive_task during start() (lines 626-634). A terminal failure occurring after start returns leaves the task completed while state remains RUNNING and the announce/adapter tasks continue; no lifecycle transition or observable failure occurs until a later stop gathers it. Add task supervision/done handling that transitions or shuts down deterministically and preserves the terminal error, with a test injecting failure after RUNNING.
close_reason: Wave 1: fix implemented/verified, tests green

title: Fragmented RPL DIO bypasses authenticated DODAG admission
description: python/src/lichen/node.py only classifies and calls DodagState.process_authenticated_dio() in the unfragmented SCHC branch (lines 832-846). After authenticated SCHC reassembly, the fragment branch proceeds directly to generic IPv6 routing/delivery, so an otherwise valid DIO that exceeds the single-frame ceiling can never install its peer SCHC policy or join/update the DODAG. The generic path may instead deliver/route it as data. Extend the LinkLayer/Node reassembly contract so a fully authenticated fragmented DIO is admitted through the same one-use authenticated DIO validation and policy commit, with tests for valid and malformed fragmented DIOs.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-3

title: SCHC replacement contexts persist duplicate admission-floor keys
description: In python/src/lichen/schc/reassembly.py, _AuthenticatedReassemblyManager.receive() consults an existing durable _floors[key] before processing a newer counter, but it never removes or folds that floor when it admits a new context or creates a rejection tombstone. export_persistence_state() then emits both an active/terminal/rejection row and a floor row for the same (local, signer, generation, Rule ID). restore_persistence_state() deliberately rejects duplicate keys, so after any hold-down has matured to a floor and the peer starts a later transfer (or sends a newer malformed opener), the signed persistence journal becomes unrestorable and the node fails on restart. Consume/fold the prior floor atomically whenever newer state takes ownership (the context/rejection high-water must retain a conservative bound), ensure terminal/expiry transition recreates the maximum floor after hold-down, and add restart round-trip tests for floor -> replacement active, terminal, and rejected states.
close_reason: Verified fixed via wave-4

title: Separate SCHC packet-size limit from reconstructed IPv6 size in Rust
description: The refreshed mqtt_sn_profile_size_exact_maximum vector encodes a valid 22,554-byte SCHC packet that reconstructs to 22,581 IPv6 bytes. Rust codec applies SCHC_FRAG_MAX_PACKET_SIZE/SCHC_MAX_DECOMPRESSED to reconstructed Rule 7 output and rejects it. Align encoded SCHC admission with MAX_PACKET_SIZE=22,554 while bounding reconstructed output by the exact maximum expansion and caller buffer; add boundary tests.
notes:
Fixed Rust SCHC profile-size enforcement on encoded length, not reconstructed IPv6 length. Rule255 and Rule7 exact 22554-byte encoded boundary accepted, +1 rejected; shared vectors and full suite pass.
Rust codec now enforces the separation across all unfragmented decompress paths: ingress/compressor admission stays on encoded length (SCHC_FRAG_MAX_PACKET_SIZE=22554, Rule ID included); rules 0-7 reconstruction is bounded only by the caller buffer (Rule 7 22554->22581, Rule 0 22554->22583, Rule 2 22554->22579 exact-max all accepted). Removed SCHC_MAX_DECOMPRESSED scratch caps in decompress_coap/icmpv6_echo/rpl_dio/rpl_dao via direct caller-buffer assembly + piecewise checksums; split has_oscore_option parser preserves no-mutation-on-error. Two tests pinning the old 1500 reconstruction cap updated to the corrected caller-capacity contract. New boundary regressions for rules 0/2/7/255. No API changes; lichen-link and lichen-node compile. Pre-existing baseline: link_layer_integration fails to compile without --all-features due to lichen-link feature gating (also fails on stashed baseline); passes with --all-features. Authenticated-path 1500 scratch caps filed as follow-up bead project-LICHEN-worker6-buh8.
close_reason: Wave 2: verified fixed at HEAD / completed missing boundary+decode regressions; suites green (schc 1366, link 836, lichen-link 18 targets, lichen-schc 164, vector-security 26).

title: Invalidate SCHC sessions across Rule-Version compatibility transitions
description: Rust FragmentationPolicy refreshes a same-key-generation peer in place. If a DIO changes compatibility from v3 to incompatible and later back to v3, preserving the policy generation and session arrays can make pre-transition fragmentation handles valid again. Rotate the policy generation and clear active/prepared/tombstone state whenever compatibility changes, while preserving live sessions for ordinary compatible same-generation DIO refreshes.
notes: Fixed compatibility flip handle revival: policy generation advances and all active/prepared/tombstone state is invalidated across incompatible/compatible transitions; stale permits remain invalid. SCHC full suite and clippy pass.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-1

title: Python DAO origin validator accepts noncanonical same-IID source aliases
description: DaoOriginValidator.validate() looks up the pinned key by source IID and checks only _pubkey_to_iid(pubkey) == source[8:16]. A signed DAO using fe80::/64 or another prefix with the same IID therefore passes key binding, contrary to the canonical 02xx source contract now enforced by dao_origin_signature vectors and Rust. Require source_address == yggdrasil_address(pubkey) before signature/replay/route mutation, retain IID_MISMATCH as the fail-closed reason, and add exact link-local/cross-prefix negative tests plus vector-to-production coverage.
close_reason: Verified fixed via wave-4

title: SCHC durable floors can alias a new key generation through Python object-id reuse
description: _AuthenticatedReassemblyManager keys generation-scoped state with id(key_generation). Active/tombstone rows retain the token object, but durable _floors retain only the integer ID. After revocation removes the generation mapping and the token is garbage-collected, Python may reuse that ID for a later generation; the stale-floor purge then mistakes the new generation for the old one. Key state by the opaque generation object itself (identity token), retaining it for the floor lifetime, and add a deterministic regression that demonstrates distinct same-pubkey generations never alias.
close_reason: Verified fixed via wave-4

title: DAO origin vectors mark non-key-derived source aliases as accepted
description: Full Rust RPL gate  fails tests/dao_origin_vectors.rs because test/vectors/dao_origin_signature.json and its generator still label fd424c... and link-local DAO sources as accepted for pubkey 207a..., while the hardened production verifier now correctly requires source == ygg_addr_from_pubkey(pubkey) and returns DaoVerifyError::IidMismatch before crypto. The hand-coded D=0 exact-length fixture likewise expects BadSignature after a DODAG mutation but now fails earlier at canonical origin binding. Artifact owner must regenerate canonical key-derived native 02xx source/target/digest/signature literals and update any expected-stage assertions; Rust production must not relax exact identity binding. Evidence: RPL lib 141/141 passes; integration failures are dao_origin_signature_vectors_match_fixed_literals (valid_d1_self_128 Err(IidMismatch)) and exact_lengths_unknown_options_and_d0_scope_reject_before_crypto (expected BadSignature).
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-2

title: AnnounceProcessor mutates gradient before TOFU key acceptance
description: Security review while implementing 4vqc found AnnounceProcessor.process updates gradient_table immediately after signature/IID validation but before checking the IID's pinned TOFU public key and pin-table capacity. A valid attacker key that collides on the 64-bit IID can therefore mutate/insert routing state even though the announce is subsequently rejected as KEY_MISMATCH; a first-seen announce rejected because the pin table is full also leaves a gradient. Complete all trust/admission checks before any routing-state mutation and add negative tests proving rejected announces leave the gradient table unchanged.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-3

title: Node SCHC ingress has no authenticated DIO bootstrap path
description: Correctness review found Node._process_received sends every non-fragment SCHC payload directly to LinkLayer.accept_authenticated_schc_packet(), which requires an already admitted authenticated peer SCHC context. Establishing that context requires accept_authenticated_dio()/accept_authenticated_schc_dio(), but Node never detects RPL DIO packets, owns/configures no DODAG admission context, and has no call path to either API (all current callers are tests or rpl/dodag.py used separately). A fresh Node therefore rejects the first valid DIO for lacking an existing peer policy and can never bootstrap ordinary SCHC data acceptance. Integrate authenticated DIO dispatch/admission into the Node/RPL receive path with configured instance/DODAG/MOP/role, then route ordinary data only after the admitted context; add cold-start tests from first signed DIO through subsequent SCHC data.
notes: Implemented optional all-or-none NodeConfig authenticated RPL admission scope, Node-owned DodagState wired into Router, structural non-consuming DIO classification, existing atomic authenticated DODAG/SCHC policy admission, and cold-start DIO-to-ordinary-data integration regression. Focused combined gate: 281 passed; Ruff, node mypy, diff check clean.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-1

title: SCHC 22,554-byte ceiling is applied to raw IPv6 instead of encoded SCHC packets
description: Correctness review of python/src/lichen/schc/headers.py found validate_full_ipv6 permits a 22,554-byte raw IPv6 packet and encode_rule255 then prepends Rule ID 255, producing a 22,555-byte SCHC Packet that FragmentSender correctly rejects. Conversely compressible packets whose raw IPv6 is slightly above 22,554 but whose encoded SCHC packet is within the 22,554-byte fragmentation ceiling are rejected early. spec/03-adaptation.md §5.6 and the SCHC draft define 22,554 as the SCHC Packet encoding/reassembly ceiling (126*179), with 1,281 explicitly meaning 1-byte Rule ID + 1,280-byte IPv6. Enforce limits on the final encoded/input SCHC packet, make Rule 255's maximum raw IPv6 length 22,553, and add exact max/max+1 tests for Rule 255 and compressed Rule 7/generic rules without conflating raw and compressed sizes.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-3

title: Node never drives SCHC fragmentation retransmission or inactivity timers
description: Correctness review of Node._transmit_peer_schc/_process_received and SchcSessionManager found outbound fragmented sends emit the initial batch and immediately return True, but Node retains no sender handle, schedules no 10-second retransmission timeout, and never calls FragmentSender.timeout(). If All-1 or its ACK is lost, there is no ACK REQ/retry/Sender-Abort and no completion/failure notification; the session only expires opportunistically when a later manager method happens to run. Inbound reassembly likewise has no driven 60-second timer and therefore cannot proactively emit the Receiver-Abort required by spec/03-adaptation.md §5.6. Integrate bounded per-session timers with Node lifecycle/cancellation, handle radio-send failures for repair outputs, drive the four-attempt state machine, emit terminal aborts, and test lost All-1, lost ACK, inactivity, shutdown, and successful completion.
notes: Implemented Node-owned outbound SCHC deadline driver, ACK/repair timer reset, MAX_ACK_REQUESTS exhaustion and Sender-Abort, radio-failure abort, cancellation/shutdown cleanup, plus receive-loop proactive authenticated reassembly expiry abort transmission. Focused combined gate: 281 passed; Ruff, node mypy, diff check clean. Follow-up review beads pm99/mcgs/bz29 fixed but left open for convergence reviews.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-1

title: Node still uses ULA as its primary address and classifies native 02xx peers as external
description: Correctness review of python/src/lichen/node.py found Node.__post_init__ constructs Router(node_address=fd00::/64 + identity.iid) through _build_address and supplies no 0200::/7 mesh prefix. spec/04-network.md §6.1 requires the key-derived native Yggdrasil 02xx address as the sole routable primary, explicitly eliminates ULA, and says local 02xx traffic stays on LoRa. Consequently packets addressed to this node's actual yggdrasil_address are not DELIVER_LOCAL, and other native mesh peers default to EXTERNAL/RPL-parent routing instead of gradient/LOADng mesh routing. Initialize the router with yggdrasil_address(identity.pubkey), classify/configure 0200::/7 as mesh-local, remove the Node ULA helper, and add local-delivery plus isolated-mesh routing tests using key-derived addresses.
notes: Implemented in python/src/lichen/node.py: exact yggdrasil_address primary, 0200::/7 mesh classification, exact native announce gradients; focused/adjacent tests green. Awaiting 3x review; do not close yet.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-1

title: Define a canonical SCHC encoding for multicast RPL DIOs
description: Security/interoperability review found that spec/09-packets-timing.md §13.3 and the packet-format artifact call the canonical ff02::1a RPL DIO 'SCHC Rule 3', while spec/03-adaptation.md, appendix-schc, and both current Rule 3 codecs require both IPv6 endpoints to be fe80::/64 and encode the destination as a 64-bit IID. The authenticated_schc_dio generator therefore emits Rule 255 (consumer security tests explicitly assert link payload 14 ff || IPv6) for ff02::1a. These two purported security oracles describe different signed bytes and size/admission paths for the same parent-selection DIO. Specify whether Rule 3 has a canonical multicast-destination mode/constant or whether multicast DIOs MUST use validated Rule 255, then align the spec walkthrough, byte counts, generator provenance, Python/Rust codecs, and independent signed admission vectors. Ensure the chosen compressed form cannot reconstruct fe80::1a in place of ff02::1a and that destination/scope checks happen before routing-state mutation.
notes: Rust complete: ff02::1a authenticated DIO admission requires SCHC Rule255 and validates destination before DIO/routing admission; Rule3 remains link-local only. Authenticated DIO and shared-vector suites pass.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-1

title: Prevent delayed prior fragments from contaminating replacement SCHC sessions
description: Security review of spec/03-adaptation.md §5.6 and draft-lichen-schc-lora-00 terminal hold-down found that the 60-second tombstone does not fully disambiguate packets when T=0. During hold-down, regular late fragments are discarded without a normative tombstone high-water update; after expiry, any Regular/All-1 with counter greater than the stored high-water may create a session. Once a replacement session is active, there is also no rule requiring every admitted fragment to be newer than an immutable session-admission floor. Because the link replay window accepts unseen out-of-order counters, a delayed authenticated fragment from the prior packet can create or contaminate a replacement context, especially when duplicate retransmissions were allocated after the frame that produced terminal success. Define a safe session-opening/admission barrier (or a bounded lifetime/DTag mechanism) that cannot admit prior-packet fragments, advance the relevant terminal barrier on every authenticated late message, and add state-machine vectors for delayed unique regular/All-1 frames both during hold-down and after a replacement starts.
notes: Rust complete: only regular W=0 FCN=62 opens T=0; every authenticated late message advances terminal high-water; expired tombstone remains durable admission floor; replacement session enforces immutable counter floor. Restart floor persistence is signed, anti-rollback, trust/replay committed, exact-generation gated. Full tests/lints pass.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-1

title: Bind SCHC fragmentation contexts and tombstones to key generation
description: Security review found an identity-domain mismatch across the updated specs. draft-lichen-link-01 §4.3 says both replay and SCHC fragmentation state use (SignerPublicKey, KeyGeneration), but spec/03-adaptation.md §5.6 and draft-lichen-schc-lora-00 §5 key active contexts/tombstones only by local/full remote signer identities plus directional Rule ID. A trust-store generation can change while the same public key/EUI alias is reinstalled, so keying only by public-key identity can let a new generation inherit or collide with retired-generation partial reassembly/tombstone state. Make the opaque current key-generation token an explicit component of remote fragmentation ownership (and local generation where relevant), require current-generation revalidation before mutation/control responses, invalidate retired generations atomically, and add vectors/tests for revoke/reinstall of the same public key.
notes: Rust complete: opaque runtime and durable trust-generation identities propagate from authenticated link evidence through peer authority, permits, active sessions, tombstones, and persisted floors. Same-key revoke/reinstall retires old capability and atomically isolates state. Full link/SCHC/node tests, clippy, fmt, and no-default checks pass.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-1

title: Include mandatory Rule-Version option in RPL DIO packet artifacts
description: Security review of the modified packet-format artifacts found that spec/09-packets-timing.md §13.3, python/src/lichen/packets/formats.py RPL_DIO_FIELDS, test/vectors/packets-formats.json, and generate_packets_timing.py list only DODAG Configuration and Prefix Information options. They omit the exactly-one authenticated Rule-Version option (Type 0x13, Length 1, Version 3) that spec/03-adaptation.md §5.7 requires before a DIO may be used for parent selection or DODAG admission. The helper dio_packet_bytes() also emits a versionless illustrative DIO skeleton, so the current security oracle normalizes a form that production must reject. Update the packet walkthrough/skeleton and independent tests to include or explicitly mark the mandatory 13 01 03 option and assert that the example is parent-selection admissible only with it; keep malformed/absent cases fail-closed.
notes: Rust complete: production DIO parsing/serialization enforces exactly one well-formed Rule-Version option 13 01 03 on canonical 24-byte base; missing/duplicate/malformed/incompatible paths fail before routing mutation. Full RPL/SCHC/node tests pass.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-1

title: Older authenticated DIO capability can roll back peer SCHC policy
description: Security codereview finding in python/src/lichen/link/link_layer.py accept_authenticated_schc_dio(): LinkLayer retains multiple exact AuthenticatedDio issuances, records admitted_counter on the resulting peer context, but never requires a newly selected DIO counter to be greater than the current context's admitted_counter. A delayed caller can accept an older already-replay-accepted DIO after a newer one and replace the current remote_version/key policy; in particular, an old compatible Version 3 capability can undo a later incompatible-version policy and reopen SCHC processing. Reject non-increasing DIO policy admission per signer (and/or revoke superseded issuances) atomically under _security_lock, without invalidating current state on rejection; add out-of-order and exact-reuse regressions across same/different rule versions.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-2

title: Python Node forwards IPv6 without decrementing Hop Limit
description: Security codereview finding in python/src/lichen/node.py: Node._process_received parses a valid IPv6 packet, routes it, recompresses the original ipv6_bytes, and forwards it without decrementing packet.header.hop_limit or dropping Hop Limit 0/1. This violates IPv6 relay semantics and spec/04-network.md 6.3.2, defeats the packet's loop/amplification bound, and allows cyclic routes to recirculate traffic after the bounded relay cache is displaced. Before passive learning/forwarding, reject exhausted Hop Limit and serialize an otherwise identical packet with Hop Limit decremented exactly once; preserve source/payload/checksum semantics and add unicast/multicast boundary regressions for 0, 1, and 2.
close_reason: Wave 1: fix implemented and validated (tests green)

title: Align link draft replay identity with full key generation
description: Cross-document correctness review found draft-lichen-link-01 §4.3/§5 still describes a trust store indexed by peer EUI-64 and a per-peer replay window, with successful verification returning only a peer identity. Updated spec/02-physical-link §4.4 normatively keys replay by (SignerPublicKey, opaque KeyGeneration), forbids SIID/EUI/address aliases as replay keys, and retires generations independently. Revise the draft so SIID only selects a bounded candidate set, verification returns full public key plus current generation token, and replay/fragment state uses that tuple; remove the misleading per-(peer,epoch) wording.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-2

title: Align packet-format vectors with mandatory signer EUI-64 overhead
description: Correctness review found test/vectors/packets-formats.json and generate_packets_timing.py still encode the pre-SIID signed-frame model: complete example says LLSec=0x21, body=76/on-wire=77 and packet-size/link overhead=53; per updated spec/09-packets-timing.md signed short-address frame is LLSec=0xA1 and includes 8-byte SIID, with link security base=61 bytes (and the complete walkthrough correspondingly +8). Per-mode signed overheads are likewise all 8 bytes low. The generator imports these stale values from python/src/lichen/packets/formats.py and the test compares against the same production constants, so it is self-confirming rather than an independent oracle. Update production constants/example, independent generator expectations, artifact, and tests to assert spec literals and mandatory SIID.

title: MIC selector signed vectors omit mandatory signer EUI-64
description: The mic_length_0_signed and mic_length_1_signed cases in test/vectors/mic_length_selector.json still set S without SI and omit signer_eui64 from the signed transcript/wire image. title: Python rejects valid fragmented Rule 255 packets at the single-frame ceiling
description: Security review: LinkLayer.accept_authenticated_schc_fragment validate() special-cases reassembled Rule 255 and calls decode_rule255(... single_frame_limit=MAX_SINGLE_FRAME_SCHC_PACKET=185). The fragmentation profile explicitly supports up to 1281 bytes mandatorily, including a 1280-byte IPv6 datagram plus Rule ID; single-frame ceiling applies only before fragmentation. Consequently valid authenticated fragmented raw IPv6 186..1281 bytes is aborted after full reassembly, enabling deterministic delivery failure and contradicting the profile. Validate complete IPv6 structure and fragmentation receiver limit without applying the unfragmented limit; add an authenticated end-to-end Rule255 fragmented boundary test.
notes: Also affects egress: create_fragment_sender() special-cases Rule 255 with the same 185-byte single-frame limit, so it rejects valid fragmented Rule 255 before session creation. Fix both egress validation and ingress post-reassembly validation.

title: Gateway HAT/serial ingress bypasses link signature and replay verification
description: P1 security review finding. rust/lichen-gateway/src/bin/lichend.rs run_hat_inner(), run_serial(), and run_sim() pass received bytes directly to forward_mesh_to_upstream(); that function calls Gateway::process_rpl() and Gateway::mesh_to_upstream() on the bare buffer. rust/lichen-gateway/src/lib.rs mesh_to_upstream() directly SCHC-decompresses the buffer and emits IPv6 toward the upstream TUN, while process_rpl() parses route-control traffic; neither path calls LinkLayer::receive_frame() nor requires opaque link-auth/replay/destination evidence. A direct SX1302 HAT receive is an on-air payload, so an attacker can inject arbitrary unsigned/spoofed SCHC IPv6 into the TUN (and separately attempt RPL mutation); valid signed LICHEN frames are not parsed at this boundary either. Require exact link-frame parsing, signature/key-pin/generation/replay verification, and destination admission before SCHC/RPL processing, with authenticated evidence threaded through APIs. If a serial transport delegates authentication, define an authenticated envelope carrying peer and replay evidence rather than accepting bare bytes. Add negative tests proving unsigned, bad-signature, replayed, and foreign-destination frames cannot affect TUN output or routing state.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-3

title: lichend treats identity/epoch storage errors and malformed records as first boot
description: P1 security review. Startup uses load_seed(&storage).ok().flatten() and load_epoch(&storage).ok().flatten().unwrap_or(128). Any read/I/O error is discarded; malformed-length records also map to None. Seed failure generates and writes a new identity before later mismatch exit, while epoch failure resets/persists 128. This contradicts fail-closed comments, destroys recovery evidence, and permits replay-state rollback. Distinguish Missing from Corrupt/Unavailable, create state only on confirmed missing first boot, never overwrite failed existing records, and test I/O errors, short/long records, corruption, and rollback.
close_reason: wave-5

title: lichend persists a replay epoch but Gateway ignores it and always starts at epoch 128
description: P1 security review. rust/lichen-gateway/src/bin/lichend.rs loads/increments/saves safe_epoch, but never passes it to Gateway. Gateway::new in gateway.rs hardcodes SecureStack::from_radio(..., 128, 0). Every daemon restart therefore reuses epoch 128 and sequence numbers from zero despite the persisted counter, enabling link tuple/signature replay and causing peers to reject legitimate restarted traffic. Accept the reserved persisted epoch in the production Gateway constructor, fail closed at epoch 255 instead of continuing/reusing it, and add restart tests proving emitted tuples advance and can never repeat.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-2

title: Gateway TOFU pins keys without authenticated proof of possession
description: Security review P1. New TrustStore::verify_tofu in rust/lichen-gateway/src/trust.rs accepts only public key plus claimed IID, verifies deterministic derivation, and immediately returns PinAndAccept/inserts the key. It does not verify a Schnorr signature, OSCORE identity, challenge, or owner-issued authenticated-message capability. An unauthenticated first-contact key claim can pre-pin a gateway identity and block the legitimate key; callers are merely expected to sequence separate helpers correctly. Require proof of possession and message/domain/freshness verification in the atomic pin operation, or accept an opaque verified gateway identity capability; add tests that a derived IID/public key without a valid signed exchange cannot create a pin.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-2

title: Rust gateway provisions a link-local DODAG ID that cannot satisfy root key authority
description: Security review P1. Gateway::new in rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs sets root_addr and DODAG ID to identity_pubkey_link_local. The convergence DIO admission path requires a root-rank signer to bind full ygg_addr_from_pubkey(pubkey) to the DODAG ID, while spec defines root/DODAG identity as primary 02xx. With a link-local DODAG, a legitimate gateway root DIO is classified as Peer then rejected for role mismatch (or mismatches a correctly configured 02xx DODAG), preventing authenticated joins and weakening root identity semantics. Provision gateway root_addr/dodag_id from the full key-derived primary 02xx address and retain a separate link-local control source; add gateway-to-node authenticated DIO admission coverage.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-2

title: Gateway slot conflict resolution accepts replayed claims from other superframes
description: Security review P1. SlotClaim carries superframe_id, but resolve_conflict in rust/lichen-gateway/src/slot.rs never compares the claims' superframe IDs or a current/freshness value. The trust helpers also verify only raw signatures and maintain no claim sequence/timestamp replay state. A captured lower-IID signed claim can be replayed in later superframes and still win/evict current slots, violating spec/08-gateway-coordination.md replay protection. Bind the signed transcript to operation/domain and superframe, require both claims match the current superframe/freshness window, persist per-gateway replay high-water, and add old/future/cross-superframe replay tests.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-2

title: Gateway slot claims expose a forgeable signature_valid authorization bit
description: Security review P1. New rust/lichen-gateway/src/slot.rs represents authentication as public bool SlotClaim.signature_valid and exposes with_valid_signature(), which simply sets it true without a signature, key, TOFU pin, transcript, or verification. resolve_conflict treats that bit as authoritative, so any caller/decoder can forge a lower-IID valid claim and win overlapping slots. Replace the boolean with an opaque verified-claim capability issued only after Schnorr/OSCORE verification and IID binding; keep raw claims separate; test that neither struct construction nor builder calls can bypass verification.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-2

title: Rust gateway DAO route mutation trusts caller-asserted sender IID without link evidence
description: Security review P1. RplStack::complete_dao_from_frame is a public state-mutating API that accepts raw compressed bytes plus a caller-supplied sender_iid, not an AuthenticatedFrame/capability. It passes that assertion into DAO sender authorization and route installation. rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs process_rpl extracts the IID from the unauthenticated decompressed IPv6 source and invokes both handle_border_control_frame and complete_dao_from_frame, so raw SLIP input can choose immediate-sender authority. Require owner-issued current link-authenticated evidence (signature, replay, destination, key generation) for production DAO handling; keep raw parsing test-only; add a test that a signed origin DAO relayed through an unauthenticated/forged immediate sender cannot mutate routes.
close_reason: Verified fixed via wave-4

title: Rust DAO authority accepts and originates noncanonical link-local identity aliases
description: Security review P1. spec/05-routing.md requires the DAO origin IPv6 address to be the signer's full primary 02xx address preserved end to end. SignatureVerifiedDao::verify_signature in rust/lichen-rpl/src/verify.rs checks only origin[8..] against iid_from_pubkey; provisioning validate_origin does the same. The new RplStack control-address split then provisions/signs/transmits DAO using canonical_link_local in provisioning.rs and transmit.rs. Thus arbitrary upper 64-bit aliases sharing the IID are signature-valid, and production emits fe80:: origins. Enforce exact ygg_addr_from_pubkey equality for DAO origin/target authority, retain link-local only for hop control where the signed origin transcript remains primary 02xx, and add rejection plus production-origin vectors.
close_reason: Verified fixed via wave-4

title: Rust authenticated DIO path lets any link peer advance the root-owned DODAG version
description: Security review P1. rust/lichen-rpl/src/dodag.rs process_authenticated_dio authenticates only the immediate link signer. For non-root rank it deliberately selects ExpectedDioRole::Peer, then process_dio adopts any lollipop-newer version and clears parents/rank. No retained root authorization or root-originated version proof is carried/checked, although spec/03-adaptation.md requires the root to originate the version and non-roots to propagate that authenticated value unchanged. A pinned non-root peer can advertise a newer version and force neighbors to reset/partition; adoption even occurs before an unusable candidate is rejected. Bind accepted version transitions to root-issued evidence preserved end-to-end, prevent peers from minting versions, and test malicious signed non-root version advances including unusable ranks.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-2

title: TDMA 250 ms slot cannot contain the profile own SF10 airtime and guard is contradictory
description: Correctness review: spec/09-packets-timing.md:630-632 says slot duration is airtime+50ms guard and gives SF10/125kHz approximately 250ms. packets-timing.json airtime vectors show even 17 bytes takes 329.727ms and a 77-byte link packet takes 821.248ms, yet tdma_slot_constants at lines 860-864 fixes slot_ms=250 and guard_ms=50. The FSM table at spec line 671 separately says Guard 100ms. A 250ms slot necessarily overlaps for the stated PHY/frame examples. Define one guard and derive/configure slot length from the maximum permitted airtime for its DR, then regenerate vectors.
close_reason: wave-5

title: EU868 duty-cycle oracle uses 200 ms while same artifact computes 369.664 ms
description: Correctness review: spec/09-packets-timing.md:141-149 and packets-timing.json duty_cycle_eu868_10pct use 200 ms for a 60-byte SF9/125kHz frame and derive 1800 packets/hour at 10%. The same generated artifact airtime_sf9_60b independently applies the stated LoRa parameters and yields 369.664 ms (packets-timing.json around lines 150-158), giving floor(360 seconds / 0.369664) = 973 whole packets/hour, not 1800. generate_packets_timing.py uses a hard-coded timing constant for one vector and computed airtime for the other. Use one explicit complete PHY parameter set and derive duty capacity from the same independent formula.
close_reason: Wave 1: fix implemented and validated (tests green)

title: Timing wrong-signer vector expects BAD_SIGNATURE for a valid signature
description: Correctness review: generate_packets_timing.py builds signed-wrong-signer by signing canonical_payload with wrong_identity and publishes that identity as signer_pubkey_hex (around lines 388-397); packets-timing.json:488-494 nevertheless expects link_receive/BAD_SIGNATURE. python/tests/test_protocol_vector_security.py:114-132 independently verifies every timing wire against its published signer key, so this signature is demonstrably valid. Because the IPv6 source IID belongs to remote_identity, the proper failure is source_signer_mismatch after cryptographic authentication if wrong_identity is trusted, or an unknown/untrusted-signer error if it is not. Regenerate with the intended trust setup and assert the exact valid rejection stage/cause.

title: Packets/timing examples use obsolete SCHC and impossible layer sizes
description: Correctness review: spec/09-packets-timing.md:29-42 says Rule 0 is only RuleID+ports+two CoAP bytes and totals 21 bytes including a 17-byte payload, contradicting the canonical 23-byte fixed Rule-0 header before token/options/payload in spec/03-adaptation.md:54-55 and appendix-schc.md:12. Lines 45-54 build a 77-byte link frame, then lines 57-62 call its LoRa PHY payload 60 bytes. Section 13.3 lines 87-89 also labels an RPL DIO as SCHC Rule 2 even though canonical DIO is Rule 3. Rewrite the worked example with bit-exact current bytes and reconcile all layer totals.

title: Non-root RPL vector silently inserts local SCHC version
description: Correctness review: test/vectors/rpl_messages.json:26-31 describes a non-root parent DIO propagating the root version unchanged, but sets schc_version_mode=insert_current with options_hex empty. Its generator repeats that at test/vectors/generate.py:2507-2513. spec/03-adaptation.md:359-369 requires a non-root parent-selectable serializer to require the authenticated root-originated value and MUST NOT silently substitute current local version. rule_versioning.json admission_policy_vectors independently encodes that requirement. Make this vector provide explicit root provenance/propagation input and assert no-current-substitution; python/tests/test_protocol_vector_security.py currently checks only its DODAGID.

title: Rule 255 minimal IPv6 vectors carry an absent ICMPv6 header
description: Correctness review: test/vectors/rule_versioning.json:228-237 and test/vectors/schc_adaptation.json:68-76 label 6000000000003a40... as a valid minimal IPv6 packet. Payload Length is zero but Next Header is 58 (ICMPv6), so the declared upper-layer header is completely absent; a truly header-only IPv6 packet must use No Next Header (59/0x3b). spec/03-adaptation.md:389-393 requires Rule 255 payload to be a complete structurally valid IPv6 packet. Current security consumer does not validate these packets. Change the vectors to NH=59 or provide a complete ICMPv6 message, and add independent IPv6/next-header structural assertions.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-2

title: SCHC ACK bitmap vectors set the wrong tile bits
description: Correctness review: spec/drafts/draft-lichen-schc-lora-00.md:462-479 defines a 63-bit bitmap ordered FCN62..FCN0 with the All-1 final tile at the rightmost position; unassigned short-window positions must be zero; compression removes the maximal trailing run of ones. test/vectors/schc_adaptation.json:609-635 (frag_ack_bitmap_single_missing) declares assigned FCNs 62,61,All-1 with bits received,missing,received but wire 78 28 00... decodes after W/C as bitmap prefix 101, marking FCN60 received instead of placing All-1 at the right edge. Normatively the retained bitmap begins 10 then zeros (78 20 00... after removing the one trailing All-1 bit). The multiple-missing wire is likewise not derived from its stated bitmap. python/tests/test_protocol_vector_security.py never decodes these wire fields, so 12/12 passes. Regenerate both from an independent bit packer and assert exact decode/compression semantics.
close_reason: Wave 2: verified fixed at HEAD / completed missing boundary+decode regressions; suites green (schc 1366, link 836, lichen-link 18 targets, lichen-schc 164, vector-security 26).

title: Canonical SCHC Rule 2/3/4 fixed-size vectors contradict their own bit arithmetic and specs
description: Correctness review: test/vectors/schc_adaptation.json:340-375 has stale/incorrect fixed-size oracles. Rule 2 says 3 bytes, stores expected≈21, but its listed fields sum to 176 bits =22 residue bytes + Rule ID =23. Rule 3 says 8 bytes and expected≈37, while its own 312-bit sum is 39 residue bytes + Rule ID =40, matching spec/03-adaptation.md:55-58 and appendix-schc.md:14. Rule 4 says 6 bytes and expected≈35, while 288 bits is 36 residue bytes + Rule ID =37, matching the same specs. spec/appendix-schc.md:12 independently and incorrectly calls Rule 2 3 bytes, while draft-lichen-schc-lora-00.md:218-238 lists the address/IID fields and calls it ~20-byte residue. Replace approximate/stale fields with exact 23/40/37-byte canonical oracles and add independent sum assertions in python/tests/test_protocol_vector_security.py.

Running the documented single-file command overwrites and deletes 27 security/interoperability vectors. title: Mandatory Signer IID reduces SCHC authenticated tile ceiling from 187 to 179 bytes
description: The SCHC profile derives TILE_SIZE=187 from a 255-byte signed Extended-unicast frame while omitting the mandatory 8-byte SIID field. With LENGTH max254, fixed body is LLSec/EPO/SEQ 4 + DST8 + SIID8 + Schnorr48 =68, leaving 186 L2 payload bytes; dispatch leaves a 185-byte fragment envelope. Final header15 + RCS32 + one padding bit consumes 6 bytes, so the fixed tile maximum is 179, and the two-window packet ceiling is 126*179=22,554 bytes. Update specs, Python/Rust constants/code/tests/vectors and all max-frame arithmetic; keep C/Zephyr untouched this session.
notes: Correctness reviewer found Rule255 vector limits also stale. Exact signed Extended+SIID budget: L2 payload 186, dispatch 1, Rule255 ID 1, so raw IPv6 max is 184 and SCHC packet limit is 185. Update rule255_fallback_max_single_frame and rule255_no_fragmentation plus consumers.

title: Python and signed vector families violate mandatory Signer IID framing
description: draft-lichen-link-01 §§3.2-4.1 requires S=1 iff SI=1 and an 8-byte signer EUI-64 covered by the signature. Python LichenFrame still treats bit7 as reserved and every signed link_frame/authenticated_schc_dio/packets-timing generator emits LLSec 0x20 without SIID. Implement mandatory SIID parsing/serialization and link signing/verification in Python, derive the wire signer EUI-64 from the authenticated signer identity, regenerate all signed vector families independently, and make independent/Python/Rust consumers reject S/SI mismatches. C is explicitly out of scope this session.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-3

title: Rule 7 compressor drops address-policy nonmatches instead of falling back
description: spec/03-adaptation requires a well-formed packet that fails only a Rule 7 address matching requirement to use another rule or Rule 255. MqttSnProfile.compress_if_matching currently raises for every address-policy failure. Return None for Rule 7 address nonmatches while retaining decoder rejection and generic IPv6 structural validation; cover direct profile and compress_packet behavior.
notes: Implemented: compressor treats Rule 7 address-policy failures as nonmatches (None), decoder rejects invalid residues, vector consumer verifies Rule 255 fallback for otherwise structurally valid invalid-policy packets. Focused gates green; independent review pending.

title: Python TOFU capacity can evict peers with active fragmentation state
description: LinkLayer.receive chooses a full-pin-table victim solely by transient _generation_leases. Long-lived SchcSessionManager sender/tombstone and authenticated reassembly context/tombstone lifetimes do not hold those leases, so a 65th authenticated peer can evict a peer with an active or hold-down-protected fragmentation tuple. That violates the spec's no-active-context eviction rule and can abort/cross-contaminate transfers. Pin eviction eligibility must also exclude any signer occupied in sender/reassembly sessions, tombstones, rejections, pending verified controls/DIO transaction state; reject atomically if no safe victim. Add active inbound/outbound/tombstone saturation and post-expiry admission tests.
close_reason: Verified fixed via wave-4

title: Python Node delivers signed frames addressed to other nodes
description: LinkLayer.receive authenticates and returns any known peer's signed frame without destination filtering. Node._process_received immediately delivers non-SCHC/non-fragment payloads to on_receive, so an Extended unicast addressed to another node is accepted locally; SCHC single-frame and other paths also rely on later partial checks. Rust filters wire_is_for_local before admission. Add one canonical local-target gate covering NONE broadcast, Extended EUI-64, configured SHORT, and ELIDED IPv6 destination before application/routing mutation; wrong-target frames must not deliver, allocate protocol state, or emit responses. Add multi-node overhearing tests for raw, single-frame SCHC, RPL, and fragments.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-3

title: Python fragmentation targets IID while Rust and link draft require Extended EUI-64
description: Python Node sends authenticated SCHC fragments/controls to peer.iid and Link accepts Extended DST == identity.iid. Rust Link/SCHC/node consistently compares Extended DST to local_eui64 (IID with RFC4291 U/L bit flipped), and draft-lichen-link-01 defines Extended as an EUI-64. Cross-language peers therefore reject every exact-target fragment/control despite correct signatures. Make Extended wire destination canonical EUI-64 in spec/02 and Python Link/Node, derive it explicitly from key-derived IID, keep trust maps keyed by IID/full key as appropriate, and add Python↔Rust address/overhear/control vectors/tests.

description: spec/02-physical-link.md keys replay acceptance only by IID and does not require signature verification before replay-state mutation, despite unsigned frames and spec/03 requiring full verified signer identity/generation plus authenticate-before-context-mutation. Define replay domain as full authenticated signer/key generation (with address only as routing metadata), verification before mutation, atomic persistence, and old-generation invalidation; align replay vectors with unsigned poisoning, alias, rotation, and rollback cases.

description: spec/03-adaptation.md and draft-lichen-schc-lora-00.md reserve 0x78 for canonical A-to-B and 0x79 for B-to-A but never define how authenticated peers deterministically become A or B. Python Link/Node sender APIs default to 0x78, which makes simultaneous transfers share the same data/control Rule ID and caused ACK-REQ ambiguity. Define canonical endpoint ordering from authenticated full signer identities (with exact treatment of local vs remote), derive the outbound rule rather than silently defaulting in production, require inbound rule direction to match, and add both-direction/simultaneous/mismatched-rule vectors and tests across Python/Rust consumers.

title: Python authenticated fragmentation uses broadcast instead of exact peer target
description: Node._transmit_peer_schc and reassembly response paths call LinkLayer.send(fragment/control) with default AddrMode.NONE and empty destination; _AuthenticatedReassemblyManager._local_target accepts that broadcast as local. Every node that pins the signer and has a compatible policy can allocate/mutate a distinct (its_local, signer, rule) session and emit broadcast ACK/abort, defeating exact hop-by-hop endpoint binding and diverging from Rust's Extended-unicast control requirement. Send fragments and controls to the peer's authenticated IID with AddrMode.EXTENDED and reject NONE/SHORT for authenticated fragmentation. Add overhearing/multi-node/wrong-target/response-target tests.
notes: Robustness acceptance: ACK/abort responses must also use Priority.ACK and the bounded control deadline rather than default BULK/120s, while data fragments retain the intended data priority.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-3

title: Rust fragmentation tombstones omit terminal replay state and cached response
description: FragmentationPolicy terminal tombstones store only one rule/deadline per direction. They omit session high-water counter, terminal outcome, and cached final ACK/abort; repeated newer terminal traffic cannot receive idempotent response, post-hold-down allocation does not require counter above prior session, and alternating rule IDs overwrite live tombstones. Persist bounded per-rule terminal state/outcome/response/high-water and enforce replay-safe hold-down/reuse with shared vectors.
close_reason: Verified fixed via wave-4

title: Rust exposes unauthenticated production RPL mutation APIs
description: RplStack::rpl_node_mut exposes RplNode, RplNode::router_mut exposes Router, and public Router process_dio/process_dio_outcome/process_dio_with_etx variants mutate neighbors/DODAG without AuthenticatedFrame. RplNode handle_frame_rpl variants likewise trust caller bytes/IID. Downstream production code can bypass process_authenticated_dio entirely. Seal raw parsers/mutators as crate-private/test/simulator APIs or require owner-issued evidence in the public production surface; add compile-fail/API tests and end-to-end bypass tests.
close_reason: Verified fixed via wave-4

title: Rust no_std peer authority accepts regressed or foreign receipt clocks
description: PeerContextAuthority entries track only signer/counter/generation; issue_verified accepts arbitrary receipt_clock_domain and receipt_ticks and does not enforce a stable domain or nondecreasing ticks for a signer. FragmentationPolicy uses those ticks to create/expire T=0 hold-down tombstones, so a higher replay counter with regressed/foreign time can shorten or bypass hold-down in no_std while std Link clocks reject it. Bind authority issuance to a ReceiptClock domain/high-water and reject regression/domain substitution; add std/no_std parity tests.
notes: ReceiptEvidence tick units are receiver-defined and receive_frame() advances one logical tick per frame, yet fragmentation hardcodes FRAGMENT_TOMBSTONE_TICKS=60000 as if ticks were milliseconds. No_std authority must bind a defined time unit/clock and convert the normative 60 seconds correctly.
close_reason: wave-10

title: Rust re-adding an unchanged peer resets its replay window
description: rust/lichen-link LinkLayer.add_peer always replaces the tracked entry and calls replay.reset_peer on the replaced public key, even when IID and public key are unchanged. Production announcement handling calls add_peer for accepted peers, so a signed announcement/data frame can advance replay state, trigger same-key re-add, erase that state, and then be replay-accepted. Preserve generation/replay/pin state for idempotent same-key refresh; only atomic authenticated key replacement may retire/reset state. Add exact replay-after-reannounce and retained-evidence liveness tests.
close_reason: Wave 2: verified fixed at HEAD / completed missing boundary+decode regressions; suites green (schc 1366, link 836, lichen-link 18 targets, lichen-schc 164, vector-security 26).

title: Python production DODAG admits peer-asserted root and unbound source IID
description: The signed authenticated SCHC DIO vector consumer manually enforces IPv6 source IID == signer IID and root DODAGID == AddrForKey(root signer), but production DodagState.process_authenticated_dio does not. Link issuance expected_role='root' only checks rank 256, so any pinned peer can sign a rank-256 DIO for a victim DODAGID; source/signature identity is likewise not bound in production. Move both checks into owner-issued production authenticated-DIO admission and add root/peer impersonation, wrong-source, rekey, and vector-backed tests.
close_reason: Verified fixed via wave-4

title: Rust FragmentSender accepts unauthenticated ACK and abort controls
description: rust/lichen-schc FragmentSender.handle_ack_bytes accepts raw bytes with no AuthenticatedFrame/Link evidence and can mark an authenticated transfer succeeded/aborted or trigger retransmission. Policy-at-construction does not authenticate ongoing controls. Require exact current Link-owned signer/local-target/generation/replay evidence for ACK/Receiver-Abort, bind it to the active session/window, and reject raw/foreign/replayed/stale controls without mutation. Add authenticated production integration and shared vectors.
notes:
Final correctness review: handle_ack_bytes() and handle_ack(Ack) remain public and mutate authenticated sender state without Link evidence. Production wrappers do not prevent callers from bypassing them. Make raw parser/state transition private or separate an unprivileged codec type that cannot own an authenticated session.
Independent security review confirms public handle_ack_bytes/handle_ack can terminate or retransmit an authenticated session from unauthenticated bytes; raw state ownership must be unreachable from production callers.
close_reason: Verified fixed via wave-4

title: Rust permits concurrent indistinguishable T=0 fragmentation senders
description: FragmentationPolicy tracks only peer generation/counter/version and FragmentSender::new consumes no active-session reservation. Multiple senders for the same authenticated local identity, remote signer, direction, and Rule 0x78 can be constructed and started simultaneously; with T=0 their interleaved fragments are indistinguishable. Add bounded atomic session reservation/release keyed by local/remote/direction/rule, terminal hold-down, cancellation/drop behavior, and concurrent construction/start tests.
close_reason: wave-11

title: SCHC fragmentation retry vector no longer matches canonical schema
description: test/vectors/schc_fragmentation.json sender retry exhaustion now uses attempts_before=4, new timing/bitmap/trigger_event/pre_exhaustion fields, and no legacy trigger, while schema.json keeps additionalProperties=false, attempts_before const 2, lacks new fields, and requires trigger. Update the schema with correct sender/receiver conditionals after the concurrent schema syntax/coverage work lands, then run full Draft7 validation and all Python/Rust vector consumers.

Old (const 2 + trigger) and new (attempts_before=4) entries both validate; mixed shapes fail closed. schc_fragmentation.json validates, python test_vectors.py + rust lichen-schc fragmentation_vectors/reassembly_state_machine green.

title: Concurrent Link persistence writers can fork one accepted revision
description: Python LinkLayer writes the signed state slot and internal digest anchor before advancing the independent revision CAS. Two instances loaded at revision 1 can both write divergent revision 2; winner A advances external CAS, stale B overwrites the shared revision-2 slot/anchor then loses CAS and disables. Restart sees external revision 2 and accepts B's state, losing A's replay floor. Add exclusive persistence ownership or a recoverable prepare/commit protocol atomically binding revision and digest so losers cannot overwrite committed state. Test divergent replay/session/pin state and all interleavings; restart must retain the CAS winner and reject same-revision forks.
close_reason: wave-9

title: Python SCHC receiver remains unauthenticated and absent from production Node
description: python/schc/reassembly.py accepts raw caller-keyed bytes with no Link RxFrame evidence, signer/local-identity/generation/replay binding, terminal tombstone/hold-down, or authenticated idempotent response. It can allocate/mutate state and emit aborts from unauthenticated input, contradicting the strengthened fragmentation spec. Node routes Rule 0x78/0x79 through generic decompression failure, so production cannot receive fragmented SCHC. Integrate Link-owned authenticated receiver sessions into Node with bounded state, replay/rekey/reboot/abort behavior and shared interop vectors; unauthenticated input must be silent.
notes: Independent correctness rereview findings: version transitions invalidated senders but retained receiver partials/tombstones; stale/unsolicited ACKs fell into receiver parsing and emitted aborts; capacity rejection could emit repeated aborts without bounded hold-down. Fixed with exact regressions; retain in final review scope.

title: Python FragmentSender cannot consume authenticated abort controls
description: SchcSessionManager.record_verified_frame parses every authenticated response as Ack, so canonical Sender-Abort 78fe and Receiver-Abort 78ffff never become pending evidence; transition_ack has no abort branch. An active FragmentSender cannot stop timers, release state, report failure, or enter terminal hold-down on an authenticated peer abort as required by the spec. Add typed authenticated control admission and terminal transitions for aborts with signer/target/generation/replay binding, plus forged/wrong-session/duplicate/timeout race tests and shared vectors.
notes: Independent rereview found stale/unsolicited canonical ACK could fall through into reassembly and elicit Receiver-Abort instead of silent discard. Fixed with regression.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-1

title: Rust production DIO admission lets peers self-assert root role
description: rust/lichen-node/src/rpl_stack/receive.rs derives ExpectedDioRole from the received DIO's own rank, and codec validation merely confirms that self-derived role. AuthenticatedPeerSchcContext binds source IID to signer but does not require a root-rank DODAGID to equal AddrForKey(root signer). Any authenticated non-root peer can claim rank 256 for the configured DODAG and pass admission. Supply trusted expected role/root identity from local DODAG policy, enforce key-derived DODAG root binding, consume root_authorization.json in Rust, and add peer-root impersonation/rekey tests.

title: Rust authenticated fragmentation API is unavailable in no_std builds
description: The auth-policy change gates the only public FragmentSender::new, FragmentationPolicy::accept_peer, and production AuthenticatedPeerSchcContext issuance behind feature=std; new_unchecked is private. lichen-schc therefore compiles no_std only because outbound authenticated fragmentation is dead/unconstructible, violating the embedded-default contract. Design a no_std-capable Link evidence/policy interface without weakening issuance or revocation, expose usable sender construction, and add no-default compile/API tests plus behavioral parity with std.

title: Modified Rust RPL source breaks default no_std build

title: Rust FragmentReceiver accepts unauthenticated bytes outside Link policy
description: rust/lichen-schc/src/fragment.rs FragmentReceiver remains a bare byte/Fragment state machine with no LinkLayer AuthenticatedFrame evidence, current authenticated peer permit, (local identity, remote signer, Rule ID) session key, replay counter binding, or tombstone. Unauthenticated bytes can allocate/reset/abort receive state and produce responses, contradicting the authenticated fragmentation requirements in spec/03-adaptation.md. Gate all production receiver transitions on exact current Link-owned evidence and bounded session ownership, with replay/rekey/reboot/foreign-signer/wrong-target tests and shared vectors.

title: Public FragmentSender can emit wire fragments without LinkLayer policy
description: python/src/lichen/schc/fragment.py exposes public FragmentSender(payload).all_fragments()/fragment builders that produce sendable wire fragments without LinkLayer.create_fragment_sender, authenticated peer Rule-version context, session ownership, or one-active-session enforcement. LinkLayer.send accepts the resulting payload. Seal wire emission behind a LinkLayer/SchcSessionManager-issued capability while preserving safe diagnostics, and add tests proving raw construction cannot emit/send policy-bypassing fragments.
notes:
Independent correctness rereview finding: a caller could wrap raw fragment bytes in the SCHC L2 dispatch and bypass _IssuedFragmentWire sealing; origin/forward large packets also dropped instead of routing through Link-issued fragmentation. Fixed with exact regressions; retain in final review scope.
Latest rereview finding: Node large-packet setup failure can abandon a prepared FragmentSender reservation/capability. Ensure every setup/send exception or rejection discards/cancels the prepared sender without freeing a replacement, with regression.
