title: Public ReplayProtector mutation APIs can roll back live Link replay floors
description: LinkLayer exposes a public replay_protector whose reset(), import_state(), and rotate() methods remain callable after activation. import_state can replace a newer live high-water floor with an older exported state; reset/rotate delete peer state outside the Link rekey transaction. A later Link save can sign that semantic rollback at a higher persistence revision. Make replay state mutation Link-owned and lifecycle sealed: one restore before activation, monotonic/non-lowering merge only, and rotation/admin recovery only through an atomic trust transition. Expose at most a read-only facade. Add tests for import/reset/rotate after receive and active SCHC pin, and prove persistence cannot bless lowered floors.
notes: Implementation integration failure: after claiming replay ownership, LinkLayer.receive still called the public check_and_update API and raised 'live replay state is owned by LinkLayer' on every valid frame. All Link-internal replay calls must use the owner capability/internal path; add a valid signed receive regression.
close_reason: wave-5

title: Provision persistence post-write failure leaves live stale verifier state
description: ProvisionVerifier persists install/clear state before post-hook reentry/mutation checks and in-memory commit. If a callback durably writes and then reenters, mutates, or raises, the method errors but the running verifier continues serving the old active metadata/floor while durable storage contains the new record or clear. This split brain can keep a lower epoch floor or active time after durable revocation. Introduce transactional persistence semantics or irreversibly poison/clear the verifier after any exception once persistence was invoked, so no stale floor/time reads proceed until authoritative reload. Add durable-store tests for write-then-reenter, mutate, and raise on install and clear, plus tracker invalidation/restart agreement.
close_reason: wave-10

title: Failed Python rekey can erase replay floor while retaining old trust
description: LinkLayer._rotate_remote_unlocked rotates ReplayProtector state before SchcSessionManager.rotate_remote; the latter can raise (for example generation exhaustion). On failure the old key remains pinned/trusted while its replay window and high-water floor have been deleted, allowing previously accepted signed frames to replay. Make rekey a true preflighted/transactional commit across replay state, SCHC sessions, pins, generations, and persistence, or permanently fail closed after any partial mutation. Add injected failure-boundary tests proving either complete old state preservation or complete new-state commit, never trusted old identity with a lowered replay floor.
close_reason: wave-5

title: Link receive rereads mutable peer identity after signature verification
description: python/src/lichen/link/link_layer.py _find_sender verifies candidate.pubkey then returns the callback-owned object; receive later rereads sender.pubkey/iid for pinning, replay, and RxFrame construction. Stateful properties or concurrent forced mutation can substitute an unverified identity after the signature check. Snapshot one exact 32-byte bytes pubkey, canonicalize to a detached PeerIdentity before verification, and use only that canonical value throughout; apply the same discipline to self/rekey/local identity candidates. Add stateful-candidate, concurrent-mutation, malformed type/length, pin/replay/RxFrame binding tests.
close_reason: wave-6

title: Production Python Node bypasses authenticated SCHC Rule-version policy
description: python/src/lichen/node.py ingress uses global decompress_packet() and records success without a LinkLayer-owned AuthenticatedPeerSchcContext; egress compresses before resolving next hop and discards _next_hop, so no peer version can be enforced. A signed peer with no version DIO or an incompatible v2 policy can deliver Rule 0/7, and the Node emits Rule 0/7 to incompatible/unadvertised peers. Require atomic current-generation per-signer policy for production ingress and resolved-next-hop egress; allow only bounded canonical Rule255 mismatch signaling. Add tests for missing DIO, v2 mismatch Rule0/7, Rule255, v3, rekey/stale races, and executable shared vectors.
notes: Independent rereview found originated/forwarded packets above the single-frame limit were dropped instead of using Link-issued fragmentation. Fixed with production helper regression.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD via batch-verify wave-1

title: Link elevation callbacks and StratumTracker use inverted locks
description: Python StratumTracker status/current/adopt paths hold the tracker RLock and then call DioTimeVerifier._with_live_generation(), which waits for LinkLayer._security_lock. Public LinkLayer elevation methods invoke synchronous user callbacks while holding _security_lock; such a callback may call tracker.status/current_time and wait for the tracker lock. Concurrent execution creates tracker->link versus link->tracker ABBA deadlock. Redesign lock ordering/transaction boundaries without losing generation linearizability and add deterministic cross-thread regression tests for authenticated-DIO, verified-receipt, and time-generation callbacks.
notes: Final rereview found remaining lease-level ABBA despite releasing _security_lock before callbacks: thread A holds StratumTracker.__lock and waits for a foreign signer generation lease; thread B owns that lease and its public elevation callback waits for the tracker lock, so neither can release. Fix callback/lease/tracker ordering and add deterministic two-thread regression for time-generation and authenticated-DIO elevation.
close_reason: wave-7

title: Fail-closed persistence disable leaves cached SCHC and time capabilities live
description: Python LinkLayer fatal persistence failure clears receipts, authenticated DIO issuances, and the SCHC session manager, but leaves _schc_peer_contexts, _schc_peer_context_issuances, and _key_generations live. _validated_authenticated_peer_schc_context(), accepts_time_generation(), and elevate_time_generation() do not enforce persistence health. A previously issued peer SCHC context or time-generation capability can remain usable after the LinkLayer marks itself permanently disabled. Fix all cached authority revocation paths and add regression tests covering SCHC compression/decompression/session creation and time-generation acceptance/elevation after a persistence write failure.
close_reason: wave-7

title: Rejected scheduled awaitable hooks remain live and mutate state after failure
description: Fresh final timing security review: _reject_awaitable and LinkLayer elevation guards close coroutine objects but do not cancel asyncio.Task/Future or other scheduled awaitables. A synchronous persistence hook can return asyncio.create_task(later_persist(state)); ProvisionVerifier.install raises TypeError, then the task runs on the next loop turn and durably advances rejected state. Use one common rejection helper that synchronously cancels Future/Task, closes coroutine/custom-closeable awaitables, and verifies termination where possible before failing closed. Add scheduled Task/Future/custom awaitable tests for provision persist/clear, MonotonicClock, verified receipt, authenticated DIO, and time-generation callbacks.
close_reason: The common rejection helper demanded by the bead already exists (lichen/_sync_callbacks.py reject_awaitable_result: synchronously cancels Future/Task, closes coroutine/custom closeables, raises TypeError) and all five callback surfaces are wired through it (provisioning _call_transition_hook->_call_sync, MonotonicClock, receipt elevation, DIO elevation, time-generation). What was missing was surface-level scheduled-awaitable tests. Implemented the persist/clear slice (the bead's named attack): 6 new parametrized tests in tests/timing/test_time_sync.py covering Task/Future/custom for provision persist and clear hooks — TypeError raised, task/future cancelled + body never runs, custom closed exactly once, fail-closed poison state asserted (clear: cleared True + metadata rejected by design of _poison_after_persistence_failure). 907 timing+sync-callbacks tests pass; ruff/mypy clean. Remaining surfaces (MonotonicClock, verified receipt, authenticated DIO, time-generation) decomposed into 4 child beads; 7 review findings filed as beads (1 P1, 1 P2, 2 P3, 3 P4) via discovered-from links.

title: LinkLayer receipt clock can self-assert and retain a forged trusted timing domain
description: Fresh final timing security review: LinkLayer.__post_init__ accepts an arbitrary receipt_clock callable plus caller-supplied receipt_clock_domain, so an attacker can pair lambda:0 with a trusted MonotonicClock.domain_identity and pass DioTimeVerifier domain checks. LinkLayer is also a mutable dataclass: object.__setattr__(link, _receipt_clock, attacker_callable) rebinds timestamps while _clock_domain remains trusted, and newly authenticated DIO time samples use attacker-selected observation times. Require an exact immutable MonotonicClock-like capability owned as one binding, derive domain only from it, reject self-asserted overrides/bare mismatched callables, and detect/fail closed on rebinding. Add construction, post-construction, active tracker, mutation race, and legitimate fake-clock tests.
close_reason: stale-check verified fixed

title: Provision epoch floor reads caller metadata after validation and accepts concurrent mutation
description: Fresh final timing correctness review: ProvisionVerifier._with_floor_snapshot passes caller-visible __current metadata into evaluate_epoch_floor. accepts() validates its stored snapshot, but evaluation then rereads metadata.epoch/content; a concurrent object.__setattr__ after the final accepts check can change the authoritative floor. Deterministic proof changed FLOOR+10 to FLOOR+999 and EpochFloorAuthority.current returned the forged value while subsequent verifier.accepts was false. Keep an internal detached primitive current-record snapshot distinct from the facade, or atomically capture validated primitives under the verifier lock and evaluate only that copy. Add forced mutation of epoch/version/digest/generation around floor current/adopt/status/policy transitions.
notes: Fresh final correctness rereview finds the public free functions evaluate_epoch_floor/effective_epoch_floor still bypass the repaired verifier-owned primitive transaction: they accept a duck-typed fake accepts() capability and reread facade metadata outside the verifier lock. Deterministic concurrent install returned stale F+100 after live floor advanced to F+500. Restrict authoritative evaluation to exact ProvisionVerifier transactional primitives (or make free functions explicitly non-authoritative diagnostics unable to influence EpochFloorAuthority); test fake verifier, concurrent install/clear, facade mutation, and monotonic floor.
close_reason: verified fixed (recovered from workflow journals)

title: Concurrent TimeSample mutation can win after authority validation and before adoption
description: Fresh final timing correctness review: StratumTracker validates the caller-visible TimeSample via authority.accepts/_claim, then continues reading that same frozen-by-convention facade through option comparison, _rejection, projection, and adoption. Another thread using object.__setattr__ can mutate source_valid or other fields after the final accepts check and before use, producing a validate/use TOCTOU. Make the authority atomically consume and return a detached internal snapshot under its lock, and perform all tracker logic only on that snapshot. Add forced-barrier mutation of every security-relevant sample/evidence field before/after claim and prove rejection or authenticated original semantics.
close_reason: wave-7

title: DIO option-mismatch rejection fails to consume network replay high-water
description: Fresh final timing correctness review: StratumTracker._adopt_locked checks caller DioTimeOption equality before advancing the authenticated network replay high-water. A sample rejected with a mismatched option consumes only that sample issuance; DioTimeVerifier can reissue from the same sealed authenticated DIO/counter, and a later matching option is then adopted. Advance signer/generation/counter consideration barriers before every semantic rejection, including option mismatch, or make DIO-to-time issuance one-use. Test mismatch→reverify same counter, mismatch→fresh higher counter, repeated verify, and no regression of direct evidence.
close_reason: Re-close (prior close lost in a store race): verified already implemented. Barrier-advance fix landed in the 660b9bf3bf lineage: _adopt_locked advances the per-authority issuance barrier (stratum.py:612) and network replay high-water (626-632) before every semantic rejection including DioTimeOption mismatch (633-636) - one-use per sealed DIO/counter. All four prescribed scenarios pinned and green (test_option_mismatch_rejection_consumes_network_replay_high_water, test_repeated_dio_time_verify_same_counter_rejected incl. direct-evidence no-regression; pinned by 32e7dd55a9). Full timing suite 73/73 on heft. 3x delegated codereview: correctness PASS, edge-cases PASS, security filed 8c0b (P2, open).

title: StratumTracker clear does not invalidate pre-clear network time samples
description: Fresh final timing correctness review: StratumTracker._clear_locked advances direct-provider issuance barriers but does not invalidate or barrier unconsidered DioTimeVerifier network samples. A valid network sample issued before clear can be adopted afterward and silently re-establish wall clock, defeating source invalidation. Clear must advance a per-authority issuance barrier or revoke all outstanding network samples while preserving replay/key-generation high-water state. Test pre-clear issued sample after clear, pre-clear rejected sample, fresh post-clear DIO, repeated clear, and unrelated authorities.
close_reason: verified fixed (recovered from workflow journals)

title: Provision persistence and integrity hooks can reenter verifier and regress rollback state
description: Fresh final timing robustness/security review: ProvisionVerifier.install and clear invoke external verify_integrity, persist_rollback_state, and persist_clear callbacks while holding a threading.RLock, which explicitly permits same-thread reentry. A one-shot persist hook can recursively install a higher version; after the inner commit returns, the outer lower-version install resumes and overwrites __rollback/__current, regressing the in-memory floor. Clear/install cross-reentry can likewise violate generation/current/cleared atomicity. Add an explicit non-reentrant transition guard covering verify/persist/commit/clear (or a transaction design with post-callback generation revalidation), fail closed on callback reentry without partial state mutation, and test v2 outer→v3 inner, install→clear, clear→install, callback exceptions, and concurrent non-reentrant callers.
notes: Also cover awaitable hooks: async persist_marker/persist_rollback_state/persist_clear return coroutine objects that are never awaited, yet current code treats them as durable success and issues/commits virgin, rollback, or cleared state. Reject coroutine functions and any awaitable return (closing coroutine objects), with no state mutation; add each hook case.
close_reason: wave-10

title: Adopted DIO time remains trusted after signer key generation is retired
description: Fresh final timing security review: DioTimeVerifier-issued samples store a signer_key_generation token, but _SampleAuthority.accepts and StratumTracker _bound/_rejection never revalidate that token against the receiving LinkLayer. After a valid network time sample is adopted, authenticated rekey/retirement removes the DIO issuance yet current_time/status continue using the retired-key time until ordinary sample expiry. Bind network sample liveness to the LinkLayer current signer generation and revalidate on adoption and every active-source read/policy transition; key rotation must immediately clear the source while preserving replay/correction barriers. Test rotate before adoption, rotate after adoption, status/current_time, same-key refresh, unrelated-peer rotation, and forced concurrency.

title: Rust production SCHC ingress does not use bounded per-signer failure tracking

Integrate the bounded tracker into authenticated production ingress, exclude output-capacity errors, drop on tracker-full without eviction, and test multi-signer threshold/reset/capacity behavior through the node path.

title: Rust stale authenticated SCHC contexts can remint current fragmentation permits

Old, foreign, removed, rekeyed, and copied stale contexts must not mint permits; add recovery and capacity tests.

title: Python fragmentation version gate accepts unknown SCHC Rule IDs 8 through 254
description: Final ACK/rule correctness review: python/src/lichen/link/link_layer.py:341 gates authenticated peer compatibility only when payload[0] is 0..7 or 255. Unknown/noncanonical Rule IDs 8..254 bypass the gate and are accepted by FragmentSender because its rule_id parameter is the fragmentation rule, not the compressed packet Rule ID. Reject unknown SCHC packet Rule IDs before manager mutation and require current peer evidence for every fragmentable Rule 0, Rule 7, and Rule 255 packet. Add all boundary IDs, unknown-peer, mismatch, and no-state-mutation tests.
close_reason: wave-6

title: Python SCHC failure streak resets before decompressed IPv6 is validated
description: Final ACK correctness review: python/src/lichen/node.py:480 calls RuleVersionFailureTracker.record_success immediately after decompress_packet, before IPv6Packet.from_bytes at 481-487. SCHC data that decompresses into structurally invalid IPv6 therefore clears a consecutive failure run and is then delivered raw, allowing notification evasion. Define success only after complete SCHC and IPv6 structural validation required by ingress, count invalid decompressed packets as failures, and drop them. Test interleaved malformed-compressed and invalid-IPv6 packets around the exact notification threshold.

title: Python malformed SCHC ingress is delivered to applications instead of dropped
description: Final ACK/rule correctness review: python/src/lichen/node.py:458-479 invokes _on_receive(payload, sender) after SCHC decompression failure, including when the bounded signer tracker is full. This contradicts spec/03-adaptation.md fail-closed drop semantics and exposes malformed compressed bytes as application data. Drop without delivery, routing, or forwarding on every SCHC decode/version failure and on tracker-capacity failure; retain exact-once operator notification for tracked signers. Add callback-negative tests for malformed, truncated, unknown-rule, mismatch, and tracker-full sources.
close_reason: wave-5

title: Link send can hang when a different queued head fails terminally
description: Final ACK correctness review: python/src/lichen/link/link_layer.py:897-911 terminally removes only the reserved head after radio false/exception, then breaks or raises. If a higher-priority preloaded entry is ahead of the frame enqueued by send(), that caller's reservation remains queued and await reservation.wait() never resolves; on exception the caller observes failure while its frame remains eligible for later delivery. Terminal drain failure must resolve/remove every affected queued reservation, or continue draining with precise per-entry outcomes, so no send hangs and no frame survives an error result. Add deterministic priority-head radio-false and exception tests proving queue/reservations/stats and at-most-once behavior.
notes: Also reproduced cancellation during CAD/backoff before reserve/cleanup: the cancelled send frame and unresolved reservation remain queued and may transmit after caller cancellation/retry. Fix must cover every post-enqueue await, not only radio.transmit exceptions, and prove exact reservation cleanup without unsafe unrelated delivery.

title: Rust FragmentSender permit is not bound to the intended remote signer
description: Final Rule/version security review: rust/lichen-schc/src/fragment.rs stores signer in FragmentationPolicyEntry, but AuthenticatedFragmentationPermit exposes only owner/slot/generation and FragmentSender::new accepts no expected remote identity. A permit issued for compatible peer A can therefore authorize fragmentation later transmitted to unknown or mismatched peer B; the constructed sender carries no peer binding that a transport can verify. Require FragmentSender construction to supply and validate the intended remote signer (or return a sender that immutably exposes the policy-resolved signer for link transmission binding), and reject wrong/unknown/mismatched targets. Test A-permit→A success, A-permit→B rejection, B mismatch, copied/foreign/stale permits, and Rule 0/7/255.

title: Rust fragmentation permit remains valid after authenticated peer version mismatch
description: Final Rule/version security review: rust/lichen-schc/src/fragment.rs FragmentationPolicy::accept_peer returns VersionMismatch before locating/revoking an existing signer entry. A previously issued Copy permit therefore remains accepted after the same authenticated signer advertises an incompatible SCHC registry, allowing new FragmentSender construction under stale agreement. On every authenticated peer update, atomically find the signer and advance/remove its generation before returning mismatch; define recovery issuance for a later compatible DIO. Test compatible permit→mismatch invalidation, mismatch rejection without affecting other signers, mismatch→compatible recovery, copied stale permits, and generation/capacity boundaries.

title: Python SCHC sessions survive an authenticated incompatible version update
description: Final ACK/version security review: LinkLayer.create_fragment_sender validates the current peer version only at creation, while accept_authenticated_schc_dio replaces the peer context without revoking already prepared or active SchcSessionManager records. A sender created under compatible v3 can therefore start after the same authenticated signer advertises an incompatible version, and an active transfer can continue under obsolete registry agreement. Bind sender permits/sessions to a monotonic per-signer SCHC-context generation and atomically revoke prepared/active records when an authenticated DIO changes compatibility; same-version refresh may remain valid only if policy is identical. Test compatible-create→mismatch→start rejection, active mismatch abort/invalidation, stale handle rejection, mismatch→compatible recovery, and concurrency with start/ACK/timeout.

title: Link persistence journal cannot detect complete deletion or signed revision rollback
description: Final ACK security review: python/src/lichen/link/link_layer.py:1280-1283 treats a completely absent slot/anchor set as a clean first boot, and the anchor-missing path accepts any signed revision-1 slot. An attacker or fault that deletes the current files (or restores a previously captured signed revision-1 slot while removing the anchor/newer slot) resets inbound replay floors, pins, retired-key lineage, and TX counters on restart. The journal signature proves authenticity but not freshness because its anchor is rollbackable in the same storage domain. Add an explicit authenticated virgin/bootstrap decision plus a monotonic anti-rollback anchor supplied independently of the journal (or a fail-closed equivalent), and test complete deletion, anchor deletion plus old rev1 restoration, full old journal restoration, normal first boot, and crash at each slot/anchor write boundary.

title: Provision verifier aliases mutable rollback state across trust and persistence hooks

New candidate objects are also passed to `persist_rollback_state` and then stored internally, so the persistence hook can retain and mutate verifier state after returning. Detach authenticated rollback state into private primitive snapshots, pass a separate persistence value, and revalidate durability generation before commit. Add caller mutation before install, persistence-hook mutation after return, digest or encoded-record mutation, lower-version rejection, and reboot tests.

The exact previously adopted direct TimeSample can be submitted after clear and accepted again. Add one-use provider issuance or per-authority adoption and invalidation high-water semantics so pre-clear and previously accepted samples cannot re-establish time while a newly issued post-clear sample can.

A network sample rejected before high-water advancement or a direct sample issued before clear/policy change can currently be resubmitted later while fresh. Decide and specify whether consideration consumes issuance; recovery after expiry should require a newly issued sample if replay rejection is normative.

title: Provision clear state cannot survive reboot without restoring cleared epoch or losing rollback floor

Reinstalling the same record after clear also skips persist_rollback because the in-memory candidate equals rollback, so live accepted state may not be durable. title: Mutable EpochFloorAuthority can lower a bound trackers firmware floor

title: radio.py: polling capture still fires on_rx_timeout after success
description:
## Problem

Callback RX at timeout is fail-closed: RadioMixin._handle_rx_timeout calls deliver_pending_packets, and if the node leaves RX_WAIT it returns without super()._handle_rx_timeout. Observers see on_rx_success only.

Polling RX (start_receive / RX_WAIT with rx_callbacks is None) does not. After _capture_polling_rx records the frame (on_rx_success + metrics.record_reception), state is still RX_WAIT, so the method falls through to _drop_delayed_rx_for_receiver and EventHandlersMixin._handle_rx_timeout, which sets IDLE and notifies on_rx_timeout.

Same-tick DelayedRxReady + RxTimeout (the 9098.40 path) therefore emits both events for one window. Dashboard / RecordingObserver / any client that treats on_rx_timeout as "nothing arrived" will drop or mis-account a packet that get_rx_result still returns from _pending_poll_rx.

test_same_tick_timeout_does_not_drop_delayed_callback asserts timed_out == [] for the callback API. test_same_tick_timeout_delivers_polling_rx does not install an observer.

## Files

- python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/radio.py (_handle_rx_timeout, _capture_polling_rx)
- python/src/lichen/sim/events.py (SimulationObserver.on_rx_timeout vs on_rx_success)
- python/tests/sim/test_radio.py
- python/tests/sim/test_observer.py (test_rx_timeout_event has no overlapping success)
close_reason: wave-11

title: radio.py: 9098.39 GE shim wipes burst state every apply
description:
## Problem

9098.39 stopped stash from walking every neighbor on one `(source, tx.id)` Gilbert-Elliott machine by applying a shim with a fresh `_link_states={}` per receiver:

```python
shim = replace(rule, _link_states={})
shim._lichen_rx_id = rx_node_id  # never read by GilbertElliottRule.apply
return shim.apply(candidate, rx_position)
```

`GilbertElliottRule` documents a two-state Markov chain **per link** that updates on each unique transmission (`lora_medium/chaos.py`: "link A→B can be in a fading burst while A→C operates normally"; average burst length `1/p_bad_to_good` packets). `apply()` still keys by `(source, tx.id)` and ignores dest / `_lichen_rx_id`. The empty shim means:

1. Every radio.py apply starts in Good. Good→Bad never survives to the next `tx.id`.
2. The original `rule._link_states` is never written. `test_ge_two_receivers_independent_of_add_order` asserts `ge._link_states == {}`, locking the wipe.
3. `_lichen_rx_id` is dead: dest is not bound. Independence is only "new empty machine + shared rng", not a per-(src, dst) chain.

Through radio.py, GE is independent Bernoulli-with-a-first-transition, not a burst process. `test_chaos.py` `test_gilbert_elliott_always_bad_state_loses_all` / `test_gilbert_elliott_burst_pattern` call `rule.apply` directly and still see memory; mesh/HIL/metrics paths do not.

With default-ish GE (`p_good_to_bad=0.02`, `p_bad_to_good=0.3`, `loss_prob_bad=0.6`), long-run loss is similar but clustering is gone. OSCORE/replay/partition tests under "burst RF" measure i.i.d. loss. `_drop_chaos_state_for_tx` at TxEnd also drops `_ge_survived`, so even a radio-side cache cannot carry Bad into the next packet.

This is not 9098.39 (intra-TX neighbor chaining on one `(source, tx.id)` key). 9098.39 option (2) was persist per `(source, dest)`. The empty shim implemented option (1) too literally.

## Why this is security (fault-injection oracle)

GE is the burst-RF oracle for mesh security and capacity. A 500-node / city-mesh run with GE must produce temporally correlated drops on a link. Radio.py makes every packet a new Good-state draw. Seeded A/B (`compare_metrics`) of hopping/OSCORE-under-burst is not the documented channel model. `test_radio.py` GE cases are single-TX (`tx`+`rx` or two RX of one TX) so the wipe is invisible.

## Files

- `python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/radio.py` (`_apply_ge_independent`, `_drop_chaos_state_for_tx` at TxEnd)
- `python/tests/sim/test_radio.py` (`test_ge_two_receivers_independent_of_add_order` asserts empty `_link_states`; no two-TX burst oracle)
- `python/.venv/.../lora_medium/chaos.py` (`GilbertElliottRule.apply` keys `(source, tx.id)`, no dest)
design: Do not keep the empty-dict shim. Persist per-link state keyed by (source_node_id, rx_node_id), not (source, tx.id) and not a fresh {} on every apply. Options: (1) radio.py owns dict[(src, dst), _LinkState], copies that one entry into the shim (or mutates it in place) so each dest has its own chain that survives TxEnd; (2) teach GilbertElliottRule.apply to take dest / honor _lichen_rx_id and key _link_states by (source, dest). title: radio.py: parked polling RX is a latch; later TXs in the window are shadowed
description:
## Problem

9098.40 parked a polling RX result in `_pending_poll_rx` so a same-tick RxTimeout cannot consume the only eligible LatencyRule microsecond. `get_rx_result` reads that map with `.get`, never `.pop`. `_capture_polling_rx` refuses to overwrite if the key is already present.

```python
parked = self._pending_poll_rx_map().get(node_id)
if parked is not None:
    payload, rssi, snr, _, _ = parked
    return payload, rssi, snr
```

The park is cleared only by `start_receive` / `enter_rx_mode` / `exit_rx_mode` / TX-start / `remove_node`. It is not consumed on read, not dropped on TxEnd, and not dropped when `_handle_rx_timeout` sets IDLE.

Two failure modes for the documented ~1 ms `get_rx_result` poll while a node waits (`metrics.py` module docstring; `start_receive` path):

1. **Later frames in the same RX window are shadowed.** `start_receive(timeout_ms=10000)` → LatencyRule DelayedRxReady parks frame A and records metrics → TX B starts before timeout → every poll still returns A. Live (no-LatencyRule) polling does not do this: after A's airtime, `get_rx_result` returns None and then B. Parking turns a multi-frame RX_WAIT window into a latch on the first delayed delivery.

2. **The latch outlives the RX window.** After timeout, the node is IDLE but the park remains. A 1 ms loop that does not re-arm `start_receive` keeps observing A forever. Live polling returns None once the medium TX is gone.

`test_same_tick_timeout_delivers_polling_rx` polls once and stops. `test_delayed_collision_does_not_permanently_silence` never parks (collision result is None). No test starts a second TX inside a still-open `start_receive` window after a DelayedRxReady capture.

This is not 9098.40 (polling RX never saw the delayed frame). The park is the 40 fix; it has no TTL and is not a one-shot.

## Files

- python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/radio.py (`_pending_poll_rx_map`, `_capture_polling_rx`, `get_rx_result` `.get`, `_handle_rx_timeout` / `_handle_event` DelayedRxReady)
- python/src/lichen/sim/metrics.py (documents ~1 ms poll)
- python/tests/sim/test_radio.py (`test_same_tick_timeout_delivers_polling_rx` — single poll)

## Why this is robustness

Production polling stays in one RX_WAIT until timeout. LatencyRule + a long `start_receive` window is the 9098.18/40 path. A latch that hides every later frame (and keeps returning a payload after IDLE) makes soak / HIL-style poll loops and sequential-burst tests measure the first delayed packet, not the radio.
design: Pop _pending_poll_rx on the first get_rx_result that returns it, or drop it when the RX window ends (RxTimeout → IDLE) after that first pull. Do not let DelayedRxReady capture block a later in-window TX. Keep same-tick timeout delivery: advance_to(expire==timeout) then one get_rx_result still returns the delayed frame. After that pull, a subsequent TX in the same or a new window must be visible.
acceptance_criteria: 1) start_receive long timeout + LatencyRule: after DelayedRxReady, first get_rx_result is frame A; a later TX B in the same window is returned once A has been pulled (or after A's park is consumed). 2) After RxTimeout, a second get_rx_result without start_receive is None (no infinite A). 3) test_same_tick_timeout_delivers_polling_rx stays green. 4) A regression test does a second TX inside the original start_receive window after the delayed capture.

description: Post-fix robustness review found rule_matches validates descriptors and MO matching but can select values a CDA cannot reconstruct losslessly. NotSent must require packet value equals target; Lsb must require the elided prefix equals the target prefix, safely at widths/arguments 0 and 128; MappingSent must require membership. Otherwise Ignore/MatchMapping combinations can silently reconstruct a different field. Enforce CDA feasibility independently of MO or reject unsupported pairs, and add round-trip tests across all MO/CDA pairs and 1/128-bit boundaries.
notes: Independent correctness review recommends canonical Python-compatible pairing: NotSent only with Equal; Lsb only with Msb using same mo_arg; MappingSent only with MatchMapping. Built-in rules already use safe pairs. Prefer this strict pair matrix over per-packet feasibility alone for cross-implementation parity.

title: Bind SCHC ACK bytes inseparably to verifier-produced authentication metadata
description: Security codereview found FragmentSender.handle_ack_bytes accepts arbitrary ACK bytes separately from a publicly constructible AuthenticatedSessionContext, so metadata from one authenticated frame can be paired with substituted C=1 bytes. Replace the detached API with a verifier-produced immutable envelope/result that binds exact payload, canonical identities, and replay acceptance (or an unforgeable payload-bound token). Add substitution tests proving authenticated NACK metadata cannot authorize different ACK bytes.
notes: Post-fix correctness review: publicly constructible RxFrame is not an authenticity capability. Make construction verifier-only or route ACK processing directly from LinkLayer, include actual receiving-local identity, and verify with signed-wire integration tests.

title: Validate LSB CDA arguments and target width during SCHC rule selection
description: Correctness codereview found descriptor validation in rust/lichen-schc/src/context.rs only applies mo_arg and target-value constraints to Mo::Msb. Cda::Lsb with another MO can select with missing or oversized mo_arg and an out-of-width target; generic decompression then subtracts mo_arg from length_bits and may underflow/panic. Validate mo_arg whenever either MO=MSB or CDA=LSB, require the argument according to LSB semantics, reject values above the field width, width-check targets consumed by LSB, and add cross-MO boundary tests at widths 1 and 128.

title: Make SCHC Sender-Abort terminal after the fourth negative ACK
description: Security review finding in python/src/lichen/schc/fragment.py handle_ack_bytes: when the negative-ACK retry limit is reached, the sender returns a Sender-Abort fragment but does not transition status to aborted. Repeated attacker-controlled negative ACKs can consequently trigger unlimited Sender-Abort transmissions and duty-cycle/resource exhaustion, while a later C=1 ACK can reverse the supposed terminal outcome and mark the transfer successful.
acceptance_criteria: The retry-limit branch atomically transitions the sender to a terminal aborted state before returning exactly one Sender-Abort. Every later ACK and timeout is ignored and cannot emit another fragment or change the terminal result. Tests exercise the fourth negative ACK, repeated later negative ACKs, a later complete ACK, and timeout after abort, proving one abort emission and no terminal-state reversal. Run three independent correctness, security, and robustness code-review passes and file every resulting finding before closure.
close_reason: verified fixed (recovered from workflow journals)

title: Bind SCHC sender ACKs to authenticated peer, session, replay freshness, and final window
description: Security review finding in python/src/lichen/schc/fragment.py handle_ack_bytes: the sender accepts any canonical ACK carrying the same Rule ID. A C=1 ACK immediately marks the transfer successful without proving the ACK came from the intended authenticated peer/current fragmentation session, without replay-freshness enforcement, and without requiring the ACK window to identify the final window. A delayed valid ACK from an earlier transfer or another peer can therefore falsely complete a new transfer and discard retransmission state.
acceptance_criteria: ACK processing receives or is called only after verified local identity, remote signer identity, fragmentation Rule ID, and link replay-counter/session context are available. It binds those values to the active sender session, rejects unauthenticated or wrong-peer ACKs and replay counters not fresh for that session, and accepts C=1 only for the active transfer's final window. Tests cover a prior-session delayed C=1 ACK, an ACK from the wrong authenticated peer, a C=1 ACK for a non-final window, replayed ACK rejection, and successful completion by a fresh valid final-window ACK. Run three independent correctness, security, and robustness code-review passes and file every resulting finding before closure.
close_reason: verified fixed (recovered from workflow journals)

title: Validate board provision metadata before raising the epoch floor
description: Security/robustness review finding discovered from the closed epoch-floor task. effective_epoch_floor in python/src/lichen/timing/time_sync.py:201-205 blindly returns max(firmware_build_epoch, board_provision_epoch) for every non-None value. It validates neither types/ranges nor the provision value presence, authentication/integrity, nonzero status, relation to build epoch, deterministic maximum lead, or recoverability. A corrupted or malicious far-future provision epoch can therefore make all legitimate time samples fail indefinitely. This contradicts docs/firmware-time-provider.md:11-64, especially its explicit invalid-metadata diagnostics and recovery requirements; test/vectors/packets-timing.json:198-205 does not exercise validity metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Model board provision epoch as validated metadata including presence, parse/range result, authentication or integrity result, and configured deterministic lead bound. Ignore missing, zero, malformed, unauthenticated, earlier-than-build, overflow/out-of-range, and beyond-lead values; retain the firmware build epoch and expose a specific rejection diagnostic. Support authenticated replacement or clearing so a poisoned value cannot permanently lock out time. Validate firmware build metadata and integer bounds rather than relying on max coercion. Add the full docs/firmware-time-provider.md:152-166 matrix to Python tests and canonical vectors, including recovery and a legitimate stricter provision floor. Ensure consumers use only the validated effective floor; run focused tests and three code-review passes per modified source module.
notes: Post-fix correctness review: provision metadata only checks board_identity is non-None and minimum_record_version defaults to 0. Require the expected device identity/settings digest and a persistent rollback/version floor with no permissive production default; add identity-mismatch diagnostics/vectors and authenticated replace/clear recovery.
close_reason: verified fixed (recovered from workflow journals)

title: Preserve GNSS versus gpsd provenance at stratum 4
description: Correctness/spec-compliance review finding. Stratum.GNSS_GPSD in python/src/lichen/timing/time_sync.py:91-109 is normatively GNSS or Local-client, but STRATUM_SOURCE_CLASS maps it unconditionally to SourceClass.GNSS. python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:96-103 asserts the collapsed mapping. spec/09-packets-timing.md:176-209 classifies gpsd as Local-client and makes that class policy-gated, while direct GNSS is a distinct default-trusted class. Treating gpsd as GNSS bypasses provenance and policy distinctions and can grant local-client data unintended authority.
acceptance_criteria: Replace the one-to-one stratum mapping with a representation that preserves the actual source class and source name/provenance, or explicitly represents every allowed class for a stratum without inferring which supplied a sample. A gpsd/local-client stratum-4 sample MUST remain Local-client and require its policy; on-device GNSS MUST remain GNSS and require GNSS time validity. Tests must cover both sources at stratum 4, distinct default policy outcomes, serialization/adoption without provenance loss, and status/diagnostic exposure. Align spec/vector wording if needed and run focused tests plus three code-review passes per modified source module.
close_reason: verified fixed (recovered from workflow journals)

title: Define freshness and correction policy for stratum tracking
description: Correctness/security review finding. python/src/lichen/timing/time_sync.py:190-198 and 235-259 update mutable tracker state whenever a received stratum is strictly higher. They do not compare the projected current wall clock, bound forward jumps, prevent backward steps, record sample age/sequence, or recover from an invalidated source. Conversely, equal-stratum samples are always rejected; python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:153-175 locks that behavior in, so a selected source can never refresh or correct its timestamp and the tracker becomes sticky at stratum 4. This conflicts with docs/firmware-time-provider.md:104-118, which requires fresher-sample preference and explicit policy before backward correction, and leaves far-future poisoning possible.
acceptance_criteria: Specify and implement a correction/freshness policy based on current accepted Unix time projected from monotonic observation, sample observation time/age, source identity/trust, and configurable backward/forward correction bounds. Reject stale, replayed, implausibly far-future, and unauthorized backward samples without mutating tracker state. Permit a fresher valid equal-stratum sample when policy allows, including periodic refresh; define source switching and recovery when the current source expires or is invalidated. Preserve lower-stratum rejection unless explicit failover policy applies. Tests must cover backward step, forward-jump bound, duplicate/replay, out-of-order sample, valid equal-stratum refresh, source expiry/failover, recovery from poisoned/stale state, and monotonic advancement between samples. Update normative docs/vectors and run focused tests plus three code-review passes per modified source module.
notes: Independent security review: per-sample forward bounds can be ratcheted repeatedly, and expiry/clear resets to the much larger initial lead. Retain last-good projected anchor across expiry, define cumulative correction/slew budget, and require stronger re-bootstrap for large jumps.
close_reason: verified fixed

title: Fail closed on untrusted DIO and invalid source samples
description: Security/correctness review finding. StratumTracker.consider in python/src/lichen/timing/time_sync.py:170-198 and should_adopt_time at 235-259 accept any higher-stratum DioTimeOption using only enum order and an epoch lower bound. They carry no signature/authentication result, peer identity, source class/name, source policy decision, observed monotonic time, freshness, or quality/validity metadata. can_establish_wall_clock at 208-232 likewise accepts GNSS and RTC from class plus timestamp alone, although spec/09-packets-timing.md:173-185 requires trusted sources and docs/firmware-time-provider.md:68-100 requires valid GNSS time, RTC/source metadata, provenance, freshness, and trust. An unauthenticated neighbor can therefore establish wall time merely by advertising a higher stratum. The same structured contract must cover GNSS validity and epoch-valid/aged RTC state, so those are consolidated here.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce a structured time-sample/adoption input that preserves source class and name, peer identity where applicable, authentication or integrity verification status, explicit policy acceptance, source-specific validity such as GNSS time-valid separate from position and RTC initialization/age, Unix time, monotonic observation time, freshness/age, and quality/accuracy. DIO/network adoption MUST require verified link/root authenticity or an explicit permitted policy path and MUST fail closed when required metadata is missing, false, stale, or malformed. Route StratumTracker and can_establish_wall_clock through the same policy boundary. Tests must cover unsigned/unverified DIO, policy-denied and policy-accepted network time, GNSS position-valid but time-invalid, uninitialized/stale RTC, missing metadata, valid authenticated samples, and preservation/exposure of rejection reasons and provenance. Align spec and vectors if the data contract changes; run focused tests and three code-review passes per modified source module.
notes: Post-fix reviews: _EVIDENCE_SEAL, TimeSample._from_provider, TimeEvidence constructor, ProvisionEpochMetadata._from_verified_record, and from_verified_network remain callable/importable; underscores do not create unforgeable evidence. RxFrame provenance is tracked by f7y6. Local provider evidence is only caller-supplied provider_validated and lacks GNSS time-valid vs position-valid and RTC initialized/age state. StratumTracker can be directly constructed or publicly mutated into a synced state without evidence. Replace self-asserted factories/state with production capability-bound provider/verifier transitions and negative package-API tests; retain structured validity/quality/policy decision diagnostics after accept/reject/status.
close_reason: verified fixed (recovered from workflow journals)

title: Allocate a valid RPL DIO Time Option type across spec and implementations
description: Correctness review finding. python/src/lichen/timing/time_sync.py:111-167 defines DIO_TIME_OPTION_TYPE = 0 and encodes an eight-byte Type/Length option. RFC 6550 assigns RPL Control Message Option Type 0 to Pad1, whose wire form is one octet and has no Length field. python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:106-141 and test/vectors/packets-timing.json:239-244 currently canonize the colliding 00 06 prefix. A standards-compliant RPL option walker will consume 00 as Pad1 and parse 06 as the next option type, so the advertised time cannot interoperate and may desynchronize all following options. spec/09-packets-timing.md:211-223 still says Type TBD.
acceptance_criteria: Select and document a non-conflicting provisional/assigned RPL option type through the project extension allocation process, or disable wire emission until such a type is selected. Update spec/09-packets-timing.md, docs/drafts as applicable, Python, Rust, Zephyr/C, and test/vectors/packets-timing.json to one canonical allocation and layout. Add independent tests showing Type 0 is handled as RFC 6550 Pad1 without reading a length, the selected time option round-trips through a normal mixed RPL option list, unknown and malformed options are handled correctly, and every implementation consumes the same vector. Run focused cross-implementation tests and three code-review passes on each modified source module.
notes: Python/spec registry is now 0x15, but Zephyr C rpl_messages.h still defines DIO Time as 0/Pad1 and messages.c ignores reserved, permits stratum outside 0-4, permits NO_SYNC with nonzero timestamp, and lacks focused codec vectors. Update C to 0x15 with strict parse/write validation and mixed option iterator tests; validate on Linux/EC2 per project rules before closing cross-implementation scope.

title: Rule 7 fe80::/64 mode conflicts with Rust fe80::/10 predicate and corrupts addresses
description: Security/interoperability review finding: spec/03-adaptation.md requires Rule 7 AddressMode=0 only when both addresses have the exact canonical fe80::/64 prefix, sending only their 64-bit IIDs; otherwise it requires full 128-bit addresses. rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs currently uses is_link_local(), which recognizes all fe80::/10 addresses, for both compression selection and decompression canonicality. For a valid link-local address with nonzero bits 10..63, compression discards those bits and reconstructs a different source or destination. Full-mode encoding of the same address can also be rejected. This can misroute traffic or change endpoint identity across a SCHC hop.
acceptance_criteria: Rule 7 mode selection uses an exact canonical fe80::/64 predicate for IID-only compression. Addresses within fe80::/10 but outside that /64 either use full-address mode and round-trip unchanged or normatively fall back to Rule 255; all implementations choose the same behavior. Tests/vectors include source and destination addresses with nonzero bits 10..63 and prove that no address bits are lost, no endpoint changes, and the canonical fe80::/64 case still uses AddressMode=0.
close_reason: verified fixed (recovered from workflow journals)

title: Rule 7 must validate lossless IPv6/UDP match constraints before compression
description: Security review finding: spec/03-adaptation.md Rule 7 now says the rule matches a UDP packet whenever either endpoint port is 10883, but it no longer states the complete lossless matching and validation preconditions. A compressor that elides/recomputes fields without validating them can normalize nonzero IPv6 Traffic Class or Flow Label, inconsistent IPv6 Payload Length or UDP Length, a non-UDP Next Header, or a zero/invalid UDP checksum into a different valid packet on decompression. This launders malformed or corrupted input across a hop and creates implementation divergence. The normative Rule 7 definition must enumerate IPv6 version=6, Traffic Class=0, Flow Label=0, Next Header=UDP, endpoint-port matching, consistent IPv6/UDP lengths, and a valid mandatory IPv6 UDP checksum. Packets that fail must be dropped or use Rule 255 without semantic normalization.
acceptance_criteria: The normative Rule 7 text contains the full IPv6/UDP matching and input-validation constraints and defines drop versus Rule-255 fallback. Canonical cross-implementation negative vectors cover nonzero Traffic Class, nonzero Flow Label, non-UDP Next Header, IPv6 payload-length mismatch, UDP-length mismatch, zero checksum, and bad checksum. Rust, Zephyr/C, and Python reject or fall back identically, while every accepted packet round-trips byte-for-byte except fields explicitly and validly recomputed by the profile. The compressor validates the original IPv6 UDP checksum before eliding it; the decoder recomputes and installs a checksum rather than claiming to validate an unavailable original. A shared vector forces a mathematical zero checksum result and all implementations encode it canonically as 0xffff, never UDP zero.
notes:
Additional interoperability/security acceptance: specify the canonical IPv6 UDP checksum representation when one's-complement checksum arithmetic produces numeric zero. The transmitted checksum MUST be 0xffff, never 0x0000; Rule 7 compression validation and decompression must agree on that mapping. Add a deliberately constructed checksum-zero payload vector and verify Rust, Zephyr/C, and Python all serialize/validate 0xffff identically while rejecting a zero wire checksum.
Correctness pass detail: Rule 7 elides the original UDP checksum, so a decoder cannot validate the sender checksum after decompression; only the compressor can validate the original. The decoder must recompute and install the checksum. If the ones-complement computation yields mathematical zero, IPv6 UDP requires transmitting 0xffff rather than zero. The current phrase validate the computed nonzero checksum is tautological and should be replaced with explicit recomputation/installation behavior.
close_reason: verified fixed (recovered from workflow journals)

title: Rust SCHC rule matching accepts values and descriptors outside declared field widths
description: rust/lichen-schc/src/context.rs validates descriptor length_bits only inside the MSB matching branch and does not reject packet field values, target values, or match-mapping entries whose set bits exceed length_bits. MSB(0) succeeds before any value-width check, and Equal, Ignore, and MatchMapping descriptors bypass the stated 1..=128 width restriction. Invalid rules or parsed values may select in Rust, diverge from Python rule_matches, and fail or truncate later during residue encoding.
acceptance_criteria: Add one centralized validation path used before every MO/CDA match. Reject descriptor widths outside 1..=128 and reject present field values, target values when applicable, and every mapping value that is not representable in length_bits. Apply this consistently to Equal, MSB including MSB(0), MatchMapping, and Ignore with all CDAs. Define handling for malformed static/custom rules without panics. Add boundary tests for widths 0, 1, 128, and 129; values and TVs at max, max+1; invalid mapping members; all MO/CDA combinations; and Rust/Python parity. Existing valid MSB prefix cases 0, 1, 127, and 128 must continue to work.
close_reason: verified fixed (recovered from workflow journals)

title: SCHC Rule 7 normative definition and rule-set version diverge across artifacts
description: spec/03-adaptation.md now makes the at-least-one-UDP-endpoint-10883 Rule 7 residue normative, including AddressMode, PortDirection, and OtherPort, but the current rule-set remains version 2. The canonical appendix and Internet-Draft still describe exact-port approximately 6-byte compression, the shared vector expects zero port residue, Python and C do not implement the new form, and Rust generic rule descriptors do not model the specialized Rust codec behavior. A version-2 peer can therefore silently interpret Rule 7 under a different wire contract.
acceptance_criteria: Atomically select and document one canonical Rule 7 wire definition across spec/03-adaptation.md, appendix, Internet-Draft, vectors, Rust descriptors/selection and specialized codec, Python, and C. Preserve the old definition under v2 or increment the rule-set version everywhere required, including DIO advertisement and compatibility handling. Add byte-exact shared vectors for source-only 10883, destination-only 10883, both ports with canonical direction, link-local addresses, global addresses, mixed addresses, and malformed/noncanonical residues. Demonstrate Rust, Python, and C encode/decode identical bytes and reject incompatible rule-set versions.
notes: Post-fix correctness review: Rust still exports generic MQTT_SN_RULE descriptors whose residue is incompatible with specialized codec Rule 7, while Python generic registry has no Rule 7. Remove generic ambiguity or make all public entry points byte-identical. Draft still says ~6 bytes, says CoAP uses Rule 7, and titles Appendix A Version 1. Shared vectors need malformed/boundary cases (20/36-byte truncation, alternate modes, padding, multicast/unspecified sources, empty/max payload) consumed by every implementation.
close_reason: verified fixed (recovered from workflow journals)

title: discovery.py: RREP hop_count overflow causes serialization failure at max depth
description: Line 181: install_hops = rrep.hop_count + 1 can exceed MAX_HOP_LIMIT (15) when processing an RREP at maximum hop depth. This value propagates to GradientEntry (line 189) and is used in proxied RREPs (line 169) and forwarded RREPs (line 216). When these RREPs are serialized via to_bytes(), messages.py line 124 raises LoadngError because hop_count > MAX_HOP_LIMIT. Failure scenario: valid RREP with hop_count=15 arrives, install_hops becomes 16, subsequent RREP generation/forwarding raises exception causing route delivery failure.
close_reason: Fix already implemented at lines 230-232 of python/src/lichen/loadng/discovery.py. The guard `if install_hops > MAX_HOP_LIMIT: return RrepResult(dropped=True)` prevents hop_count overflow before it propagates to GradientEntry or proxied RREPs. The comment explicitly references this bead ID confirming this is the fix.

title: discovery.py: Unconditional cache.add may install stale routes
description: Lines 196-205: gradient.update is conditional on _is_seq_fresher check, but cache.add runs unconditionally. When a stale RREP arrives (older seq_num from retransmission/delay), the gradient preserves the fresher entry but cache is overwritten with stale data. This creates gradient/cache inconsistency and could cause routing to use outdated next_hop information.

title: Cross-validate: SenML parity
close_reason: Cross-validated SenML-CBOR parity against test/vectors/senml_location.json on both sides. Rust side had three real divergences, all fixed: (1) upstream senml-cbor 0.1 encoder always emits bt/t as 9-byte f64 while the oracle pins shortest-form CBOR integers for whole-second timestamps (Python/cbor2 reference behavior) — added rust/lichen-senml/src/wire.rs canonical encoder (integral i64-window bt/t -> shortest-form int; v always f64; bn,bt,n,u,v,vs,vb,t label order; up-front validation: one-of value fields, 128-byte name cap, finite-only). (3) Position::to_senml_cbor accepted out-of-range/non-finite coordinates that Python profiles.location rejects — pos.rs now enforces F.3 lat/lon bounds and finiteness (converged with parallel worker's concurrent edits). New tests: lichen-senml/tests/location_vectors.rs (6 cross-language tests: byte-exact encode parity on all 5 positive vectors, decode field parity, re-encode stability vs oracle bytes, NaN encode reject, all 3 decode rejects, partition check) + 13 wire unit tests incl RFC 8949 A.1 literals; lichen-client/tests/position_senml_vectors.rs (4 client-level parity tests, fixed 2 borrow-compile errors in parallel worker's draft). title: Transit Information option (type 6) - all impls
notes: 2026-08-26 bounded all-implementation audit: NOT ready to claim/close. Spec/05-routing.md:272 requires exact Data Length 20 with a 16-byte Parent Address, and :376 assigns E to external reachability (not parent presence). Python TransitInformation supports exact 4/20 RFC forms and models E as external ownership; its production DAO path accepts E and applies the DODAGID fallback for the 4-byte form. Rust's current profile codec enforces exact 20, parent present, and flags byte exactly zero, so it rejects E=1 and cannot represent spec-required external reachability. Zephyr C is internally contradictory: lichen_rpl_transit_info_parse/write in messages.c:398-443 require/write flags=0x80 under the incorrect comment that E means parent present, but production rpl_dao_process.c:171-180 first rejects opt.data[0] != 0 and then calls that parser. Excluded C/Zephyr changes are necessary, so leave open/unclaimed until E semantics are unified, the C contradiction is fixed, exact length/parent rules are enforced, and one schema-backed positive/negative corpus is independently consumed by all three. No files modified or tests run because source/vector inspection conclusively fails acceptance.

title: SRH processing at intermediate nodes
notes:
BLOCKED 2026-08-26 after read-only parity audit; no files modified. Python production routing.py is externally dirty/read-only and fails required policy: SourceRoutingHeader.from_ext_data accepts CmprE=1 (wire prefix 03 01 00 10 00 00), RoutingTable.add_route accepts cyclic duplicate-hop path [fd00::a, fd00::b, fd00::a, fd00::d], and _find_routing_header selects the first Routing header without rejecting duplicates. C lichen/subsys/lichen/rpl/rpl_srh.c provides encode/decode/check_nonstoring only; it has no intermediate transition that decrements Hop Limit, advances destination, and decrements Segments Left. Rust lichen-rpl/src/srh.rs likewise has codec + hop-limit predicate only. Implementing Rust alone would violate parity. Required convergence: fix/read-test Python compression/cycle/duplicate-header handling, add C intermediate processing or explicitly defer C under current phase, then implement Rust raw-packet intermediate transition with canonical cross-language vectors covering next-hop, Hop Limit, Segments Left, compression/padding, malformed/duplicate/loop, and 8-hop cap.
Implemented isolated Zephyr intermediate-node RFC 6554 forwarding in rpl_srh without touching route-table, DODAG, or network-stack files. New lichen_rpl_srh_advance validates the entire bounded route before mutation; rejects malformed counts, exhausted/insufficient Hop Limit, multicast source/destination/hops, source/current-destination entries, duplicates/loops, overlong routes, and NULL inputs; atomically extracts next hop, swaps current IPv6 Destination into the consumed SRH slot, decrements Segments Left and Hop Limit, and distinguishes local completion from forwarding. API contract documents RFC 8200 pseudo-header behavior: transport checksum remains based on final destination and is not changed by relays, so no dirty stack integration was needed. Validation: sanitizer-backed host C ctest 1/1 and direct 11/11; cppcheck and git diff --check clean; Rust two-relay destination-swap/restoration parity test passed (1/1).

title: Cross-validate: position SenML parity across impls
description: Verify Python/Rust/Zephyr produce identical SenML encoding
notes: STATUS: Python<->Rust byte-parity PROVEN and deviations FIXED; Zephyr C side BLOCKED (see notes). Rust fixes: (1) pos.rs lat/lon records used u="deg" instead of u="lat"/"lon" (spec appendix-senml F.3; new SENML_LOCATION_UNIT_LAT/UNIT_LON constants in lichen-core). (2) bt was always 9-byte 0xfb f64 while oracle/python emit shortest-form int (0x1a66536a90); new canonical codec rust/lichen-senml/src/wire.rs (encode+decode) reusing senml-cbor Record/CborError. NOTE: upstream senml-cbor cbor::decode cannot parse 4/8-byte int args (dec_head caps info<=25), i.e. it rejected the committed oracle bytes AND any Python-produced position pack - wire::decode replaces it on all Position decode paths. wire::decode enforces RFC8428 one-value-field rule (vector err-multiple-value-fields was silently accepted before); fixed skip_depth major-7 sizing bug (must use head size, not argument value). (3) Position::to_senml_cbor now rejects NaN/Inf + lat/[-90,90] + lon/[-180,180] matching python profiles.location and C senml_encode_location*. Tests: rust/lichen-client/tests/position_senml_vectors.rs (Position-level, all 12 vectors) + rust/lichen-senml/tests/location_vectors.rs (codec-level, incl oracle->re-encode stability) + 23 inline unit tests; oracle = test/vectors/senml_location.json (never code-under-test). All cargo tests green (lichen-senml 21+2+6, lichen-client 75+4+, lichen-core 300+), clippy clean, fmt applied; pytest senml_location_vectors+senml_resources 46 passed. ZEPHYR BLOCKERS in lichen/subsys/lichen/senml/senml.c (cannot build/test on macOS host; needs EC2 zephyr builder): a) duplicate definition of senml_encode_location_full (~L402 and ~L545) -> compile error; b) zcbor_float32_put emits 0xfa f32 values vs oracle 0xfb f64 (byte-parity break vs python/rust); c) encode order BT-before-BN contradicts oracle (a2 21(bn)..22(bt)) and its own 'canonical CBOR ordering' comment (deterministic CBOR sorts 0x21<0x22 => bn first); d) C uses float (f32) throughout so e.g. 37.774929f != f64 bits of oracle.

title: Session resumption
close_reason: Closed as superseded/not normative in the current LICHEN EDHOC profile; no code changes required. spec/06-security.md §8.9 defines only the RFC 9528 three-message EDHOC exchange and explicitly requires periodic refresh by re-running EDHOC every 24 hours or at OSCORE sequence exhaustion. It defines no ticket, PSK binder, 0-RTT, abbreviated handshake, wire format, state machine, replay policy, or test oracle for "session resumption." Repository-wide searches of the Python EDHOC implementation, in-repo Rust wrapper, vectors, and the dirty external Rust oscore dependency found no resumption API/format. Durable OSCORE context continuity is separate: Python MemorySecurityContext.from_edhoc supports restoring a persisted sender sequence, and Rust Context::restore_existing restores authoritative sender state; that preserves nonce/replay safety after reboot but is not EDHOC session resumption. Key refresh is separately owned by 13.4.2. Adding an ad-hoc resumption protocol would violate interoperability and expand beyond RFC 9528/current spec. The stale Python/Rust/Zephyr/vector resumption beads 6.8.10-.13 should be reconciled separately rather than used as an implementation oracle.

title: [review] TH_2 input not CBOR-encoded per RFC 9528
description:
## Summary

`_compute_th()` in `python/src/lichen/crypto/edhoc.py` expects raw bytes and hashes them directly via SHA-256. The inputs must already be properly CBOR-encoded for RFC 9528 compliance.

## Bug

**TH_2** is computed with raw concatenation (both initiator at L323 and responder at L568):

```python
th_2_input = self._g_y + self._c_r + h_msg1  # L323 initiator
th_2_input = self._eph_pk + self.c_r + h_msg1  # L568 responder
```

Per RFC 9528 Section 4.1 and 4.1.2, the EDHOC hash function H() applies SHA-256 to a CBOR sequence of its arguments. Each argument must be encoded in CBOR (bstr for G_Y, C_R, H(message_1)).

## Evidence of inconsistency

TH_3 (L379) and TH_4 (L424) correctly use `cbor2.dumps()`:
```python
th_3_input = cbor2.dumps(self._th_2) + cbor2.dumps(ciphertext_2) + cbor2.dumps(id_cred_r)  # L379
th_4_input = cbor2.dumps(self._th_3) + cbor2.dumps(ciphertext_3)  # L424
```

The same for responder (L608, L678).

## Impact

- Both initiator and responder use the same incorrect encoding, so self-tests pass
- Will **not interoperate** with any RFC-9528-compliant EDHOC implementation
- TH_2 feeds into all subsequent key derivation (PRK_2e, KEYSTREAM_2, MAC_2, etc.), so all derived keys are wrong for interop

## Fix

```python
# TH_2 input should be CBOR-encoded bstrs:
th_2_input = cbor2.dumps(self._g_y) + cbor2.dumps(self._c_r) + cbor2.dumps(h_msg1)
```

Same for responder L568.

## Scope

Pre-existing bug, not introduced by this commit. This commit correctly adds C_R to TH_2 (which was previously missing entirely), but preserves the same raw-concatenation encoding approach.
close_reason: wave-8

title: [review] project-LICHEN-worker6-ps69: POST /sos returns CREATED but resource already exists
description:
Commit bd90d6b2 changed SosResource.render_put() to render_post() and switched the response code from CHANGED (2.04) to CREATED (2.01).

Per RFC 7252 Section 5.8.1:
- 2.01 Created MUST include Location-Path or Location-Query option(s)
- 2.01 Created is for when a new resource was created by the request

The /sos resource is pre-registered as an ObservableResource — it always exists. Activating SOS via POST updates the state of an existing resource, which should return 2.04 Changed, not 2.01 Created.

Additionally, the response lacks a Location-Path option, which is a MUST per the RFC for 2.01 responses.

File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources.py:393 — SosResource.render_post()

The AGENTS.md mandates both implementations produce identical output for test vectors. While 2^32 packets is unlikely in practice, this is a correctness divergence.

Files affected:
- lichen/subsys/lichen/link/rf_health.c:26 (record_tx: wrapping ++), :32 (record_rx: wrapping ++), :47 (record_tx_fail: wrapping ++)  
- lichen/subsys/lichen/link/include/lichen/rf_health.h: SnrStats.count is uint32_t, ++ in record_rx

Fix: Use conditional saturating add (if count < UINT32_MAX) or accept the divergence per platform constraints after documenting in AGENTS.md.

Additionally, the EMA diff computation in rf_health.c:39-40 uses plain int32_t subtraction/addition instead of saturating variants. While SNR ranges [-128,127]*2^16 won't overflow int32_t, this is a further divergence from Rust's saturating_sub/saturating_add.
close_reason: verified fixed

title: [rereview] project-LICHEN-a4n2.3: missing tx_queue_destroy in lichen_link_cleanup leaks POSIX mutex
description:
Commit 1a774fce5 adds tx_queue to struct lichen_link_ctx and calls tx_queue_init() in lichen_link_init() (link_ctx.c:186), but does NOT call tx_queue_destroy() in lichen_link_cleanup() (link_ctx.c:572-597).

Impact:
- On POSIX/Linux: pthread_mutex_t inside tx_queue is never destroyed, causing a mutex resource leak on every cleanup. Worse, if cleanup is followed by re-init (common in enable/disable cycles), tx_queue_init() re-initializes the mutex without destroying first, which is undefined behavior per POSIX.
- On Zephyr: tx_queue_destroy is a no-op, so no issue.

Fix: Add tx_queue_destroy(&ctx->tx_queue) at the start of lichen_link_cleanup(), before the seq_lock destroy.
close_reason: verified fixed

title: Enforce exclusive OSCORE receiver ownership
description: Repeated Context::load_existing calls can create concurrent receiver contexts with independent replay windows for the same durable record, so both may accept one authenticated packet. Enforce synchronized exclusive ownership or shared atomic recipient replay state. Found reviewing convergence OSCORE slice; outside frozen ledger.
notes: Not a spec gap -- runtime implementation bug. Need mutex or shared atomic replay state to prevent concurrent receivers accepting same packet. Ready for implementation.
close_reason: Fixed in f4b089027c (rust/lichen-oscore). Mechanism (a) process-wide OwnershipRegistry: claims keyed by ContextId; second register_fresh/restore_existing for a live record fails with OwnershipError::AlreadyOwned (fail closed); explicit release(); drop-without-release keeps the claim; activation failure rolls back the claim; fixed-capacity, no_std, allocation-free. WHY (a): the oscore crate derives one stable ContextId per directional context (types.rs: 'Stable identifier for one directional OSCORE sender context'), so ContextId pins exactly one recipient replay window; production call sites (lichen-node/src/secure.rs:542, lichen-node/src/rpl_stack/secure.rs:24, lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:1016) use map-replace install (contexts.insert(peer_iid, ..)) and never retain two live contexts per peer, so fail-closed on double-load is tolerated and converts the silent split-brain into a loud error. Alternative (b) shared atomic replay window rejected: replay windows are ephemeral by decision on 38qm (restart clears, MUST NOT persist) and Context is a foreign re-export (path dep crates/oscore), so sharing one window across instances would require restructuring the external crate. CALL-SITE AUDIT: no site requires independent windows (escalation clause not triggered); node/gateway adoption of the registry filed as project-LICHEN-worker6-yj0c. TESTS: new tests/ownership.rs 7 tests (second activation of a live record fails AlreadyOwned after instance 1 accepted seq N; claim rollback on activation failure; distinct directional records own independently; capacity exhaustion fails closed; register_fresh exclusivity; claim survives drop until release; release of unowned record is false). Staged slice verified in isolation on HEAD in a clean worktree: cargo test -p lichen-oscore 33 passed/0 failed (1 pre-existing ignored), fmt clean, clippy --all-features and --no-default-features -D warnings clean. Full working tree: 36 passed/0 failed (existing tests green incl. vectors/parity/persistence round-trip via SenderStateStore CAS).

title: Border router: Core mesh-to-internet forwarding
description:
## Problem

The gateway app exists but only handles local interfaces (BLE/USB to mesh). The actual border router functionality — forwarding packets between mesh and internet — is not built.

## What exists
- LoRa L2 integration
- BLE interfaces (Meshtastic/MeshCore/LCI compat)
- CoAP server for local config
- RPL root config flag
- Announce ingestion

## What's missing (this epic)

### Core forwarding
- Mesh → Internet: packets from LoRa destined for off-mesh addresses
- Internet → Mesh: packets from upstream destined for mesh nodes
- RPL DODAG root: advertise prefix, accept DAOs, build routing table

### IPv6 integration
- Prefix delegation: get /64 from upstream (DHCPv6-PD or static)
- Prefix advertisement: RA to mesh with delegated prefix
- Routing: install routes for mesh nodes, forward bidirectionally

### IPv4 support (optional but practical)
- NAT64: translate IPv4 internet to IPv6 mesh
- DNS64: synthesize AAAA records for IPv4-only hosts
- Or: just require IPv6 upstream (simpler, less compatible)

## Architecture

```
Internet (IPv6 or IPv4)
        │
    [Backhaul]  ← WiFi, Ethernet, or cellular
        │
   ┌────┴────┐
   │ Border  │  ← This epic
   │ Router  │
   └────┬────┘
        │
    [LoRa L2]   ← Already exists
        │
   Mesh nodes
```

## Shared vs hardware-specific

### Shared (this epic)
- IPv6 forwarding logic
- RPL DODAG root implementation
- Prefix management
- Routing table for mesh nodes
- NAT64/DNS64 (if needed)

### Hardware-specific (separate beads)
- WiFi driver (ESP32, RPi)
- Ethernet driver (RPi, PoE gateways)
- Cellular modem (future)
- Platform-specific network config

## Dependencies

- RPL implementation (spec section 8)
- SCHC compression (already built)
- LoRa L2 (already built)

## Acceptance criteria

- Gateway receives IPv6 prefix from upstream
- Gateway advertises prefix to mesh via RPL DIO
- Mesh node can ping internet host (via gateway)
- Internet host can reach mesh node (via gateway)
- Works on at least one hardware target (Heltec V3 or RPi)
notes:
## Updated backhaul priority

Based on discussion, revised priority order:

### 1. Yggdrasil (global LICHEN backbone)
- Any LICHEN node can reach any other LICHEN node
- No RIR bureaucracy, cryptographic addressing
- See epic: project-LICHEN-zt3c

### 2. Tailscale/WireGuard (internet access)
- Works anywhere (behind NAT, IPv4-only)
- Mesh nodes reachable from your devices
- Easy setup

### 3. ULA (mesh-internal, always works)
- fd00:lichen::/32 + IID
- No config needed
- Baseline connectivity

### 4. DHCPv6-PD ("proper" IPv6)
- For enterprise/ISP deployments that have it
- Nice to have, not required

## Addressing summary

```
Local mesh:     fd00:lichen:<mesh>::<iid>  (ULA)
Global LICHEN:  02xx:...::<iid>            (Yggdrasil)
Internet:       via Tailscale/WireGuard    (overlay)
"Proper" IPv6:  via DHCPv6-PD             (if available)
```
## Addressing update: Drop ULA

Per Yggdrasil integration (project-LICHEN-zt3c), we're simplifying to:

### Node addresses
- fe80::<iid> — link-local (control plane)
- 02xx::<iid> — primary (derived from Ed25519, works everywhere)

### No more ULA
- Drop fd00:lichen::/32 prefix
- No prefix delegation needed for mesh-internal
- 02xx addresses work locally without Yggdrasil connectivity

### Gateway routing
```
if dst is link-local:
    forward via LoRa neighbor
elif dst is 02xx:
    if in_local_mesh(dst):
        forward via LoRa (RPL/gradient)
    else:
        forward via Yggdrasil
elif dst is internet (other):
    forward via Tailscale/backhaul
```

### Prefix delegation (p2y5.3) becomes optional
- Only needed for "real" internet IPv6 (GUA)
- Most deployments: Yggdrasil + Tailscale, no DHCPv6-PD needed
- Keep as option for enterprise deployments

title: tx_queue.rs: sequence counter wrapping could cause priority inversion
description:
TxQueue uses a u32 sequence counter that wraps via wrapping_add(). When the counter wraps around, older items (with high sequence numbers like 0xFFFFFFFF) will compare as 'newer' than recent items (with low sequence numbers like 0x00000001), causing priority inversion within the same priority level.

At 1 packet/second this takes ~136 years to wrap, so this is extremely unlikely in practice, but the theoretical bug exists. Consider using saturating_add() and clearing the queue when approaching saturation, or document the limitation.

File: rust/lichen-core/src/tx_queue.rs lines 176-177
notes: Verified current HEAD retains the historical wrap-safe serial comparison in TxItem::cmp and the focused fifo_across_sequence_wrap boundary test spanning u32::MAX-1, u32::MAX, 0, and 1. No regression and no source edit required. Validation: cargo test -p lichen-core tx_queue --lib (33 passed); cargo fmt --check --package lichen-core (pass); cargo clippy -p lichen-core --lib --no-deps -- -D warnings (pass).
