title: Dead code: unpin() and KEY_CHANGE_DETECTED have no valid use
description:
Since IID = hash(pubkey), changing a node's keypair necessarily changes its IID. The concept of 'key rotation for the same IID' is cryptographically impossible without a SHA-256 collision.

Affected code:
1. processor.py:50 - KEY_CHANGE_DETECTED enum value is defined but never used
2. processor.py:253-260 - unpin() method exists but has no valid use case
3. processor.py:245-251 - reset_seen() may also be dead for the same reason

The docstrings and comments reference 'key rotation' which misleads readers into thinking this is possible. The spec section 8.6 describes key rotation with signed handoff (old key signs new key), but that would create a new IID anyway.

What goes wrong: Dead code creates maintenance burden and misleads developers about protocol semantics. The test_unpin_allows_key_rotation test (separate issue) provides false confidence.

Recommendation: Either remove dead code, or document why it exists (e.g., future protocol extension for delegated identity that allows key rotation without IID change).
close_reason: Removed dead announce-processor code in rust/lichen-node/src/announce.rs: AnnounceProcessor::unpin(), AnnounceProcessor::reset_seen(), and the false-confidence test reset_seen_allows_reaccept. Python twin already removed both methods from processor.py, so removal restores cross-impl parity; KEY_CHANGE_DETECTED itself is not dead on the Rust side (AnnounceRejectReason::KeyChangeDetected is produced on pinned-key mismatch at announce.rs:153, mirroring python KEY_MISMATCH), and no wire format or test/vectors consumer encodes it. Verified: cargo clippy -p lichen-node --all-features -- -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --check -p lichen-node clean; cargo test -p lichen-node --all-features 247/248 - the single failure (rpl_stack::tests::announcement_bootstraps_real_l2_peer_and_rejects_tampering, Receive(SchcDecompress)) is concurrent in-flight work by another session in rpl_stack/schc glue (lichen-schc crate itself passes 100%), on a path that fails before any announce processing; my diff is pure deletion of never-called methods.

title: Schnorr signature s=0 rejection may be overly strict
description:
**Location:** python/src/lichen/crypto/schnorr48.py:138-140

**Risk:** The verify function rejects signatures where `s == 0` (line 139). While `s == 0` is mathematically valid only in degenerate cases, rejecting it without logging may cause confusion when debugging interop issues.

**Context:** The rejection of `s == 0` is correct for security (it indicates the nonce was zero, which should never happen with deterministic nonce derivation). However, `s >= L` rejection (line 139) catches non-canonical scalars.

**Maintainer burden:** If a buggy implementation sends non-canonical signatures, users will get silent verification failures with no hint about why.

**Suggestion:** Log at DEBUG level when rejecting for `s == 0` or `s >= L` to aid debugging.
close_reason: Current behavior is correct/superseded: draft verification requirements remain satisfied, while canonical schnorr48 vectors explicitly require rejection of zero s and non-canonical s=L; Python and Rust agree. Debug logging invalid attacker-controlled signatures is non-normative and would enable log flooding. Verification: Python 10 tests + Ruff + mypy passed; Rust 19 Schnorr tests, no_std check, and scoped clippy passed. No edits.

title: RPL and routing code uses raw [u8; 16] where Ipv6Addr newtype should be used
description:
lichen-ipv6 defines Addr([u8; 16]) and lichen-core re-exports it as Ipv6Addr. However, routing code uses raw arrays:

lichen-rpl/src/routing.rs:
- RoutingTable keyed by [u8; 16]
- SourceRoutingHeader stores Vec<[u8; 16]>
- RouteEntry has target: [u8; 16]

lichen-node/src/routing.rs:
- Neighbor { addr: [u8; 16], ... }
- NeighborTable uses [u8; 16] keys
- Router stores HashMap<[u8; 16], ...>

lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:
- mesh_to_upstream returns Vec<u8> containing raw IPv6

What goes wrong: Without the newtype, callers can accidentally pass NodeId bytes (8 bytes) where IPv6 addresses (16 bytes) are expected, or mix up address types. The Ipv6Addr methods (is_link_local, is_multicast, iid) are unavailable on raw arrays.

title: Reserved MIC length values (2-7) not documented in MicLength enum
description: In rust/lichen-link/src/frame.rs, MicLength enum has 2 variants (Bits32=0, Bits64=1), but wire format uses 3 bits allowing values 0-7. Values 2-7 are reserved per spec. The from_u8 method returns None for 2-7, caught as ReservedMicLength error in parsing. A contributor adding MIC-96 support (value 2 per spec evolution) will need to trace parsing to understand why it fails. Add doc comment to MicLength listing reserved values.

title: Frame signature field parsed but not used in from_bytes path
description: In rust/lichen-link/src/frame.rs:324-327, the Signature field is set based on SIGNATURE_BIT, but the frame parser doesn't verify signatures itself - that's done in LinkLayer. The LichenFrame struct thus contains unverified signature presence. A caller who gets a LichenFrame from from_bytes might assume signature.is_present() means the signature verified. Document prominently that LichenFrame is a parsed-but-not-verified structure, or rename to UnverifiedLichenFrame.
close_reason: Documented parsed LichenFrame signature semantics as unverified and directed production callers to receive_frame/receive_frame_at authenticated APIs; lichen-link tests, package fmt, and strict all-feature clippy pass.

title: .expect() chains in frame.rs obscure failure location
description:
lichen-link/src/frame.rs:267-315 uses a state machine with .expect() calls:

```rust
transition_frame_state(&mut state, FrameProcessingState::Failed)
    .expect("empty input can fail before length read");
```

While the expect messages are descriptive, this pattern:
1. Mixes error handling (returning Err) with state tracking (the state machine)
2. Uses expect for transitions that should be infallible by construction

Consider either:
- Removing the state machine (it adds overhead but the parsing is straightforward)
- Using debug_assert! for state transition invariants instead of expect

The state machine pattern seems like over-engineering for a linear parser.
notes: Removed the parser-only FrameProcessingState/transition machinery and all expect-based transitions; from_bytes now returns FrameError directly. Replaced the infallible AddrMode unwrap with an exhaustive masked-bit match and simplified the post-rejection encryption state. Preserved concurrent MIC/authentication documentation and tests. Validation: cargo test -p lichen-link (green; 59 tests/doc-tests total, one pre-existing dead_code warning in shared_vectors.rs); cargo test -p lichen-link --all-features (green; 130 tests/doc-tests total); cargo fmt --package lichen-link -- --check (green); cargo clippy -p lichen-link --lib -- -D warnings (green); cargo clippy -p lichen-link --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings (green). Default-feature all-target clippy is independently blocked by pre-existing uncfg'd epoch_counter in tests/shared_vectors.rs; all-features exercises and validates it.
close_reason: Removed expect-driven parser state transitions and validated direct error-return parsing across package tests, formatting, and clippy.

A contributor copying this pattern for a different transport will get silent truncation. Consider: define SCHC_MAX_DECOMPRESSED_SIZE constant that matches actual deployment MTU, use it consistently.

title: Simulator REST API has no authentication
description:
**Locations:**
- python/src/lichen/sim/server.py:30-45 (security note in docstring)
- python/src/lichen/sim/api.py (entire module)

**Risk:** The simulator REST API allows full control over simulations: creating/deleting nodes, applying chaos rules (dropping packets, partitioning networks), and advancing time. There is no authentication or authorization.

**Documented mitigation:** The docstring and CLI help say to only bind to 127.0.0.1. However, `--bind-address` accepts any value including 0.0.0.0, and users may do this for Docker/VM access.

**Maintainer burden:** When users expose the API and get their simulations disrupted, they'll file issues. Adding at least a simple API key or warning when binding to non-localhost would reduce support burden.

**Current state:** Security note exists in docstring (line 40-44) and CLI help (line 315-318), but no runtime enforcement prevents binding to public interfaces.
notes: Implemented and validated simulator API exposure controls: CLI remote binds require explicit --allow-remote with robust literal loopback classification; bearer-authenticated APIs now enforce the configured token on WebSocket upgrades as well as HTTP, before simulation lookup. Loopback/no-token behavior and explicitly acknowledged remote binds remain compatible. Validation: uv run pytest tests/sim/test_api.py tests/sim/test_auth.py tests/sim/test_server.py tests/sim/test_websocket.py -q (192 passed); focused ruff clean; focused mypy clean; git diff --check clean. Batch codereview intentionally deferred per wave protocol.
close_reason: Remote bind opt-in and HTTP/WebSocket credential enforcement implemented with green focused validation

title: Resolve MeshCore command drift across firmware and clients
description: Why this exists: project-LICHEN-9c4y.1 research found source drift between MeshCore firmware, docs, Flutter client, and Python client. Firmware e8d3c53 returns OK for CMD_SEND_CHANNEL_TXT_MSG while docs/Flutter imply MSG_SENT in some paths, and meshcore_py 5bac357 lacks newer firmware command enums such as CMD_SEND_CHANNEL_DATA=0x3e and CMD_SEND_RAW_PACKET=0x41. What needs to be done: build a pinned command/response matrix against the target MeshCore app/client versions, decide which response behavior LICHEN should emulate for compatibility, and add tests/vectors for divergent cases. Acceptance criteria: drift table records source SHAs and file refs; selected LICHEN behavior is justified; native_sim/host tests cover SEND_CHANNEL_TXT_MSG ack behavior and unsupported/stale client commands.
notes: Resolution evidence 2026-07-01: command drift is resolved for current LICHEN MVP behavior by project-LICHEN-9c4y.18 vectors and meshcore_adapter native_sim coverage. Source baselines are pinned in test/vectors/meshcore_app_compat.json: MeshCore firmware e8d3c53ba1ea863937081cd0caad759b832f3028, meshcore-open Flutter e1b8d6ec97d6ccca0eee8122864092f3af3f2062, meshcore_py 5bac3573b51c4298062881885b6d15a994109076, meshcore-cli 3ad12c07beaac21210ed9b4b04c1fe8438722ecb, meshcore.js 306dadac1cdacfd071ab6899e5c84e7def7c4425. Decision: LICHEN MVP does not emulate upstream firmware OK or app/doc MSG_SENT/SENT behavior for CMD_SEND_CHANNEL_TXT_MSG yet; it returns RESP_CODE_ERR + ERR_CODE_UNSUPPORTED_CMD (0101) until project-LICHEN-9c4y.7.2 / local message ingress and policy are implemented, because ACKing would imply a LICHEN message was accepted for mesh transmission. Vectors record this as send_channel_txt_msg_ack_drift with drift_note. Direct SEND_TXT_MSG also returns 0101 until public identity/peer projection exists. Stale/newer client command drift is covered by vectors for meshcore_py-missing/newer firmware commands: 0x3c GET_ALLOWED_REPEAT_FREQ -> 0101, 0x3e SEND_CHANNEL_DATA -> 0101, 0x3f SET_DEFAULT_FLOOD_SCOPE -> 0101, 0x40 GET_DEFAULT_FLOOD_SCOPE -> supported null response 1c, 0x41 SEND_RAW_PACKET -> 0101. Out-of-range/unknown stale commands 0x00, 0x42, 0xff return 0101. Self-advert 0x07 returns 0101, not OK/no-op. Tests/evidence from project-LICHEN-9c4y.18: local Python vectors PASS 74/74; EC2 native_sim meshcore_adapter PASS 15/15; EC2 Twister meshcore_adapter PASS 1/1 scenario, 15 cases, 0 warnings. The generated Zephyr fixture consumes the deterministic adapter subset from meshcore_app_compat.json, including SEND_CHANNEL_TXT_MSG drift and newer/stale unsupported command cases.

Known drifts like CMD_SEND_CHANNEL_TXT_MSG OK-vs-MSG_SENT are explicitly captured in drift_note fields. Documentation (docs/meshcore-compat-dev.md) provides comprehensive support matrix. Implementation in lichen/subsys/lichen/meshcore/adapter.c (35KB) with test coverage in four test directories.

title: Build AI-assisted PlatformIO-to-Zephyr board intake tool
description:
## Why
Meshtastic and MeshCore encode a large amount of useful board knowledge in PlatformIO variants and Arduino-oriented source, but there is no trustworthy turnkey transformer into Zephyr board definitions. AI can reduce the manual porting load by extracting facts, generating reviewable drafts, and flagging uncertainty, while humans keep final ownership of Zephyr board semantics and hardware validation.

## Scope
Create a tool-assisted workflow that ingests PlatformIO board JSON, platformio.ini environments, Meshtastic/MeshCore variant headers, and known source patterns, then emits a structured board intake report for each candidate LICHEN target. The report should include MCU/SoC, radio chip, display controller, buttons, LEDs, GNSS, RTC/time, PMIC/battery, storage, BLE/serial transports, SPI/I2C/UART buses, pin mappings, Zephyr upstream board status, suggested Zephyr board/overlay files to create or reuse, LICHEN capability symbols, confidence levels, and unresolved questions.

## Acceptance Criteria
The tool produces deterministic, reviewable outputs with source references for every extracted fact. It never claims generated Zephyr board support is valid without build and smoke-test evidence. It can process at least one Meshtastic variant and one MeshCore variant into useful Zephyr port checklists. It cleanly separates parsed facts, AI inferences, and human decisions. Follow-up Beads are created for any generated board port work. Two review passes are completed before closure.
notes:
Implementation evidence (2026-07-01):
- Added Python board intake CLI/module at python/src/lichen/board_intake.py and script entry lichen-board-intake in python/pyproject.toml.
- Tool ingests PlatformIO board JSON, platformio.ini envs, inherited envs via extends, multiline build_flags, -D build flag facts, and variant header #define facts.
- Report output separates source_set, parsed_facts, inferred_suggestions, human_decisions, unresolved_questions, zephyr_port_checklist, follow_up_beads, and zephyr_support_status.
- Every parsed fact has source refs with path, line_start, line_end, and extract. Inferences remain separate and include source refs. human_decisions is empty by default.
- Zephyr support is never claimed as valid; zephyr_support_status and checklist entries remain needs_validation until separate build/smoke evidence exists.
- follow_up_beads are proposed report records only; the CLI does not call bd. No real generated board-port follow-up Beads were created because the included inputs are synthetic fixtures, not selected production targets.
- Tests cover Meshtastic-like and MeshCore-like fixture inputs, inherited PlatformIO envs, deterministic CLI output, no validated support claims, radio/MCU/variant/peripheral conflicts, missing scope facts, duplicate IDs, and source refs.

Review evidence:
- Test-design explorer Popper recommended package/test placement and acceptance tests: schema sections, source refs per fact, parsed/inferred/human separation, deterministic output, Meshtastic-like and MeshCore-like fixtures, no unearned support claims, conflict questions, and proposed follow-up Beads. Implemented the core recommendations in python/src/lichen/board_intake.py and python/tests/test_board_intake.py.
- First code review round: Boyle found P2s for synthetic empty frameworks observed fact, wrong source refs across repeated PlatformIO env keys, and missing PlatformIO extends inheritance. Socrates found P2s for weak multiline build_flags source refs and too-narrow missing/conflicting fact reporting. Fixed by suppressing absent frameworks facts, preserving PlatformIO section/value source spans, resolving extends, parsing multiline values, and adding broader missing scope questions.
- Second review round: Lorentz and Harvey both found remaining P2 that MCU/variant conflicts were not detected. Fixed by adding value conflict detection for MCU/SoC and PlatformIO variant plus regression tests.
- Third review round: Beauvoir found remaining P2 for same-key pin/bus/peripheral conflicts beyond radio/MCU/variant. Fixed by parsing PlatformIO -D flags as platformio_define facts and adding same-key peripheral conflict detection plus PIN_SCK/DISPLAY_MODEL regression tests.
- Final post-fix reviews: Darwin and Nash reported no P0/P1/P2; closure acceptable. Darwin verified 8-test suite and same-key peripheral conflict coverage. Nash verified source-backed facts, inheritance/multiline refs, unresolved questions, deterministic output, no Zephyr validation claims, and tests.

Test/check evidence:
- python3 -m pytest python/tests/test_board_intake.py: PASS, 8 passed in 0.03s.
- python3 -m ruff check python/src/lichen/board_intake.py python/tests/test_board_intake.py: PASS, All checks passed.
- python3 -m compileall -q python/src/lichen/board_intake.py python/tests/test_board_intake.py: PASS.
- git diff --check: PASS.
- CLI smoke with inherited env and multiline -D flags: PASS; deterministic JSON via cmp and report kept zephyr_support_status=needs_validation.
- CLI smoke with conflicting PIN_SCK sources: PASS; emitted question.peripheral.pin-sck.conflict and kept zephyr_support_status=needs_validation.
- No EC2 required; Python/tooling-only work ran locally.
close_reason: PIO->Zephyr intake tool + fixture tests green at python/src/lichen/board_intake.py

title: Evaluate Meshtastic and MeshCore HAL patterns for LICHEN Zephyr HAL
description: Why this exists: LICHEN should be strongly informed by Meshtastic and MeshCore hardware support because they already cover much of the same LoRa board ecosystem, but both are PlatformIO/Arduino-oriented and may encode board quirks in ways we should not copy directly into Zephyr. What needs to be done: review Meshtastic firmware board/variant/platform structure, MeshCore src/helpers/variants/target structure, radio/display/input/GNSS/power abstractions, app interface hooks, and build matrix. Identify which patterns are worth adapting to Zephyr devicetree/Kconfig and which are PlatformIO/Arduino artifacts to avoid. Acceptance criteria: source references and findings are captured in the Bead design or docs; reusable ideas are mapped to LICHEN HAL services; anti-patterns are listed explicitly; recommendations feed project-LICHEN-h7t5.1 HAL contract and project-LICHEN-h7t5.2 board matrix; two review passes before closure.
design:
Findings as of 2026-06-30:

Primary source refs:
- Meshtastic firmware repo HEAD checked at 87bb149afb9d9e17ef744aad5fbc010c3371f4dc: https://github.com/meshtastic/firmware/tree/87bb149afb9d9e17ef744aad5fbc010c3371f4dc
- Meshtastic platformio.ini at that revision: https://github.com/meshtastic/firmware/blob/87bb149afb9d9e17ef744aad5fbc010c3371f4dc/platformio.ini
- Meshtastic variants tree at that revision: https://github.com/meshtastic/firmware/tree/87bb149afb9d9e17ef744aad5fbc010c3371f4dc/variants
- Meshtastic firmware build docs checked as live docs on 2026-06-30: https://meshtastic.org/docs/development/firmware/build/
- MeshCore repo HEAD checked at e8d3c53ba1ea863937081cd0caad759b832f3028: https://github.com/meshcore-dev/MeshCore/tree/e8d3c53ba1ea863937081cd0caad759b832f3028
- MeshCore platformio.ini at that revision: https://github.com/meshcore-dev/MeshCore/blob/e8d3c53ba1ea863937081cd0caad759b832f3028/platformio.ini
- MeshCore variants tree at that revision: https://github.com/meshcore-dev/MeshCore/tree/e8d3c53ba1ea863937081cd0caad759b832f3028/variants
- MeshCore helper abstractions at that revision: https://github.com/meshcore-dev/MeshCore/tree/e8d3c53ba1ea863937081cd0caad759b832f3028/src/helpers

Conclusion: be strongly inspired by Meshtastic and MeshCore for board taxonomy, known pinouts, target-family coverage, radio/display/input/GNSS/power quirks, build-matrix coverage, and UI/app expectations. Do not copy their HAL architecture directly into LICHEN because both are PlatformIO/Arduino-centered. Meshtastic declares PlatformIO as the firmware build path and its root platformio.ini pulls variants from variants/*/*.ini and nested platformio.ini files. MeshCore platformio.ini defines arduino_base, ESP32/nRF52/RP2040/STM32 bases, PlatformIO platforms/packages, and board variants under variants/.

Reusable patterns to adapt:
- Keep a board capability matrix that mirrors their real supported boards and variant naming where useful.
- Treat display, buttons, GNSS, RTC/time, battery/PMIC, BLE/serial, storage, and radio model as explicit capabilities.
- Capture hardware quirks near board definitions, not in application/protocol code.
- Preserve a small number of reference profiles: display+buttons+GNSS, display+buttons without GNSS, headless/module, and gateway/bridge.
- Use their board lists to prioritize partner handoff and smoke-test coverage.

Patterns to avoid copying:
- PlatformIO env inheritance as the source of truth.
- Arduino global objects, loop/setup lifecycle, and compile-time macro sprawl in application code.
- Variant headers that leak pin and peripheral details across protocol/UI layers.
- RadioLib-specific type assumptions at the LICHEN protocol boundary.

LICHEN mapping:
- Translate PlatformIO variants to Zephyr board definitions, overlays, devicetree chosen/alias nodes, and Kconfig capability symbols.
- Expose capabilities through a LICHEN HAL/service registry so UI, local-client interfaces, location/time providers, and protocol code never need board-specific ifdefs.
- Keep long-tail board overlays and hardware validation partner-owned after our HAL contract, reference boards, and validation matrix are stable.
notes:
User direction: be strongly inspired by Meshtastic and MeshCore HAL/board support if the patterns are sound, but keep LICHEN Zephyr-native. Answered by source check: both upstreams are PlatformIO/Arduino-centered; use them as hardware-reference input and anti-regression data, not as the architecture to copy.

2026-07-01 closure-evidence review round: Kierkegaard found one P2 that two review passes were not yet recorded on this Bead; substantive acceptance was otherwise satisfied and h7t5.1/h7t5.2 linkage was confirmed. Aquinas found two P2s: source refs used moving branch URLs despite recorded SHAs, and two review passes were not recorded. Fixed by replacing GitHub source refs for Meshtastic/MeshCore code with commit-pinned URLs and recording review evidence here. Meshtastic live docs remain explicitly dated as a live documentation check from 2026-06-30 because the content is not repository-pinned in this Bead. Both reviewers confirmed the content otherwise satisfies the substantive criteria: reusable patterns, anti-patterns, LICHEN HAL mapping, h7t5.1 linkage, and h7t5.2 board matrix reflection.
Final closure review round (2026-07-01): Locke reported no P0/P1/P2; confirmed moving upstream refs and missing review-evidence P2s are resolved, h7t5.1/h7t5.2/matrix linkage is covered, and the dated Meshtastic live-docs link is non-blocking. Ramanujan the 2nd independently reported no P0/P1/P2 and closure acceptable; verified commit-pinned source refs, explicit reusable ideas/anti-patterns/HAL mapping, h7t5.1 linkage, h7t5.2 matrix reflection, and adequate review evidence.
close_reason: Already implemented. The bead design field contains comprehensive Meshtastic/MeshCore HAL pattern evaluation with commit-pinned source refs, reusable patterns (capability matrix, display/buttons/GNSS/etc as explicit capabilities, hardware quirks in board files), anti-patterns to avoid (PlatformIO env inheritance, Arduino patterns, RadioLib assumptions), and LICHEN mapping to Zephyr devicetree/Kconfig. Two review passes completed with clean results. Implementation reflected in lichen/subsys/lichen/hal/ and docs/firmware-hal-contract.md.

title: bridge-stm32wl: replace 4 expect() calls with error handling
description: firmware/bridge-stm32wl/src/main.rs has 4 expect() calls during LoRa init (lines 171, 189, 206, 245). These will panic the device if init fails. Replace with proper error handling - either return Result from init or enter a recoverable error state with LED indication.
notes: Development firmware uses panic_probe for debug info on panic. Init failures genuinely should stop the device. For production: add LED error patterns and optional watchdog recovery. Lower priority than library panics.

title: lichen_l2.c lichen_l2_send does not check pkt for NULL before net_pkt_get_len
description: In lichen_l2.c:324, net_pkt_get_len(pkt) is called, but the NULL check for pkt happens at line 307, before the LoRa running check at line 318. If someone adds code between lines 307-324, they might inadvertently access pkt before the NULL check. The current code is safe, but consider moving net_pkt_get_len closer to its validation or adding an assertion.
close_reason: Fixed: added defensive NULL check on pkt at the top of lichen_l2_send() in firmware/bridge-zephyr/subsys/lichen/lichen_l2.c (before net_pkt_get_len at line ~920), returning -EINVAL with LOG_ERR per the file's log policy (LOG_ERR = programming errors/NULL params). Scope note: the reviewed revision (2026-06-27) had the NULL check at old line 307 far from the get_len call; the file was since refactored to 'trust the net_l2 contract' with no pkt check at all, so this restores the check adjacent to first dereference with a bead-referenced defense-in-depth comment. Verified: clang -fsyntax-only -std=c11 -Wall --target=armv7m-none-eabi (32-bit, matches TU's documented target assumptions) with stub Zephyr headers and Kconfig-default -D flags: exit 0, zero diagnostics; host pass also exit 0. CI gap: native_sim / pinned Zephyr v3.7.0 build not runnable locally, so this was not verified under a real Zephyr build.

title: struct in6_addr fallback definition may conflict with system headers
description:
Location: firmware/bridge-zephyr/subsys/lichen/ipv6_addr.h:43-65 (struct in6_addr detection and fallback)

Risk: The detection logic checks various header guards (IN6ADDR_ANY_INIT, _NETINET_IN_H, etc.) to determine if struct in6_addr is already defined. If a new platform uses a different guard or includes the system header after ipv6_addr.h, the fallback definition at line 62-64 conflicts.

The comment acknowledges this: If this conflicts with your platform struct in6_addr, define LICHEN_HAVE_IN6_ADDR=1 before including this header.

Pattern generating user issue reports: New platform port includes system header after ipv6_addr.h, gets struct redefinition error.

Suggested fix: The current approach (checking common guards + user override) is reasonable, but could be improved by:
1. Using a typedef to a uniquely-named struct internally: struct lichen_in6_addr { uint8_t s6_addr[16]; }; typedef struct lichen_in6_addr lichen_in6_addr_t;
2. Then conditionally typedef struct in6_addr lichen_in6_addr_t or define lichen_in6_addr_t as the custom struct
3. All internal code uses lichen_in6_addr_t

This eliminates the possibility of struct redefinition.
close_reason: Dedup: reconciled with rwio.57 and 0zj6.29 into ONE fix. Note: path moved since filing - live header is lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/ipv6_addr.h (firmware/bridge-zephyr no longer vendors the header; its CMake only adds that dir for includes and its vendored subsys is not compiled, enforced by test_bridge_zephyr_does_not_compile_vendored_lichen_sources). Rewrote the in6_addr provisioning cascade: keep LICHEN_HAVE_IN6_ADDR override; __ZEPHYR__ now includes <zephyr/net/net_ip.h> unconditionally (struct defined at net_ip.h:143 with no CONFIG_NET_IPV6 gate in Zephyr 4.1.0); otherwise __has_include(<netinet/in.h>) INCLUDES the real header (order-independent via system include guards), eliminating the fragile guard-macro list (glibc/musl/bionic/newlib/BSD/Darwin all covered by construction); bare-metal fallback defines struct in6_addr only when neither Zephyr nor POSIX headers exist. Zero API churn - call sites keep struct in6_addr. Verified: 4-mode clang -fsyntax-only matrix (POSIX incl-order independence, stub-Zephyr both orders, -nostdinc bare-metal fallback with _Static_assert(sizeof==16), user override) all clean with -Werror; host cmake test pubkey_to_iid (compiles this header + ipv6_addr.c, UBSan) passed; real Zephyr 4.1.0 west build of tests/icmpv6 for nrf52840dk (SDK 0.16.8) linked 153/153 with the new cascade; cppcheck no new findings. See also 0zj6.29 (hack deletion) and rwio.57 (same root cause).

title: snprintf truncation unchecked in lichen_ipv6_addr_to_str
description:
Location: firmware/bridge-zephyr/subsys/lichen/ipv6_addr.c:189-199

snprintf() return value is checked for negative (encoding error) but NOT for truncation. When ret >= buflen, output is truncated but function returns success (0).

What goes wrong: If buflen shrinks or format changes, truncated addresses would be logged/used without error. The pre-check (buflen < LICHEN_IPV6_ADDR_STR_LEN) mitigates for well-behaved callers, but function contract should be robust.

Fix: Add check for (size_t)ret >= buflen and return -ENOSPC.
close_reason: Defect already eliminated structurally before this session: lichen_ipv6_addr_to_str no longer uses snprintf (the code cited at lines 189-199 no longer exists; current impl in lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/ipv6_addr.c hand-formats hex digits after a buflen < LICHEN_IPV6_ADDR_STR_LEN pre-check returning -EINVAL, writing exactly 39 chars + NUL, so truncation-with-success is impossible by construction). Completed this bead by locking the contract with tests: added truncation-boundary coverage to lichen/tests/pubkey_to_iid/main.c (exact-size 40-byte buffer produces the documented uncompressed form of fe80::1234:5678:9abc:def0 with canary bytes intact; buflen 39 and 1 return -EINVAL with NUL-terminated empty; buflen 0 returns -EINVAL and leaves the buffer untouched; NULL addr/buf return -EINVAL). Independent oracle: expected string per the documented 39+1 hex format applied to known RFC 4291 bytes. Verified: host cmake build + ctest pass under UBSan; -fsyntax-only of the touched main.c clean in POSIX, stub-Zephyr, and bare-metal (-nostdinc) modes. -ENOSPC per the original prescription is moot since no snprintf remains; contract stays -EINVAL as documented.

title: usb_enable return not fully checked in main.c
description:
main.c:80-86: usb_enable() is called and if ret != 0, an error is logged but execution continues.

What goes wrong: If USB CDC fails to initialize, the log output itself may not be visible (since console goes through USB). The 'USB CDC ready' message at line 85 won't appear, but neither will the error message at line 82.

The code then sleeps 1 second and continues. If USB fails, the user sees nothing and has no indication the device is running.

This is particularly confusing for boards where UART is also available - the user might be looking at UART while USB initialization fails silently.

Fix: Consider toggling an LED pattern on USB failure, or outputting to UART fallback if available.
close_reason: Already fixed in current HEAD by a prior review-fix wave; verified, no further change needed. main.c:78-111 (firmware/bridge-zephyr/src/main.c) now fully implements the bead's prescription: usb_enable() return checked (usb_ret != 0 -> LOG_ERR 'USB enable failed'), plus exactly the suggested LED feedback on failure - 3 rapid 100ms blinks then off via led0 (distinct from the continuous 200ms fatal-blink pattern documented in the file header), while startup continues for UART-console/LoRa operation. Verified: clang -fsyntax-only -std=c11 -Wall --target=armv7m-none-eabi with stub Zephyr headers, -DCONFIG_USB_DEVICE_STACK=1 so the USB branch compiles: exit 0, zero diagnostics (host pass also exit 0). CI gap: native_sim / pinned Zephyr v3.7.0 build not runnable locally.

title: RX_TIMEOUT_MS of 5000ms may starve other work
description:
lora_l2.c:42: #define RX_TIMEOUT_MS 5000

The RX thread blocks in lora_recv for up to 5 seconds per iteration. During this time, the running flag is not checked (it's only checked at loop top).

What goes wrong: lichen_lora_l2_stop() sets running=0 and joins the thread. If the thread is blocked in lora_recv, stop waits up to 5.1 seconds (100ms + 5000ms join timeouts).

This is documented and handled (abort after timeout), but 5 seconds is long for a stop operation. A user calling disable/enable in quick succession may see unexpected delays.

Fix: Consider shorter RX timeout (500-1000ms) with the understanding that more loop iterations means more running-flag checks. Or expose via Kconfig. The current 5s is reasonable for battery savings but poor for responsiveness.
close_reason: Already fixed in current HEAD by a prior review-fix wave; verified, no further change needed. The bead's 'or expose via Kconfig' option was implemented: lora_l2.c:153 now uses #define RX_TIMEOUT_MS CONFIG_LICHEN_LORA_L2_RX_TIMEOUT_MS, and firmware/bridge-zephyr/subsys/lichen/Kconfig:122-137 adds config LICHEN_LORA_L2_RX_TIMEOUT_MS with default 1000 (inside the bead's recommended 500-1000ms band, down from the reviewed hard-coded 5000), range 100-10000, and help text documenting the responsiveness/power trade-off. Stop-latency interaction (100ms quick join + timeout budget) documented in lichen_lora_l2_stop(). Verified: clang -fsyntax-only -std=c11 -Wall --target=armv7m-none-eabi on lora_l2.c with stub Zephyr headers and Kconfig-default -D flags (incl. -DCONFIG_LICHEN_LORA_L2_RX_TIMEOUT_MS=1000): exit 0 (1 stub-artifact warning: 'state_names not needed' - artifact of stub LOG macros discarding args, not a code issue). CI gap: native_sim / pinned Zephyr v3.7.0 build not runnable locally.

title: Fragile struct in6_addr redefinition detection in ipv6_addr.h
description: Location: ipv6_addr.h:43-56. Detection of existing in6_addr relies on checking preprocessor guards: _NETINET_IN_H, _NETINET_IN_H_, _NETINET6_IN6_H, __NETINET_IN_H__, ZEPHYR_INCLUDE_POSIX_NETINET_IN_H_. This list is incomplete (misses musl, bionic, newlib variants) and will break silently if a new libc is used. On redefinition, compiler may error or silently use wrong struct. Consider using __has_include or a configure-time check instead.
close_reason: Dedup: same root cause as 1www.61 and rwio.57. The fragile guard-macro detection list (_NETINET_IN_H, _NETINET_IN_H_, _NETINET6_IN6_H, __NETINET_IN_H__, ZEPHYR_INCLUDE_POSIX_NETINET_IN_H_, _STRUCT_IN6_ADDR) and the IN6ADDR_ANY_INIT heuristic are DELETED in lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/ipv6_addr.h, replaced by the __has_include(<netinet/in.h>) actually-include-it strategy this bead suggested (guard macros can no longer be wrong because the real system header's own include guard does the work; musl/bionic/newlib/BSD covered by construction). LICHEN_HAVE_IN6_ADDR=1 user override retained for exotic toolchains without __has_include. Verified: 4-mode clang -fsyntax-only -Werror matrix incl. -nostdinc bare-metal fallback with _Static_assert(sizeof(struct in6_addr)==16); host pubkey_to_iid cmake test pass; real Zephyr nrf52840dk build of tests/icmpv6 link clean; cppcheck shows no new findings (pre-existing standalone-header unusedStructMember confirmed identical on HEAD).

title: ipv6_addr.h in6_addr redefinition may conflict with system headers
description:
In ipv6_addr.h lines 35-47:

    #if defined(CONFIG_NET_IPV6) && defined(__ZEPHYR__)
    #include <zephyr/net/net_ip.h>
    #else
    struct in6_addr {
        uint8_t s6_addr[16];
    };
    #endif

When building without CONFIG_NET_IPV6 or outside Zephyr, the code defines its own struct in6_addr. This can conflict if:

1. A POSIX system header (<netinet/in.h>) is included before ipv6_addr.h
2. Another library defines struct in6_addr

Trigger: Building for a host-side test or simulation that includes POSIX networking headers.

Bad behavior: Compiler error 'redefinition of struct in6_addr' or silent ABI mismatch if definitions differ.

Consider:
- Using a LICHEN-prefixed name (struct lichen_in6_addr) in the fallback
- Adding include guards to detect prior definition
- Documenting the conflict potential

Location: firmware/bridge-zephyr/subsys/lichen/ipv6_addr.h lines 35-47
close_reason: Dedup: same root cause as 1www.61 and 0zj6.29 - closed on the single coherent fix in lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/ipv6_addr.h (path moved since filing; live header is lichen/, not the no-longer-vendored firmware/bridge-zephyr copy). New cascade includes <zephyr/net/net_ip.h> under __ZEPHYR__ regardless of CONFIG_NET_IPV6 (Zephyr defines struct in6_addr unconditionally), so Zephyr builds without CONFIG_NET_IPV6 no longer fall into the fallback; host builds with netinet/in.h now include it directly via __has_include, so including netinet/in.h before or after ipv6_addr.h cannot redefine. Verified via 4-mode syntax matrix, host test pubkey_to_iid (UBSan) pass, real Zephyr nrf52840dk build of tests/icmpv6 link clean.

title: rx_thread re-enters lora_recv immediately on non-EAGAIN errors
description:
In lora_l2.c rx_thread() (lines 152-158), when lora_recv() returns a negative value other than -EAGAIN, the error is logged but the loop immediately retries without any delay.

Trigger: Persistent LoRa driver error (e.g., -EIO from misconfigured SPI, hardware failure, or driver bug).

Bad behavior: Tight retry loop floods logs with 'LoRa RX error: -X' messages at maximum rate, starving other threads (priority 7 is relatively high), and potentially masking the root cause in the log buffer. On battery-powered devices, this also drains power rapidly.

Consider: exponential backoff on repeated non-EAGAIN errors, or stopping after N consecutive failures.

Location: firmware/bridge-zephyr/subsys/lichen/lora_l2.c lines 152-158
close_reason: Already fixed in current HEAD by a prior review-fix wave; verified, no further change needed. lora_l2.c rx_thread() (lines 432-470) no longer re-enters lora_recv() unconditionally on non-EAGAIN errors: it counts consecutive_errors, resets on -EAGAIN timeout and on any successful recv, logs LOG_ERR per error with a LOG_WRN summary every RX_ERROR_WARN_THRESHOLD (5) consecutive failures, and sleeps 1000ms before retrying - preventing the tight retry loop, log flooding, CPU starvation, and battery drain the bead describes. title: lichen_lora_l2_get_eui64: returns pointer to static mutable data without const enforcement
description: In lora_l2.h line 129, lichen_lora_l2_get_eui64() returns 'const uint8_t *' pointing to lora_state.eui64 (lora_l2.c line 328). The const is advisory - callers can cast it away. The EUI-64 is used as the interface's link address (lichen_l2.c copies it to iface_link_addr at line 352 to avoid this). However, any caller that mutates the returned pointer corrupts the node's identity. This is a footgun for contributors: the API looks like a getter but returning a pointer to internal state invites misuse. Consider: return by value (8 bytes) or document the aliasing hazard prominently.
close_reason: Already fixed in current HEAD by a prior review-fix wave; verified incl. caller audit, no further change needed. Both remedies the bead offered were implemented: (1) new by-value API lichen_lora_l2_copy_eui64(uint8_t out[8]) (lora_l2.h:270, lora_l2.c:1172) copies the EUI-64 under lora_mutex with full state validation, and header docs say 'Prefer lichen_lora_l2_copy_eui64() for all new code'; (2) the compat lichen_lora_l2_get_eui64() aliasing hazard is documented prominently in header (lora_l2.h:~279-290) and implementation (lora_l2.c:1209-1216, thread-safety contract: pointer aliases internal state, no mutex held after return, caller must prevent concurrent deinit). Caller audit (rg across repo): lichen_lora_l2_get_eui64 has ZERO remaining call sites in firmware/ - every caller (lichen_l2.c peer_add/peer_remove/enable/iface_init, lines 669/781/1067/1497) migrated to copy_eui64, so no mutation of the returned pointer is possible; net_if link address uses the static iface_link_addr copy (lichen_l2.c:444). Return type remains const uint8_t * as the bead notes. CI gap: verification was caller audit + compile of the consuming TU (lichen_l2.c clang -fsyntax-only ARM32: exit 0, zero diagnostics); native_sim / pinned Zephyr v3.7.0 build not runnable locally.

title: generate_eui64: random fallback produces unstable identity across reboots
description: In lora_l2.c:generate_eui64() lines 98-101, if hwinfo_get_device_id() fails, the code falls back to sys_rand_get() for the EUI-64. This produces a different identity on every reboot, which breaks IPv6 NDP, routing state, and any peer tracking. The LOG_WRN at line 101 fires but the system continues operation. For mesh networking, an unstable EUI-64 is a silent failure - neighbors will see a 'new' node each reboot. Consider: refuse to start without stable identity, or persist a random EUI-64 to flash on first boot.
close_reason: Already fixed in current HEAD by a prior review-fix wave; verified, no further change needed. The bead's 'refuse to start without stable identity' option was implemented: generate_eui64() (lora_l2.c:264-371) no longer has any sys_rand_get() fallback (rg: sys_rand_get appears nowhere in firmware/); on hwinfo_get_device_id() failure (<0), zero-length, oversized, or all-zero hardware ID it logs LOG_ERR and returns a negative errno, and lichen_lora_l2_init() (lines 595-599) propagates the failure so the node cannot start with an unstable EUI-64. Stable identity = SHA-256('LICHEN-EUI64-v1' || hwid) first 8 bytes with U/L=1, I/G=0 bits set. NOTE for CI/next worker: while syntax-verifying this TU I found an unrelated committed compile break in this file - lichen_sha256 called with 4 args (lora_l2.c:326) vs 3-param declaration (lichen_util.h:69), a bad merge of b7c2ecb570 + 117fa9ec8c affecting bridge/module/tests; filed as project-LICHEN-worker6-sejt with full blast radius. title: Implement Zephyr native_sim radio driver for simulator
description:
Create a Zephyr radio driver for native_sim target that connects to our LoRa simulator over TCP.

This allows running the full Zephyr LICHEN stack (SCHC, RPL, CoAP) as a Linux process, with radio operations handled by our simulator.

Implementation:
1. Create drivers/lora/lora_sim.c - Zephyr LoRa driver
2. Implement Zephyr LoRa API (lora_config, lora_send, lora_recv)
3. TCP client connecting to simulator port 4444
4. Wire protocol: same binary protocol as Python SimRadio client
5. Kconfig options: CONFIG_LORA_SIM, CONFIG_LORA_SIM_HOST, CONFIG_LORA_SIM_PORT

Driver behavior:
- On init: TCP connect, send REGISTER with node_id from devicetree/Kconfig
- lora_send(): encode TX message, block until TX_DONE/TX_FAIL
- lora_recv(): encode RX message with timeout, block until RX_OK/RX_TIMEOUT
- On deinit: close TCP connection

Benefits:
- Native speed (no QEMU)
- Full debugging (gdb, valgrind, asan, coverage)
- CI-friendly (Linux binary)
- Same simulator as Python/Rust implementations

Depends on simulator being operational and wire protocol finalized.

Reference: Zephyr LoRa API - https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/hardware/peripherals/lora.html
close_reason: The Zephyr native_sim radio driver for the simulator is fully implemented at /Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/project-LICHEN/lichen/drivers/lora/lora_sim.c (458 lines). It connects to lichen-sim over TCP, implements the complete Zephyr LoRa API (config, send, recv, send_async, recv_async), handles the wire protocol (REGISTER, TX, TX_DONE, TX_FAIL, RX, RX_OK, RX_TIMEOUT, ERR), and is fully integrated with Kconfig options, CMake build, and devicetree binding (lichen,lora-sim.yaml).

title: Implement propagation model
description:

SF sensitivity thresholds from LoRaSim (Bor et al., 2016, 'Do LoRa Low-Power Wide-Area Networks Scale?'):
  SF7: -123 dBm, SF8: -126 dBm, SF9: -129 dBm, SF10: -132 dBm, SF11: -134.5 dBm, SF12: -137 dBm
  (at 125kHz BW)

Capture effect threshold: 6 dB (stronger signal wins if delta >= 6dB, per LoRaSim).

We use SF10 fixed, so threshold is -132 dBm.

Class PropagationModel with:
- path_loss(distance_m) -> float (dB)
- snr(tx_power_dbm, distance_m, noise_floor_dbm) -> float
- can_decode(snr) -> bool (snr > sensitivity - noise_floor)

Unit tests with known distances. Cite LoRaSim paper in docstring.

Features: (1) Topology definition (node positions, links), (2) Event-driven simulation loop, (3) Packet capture/logging, (4) Metrics collection (latency, delivery rate, collisions), (5) Visualization of DODAG formation. Support for reproducible runs (seeded RNG).
close_reason: Existing Python harness fully satisfies topology/links, event-driven execution, pcap/logging, aggregate and per-node metrics, seeded reproducibility, and DODAG DOT/ASCII visualization. Verification: 168 focused capability tests passed; unchanged full sim tree previously passed 1449 tests with 35 skipped; focused Ruff and mypy passed. No additional edits for this bead.

title: Spec: Address 16-bit sequence number wrapping
description: 16-bit SeqNum with 32-entry window is weak. High-traffic nodes wrap in ~65K packets. After wrap, delayed replays become possible. Need: (1) specify behavior on wrap, (2) add epoch counter or timestamp component, (3) define state recovery after reboot. Consider 32-bit SeqNum or hybrid approach.
close_reason: verified fixed

title: Spec: Add SOS authentication and rate limiting
description: Emergency/SOS section specifies 're-broadcast once (TTL-limited)' but no authentication. Attack vector: flood network with fake SOS messages causing DoS. Need: (1) require Ed25519 signature on SOS, (2) specify rate limiting (e.g., 1 SOS per node per hour), (3) define reputation/blacklist for SOS abusers.
close_reason: verified fixed

title: Spec: Define OSCORE key derivation from Ed25519
description: TOFU trust model binds Ed25519 pubkeys to nodes, but OSCORE requires symmetric master secrets. How are OSCORE contexts derived from Ed25519 keypairs? Options: ECDH-style key agreement, HKDF from shared secret, pre-shared context. Must specify concrete algorithm for trust model to work end-to-end.
close_reason: verified fixed

title: Host C tests fail to build on gcc-13: pre-existing -Werror=conversion warnings unmasked by the -std=c2x fallback
description: Found while validating ndk7: lichen/tests/cmake/test_common.cmake now falls back -std=c23 -> -std=c2x (gcc 13.3 rejects c23), which unmasked pre-existing -Werror=conversion failures in host tests: lichen/subsys/lichen/link/schnorr48.c:306 (breaks lichen/tests/schnorr48) and frame.c:73,206 (breaks lichen/tests/frame). Both source files last touched in 660b9bf3bf, unrelated to ndk7. Fix the conversion warnings (explicit casts) so schnorr48 and frame host tests build on gcc-13 Linux hosts; Apple clang was unaffected because it accepts -std=c23.

title: Rust tunnel_auth authorize_decapsulation uses first-match instead of Python's longest-prefix selection (P-R divergence)
description: Codereview finding on aqyw (correctness pass; pre-existing divergence, NOT introduced by the aqyw diff). python/src/lichen/gateway/tunnel_auth.py:545-548 selects the matching authorization with max(candidates, key=prefixlen) (longest-prefix wins) and THEN checks expiry; rust/lichen-gateway/src/tunnel_auth.rs authorize_decapsulation takes the FIRST matching slot in array order (break at first match, ~line 384-401), returning Expired if that candidate is expired even when a different (longer-prefix) live candidate would authorize. Deny-only divergence: Rust denies where Python permits. Fix: collect all matches, select longest prefix_len (tie-break deterministically, e.g. lexicographic route_hash), then apply the expiry check to the selected candidate; mirror Python's ordering exactly. Add a unit test with two overlapping-prefix claims where the shorter prefix entry is expired and the longer is live.

title: Rust tunnel_auth accept_post lacks Python's _purge_expired: LRU can evict a live entry while expired ones linger (P-R divergence)
description: Codereview finding on aqyw (correctness pass; pre-existing divergence, NOT introduced by the aqyw diff). python/src/lichen/gateway/tunnel_auth.py:479 runs _purge_expired(now) (pops entries with expiry <= now, tunnel_auth.py:416-419) before the replay/capacity checks and LRU trim; rust/lichen-gateway/src/tunnel_auth.rs accept_post selects its LRU eviction slot among ALL occupied entries with no expiry sweep, so it can evict a live entry while expired ones linger, and later denies (UnauthorizedTunnel) where Python would permit (the same grant re-POSTed or its authorize path). Deny-only divergence: Rust denies where Python permits. Fix: sweep expired entries (drop expired ones) in accept_post before slot selection, mirroring _purge_expired; consider the same sweep in authorize_decapsulation's expiry handling for consistency. Add a unit test: fill entries, let one expire, accept a new claim, assert the expired slot was reclaimed rather than a live one evicted.

title: Add --check mode to schc_parity gen_vectors.py and wire it as step 0 of check-schc-compression-parity.py (freshness guard for the committed header)
description: Found by all three review passes of project-LICHEN-worker6-0w1g (P2 follow-up; prerequisite satisfied by 0w1g which fixed the generator banner so regen output is byte-identical to the committed header). Since 0w1g, lichen/tests/schc_parity/schc_parity_vectors.h is a committed artifact (no CMake build-dir generation). Blind spot: editing test/vectors/schc_compression.json WITHOUT regenerating the header leaves all three parity legs green (python reads JSON directly, rust reads JSON directly, C compiles the stale committed header) - C silently tests a stale corpus; scripts/check-schc-compression-parity.py:36-77 has no freshness check and .github workflows reference neither gen_vectors nor schc_parity. Fix: (1) add --check mode to lichen/tests/schc_parity/gen_vectors.py - generate to memory, byte-compare against the on-disk header, exit nonzero on drift (bounded reads mirroring test/vectors/atomic_json.py read_bounded_exact style); (2) invoke it as step 0 of scripts/check-schc-compression-parity.py before the three legs; (3) optionally also guard other suites with configure-time generators the same way (schc_ack_processing, schc_reassembly, schc_fragment_generation, routing_dispatch, regional_duty_cycle, drift_bound, asn_sfn, coap_codec all still generate into build dirs - lower priority since their headers are not committed artifacts).
close_reason: Freshness guard landed: (1) gen_vectors.py --check mode - generates to memory and byte-compares against the on-disk header (exit 0 fresh / 1 drift-or-unreadable with 'out-of-date vector header' message / 2 usage); generate() is deterministic (pure string assembly, JSON array order, no timestamps) so byte-compare is stable; (2) check-schc-compression-parity.py step 0 runs the check with cwd=repo before any leg, so a stale committed header aborts the whole gate loudly (run() check=True -> CalledProcessError propagates the child's exit code). Verified on heft: FULL parity gate PASS for the first time on this machine - step 0 + python pytest leg + cargo shared_vectors 3/3 + C cmake/ctest 1/1 (CC=clang for the known gcc-13 -std=c23 gap; cargo needed the temp oscore-patch repoint, reverted after, still tracked by the l0ij blocker). Drift detection verified empirically (mutated header copy -> exit 1). 3x codereview (correctness/security/robustness combined pass): converged clean - only a P4 informational (a file literally named --check is swallowed as the flag; fails loudly with usage, no data risk; no action). CRLF checkouts safe (universal-newline read matches generated LF). The header's only consumer is the C leg, exactly the scope step 0 covers.

title: patches/rust-oscore-local.patch and README linkage stale after oscore v0.1.2 vendoring
description: Artifact governance from 3x codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-ythw: (1) rust/Cargo.toml [patch.crates-io] now points at the vendored in-tree rust/crates/oscore (v0.1.2, commit 61540bccff) - nothing applies patches/rust-oscore-local.patch anymore, and the patch no longer applies at external clone HEAD 76cee08 (26f2b32 superseded the design: dedicated received_response_piv window instead of response_window+mark_response_used). Decide: delete the patch file, or mark it historical. (2) patches/README.md:33-39 says upstream 'does not ship yet' - false since v0.1.2 shipped begin_unprotect_observe_response and master_secret; the patch-apply instructions would mislead a future session. (6) lichen-node secure.rs: a replayed committed CON notification missing the single-slot completed_confirmable cache is dropped silently (no ACK/RST) - harmless while ObserveServer backpressure permits only one outstanding CON; document the coupling or add a MID-keyed ACK cache if multiple outstanding CONs are ever allowed.
close_reason: Completed items 1,2,4,5,6 (+ one security P2). (1+2) patches/README.md rust-oscore section rewritten for the vendored reality: rust/crates/oscore is the build source (61540bccff, [patch.crates-io] -> crates/oscore), carries upstream v0.1.2 content with the manifest version-field caveat noted, both shipped APIs documented, every code span kept on one line so rendered identifiers grep correctly. rust-oscore-local.patch retained as a historical record explicitly marked DO-NOT-APPLY; deleting the file needs Mark's decision under workspace no-delete rules - flagged in the README and this bead's close for the maintainer. (5) debug_assert!(diff < WINDOW_SIZE) added before the three unguarded window shifts (mark_response_used/mark_received_response/mark_received_response_piv else-branches); reviewers traced every call path - unreachable in practice, fail-fast on invariant drift, release builds byte-identical. (6) secure.rs comment documents the single-outstanding-CON coupling (completed_confirmable single slot + ObserveServer backpressure; older retransmissions silent-drop with OSCORE PIV replay-reject). PLUS security-P2 fix: vendored crate manifest now carries an empty [workspace] table so its 101 unit tests (incl. both replay-window pins) run IN PLACE - previously dead tests (not a workspace member, no CI step). Item 3 (dead-module cleanup in the vendored/external source) filed as project-LICHEN-worker6-6i9x - needs Mark's upstream-push authorization. Validation: vendored crate 101+9 tests green in place; lichen-node 294 lib + integration suites green; cargo fmt clean (vendored crate formatted, lichen-node pre-existing receive.rs drift untouched); 3x codereview passes (correctness/security/robustness) - all P2s from the passes addressed, remaining P3 doc nits fixed.

title: 5pod rollback test: raw fs::write creates the restored record 0644, not FileStorage's 0600 - test may pass via Io instead of the precedes path
description: Found by security codereview of the new processor-level rollback test in project-LICHEN-worker6-5pod. rust/lichen-node/src/announce.rs rolled_back_durable_state_fails_admission_closed writes the restored snapshot with std::fs::write (default 0644, umask-dependent), but FileStorage.read verifies private-file mode 0600 (verify_private_file). If the mode check fires, load() returns Err(Io) and the processor maps any store error to PersistenceError - so the test would keep passing even if the precedes logic regressed, pinning the wrong code path. Fix: after fs::write, set mode 0600 (announce_store.rs tests' write_record_raw pattern: fs::write + set_permissions(0o600)), making the restored record indistinguishable from a FileStorage-written one so the test exercises the genuine precedes-fails-closed path.
close_reason: Fixed in the 5pod test: the restored snapshot record is now written with FileStorage's hardened 0600 mode (fs::write + set_permissions 0o600, unix-gated, matching announce_store.rs write_record_raw pattern), and the test additionally pins the exact store-level failure mode: assert_eq!(trust_store.load(iid), Err(AnnounceStoreError::Corrupt)) - so the test can only pass via the genuine precedes-fails-closed path; a permission-based Io rejection would now fail loudly, and the edge-cases reviewer confirmed every alternative Corrupt source (length, seal, half-present) is unreachable with a byte-exact sealed snapshot.

title: C generic Rule255 fallback decodes without payload validation; Rust/Python validate full IPv6 structure (cross-impl divergence)
description: Found by robustness review pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-1dft (P2, pre-existing - NOT introduced by the ingress-ceiling change; the new test pins the lenient behavior so it looks like a parity test). C generic dispatcher rule255/uncompressed fallback (lichen/subsys/schc/schc.c, post-ceiling) is a bare memcpy of the payload: it accepts EMPTY payloads and non-IPv6 bytes and returns success. Rust decode_rule255 (rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs:1459-1468) runs validate_full_ipv6_structure on the payload (version 6, exact lengths, ext-header walk, UDP checksums); Python decode_rule255 (python/src/lichen/schc/headers.py:201-213) runs validate_full_ipv6. So data_len==1 rule255 -> C returns 0 (success with zero-length delivery; lichen_link_rx.c:353 only tests ret<0 so it would report success with out_len 0), Rust/Python return errors. Per spec/03-adaptation.md Rule255: 'Its payload MUST be a complete, structurally valid IPv6 packet'. Fix: mirror Rust/Python - route the generic fallback payload through the same structural validation (the C per-rule decompressors' validate_ipv6_transport_lengths/validate_ipv6_header_chain machinery exists in schc_helpers.c; reuse it for the rule255 payload), keeping the RX/TX address-policy split (emission policy NOT applied on receipt). Decide the zero-payload/short-payload edge (< IPV6_HDR_LEN -> reject as malformed). Then re-pin tests/schc test_rule255_ingress_profile_ceiling with a NON-IPv6 payload to assert rejection parity with Rust/Python (current 0x41-fill vector would flip from accepted to rejected). Coordinate with hahk/7v5f (non-IPv6 Rule255 emission on the compress side) - same spec sentence governs both directions.

title: Intermittent EDHOC test failures need macOS canonical-build verification (wtxl family 3)
description: Child of wtxl family (3): intermittent failures across runs of test_edhoc_transport.py::test_derived_contexts_have_matching_keys and test_edhoc_responder.py::test_publication_failure_cleans_session_without_publishing. wtxl instructs verifying against the macOS canonical build before touching any vectors - a Linux/heft worker cannot distinguish environment flakiness (timing, async scheduling, filesystem) from a real cross-platform divergence, and the EDHOC vectors are cross-implementation oracles that must not be regenerated to chase a flake. Work for the claimer (or Mark on the Mac): run both tests repeatedly (e.g. 50x) on the macOS canonical checkout and on heft; if both pass repeatedly, record as environment flake and close; if the Mac reproduces, capture the failing state, diff against the oscore/edhoc crate behavior, and fix code (not vectors). Do NOT regenerate edhoc vector files as part of this.

title: secure_transport RH3 validation diverges from aligned survey (blackholes HBH+RH3 downward traffic)
description: Security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-xyix: rust/lichen-node/src/secure.rs secure_transport (secure.rs:1932-1950) rejects any RH3 not in first position, requires routing_len >= 24, and requires octets 6-7 plus the pad low nibble to be zero. The aligned survey (rpl_stack/util.rs) and the C router admit HBH-then-RH3, the 8-octet degenerate RH3, and ignored reserved bits (pinned by srh_admission.json vectors hop_by_hop_then_routing_in_transit, degenerate_zero_address_consumed, reserved_ignored_octets_admitted). receive.rs:244 runs secure_datagram_from_received before the survey on every non-RPL datagram, so RPL relays drop legitimately shaped downward traffic where C forwards it (availability divergence, and a survey-vs-gate contradiction within one binary). Fix: align secure_transport's RH3 parsing/validation with survey_routing_headers policy.

title: Gateway border-ingress consumes in-transit RH3 datagrams (survey bypass)
description: Security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-xyix: ingest_border_frame (rust/lichen-node/src/rpl_stack/receive.rs:121-123) returns non-RPL IPv6 to the gateway with no survey_routing_headers call; dispatch_runtime_gcp (rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:1291-1300,1343) then feeds it to secure_datagram/secure_transport, which can decrypt and locally execute an RH3-bearing datagram the C router would relay (router.c:505-522), or write it unadvanced to the TUN (lichend.rs:947-951). Requires installed GCP peer context and valid OSCORE. Fix: run survey_routing_headers on gateway-ingress datagrams and drop/relay per RFC 6554 forwarding precedence before GCP dispatch.

title: schc_parity_vectors.h source-dir copy shadows CMake build-dir generation; pick one source of truth
description: Found by robustness+security codereview passes of project-LICHEN-worker6-wrxl (P2). lichen/tests/schc_parity/main.c:9 includes "schc_parity_vectors.h" with quotes, so clang resolves it to the SOURCE-DIR copy (includer-dir precedes -I), while lichen/tests/schc_parity/CMakeLists.txt:10-24 also generates a build-dir copy at configure time. The two were byte-identical when wrxl landed, but any future JSON edit regenerates the UNUSED build copy while tests compile the stale source copy - silent stale-vector testing; the source copy is also untracked, polluting git status. Fix: pick one source of truth - either (a) delete the source-dir copy and let CMake generation be authoritative (matches pre-wrxl behavior), or (b) commit the source copy as the artifact and drop the CMake generation step. Option (a) preferred (no generated artifacts in git); then verify schc_parity still builds+passes on a fresh checkout.
close_reason: schc_parity now has a single source of truth for its vectors: the committed source header schc_parity_vectors.h is the only include (main.c quoted include resolved to it anyway - includer-dir precedes -I), and the CMake build-dir generation (find_package(Python3), execute_process, build-dir include path) is removed. Chose the commit-the-artifact option over deletion (no file deletions; fresh checkouts previously depended on configure-time generation). Regen path documented in BOTH the CMakeLists comment and the header banner (from the repository root), and - the key fix from review - gen_vectors.py's banner now emits the identical 6-line comment so generator output is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed artifact (verified: regen diff empty; first regen would otherwise have silently clobbered the instructions). Fresh-checkout simulation green: no generated header in build tree, compiles from source copy, ctest 1/1 (clang+ASan/UBSan, 57/57 vectors). 3x codereview (correctness/security/robustness, reviewer-model passes): no P0-P2 on the delta; all three converged on the residual staleness blind spot (JSON edit without regen leaves all three parity legs green) - filed as es5w (--check mode + parity-script step 0), a follow-up task, not part of this fix. CMakeLists hygiene verified (no leftover vars; sibling suites unaffected; test_common.cmake sanitizer posture identical).

title: Rust decompress-side finalize_checksum lacks computed-zero to 0xFFFF mapping; reconstructed UDP datagram can emit illegal wire 0x0000
description: P2, out-of-scope note from kimi edge-cases codereview pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-hahk. rust/lichen-schc/src/headers.rs:203-209 finalize lacks the computed-zero -> 0xFFFF mapping that C (lichen/subsys/lichen/schc/schc_checksum.c:62 finalize_checksum) and Python (python/src/lichen/schc/udp.py:77 or 0xFFFF) implement, and headers.rs:466 uses it for packet reconstruction on decompress. A UDP datagram whose true checksum computes to 0x0000 (legal; RFC 768/8200 require transmitting it as 0xFFFF) would be reconstructed by Rust emitting the illegal wire value 0x0000, where C and Python emit 0xFFFF - cross-impl divergence on the decompress/reconstruct path. Compress-side (ones_complement_sum codec.rs:602-613) is correct. Fix: apply the same mapping in headers.rs finalize (or route reconstruction through the compress-side checksum), pin with a shared vector whose UDP checksum computes to zero, rerun the parity gate.
close_reason: Fixed and pinned, with a correction to the original premise. CORRECTION: the live rust decompress path (lichen_schc::decompress -> decompress_coap -> udp_checksum_parts -> ones_complement_sum, codec.rs:602-613) ALREADY mapped computed-zero to 0xFFFF - there was no wire divergence on the production path. The actual gap was in the secondary public reconstruct API: headers.rs PacketProfile::build -> build_coap_udp -> udp_checksum -> finalize (headers.rs:203-209), which lacked the mapping and is reachable via the re-exported PacketProfile trait (lib.rs:46-49) though it has no in-tree production caller (verified: only fuzz targets call .parse, one codec.rs test calls .build). Fix: headers.rs udp_checksum now maps computed-zero to 0xFFFF (RFC 768; mirrors C finalize_checksum schc_checksum.c:53-63 and python UdpDatagram.to_bytes udp.py:77), deliberately UDP-scoped - icmpv6_checksum stays raw-complement to match python (C diverges on ICMPv6, filed au9y with corrected rust-internal split details). Pinned by: (1) new shared vector schc_compression.json coap_linklocal_computed_zero_checksum (rule-0 round trip, wire 0xFFFF, true checksum zero; packet hex built with a from-scratch RFC 1071 oracle, compressed bytes from python reference, consumed generically by all three suites - it discriminates mapped vs unmapped reconstruct and would catch any future regression of the live path onto an unmapped helper); (2) new headers.rs unit test coap_linklocal_computed_zero_checksum_round_trip (parse->build byte-identity + explicit checksum field FF FF). Gates: python 770/770; rust cargo test -p lichen-schc --features std all suites green (82 lib incl. new test), no_std build clean, clippy -D warnings clean; C schc_parity PASS (clang+ASan/UBSan, regenerates from JSON). Codereview 3x per step 4 (reviewer model): correctness kimi-k3 PASS (independent RFC 1071 recompute, residue bit layout hand-verified, confirmed live path unchanged); edge-cases kimi-k3 PASS (odd-payload pad path consistent across all 4 impls incl. lichen-core/src/udp.rs:166-167 which also maps; rule-1 global variant uses the same mapped sum; rust ICMPv6 internal split matches corrected au9y; vector CoAP shape valid); security: claude-opus-4-5 down all round (server errors err_9a376cc7, err_45a17586 - 4 opus failures today) so kimi-k3 fallback ran per protocol: wire-0x0000 acceptance gates confirmed load-bearing in all three impls, checksum is recomputed never copied so no attacker-controlled field injection, no weakening of udp_zero_checksum_malformed. New finding filed: au9y (P3 ICMPv6 computed-zero convention divergence C vs python/rust-headers, needs coordinated decision) - description corrected by the correctness pass before close.

title: SCHC profile ceiling off-by-one: C emits 22555-byte Rule255 datagram peers reject; 31-byte reject band vs peers
description: P2, found by kimi correctness and kimi edge-cases passes of project-LICHEN-worker6-hahk. lichen/subsys/lichen/schc/schc.c:538-540 caps compress INPUT at SCHC_FRAGMENT_MAX_PACKET_SIZE (22554) but the ceiling is on the ENCODED datagram including the rule byte (per size_boundary vectors; Rust codec.rs:2258). Two divergences: (a) pkt_len == 22554 passes the > check and the fallback emit (lichen/subsys/schc/schc.c:125-131) writes 1 + 22554 = 22555 bytes - one over the ceiling; Rust decode_rule255 (codec.rs:1460) and Python decode_rule255 (headers.py:206) reject len > 22554, so C emits a datagram peers drop (silent TX blackhole at the boundary); (b) conversely well-formed compressible inputs in (22554, 22585] (rule-0 encoded size = pkt_len - 31) are accepted by Rust enforce_encoded_profile_limit (codec.rs:2181) and Python (headers.py:872-873) but rejected by C's input cap - fail-closed, local-only. Pre-existing (blame 660b9bf3bf), adjacent to the hahk gate. Fix: drop the input cap, enforce needed > SCHC_FRAGMENT_MAX_PACKET_SIZE at the two Rule255 emit sites and per-rule encoded-size checks, mirroring Rust's structure; pin both boundary directions with size_boundary vectors and rerun the parity gate.

title: C compress emits non-IPv6/short input as Rule255 while Python/Rust reject - mixed-fleet blackhole
description: P2, found independently by all three codereview passes of project-LICHEN-worker6-hahk (kimi correctness, kimi edge-cases, worker5 subagent security). lichen/subsys/lichen/schc/schc.c:542-555: any pkt_len < 40 or version != 6 input is emitted verbatim as 0xFF + raw bytes (raw uncompressed fallback branch, predates the fix). Python compress_packet (headers.py:860) and Rust compress (codec.rs:2160 -> validate_full_ipv6_structure codec.rs:272-277) both reject non-IPv6 input instead. Probe: 3-byte garbage -> C rc=4 rule=0xff; 45-byte IPv4-shaped buffer -> C ACCEPT ret=46 rule=255 while Python raises (version must be 6). Same blackhole shape bead hahk closed for malformed IPv6: C emits Rule255 datagrams every Rust/Python peer fatals on at ingress decode_rule255. Pure-C fleets round-trip it (C RX rule255 branch lichen/subsys/schc/schc.c:152-165 does no payload validation), masking the divergence. No vector in test/vectors/schc_compression.json covers non-IPv6 input (all malformed_input packets start 0x60). Fix: reject non-IPv6 like the references, or deliberately re-contract the C-only passthrough and pin it; either way add malformed_input vectors (short garbage, version-4) and rerun scripts/check-schc-compression-parity.py. Reachability low (in-tree callers feed IPv6) hence P2 not P1.
close_reason: Fixed and pinned. lichen_schc_compress (lichen/subsys/lichen/schc/schc.c) now rejects non-IPv6 input - pkt_len < IPV6_HDR_LEN or version nibble != 6 returns SCHC_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT (-6) instead of emitting 0xFF+raw bytes as Rule255, closing the mixed-fleet blackhole where a C node emitted datagrams every Rust/Python peer fatals on at decode_rule255. Error-code choice: -6 is the existing shared-enum value already used for contract violations (NULL packet) and is distinct from BUFFER_TOO_SMALL; all callers (lichen_link_tx.c:136-138, lichen_l2_tx.c:149-157, bridge lichen_l2.c:988-996) handle <0 generically, so no caller churn. The rule255 raw-emit branch previously guarded an overflow check that became dead with the emit removed. References aligned: python compress_packet raises SchcError for len<40 (headers.py:142-145) and version!=6 (packet.py:116-117); rust compress -> validate_full_ipv6_structure raises InvalidPacket (codec.rs:272-277). Pinned by two new shared malformed_input vectors in test/vectors/schc_compression.json: non_ipv6_short_input_malformed (deadbeef) and non_ipv6_version4_input_malformed (45-byte version-4 datagram whose internal length fields are self-consistent) - consumed by python test_schc_vector (pytest.raises SchcError), rust shared_vectors (compress is_err), C parity check_malformed_input (negative return + untouched output sentinel). C host test test_uncompressed_fallback (which pinned the abolished raw-emit behavior by round-tripping deadbeef as Rule255 - that was the bug) replaced by test_reject_non_ipv6_input asserting SCHC_ERR_INVALID_ARGUMENT for both classes. Gates on heft: C host schc suite 15/15 (clang, ASan/UBSan); C schc_parity 51 vectors PASS; python test_vectors.py 772/772; rust shared_vectors 3/3 (scratch worktree, oscore path redirected, not committed); cppcheck clean on schc.c. title: StratumTracker network replay high-water LRU is eviction-exposed to DIOs never authorized for time (replay-window bypass)
description: Found by security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-fxrh. python/src/lichen/timing/stratum.py:629-632 inserts and move_to_end-refreshes the (signer,generation)->counter barrier UNCONDITIONALLY once the counter is new, BEFORE the time-authorization and payload-binding checks that run later inside _rejection via _adopt_claimed_locked (network-transport-not-authorized / network-peer-not-authorized-for-time at stratum.py:185-188, network-option-evidence-mismatch at 193-197). Rejected, unauthorized-for-time DIOs therefore consume and order LRU slots. Same-signer eviction (626-628) caps each signer at one entry, but with MAX_NETWORK_REPLAY_GENERATIONS=256 (time_sync.py:58) an attacker controlling >=256 distinct signer keys admitted to the verifier's peer_origins can flood the OrderedDict and evict a victim signer's high-water entry; __network_high_water.get(replay_key,-1) at 623 then returns -1 and ANY counter passes: a previously-considered validly-signed victim DIO re-verified into a fresh sample is considered again. With no current sample the stale sample skips backward-step (690-691) and stratum/precedence (680-685) checks, so a sufficiently old floor-passing timestamp can adopt = time rollback. Preconditions (256+ keys in peer_origins, LRU race vs the victim's refresh, low epoch floor) are deployment-dependent but plausible under open mesh admission. Fix directions: only insert/refresh LRU entries for samples whose authority is authorized for time (move the barrier insert after _rejection's authorization checks, or gate on the authorization verdict before 629); or track victim eviction via a tombstone floor that survives eviction; or size-bound per-signer with a persistent floor file like the announce/gateway stores. Also consider whether issuance_high_water (609-612, no eviction) already bounds the same reissue path and document the interplay.

title: Shared Rule255 endpoint-policy parity vectors + parity script rerun; then close k0r2
description: Child of project-LICHEN-worker6-k0r2 (last step). After the Rust RX-side split lands and Python's TX-side emission enforcement is confirmed, add shared malformed/divergence vectors in test/vectors/ (schema-consistent with existing SCHC Rule255 vectors) covering the k0r2 trigger classes on BOTH sides: src=::1, src=::ffff:192.0.2.1, dst=::1, dst=ff01::1 (scope 1), dst=ff0f::1 (scope 15) - each asserting encode_rule255 REJECTS (both impls, emission policy) and decode_rule255 of the byte-preserving frame ACCEPTS (both impls, RX rule). Wire Python (python/tests) and Rust (rust/lichen-schc tests) to consume the same JSON per the shared-vector discipline (oracles must be the committed JSON, not code outputs), then rerun scripts/check-schc-compression-parity.py (needs C clang on heft: use clang, gcc-13 lacks -std=c23) and close k0r2. This round's changes: (1) replaced the duplicate rx row (was byte-identical assertions to tx_reject_loopback_source - edge-codesreview finding) with the dual-violation row; (2) added scope-2 and scope-14 accept boundary rows (edge finding: the Python emission predicate _validate_rule255_emission_endpoints is a separate function from the Rule 7 validator so rule7 boundary rows never exercised it); (3) expected_counts.rule255_endpoint_policy 8->10; (4) python coverage test now enforces the committed expected_counts table (mirroring rust ExpectedCounts semantics incl. p0/endpoint_direction/duplicate_idempotence) - previously python consumed no count guard and a mis-categorized row skipped silently (edge finding); (5) dispatch chain gained a fail-closed else for unknown categories; (6) security-review P2: the endpoint_direction count leg was initially a no-op (popped, never asserted) - fixed to a real assertion. Independent verification: worker5 probe with from-scratch RFC 1071 oracle confirmed encode-reject/decode-accept for all 5 original k0r2 trigger classes on both impls. title: gateway oscore stores: records cache has no eviction; Err(Full) permanently rejects existing durable contexts past 64
description: Found by 3x codereview of the recipient-store heal (9liz). rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs: GatewayOscoreRecipientStore.records and GatewayOscoreSenderStore cache are Vecs that only grow (recipient capacity gate at ~475-477, sender ~604-606; MAX_GCP_OSCORE_CONTEXTS=64 at gateway.rs:48). After a restart with >64 durable contexts, the first 64 touched fill the cache and every further context - including ones with valid durable sealed state - fails load() with Err(Full) forever, order-dependently; callers drop packets on any error (~1360-1380). The sibling announce store explicitly fixed this class: 'Full is a new-pin admission outcome, never a load outcome' (lichen-node/src/announce_store.rs:300-339, LRU eviction + uncached loads). Additional growth vector: persistent (None,None) load() caches an empty state for any probed context, consuming slots; stale records accumulate across PSK/epoch rotations (ContextId deterministic, so reinstalling same peer reuses its record; rotations mint new ids). Also: Err(Full) is never cached, so each packet for an uncached context repeats the full 2-read + double-schnorr-verify sequence. Fix: adopt the announce store's admission policy (evict LRU on capacity for contexts with durable state; never return Full from load for an already-durable context).

title: oscore response_window is dual-role across server/client contexts: false-replay DoS on bidirectional contexts
description: Found by 3x codereview of the rust-oscore observe port (9liz unblock work). Same root cause as project-LICHEN-worker6-ythw. In /home/mark/crates/oscore/src/lib.rs, response_seq/response_window is written by mark_response_used only from protect_response's no-PIV branch (server role: 'request PIVs whose nonce I reused for my own no-PIV responses') but is consulted by begin_unprotect_response_inner (~lib.rs:1308) as 'peer response PIVs I have accepted' (client role). A Context legitimately serves both roles; the two are independent sequence spaces, so on a bidirectional context a legitimate notification/response whose PIV numerically falls in the marked range of previously-answered request seqs is falsely rejected as Err(Replay) — a fail-closed DoS. Fix together with ythw by separating the windows or using the recipient window consistently on both paths. Machine-local clone; regenerate patches/rust-oscore-local.patch after the fix.
