title: announce_store: no single-writer exclusion on durable roots; second store instance seals a regression via its stale cache
description: Found by security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-t8ox (P2). rust/lichen-node/src/announce_store.rs:164-182: persistent() opens state_root/floor_root with no lock or exclusive-claim check; FileStorage::new takes no lock either. Every guarantee (pin binding, floor monotonicity, replay rejection, cache consistency after failed-floor-write eviction) rests on all writes flowing through ONE store instance so the cache mirrors durable state. A second AnnounceTrustStore on the same roots (stale systemd unit beside a debug run, or a second persistent() in-process) has an independent cache: instance B load/accept validates against its stale cache, so after instance A commits seq 200, B accept(150) passes B checks and seals a CONSISTENT (state=150, floor=150) pair that load() precedes() can never flag - bypasses replay protection with zero tamper evidence. Fix directions: (a) accept() validates against the DURABLE record (re-read from storage, same fail-closed matrix as load) instead of the cache-first load() - closes the seal-regression vector regardless of instance count at one extra disk read per accept (accepts are rare; announce intervals); also subsumes the p4mf re-validation window as defense in depth; or (b) exclusive claim (flock on a lockfile in the state dir - note std File::try_lock needs rustc 1.89 > MSRV 1.81, so needs a dep or the MSRV bump; lockfile must not match the announce-pin- count filter) or (c) documented+asserted single-instance contract (weakest). Prefer (a) implemented where tests can run.

title: Persistent announce trust store capacity is a permanent admission brick after 64 originators
description: Found by security+robustness review of project-LICHEN-worker6-dowx. AnnounceTrustStore::accept returns Full for a fresh IID once records.len() >= MAX_TRACKED_ORIGINATORS (64) and durable records are never deleted (deliberately no removal API, announce_store.rs:17-21,302-304); AnnounceProcessor::process maps any load/accept error incl. Full to AnnounceRejectReason::PersistenceError (announce.rs:250-252). On a persistent gateway, 64 distinct lifetime originators - trivially cheap for an attacker (throwaway keypairs, one valid announce each) - permanently reject all future new-origin admission, across restarts. In-memory LRU eviction cannot relieve it (durable check runs before memory admission). Availability-only (existing pinned origins keep working) but converts a bounded self-healing memory cap into a permanent remote DoS on gateway onboarding. Also: Full is conflated with corrupt/io in PersistenceError so operators cannot diagnose store-full. Needs a design decision: durable cap sized above real mesh population, or prune policy that preserves pins (key-change protection) while still preventing floor regression, or operator recovery path, plus a distinct reject reason for Full. Recovery today = manual deletion of state roots.

title: C Rule-255 decompress validates nothing: verbatim memcpy where Python and Rust decode_rule255 enforce validate_full_ipv6
description: Confirmed empirically by two independent codereview passes of project-LICHEN-worker6-njdx. lichen/subsys/schc/schc.c:151-165 copies Rule-255 payloads to out without any validation; Python decode_rule255 (headers.py:193 -> validate_full_ipv6) and Rust decode_rule255 (codec.rs:1444) run the full validator and reject. Demonstrated: ff + RH3(sl=1)+UDP with bad checksum -> C lichen_schc_decompress ret=76 payload copied, P/R reject; ff + IPv6 Fragment header packet -> C ret=60 accepted, P/R reject. The parity corpus has no malformed-category vector with rule_id 255 (all use 0-7), so this cannot be caught by the current gate. Impact: a C receiver admits on-air Rule255 frames that every Rust/Python peer rejects, and locally accepts packets the firmware's own compress gate rejects (asymmetric admission). Fix: run validate_ipv6_transport_lengths + the chain policy over the decoded payload in the C rule-255 decompress branch, then add shared malformed rule-255 compressed vectors (fragment header, bad checksum, non-RH3 routing) so the parity gate pins it. Related: project-LICHEN-worker6-prld covers Python/Rust Rule255 laxness; this is the C-side decode gap.

(1) FIXED in sb0b: coap_status.c trust_level_str lacked a case for LICHEN_COAP_TRUST_UNKNOWN -> -Werror=switch-enum (default: does not suppress -Wswitch-enum); case added, behavior identical to old default. Workaround exists (set =14, done in ping_l2 + coap_client tests) but gateway/puck prj.confs do NOT set it - audit all apps/boards (pre-existing boot-assert risk on real boards). (3) OPEN: base lora_l2.c defined a global rx_stack that collides with Zephyr net_tc.c rx_stack (multiple definition at link) - latent, only bites configs building net TC + old L2; gone after sb0b but symbols were renamed only in the new code. Verify (2) and (4) after fixing.

title: lichen_radio_progress watchdog contract narrowed: idle-armed radio feeds no heartbeat; puck docs stale
description: Found by security+robustness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-sb0b (P2). The old RX thread bumped lichen_radio_progress() every loop pass (<=RX_TIMEOUT_MS), proving the radio path alive even during silence. The async RX (sb0b) bumps only on packet deliveries and successful arms - deliberately not on retry attempts, which masked wedges by keeping the heartbeat fresh. Net effect: while the radio sits idle and armed (the common case), nothing bumps the hook; puck's watchdog survives only because its main loop kicks every <=1s (apps/puck/src/main.c:542). The original purpose - keeping WDT fed while main blocks in a long network call - no longer holds, and the puck main.c comment block (main.c:226-255) still describes thread-poll semantics. Fix: either a low-rate keepalive work item while armed-and-idle (careful: reintroduces polling the 9hfe epic removed), or liveness sourced from driver IRQ counters, plus update puck's stall-contract comment. Related: a hung lora_send() (SPI fault) holds modem_mutex indefinitely and masks stalls from the watchdog - pre-existing shape.

title: L2 RX packet processing on system workqueue can starve all other system work
description: Found by security+robustness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-sb0b (P2). rx_work_fn on the cooperative system workqueue runs the full lichen_l2_input chain: rx_mutex K_FOREVER, Schnorr-48 verify (CPU-bound, up to N peers per attacker frame), SCHC decompress, and net_pkt_rx_alloc_with_buffer with CONFIG_LICHEN_L2_RX_ALLOC_TIMEOUT_MS (default 50ms) - all unpreeemptible at cooperative priority, shared with USB/udc work, net DAD/ND delayed work, mgmt events. A radio-range attacker (~40fps at SF7) can hold sysworkq near-permanently. Mitigations to evaluate: dedicated RX workqueue (k_work_queue_start, prio like old RX_THREAD_PRIORITY), shrinking the alloc timeout for sysworkq builds, or moving net_pkt alloc off the hot path. Stack budgets were migrated in sb0b (puck 8192, gateway boards 12288, nucleo_wl55jc 2048 = old RX default); budget parity is verified, sharing is the issue.

title: Test gap: announce_store heal durability is mutation-untested

The held-seq assertion at :518-521 passes via the in-memory cache populated by load (:288), and the follow-up accept (:525) rewrites both sides itself, so no test observes that the healed floor was actually durably rewritten - the security-relevant half of the fix that re-arms rollback detection via precedes (:276). The pre-existing store_rejects_state_rollback_and_heals_floor_lag durability claim (:565-572) has the same gap and also passes under the mutation. Fix: after a heal load, assert the floor record exists and verifies, e.g. assert store.read(iid, true) is Ok(Some(state)) (tests module can call the private read) or record_path(floor_root, iid, true).exists().

title: Poison floor pin targets _missing_metadata_floor branch, not the tracker-consumed _floor_result_locked branch

title: Rust compress writes out buffer before failing: error returns leave partial bytes (decompress is atomic)
description: Confirmed empirically (discovered-from project-LICHEN-worker6-xuc8, robustness pass). compress_mqtt_sn (rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs:1014-1047) sets out[0]=RULE_MQTT_SN (:1017), zero-fills out[1..] via BitWriter (:143), writes residue and copies tail BEFORE the needed>out.len() check (:1044); enforce_encoded_profile_limit (:2161) fires only after full encoding written. Probe: input needing 121 bytes with 25-byte out -> Err(BufferTooSmall) with all 25 bytes modified, out[0]=0x07; over-profile input with 40000-byte out -> Err(profile limit) with all 40000 bytes written. decompress side is fully atomic on error (0 bytes modified) and Python is atomic by construction. No current in-repo caller reads out after Err (checked link.rs:263, decompress_authenticated_frame_tracked) so impact is latent, but the compress/decompress asymmetry is undocumented and any caller assuming error implies untouched buffer gets stale/garbage bytes. Fix: size-check before first write in compress_mqtt_sn (and audit other per-rule compress fns for the same pattern), or document the contract explicitly plus a regression test asserting buffer-untouched-on-error.

title: on_persistence_failure clears TX queue without _tx_lock and off the event loop
description: link_layer.py:2108 on_persistence_failure synchronizes on threading.RLock/Condition and is documented callable from any thread (persistence.py:262), yet calls tx_queue.clear() -> signal_all_pending(False) -> asyncio.Future.set_result, which is not thread-safe (lost wakeup/hang; RuntimeError under debug) and the queue mutation is not serialized against an in-flight drain holding _tx_lock. Failure interleaving: drain suspended in radio.transmit(E); persistence thread hits terminal failure -> clear() resolves E's reservation False; transmit completes on air -> complete(E, True) finds E removed, set_result(True) is idempotent first-wins -> send() returns False for a frame that was emitted -> upper layer retransmits -> duplicate frame on air. Outcome is timing-dependent (True may win if loop thread completes first). Fix: marshal the clear through loop.call_soon_threadsafe and acquire _tx_lock on the loop, or document/enforce loop-affinity for on_persistence_failure. Found by correctness+robustness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-9qpz.

title: Reformat rust Cargo.tomls: multi-line feature arrays + alphabetical dep convention
description: Context: parallel beads workers (7 TUI agents) edit Cargo.toml concurrently and collide on single-line feature arrays — git merges by lines, and 'std = [...]' is one line, so any two agents adding a dep hit the same line (seen live: zeroize vs hex both-added conflict resolved manually in 54e2c2cc5b). Fix: in rust/*/Cargo.toml, reformat [features] arrays (and any long dep arrays) one entry per line, and document/apply the convention that new [dependencies]/[dev-dependencies] entries are inserted alphabetically (appends land at different points instead of section-end collisions). Add a short comment block at the top of each Cargo.toml: 'Swarm note: one feature per line; insert deps alphabetically; keeps parallel agent merges conflict-free. Do not collapse to single-line.' Scope: rust/*.crates only — leave vendor/workspace tomls alone. Verify with cargo metadata/cargo check per touched crate and a clean git merge simulation between two branches that each add a different optional dep.

title: BlockReceiver loses negotiated szx across re-requests after mid-transfer size change
description: Found by 3x review of bead 0oim (pre-existing, receiver side, NOT introduced by the acknowledge clamp fix). rust/lichen-coap/src/block.rs: receive_block (block.rs:396-424) accepts a server block with a NEW szx (mid-transfer size change is legal and tested at block.rs:742-769) but never persists it into self.block_size; next_request_block (block.rs:434-438) rebuilds requests at the stale requested size with expected num taken from the server. Concrete hang trace: transfer requests {0,szx=2}+{1,szx=2}; server responds {1,szx=3} (128B blocks) and later blocks at szx=3; a lost final block {2,szx=3} triggers a re-request built as {num:2,szx:2} = byte offset 128 while the server has sent through 256 -> server resends overlapping data -> receive_block rejects BlockOutOfOrder (block.rs:402-407) -> caller retry loop never converges. Fix: persist self.block_size = block.size() in receive_block (and verify num accounting matches the new size), plus a regression test: mid-transfer size change then lost-final-block re-request converges.

title: Rust/Python route-state consumers bypass the DAO delegation gate on grouped vectors

But the Rust consumer (rust/lichen-rpl/tests/rpl_route_state_vectors.rs) uses process_route_state_diagnostic which per its own comment (rpl_route_state_vectors.rs:440) has no delegation gate, and the Python consumer (python/src/lichen/rpl/dao_manager.py evaluate_dao_semantics_for_test_at) passes source_address=None which skips the authorization gate (dao_manager.py:906-912). So the cross-implementation identical-output guarantee for the delegation authorization path currently rests on C alone. Follow-up: wire the oracle's delegations array into the Rust PrefixDelegations (delegate_prefix by public key - note the C delegates by origin address, Rust by pubkey; the oracle may need a key binding field) and the Python dao manager, then assert the grouped vectors through the same gate.

title: FileStorage::read unbounded read_to_end amplifies planted oversized records to OOM
description: lichen-hal/src/storage.rs fs::FileStorage::read (~line 529) does read_to_end into an unbounded Vec before copying min(stored, buf.len()). Callers pass small buffers (announce store: 82 bytes) but the allocation is file-sized; a planted multi-GB file at any record key turns load() into unbounded allocation instead of Err(Corrupt). Newly reachable via rust/lichen-node/src/announce_store.rs load(); gateway stores share the exposure (pre-existing). Fix: pre-stat the file and cap the read at buf.len()+1, rejecting anything larger. Found by security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-12zy.

title: Announce store doc overclaims rollback resistance vs whole-volume snapshot restore
description: announce_store.rs module doc claims separate state/floor roots mean 'a rollback snapshot cannot silently rewind both sides'. True only for single-root rollback or crash windows; an attacker who restores a same-volume snapshot predating an IID's first accept() rewinds BOTH roots, load() returns Ok(None), and accept() silently TOFU-pins whatever key arrives. Options: persist a monotonic generation marker in a third root so (None,None) with a marker present fails closed, and/or correct the doc to state the TOFU-inherent limit. Found by security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-12zy.

title: AnnounceTrustStore::ephemeral() is a public silent downgrade

title: GCP trust anchor pin removal is not revocation; partial federation failure leaves pinned-but-contextless anchor
description: Found in 3x codereview of w0fp. Two related semantics in the lichend GCP-3.1 flow: (1) TrustStore provisioning is monotonic (rust/lichen-gateway/src/trust.rs provision_configured_peer 672-713 only adds/raises level; TrustStore::remove 1067 has no daemon caller), so dropping a compromised peer key from gateway_coordination.peer_public_keys in deploy/lichend.toml.example does NOT revoke its durable BrProvisioned pin or GCP context — an explicit operator revocation path (config change -> pin+context removal, atomic with persistence) is missing. (2) provision_closed_federation (rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:1039-1099) commits trust anchors durably (save_atomic_with_floor 1081-1090) before installing contexts (1091-1097); a context-install failure exits the daemon with the anchor pinned but contextless — fail-closed direction and self-heals on next restart, but document/handle the intermediate state deliberately. Design revocation carefully against IID-collision trust-replacement protections; add tests for config-removal revocation and restart-after-partial-install.

title: Slot-claim seq store: cap NV growth and define eviction for dead gateway IIDs
description: Codereview finding (P2, security/robustness) on lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/slot_claim_settings.c: one settings entry per distinct committed gateway IID, never deleted (no settings_delete path). Gateway IID churn grows NV unbounded; NVS-full makes settings_save_one fail -> every claim rejected LICHEN_CLAIM_REJECT_PERSIST (liveness kill of GCP-6), and dead IIDs permanently consume load-order cache slots (8 max) which decides which floors survive reboot. Commits only happen after Schnorr48 verify so remote garbage is bounded by the TOFU key store, but the store still needs a cap/eviction/LRU policy decision plus a boot-time cleanup for entries over capacity. Discovered from project-LICHEN-worker6-uiun 3x codereview.

title: Slot-claim replay gate: re-check claim_seq under s_coord_lock before applying
description: Codereview finding (P2, correctness+security) on coap_slot_coord.c:429-438 vs 453-502: the claim_seq gate lookup runs BEFORE k_mutex_lock(s_coord_lock) and the monotonic no-op in commit returns 0, so a stale lower-seq claim racing a higher-seq one can be applied after the newer grant (highest-seq-wins violated at the coordination layer). Latent today (single CoAP RX thread) but process_claim is public API. Fix: re-run the claim_seq gate inside the critical section just before conflict resolution (lookup under lock; s_coord_lock -> s_lock ordering already acyclic), or make lichen_slot_claim_seq_commit return a distinct nonzero (-EALREADY) from the monotonic no-op so process_claim rejects. Add a regression test for out-of-order same-IID claims. Discovered from project-LICHEN-worker6-uiun 3x codereview.
close_reason: In-lock re-check added before conflict resolution in lichen_slot_coord_process_claim (pre-lock gate kept as flood fast-reject). Regression test test_seq_recheck_under_lock simulates the stale pre-lock view via a fail-first-lookup hook; verified load-bearing (fails without the fix, passes with it). coap_slot_claim + slot_claim_settings host tests green.

title: GCP-6: Tighten slot claim duration / consider implicit-renewal model
description:
Current spec only checks expiry > now, no upper bound. A griefer can claim slots with expiry = now + 10 years and squat forever.

Reconsider the entire claim model:

**Option A: Short wall-clock cap**
- expiry <= now + MAX_CLAIM_DURATION_SEC
- Default 5-10 minutes (not 30-60)

**Option B: Superframe-denominated**  
- Claim duration = N superframes (e.g. 5-10)
- Units match the protocol

**Option C: Implicit renewal (no expiry field needed)**
- Slot held while active
- Revoked after M consecutive missed TXes in your slot
- No renewal messages, just keep transmitting
- Squatter must actually TX to hold slot (costs real airtime)

Option C is most hostile to griefers — can't squat without burning airtime.

Touches:
- spec/08-gateway-coordination.md (GCP-6 claim model)
- lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/coap_slot_coord.c

title: Mobility patterns accept NaN/inf and RandomWaypoint validates nothing - silent position corruption
description: Found in 3x codereview of uory fix. (1) RandomWaypoint has no __post_init__ validation at all (speed<=0, bounds, pause) unlike its three siblings. (2) NaN bypasses the 'x <= 0' checks in all four patterns (nan <= 0 is False): speed_m_s=nan or NaN bounds construct cleanly and poison geometry - max_distance >= distance is False for NaN, flow falls into the ratio branch and writes NaN into node.set_position, propagating silently through every later distance/sqrt. (3) speed_m_s=inf passes validation; every arrival charges distance/inf*1e6 == 0.0 so each step() burns the full 100k iteration cap (bounded ~0.1-0.3s/node/tick hostile-scenario amplification). Fix: add RandomWaypoint validation matching siblings; use math.isfinite on speed/spacing/bounds/pause across all four patterns.
acceptance_criteria: constructing any pattern with NaN/inf speed, spacing, or bounds raises ValueError; existing valid configs unchanged

title: Wire or remove committed-but-unbuilt coap sources: coap_codec.c, coap_blockwise.c, coap_waypoints.c, presence.c
description: Found during 4xln codereview. lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/ contains coap_codec.c, coap_blockwise.c, coap_waypoints.c, presence.c that are committed but not referenced by lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/CMakeLists.txt, so no build target compiles them (same class as commit 609a648228 'drop refs to unlanded WIP sources'; the sources were landed by 660b9bf3bf without CMake wiring). Also no Kconfig symbols gate them (no LICHEN_COAP_WAYPOINTS etc.). Decide per file: wire with proper Kconfig + fix any compile breaks they expose (use the qemu_x86 overlay-proof approach from bd 4xln), or remove the dead sources. Verify each choice with a build that includes it.

title: lichen-link tests silently skipped without --features schnorr,std; lichen-node blockwise test fails
description: Discovered in wave 2 (b4f7/d9ab verification, both reproducible with changes stashed): (1) plain 'cargo test -p lichen-link' never compiles link_layer.rs - the whole link-layer suite (incl. peer/replay tests) is gated behind 'schnorr,std', so default CI-style runs report 93 tests/0 failures while skipping the actual link-layer suite; lichen-schc's link_layer_integration test likewise fails to compile without --all-features (12 errors: authenticated_frame, write_to missing) - feature-gating drift between lichen-link and lichen-schc consumers. (2) Pre-existing deterministic failure: cargo test -p lichen-node :: secure::tests::secure_block1_and_block2_roundtrip_replay_order_and_pivs at rust/lichen-node/src/secure.rs:2568 with Blockwise(BlockOutOfOrder) (274/275 pass). Also tracked-already: project-LICHEN-worker6-buh8 (authenticated-path 1500 scratch caps, filed by wave-2 agent).

title: Bound authenticated-path SCHC scratch decoding by caller intent, not SCHC_MAX_DECOMPRESSED
description: Follow-up from project-LICHEN-worker6-d9ab (codec reconstruction caps removed). Remaining in-crate sites decode into [0u8; SCHC_MAX_DECOMPRESSED] (1500) scratch and thereby still cap reconstruction of valid profile-max SCHC packets: rust/lichen-schc/src/link.rs:219 (elided-address ingress scratch), link.rs:261 (create_fragment_sender validation), codec.rs parse_authenticated_dio_evidence (~line 1696) and authenticated_dio_destination_is_local (~line 2037). Fixing needs either a max-expansion-sized scratch (~22.6KB stack, unacceptable for STM32WL) or a redesign (header-only destination extraction from residue). Security-sensitive: decode-into-scratch exists so foreign packets cannot mutate caller output before rejection. Needs design judgment; not a minimal-diff change.

title: SecureStack: failed send leaves stale pending_requests entry causing CorrelationMismatch on identical retry
description: Discovered during milq/mybk gateway handoff tests. SecureStack::send_secure_response_to (rust/lichen-node/src/secure.rs:1427-1431) correlates the outgoing response to pending_requests by inner request equality (code+options+payload+sender); the entry is removed only on successful send (secure.rs:1511). After a failed send (e.g. GatewayOscoreSenderStore persistence failure), the stale entry remains, so a retry whose inner payload is byte-identical builds its response from the stale entry's token/MID/request-PIV and the client sees CorrelationMismatch. Retry tests in end_to_end.rs work around it by rebuilding the handoff payload with a fresh timestamp (realistic but masks the bug). Fix: drop the pending entry on send failure, or match by request PIV.

title: TUI plugin: display in-progress bead in sidebar footer
description: Add .opencode/plugins/beads-status.tsx — an opencode TUI slot plugin that polls bd for in_progress beads and renders the active one (id + title) in the sidebar_footer slot. Registered via project opencode.json plugin entry. Deps pinned in .opencode/package.json (@opentui/solid 0.4.5, solid-js 1.9.12 to match host).
close_reason: Implemented .opencode/plugins/beads-status.tsx (TUI sidebar_footer slot) + beads-tracker.ts (tool.execute.before hook mapping sessionID->bead on bd update/close; unit-tested via node driver: claim, close-clears, flag-first form, close-other no-op). Deps pinned in .opencode/package.json; registered via tui.json. Pending: visual confirmation on next TUI restart.

title: Register lichen-schc link_layer_integration test with required-features
description: cargo test -p lichen-schc with default features fails to compile: tests/link_layer_integration.rs is auto-discovered (no [[test]] entry in rust/lichen-schc/Cargo.toml) and uses std-only APIs (FragmentationPolicy::accept_peer, AuthenticatedFragmentReceiver::new, lichen_link::identity) without a crate-level cfg gate. Introduced when commit f8cdaec2b3 touched the file; Cargo.toml has [[test]] entries with required-features = ["std", "raw-fragment-codec"] for the other four integration tests but none for this one. Fix: add [[test]] name = "link_layer_integration" required-features = ["std", "raw-fragment-codec"] (or a #![cfg(feature = "std")] gate). Verified 2026-08-29: 12 compile errors under default features; full suite passes with --features std,test-utils,raw-fragment-codec.

title: atomic_json reserved-name guard bypassed by case aliasing on case-insensitive filesystems
description: Wave-1 review (security, P2): test/vectors/atomic_json.py:577-583 rejects reserved targets by exact name only. On case-insensitive APFS (primary dev platform), a batch target like .LICHEN-VECTOR-BATCH.LOCK resolves to the live lock inode; the batch then os.replace()s a new inode over the lock directory entry while holding flock on the old inode, letting a concurrent writer lock the new inode and run its critical section concurrently (breaks the mixed-generation mutual exclusion invariant). Journal alias (.LICHEN-VECTOR-BATCH.TRANSACTION.JSON as target) ends with os.unlink(journal) + backup deletion: silent data destruction with no journal left for recovery. Fix: case-fold the reserved comparison (names are ASCII) in atomic_write_json_batch and journal validation; add an aliased-case regression asserting rejection with no mutation. Discovered-from wave 1 bead project-LICHEN-worker6-blqw.
close_reason: Fixed in wave 1 follow-up: casefold guard + aliased regression, parametrize entry, fsync-ordering pin, hold-down constants, wait_for timeouts + ctime_ns. Suites green (44+178+130).

title: Flaky timing tests fail under load: tofu_capacity hold_down, edhoc_transport handshake, edhoc_responder deadline
description: P2 flakiness (edhoc only — the tofu_capacity hold_down case was reclassified as a deterministic failure owned by hg27): python/tests/coap/test_edhoc_transport.py::test_edhoc_handshake_via_coap and 3 TestEdhocResource tests in python/tests/coap/test_edhoc_responder.py (completed_m3_can_publish_after_deadline, completing_session_holds_capacity_until_finalized, close_during_completion_cancels_publication_without_success) failed one full-suite run, passed the next (wall-clock deadline dependence under parallel load). Fix by injecting a fake clock / relaxing wall-clock deadlines rather than raising timeouts blindly.

title: DAO RX floor catalog requires durably-anchored state outside base_dir; enforce/document
description: Security review of worker6-bidu fix: if dao_rx_catalog.bin, both per-key slot files, AND the anchor state are all absent, load_rx_floor degrades to first-DAO bootstrap and old signed DAOs replay. Slot files and catalog live in the same directory with identical permissions, so any actor able to delete slots can delete the catalog; protection only holds when StateRevisionAnchor is externally durable. Fix: enforce or document that production construction requires a durable anchor stored outside base_dir (e.g. requires_durable_anchor flag or gateway-config assertion) and add a test asserting the fail-open path is unreachable with the durable anchor. Ref dao_persistence.py:625-627,722-725,992-1007.

title: [review] C root applies delegated-prefix-only DAOs that Rust rejects (identical-decisions invariant break)
description: P2, wave-7 review. rpl_dao_process.c:756-886 process_dao has no found_origin equivalent: a verified-origin DAO advertising ONLY delegated prefixes (no self /128 target) is APPLIED by the C root, while Rust rejects it (routing.rs:669 + sender_is_authorized routing.rs:727-760 requires >=1 canonical target == origin). Wave-7 created this class (the old all-targets==origin gate made it unreachable in C). Not a bypass (origin IS delegated) but breaks identical-decisions for mixed C/Rust meshes. Fix: add the found_origin check (>=1 canonical target == origin) to process_dao after the gate, or document the C extension as intentional in spec/05-routing.md 8.7 - coordinate the decision across impls.

title: lichen-oscore provisioning.rs is orphaned dead code holding secret-bearing types
description: rust/lichen-oscore/src/provisioning.rs declares BRProvisioningSession/NodeProvisioningSession (both hold secret key material, both have manual Drop->wipe()) but no 'mod provisioning;' exists in lib.rs, so the module never compiles. Silently dead today. Decide re-wire vs delete; if re-wired, add Zeroize/ZeroizeOnDrop impls + compile-time assertions consistent with zeroize_asserts.rs, and note it uses aes/ccm/hkdf which would need direct deps.

title: Owner decision: confirm ham-band Part 97 operating plan vs spec-default ISM for ARDC framing
description: docs/grant-ardc-application.md claims operation under amateur radio licenses; docs/grant-technical-description.md Physical row says unlicensed ISM bands. Reconcilable (902-928 MHz is dual-use Part 15 ISM / Part 97 33cm; Meshtastic ham-mode precedent; spec defaults to US915 ISM), but ARDC's funding rationale hinges on ham-band operation. Owner must confirm: does the 500-node deployment actually operate Part 97 with callsign ID? Then align the two docs.

title: Fix test_common.cmake ASan detection broken repo-wide on Apple clang
description: check_c_compiler_flag("-fsanitize=address") in lichen/tests/cmake/test_common.cmake:48 fails on Apple clang (Xcode 26.6): the try-compile links WITHOUT the flag on the link line, ___asan_init is undefined, _has_asan caches false, and ASan is silently dropped for EVERY host test dir even though lichen_test_target() applies _san_flags to both compile and link options (lines 62-65). Verified empirically 2026-08-28: tx_queue binary without the per-test workaround links only ubsan runtime; with CMAKE_REQUIRED_LINK_OPTIONS re-check it links libclang_rt.asan_osx_dynamic.dylib. Fix once in test_common.cmake (set CMAKE_REQUIRED_LINK_OPTIONS before the check), then remove the per-test workaround in lichen/tests/tx_queue/CMakeLists.txt. COORDINATION: doing this mid-multi-agent-session flips sanitizer behavior for all concurrent test builds; latent UB in other dirs will start failing tests. Land it when no other waves are in flight.

title: Dev-provisioned peers keyed by hwid EUI-64, not canonical SHA-512(pubkey) - SIID key selection always misses
description: Wave review of jfln (SIID-indexed key selection) found: the new comment in lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/lichen_l2_peer.c:113-128 claims trust-store entries are keyed by canonical key-derived EUI-64, but the only in-tree populator (dev_provision_peer, lichen_l2_dev.c:62-82) keys entries by CONFIG_LICHEN_L2_DEV_PEER_EUI64 (board/hwid form), while wire SIID is SHA-512(pubkey)[0:8] | U/L. On every dev-provisioned build peer_find_locked(parsed.signer_iid) misses and ALL signed frames reject -EAUTH. Same outcome as the old trial-verify (binding gate rejected them too), so not a regression, but the wave enshrines an unenforced invariant and the new 'unknown SIID rejected' log misleads field debugging (the peer IS pinned, under a different key form). Fix options: enforce canonical keying at pin time in lichen_peer_add (SHA-512 of pubkey, memcmp vs key arg) or key dev provisioning by the canonical form. No announce/EDHOC populator exists in-tree yet.

title: C root DAO processing installs delegated sub-/128 targets as host routes, not prefix routes
description: With the generalized prefix gate (project-LICHEN-worker6-ekcc, l327) delegated sub-/128 Targets now install end-to-end: process_dao stores the canonical snapshot and rebuild_routes inserts the canonical prefix bytes as a host-style route (lichen_rpl_routing_table_add, is_prefix=false, path ends at the prefix value). Proper semantics per spec/05-routing.md 8.7.1 ('a Target prefix is reachability information, not a hop address; its zero-filled canonical value MUST NOT be inserted into a source route') require lichen_rpl_routing_table_add_prefix with egress=origin and managed-prefix reconciliation (Rust rebuilt_routes reconciles managed prefixes; C preserve_prefix_routes only preserves). Observable gap: exact-address lookup of the canonical prefix matches, but LPM for hosts inside the prefix does not. Discovered-from: project-LICHEN-worker6-ekcc. Needs snapshot prefix_len tracking or a parallel prefix-snapshot path.

title: tunnel_auth: revoked re-post returns Revoked instead of Replay
description: cargo test -p lichen-gateway --lib tunnel_auth::tests::revocation_root_change_expiry_and_lru_fail_closed fails deterministically at lichen-gateway/src/tunnel_auth.rs:954: after table.revoke(...), re-accepting the same root post asserts Err(TunnelAuthError::Replay) but accept_post returns Err(TunnelAuthError::Revoked). Pre-existing failure in committed code (tunnel_auth.rs last modified in 660b9bf3bf, no working-tree changes). Discovered while verifying bead project-LICHEN-worker6-5a5h; out of that bead's scope. Either the revocation check should report Replay for an already-seen post (ordering), or the test expectation needs updating after design review — do not weaken the test to pass; fix the check ordering or document the intended precedence.

title: Wire remaining orphaned vector files to Python consumers (f4z7 remainder)
description: f4z7 disposition remainder after the 2026-08-29 session wired root_dio_signature.json (14), capability_announcements.json (9), node-addresses.json (3) via python/tests/crypto/test_orphan_vector_consumers.py. NOT WIRED, with per-file disposition: (1) coap_lci_auth.json (14) - vectors need source-address+iface-scoped is_local_admin policy; Python lichen.coap.access is transport-level only (TRANSPORT_LEVELS dict), no address-based admin surface. (2) gateway_discovery.json (22) - wire-format CoAP messages, no Python CoAP wire parser surface. (3) dodag_version_authorization.json (1) - Rust-only surface (rust/lichen-node/src/routing/router.rs DODAG-VERSION), no Python verifier. (4) ccp5_coordination_mechanism_negotiation.json (8) - needs mechanism_enum priority selector; Python has select_channel but no mechanism+slot negotiation surface (stale pycache shows an old consumer once existed - regression risk). (5) lr_fhss.json (12) - airtime table, no Python airtime function. (6) propagation.json (14) - path-loss model, no Python surface. (7) gcp_handoff_cose_sign1.json - COSE_Sign1 handoff messages; lichen.gateway.handoff has HandoffRequest/Response CBOR encode/decode but no signature verify surface. (8) Python consumers also missing for Rust/C-consumed files: checkin_rollcall, dio_time_option_malformed, gcp_psk_oscore, gradient_table, node_handoff, sf_assignment, wire_format_v2. Work item: add real Python surfaces or mark files C/Rust-only in test/vectors/README.md, then drive them.

title: Spec 02-physical-link.md duplicated section 4.5 contradicts itself (FNV vs CRC32 canonical)
description: While fixing the crc32_init drift (worker6-6qy5): spec/02-physical-link.md section 4.5 DAD Retry Strategy pins fnv1a32 pseudocode (derive_short_addr = fnv1a32(eui64) & 0xFFFF), and the section 3.4 summary line also says short-address DAD uses FNV-1a32. But the canonical decision (project-LICHEN-bo37, resolved) and both implementations - Python lichen.link.short_addr.derive_short_addr (crc32_ieee with init 0x4348454e = low32 of ASCII LICHEN) and Rust lichen-core short_addr.rs (LICHEN_CRC32_INITIAL = 0x4348_454e) - use CRC32-IEEE. The committed tests assert crc32 (python/tests/test_vectors.py test_dad_hash_algorithm_resolution, rust/lichen-core/tests/short_addr_vectors.rs authoritative_crc32_clarification_vectors). The module docstring calls the spec fnv section 'the duplicate 4.5 at the end'. Fix: deduplicate section 4.5 in spec/02-physical-link.md to the crc32_ieee pseudocode, fix the 3.4 summary line, and keep FNV-1a32 only for TDMA/channel-selection hash_32. Spec file - outside agent scope for the vector-fix session, hence this bead.

title: Capability announcement prefix encoding: vector pins 16-byte prefix for /64, Python requires prefix_len/8 bytes
description: Found wiring test/vectors/capability_announcements.json. capability_prefix_delegation and capability_both pin prefix=fd000000000000000000000000000000 (16 bytes) with prefix_len=64, but python/src/lichen/crypto/capability_announcements.py CapabilityPayload enforces prefix length == prefix_len/8 (8 bytes for /64) and raises ValueError('prefix must be 8 bytes for prefix_len 64, got 16') at decode. The vectors were generated by the independent reference oracle, so both sides are internally consistent - this needs a spec ruling (spec section 8.12 / 08-gateway-coordination.md): is the on-wire prefix field truncated to prefix_len bits (compact) or always 128-bit? Whichever side loses must be regenerated. Related layering notes from the same wiring session: reserved-bits and kid-vs-announcer_iid checks fire at DECODE level in Python while the vectors expect verify-level detection (net decision identical: invalid); invalid_reserved_bits pins capabilities=255 which Python cannot even construct. Consumer documents these as _DECODE_REJECT cases in python/tests/crypto/test_orphan_vector_consumers.py.

title: COSE decoders reject RFC 9052 tag-18 COSE_Sign1; vector corpora embed the tagged form
description: Found wiring test/vectors/root_dio_signature.json and capability_announcements.json (both embed cose_sign1 as RFC 9052 tag-18-tagged CBOR). Python RootDioSignature.from_cose_sign1 and decode_cose_sign1_announcement do cbor2.loads then require isinstance(list) of len 4 - a tag-18 CBORTag raises ValueError('COSE_Sign1 must be a 4-element array'). Every cross-impl consumer must unwrap tag 18 first (see _untagged_cose_sign1 helper in python/tests/crypto/test_orphan_vector_consumers.py). Decide one side: (a) accept both tagged and untagged forms in the decoders (RFC 9052 tags COSE_Sign1 when standalone), or (b) regenerate the vector corpora untagged and document the convention. C/Zephyr decoders should be audited for the same strictness.

title: create_sender accepts key_generation=None; fragment-wire consume has vacuous None match
description: SchcSessionManager.create_sender (python/src/lichen/schc/session_manager.py) accepts key_generation=None. activate_and_start then records a session whose key_generation is None, and the fragment branch of consume_fragment_wire (line ~353) checks self._key_generation_lookup(record.remote_signer_identity) is key_generation, which is vacuously true when the peer is unknown (lookup returns None). A caller holding the manager can therefore mint fragment wires for a keyless stranger that pass consume-time validation. Discovered while fixing project-LICHEN-worker6-edbw (control-wire branch fixed there with a non-None + identity check; the fragment branch needs the same guard, or create_sender should reject None at the trust boundary). No legitimate flow passes None: link/schc_handler.py create_fragment_sender indexes _key_generations[remote] (real object) and restore_persistence_state rejects None.

title: C RPL: DAO Origin Signature option (0x12) is never cryptographically verified; origin_authenticated is caller-asserted
description: rpl_dao_process.c:226-245 validates the 0x12 DAO Origin Signature structurally only (present, exactly one, 56 bytes, final option). No DAO-domain Schnorr48 verifier exists in the C tree — lichen/subsys/lichen/link/sos_origin.c is the SOS domain (LICHEN-SOS-ORIGIN-v1), not spec/05 8.6's LICHEN-DAO-ORIGIN-v1. The test helper add_origin_signature (lichen/tests/rpl_routing/src/main.c:91-97) writes 56 dummy 0x5a bytes and the root APPLIES the DAO — pinning the absence of verification. origin_authenticated is purely caller-asserted, yet spec 05 8.6 says the root MUST verify DAO provenance, and a link-layer signature of the immediate sender does not bind the preserved DAO source to a key: an authenticated neighbor that forges the preserved source picks both origin and target and the byte-equal check passes. Fix: verify the 0x12 Schnorr48 at root ingest (schnorr48.c exists in the link subsystem — needs a DAO-domain transcript string per spec 05 8.6), or amend spec 05 8.6 to specify exactly what evidence origin_authenticated=true must represent. Discovered reviewing 65ca175106.

title: oscore: KeyUpdateContext::update() bypasses OwnershipRegistry (stuck claim + unclaimed new record)
description: rust/lichen-oscore/src/lib.rs:201/236-237: KeyUpdateContext::update() swaps the live context to a NEW ContextId via bare candidate.register_fresh without registry knowledge. For a registry-claimed context: (a) the old claim is stuck — release() with the new context returns false and the old id cannot be released without reconstructing old key material; (b) the new record is live and unclaimed — recreating the concurrent-receiver hazard. Fix: registry-aware rekey API (atomic release-old + claim-new), or minimally document a prohibition on update() for registry-managed contexts plus a debug assertion.

title: OwnershipRegistry not wired to production call sites; bare Context activation still recreates the split-brain
description: f4b089027c added rust/lichen-oscore/src/ownership.rs but enforcement is opt-in: rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:1016-1018 activates via bare Context::restore_existing/register_fresh and rust/lichen-node/src/secure.rs:542-549 via register_fresh_context — lib.rs:65-67 documents bare methods remain unguarded. Two separate registry instances, or one registry plus any bare call, recreate the concurrent-receiver split-brain the bead v0ee set out to close. Fix: migrate gateway.rs and node secure.rs activation paths through OwnershipRegistry (or deprecate/private the bare methods so the contract is enforced where traffic flows).

title: [review] process_route_state_diagnostic is an ungated gate-free install path for sub-/128 prefix routes
description: P2, wave-6 review. rust/lichen-rpl/src/routing.rs:862-897 is #[doc(hidden)] pub and NOT feature-gated (unlike process_dao/process_dao_at at :1055/:1091 which are #[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-helpers"))]). It calls extract_updates WITHOUT authorize_dao_prefixes then installs via process_dao_inner. Pre-wave-6 extraction required prefix_len==128 so only host routes could install; now a well-formed /64 body extracts and installs with no delegation check and arbitrary sequence_authority. In-process callers only, no wire path (production ingest is gated); in-tree callers are tests. Fix: feature-gate it like its siblings, or document deliberate trust-the-caller semantics.

title: OSCORE spec gap: C firmware has no production path satisfying spec 15.3 OSCORE state persistence
description:
SPEC: spec/06-security.md §15.3 (lines 1219-1238, landed 2026-08-28 in 660b9bf3bf): sender sequence reservations, recipient replay window, and response replay/correlation state MUST remain valid across restart; state MUST be persisted in a versioned authenticated record bound to the context under an independent monotonic rollback-and-deletion authority; missing/corrupt/unavailable state MUST fail closed. Implements RFC 8613 §7.5.

IMPL (two halves, both verified):
1. The compliant path exists and is correct: CONFIG_LICHEN_OSCORE_SETTINGS (lichen/subsys/lichen/oscore/Kconfig:36, default y) requires a platform-protected authority via oscore_settings_register_protection() (oscore_settings.c:166) before any context creation; restore/commit are bound to a BLAKE2b digest over IDs/algo/keys/IV (oscore_settings.c:108-139) with A/B slots + revision+digest authority (oscore_persist.c:309-386, fail-closed on deleted/torn/rolled-back state). BUT no caller registers the authority anywhere in the repo (grep for oscore_settings_register_protection outside tests: zero hits). With the default (SETTINGS=y, e.g. lichen/apps/puck/boards/t1000_e_nrf52840.conf:100-101), oscore_ctx_create* fails OSCORE_ERR_NVM_FAILED (oscore_ctx.c:355-368) — fail-closed and safe, but OSCORE is unusable in every default production C build.
2. With CONFIG_LICHEN_OSCORE_SETTINGS=n (or SETTINGS=n), contexts CAN be created with no persistence at all: only the sender SSN has an app-supplied NVM hook (oscore_nvm_register_callbacks — registered only by tests); the recipient replay window and response correlation state are RAM-only. Contexts are static across reboots (coap_keys_oscore.c:56 derives the master secret deterministically from the peer public key via oscore_ctx_create_from_peer_key), so after restart the device accepts previously-received requests — a direct spec §15.3 / RFC 8613 §7.5 violation (nonce-safety of the sender side is preserved by the set_sender_seq gate, but the replay window is not).

OBSERVED: no production-viable C configuration satisfies §15.3 today: settings-on fails closed at context creation (feature dead), settings-off loses replay protection across restart.

FIX: register a platform-protected monotonic authority (e.g., NVS-backed counter namespace separate from the blob slots) during native/board init before first OSCORE context creation, and wire it in puck/gateway C init; alternatively gate context creation on persistence being ready in ALL configs (remove the unprotected fallback) so the unprotected path cannot be built. Related: project-LICHEN-r6fu.2 (stale: 'OSCORE not implemented in C firmware'), project-LICHEN-ow3c.1.4 (tests for NVM failure paths).

title: OSCORE spec gap: C client sends outer code FETCH (0.05) for every OSCORE request
description:
SPEC: RFC 8613 §4.2 (normative, adopted by spec/06-security.md §8.8 'OSCORE (RFC 8613)'): 'With one exception (see Section 4.1.3.5), the Outer Code SHALL be set to 0.02 (POST) for requests'; only messages carrying the Observe option MUST use 0.05 (FETCH).

IMPL: lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/coap_client.c:604-610 — for every OSCORE-protected request (regardless of Observe), client_req.method is overridden to COAP_METHOD_FETCH, with comment 'For OSCORE requests, outer code is always FETCH (0.05) per RFC 8613.' The inner (encrypted) method is correct; only the outer code is wrong.

OBSERVED: every C-originated OSCORE request (GET/POST/DELETE alike) travels with outer code 0.05 FETCH instead of 0.02 POST.

IMPACT: SHALL violation. Compliant receivers discard the outer code (§8.2 step 1) so decryption is unaffected; residual impact is conformance and OSCORE-aware proxy semantics (FETCH vs POST cacheability, RFC 8613 §10). No cryptographic impact.

FIX: set outer method to COAP_METHOD_POST for non-Observe OSCORE requests; use FETCH only when an Observe option is present (and then the request also needs Inner+Outer Observe handling, which the C client currently lacks). Correct the comment.

title: ruff I001 x3 in python/src/lichen/crypto/__init__.py fails repo-root ruff check gate
description: Discovered while linting during worker6-xxpn validation. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml line 20) runs uv run --directory python ruff check; python/src/lichen/crypto/__init__.py has 3 un-sorted/un-formatted import blocks (I001, lines ~17, ~26, ~38 - capability_announcements, delegation_tokens, root_dio_signature imports), all autofixable with ruff check --fix. File is committed and untouched by the relay-signer work; the gate is red at HEAD 68c6e60d6f. Note: ruff format drift also exists in python/src/lichen/link/link_layer.py and replay.py at HEAD but format is not CI-enforced (only ruff check is), so those are out of scope.

title: edhoc responder tests fail/flaky at HEAD (capacity hold + close-during-completion)
description: Discovered during full python pytest run while validating worker6-xxpn on main 68c6e60d6f; pre-existing (reproduced in clean HEAD worktree). Failures: tests/coap/test_edhoc_responder.py::TestEdhocResource::test_completing_session_holds_capacity_until_finalized[False] and ::test_close_during_completion_cancels_publication_without_success. Count varies 2-3 between full-suite runs (one parametrized variant intermittently passes) - timing-dependent capacity/publication handling. Not touched by relay-signer work; separate from the tracked schc test_fragment failures (worker6-m8or).

title: Slot claim: signer authorization/quota model needs decision; validate_interleaved unused
description: Any pinned key-store entry can claim up to all 60 slots for its own IID; first claim never conflicts (scan sees only registered gateways); no per-gateway quota and lichen_slot_coord_validate_interleaved is never called to enforce ordinal/pattern consistency. Not a regression (pre-rewrite had the same model) and TOFU self-pinning is not mesh-reachable (key PUT is local-admin-gated), but one compromised provisioned key starves the DODAG capacity plan. Needs a spec-level decision on signer role/root-gateway authorization and quota policy (possibly human-flagged), plus calling validate_interleaved on accept.

title: GCP-6.5 slot claim: no canonical cross-implementation COSE vectors
description: test/vectors/gcp_slot_claim.json is still the legacy string-keyed format (no COSE_Sign1, no claim_seq/expiry, not the new integer-key 1-7 map), and no Python generator emits the new format - violating the repo invariant that all implementations match test/vectors. Extend the GCP handoff generator (see generate_gcp_handoff_cose_sign1.py / capability_announcements.py, which the C verifier was byte-parity-validated against) to emit canonical slot-claim vectors (valid, tampered-slots, replay, expiry, conflict) consumed by the C host test and Python/Rust.

title: Slot table: overridden/expired gateway entries never evicted; conflict scan ignores expiry
description: coap_slot_coord.c:461-462,501 - when a lower-IID claim overrides an existing entry the loser stays .valid with overlapping slots (double-booked table feeding later conflict checks); register_gateway never stores claim->expiry into valid_until and nothing evicts, so a decommissioned gateway's allocation blocks slots indefinitely; conflict scan (:441-481) checks only .valid. Fix: evict or invalidate the overridden entry, store expiry at registration, skip/expire entries past valid_until in the conflict scan.

title: slots_post resp_buf[128] too small: valid max-slot claims get 5.00 instead of 2.04
description: coap_slot_coord.c:1495 - encode_grant needs 173 B worst case (60x 2-byte slots), 149 B natural 0..59; empirically fails from ~40 high-numbered slots (129 B). Valid spec-max claims are rejected with 5.00 after full signature verification. Fix: size resp_buf >= 192 and add a host test exercising encode_grant at 60 slots (the suite currently never exercises the grant-encode path because slots_post is compiled out on host).

title: C RPL gate must adopt sub-/128 delegation semantics (match final Rust resolution (b))
description: The in-flight C port of the prefix gate (rpl_dao_process.c dao_targets_match_origin + lichen/tests/rpl_dao_auth) mirrors the PRE-i3m9 Rust behavior: every Target must be the origin's /128, sub-/128 and delegated prefixes are uninstalleable. The Rust reference has since moved to resolution (b) (i3m9, closed; review bead y00u closed): envelope accepts generalized Target bodies (spec/05-routing.md 8.7.1), extract_updates installs canonicalized sub-/128 delegated prefixes, /0 fails closed at every layer, authorization stays in the gate. The C gate needs: (1) operator-seeded static delegation table (C equivalent of PrefixDelegations, keyed by verified origin address; suggested API/impl preserved in /Volumes/Attic/tmp/lichen-ekcc-delegation/ snapshots), (2) generalized Target parsing in extract_updates (prefix_len 1..=128, >=ceil(prefix_len/8) octets, canonicalize; /0 rejected), (3) parity tests: delegated /64 end-to-end Applied, foreign /64 + /0 denied pre-mutation, delegation API fail-closed (DefaultRoute/PrefixLength/Capacity, idempotent re-register). Implemented once this session and surgically reverted due to a live write-write conflict on the same files — snapshots contain both workers' edits.
notes: Uncommitted implementation in lichen/subsys/lichen/rpl/include/lichen/rpl_routing.h. Adds lichen_rpl_prefix_delegate(), lichen_rpl_prefix_revoke(), lichen_rpl_prefix_delegation_authorizes() API. CONFIG_LICHEN_RPL_MAX_PREFIX_DELEGATIONS=64.
close_reason: C gate adopted resolution (b) sub-/128 generalized semantics; closed with ekcc (same change set). All three l327 asks delivered: (1) operator-seeded static delegation table = lichen_rpl_prefix_delegate/revoke/delegation_authorizes/delegations_reset implementing the free-function API this issue noted as uncommitted in rpl_routing.h (static storage, bounded CONFIG_LICHEN_RPL_MAX_PREFIX_DELEGATIONS=64, no malloc, canonicalizing, idempotent, fail-closed: /0 and >128 -> LICHEN_RPL_ERR_INVALID, capacity -> LICHEN_RPL_ERR_FULL, exact-match only); (2) generalized Target parsing in extract_updates (prefix_len 1..=128, >=ceil(prefix_len/8) octets, canonicalized, /0 rejected) AND the wire validator validate_dao_options relaxed to Rust is_generalized_target_body semantics (this was the hidden fourth layer - it rejected generalized bodies at DAO parse before the gate ever ran); (3) parity tests in lichen/tests/rpl_dao_auth: delegated /64 end-to-end Applied (canonical snapshot + route), foreign /64 + /0 denied pre-mutation (whole-root_state memcmp), delegation API fail-closed incl. capacity/idempotency/exact-match/origin-binding, /127 boundary, non-canonical bodies canonicalized, /63 vs /64 denied. /0 fails closed at all four layers (delegate, wire, gate, extract). Evidence: 9/9 rows under ASan+UBSan; five regression suites green; cppcheck zero new findings vs HEAD. Discovered follow-up: project-LICHEN-worker6-8t7x (sub-/128 installs as host-style route; needs add_prefix egress semantics). Cross-ref: project-LICHEN-worker6-ekcc close reason has full design + parity matrix.

title: spec: 9 stale decoy-hex COSE_Sign1 examples in spec/05, 06, 12 emit the alg spec/08 step 4 MUST-rejects
description: Commit 341e6cf78b fixed the protected-header example in spec/08:135 (h'a10139ffff' actually encodes {1:-65536}, not the stated {1:-65537}; correct bytes h'47A1013A00010000' = bstr-wrapped canonical {1:-65537}). The same stale example remains at 9 sites in 3 sibling specs: spec/05-routing.md:518 (the 8.7.2 delegation protocol the DAO authz test exercises), spec/06-security.md:323, 592, 884, 1010, spec/12-apps.md:1026, 1068, 1344, 1390. The Python reference delegation_tokens.py:_encode_protected_header emits a1013a00010000 -> on-wire bstr 47a1013a00010000, so an implementer following spec/05/06/12 literally emits the decoy alg that spec/08 step 4 says MUST be rejected — cross-impl divergence and mutual rejection by design. Fix: replace all 9 with h'47A1013A00010000' plus a one-line pointer to spec/08's wrapper paragraph (or fold into bead 5brg's scope which covers GCP-7.1's identical decoy in spec/08). Verify each with cbor2.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 4adc69db4e. All 9 sites replaced h'a10139ffff' -> h'47A1013A00010000' plus one-line pointer to spec/08-gateway-coordination.md 6.5 wrapper paragraph. Per-site: spec/05-routing.md:518; spec/06-security.md:323,592,884,1010; spec/12-apps.md:1026,1068,1344,1390. cbor2 proof: old a10139ffff decodes to {1: -65536} (MUST-reject decoy per spec/08 step 4); new 47A1013A00010000 decodes to bstr wrapping a1013a00010000 = {1: -65537}, canonical round-trip byte-exact. All 9 verified OK; each confirmed a genuine COSE protected-header context (none skipped). Leftover 39ffff: spec/08:144 (intentional decoy-explanation prose, kept) and spec/08:295,334 (GCP-7.1, owned by bead 5brg, out of scope). spec/05/06/12 now contain zero 39ffff occurrences.

title: [review] E=1 TransitInfo parse relaxation: non-root nodes now forward signed E=1 DAOs (wasted airtime, uncovered behavior change)
description: P2, wave-5 review. message.rs:1246-1249 makes E=1 parse (previously aborted parse). dao_parents_for_source (lichen-node/src/routing/router.rs:1151-1155) consumes TransitInfo without checking external; previously node.rs:597-601 refused to forward E=1 transits; now non-roots forward signed E=1 DAOs toward a root that rejects them (routing.rs:1504) - wasted airtime on LoRa, behavior change with no test. Fix: if transit.external { return None; } in dao_parents_for_source, or add a test documenting the new forwarding behavior as intended.

title: [review] PrefixDelegations has no revocation API; 64-entry exhaustion permanent until process restart
description: P2, wave-5 review. rust/lichen-rpl/src/routing.rs:199-248: PrefixDelegations exposes only delegate/authorizes/len/is_empty. On Err(Capacity) the only recovery is a process restart (table volatile by design). A mis-delegation to the wrong key cannot be undone without restarting the border router. Fix: add revoke(public_key, prefix_len, prefix) and optionally clear_origin(public_key); trivial against the HashMap<key, HashSet<(len,prefix)>> layout; add tests (revoke then deny; revoke then re-delegate; revoke unknown is Ok/noop).

title: [review] sub-/128 prefix delegations are gate-authorized but uninstalleable end-to-end (operator trap)
description: P2, wave-5 review (2 reviewers independently). rust/lichen-rpl/src/routing.rs: delegate() (routing.rs:205-230) accepts /1../127 and authorize_dao_prefixes (routing.rs:797-816) authorizes them, BUT no DAO can ever deliver one: envelope profile rejects Target options with length != 18 (message.rs:472-476) so truncated sub-/128 targets fail signature verification before the gate, and the 18-byte encoding with prefix_len < 128 is rejected by extract_updates (routing.rs:1481, parsed.prefix_len != 128 -> None). Net: operator who delegates a /64 gets RouteRejected on every DAO forever, indistinguishable from hostile origin. Test suite masks it: /64 rows only call authorize_dao_prefixes directly, no full-pipeline test (tests/dao_prefix_authorization.rs:483-530). Fix (choose one): (a) make delegate() reject prefix_len != 128 with explicit error until the 8.7.1 generalized profile ships, or (b) extend extract_updates to install delegated sub-/128 targets; add a full-pipeline test pinning the chosen outcome.
close_reason: Resolved via resolution (b) per project-LICHEN-worker6-i3m9 (the more recent decomposition, matching spec/05-routing.md 8.7.1 generalized Targets): envelope now accepts structurally-valid non-18-byte Target bodies (message.rs is_generalized_target_body) and extract_updates (routing.rs) installs canonicalized sub-/128 delegated prefixes; authorization stays in the routing gate which denies unauthorized sub-/128 pre-mutation; /0 fail-closed at every layer (delegate() refuses, gate denies DefaultRoute, extraction rejects prefix_len==0). Evidence: delegated /64 DAO installs end-to-end Applied (rust/lichen-rpl/tests/dao_prefix_authorization.rs delegated_slash64_dao_installs_end_to_end); foreign /64 and /0 RouteRejected with zero storage writes and empty high-water; full cargo test -p lichen-rpl green (232 lib + suites), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean. Candidate (a) (rejecting prefix_len!=128 in delegate()) was rejected: it would make the already-landed gate-authorized delegations permanently uninstalleable and contradict spec 8.7.1.

title: Make prefix-policy denial a distinct DaoProcessError variant
description: The prefix-authorization gate (project-LICHEN-2auf.44.9.2) returns rich reasons via DaoManager::authorize_dao_prefixes (PrefixAuthorizationError::Unauthorized(DefaultRoute|ForeignPrefix) / MalformedTarget), but at the process level DaoManager::process_signature_verified_inner maps denial to the pre-existing DaoProcessError::RouteRejected. Introducing DaoProcessError::UnauthorizedPrefix was blocked in scope: lichen-node/src/node.rs (~line 416-425) matches DaoProcessError exhaustively with no wildcard arm, and lichen-node was outside that task's touch scope (rust/lichen-rpl/ only). Fix: add variant UnauthorizedPrefix(UnauthorizedPrefixReason) (or similar) to DaoProcessError in rust/lichen-rpl/src/routing.rs, map the gate denial to it in process_signature_verified_inner, then add the one match arm in lichen-node/src/node.rs mapping it to DaoHandlingOutcome::RouteRejected (or a new outcome variant if desired). Keep gate-level literal tests in rust/lichen-rpl/tests/dao_prefix_authorization.rs green.

title: Delegation delivery: CoAP provisioning + persistence for prefix delegations (spec 8.7.2)
description: Spec 05-routing.md 8.7.2 defines how the root DELIVERS delegations: POST coap://[delegate]/.well-known/prefix-delegation, Content-Format application/cose cose-sign1, OSCORE root-delegate pairwise context, COSE_Sign1 payload {prefix, prefix_len, delegate_iid, E flag, delegation_seq, expiry}; node verifies root signature, delegation_seq > cached, caches by (prefix, prefix_len); root SHOULD send delegation on capability announce (spec 8.12 bit 1) or admin config. Nothing implements this. Scope: CoAP resource on root + handler on delegate, delegation_seq persistence, expiry enforcement, OSCORE requirement. The in-flight Rust PrefixDelegations table explicitly documents 'Provisioning and persistence out of scope; operator API seeded, re-seeded after restart' - this bead closes that gap per spec. Cross-impl alignment with python delegation_tokens.py. Decomposed from project-LICHEN-2auf.44.9.2.

title: Vectors: DAO prefix-authorization allow/deny matrix (cross-impl)
description: Repo rule: every packet format / cross-impl decision needs canonical vectors in test/vectors/. Add e.g. test/vectors/dao_prefix_authorization.json pinning the literal matrix: self /128 allow; foreign host route (/128 != origin) deny; /0 deny; undelegated broad prefix (e.g. /64) deny; delegated prefix allow (exact delegation, node-owned E=0); external E=1 with delegation allow only if delegation names external; expired delegation deny; wrong-origin delegation deny. Each vector: signed DAO wire bytes (Schnorr48 DAO Origin Signature per spec 8.6, origin pubkey, origin_sequence), root state (delegation table seed), expected outcome + rejection reason. Consumers: Rust DaoManager::process_signature_verified, Python dao_manager.validate_and_process_dao_wire_at, C process_dao (once foreign-host-route + origin binding land). Independent oracle: vectors computed once from the spec rules with the Python reference crypto, then hardcoded - never from the implementation under test. Decomposed from project-LICHEN-2auf.44.9.2.

title: Python: wire delegation_tokens into root DAO validation per spec 8.7.2
description: python/src/lichen/crypto/delegation_tokens.py (COSE_Sign1 create/verify/scope, spec 18.8.6) exists but nothing consumes it. python/src/lichen/rpl/dao_manager.py validates DAOs (validate_and_process_dao_wire_at) and enforces the .44.7 self-/128 profile only (dao_manager.py:869-886: multiple_target, target_mismatch); there is no delegation cache and no sub-/128 target path. Implement spec 8.7.2 root-validation steps: on DAO Target prefix != origin /128, lookup delegation for (target_prefix, target_prefix_len); reject expired/missing/E-flag-mismatched delegations before route or replay mutation; cache keyed by (prefix, prefix_len) with delegation_seq monotonicity. Keep /0 denied (spec 8.7.1: only exact ::/0 delegation ever authorizes, reserved for generalized-profile work). Add table-driven allow/deny tests mirroring rust/lichen-rpl/tests/dao_prefix_authorization.rs (self /128 allow, foreign /128 deny, /0 deny, broad undelegated deny, delegated allow once cache is seeded). Decomposed from project-LICHEN-2auf.44.9.2.
close_reason: Implemented spec 8.7.2 root DAO prefix-delegation authorization (commit 15a03b21b1). delegation_tokens.py: added PrefixDelegationTokenPayload/PrefixDelegationToken (spec 8.7.2 CBOR payload keys 1-6, E-flag bit0, reserved bits zero), create_prefix_delegation_token + verify_prefix_delegation_token reusing the module COSE_Sign1/Schnorr48 core. dao_manager.py: install_prefix_delegation() verifies token vs root identity (sig, IID binding, expiry, per-key delegation_seq monotonicity), rejects /0 (default_route) and caps table at 64 (delegation_capacity); _authorize_delegated_target() wired at the step-4 authenticated target boundary in _apply_dao_at_unlocked BEFORE any route/replay/persistence mutation: foreign /128 without delegation keeps the vector-pinned target_mismatch reason (test/vectors/dao_origin_signature.json coverage=target_mismatch stays green), else delegate_mismatch/delegation_expired/delegation_external_flag, exact (canonical prefix, prefix_len) lookup. Sub-/128 and /0 Targets are rejected at the .44.7 wire profile (malformed_option) before authorization, mirroring Rust InvalidOptionLength-before-authorize; a seeded /64 delegation cannot relax the wire profile. Tests: python/tests/rpl/test_dao_prefix_authorization.py, 12 table-driven tests mirroring rust/lichen-rpl/tests/dao_prefix_authorization.rs (self /128 allow, foreign /128 deny, /0 deny, broad undelegated deny, delegated allow after seeding with zero-mutation + floor-advance proofs, delegate binding, expiry, external transit, install fail-closed, capacity+seq monotonicity). Fixtures use create_prefix_delegation_token as round-trip/wiring only; token codec oracle suites tests/crypto/test_delegation_tokens*.py (31 tests) remain green. Verification: touched + dao/delegation suites 916 passed; tests/rpl+tests/crypto+test_vectors.py 2119 passed, 7 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (test_short_addr_derive_vector, test_dad_hash_algorithm_resolution; exist at HEAD per f099357cb8). ruff format + check clean. Note: delegated sub-/128 routes stay unrouteable pending the .44.9 generalized profile (Python routing table is /128-only); authorization API is prefix-len-general.

title: [review] EDHOC CID decode maps negative ints two's-complement, contradicting RFC 9528 3.3.2 encode side (roundtrip break)
description: P2, found during gt6u fix. ENCODE now per RFC 9528 3.3.2: byte h'21' transports as int -2 (wire 0x21). But DECODE maps wire int 0x20-0x37 two's-complement: wire 0x21 decodes to h'FE' (255-2), not h'21'. Per RFC 3.3.3 (0xFF -> 0x41FF) and 3.3.2, wire int -2 must mean byte string h'21' - so encode(h'21')=0x21 but decode(0x21)=h'FE': roundtrip breaks and cross-endpoint handshakes diverge whenever a CID byte is in 0x20-0x37. Unobservable today (all current CIDs <= 0x17 or multi-byte) but latent interop break. Fix: Python _validate_connection_id int branch (n<0 -> byte 0x1F-n... verify: -1 -> 0x20 => byte 0x20, -24 -> 0x37) and Rust external-crate parse_identifier 0x20-0x37 branch (cbor.rs:110); also responder.rs:263-275 inline msg1 C_I parse rejects negative-int and 0x58+ bstr forms. Add roundtrip tests: bytes 0x00..0xFF encode->decode identity for 1-byte CIDs.

title: Vectors: gcp_slot_claim_cose_sign1.json + generator (replay/expiry/mutation cases)
description:
Canonical test vectors + generator for GCP-6.5 slot-claim COSE_Sign1, focused on the parent bead's deltas (signature coverage of slots/expiry/claim_seq, replay gate, expiry, header-encoding bug). Complements — does not duplicate — qpco.4/qpco.8 (happy-path COSE cases); coordinate file naming so both land: propose test/vectors/gcp_slot_claim_cose_sign1.json + test/vectors/generate_gcp_slot_claim_cose_sign1.py.

Generator modeled on test/vectors/generate_gcp_handoff_cose_sign1.py (RFC 9052 Sig_structure :67, SHA256(CBOR(Sig_structure)) signing input, deterministic keys fixed for reproducibility — never derive vectors from the C/Python code under test; the generator + spec are the oracle).

Required cases (each: valid-sig positive and byte-level mutation negative where applicable):
1. happy_path_n1 / n4 / n60 — payload keys 1-7 (slots, superframe_epoch, mode, expiry, gateway_iid, claim_seq, ordinal), canonical CBOR field order 1..7 (RFC 8949 4.2.1; all single-byte keys sort numerically). Include exact COSE_Sign1 hex, Sig_structure hex, SHA-256 digest, signature hex.
2. slots_array_mutation — valid envelope signature, payload slots bytes altered -> MUST fail verification. THE regression case for the parent bead (old code verified only ordinal/IID/superframe_id, coap_slot_coord.c:316-337).
3. claim_seq_replay_equal / replay_lower — two claims same IID, second with claim_seq <= first -> receiver MUST reject (drives the NV high-water child).
4. expiry_boundary — now-1 (reject), now (reject: spec says expiry > now, :192), now+1 (accept). Use fixed timestamps.
5. header_alg_decoy — protected h'a10139ffff' ({1: -65536}, the spec/08:135 typo) -> MUST reject; h'47A1013A00010000' ({1: -65537}) -> accept.
6. kid_payload_iid_mismatch — unprotected {4: kid} != payload key 5 -> reject (spec step 6, :191).
7. ordinal_absent — 6-key payload without key 7 -> reject (receiver needs ordinal for register_gateway, coap_slot_coord.c:376).
8. expired_claim_stripped_seq / sig_over_wrong_payload — reuse-one-signature-across-two-payloads demonstrator: same sig attached to two different canonical payloads, exactly one verifies.

Schema: follow gcp_handoff_cose_sign1.json structure (include Sig_structure, signature_input field = "SHA256(CBOR(Sig_structure))", expected verify outcome per case, and a "reject_reason" aligned with the C enum values LICHEN_CLAIM_* where meaningful).

Acceptance criteria:
- JSON + generator committed; generator runs offline (fixed keys, no network) and reproduces the JSON byte-for-byte.
- Every case states expected outcome and reason; positives verify against python/src/lichen/crypto/schnorr48.py as the independent oracle (sign in generator, cross-check verify).
- Cases 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 are present (parent-bead-specific) and cross-referenced from the qpco.4 vector list.
- Existing test/vectors/gcp_slot_claim.json + gcp6_slot_coordination.json left untouched (old model; retired by the cross-validation child).

title: [review] lora_l2_tx.c:354 ignores lichen_csma_tx_complete result and passes raw lora_send ret (positive) to it
description: P2, discovered-from worker6-c4m7 (same wedge class). lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/lora_l2_tx.c:354 does (void)lichen_csma_tx_complete(&lora_data.csma, ret) where ret is the raw lora_send() result, which can be POSITIVE (bytes sent). tx_complete rejects tx_status>0 with -EINVAL BEFORE csma_try_lock (csma.c:216), so the machine stays in LICHEN_CSMA_TX_ALLOWED -> subsequent acquire calls return -EALREADY forever, same self-wedge as the c4m7 CCA gate bug, on the radio-boundary CSMA path. Also ignores CANCELLED (authorizes nothing here but the machine ends CANCELLED — actually safe phase-wise) and -EBUSY/-EPROTO (strand TX_ALLOWED). Suggested fix: normalize status (ret < 0 ? ret : 0), check the result like link_cca.c now does, and consider the same in-lock fail-closed validation for tx_complete in csma.c that c4m7 added for cad_complete (needs design care: marking ERROR after a physically successful TX is wrong bookkeeping; normalize at the caller). File is outside the c4m7 task allowlist, so tracked here.

title: group_oscore: epoch semantics not wrap/grace coherent (validate_epoch, key_valid_at, id_context collision)
description: python/src/lichen/crypto/group_oscore.py. Three coherent problems: (1) validate_epoch (:137-148) rejects every epoch < current immediately, but spec 18.8.2 (spec/12-apps.md:1218) says old key_epoch is rejected only AFTER a 1-hour grace period — grace lives only in key_valid_at; two exported predicates encode contradictory acceptance policy. (2) Wrap unsafety: at current=0xFFFFFFFF the true successor (epoch 1, what rekey emits) is numerically < current -> rejected as rollback; key_valid_at tests material.epoch == self._current.epoch and key_for_epoch searches by number (:160,166), so after wrap the original epoch-1 material becomes unresolvable and the original epoch-max material reads future_epoch_unknown; test_wrap_boundary_validation (test_group_oscore.py:101-105) blesses the inconsistency instead of pinning the laggard side. (3) id_context = group_id||epoch collides across wrap (epoch 2 recurs): if key material were ever reused across the wrap boundary, nonce reuse gives full plaintext recovery. Fix: wrap-aware comparison via wrap-generation counting or distance metric; identity compare (material is self._current) in key_valid_at; drop/replace _previous entries whose epoch would collide on wrap; mix wrap generation into id_context or document never-reuse as an invariant; add the laggard-side test; reconcile validate_epoch with the grace window or explicitly document the split.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 1ee62b6a51: validate_epoch is now the documented accept-for-processing gate (wrap-aware signed distance on the cyclic epoch space; accepts current, +1 successor, and -1 predecessor while its material is held within the spec 18.8.2 grace window); key_valid_at is use-authorization scoped to held material by identity, not epoch-number equality; rekey drops retained entries whose epoch would collide with the wrapped epoch and enforces the never-reuse-across-wrap invariant via explicit RuntimeError (hmac.compare_digest), keeping the vector-pinned group_id||epoch id_context encoding unchanged. test_wrap_boundary_validation replaced by TestWrapCoherentSemantics (laggard-side accepts both directions, strict grace boundary, identity disambiguation, collision drop, reuse refusal). Vector verdicts in group_oscore_key.json unchanged (key_epoch_increment, epoch_rollback_reject current=5/message=3, epoch_future_reject current=5/message=7 all green). Tests: python/tests/crypto/test_group_oscore.py 19 passed; group_oscore_key.json consumer suites (test_group_oscore_epoch.py, test_group_oscore_wrap.py, test_security_app_vector_consumers.py) green, 159 total passed. ruff format + check clean.

Fix: add one byte-exact fixture from an external source (RFC 8037 A.4 ECDH-ES+A128KW example, or value computed offline with an independent JWE implementation) asserting the wrapped blob and 40-byte length for 32-byte secret / 24 for 16-byte. Also assert len(wrapped_key)==40 in round-trip tests.

title: [review] DRX2/DAD1 persistence: document tamper/rollback boundary (CRC32 detects corruption, not tampering)
description: P2 disposition-bead, wave-3 security review. lichen-hal/src/storage.rs:47-75 slot integrity is CRC32 only; generation u64 lives inside the record it orders, so an attacker with flash-write access can (a) roll back BOTH slots, (b) delete the newer slot so open_redundant picks the old one, or (c) forge a minimal record (origin_sequence=1 floor, recompute CRC) -> open_root trusts it as high-water and replay checks accept captured signature-valid DAOs as fresh. Bounded: same flash-write capability already means total compromise (identity keys live there too); format is explicitly provisional/unshipped. Disproportionate fixes rejected. FIX (in scope): document the boundary in persistence.rs/storage.rs module docs: DRX2/DAD1 provide corruption detection, NOT tamper resistance; anti-rollback anchor is physical flash possession. Optionally note the defense-in-depth path (device-key MAC + independent monotonic NVS counter) as future work. Do NOT implement the MAC now.

title: [review] extracted SX1262.cs: oversize length prefix permanently kills reader while socket looks Connected (node silently deaf)
description: P2 (pre-existing, inside reviewed ReaderLoop scope). .extraction/renode-lora-peripherals/peripherals/sx126x/SX1262.cs:801 ReadMessage returns null for len > 1024; ReaderLoop treats null as peer-closed and breaks (:707-709) WITHOUT closing the socket; EnsureConnected sees socket.Connected==true (:629) and never restarts a reader -> TX_DONE/RX_PACKET/RX_TIMEOUT never dispatched again until peripheral reset. One corrupted 4-byte header bricks RX. Fix: treat oversize as protocol fault: log + Disconnect() (forces reconnect + fresh reader) instead of returning null as EOF; same for peer-close path: close the socket before break (:795,801,808).

title: [review] CCA gate ignores lichen_csma_tx_complete result; TX_ALLOWED can strand after concurrent cancel/lock
description: P2, wave-3 review. link_cca.c:111 does (void)lichen_csma_tx_complete(&ctx->csma, 0); return 0. If tx_complete returns -EBUSY (csma lock held by concurrent snapshot/TX) phase stays TX_ALLOWED -> all future gate calls -EALREADY -> -EPROTO wedge (same class as the positive-cad_status P1). If cancel was requested tx_complete returns CANCELLED (positive) and the gate still returns 0, authorizing TX after cancellation. Fix: check the result; on failure lichen_csma_reset(&ctx->csma) or map CANCELLED -> -ECANCELED. Add test if cheap (cancel during gate).
close_reason: Fixed in link_cca.c TX_ALLOWED case: lichen_csma_tx_complete result is now checked. LICHEN_CSMA_RESULT_CANCELLED -> return -ECANCELED (cancellation wins, TX not authorized; CANCELLED phase self-recovers on next start). Negative result -> best-effort lichen_csma_reset(&ctx->csma) then propagate the error (reset cannot fully fix a contended lock but prevents a stranded TX_ALLOWED phase from wedging once the lock frees). Test NOT added: the two failure branches need an actor between cad_complete (TX_ALLOWED) and tx_complete, or a concurrently held csma lock — no single-threaded injection point exists in the link_ctx gate harness (cancel-during-gate would need a new hook in link_cca.c); tests/csma/main.c was outside this task's file allowlist. Discovered while closing sibling c4m7.

title: (authz) Slot-claim replay protection in C slot coordinator
description: AUDIT (epic 6mij decomposition): coap_slot_coord.c has NO sequence/replay tracking: 'rg -n seq|replay|seen' over lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/coap_slot_coord.c returns zero matches. A captured, validly-signed claim (Schnorr48 verify at coap_slot_coord.c:331 passes) can be REPLAYED to re-mutate allocation state; conflicting resolution is lowest-IID-wins (coap_slot_coord.c:11, spec/08-gateway-coordination.md:100-105), so a replay of an older low-IID claim can evict a newer legitimate owner. The Rust reference already advances replay high-water durably (see bd project-LICHEN-worker6-07cg: 'GatewayCoordinator::handle_post_slots durably advances SlotClaimVerifier replay state') - the C side has no equivalent. spec/06-security.md:16 mandates 'Replay: Sequence numbers, OSCORE replay window'. FIX (after the dispatch gate lands, worker6-2hte): either (a) rely on the OSCORE request-freshness window for protected claims and document that reliance here, or (b) add explicit per-peer claim seq monotonicity check in lichen_slot_coord_process_claim() mirroring the Rust SlotClaimVerifier; state which and test it. ACCEPTANCE: (1) replaying an accepted signed claim does not re-mutate state (test: POST same captured claim twice, second is rejected/ignored); (2) behavior matches the Rust reference path for the same claim sequence; (3) documented decision recorded in this issue.
