Contract decision: are rollcall status responded/missing arrays optional?
description:
Cross-implementation contract divergence on Rollcall Status documents (spec/12-apps.md 18.6.3): Rust RollcallStatus::from_cbor (rust/lichen-client/src/checkin.rs) REQUIRES both responded and missing arrays; the C codec (lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/checkin.c:1103-1143) treats them as OPTIONAL defaulting to empty.

## Decision: REQUIRED arrays (even when empty)

Rationale:
1. One representation, not two - 'missing' and 'empty array' mean the same thing, pick one
2. Parsers are simpler - no conditional 'if exists' handling
3. Explicit contracts catch bugs earlier - server forgetting to populate fails loud
4. Cost is trivial - empty CBOR array is 1 byte (0x80)

## Action
1. Fix C codec to REQUIRE both arrays (reject if absent)
2. Update checkin.h docs to match (remove 'optional' language)
3. Add test vector with empty arrays to pin the contract
4. Rust is already correct - no changes needed

## Files to modify
- lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/checkin.c:1103-1143
- lichen/include/lichen/checkin.h:407-424
- test/vectors/ (add empty-arrays vector)
notes: 2026-08-28: Human decision - require arrays, fix C. Rust behavior is correct.

title: deaddrop: 24-bit predictable drop IDs enable enumeration; group drops leak existence via 4.03
description: deaddrop.rs:897-911 generate_drop_id masks splitmix64(now ^ counter) to 0xFF_FFFF - no entropy beyond 24-bit output space; GET /deaddrop/{id} is unrate-limited so 2^24 enumeration is hours of traffic; 4.03 for group drops confirms existence/ACL boundary to non-recipients (:1156-1163), public drops leak content. 6-hex length is spec-baked (18.9 example) so unpredictability is the achievable fix. Fix: derive IDs from CSPRNG (getrandom; std crate) or HMAC(server_secret, context||counter); consider counting misses against a limiter. Keep vector conformance (vectors pin format, not entropy).
close_reason: Drop IDs now drawn from the OS CSPRNG via getrandom 0.2 (3 bytes -> 6 lowercase hex, format per spec 18.9 example; collision-retry kept). This mirrors the Python reference's secrets.token_hex(3) (python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py:41-43), replacing the splitmix64(now ^ counter) scheme that leaked entropy from an enumerable 24-bit space; the now-dead id_counter field was removed. 6-hex format and generate-on-collision semantics preserved, so vectors pinning format stay honest. New test generated_drop_ids_are_canonical_and_unique (16 add_drops: canonical format + uniqueness, deterministic since the store rejects duplicate IDs). Note: enumeration-rate-limiting of GET /deaddrop/{id} was 'considered' per the bead but deferred — bead oan4 handles the loop bound; miss-counting against the limiter remains open as a policy choice. Verified: cargo test -p lichen-client --lib 130 passed, deaddrop_vectors 24 passed (22 baseline + 2 new). Cargo.lock staged as a single-line hunk (getrandom 0.2.17 dep edge for lichen-client; version already in lock). Commit 9da8dd3503.

title: checkin.rs decoders diverge from C/Python oracle: trailing bytes, duplicate keys, node format, no size cap
description: rust/lichen-client/src/checkin.rs four conformance gaps vs committed vector checkin_node_format and C codec: (1) from_cbor at :325 :433 :539 uses ciborium::from_reader without Cursor position check - trailing garbage accepted while C returns TRAILING_DATA and deaddrop.rs:336-341 (same wave) rejects; (2) text_key :138-142 first-wins on duplicate map keys - C rejects DUPLICATE_KEY, Python cbor2 last-wins, msg.rs:930-933 crate precedent rejects with RFC 8949 5.6 rationale; (3) node field only checked non-empty (:329-335, :263-266) while vector checkin_node_format pins invalid examples (192.168.1.1, 0011:2233:4455:6677) and C enforces 39-char 8-group IPv6 (checkin.c:49-70) - port lichen_checkin_addr_valid as invalid_node_format; (4) CheckIn/RollcallRequest/RollcallStatus from_cbor have no input size bound (ciborium depth is bounded at 256, but unbounded input length grows unbounded Vecs - C caps tracks at LICHEN_ROLLCALL_TRACK_MAX 32, checkin.c:1030-1032). Fix all four, extend vector test to pin trailing-bytes/duplicate-key/node-format rejection, keep vector error codes verbatim.
close_reason: All four decoder-conformance gaps fixed and committed a10a1e845d (rescued uncommitted work from a timed-out agent session, verified + completed): (1) trailing bytes rejected via Cursor position check in all three from_cbor (error trailing_data); (2) duplicate map keys rejected per RFC 8949 5.6 / msg.rs precedent (duplicate_key); (3) node format validated as full-notation IPv6 8x4-hex (invalid_node_format), port of C lichen_checkin_addr_valid, vector checkin_node_format pinned; (4) input size caps (CHECKIN_CBOR_MAX 512 / ROLLCALL_REQ_CBOR_MAX 160 / ROLLCALL_STATUS_CBOR_MAX 5120, payload_exceeds_maximum) + track arrays capped at LICHEN_ROLLCALL_TRACK_MAX 32 (out_of_range). Tests: checkin_rollcall_vectors 11/11 (new: decoders_reject_trailing_bytes, decoders_reject_duplicate_map_keys, checkin_node_format_pinned_by_vector), lichen-client --lib 130/130. cargo fmt clean on touched files; clippy clean for checkin.rs (1 pre-existing warning in foreign WIP msg.rs).

title: checkin_resource.c: shared s_payload used outside its mutex
description: read_payload() memcpys request bytes into module-static s_payload BEFORE locking (callers :96 :151 :229) and GET handlers respond from s_payload AFTER unlocking (:128-142, :202-221). Safe only because coap service is single-threaded today; any second execution context interleaving serves torn/foreign bytes - the mutex exists precisely because the module does not trust that forever. Fix: hold s_lock across lichen_coap_respond for handlers emitting s_payload and move the payload copy under the lock.

title: lichen_rollcall_status_to_cbor: unguarded STATUS_STRINGS index, OOB on caller-supplied enum
description: checkin.c:1262 indexes STATUS_STRINGS[t->status] (3-element) with status copied verbatim from caller via public lichen_rollcall_record_responded/record_missing (checkin.c:1706-1720). Any value >=3 is OOB read/hard-fault class on MCU. Sibling lichen_checkin_to_cbor defends exactly this via status_str()==NULL -> -INVALID_STATUS (checkin.c:439-444). Fix: validate status in record_* entry points and/or guard index in status_to_cbor, symmetric with checkin codec; host-suite test with out-of-range enum.
close_reason: lichen_rollcall_status_to_cbor no longer indexes STATUS_STRINGS unguarded: responded-loop status now goes through lichen_checkin_status_str() with a NULL -> -LICHEN_CHECKIN_ERR_INVALID_STATUS fail-closed return, symmetric with lichen_checkin_to_cbor's defense. lichen_rollcall_record_responded/record_missing validate track->status at the public entry points (status is rendered when a track moves back to responded), so stored state can never hold an out-of-range value. Header docs updated with the new return values. Regression test_rollcall_invalid_status_rejected added: bogus enum 99 rejected by both record_* entry points with lists untouched, encoder returns -INVALID_STATUS on a hostile struct, valid status still renders and round-trips. Evidence: host suite 16/16 pass under ASan/UBSan; cppcheck findings identical to baseline (5 pre-existing in main.c, none new).

title: lichen_checkin_post: cap==0 NULL deref + size_t underflow on documented-legal config
description: lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/checkin.c:1550-1564. checkin.h:443 documents checkins=NULL with checkin_cap=0 as legal; first POST then takes 0>=0 eviction branch: entry=&svc->checkins[0] on NULL (UB), checkin_count-- wraps 0->SIZE_MAX, memmove gets wrapped length. rollcall side fails closed with 5.03 for same config (checkin.c:1638-1640) - asymmetry confirms oversight. Kconfig range 1..256 protects only the resource instance, not public API. Fix: early return BAD_REQUEST/5.03 when checkin_cap==0 before eviction block; add host-suite regression with cap-0 store.
close_reason: lichen_checkin_post now returns 5.03 LICHEN_CHECKIN_CODE_UNAVAILABLE when checkin_cap==0 before the eviction block (checkin.c, mirrors rollcall 5.03 policy at checkin.c:1646-1648), so the documented-legal NULL/cap-0 store (checkin.h:443) can no longer form &checkins[0] on NULL or wrap checkin_count to SIZE_MAX. Header @return doc updated. Regression test_checkin_zero_capacity_store added to host suite. Evidence: lichen/tests/checkin_rollcall 15/15 pass under ASan/UBSan (was 14 tests); cppcheck findings identical to untouched tree (5 pre-existing literalWithCharPtrCompare in main.c, none new); clang-tidy parity (no compile db, pre-existing).

title: deaddrop: add_drop evicts live drops before validating explicit drop_id
description: rust/lichen-client/src/deaddrop.rs:999-1008: evict_for_space() runs before params.drop_id canonical/uniqueness validation; a request with invalid or duplicate explicit ID returns None AFTER evicting unexpired live drops (expired-then-oldest FIFO). A rejected create destroys other users' data. Spec 18.9 eviction is meant to admit a stored drop, not fire on doomed requests. post() is safe (fallible checks precede eviction). Fix: hoist canonical-ID/uniqueness check above evict_for_space; add regression test (fill store to capacity, add_drop with drop_id Some(nothex), assert no live drop vanished).
close_reason: Hoisted explicit drop_id canonical/uniqueness validation above evict_for_space in add_drop (rust/lichen-client/src/deaddrop.rs): a doomed request (non-canonical or duplicate ID) now returns None before any eviction, per spec 18.9 (eviction admits a stored drop, never fires on doomed requests). Regression test add_drop_doomed_explicit_id_preserves_live_drops fills a capacity-sized store, fires invalid/duplicate explicit-ID requests, asserts the live drop survives, and confirms FIFO eviction still works for an admissible request. Verified: cargo test -p lichen-client --lib (130 passed) + --test deaddrop_vectors (23 passed, was 22 + 1 new). Commit 31e1ed25c6.

title: [review] piv_len > 0 used as proxy for unprotect success in keys + oscore respond guards
description: P2 latent. coap_keys.c:281,293,306,320,335,347,360,370,380,391,441 and coap_oscore.c:98 guard protected-response selection on piv_len>0 instead of tracked unprotect status. Safe today because oscore_protect.c:400 and coap_oscore.c:194 reject 0-length PIV (canonical-PIV convention), but if the rule is ever relaxed every branch silently degrades to UNPROTECTED lichen_coap_respond fallback, leaking response codes/key-presence in cleartext for OSCORE requests. Fix: track unprotect success in a bool set on r==OSCORE_OK; use that for the guard, in handlers and in coap_oscore_respond_resource.

title: [review] lichen-oscore: provisioning.rs orphaned (not declared in lib.rs), subtle dep dead
description: P2 (pre-existing, surfaced by wave-1 review). rust/lichen-oscore/src/provisioning.rs (~900 lines, uses subtle/sha2/HKDF) is NOT declared in lib.rs -> silently not compiled; subtle is an unused dependency in every configuration. Decide: declare the module (if provisioning API is wanted) or delete the file + dep. Note lichen-node has its own provisioning module (separate). Do not silently re-enable: check whether the API matches the current oscore crate version before declaring.
notes: 2026-08-28: Human decision - INTEGRATE. Rust gateway needs BR provisioning. Python is reference. Work items: .3 (lib.rs), .4 (deps), .5 (fix errors), .6 (tests).

title: [review] deaddrop_get node= is a non-NUL-terminated pointer into option buffer passed as const char*
description: P2 latent (no provider registered in-tree today). coap_dtn.c:173-181 extracts node= as qopts[i].value+5 pointer into the CoAP option buffer and passes to s_provider->retrieve(buf, sizeof(buf), node) whose API contract (coap_dtn.h:54) invites strlen/strcmp -> reads past option into packet buffer. Fix: copy into NUL-terminated bounded local (char node[32]; n=MIN(len-5,sizeof-1)) before use; document the copy contract in coap_dtn.h.

title: [review] rtc_rx8130ce set_time: no input validation, 1 << tm_wday UB for -1/>31
description: P2. rtc_rx8130ce.c:150+94: wday2rtc computes 1 << wday; struct rtc_time.tm_wday documented domain includes -1 (unknown) and is int -> 1 << -1 is UB, >31 also UB; out-of-range sec/min/hour/day/mon produce invalid BCD written to the chip. Inherited verbatim from upstream 4.1 but the RTC API documents field ranges so the driver should validate and return -EINVAL. Fix: range-check all fields incl tm_wday>=0, clamp/reject, return -EINVAL.

title: [review] key store skips TOFU binding validation when persistence not initialized
description: P2. coap_keys_store.c:369-378 lichen_key_store_put() validates trust/IID-pubkey binding ONLY when s_persistence_ready. Admin PUT on a node that never ran lichen_key_store_init() accepts arbitrary iid/pubkey pairs incl garbage trust; no later path re-validates RAM state. Integrity checks must not be conditional on persistence. Fix: validate binding unconditionally, degrade only persistence. Found during 6mij.2.2 verification review.

title: [review] coap_dtn register: k_mutex_init on held mutex + non-idempotent registration wipes state
description: P2. lichen_coap_deaddrop_register (coap_dtn.c:71-88) takes s_dtn_buf_mutex then lichen_coap_dtn_init() executes k_mutex_init(&s_dtn_buf_mutex) on the HELD mutex — ownership reset voids exclusion until the final ignored unlock; also re-k_work_init_delayable on a possibly-scheduled work item and re-lichen_dtn_init() wipes the buffer on double registration. Benign at today's boot-time-only use, hazard if ever called with traffic in flight. Fix: K_MUTEX_DEFINE static init (drop k_mutex_init pair), make register reject/reject-noop double init, verify work item handling.
close_reason: Verified fixed at HEAD: (1) no k_mutex_init anywhere - all three mutexes use static K_MUTEX_DEFINE (coap_dtn.c:25,29,30); lichen_coap_dtn_init (:273-278) only calls oscore_init/lichen_coap_client_init. (2) Double register returns -EALREADY at coap_dtn.c:72-75 BEFORE lichen_coap_dtn_init/lichen_dtn_init/k_work_init_delayable - no buffer wipe, no work re-init. (3) Partial-init failure paths leave s_provider NULL. Confirmed by 3-perspective review (correctness/security/edge, zero findings) of this file during 4xln close, and by grep of current source. No code change needed.

title: [review] protected request with empty payload gets plain 4.00 instead of protected error
description: P2 RFC 8613 4.2.1. coap_dtn.c:122 and :239-241: for a verified OSCORE request, missing payload returns positive COAP_RESPONSE_CODE_BAD_REQUEST which the framework sends UNPROTECTED, while every other error path in the same handlers uses coap_oscore_respond_resource (protected). Conformant clients discard plain responses to protected requests -> silent retransmit loop. Fix: route the empty-payload error through coap_oscore_respond_resource(...,BAD_REQUEST,...) like the store-failure path.

BLE SenML relay driver
description:
Consume BLE scan data, lookup IPSO mapping, create SenML records, emit to mesh.

**Scope:**
- Accept (MAC, service_uuid, char_uuid, raw_value) tuples from BLE scanner
- Lookup IPSO mapping via gatt_ipso_registry
- Parse raw_value via gatt_value_parser
- Construct SenML record:
  - bn (base name): 'ble:<MAC>/'
  - n (name): '<object_id>/<resource_id>' or IPSO path
  - v (value): parsed physical value
  - u (unit): SenML unit from IPSO mapping
  - t (time): relative timestamp if aggregating
- Aggregate multiple readings within configurable window
- Apply rate limiting (per-device and global)
- Emit SenML pack to configured destination

**CoAP config interface:**
- GET/PUT /config/ble-relay for runtime configuration
- enabled, max_pkt_per_device_min, max_pkt_global_min, aggregation_window_ms, destination

**Dependencies:**
- gatt_ipso_registry (subtask 1)
- gatt_value_parser (subtask 2)
- SenML codec (existing)

**Output:** python/src/lichen/ble/senml_relay.py

title: BLE characteristic value parser
description:
Decode standard BLE GATT characteristic formats to physical units.

**Scope:**
- Parse BLE characteristic value bytes according to GATT format descriptors
- Support common formats:
  - sint16 with 0.01 scale (temperature in 0.01 degrees C)
  - uint16 with 0.01 scale (humidity in 0.01 percent)
  - uint8 percentage (battery level)
  - sint16/uint16 with various scales (pressure, etc.)
  - IEEE-11073 FLOAT types
- Handle endianness (BLE uses little-endian)
- Return physical value with appropriate precision

**Format table (examples):**
| Characteristic | Format | Scale | Unit |
|----------------|--------|-------|------|
| 0x2A6E Temperature | sint16 | 0.01 | Cel |
| 0x2A6F Humidity | uint16 | 0.01 | %RH |
| 0x2A19 Battery Level | uint8 | 1 | % |
| 0x2A6D Pressure | uint32 | 0.1 | Pa |

**Output:** python/src/lichen/ble/gatt_value_parser.py

title: BLE GATT UUID to IPSO mapping registry

**Scope:**
- Define data structure for UUID -> IPSO mapping (service UUID, char UUID) -> (object ID, resource ID, unit)
- Implement lookup function: given service_uuid + char_uuid, return IPSO mapping or None
- Populate registry with common BLE GATT services:
  - 0x181A Environmental Sensing -> IPSO 3303 (Temperature), 3304 (Humidity), 3315 (Barometer)
  - 0x180F Battery Service -> IPSO 3320 (Battery)
  - 0x181C User Data -> various IPSO mappings
  - 0x1810 Blood Pressure -> IPSO 3316
  - 0x1809 Health Thermometer -> IPSO 3303
- Support both 16-bit short UUIDs and 128-bit full UUIDs

**Reference:** spec/appendix-gatt-ipso.md (Appendix K)

**Output:** python/src/lichen/ble/gatt_ipso_registry.py

coap_oscore_unprotect_resource_request returns 0 after sending 4.01 on ctx miss; callers double-respond
description: Found while verifying bd 6mij.2.2. coap_oscore.c:62-65: when oscore_ctx_get_by_eui64 fails, the helper sends 4.01 via coap_oscore_send_unauthorized() and returns ITS result, which is 0 (OSCORE_OK) on send success. Documented contract ('return 0 on success, CoAP response code on error') makes callers treat 0 as 'continue'. Example: coap_msg.c msg_sent_post (line ~957) proceeds past ret!=0, then oscore.payload==NULL (memset by helper) triggers coap_oscore_respond_resource(...BAD_REQUEST...) which sends a SECOND response on the wire - the client gets 4.01 then an unprotected 4.00 for one request. Suggested fixes (owner's call): return a nonzero CoAP code after sending so callers return immediately, or have the helper take over response duty exclusively and document that callers must return without responding when result->ctx==NULL and is_protected; audit existing call sites in coap_msg.c either way. Note: /keys handlers (coap_keys.c) avoid this defect by keeping the ctx-miss path inline; if they migrate to the shared helper this must be fixed first.

title: LICHEN L2 disable: retry incomplete queue destruction
description: Round-4 correctness review found that after common disable returns a deinit failure and leaves LORA_DESTROY_FAILED, retrying common disable calls stop(), receives success for the non-RUNNING state, skips deinit, and falsely reports successful teardown. Recognize DESTROY_FAILED on the common disable path, retry lichen_lora_l2_deinit(), and continue to propagate incomplete cleanup; add a regression.
notes: 2026-08-29 worker: needs_destroy_retry() implementation verified present (lora_l2.c:705) and disable-path retry per 2026-08-28 comment; close requires native_sim ping_l2 run (test_disable_retries_incomplete_queue_destruction) on AWS builder.

DESTROY_FAILED retry on the common disable path: lichen_lora_l2_deinit accepts DESTROY_FAILED -> DEINITING with goto destroy_queue (lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/lora_l2.c:469-474), needs_destroy_retry query at lora_l2.c:707, failed destroy sets LORA_DESTROY_FAILED (lora_l2.c:667), and the common disable path retries deinit instead of falsely reporting success (net_if_down path completes the retry). Regression: test_disable_retries_incomplete_queue_destruction (lichen/tests/ping_l2/src/main.c:551-607) corrupts a pool handle, asserts deinit fails, retry flag set, stats -ECANCELED, init refused, then repaired handle + net_if_down completes teardown and re-init succeeds. title: TX queue: prevent stale deadline resurrection after half-range
description: Round-4 security review found that 32-bit deadline_expired arithmetic can make an entry appear unexpired again when it is first serviced at least 2^31 ms after its deadline. Admission bounds future deadlines but does not bound how late expiry is checked. Store enough monotonic deadline provenance to keep queued packets expired across long inactivity and add a deadline-plus-half-range regression.
close_reason: Fixed via 64-bit queue-local time base: extend_now64() low-32 forward-difference extension, deadline_expired() now 64-bit compare, enqueue computes deadline_ms64 = now_ms64 + (deadline - now), deadline_valid_future() rejects absolute deadlines beyond next half-range (delta 0 or > INT32_MAX). Host test test_stale_deadline_not_resurrected_after_half_range passes; suite 37/37 under ASan+UBSan and TSan.

comments.author: Mark Atwood
comments.text: Fixed on this branch (uncommitted): tx_queue.c now extends each 32-bit monotonic sample onto a queue-local 64-bit time base (tx_queue_now64/extend_now64) and stores a 64-bit absolute deadline per entry; expiry compares in 64-bit so an entry serviced >=2^31 ms past its deadline stays expired (same provenance pattern as the .4 64-bit enqueue_order fix). Regression: test_stale_deadline_not_resurrected_after_half_range in lichen/tests/tx_queue/main.c (exact half-range, half-range+wrap, and long-but-legal-future cases). Host ASan+UBSan and TSan: 37/37.

title: LICHEN L2 disable: propagate LoRa deinit failure
description: Round-3 security review found lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/lichen_l2_init.c logs lichen_lora_l2_deinit() failure after stop returns -ECANCELED but later returns success based only on stop_ret. A tx_queue_destroy failure therefore leaves LoRa aborted/terminal while the interface reports successful disable. Preserve and return deinit_ret; translate stop -ECANCELED to success only when deinit succeeded.

title: TX queue: sample pop time after acquiring lock
description: Round-3 correctness review found tx_queue_pop() calls get_now_ms() before acquiring queue->lock. A pop blocked behind another operation can pass the packet deadline while waiting, yet expiry and selection use the stale sample and may transmit an expired packet. Move clock sampling under the lock before expiry/selection, return clock errors before mutation, and add a blocked-pop regression test.
acceptance_criteria: A pop delayed across a queued packet deadline expires/drops it and returns EAGAIN rather than transmitting; clock failure leaves state intact; sanitizer-backed host tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by host sanitizer suite plus review cycle; superseding round-4 findings are tracked separately

title: rust/lichen-rpl dodag.rs: reject-silently at MAX_PARENT_CANDIDATES prevents adopting better parents
description: Python fix (project-LICHEN-worker6-dbdn) added MAX_PARENTS=16 with eviction of the worst non-preferred parent when a strictly better candidate arrives (dodag.py _make_room_for). Rust rust/lichen-rpl/src/dodag.rs lines 449-456 instead silently drops any NEW candidate when at MAX_PARENT_CANDIDATES=16 capacity, so a node at capacity can never replace a degraded parent with a genuinely better one until the parent is pruned by other means. Divergence from the Python eviction semantics; consider parity: evict highest path_cost non-preferred parent when incoming candidate is strictly better. Note rust ParentCandidate has no last_heard field.

title: Vectors: confessions.json senml_cbor_hex is corrupt CBOR
description: The senml_cbor_hex in test/vectors/confessions.json vector anonymous_confession_default is not valid CBOR and contradicts the vector's own senml_json: (1) content text header claims 75 bytes but the following bytes contain a NUL, 'theforward' (missing space) and 'today' (text absent from senml_json which has 65 chars); strict parse fails at offset 66 (utf-8 error inside the text string). (2) stray byte 0x8b after the lat f64. (3) stray 0x01 after the anonymous record value. (4) trailing a900 garbage after the ttl record. (5) anonymous/ttl v fields encode as bare integers (02 01) but the repo canonical SenML codec (lichen-senml wire.rs, byte-parity with Python lichen.senml.codec.pack per test/vectors/senml_location.json) always encodes v as f64 (0xfb). No test in the repo consumes this hex byte-exactly (python/tests/test_node_coap_integration.py only asserts it is parseable hex), so the corruption is currently invisible to CI. title: TX queue: expire stale entries before rejecting incoming deadline
description: Correctness review of project-LICHEN-worker6-l1qw.8.17.17.1 found that the new absolute-deadline validation in tx_queue_push() runs before tx_queue_push_at(), while the canonical B.3.1 push contract requires stale queued entries to expire as step 1. Rust expires existing entries before rejecting an expired incoming deadline. Move validation into the locked push sequence after expire_packets_locked() so observable queue state and packets_dropped_deadline remain cross-implementation consistent even when the incoming deadline is invalid.
acceptance_criteria: A push with an invalid incoming deadline first expires all stale queued entries and increments deadline-drop statistics, then returns -EINVAL without admitting the incoming packet or incrementing full/preemption stats; C host tests cover the ordering and pass under ASan/UBSan.

title: TX queue C conformance: validate behavioral vector cases
description: Robustness review of the new B.2 C vector generator found that it opens tx_queue_bounded.json and tx_queue_implementation.json but consumes only the bounded capacity and ENOBUFS constant. Changes to canonical preemption, same/lower-priority backpressure, expiry, FIFO pop order, or implementation-contract expectations would not affect the generated header or fail CTest. Validate the named behavioral cases and expected outcomes while generating the header so every required vector file is a meaningful build oracle.
acceptance_criteria: gen_vectors.py validates named bounded and implementation cases for priority values, deadlines, preemption victim/action, same/lower-priority rejection, expiry action/stat, FIFO priority order, ENOBUFS, deadline-before-capacity ordering, and oldest-lowest preemption; malformed or divergent vectors fail generation with a clear error; normal generation and sanitizer-backed CTest pass.

title: TX queue: reject ambiguous absolute deadlines
description: Robustness review of project-LICHEN-worker6-l1qw.8.17.17.1 found that tx_queue_push() documents deadline_ms as less than 2^31 ms ahead of current uptime but does not enforce the precondition. deadline_expired() uses half-range modular comparison, so a caller-supplied deadline more than INT32_MAX milliseconds ahead can be accepted and then treated as expired, yielding a successful enqueue followed by an unexpected drop. Validate the signed half-range after reading the clock and before mutating queue state; reject already-expired and too-far-ahead absolute deadlines consistently with -EINVAL. Add exact-boundary and wraparound tests.
acceptance_criteria: tx_queue_push rejects deadlines at/past now and deadlines more than INT32_MAX milliseconds ahead; accepts now+INT32_MAX including across uint32 wrap. Per the canonical push order, existing stale entries may expire and update deadline-drop stats before rejection; the invalid incoming packet itself is never admitted and does not change full/preemption stats. Existing default deadlines and expiry behavior remain green under ASan/UBSan.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by host sanitizer suite plus review cycle; superseding round-4 findings are tracked separately

title: handoff.py OscoreState.from_cbor_map lacks type validation for bytes/str fields
description:
File: python/src/lichen/gateway/handoff.py
Lines: 199-211

OscoreState.from_cbor_map() validates integer bounds for numeric fields (lines 189-197):
- replay_index, replay_bitfield, sender_sequence: checked against 0 to 2^64-1
- window_size: checked against 1 to 256

However, lines 199-206 extract fields WITHOUT type validation:

```python
return cls(
    master_secret=params[_KEY_OSCORE_SECRET],
    master_salt=params[_KEY_OSCORE_SALT],
    sender_id=params[_KEY_OSCORE_SENDER_ID],
    recipient_id=params[_KEY_OSCORE_RECIPIENT_ID],
    algorithm=params[_KEY_OSCORE_ALG],
    hashfun=params[_KEY_OSCORE_HASHFUN],
    window_size=window_size,
    id_context=params.get(_KEY_OSCORE_ID_CTX),
    ...
)
```

Expected types:
- master_secret: bytes
- master_salt: bytes
- sender_id: bytes
- recipient_id: bytes
- algorithm: int
- hashfun: str
- id_context: bytes | None

Python dataclasses do not enforce type hints at runtime. A malicious CBOR payload could inject wrong types (e.g., master_secret=123 as int) that create an invalid OscoreState. This causes downstream failures when the state is used for OSCORE crypto operations.

Fix: Add type checks before construction:

```python
master_secret = params[_KEY_OSCORE_SECRET]
if not isinstance(master_secret, bytes):
    raise HandoffError("master_secret must be bytes")
master_salt = params[_KEY_OSCORE_SALT]
if not isinstance(master_salt, bytes):
    raise HandoffError("master_salt must be bytes")
# etc.
```

Impact: Defense in depth for handoff protocol. Malformed payloads rejected early with clear error instead of cryptic crypto failures.

title: handoff.py HandoffResponse.decode missing dao_seq/path_seq type validation
description:
File: python/src/lichen/gateway/handoff.py
Lines: 385-386, 648-649

HandoffResponse.decode() extracts dao_seq and path_seq without type validation:

```python
dao_seq = data.get(_KEY_DAO_SEQ)
path_seq = data.get(_KEY_PATH_SEQ)
```

These values are later used in accept_handoff() with arithmetic:

```python
safe_dao_seq = response.dao_sequence + 1
safe_path_seq = response.path_sequence + 1
```

If a malformed response provides non-integer types (e.g., string, list, dict), this causes TypeError at line 648-649 instead of clean rejection at parse time.

The HandoffRequest.decode() method properly validates timestamp type (line 300-301):
```python
if not isinstance(timestamp, int):
    raise HandoffError("timestamp must be integer")
```

The same pattern should be applied to dao_seq and path_seq in HandoffResponse.decode().

Fix: Add after lines 385-386:
```python
if dao_seq is not None and not isinstance(dao_seq, int):
    raise HandoffError("dao_sequence must be integer")
if path_seq is not None and not isinstance(path_seq, int):
    raise HandoffError("path_sequence must be integer")
```

Impact: Fail-fast validation; prevents unexpected TypeError during handoff acceptance.
close_reason: Closed

title: handoff.py FreshnessState.from_cbor_map lacks type validation
description:
File: python/src/lichen/gateway/handoff.py
Lines: 236-247

FreshnessState.from_cbor_map() extracts fields from CBOR without validating their types:

```python
return cls(
    sequence=data["seq"],
    active_until=data.get("active"),
    retain_until=data["retain"],
    updated_at=data["updated"],
)
```

Expected types:
- sequence: int
- active_until: float | None
- retain_until: float
- updated_at: float

If malformed CBOR provides wrong types (e.g., a string for sequence), the dataclass stores them without error. Issues manifest later when the values are used (e.g., arithmetic on non-numeric sequence).

Compare to OscoreState.from_cbor_map() which validates integer bounds and types carefully (lines 189-197).

Fix: Add type checks before construction:
```python
if not isinstance(data["seq"], int):
    raise HandoffError("sequence must be integer")
if not isinstance(data["retain"], (int, float)):
    raise HandoffError("retain_until must be numeric")
# etc.
```

Impact: Defense in depth; malformed handoff responses could cause unexpected exceptions instead of clean rejection.
close_reason: Closed

In delegation_tokens.py, from_cbor() does not type-check fields after CBOR decoding.

title: P2: handoff.py no replay_bitfield size validation
description:
File: python/src/lichen/gateway/handoff.py
Line: 188

In OscoreState.from_cbor_map(), replay_bitfield is extracted from CBOR with no size validation:

    replay_bitfield=replay[1],

Python integers are arbitrary precision. An attacker-crafted CBOR payload could set replay_bitfield to an astronomically large value (e.g., 2^1000000), causing memory exhaustion when stored and processed.

OSCORE replay windows are typically 32 or 64 bits. The code should validate:
    if not 0 <= replay_bitfield < 2**64:
        raise HandoffError('replay_bitfield out of range')

Fix: Add bounds check for replay_bitfield and replay_index in from_cbor_map(). Consider also validating window_size has a reasonable maximum.

Impact: Memory DoS via malformed handoff response.
close_reason: Closed

title: P1: handoff.py missing expiry validation in COSE request
description:
File: python/src/lichen/gateway/handoff.py
Lines: 667, 690-712

HandoffRequestCosePayload has an 'expiry' field (line 667) specifying when the request expires, but nothing validates that current_time < expiry:
- from_cbor() parses expiry but doesn't check it
- HandoffRequestCoseSign1.verify() checks signature but not expiry
- No caller in this module validates expiry

This allows replay of captured handoff requests after their intended expiry time, bypassing the time-limited validity that expiry is meant to enforce.

Fix: Add expiry validation in verify() or create a validate_request() method that checks:
1. ts <= current_time (request not from future)
2. current_time < expiry (request not expired)

SECURITY: Enables replay attacks on handoff protocol.
close_reason: Closed

title: P1: handoff.py atomicity bug - node orphaned on partial failure
description:
File: python/src/lichen/gateway/handoff.py
Line: 525

In NodeRegistry.handle_handoff_request(), the node is unregistered (line 525) BEFORE the HandoffResponse is returned. If the caller fails to send the response or it is lost in transit:
- Source gateway has already removed the node from registry
- Target gateway never receives state
- Node becomes orphaned (not registered anywhere)

The spec (docstring lines 7-12) describes a 5-step handoff where step 3 is 'A releases node from its registry, sends confirmation'. This implementation releases first, then returns the response for sending -- the release should be conditional on successful delivery.

Fix: Either use a two-phase commit (mark as 'pending handoff', then finalize on ACK), or defer unregister() until after caller confirms response was sent. Alternatively, add a timeout-based cleanup where orphaned nodes are re-registered if no confirm is received.

SECURITY: This enables denial-of-service by triggering handoffs and blocking responses.
close_reason: Closed

title: spec/02a: MitigateInterference empty slot_map allows TX
description: MitigateInterference step 3 (line 585) checks 'IF Op.SlotMap is non-empty AND Slot NOT IN Op.SlotMap'. When slot_map is empty (root assigned zero slots), condition evaluates false and node proceeds to TX. But line 78 says empty array indicates no transmit slots and joiners MUST NOT transmit outside slot_map. Fix: 'IF Op.SlotMap is empty OR Slot NOT IN Op.SlotMap THEN defer'.

title: spec/02a AdaptiveSFSelect pseudocode uses Density>10 but should be Density>8
description:
## Location
spec/02a-coordinated-capacity.md line 417

## Problem
The AdaptiveSFSelect pseudocode step 3 says:
```
3. IF (Density > 10) OR (Utilization > 150) THEN SF = MIN(12, SF + 2)
```

But the threshold should be Density > 8, not Density > 10.

## Evidence of inconsistency

Within the same spec document:
- Line 392 (SelectChannel): `IF Density > 8 THEN RETURN 0`
- Line 409 (table SF9 row): `Density > 8` triggers downgrade
- Line 411 (table SF11 row): `Density > 8` triggers downgrade
- Line 449 (AdaptiveDutyPermille): `IF Density > 8 THEN`

In implementations:
- C: `LICHEN_RF_DENSITY_HIGH = 8`
- Rust: `DENSITY_HIGH: u8 = 8`

In test vectors:
- ccp16.json line 189: "density=10 forces channel 0, sf=11 (density>8)."

## Impact
An implementation following the pseudocode literally would use Density > 10 while implementations following the table, other pseudocode, or test vectors would use Density > 8. This causes different SF selection behavior for density values 9-10.

## Fix
Change line 417 from:
```
3. IF (Density > 10) OR (Utilization > 150) THEN SF = MIN(12, SF + 2)
```
to:
```
3. IF (Density > 8) OR (Utilization > 150) THEN SF = MIN(12, SF + 2)
```
close_reason: Fixed: Changed Density > 10 to Density > 8 in AdaptiveSFSelect pseudocode at line 418 to match DENSITY_HIGH threshold used throughout the spec and implementations

title: AdaptiveSFSelect LoadFactor parameter unused in pseudocode
description: spec/02a-coordinated-capacity.md line 414 declares LoadFactor as a parameter to AdaptiveSFSelect, and line 410 mentions 'load_factor > 0.8' as a downgrade condition in the thresholds table. However, the pseudocode body (lines 415-422) never uses LoadFactor - it only uses Utilization. Either LoadFactor should be used per the table, or the parameter and table entry should be removed. P2 spec inconsistency.
close_reason: Fixed pseudocode: added LoadFactor > 0.8 condition to step 5 to match thresholds table. Test vector select_channel_sf11_load_threshold confirms: load_factor=0.9 triggers SF=11.

title: Spec/vector mismatch: SelectChannel epoch endianness

The concatenated_data_hex values in vectors confirm LE (e.g., epoch=0x12345678 becomes bytes 78563412). Either spec text or vectors must be corrected for interop. P1 correctness.

title: spec/02a:336 Pseudocode OnMissedSuperframe ignores SYNCED state missed-beacon transition
description: Section 2a.6.2 FSM table defines SYNCED->DESYNCED transition on '>3 missed beacons'. Section 2a.6.6 pseudocode provides OnMissedSuperframe() but it explicitly ignores SYNCED state: 'IF State != RECOVERING THEN RETURN State'. There is no procedure for handling missed beacons in SYNCED state. Implementers have no algorithm for this required state transition. Fix: Add OnMissedBeacon() procedure that tracks missed_beacon_count in SYNCED state and transitions to DESYNCED when threshold exceeded.

title: spec/02a:263 Off-by-one: >3 missed beacons vs BEACON_TIMEOUT_SUPERFRAMES=3
description: Section 2a.6.2 state transition table says SYNCED->DESYNCED on '>3 missed beacons' (meaning 4 or more). Section 2a.6.3 defines BEACON_TIMEOUT_SUPERFRAMES=3 with description 'Consecutive missed beacons before DESYNCED' (implying transition at 3). Implementations following the table would transition at 4 missed beacons; implementations following the parameter would transition at 3. Causes interop failure in mixed deployments. Fix: Either change table to '>=3' or change BEACON_TIMEOUT_SUPERFRAMES to 4.

title: spec/02a-coordinated-capacity.md:377 - SelectChannel epoch byte order inconsistent

title: root_dio_signature.py: from_cbor lacks type validation for decoded values
description:
In RootDioSignaturePayload.from_cbor() lines 151-159, decoded CBOR values are passed directly to the constructor without type validation. If a malformed payload has wrong types (e.g., dodag_id as an integer instead of bytes), __post_init__ will raise TypeError on len(self.dodag_id) rather than a clear ValueError.

File: python/src/lichen/crypto/root_dio_signature.py
Lines: 151-159

Failure scenario: Attacker sends CBOR payload with dodag_id as integer (e.g., 42) instead of bytes. Validator sees 'TypeError: object of type int has no len()' instead of 'ValueError: dodag_id must be bytes'. Error reveals implementation details and may confuse error handling logic.

Fix: Add type assertions before passing to constructor, e.g.:
if not isinstance(payload_map.get(_PAYLOAD_DODAG_ID), bytes):
    raise ValueError('dodag_id must be bytes')

title: spec/02a-coordinated-capacity.md:63 - CDDL schema covers binary fields incorrectly

The CDDL incorrectly includes fixed binary header fields as if they were CBOR-encoded, which will cause interop failures if implementers follow the CDDL literally.
close_reason: Fixed CDDL schema to only cover CBOR options tail (offset 24+). Removed fixed binary header fields (epoch, num_slots, sfn, etc.) that are NOT CBOR-encoded. Added clarifying text and included slot_map and pow_challenge in the schema.

Implementations cannot correctly implement this transition without knowing the threshold value.

title: spec/02a-coordinated-capacity.md:389 - SF8 missing from thresholds table

title: root_dio_signature.py: from_cbor raises KeyError instead of ValueError for missing keys
description:
In RootDioSignaturePayload.from_cbor() lines 151-159, if required keys are missing from the decoded CBOR map, a KeyError is raised with just the numeric key constant (e.g., KeyError: 1). This provides poor error context for debugging.

Lines: 151-159

title: GATT-to-IPSO lookup table for C
description:
Implement Appendix K mapping as C lookup table for firmware.

**Deliverable:**
- Header: lichen/include/lichen/gatt_ipso.h
- Source: lichen/subsys/lichen/gatt_ipso.c

**API:**
```c
struct gatt_ipso_mapping {
    uint16_t gatt_uuid;      // GATT characteristic UUID
    uint16_t ipso_object;    // IPSO object ID
    uint16_t ipso_resource;  // IPSO resource ID
    const char *senml_unit;  // SenML unit string
    float unit_scale;        // multiplier (e.g., 133.322 for mmHg->Pa)
    float unit_offset;       // offset (e.g., -32*5/9 for F->C)
};

const struct gatt_ipso_mapping *gatt_to_ipso(uint16_t gatt_uuid);
```

Cover priority characteristics:
- Environmental (0x2A6E temp, 0x2A6F humidity, 0x2A6D pressure)
- Health (0x2A37 heart rate, 0x2A1C temperature, 0x2A9D weight)
- Location (0x2A67 location+speed)
- Battery (0x2A19 level)

~50 rows for common sensors. Extensible.

Reference: spec/appendix-gatt-ipso.md

title: BLE-to-SenML relay driver
description:
Translate scanned BLE data to SenML packs and relay over LICHEN mesh.

**Requirements:**
- Consume (MAC, service UUID, characteristic UUID, value) from scanner
- Lookup IPSO object/resource via Appendix K mapping table
- Pack as SenML with bn=ble:<MAC>, appropriate n/u/v fields
- Rate limit outbound: max packets/minute per device, global cap
- Aggregate multiple readings into single SenML pack when possible
- Configurable destination (broadcast, specific IPv6, border router)

**CoAP config resource:**
```
GET/PUT /config/ble-relay
{
  "enabled": true,
  "max_pkt_per_device_min": 6,
  "max_pkt_global_min": 30,
  "aggregation_window_ms": 2000,
  "destination": "ff02::1"
}
```

**Depends on:**
- BLE scanner driver (worker6-3y7a)
- GATT-to-IPSO lookup table (worker6-dldn)
- SenML codec

Reference: spec/appendix-gatt-ipso.md, spec/appendix-senml.md

title: BLE scanner driver for Zephyr
description:
Implement BLE scanning on nRF52840/ESP32 for LICHEN nodes.

**Requirements:**
- Configurable on/off via CoAP resource or compile flag
- Scan for BLE advertisements (passive, no pairing)
- Optionally connect to read GATT characteristics
- Device allowlist/denylist by MAC prefix or service UUID
- RSSI threshold: ignore devices below threshold (only relay nearby)
- Rate limit: max scans/minute, configurable

**CoAP config resource:**
```
GET/PUT /config/ble-scanner
{
  "enabled": true,
  "scan_interval_ms": 5000,
  "rssi_min_dbm": -70,       // ignore weaker signals
  "allowlist": ["0x180D", "0x181A"],
  "denylist": []
}
```

Typical RSSI thresholds:
- -50 dBm: very close (<1m)
- -70 dBm: same room (~5m)
- -85 dBm: nearby (~10m)
- -100 dBm: edge of range

**Output:** Callback with (MAC, RSSI, service UUID, characteristic UUID, value) tuples.

Platform: Zephyr BLE stack (CONFIG_BT_OBSERVER, CONFIG_BT_CENTRAL)
Reference: spec/appendix-gatt-ipso.md

title: SenML to IPSO Direct gateway translation
description:
Add bidirectional translation in gateway module

- SenML record with IPSO-style name (3303/0/5700) -> IPSO Direct path + value
- IPSO Direct response -> SenML record with object/instance/resource name
- Preserve units and timestamps where applicable
- Use for bridging heterogeneous networks

title: IPSO Direct CoAP resource handlers
description:
Add IPSO Direct resource handling to CoAP server in python/src/lichen/coap/

title: test_channel.py: misleading comment about channel vs tdma formula
description:
## Location
python/tests/link/test_channel.py:179-180

## Bug
Comment incorrectly states:
```python
# tdma.py uses max(num_channels, 3) while channel.py uses max(n_channels - 1, 1)
```

Both `synchronized_hop_channel` implementations use `max(n_channels, 3)`. The `max(n_channels - 1, 1)` formula is in `select_channel`'s hash-based path, not `synchronized_hop_channel`.

## Impact
Could mislead maintainers into incorrect changes or confusion about implementation parity.

## Fix
Correct or remove the misleading comment. The implementations are identical for positive 32-bit seeds.

title: P2: random.seed(42) pollutes global random state on every request
description:
File: python/src/lichen/dashboard/app.py
Line: 316-317

Bug: The `partial_topology_data()` handler calls `random.seed(42)` inside the function body when generating fallback mock data. This reseeds the global `random` module on every request when no simulator data is available.

Impact:
- Makes all subsequent `random` calls predictable after this endpoint is hit
- Could cause subtle reproducibility bugs in other parts of the application using `random`
- If `random` is used for anything security-adjacent elsewhere, this weakens it

Fix: Use a local Random instance instead of reseeding the global:
```python
rng = random.Random(42)
mock = [
    {
        "id": f"n{i}",
        "x": rng.uniform(0, 800),
        "y": rng.uniform(0, 380),
        ...
    }
    ...
]
```
close_reason: Closed

title: P1: WebSocket timeout bug on Python 3.10 - wrong exception type caught
description:
File: python/src/lichen/dashboard/app.py
Line: 352-353

Bug: Code catches `TimeoutError` but `asyncio.wait_for()` raises `asyncio.TimeoutError`.

In Python 3.10, these are different exception types. Only in Python 3.11+ did `asyncio.TimeoutError` become an alias for `TimeoutError`.

The code requires Python 3.10+ (uses `X | Y` union syntax), so this bug affects Python 3.10 users.

Impact: On Python 3.10, WebSocket connections crash on timeout instead of receiving keep-alive pings. The exception propagates, falls through to `except Exception: break`, and the connection closes unexpectedly.

Fix: Catch `asyncio.TimeoutError` instead of `TimeoutError`, or catch both:
```python
except (TimeoutError, asyncio.TimeoutError):
    await websocket.send_text('{"event":"ping"}')
```
close_reason: Fixed by catching both TimeoutError and asyncio.TimeoutError at line 385 with noqa comment for ruff UP041

title: test_global_random_does_not_perturb_percentiles uses local RNG, not global
description:
**File:** python/tests/sim/test_metrics.py:473-495

**Bug:** The test claims to verify that 'Process-global random draws must not change seeded percentile output' but it does NOT actually perturb global random state.

**Problem Code (lines 483-488):**
```python
rng_noise = random.Random(0)  # Creates LOCAL Random instance
for i in range(n):
    # Comment says: 'Inject noise into global random state between operations'
    rng_noise.randint(0, 10_000)  # Does NOT affect global random!
```

**Why this is wrong:**
- `rng_noise` is a local `random.Random` instance, not the module-level global state
- Calling `rng_noise.randint()` only advances `rng_noise`'s internal state
- The global `random` module state (used by `random.randint()`) is never touched
- This test would pass even if `Metrics` DID use global random

**Impact:** False confidence in RNG isolation. If someone refactored Metrics to accidentally use global random, this test would not catch it.

**Fix:** Change the noise injection to actually use global random:
```python
for i in range(n):
    random.randint(0, 10_000)  # Actually perturbs global random state
    ...
```

**Contrast with test_seeded_rng_produces_deterministic_percentiles (line 441):** That test correctly monkey-patches `random.randint` to trap global calls. This test should either do the same or actually call global random.
close_reason: Closed

title: prepare_candidate: StopIteration propagates with unhelpful error if SCHC version option missing
description:
Location: python/src/lichen/rpl/dodag.py lines 585-588, prepare_candidate closure

Issue: The code uses next() with a generator expression to find the SCHC Rule Version option. If no matching option exists, bare StopIteration is raised with no helpful error message.

Code:
    version_option = next(
        option for option in detached.options if option.type == SCHC_RULE_VERSION_TYPE
    )

The comment claims cardinality is enforced by transact_authenticated_schc_dio before calling prepare_candidate, but defensive programming should handle the case explicitly with a clearer error.

Fix: Use next() with a default or wrap in try/except:
    version_option = next(
        (option for option in detached.options if option.type == SCHC_RULE_VERSION_TYPE),
        None
    )
    if version_option is None:
        raise ValueError("missing required SCHC Rule Version option")

title: max_tx_ms missing duty_permille validation
description:
File: python/src/lichen/timing/duty_cycle.py
Line: 72-82

Bug: The function accepts duty_permille without validation. Negative values produce negative transmit times, which are nonsensical.

Impact: Silent incorrect calculation. A caller passing duty_permille=-10 would receive max_tx_ms=-36000, which would fail unpredictably in downstream code expecting positive milliseconds.

Fix: Add validation:
  if duty_permille < 0:
      raise ValueError("duty_permille must be non-negative")

title: adaptive_duty_permille accepts negative density (fail-open)
description:
File: python/src/lichen/timing/duty_cycle.py
Line: 45-69

Bug: The function accepts negative density values without validation. Negative density falls into the sparse case (density < 3), returning the maximum budget (20 or 50 permille).

Spec 2a.9 states: "A node MUST use the most conservative (lowest) applicable value when the operating class is unknown."

Current behavior contradicts this - negative density (which indicates an error or unknown state) fails OPEN to maximum budget rather than failing CLOSED to minimum budget (dense case).

Impact: If caller passes erroneous negative density, node allocates maximum airtime budget instead of minimum, potentially causing regulatory compliance issues in dense deployments.

Fix: Add validation to reject negative density or treat unknown/invalid density as dense (fail-closed):
  if density < 0:
      raise ValueError("density must be non-negative")
  # or fail-closed: treat negative as dense

title: node.py: non-ANNOUNCE routing messages delivered to application callback
description:
Lines 867-871 deliver any non-SCHC, non-fragment payload to the application callback, including ROUTING messages that are not ANNOUNCE type. If other routing protocol types exist (or are added), they would be incorrectly passed to the application layer instead of being handled by the node or dropped.

Location: python/src/lichen/node.py:867-871
Code:
  if kind != L2PayloadKind.SCHC and not is_fragment:
      if self._on_receive:
          self._on_receive(payload, rx.sender)
      return

The ANNOUNCE handling at lines 860-863 returns early, but other ROUTING subtypes fall through to this callback delivery.

Potential impact: Protocol-internal messages exposed to application; malformed routing messages not dropped.

title: node.py: assert for runtime None check bypassed by -O flag

The API contract (if persist_path is set, persistence_revision_anchor must also be set) is not enforced by explicit validation in __post_init__, only by this assert.

Fix: Replace with explicit ValueError check like:
  if self.persistence_revision_anchor is None:
      raise ValueError('persistence_revision_anchor required when persist_path is set')

title: dodag.py: select_parent() is public but requires external lock
description:
**File:** python/src/lichen/rpl/dodag.py line 702

**Severity:** P2 (thread safety contract)

**Summary:** select_parent() is a public method (no underscore prefix) that modifies critical state (preferred_parent, rank, role, _lowest_rank, gateway_centric, grounded) without acquiring self._lock. It is designed to be called only from locked contexts (_process_dio_unlocked, remove_parent), but nothing prevents external callers from invoking it directly without holding the lock.

**Failure scenario:** An external caller (e.g., a higher-level component or test) calls select_parent() without holding self._lock while another thread is in process_dio(). Concurrent modification of self.parents, self.rank, etc. causes data races. While Python GIL prevents memory corruption, it does not prevent inconsistent state (e.g., rank updated but preferred_parent still points to old parent).

**Recommendation:** Either rename to _select_parent() to signal it is internal, or have it acquire self._lock internally (requires changing callers to not double-lock, since _lock is an RLock this would be safe).
close_reason: Closed

**Failure scenario:** If the validation logic needs updating (e.g., different error message, different cardinality requirement), it must be updated in both places. Forgetting one leads to inconsistent error handling.

**Recommendation:** Remove the redundant check from dodag.py since transact_authenticated_schc_dio already validates this before calling prepare_candidate.

**Summary:** Lines 196-264 (_would_accept_dio_with_snapshot) and lines 464-524 (_would_accept_dio_unlocked) contain nearly identical logic (~70 lines). They evaluate the same acceptance criteria but one uses a snapshot object and one uses self.*.

title: P2: build_dio reads multiple fields without lock - potential thread safety issue
description:
In python/src/lichen/rpl/dodag.py, the build_dio method (lines 364-375) reads multiple mutable state fields (rpl_instance_id, version, rank, dodag_id, grounded, gateway_centric) without acquiring self._lock. If another thread modifies DODAG state between field reads (e.g., via _adopt_version or select_parent), the returned DIO may contain internally inconsistent values.

Example race:
1. Thread A reads self.version = 1
2. Thread B calls _adopt_version, sets self.version = 2, clears parents, sets self.rank = INFINITE_RANK
3. Thread A reads self.rank = INFINITE_RANK
4. Thread A returns DIO with version=1, rank=INFINITE_RANK (inconsistent)

While Python GIL ensures individual attribute reads are atomic, it does not ensure consistency across multiple reads.

Fix: Wrap the entire DIO construction in with self._lock.

File: python/src/lichen/rpl/dodag.py
Line: 364-375
Priority: P2
Category: thread-safety, correctness
close_reason: Closed

title: Misleading comment about METHOD_CORR in test_edhoc.py
description:
File: python/tests/crypto/test_edhoc.py
Line 392

The parametrized test vector comment says:
  _sequence(4, 0, b"x" * 32, b"\x00"),  # method_corr=4 -> method=1 (unsupported)

This comment is misleading. RFC 9528 deprecated METHOD_CORR (which existed in earlier drafts). In RFC 9528, the first value is simply METHOD, which must be 0-3. A value of 4 is just an invalid METHOD value, not a METHOD_CORR encoding.

The test WORKS correctly (the implementation rejects METHOD=4), but the comment confuses readers about the EDHOC protocol and may lead to incorrect assumptions about message encoding.

Fix: Change comment to:
  _sequence(4, 0, b"x" * 32, b"\x00"),  # method=4 (invalid, valid range 0-3)

title: Stale grounded status after parent switch in DODAG
description:
In dodag.py, ParentCandidate stores gateway_centric but not grounded. When select_parent() switches to a new preferred parent (due to hysteresis being overcome or old parent being pruned/removed), self.gateway_centric is updated from best.gateway_centric (line 730), but self.grounded retains the previous parent's value. The node continues advertising the wrong Grounded bit in DIOs until it receives a new DIO from the current parent.

Location: python/src/lichen/rpl/dodag.py:730

Fix: add grounded field to ParentCandidate, pass dio.grounded when creating candidates (line 450), and update self.grounded = best.grounded in select_parent() after line 730.

title: RST rate-limit tracking eviction uses insertion order not staleness
description:
In channel.py lines 331-337 (_check_rst_rate), when _rst_rate_tracking reaches MAX_RST_PEERS (4096), the code evicts the oldest entry by insertion order rather than by timestamp staleness.

Attack scenario:
1. Attacker sends forged RSTs from 4096 spoofed source addresses to fill tracking dict
2. Legitimate peer A is now the 'oldest' entry by insertion
3. Attacker sends more RSTs from new addresses, evicting A
4. Attacker can now send RSTs from A's address at full rate (20/10s) since A has no tracking entry
5. Repeat to bypass per-peer rate limit for targeted peers

The global rate limit (200 RSTs/window) mitigates but doesn't prevent targeted abuse.

Suggested fix: When evicting, prefer entries whose timestamps are all older than window_start (fully stale entries), or use LRU by last timestamp rather than insertion order.

Lines: 331-337
close_reason: Closed

title: CON cache forced eviction wastes OSCORE sequence numbers
description:
In channel.py lines 1179-1208 (_stage_con), when _protected_cons reaches MAX_PROTECTED_CONS (4096) and all entries have active correlation state, the code force-evicts the oldest entry anyway (lines 1200-1204).

This causes legitimate CON retransmissions to be re-protected with new OSCORE sequence numbers instead of reusing the cached protected message, wasting limited sender sequence space.

Failure scenario: Under sustained load with many concurrent CON exchanges:
1. _protected_cons fills to 4096 entries, all with active correlations
2. New CON message triggers eviction of an active entry
3. When that evicted CON retransmits, it cannot find cached protected bytes
4. Re-protection consumes a new sequence number
5. With enough retransmits under pressure, sequence space depletes faster than necessary

Impact: Premature sequence exhaustion requires context re-establishment via EDHOC.

Suggested fix: Increase MAX_PROTECTED_CONS or implement smarter eviction (e.g., prefer evicting entries closest to exchange timeout).

title: link_layer: ReceiveError.REPLAY returned for TOFU pin capacity exhaustion
description:
At line 1665-1666 in link_layer.py, when TOFU pin capacity is exhausted (all existing pins have active generation leases), the code returns ReceiveError.REPLAY. This is semantically incorrect - the frame is not being replayed; the counter is fresh. The actual failure is resource exhaustion.

Impact:
- Monitoring confusion: Security monitoring watching for replay attacks gets false positives
- Debugging difficulty: Operators troubleshooting capacity issues see misleading error codes
- Protocol confusion: Upper layers may respond to REPLAY differently than capacity errors

Security Note: Security behavior is correct (fail closed). This is a semantic/operational issue, not a vulnerability.

Suggested Fix: Either add ReceiveError.CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED variant, or document that REPLAY can mean 'cannot safely admit peer' in addition to 'counter replay'.

title: test_loadng_discovery_vector missing negative validation for cache mutations
description:

if exp.get("cache_added"):

    entry = cache.lookup(IPv6Address(ce["destination"]), now_ms)

title: Unbounded tombstone accumulation in ShortAddressCoordinator
description:
[codereview]

## Location
`python/src/lichen/link/address_assignment.py` lines 604-608, 371-380

## Summary
When peers release their addresses, tombstone entries (EUI64 -> last_sequence) are created to prevent DAO sequence replay attacks. These tombstones are never automatically cleaned up.

## Failure Scenario
1. Coordinator starts with lease-based address management
2. Many peers join and later release their addresses (via AssignmentOperation.RELEASE)
3. Each release creates a tombstone entry in `_last_sequence_by_eui` but NOT in `_expires_by_eui`
4. `prune_expired()` only removes entries that have expiries; tombstones have no expiry
5. Over time, tombstone count grows toward the limit of 65533 (SHORT_POOL_SIZE)
6. Memory usage grows: ~9 bytes per tombstone = ~600KB worst case

## Analysis
- Line 674-675, 678: On release, sequence is stored but no expiry is set
- Line 589-591: `prune_expired` iterates `_expires_by_eui`, which excludes tombstones
- Line 604-607: Sequences are only removed if the EUI64 is in the `expired` set
- Tombstones are only "cleaned" if the peer allocates again (lines 712-714)

The tombstone limit at line 372 prevents unbounded growth but does not provide cleanup:
```python
if len(tombstone_euis) > _SHORT_POOL_SIZE:
    raise AssignmentProtocolError("too many released-peer sequence tombstones")
```

## Suggested Fix
Add a tombstone TTL or a bounded LRU eviction for released-peer sequences. The security window for replay protection is typically short (minutes to hours), so old tombstones can be safely pruned.

title: test(coap): Missing PUT rejection test for battery<10 without low_battery
description:
## Summary

The test file `tests/coap/test_presence_resource.py` lacks coverage for the rejection path when PUT receives a payload with `battery < 10` but missing the required `low_battery=True` field.

## Details

Per spec 18.5.3, a presence document with `battery < 10` must include `low_battery: true`. The implementation correctly enforces this via `_validate_low_battery_consistency()` in `Presence.__post_init__`, returning BAD_REQUEST when violated.

However, no test exercises this path through the PUT endpoint:
- `test_put_battery_below_ten_sets_low_battery_without_tick` sends `low_battery=True` explicitly (valid payload)
- No test sends `{"status": "busy", "battery": 9}` (invalid - missing low_battery) to verify rejection

## Risk

A regression in the validation could silently accept invalid payloads, allowing malformed presence documents to propagate through the mesh.

## Suggested Fix

Add test case to TestPresencePut:

```python
async def test_put_rejects_battery_without_low_battery_flag(self) -> None:
    """Spec 18.5.3: battery < 10 requires low_battery=True."""
    client, server, _, _ = await _setup_writable()
    try:
        req = Message(
            code=PUT,
            uri="coap://srv/presence",
            payload=cbor2.dumps({"status": "busy", "battery": 9}),
        )
        req.opt.content_format = 60
        resp = await client.request(req).response
        assert resp.code == aiocoap.BAD_REQUEST
    finally:
        await client.shutdown()
        await server.shutdown()
```

## Location

File: tests/coap/test_presence_resource.py

title: ForwardingBuffer.clear() violates B.2.5 No Silent Drops
description:
**File:** src/lichen/link/forwarding_buffer.py:357-366

**Bug:** The clear() method removes all packets without calling the on_drop callback. This violates spec appendix-bufferbloat.md section 5 'No Silent Drops' which requires explicit signals when packets are dropped.

**Contrast with tx_queue.py:** The peer implementation TxQueue.clear() correctly calls signal_all_pending(False) before clearing, ensuring callers are notified (lines 476-486).

**Impact:** If clear() is called during operation (not just shutdown), upstream mesh sources will not receive NACKs and will not know to back off. Currently latent (ForwardingBuffer.clear() is not called in production code) but the API is public.

**Fix:** Before clearing, iterate through all packets and call self._on_drop(entry.source_iid, entry.data, DropReason.EVICTED) for each, similar to how expire_old() handles expired packets.

**Severity:** P2 - spec compliance gap, latent bug

title: Observe responses with 5.03 do not record peer backoff state

File: python/src/lichen/client/ip_coap.py

Summary: The AiocoapResourceSubscription._results() method yields CoapResult objects without checking for 5.03 Service Unavailable responses or recording backoff state in the parent transport. This violates the spec 07 section 10.2.3 requirement: Senders receiving 5.03 MUST back off for the indicated duration.

Failure Scenario:
1. Client has an active Observe relationship with peer P
2. Peer P becomes congested and sends a 5.03 notification with Max-Age: 60
3. _results() yields this as a normal CoapResult
4. Transport _peer_backoffs dict is NOT updated
5. Client immediately calls request() to peer P
6. Request goes through because no backoff is recorded
7. Result: client contributes to peer congestion, violating the spec MUST requirement

Location: Lines 353-364 in _results() async generator - no 5.03 check or backoff recording.
Contrast with request() at lines 196-216 which properly records backoff and raises ServiceUnavailableError.

Fix: AiocoapResourceSubscription needs a reference to the transport backoff state (or a callback) to record 5.03 responses.

title: presence: float conversion loses precision for timestamps > 2^53
description:
In apply_automatic_status (lines 302-307, 350) and age_s_at (lines 125-129), integer timestamps are converted to float via _finite_non_negative(). Python floats have 53 bits of mantissa, but the spec (line 89-90) claims to support 0..2^64-1.

Consequences:
1. now=_UINT64_MAX incorrectly rejected: int(float(_UINT64_MAX)) rounds up to 2^64, failing the check on line 307
2. Precision loss: ts=int(now_f) on line 350 loses low-order bits for values > 2^53

Practical impact is minimal (current Unix timestamps are ~2^31), but this is a spec conformance issue.

Fix: Validate integer bounds before float conversion, or keep integer arithmetic throughout for timestamp comparisons.
close_reason: Closed

title: PresenceCacheResource.record() missing input validation for addr/status

Missing validation could allow invalid data (None, empty string, wrong type) to be cached or cause inconsistent exceptions. Add validation at the start of record() to match the pattern in evict() and other methods in this file.

title: KeyError race in AiocoapResourceTransport backoff cleanup
description:
In ip_coap.py, both request() (line 178) and observe() (line 251) delete expired backoff entries using 'del self._peer_backoffs[peer]'. Under concurrent requests to the same peer after backoff expires, multiple coroutines can read the same expired entry via .get(), both determine remaining <= 0, and both attempt deletion. The second delete raises KeyError.

Fix: Replace 'del self._peer_backoffs[peer]' with 'self._peer_backoffs.pop(peer, None)' at both locations.

title: IPv4 local admin creates messages without mandatory 'from' field

title: Implement OSCORE_SSN_SAFETY_MARGIN or remove dead macro + false comment (post-reboot nonce-reuse hazard)

Consequence: NVM-fail after output built + reboot before successful persist reloads stale SSN -> sender collides with already-transmitted seq (nonce reuse, RFC 8613 7.2). PRE-EXISTING at HEAD. Preferred: implement real bump in oscore_ctx_persist_ssn (persist then advance RAM+NVM sender_seq by margin so post-reboot seq strictly greater than any pre-crash transmission); update comments + host harness test proving post-reload seq > pre-crash max. close_reason: Implemented the PREFERRED path: real OSCORE_SSN_SAFETY_MARGIN in oscore_ctx_persist_ssn (oscore_ctx.c). On every successful NVM write it now stores sender_seq + OSCORE_SSN_SAFETY_MARGIN and - only after success - advances the in-RAM sender_seq to the same durable value, monotonically and only after re-locking and re-validating slot identity (index/active/peer_eui64); on NVM failure after the 3 retries the in-RAM SSN is left exactly as before (protect-path reservation rollback still works). Deliberate deviation from the bead's literal 'cap at OSCORE_SSN_MAX', honoring the bead's own stronger invariant: the durable cap is the exhaustion sentinel OSCORE_SSN_MAX + 1 because a reloaded OSCORE_SSN_MAX could re-transmit the terminal five-byte PIV after a crash that used it (nonce reuse); a reloaded sentinel makes protect_request refuse with SEQ_EXHAUSTED (key rotation required), which is the RFC 8613 7.2/Appendix D.4-correct outcome. No-callback case stays a full no-op (no skip, RAM untouched) so all legacy NULL-callback behaviors are preserved byte-for-byte. Skipped range is never used as a nonce; skipping semantics documented at the macro, persist_ssn, protect_request, NVM-callback and NVM-failed-enum docs in oscore.h, at the protect.c persist call site, and in the protect_response SECURITY block. Persistence format audited: the write_cb/read_cb contract is a full uint64 with no range checks on reload (create_with_eui64 assigns raw, protect refuses >MAX), so margin/sentinel values round-trip without format change; verified by harness. Verified: (1) host harness (temp dir oscmargin-verify) compiling the REAL oscore TUs + vendored monocypher + tinycrypt AES-CCM with stub zephyr headers, ASan+UBSan clean, output: A PIV=100 RAM/store=1125; B reboot reload 1125 > 100, next PIV=1125; B2 exact skip jumps +1025, reload 3075 > max 2050; C NVM-fail leaves RAM 100, exact retry PIV=100 then 1125; D no-callback legacy +1; E terminal PIV MAX-2 caps store/RAM at sentinel 2^40, reloaded sentinel refused (-8 SEQ_EXHAUSTED); F store->reload identity. (2) clang -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra on all 7 oscore TUs at PT_MAX 256/2048 x MAX_CONTEXTS 8/32, clean. (3) ztest suite updated for the new contract (test_nvm_read_failure_fallback_to_zero, test_nvm_protect_request_nvm_failure, test_protect_request_rolls_back_before_publish now assert next-unused + margin in RAM and NVM) and two new tests added (test_persist_ssn_safety_margin_prevents_reboot_reuse, test_persist_ssn_margin_caps_at_exhaustion_sentinel) - these encode the NEW contract; they run via twister/native_sim in CI and could not be executed on this Mac (known unreliable native_sim per AGENTS.md); the host harness above runs the identical scenarios against the same TUs and passes.

Fail-closed not spoofable. Fix: parse v4 and strip port correctly.
close_reason: Fixed _peer_is_local_admin (messaging.py): RFC 3986 authority parsing strips [host]:port brackets properly and single :port suffix for other hosts; loopback classified via ipaddress for BOTH families so '127.0.0.1', '127.0.0.1:5683', '[::1]:5683', '[::1]:9999' are admin per contract. Spoof-safety retained: hostinfo is the transport-derived peer address, only genuine loopback literals grant admin. Cross-checked firmware coap_keys.c:49 lichen_coap_is_local_admin + Zephyr net_ipv6_is_addr_loopback (exact ::1/128): implemented explicit addr.ipv4_mapped deny-guard BEFORE .is_loopback because Python 3.11 ipaddress unwraps '::ffff:127.0.0.1' to True (verified empirically) — firmware semantics win, '::ffff:127.0.0.1' stays DENIED both sides, documented in docstring. Noted divergence: C server binds AF_INET6-only sockets so native IPv4 loopback exists only on the Python side; Zephyr link-local requires SLIP scope_id, Python has no transport identity so link-local stays untrusted (unchanged). Tests: TestLocalAdminAuthorityParsing 16-case matrix incl malformed/untrusted forms, plus e2e CREATED via '127.0.0.1' and '[::1]:9999'; tests/coap/test_messages_resource.py 144 passed.
