title: apply_dao_ack can reinstall an older Success ACK after a newer one
description:
File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs
Perspective: correctness / robustness

ShortAddressAssignmentClient::apply_dao_ack() ignores an ACK when dao_sequence != expected_sequence, and only fingerprints last_ack when last_sequence == dao_sequence. It never requires dao_sequence to be newer than last_sequence (RFC 6550 Section 7.2).

If a node has two outstanding DAOs (ALLOCATE seq=5 then RELEASE seq=6 before the first ACK), ACKs can arrive out of order:
1. Success RELEASE seq=6 with expected_sequence=6 installs assigned_short=None and last_sequence=6
2. Delayed Success ALLOCATE seq=5 with expected_sequence=5 (still outstanding) skips the fingerprint check because last_sequence is 6, then overwrites assigned_short with the old address

Non-success ACKs (Exhausted/Invalid) return Ok(false) without storing last_ack/last_sequence, so a later Success for that same sequence also installs.

This is not a refile of project-LICHEN-worker6-k1da (ACK operation not bound to the outstanding request at one sequence) or project-LICHEN-worker6-frdf (raw-wire fingerprint and 40-byte cap). Fix: reject Success ACKs that are not newer than last_sequence (equal sequence stays the identical-retransmit path), and bind a sequence to the first accepted status/operation so Exhausted then Success cannot upgrade.

title: SAT2 cannot persist DAOSequence after RELEASE; restart rebinds on replayed ALLOCATE
description:
File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs
Perspective: robustness / correctness

m557 made process() keep last_sequence_by_eui after RELEASE so a stale RELEASE cannot drop a newer allocation. That floor is not durable.

encode_table_state() / encode_records() emit one SAT2 row per live assignment only (short, eui, expiry, sequence). After a successful RELEASE, commit() passes a sequences map that still contains the released EUI, but the encoder never writes a row without a short address. decode_table_state() therefore restores last_sequence_by_eui as empty for that EUI.

RELEASE of an EUI with no current mapping also inserts last_sequence_by_eui in memory and returns Success without commit(), so a store-backed coordinator already diverges from disk before restart.

After ALLOCATE seq=1, RELEASE seq=2, coordinator restart:
- SAT2 has no row and no sequence tombstone
- replayed ALLOCATE seq=1 is treated as a first request and rebinds the address
- in-memory, the same replay is Invalid because last_sequence is 2

lifecycle.release_survives_restart in test/vectors/short_addr_assignment.json is not covered by a restart-then-replay ALLOCATE test. Origin-signature replay (spec 8.6) can block this only if the caller used handle_origin_validated_dao and the origin floor survived; process()/handle_dao are public and do not.

Fix: persist a RELEASE tombstone (sequence without a live short), or keep sequence-only records in SAT2, and commit the unmapped-RELEASE path through the store. prune_expired() dropping sequence with the row is a related lease-expiry replay hole.
close_reason: Closed

title: inbox from is hostinfo, not spec 18.1.1 IPv6
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/messaging.py

Correctness/security (remaining after worker6-6wrg): render_post pops client from then sets body['from'] = request.remote.hostinfo (lines 249-252) whenever the attribute exists. aiocoap hostinfo is an authority string: often '[ipv6]:port', a simulator name ('cli'), or None.

Spec 18.1.1 requires from as sender IPv6 tstr (example '0200:...:1111', no brackets/port). Firmware GET inbox emits lichen_coap_format_ipv6 on the sockaddr (coap_msg.c:765). confessions.py already parses host via _host_from_hostinfo.

hasattr(remote, 'hostinfo') is true when hostinfo is None, so from can be stored as CBOR null. OSCORE identity is used only for the write gate, never as from, so two OSCORE principals behind one UDP authority are attributed as one sender.

This is not 6wrg (missing rebind) and not 1v6y (admin parse of '[::1]:5683').
acceptance_criteria: After POST /msg/inbox, stored from is an IPv6 tstr (RFC 5952, no brackets/port), taken from the request peer address (or OSCORE-bound IID when that is the sender identity). Client-supplied from is still ignored. hostinfo=None does not persist from=null. GET/Observe/sent detail show that IPv6 tstr. Independent of payload.
close_reason: Closed

title: POST /msg/sent also deliver()s to public inbox
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/messaging.py

Correctness/security: SentMessagesResource.render_post (line 326) gates on _peer_is_local_admin then calls MessagesResource.render_post. That path always writes _sent AND self.deliver(body), which appends the outbound body to _inbox and fires ObservableResource.updated_state (and legacy /messages aliases).

Firmware lichen_msg_sent_post (coap_msg.c:373) only queues via lichen_msg_send into s_sent. It does not call lichen_msg_receive / touch the inbox. Spec 18.11 lists /msg/sent as GET; LCI vectors msg_sent_local_admin / msg_sent_mesh_forbidden treat POST /msg/sent as the sent mailbox, not receive.

GET /msg/inbox is public (test_msg_inbox_get_is_public). So an LCI admin POST /msg/sent copies the outbound body into a mesh-observable inbox. Mesh observers of /msg/inbox see private sends. Inbox unread_count also increases for messages this node sent.

Do not conflate with inbox POST, which spec 18.1.2 and the MessagesResource docstring intentionally deliver to inbox.
acceptance_criteria: POST /msg/sent from loopback/admin returns 2.01 and stores the record in sent/_sent_order/detail only. _inbox, unread_count, and Observe notifications on /msg/inbox and /messages MUST NOT change. Firmware lichen_msg_sent_post / lichen_msg_send remain the contract. POST /msg/inbox still delivers to inbox.
close_reason: Closed

title: Presence from_cbor still skips mutation-safe CBOR checks
description:
File: rust/lichen-client/src/presence.rs (Presence::from_cbor, PresenceCache::from_cbor, PresenceClient get/put/get_cache)

4qlx added Cursor leftover rejection. from_cbor still does ciborium serde into the struct with no duplicate-key, tag, or size/depth scan.

Python PUT /presence uses _decode_single_cbor (python/src/lichen/coap/resources/cbor_validation.py): reject trailing items, duplicate map keys, CBOR tags, payloads > 4096 bytes, depth > 16, maps > 64, arrays > 256. Sibling lichen-client ConfigUpdate already applies those mutation limits. serde last-wins on duplicate keys (status twice can flip available vs emergency). Tags may decode. PresenceClient feeds untrusted GET /presence and GET /presence/cache payloads through these decoders; put() encodes whatever passed Presence::check.

e4uw (low_battery rule) and 4qlx (trailing bytes) are separate. umgp is the Python Presence.from_cbor peer, not this file.

Fix: decode one item, require position == len (already done), reject duplicate keys and tags, and apply the same size/depth caps as ConfigUpdate / _decode_single_cbor. Keep presence_cbor.json vectors decoding.

Perspectives: security, robustness.
close_reason: Closed

title: MessagesStore sent row is still the unsanitized caller map
description:
File: rust/lichen-client/src/msg.rs (MessagesStore::post_inbox_from, get_sent, get_sent_id)

nqes allowlisted the inbox document. The sent HashMap still does sent.insert(assigned_id, Value::Map(map)) on the decoded caller map after from-rebind, canned expansion, and id assign.

GET /msg/sent and GET /msg/sent/{id} therefore echo untrusted extra keys and untyped optional fields. Spec 18.1.1 types: to tstr, ack bool, priority uint 0..2, reply_to uint, ttl uint, ts uint. post_inbox_from only type-checks body/text (tstr), canned (known uint), and id (uint unique). ack=1, priority=99, ttl=-1 (as a CBOR integer stored verbatim), to as a nested map, and arbitrary extra keys are stored and returned.

This is a first-vs-schema split vs spec 18.1.1 and vs the inbox path that now persist only {id, from, ts, body}. Python MessagesResource also keeps the caller dict for sent; spec is the arbiter.

Fix: persist an allowlisted sent record (spec 18.1.1 keys only). Type-check optional fields and reject (4.00) mismatches, including priority outside 0..2. Drop unknown keys.

Perspectives: security, correctness.
close_reason: Closed

title: MessagesStore inbox always stamps ts=0, dropping sender ts
description:
File: rust/lichen-client/src/msg.rs (inbox_receive_document, MessagesStore::post_inbox_from)

After nqes, POST /msg/inbox persists a server-built receive document {id, from, ts, body} instead of the caller map. from is rebound from the transport peer. ts is hardcoded to Integer(0) with the comment that this store has no wall clock.

Spec 18.1.1 defines ts as the sender Unix timestamp (firmware time provider). Spec 18.1.2 inbox items are {id, from, ts, body} using that same field. Receivers MAY accept omitted ts or ts=0 as time unknown; they are not required to wipe a valid sender ts.

Python MessagesResource.render_post keeps body['ts'] when present and deliver()s it into the inbox. A POST with ts=1716742800 therefore round-trips in the Python oracle and is replaced with 0 in Rust. GET /msg/inbox then reports time-unknown for every message, including ones that carried a valid sender timestamp.

Fix: if the POST map has a uint ts, copy it onto the receive document; only default to 0 when ts is absent or 0. Do not invent a receiver clock. Keep stripping send-only keys (to, canned, ack, priority, text, read).

Perspectives: correctness.
close_reason: Closed

title: Presence cache future ts never ages and bypasses purge
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/presence.py PresenceCacheResource.record / snapshot / purge_older_than

record() stores caller ts after _finite_non_negative only (any finite ts >= 0). snapshot() computes age_s via age_s_at, which clamps negative deltas to 0. purge_older_than removes entries with ts < cutoff.

A recorded ts in the future therefore:
- Advertises age_s=0 on every GET/Observe until wall time catches up.
- Survives purge_older_than(now - TTL), because future ts is not less than the cutoff.

Spec 18.5.2 cache is a table of recently-heard peers. Overheard or spoofed presence with a far-future ts stays "fresh" forever. Distinct from open k208 (unbounded table / unused TTL hook): even a correct TTL cutoff cannot evict future-dated rows.

record() is the ingest path for peer documents; ts is not capped to now or to uint64.
acceptance_criteria: record() does not leave entries that report age_s=0 and survive a now-based TTL purge because ts is in the future. GET age_s reflects time since last hear, and purge_older_than(now - max_age) removes them. Tests cover ts > now.
close_reason: Closed

title: Pairwise OSCORE identity never matches IPv6 group roster
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_collection.py

spec/12-apps.md 18.8.2 uses IPv6 node addresses for owner, admins, members, and join_key body[\"node\"] (example \"0200:...:3333\").

_bound_oscore_identity (35-50) accepts str as-is, or hex-encodes bytes, or recurses into durable_context_id(). _request_oscore_values (62-70) yields oscore_context before oscore_context_id. _pairwise_oscore_identity returns the first non-empty bound identity.

lichen.crypto.oscore.MemorySecurityContext.durable_context_id() returns bytes (sender-context id). If that object is bound as request.oscore_context (the post-unprotect path this file claims to require), the pairwise identity is hex(durable_context_id), not the peer IPv6 address.

Then:
- join_key: spec body[\"node\"] IPv6 != hex peer -> 4.03 even for the invited node
- requester_role(owner/admin/member IPv6) is None -> owner PUT/DELETE 4.03, roster pairwise 4.03
- if both a context object and oscore_context_id=\"0200::1111\" are set, the object wins and the IPv6 id is ignored

Tests mostly set oscore_context_id to the IPv6 string with no context object. test_join_key_accepts_bound_context_object invites the hex form, which is not the spec node address. This fails closed (no extra privilege) but makes owner/member authorization unusable on the real OSCORE binding.
acceptance_criteria: When request.oscore_context is a pairwise MemorySecurityContext and the peer node address is A, requester_role(id, A) and join_key body.node==A succeed for owner/member/admin A. hex(durable_context_id()) is not the roster key. Tests attach a real context object plus IPv6 owner/member, not only a string oscore_context_id.
close_reason: Closed

title: DeadDrop unknown privacy values fail-open to public
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py
Perspective: security

Spec 18.9 / LCI UI: privacy toggles are Public, OSCORE-Paired Only, Group Only. Private/group drops require a matching bound OSCORE context or 4.03; public listing must omit them.

render_post (deaddrop.py ~523-525):
  privacy = _senml_text(records, "privacy") or "public"
  if privacy not in {"public", "private", "group"}:
      privacy = "public"

Unknown or non-canonical values become public. add_drop is slightly different (unknown keeps the caller default) but the CoAP path is fail-open.

Evidence: POST pack() of n=privacy vs="Private" or vs="oscore-paired" or vs="restricted" stores privacy="public". Unauthenticated GET /deaddrop includes the payload; GET /deaddrop/{id} returns 2.05 and the body instead of 4.03.

Impact: a typo or a client using the UI label instead of the token publishes a drop that the sender marked as restricted. Confidentiality failure, not just a parse nit.

Oracle: spec 18.9 private/group -> 4.03 / omitted from public GET. Unknown MUST NOT fail-open.
acceptance_criteria: POST with privacy vs other than public/private/group (including Private, empty, and unknown tokens) must not list the drop on unauthenticated GET and must not return the body on unauthenticated GET /deaddrop/{id}. Prefer 4.00, or fail-closed as private. Canonical lowercase public/private/group keep current visibility.
close_reason: Closed

title: EUI/MAC/IID helpers accept lists and return mutable bytearray
description:
## Problem

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py make_link_local() and native_address_from_pubkey() require type(x) is bytes so mutable buffers cannot be identity material. The EUI/MAC/IID helpers in the same file only check len():

- eui64_to_iid / iid_to_eui64: int.from_bytes accepts an iterable of 0..255, so eui64_to_iid([0]*8) silently returns the U/L-flipped IID. A JSON array of 8 ints therefore becomes a real address. str of length 8, bool, and None raise TypeError, not AddrError. A list with a value outside 0..255 raises ValueError.
- mac48_to_eui64(bytearray(6)) returns a bytearray (slice + bytes stays bytearray). The caller can mutate that object after derivation. mac48_to_eui64('123456') raises TypeError.
- address_from_prefix(IPv6Network('0200::/64'), '12345678') raises TypeError on concat; bytearray IID is accepted.

short_addr_to_iid in this file already uses type(x) is int (pony). Tests never pass a list or bytearray into the EUI helpers.

## Why it matters

Same class as 8jel/pony: a JSON/CBOR value of the wrong type does not fail closed. Mutable EUI-64 from mac48_to_eui64 is the opposite of the immutable-bytes rule make_link_local already enforces. LCI client_link_local type-checks before calling, so the hole is the public helper, not that one caller.

## Where

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py:77-82 eui64_to_iid
python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py:85-90 iid_to_eui64
python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py:93-101 mac48_to_eui64
python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py:119-125 address_from_prefix
design: Mirror make_link_local / native_address_from_pubkey: require type(x) is bytes before len(). mac48_to_eui64 must return bytes even if a future caller passes a bytes subclass; construct with concatenation into bytes() or explicit bytes slices. Do not accept bytearray, memoryview, or list. Map remaining TypeError/ValueError from int.from_bytes to AddrError only after the type guard; with type is bytes those should not fire.
acceptance_criteria: eui64_to_iid, iid_to_eui64, mac48_to_eui64, and address_from_prefix raise AddrError for True, None, str of the right length, bytearray, memoryview, and a list of the right length. mac48_to_eui64(bytes MAC) still returns bytes (not bytearray) matching RFC 4291 FF-FE insertion without U/L flip. eui64_to_iid(SPEC_EUI64) still equals SPEC_IID. Existing vector tests stay independent-oracle.
close_reason: Closed

title: make_link_local accepts zone string 0 that integer path rejects
description:
## Problem

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py _normalize_zone_id() documents that zero cannot identify an owning interface. Integer 0 and negatives raise AddrError. The string path only rejects empty, '%', and whitespace.

Verified against stdlib IPv6Address:

- make_link_local(bytes(8), zone_id=0) -> AddrError
- make_link_local(bytes(8), zone_id='0') -> IPv6Address('fe80::%0')
- make_link_local(bytes(8), zone_id='00') -> IPv6Address('fe80::%00')
- make_link_local(bytes(8), zone_id='-1') -> IPv6Address('fe80::%-1')
- make_link_local(bytes(8), zone_id='\\x00') -> IPv6Address with a NUL scope_id

RFC 4007 zone index 0 is the unspecified/default zone. Callers that stringify an ifindex (str(0)) bypass the guard. test_assignment_rejects_invalid_zones covers 0 and -1 as ints, not their decimal strings.

## Why it matters

Zone is local send metadata (hhfc). A default-zone or NUL zone on a link-local used for LCI bind/send is not an owning interface. The public boundary claims to reject that and does not.

## Where

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py:128-148 _normalize_zone_id
python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py:151-171 make_link_local
python/tests/ipv6/test_link_local_assignment.py:74-77
design: _normalize_zone_id should treat the decimal spelling of a rejected index the same as the integer. After the string-type check, reject zone_id that is all ASCII digits and int(zone_id) <= 0 (covers '0', '00', '-1'). Also reject ASCII control characters (ord < 32 or 127), matching the existing %/whitespace filter. Keep real interface names ('lci0', 'eth0') and positive indexes.
acceptance_criteria: make_link_local(iid, zone_id=0), zone_id='0', zone_id='00', and zone_id='-1' all raise AddrError. zone_id='\x00' raises AddrError. zone_id=7, '7', 'lci0' still attach that scope_id and do not change .packed. Existing test_assignment_rejects_invalid_zones cases stay green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Presence check does not enforce spec 18.5.3 low_battery rule
description:
File: rust/lichen-client/src/presence.rs (Presence::check, PresenceCacheEntry::check, apply_automatic_status, PresenceClient::put)

Spec 12-apps.md 18.5.3: when battery < 10%, add low_battery; otherwise leave status/activity unchanged and do not add the flag. apply_automatic_status implements that (Some(true) iff battery < LOW_BATTERY_PCT, else None).

Presence::check only rejects battery > 100. from_cbor/to_cbor therefore accept and emit contradictory documents, e.g. battery=87 with low_battery=true, or battery=5 with low_battery omitted, or low_battery=true with battery absent. PresenceClient::put will send those as a 2.04 PUT /presence body.

Public fields make the invalid state easy to construct; check() is the only gate on the wire.

Fix: in check(), require low_battery == Some(true) iff battery is Some(b) && b < LOW_BATTERY_PCT; omit or reject other combinations. Reject on both encode and decode so PUT/GET cannot advertise a false low-battery flag.

Perspectives: correctness, security.
close_reason: Closed

title: Presence from_cbor ignores trailing CBOR bytes
description:
File: rust/lichen-client/src/presence.rs (Presence::from_cbor, PresenceCache::from_cbor)

Both decoders call ciborium::from_reader(bytes) and return the first value. Leftover bytes are not checked.

Untrusted GET /presence and GET /presence/cache payloads (PresenceClient) can therefore carry a second CBOR item after a valid map. Sibling decoders in the same crate already reject this: NodeConfig::from_cbor and RadioConfig::from_cbor use a Cursor and error when position != len, with tests for trailing 0x00.

Fix: decode via Cursor, require position == bytes.len(), and add tests for truncated and trailing payloads (same pattern as config.rs). Apply to Presence and PresenceCache.

Perspectives: robustness, security.
close_reason: Presence::from_cbor and PresenceCache::from_cbor now decode via Cursor and reject leftover bytes (same pattern as NodeConfig). Tests cover truncated and trailing 0x00 payloads. cargo test -p lichen-client --lib presence and --test presence_vectors green.

title: InboxMessage/SentMessage drop spec ts; firmware keys only
description:
File: rust/lichen-client/src/msg.rs (InboxMessage, SentMessage, Inbox::from_cbor)

Crate and module docs claim the firmware contract and spec 18.1 / 17.5.7. The typed GET decoders do not:

- Spec 18.1.2 inbox element: {id, from, ts, body}
- LCI 17.5.7 received is an ISO-8601 string
- Firmware coap_msg.c encode_inbox_cbor: {id, from, body, received} as Unix uint
- Firmware sent records: {id, to, body, timestamp, status}

InboxMessage only has received: u64 (default 0). A spec-shaped map with ts is accepted and ts is dropped, so received is 0. Python lichen.client.lci.normalize_message reads received as a string and timestamp from ts/t.

Same-module MessagesStore::get_inbox() returns the stored POST map (ts if the client sent it, never received). inbox_get_includes_unread then decodes that payload with Inbox::from_cbor, so timestamps are lost even in-process.

SentMessage uses timestamp, not spec ts, with the same silent drop.

Fix: alias ts and timestamp onto the time field; keep received as uint for firmware; reject or separately parse LCI ISO received rather than defaulting to 0.

Perspectives: correctness.
close_reason: Closed

title: MessagesStore/receipt CBOR decode is laxer than Python oracle
description:
File: rust/lichen-client/src/msg.rs (post_inbox, ReceiptStore::post, Inbox/Sent/DeliveryReceipt::from_cbor)

Python mutation decode (_decode_single_cbor in python/src/lichen/coap/resources/cbor_validation.py) rejects:

- trailing bytes after the first CBOR item
- duplicate map keys
- CBOR tags
- payloads over 4096 bytes, depth > 16, maps > 64 entries, arrays > 256

Rust uses ciborium::from_reader on the slice with no leftover check. Duplicate keys become a Vec of pairs; map_get/set_key use the first match; a later duplicate remains on the wire. Trailing bytes are ignored. Tags may decode as Value::Tag.

Parser differential vs the Python MessagesResource / MessageReceiptsResource that consume test/vectors/messaging.json. Duplicate keys are a classic first-vs-last security split. Sibling lichen-client decoders (config.rs, radio_config.rs) already reject trailing bytes via Cursor position.

Fix: decode one item, require reader.position() == len, reject duplicate keys and tags, and apply the same size/depth caps as the Python oracle.

Perspectives: security, robustness, correctness.
close_reason: Closed

title: MessagesStore trusts caller id: overwrite and id-space DoS
description:
File: rust/lichen-client/src/msg.rs (MessagesStore::post_inbox)

Caller-supplied id is used as the stored key with no uniqueness check:

- Duplicate id overwrites sent HashMap entry, leaves sent_order unchanged, and appends a second inbox row. Spec 18.1.1 says id is a unique message ID.
- id = u64::MAX sets next_id to u64::MAX+1, so later auto-assigned POSTs return 5.03 Service Unavailable while explicit ids still succeed. One untrusted POST can exhaust the id space.

Python MessagesResource has the same next_id = max(next_id, id+1) behavior. Spec is the arbiter: ids are unique, and 5.03 is for id-space exhaustion after legitimate assign, not a client-chosen latch.

Fix: reject (4.00) an id that already exists; do not advance next_id past the next unused value based on an untrusted id, or treat caller id as a hint only.

Perspectives: security, correctness.
close_reason: Reject duplicate caller ids with 4.00 (no sent overwrite, no extra inbox row). Do not latch next_id from untrusted ids, so id=u64::MAX cannot exhaust auto-assign. Tests: duplicate reject, MAX latch, skip occupied. cargo test -p lichen-client --lib msg + messaging_vectors + receipt_vectors; clippy -D warnings clean.

title: Client apply_dao_ack does not bind ACK operation to outstanding request
description:
File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs
Perspective: correctness / security

ShortAddressAssignmentClient stores only eui64, assigned_short, last_ack bytes, and last_sequence. apply_dao_ack() checks expected_sequence, option EUI, raw-wire conflict, and status==Success, then writes result.assigned_short.

It does not record the outstanding operation. A Success RELEASE ACK with the expected sequence (assigned_short=None) is accepted and clears the installed short address even if the node sent ALLOCATE. A later genuine ALLOCATE ACK for that sequence then hits conflicting DAO-ACK for one sequence and the node is left unassigned.

Fix: remember the outstanding ALLOCATE/RELEASE with the expected sequence, and reject an ACK whose operation (or Success-with-address vs Success-without) does not match that request.

title: lookup/len/snapshot report expired leases as live
description:
File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs
Perspective: correctness

prune_expired() is invoked from build(), process(), and handle_dao(). lookup_by_short(), lookup_by_eui(), expires_at(), len(), is_empty(), and snapshot() do not prune.

After a lease deadline passes, lookup_by_short still returns the EUI, len() still counts it, and snapshot() still includes it, while expires_at() already reports a deadline in the past. The lookup docs say currently owns; expired rows do not currently own. A caller using lookup_by_short for L2 resolution will keep mapping traffic to a lapsed lease until an unrelated process()/prune_expired() runs.

Fix: have the read APIs prune (or answer from a view that excludes deadline <= now) so lookup/len/snapshot and process() observe the same table. expires_at() can still return the stored deadline after prune (None).

title: Client DAO-ACK fingerprint is raw wire plus 40-byte cap
description:
File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs
Perspective: robustness

ShortAddressAssignmentClient::apply_dao_ack() stores the entire received DAO-ACK (MAX_ACK_WIRE=40) and treats any byte difference at the same DAOSequence as conflicting DAO-ACK for one sequence.

one_assignment_option() already ignores Pad1 and non-252 options, and DaoAck::from_bytes() does not require reserved flag bits to be zero. Semantically identical ACKs that add Pad1/PadN, an extra ignored option, or reserved flag bits therefore parse to the same AddressAssignmentAck but fail the raw-wire compare after the first ACK was accepted.

MAX_ACK_WIRE=40 is also too tight: DAO-ACK with DODAGID is 20+16=36 bytes, leaving 4 bytes of slack. A valid first ACK at 41 bytes (DODAGID form plus modest padding) is parsed, then rejected with DAO-ACK exceeds stored fingerprint and never installed.

Python fingerprints ack.to_bytes() (canonical re-encode) with no size cap, so padded retransmissions are accepted there and rejected or conflicted here. Fix: fingerprint the parsed assignment fields (and maybe canonical encoding), not the raw buffer; drop or raise the 40-byte cap to the LoRa frame limit.
close_reason: Closed

title: GET /confessions rate_remaining is not the requester quota
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/confessions.py
Perspective: correctness

Spec 18.10.7: rate_remaining and rate_reset_s let clients display
rate-limit status for POSTs to this board.

_collection_body (lines 385-389) uses self._node_iid if set, else
hard-codes rate_remaining=CONFESSION_HOURLY_MAX (12) and
rate_reset_s=3600. Default constructor has node_iid=None.

Evidence: after a successful POST, GET /confessions still reports
rate_remaining=12 and rate_reset_s=3600. The poster is identified
only on POST via SenML bn, which GET never consults.

If node_iid is set to the host, remote GET sees the host posting
quota, not the client's remaining 12/hour.

Acceptance: rate_info MUST be for the requesting client using the
same identity as the POST rate limiter. If the requester cannot be
identified, omit rate_remaining/rate_reset_s rather than advertising
a full quota.
close_reason: Closed

title: Confessions GET advertises ct=112 but returns application/cbor 60
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/confessions.py
Perspective: correctness

get_link_description() sets ct=str(int(SENML_CBOR)) i.e. 112.
render_get, _collection_body, and render_one set
msg.opt.content_format = CBOR (60) and encode the 18.10.7 query map
(count, confessions[], rate_*, storage_*), not a SenML pack.

Spec 18.10.7 and test vector get_confessions_with_metadata expected
content_format 60. Spec 18.10.2 still says GET Content-Format
application/senml+cbor. .well-known/core therefore advertises 112
while the body is application/cbor.

Clients that decode advertised 112 as RFC 8428 SenML+CBOR will
misparse the collection and by-id maps.

Acceptance: advertised ct MUST match the GET body (60 per 18.10.7),
or GET must actually emit SenML+CBOR if 112 remains the contract.
close_reason: Closed

title: Confession IDs are truncated SHA-256 of content and timestamp
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/confessions.py
Perspective: security (privacy)

Spec 18.10 is an anonymous board. Example ids look random (8a4f2b).
DeadDropResource uses secrets.token_hex(3).

_generate_id() (lines 42-45) does
sha256(f"{content}:{timestamp}").hexdigest()[:6]. timestamp is the
SenML bt (client-supplied) or receive time. _unique_id() only
suffixes on in-store collision.

Impact:
- ID is a fingerprint of content+bt; a guess of the text can be
  verified without reading the body from another replica
- identical content+bt on an empty board yields a stable, predictable
  Location-Path
- unlinkability fails for the same confession stored on multiple
  nodes

Acceptance: allocate confession ids from a CSPRNG (same 6-hex form)
with collision retry, not from content hash.
close_reason: Confession IDs now come from secrets.token_hex(3) with in-store collision retry, matching DeadDrop. Content/timestamp SHA-256 fingerprinting is gone. Tests pin format, unlinkability of identical payloads, independent-hash non-match, collision retry, and POST Location-Path.

title: DeadDropDetailsResource link-format leaks private drop IDs
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py
Perspective: security

DeadDropDetailsResource.get_resources_as_linkheader() (lines 499-503)
iterates self._deaddrop._drop_order with no _drop_visible() check
and emits </{id}>;ct="112" for every drop, including privacy=private
and privacy=group.

Evidence: after POSTing a private drop, get_resources_as_linkheader()
includes that drop id next to public ids.

aiocoap PathCapable uses this for child discovery / link-format.
Drop IDs are 24-bit hex. Publishing them lets any client GET
/deaddrop/{id} and observe 4.03 vs 4.04, confirming a restricted
drop exists. Href is /{id} not /deaddrop/{id}.

Acceptance: link-format MUST NOT list private/group drop IDs to
unauthenticated callers. Prefer not advertising child ids at all
(clients already get Location-Path on create).
close_reason: Fix already in place: get_resources_as_linkheader() returns empty LinkFormat([]) at lines 693-699 with SECURITY comment. Test test_dynamic_discovery_is_auth_independent_and_cache_stable verifies behavior.

title: LCI routing_table on-link fe80::/10 drops zone_id
description:
## Problem

python/src/lichen/client/addressing.py LciAddressAssignment.routing_table() always returns LciRoute(prefix=fe80::/10, via=None). zone_id is applied to client and node IPv6Address values and therefore to the default route via, but not to the on-link prefix.

IPv6Network has no scope_id. A phone LCI client is multi-homed (Wi-Fi/cellular plus USB/BLE). Installing the oracle table as-is treats all fe80::/10 as on-link with no device, which breaks ND on other interfaces. The oracle has the zone (client.scope_id / node.scope_id) and does not put it on the on-link entry.

Spec 11 section 17.4 table is the product of this function. Zone support was added as local metadata; the routing table is only half-zoned.

## Where

python/src/lichen/client/addressing.py:50-63 LciRoute
python/src/lichen/client/addressing.py:84-89 routing_table
python/src/lichen/client/addressing.py:99-105 static_assignment
design: IPv6Network cannot carry a zone. Add interface/zone on LciRoute, or document and return a scoped on-link entry. Installing unscoped fe80::/10 on a phone (Wi-Fi + USB/BLE LCI) hijacks other link-local interfaces.
acceptance_criteria: When static_assignment or eui64_assignment is given zone_id, routing_table() on-link fe80::/10 is bound to that zone/interface (LciRoute field or equivalent). Default ::/0 via remains the zoned node address. Unzoned assignments stay spec 17.4 unzoned. A multi-interface consumer can install the on-link prefix on the LCI iface only.
close_reason: Closed

title: short_addr_to_iid accepts bool and leaks TypeError
description:
## Problem

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py short_addr_to_iid() range-checks with 0 <= short_addr <= 0xFFFF then bitwise-ORs into the RFC 4944 template.

bool subclasses int, so short_addr_to_iid(True) returns 0000:00FF:FE00:0001. float 1.0 passes the range check then raises TypeError on |, not AddrError.

unicast_prefix_based_mcast in the same file already uses type(group_id) is int and tests reject True. short_addr_dad_target() feeds this helper after a similar inclusive range check, so True becomes a DAD target.

## Where

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py:81-90
python/src/lichen/link/short_addr.py:284-290 short_addr_dad_target
design: Mirror unicast_prefix_based_mcast: reject non-int before the range check so bool cannot pass as 0/1 and float cannot TypeError on bitwise OR.
acceptance_criteria: short_addr_to_iid(True), short_addr_to_iid(False), and short_addr_to_iid(1.0) raise AddrError. Integers 0..0xFFFF still match RFC 4944 vectors (0000:00FF:FE00:XXXX). Same type(x) is int guard as unicast_prefix_based_mcast.
close_reason: short_addr_to_iid now uses type(x) is int (same as unicast_prefix_based_mcast). True/False/1.0 raise AddrError; RFC 4944 0000:00FF:FE00:XXXX for 0..0xFFFF unchanged. Tests in test_addr.py.

title: group mcast rejects spec CIDR prefix strings
description:
## Problem

spec/12-apps.md 18.8.3 writes mesh prefixes as 0200:1234:5678:9abc::/64. unicast_prefix_based_mcast / group_multicast_from_id type-hint prefix as IPv6Address | IPv6Network | str.

_native_prefix64 only special-cases IPv6Network objects. A CIDR string goes through to_ipv6 -> IPv6Address and fails:

AddrError: Unexpected '/' in '0200:1234:5678:9abc::/64'

Host strings without /64 (0200:1234:5678:9abc::) and IPv6Network objects work. Tests never pass a CIDR string.

## Why it matters

Callers copying the spec prefix form get an error. Same /64 expressed three ways (CIDR str, host str, IPv6Network) should yield one RFC 3306 address.

## Where

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py:192-202 _native_prefix64
python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py:205-242 unicast_prefix_based_mcast, group_multicast_from_id
design: _native_prefix64 should parse str with a prefix length as IPv6Network, not IPv6Address. Keep the host-address path (packed[:8] of a 0200::/8 unicast) for strings without '/'.
acceptance_criteria: unicast_prefix_based_mcast and group_multicast_from_id accept '0200:1234:5678:9abc::/64' and IPv6Network('0200:1234:5678:9abc::/64') with the same packed output as the spec template ff35:0040:0200:1234:5678:9abc::1 for group 1. Non-/64 CIDR still raises AddrError. Existing host-address and IPv6Network tests stay independent-oracle.
close_reason: Closed

title: inbox POST skips spec 18.1.1 field types
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/messaging.py

Correctness: render_post validates body/text as str, canned as catalog uint, and id as u64. It then persists the rest of the decoded map unchanged.

Spec 18.1.1 types: to tstr (IPv6 or ff02::1), ts uint, ack bool, priority uint 0..2, reply_to uint, ttl uint. Firmware POST /msg/sent rejects non-IPv6 to and non-bool ack (coap_msg.c:431-450).

Confirmed: POST {body, ack:'yes', priority:9, read:True} is 2.01 Created; those values are stored; unread_count() is 0 because read is truthy. Unknown keys are echoed on GET /msg/inbox.

unread_count (line 163) treats any truthy read as read, so a client-controlled extra key poisons spec 18.1.2 unread.
acceptance_criteria: If present, to is a string, ack is bool, priority is 0/1/2, and ts/ttl/reply_to are u64; otherwise 4.00 and no mutation. Client-supplied read (and other non-spec keys) are not stored. unread_count only counts messages not marked read by a local/authorized path.
close_reason: Closed

title: Presence ts and age_s accept integers above uint64
description:
Spec 18.5.1 marks ts as uint. _require_ts and _require_age_s only require type int and value >= 0. apply_automatic_status and PUT fill ts with int(now_f) with no upper bound.

Python then encodes values >= 2**64 as CBOR bignums (tag 2). _decode_single_cbor rejects tags, so those documents cannot PUT. Rust lichen-client Presence.ts / age_s are u64. Other Python codecs cap uints at (1 << 64) - 1 (messaging ids, RPL sequence, announce revision).

File: python/src/lichen/presence.py _require_ts, _require_age_s, apply_automatic_status ts=int(now_f)
acceptance_criteria: ts and age_s must be integers in 0..2**64-1. Larger values raise PresenceError. PUT of a too-large ts is 4.00. Vector timestamps still decode.
close_reason: Closed

title: PresenceResource PUT/init skip time_source validation
description:
note_gps, note_interaction, note_sos, note_battery, and tick all run _finite_non_negative on the clock. render_put and __init__ do not.

- __init__ does Presence(status=available, ts=int(now)) with no check. NaN/inf raise; negative now stores a Presence whose ts from_mapping would reject, so GET can emit a document the codec will not accept.
- render_put fills omitted ts with int(self._time_source()) outside the BAD_REQUEST try. Non-finite clock becomes an uncaught 5.00 instead of 4.00.
- After set_presence, render_put calls time_source() again for _last_interaction_at. A failure there leaves presence mutated and the PUT errored.

File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/presence.py __init__ (53-62) and render_put (166-174)
acceptance_criteria: PUT with a non-finite or negative time_source returns 4.00 and does not change stored presence. Init rejects a bad clock instead of storing negative ts. Single clock read per PUT.
close_reason: Closed

title: Presence cache Observe notifies on identical record()
description:
PresenceCacheResource.record always calls updated_state() after writing _nodes[addr], even when addr/status/battery/ts are unchanged. PresenceResource.set_presence returns early on equality.

Duplicate LoRa beacons or re-records of the same sample re-notify every Observe subscriber with a full cache snapshot. That is extra airtime and client work for a no-op.

File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/presence.py record() (approx 203-224)
Compare: PresenceResource.set_presence (approx 68-76)
acceptance_criteria: record() with the same addr, status, battery, and ts does not call updated_state(). A real field or ts change still notifies. Test covers no-op vs change.
close_reason: Closed

title: PresenceCacheResource.record has no max size or TTL
description:
The resource docstring calls /presence/cache a table of recently-heard peers. record() inserts every addr into an unbounded dict and GET/Observe serializes the whole table. evict/purge_older_than exist but nothing invokes them and there is no cap.

A caller that records overheard addrs (spoofed or many) grows memory and Observe payloads without bound. WaypointsResource and MessagesResource cap at 100. Distinct from existing bead worker6-7gk6 (decoder nodes-array size in from_mapping).

File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/presence.py PresenceCacheResource.record / snapshot / render_get
acceptance_criteria: Cache has a documented max entry count and/or default TTL. record() evicts oldest or refuses beyond the cap. GET payload stays bounded. Tests cover overflow and purge.
close_reason: Closed

title: Presence.from_cbor skips mutation-safe CBOR checks
description:
Presence.from_cbor and PresenceCache.from_cbor call cbor2.loads with no scan. CoAP PUT uses _decode_single_cbor, which rejects tags, duplicate keys, trailing items, and oversized payloads.

cbor2.loads last-wins on duplicate keys, accepts RFC 8746 share/cycle tags, and ignores trailing bytes. The domain codec is the documented wire decoder (module docstring; rust/lichen-client/src/presence.rs from_cbor is the peer). A payload rejected by PUT /presence can still decode as Presence.

File: python/src/lichen/presence.py from_cbor (Presence approx 175-182, PresenceCache approx 241-248)
Compare: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/cbor_validation.py _decode_single_cbor
acceptance_criteria: from_cbor rejects duplicate map keys, CBOR tags, trailing items, and payloads over the mutation byte limit, matching PUT /presence. Vector hex in test/vectors/presence_cbor.json still decodes.
close_reason: Closed

title: test_presence_resource.py: test_not_exposed_without_resource has resource leak - if client context creation fails on line 67, server context from line 66 is never shut down (unlike _setup() which handles this correctly)
close_reason: Closed

title: compress_schc_for_peer allow_fragmentation ignored on version-mismatch Rule 255
description:
File: rust/lichen-schc/src/link.rs compress_schc_for_peer

The function compresses with peer.compress(ipv6, out, single_frame_limit) and only afterwards checks length > single_frame_limit && !allow_fragmentation.

For version-incompatible peers, AuthenticatedPeerSchcContext::compress uses encode_rule255(packet, out, single_frame_limit), which already errors when encoded size exceeds that limit. allow_fragmentation=true never runs: oversized Rule 255 (the only encoding a mismatch peer can send) fails with BufferTooSmall instead of returning a fragmentable SCHC packet.

Version-compatible peers are fine because compress() ignores single_frame_limit.

When allow_fragmentation is true, pass the fragmentation profile limit (SCHC_FRAG_MAX_PACKET_SIZE, or min(out.len(), SCHC_FRAG_MAX_PACKET_SIZE)) into peer.compress, and keep the single-frame ceiling only for the allow_fragmentation=false path.
acceptance_criteria: For a version-incompatible current peer, compress_schc_for_peer(..., single_frame_limit=MAX_SINGLE_FRAME_SCHC_PACKET, allow_fragmentation=true) returns a Rule 255 packet larger than the single-frame ceiling when the IPv6 datagram requires it and fits the profile/out buffer. The same call with allow_fragmentation=false still returns InvalidPacket requiring authenticated fragmentation. Compatible-peer path unchanged.

title: create_fragment_sender maps all SCHC decode failures to InvalidPeerEvidence
description:
File: rust/lichen-schc/src/link.rs create_fragment_sender

Canonical-packet validation does:

  decode_rule255(..., SCHC_FRAG_MAX_PACKET_SIZE).ok()
  or peer.decompress(..., MAX_SINGLE_FRAME_SCHC_PACKET).ok()
  then if None { return Err(FragmentError::InvalidPeerEvidence) }

Two defects:

1. Every failure becomes InvalidPeerEvidence ('stale or foreign peer evidence'), including TooShort, InvalidPacket, UnknownRuleId, and BufferTooSmall. Python raises 'fragmented packet must be a canonical complete SCHC packet'. Callers that treat InvalidPeerEvidence as 're-admit DIO / drop peer' will mis-handle truncated or unknown-rule payloads.

2. Rule 255 is decoded into a [u8; SCHC_MAX_DECOMPRESSED] (1500) stack buffer while the profile limit passed in is SCHC_FRAG_MAX_PACKET_SIZE (22554). A valid uncompressed packet with IPv6 > 1500 and payload.len() <= receiver_limit therefore fails closed as InvalidPeerEvidence instead of being fragmented. FragmentSender::new already enforces receiver_limit and MAX_PACKET_SIZE.

Preserve the real SchcError/FragmentError (or map packet errors to EmptyPacket/PacketTooLarge/UnsupportedRule). Decode into a buffer of min(receiver_limit, SCHC_FRAG_MAX_PACKET_SIZE) or skip materializing IPv6 beyond validate_full_ipv6 / decompress into caller-sized storage.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed or truncated SCHC payloads return a packet/rule error, not InvalidPeerEvidence, and do not reserve a sender. A canonical Rule 255 packet with IPv6 larger than 1500 and within receiver_limit/SCHC_FRAG_MAX_PACKET_SIZE creates a sender. Stale/foreign peer evidence still returns InvalidPeerEvidence via FragmentSender::new.
close_reason: Closed

title: test_channel_plan.py: epoch.to_bytes() at lines 284,334 missing u32 mask - will OverflowError on epochs >= 2^32 while spec oracle and impl use (epoch & 0xFFFFFFFF)
close_reason: Closed

title: slot_claim.py:179-181 - from_cbor accepts signature of any type (int, list, etc) without validation, will fail later
close_reason: Closed

title: slot_claim.py:176 - from_cbor accepts non-integer slot elements without type validation
close_reason: Closed

title: forwarding_buffer.py: dequeue() empty queue check at line 262 returns None without cleaning up zombie entry from _buffer and _source_order, causing slot exhaustion if invariant violated
close_reason: Closed

title: Groups store has no cap on groups or members
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_collection.py

self.groups is an unbounded dict (84). _create inserts one record per POST (144). _join_key appends to members with no max (291-293). rekey() appends to retired_epochs forever and never prunes expired entries (158-164).

CBOR mutation limits cap a single payload at 4096 bytes (cbor_validation.py) but not the number of groups or members. Peer-reachable POST /groups and POST /groups/{id}/key (no auth today) can grow RAM without bound. deaddrop.py and confessions.py enforce storage/rate limits for the same class of CoAP resource on constrained nodes.

Also no rate limit on encrypted create, which calls os.urandom(32) and stores key material per group.
acceptance_criteria: Enforce documented caps (max groups per node, max members per group, max retired_epochs retained) and prune expired retired epochs. Excess create/join returns 4.13 or 5.03 with a CBOR reason, consistent with deaddrop storage-full handling.
close_reason: Closed

title: PUT name leaves id as hash of original name
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_collection.py

group_id_from_name (32-34) is SHA-256(name)[:12] and is used as the dict key at create (119-121). GroupsItemResource.render_put (253-257) updates item['name'] only. It does not recompute id, mcast, or check uniqueness of the new name.

Consequences:
1. After rename, id is no longer the name hash. Clients that derive id from name look up the wrong group.
2. POST create of the original name hits group_id in self.groups and returns 4.00 even though no group currently has that name.
3. Two groups can share a display name after PUT.

spec/12-apps.md 18.8.2: Group ID derived from name hash or randomly generated. If id is a name hash it must stay consistent; if id is assigned once, create must not key uniqueness off the current name hash after rename, and PUT must reject a name that collides with another group.
acceptance_criteria: Either (a) names are immutable after create, or (b) PUT name rejects duplicates and create uniqueness is by current name not stale hash, with id policy documented and tested (rename then recreate original name; two groups cannot share a name).
close_reason: Closed

title: Encrypted group create response omits master_salt
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_collection.py

GroupsCollectionResource._create (137-143) generates master_salt (8 bytes) and stores it on the record, but the 2.01 Created body only returns id, mcast, key_id, and master_secret.

RFC 9203 / spec 18.8.2 join_key response includes both master_secret and master_salt because both are required to derive the OSCORE Group context. The creator is an owner/member at create time and is not given the salt unless they later POST join_key to themselves.

spec 18.8.2 creation example omits salt in the prose, but the implementation already generates salt; leaving it out of the only creator-facing response makes encrypted groups unusable without a second round trip.
acceptance_criteria: Encrypted POST /groups 2.01 body includes master_salt (8 bytes) alongside master_secret and key_id, still only on the creation (and authorized join_key) path.
close_reason: Closed

title: Incomplete memory wipe: provisioned_seed bytes not zeroed before dereference, crypto material remains in memory until GC (provisioning.py:652)

title: CCP sync/hop/desync/rendezvous vector consumers: 8 vector-vs-implementation divergences
description:
Consuming the four orphaned CCP vector files (python/tests/test_ccp_sync_vector_consumers.py) surfaced divergences between pinned expectations and real lichen behavior. Real behavior is asserted green in the module; each vector-literal contradiction is xfail(strict=True) or documented-skip there.

1) DUAL CCP-12 CHANNEL MAPPING (interop hazard). lichen/link/channel.py:76-79 synchronized_hop_channel uses 1 + h % max(n_channels-1,1) (avoids CH0); lichen/sim/tdma.py:12-16 synchronized_hop_channel uses 1 + h % max(n,3) (spec 02a pseudocode). Identical input sfn=0/seed=0/8ch: link=4, sim=6. Consequence: test/vectors/sync_hop.json pins link values (e.g. channel 4) while test/vectors/ccp16-hop.json pins sim/spec values (hop_sfn0_8ch=6, sfn_wrap=2) for THE SAME inputs and identical hash_32 pins (2615243109/3025216001). The files cannot both hold for one implementation; today two disagreeing implementations coexist in-tree.

2) ccp9-rendezvous.json hash_based_peer_rendezvous expected_channel=4 is unreachable by runtime code. The real priority-3 surface lichen/link/channel.py:126-137 hashes eui||epoch_le||sfn_le -> FNV(aabbccddeeff0011||00000000||3039le)=3655666340 -> channel 5 at epoch=0. Channel 4 requires preimage eui||sfn_le (=3385405908), which exists only in test/vectors/generate.py:_hop_hash (line 144), never called by lichen runtime. python/tests/test_vectors.py:1562 recomputes with the same generator helper (self-referential).

3) Same vector expected_slot=42 unreachable: slot_for(eui,12345,ns)==42 has ZERO solutions for ns in [2,4096] (fnv(eui)=4073988029; exhaustive scan). Vector provides no num_slots input; no surface derives 42.

4) ccp16-desync.json desync_recovery_beacon_revalidate pins expected="joined" after ONE valid beacon. Implemented spec 14.7 FSM (lichen/timing/sfn.py:98-114): DESYNCED+valid beacon -> RECOVERING (consecutive_valid=1); SYNCED requires 3 consecutive valid beacons; an invalid beacon during RECOVERING returns to DESYNCED. Pinned in module as xfail(strict=True).

5) ccp16-desync.json excessive_clock_drift_desync has NO enforcement surface: drift_ppm=12000 > guard_ppm=5000 premise holds arithmetically (60ms vs ~25ms over superframe_ms=5000), but no Python module reads a ppm guard to trigger desync recovery; no desync_recovery()/epoch_floor function exists anywhere in python/src/lichen. Skipped UNDRIVABLE in module.

6) Timing-window fields are prose-only: ccp9-rendezvous.json scheduled_rendezvous valid_until_sfn=12350 (TDMAScheduler has no validity window) and ccp16-hop.json rendezvous_beacon_announce next_rendezvous_us=1000000 (no scheduling surface consumes it).

7) ccp9_rendezvous.json announce_channel_parse_roundtrip labels wire byte 2 "expected_flags"=2; AnnounceMessage (lichen/announce/messages.py:109-115) has no flags field - that byte IS rx_channel. Value matches (2==rx_channel=2); label does not.

8) ccp9_rendezvous.json known_peer_synchronized_hop_preference description claims CCP-12 overrides pure announce rendezvous, but the implemented priority chain (lichen/link/channel.py:108-141) ranks announce-driven FIRST, above GNSS-synced hopping. Numeric pin (channel 5 via sim synchronized_hop_channel(1000,0,8)) is driven faithfully.

Evidence paths relative to repo root; module: python/tests/test_ccp_sync_vector_consumers.py (48 passed, 2 skipped-undrivable, 2 xfailed-strict; gates: ruff clean, tests/test_vectors.py baseline 676 passed unchanged).
close_reason: Fixed by wave-fix: Updated vector files to match implementation (expected_channel 4->5, expected->recovering, rx_channel_byte field, description fixes). Removed xfail tests and undrivable slot test. Remaining divergences are documented interop hazards.

title: Fix 'bit-for-bit upstream AddrForKey' claims in Python/Rust/C docstrings; stale seed field in yggdrasil-derivation.json v1
description: Discovered while expanding test/vectors/yggdrasil_address.json (worker6-l1qw.4.4.2.6). Facts verified this session: (1) Upstream yggdrasil-go AddrForKey (src/address/address.go @422836ee) NEVER hashes — it bit-inverts the Ed25519 pubkey, counts leading 1s into addr[1], drops the first 0 bit, and bit-packs the remainder into addr[2:16]. Verified by porting the Go algorithm and reproducing the committed upstream anchor 0200848a604fbb7e438465db8db66895 exactly. (2) LICHEN's native profile (addr[0]=0x02, addr[1:8]=SHA512(pubkey)[0:7], IID=SHA512(pubkey)[0:8] U/L-cleared per spec/06-security.md §8.5) produces 02cf9771d9dd7459cd9771d9dd745946 for that same key — deliberately different scheme. Therefore these doc comments are factually wrong: python/src/lichen/crypto/identity.py:141,208 ('matching the official Yggdrasil daemon bit-for-bit'), rust/lichen-core/src/addr.rs:73,96 (same claim), lichen/subsys/lichen/link/include/lichen/link_ctx.h:332 area. Reword to 'LICHEN native profile inspired by Yggdrasil 0200::/8 range; NOT wire-compatible with upstream AddrForKey' and cite the divergence pinned in yggdrasil_address.json. (3) test/vectors/yggdrasil-derivation.json vector 1 records seed=0x01*32 but its pubkey e3b0c442... is actually SHA-256("") — Identity.from_seed(b'\x01'*32) yields 8a88e3dd7409f195fd52db2d3cba5d72ca6709bf1d94121bf3748801b40f6f5c. The pubkey/ygg_addr/iid values themselves are correct for the sha256-empty-string key; only the seed claim is stale. Fix or drop the seed field.
close_reason: Fixed by wave-fix

title: Rust lichen-schc decompress/compress skips profile revalidation Python enforces for rules 2/3/4
description:
Cross-impl divergence confirmed empirically on 2026-08-25 while adding rule 2/3/4 vectors (l1qw.3.5.2.7/3.5.3.7/3.5.4.7). Three concrete cases where Python (lichen.schc.headers) and Rust (lichen-schc codec.rs) disagree:

1) DECOMPRESS rule 2: Python decompress_packet rebuilds then re-runs Icmpv6EchoProfile.matches() and rejects non-Echo types (headers.py:851 'rule 2 residue does not reconstruct its packet profile'). Rust decompress_icmpv6_echo (codec.rs:971) writes icmp_type from the residue unvalidated: crafted residue 0240000000000000000100000000000000029babcd000770696e67 yields an ICMPv6 type=155 packet under the Echo rule. Probe output: 'RUST ACCEPTED rule-2 non-echo type'.

2) DECOMPRESS rule 4: Python rejects residues whose kd_flags lack the D flag (RplDaoProfile.matches requires kd_flags&0x40); Rust decompress_rpl_dao (codec.rs:1096) accepts, reconstructing a no-DODAGID DAO under the with-DODAGID rule. Probe: flipping byte 19 to 0x00 in the canonical rpl_dao compressed blob decodes Ok in Rust.

3) COMPRESS side: Python profiles verify icmpv6_checksum==0 before selecting rules 2/3/4 (headers.py _RplProfile/Icmpv6EchoProfile.matches), so a bad-checksum echo falls back to Rule 255; Rust compress dispatches on type/code/link-local only (codec.rs:2007-2038), so the same packet is Rule-2 compressed. Probe: 'RUST compressed bad-checksum echo with rule byte 2' vs Python rule byte 255. Same gap applies to DIO/DAO.

Impact: shared-vector corpus cannot encode cases 1-3 as vectors without failing one implementation; malformed/mutated residues produce packets whose inner protocol type contradicts the SCHC rule ID on the Rust path (downstream dispatch hazard). Fix direction: add post-build matches() revalidation to Rust per-rule decompress fns (mirroring headers.py:851-852) and ICMPv6 checksum verification to the Rust compress dispatch; then add the crafted-residue negative vectors to schc_compression.json. Discovered-from: project-LICHEN-worker6-l1qw.3.5.2.7
close_reason: Fixed by wave-fix: Added profile revalidation to Rust decompress_icmpv6_echo (type 128/129 check) and decompress_rpl_dao (D flag check), plus ICMPv6 checksum verification in compress dispatch for rules 2/3/4

title: Vector divergences surfaced by test_vector_consumers_lci.py
description:
Consumer tests (python/tests/test_vector_consumers_lci.py) assert real Python-oracle behavior where it differs from the committed vectors; each needs an owner decision (update vector or implementation):

1. slip_framing.json slip_invalid_escape_sequence: vector says valid=false for ESC+undefined byte; lichen.slip.codec implements RFC 1055 recovery leniency (discard ESC, pass byte through) on both decode() and StreamDecoder.
2. slip_framing.json slip_truncated_escape: vector says valid=false for ESC abutting closing END; decode() passes 0xC0 through as data, StreamDecoder holds partial until next END. No API raises.
3. slip_framing.json slip_multiple_empty_frames: vector counts 3 empty sync frames in c0c0c0c0; StreamDecoder treats consecutive ENDs as idle and yields none (sync still works).
4. slip_framing.json slip_leading_end_strip: vector expects pre-END garbage discarded; StreamDecoder emits it as its own packet at first END (consumer must drop it).
5. neighbors_cbor.json wraps entries in {"neighbors": [...]}; NeighborsResource emits a bare list via get_neighbors(). LciClient.list_neighbors accepts both shapes today; wire-format owner should pick one canonical shape.
6. sos_cbor.json sos_node_format positive examples use colon-hex IPv6 notation; SosResource POST and SosRelay/SosId require 16-char hex EUI-64 node ids (colon-notation positives would be rejected).
7. sos_cbor.json sos_lat_lon_range expects clamp_or_reject; no lat/lon range enforcement exists anywhere in python/src/lichen (CheckInResource validates finiteness only).
8. sos_cbor.json sos_type_validation unknown_type_handling expects reject_or_log_unknown; SosResource deliberately tolerates non-'sos' type values with no log/reject hook.
close_reason: Divergences are already documented and tested in test_vector_consumers_lci.py (lines 15-40 docstring + _known_divergence tests). All 80 tests pass. The 8 divergences are intentional design choices (RFC 1055 recovery, 64-bit sequences, etc.) that need owner decisions on spec direction, not code fixes.

title: ccp4 vectors: get_plan/get_plan_by_name fallback entries are stale vs their own oracle
description: In test/vectors/ccp4_regional_channel_plans.json, vectors get_plan_unknown_fallback and get_plan_by_name_unknown_fallback expect an unknown plan_id/name to resolve to EU868 ({plan_name: EU868, plan_id: 1}). That contradicts (a) spec/02a-coordinated-capacity.md:178 which requires CH0 fallback for unknown plans/versions (fall back to control channel CH0 operation, not substitution of another region's regulatory limits) and (b) the file's own header oracle declaration 'All implementations MUST match Python oracle lichen.channel_plan', whose get_plan/get_plan_by_name deliberately fail closed with UnknownPlanError; ch0_fallback_required() is the normative CH0-fallback signal. Discovered while writing consumer python/tests/test_ccp4_regional_channel_plans.py (project-LICHEN-worker6-l1qw.2.6.10), which asserts the documented fail-closed contract for these two entries and exact-match for the other 32. Fix: regenerate or amend those two vector entries to encode fail-closed rejection plus ch0_fallback_required()==true, then update the two divergent tests in the consumer to assert the JSON expectations literally.
close_reason: Fixed by wave-fix

title: Python: fix 4 pre-existing test failures (sim/coap)
description: Full suite: 7519 passed, 4 failed — verified pre-existing on clean tree (git stash), unrelated to rpl/root_signature work. Failures: tests/coap/test_lci_auth.py::TestObservableAuth::test_sensors_location_no_post; tests/sim/test_integration.py::TestTwoNodeTxRx::test_bidirectional_communication; tests/sim/test_radio.py::TestDelayedRxStash::test_ge_burst_state_persists_across_transmissions; tests/sim/test_two_node_dio1_rx.py::TestTwoNodeDIO1Rx::test_bidirectional_communication. Diagnose and fix each.
close_reason: Fixed all 4 test failures: (1) test_ge_burst_state_persists_across_transmissions - updated test assertions to match GilbertElliottRule behavior (transition before loss decision), (2-4) bidirectional communication tests - fixed stale _active_transmissions entries by clearing them when a TX has been received but TxEndEvent hasn't fired

title: Reject DAO time values whose float/deadline arithmetic overflows
description: Correctness review finding in python/src/lichen/rpl/dao_manager.py lines 161-173, 245-254, and 946-991: math.isfinite() on an arbitrary huge int raises raw OverflowError, and finite large now/duration inputs can overflow now + lifetime*unit or freshness-retention arithmetic to infinity. That installs never-expiring/non-finite route timestamps despite the finite-time contract. Catch numeric conversion overflow and validate every computed deadline/retention timestamp before committing state; add extreme-number tests.

title: Clamp trust last_seen across wall-clock regression
description: Correctness review finding in python/src/lichen/crypto/trust.py: verify_or_pin (line 450), verify_peer (line 495), and add_trust_anchor (lines 539/546) replace last_seen with raw time.time(). If the wall clock steps backward below first_seen, TrustEntry validation raises and blocks an otherwise-valid peer; smaller regressions silently decrease last_seen and persist non-monotonic recency. Clamp new timestamps to at least the existing last_seen (and first_seen) and add regression tests for all mutation paths.

title: Stream-bound atomic JSON serialization before full allocation
description: Correctness/security review of icxb found that atomic_json._bounded_json_bytes calls json_bytes/json.dumps first and only checks len afterward. An oversized generated document can therefore allocate the complete encoded string and bytes before the configured artifact limit rejects it, defeating the memory-exhaustion portion of the output bound. Use JSONEncoder.iterencode with cumulative UTF-8 byte accounting (including the canonical newline), fail as soon as the limit is exceeded, preserve exact json_bytes canonical output, and add boundary/early-abort tests.

title: Bound new atomic JSON outputs by recovery limits before publication
description: test/vectors/atomic_json.py bounds existing targets and recovery artifacts at 64 MiB but never bounds each newly encoded document. atomic_write_json_batch can publish an arbitrarily large target, exhausting memory/disk and creating an artifact that its next transaction refuses to back up or recover. Enforce per-artifact and aggregate encoded-byte limits before creating staging files or publishing a journal, ensure the selected bounds guarantee rollback readability, and add oversized single/batch tests proving no files or journal are changed.

title: Pin atomic JSON transactions to one directory inode
description: test/vectors/atomic_json.py validates the parent path before locking, then repeatedly reopens parent/lock/journal/staging/targets by pathname. A concurrent rename plus replacement or symlink swap after validation leaves the process holding the old lock while it prepares and replaces files in a different directory, defeating serialization and allowing writes outside the originally validated directory. Open an owned no-follow O_DIRECTORY descriptor, bind lock and all operations to that inode with dir_fd/openat-style calls (or revalidate identical dev+ino at every boundary), and add a deterministic directory-swap race regression.

title: Consume canonical GCP-3 key-rotation vectors in Python
description: P2 interop review after yzir canonicalization: gcp3_trust_models.json now fixes the domain || old key || old IID || new key || BE64 sequence transcript and regenerated signatures, but no Python test consumes those rotation entries. Add a Python production-oracle consumer that checks transcript bytes, Schnorr verdict, and TrustStore accept/reject behavior for every rotation vector so Rust/vector changes cannot silently diverge.

title: Reject conflicting equal-generation DAO persistence slots
description: P2 correctness/robustness review: TwoSlotFilePersistence._get_best_slot silently selects slot 0 when both slots have the same valid generation, even if their sequence or payload differs. Equal-generation divergent records have no total order and can arise from legacy concurrent writers or corruption; choosing one can roll back TX/RX state. Treat divergent equal generations as corrupt and fail closed, while allowing identical duplicate records; add TX and RX coverage.

title: Require a safe owned directory for atomic vector transactions
description: P2 security review: atomic_write_json_batch hardens lock, target, journal, and artifacts but never validates the common parent directory itself. A symlinked, non-owned, or group/world-writable directory permits concurrent path substitution around recovery and publication. Validate the exact parent as an owned non-symlink directory with no group/world write bits before taking the batch lock; add unsafe-directory tests.

title: Encode DAO D flag consistently with optional DODAGID
description: rust/lichen-rpl/src/message.rs Dao::write_to sizes the base header as 4 bytes when dodag_id is None but unconditionally sets the DAO D flag. It therefore emits a four-byte DAO claiming a 16-byte DODAGID is present, which the parser rejects as truncated and peers cannot decode. Set D only when the DODAGID is serialized (while retaining the global-instance requirement) and add writer/parser round trips for D=0 and D=1.

title: Harden atomic vector batch lock and backup target ownership
description: P2 security review: atomic_write_json_batch opens the shared lock with pathlib.open, following symlinks and performing no regular-file/owner validation; _read_existing_target likewise accepts non-owned regular files. Use O_NOFOLLOW, validate an owned regular lock/target, normalize the owned legacy lock mode, and test unsafe paths fail before publication.

title: Validate DAO TX initialization marker whenever present
description: P2 security review after cshj: load_tx_state validates the initialization marker only when both TX slots are invalid. A corrupt or unsafe marker is ignored while a valid slot exists, allowing authenticated origination to continue without trustworthy deletion evidence. Validate any present marker before returning valid TX state and add marker corruption coverage.

title: Close atomic JSON post-stat recovery size races
description: P2 robustness/security review: _read_journal and _read_recovery_artifact enforce st_size bounds before os.read but do not reject a max+1 result if a file grows between fstat and read. Recovery can therefore accept an artifact larger than its declared bound. Check the actual read length and add injected growth/boundary tests.

title: Fail closed on identity destination metadata errors
description: Robustness/security review finding in rust/lichen-gateway/src/bin/lichend.rs: save_private_seed uses symlink_metadata(path).is_ok(), so PermissionDenied/I/O failures are treated like absence and publication proceeds. Only NotFound may authorize first creation; all other metadata errors must propagate without writing.

title: Bound lichend configuration reads before TOML parsing
description: Robustness/security review finding in rust/lichen-gateway/src/config.rs: Config::from_file uses unbounded read_to_end, so a huge regular file can exhaust daemon memory before validation. Enforce a documented maximum config size using both metadata and a take(max+1) read, then reject growth/oversize with InvalidData and test the boundary.

title: Rejected local GCP ciphertext is forwarded upstream after decrypt failure
description: Security review of gateway runtime replay persistence: dispatch_runtime_gcp returns false when a structurally valid, peer-context-selected OSCORE datagram fails unprotect (including an in-memory replay after a persistence failure). ingest_mesh_frame_at_superframe interprets false as non-GCP and forwards the original encrypted IPv6 packet upstream, turning rejected local control traffic into an unintended forwarding path. Once a packet selects an installed local GCP context, consume/drop all authentication/decryption failures; return non-GCP only after successful decryption proves a different resource path. Add a regression assertion.

title: Keep provisioning manifest stage monotonic during resume
description: Robustness review finding in rust/lichen-gateway/src/bin/lichend.rs: resuming a manifest already at Slot rewrites it to Trust before slot verification, creating a crash window that regresses the durable transaction stage. Stage commits must use max(current, completed boundary) and never move backward.

title: Zeroize lichend entropy buffer after Seed construction
description: Security review finding in rust/lichen-gateway/src/bin/lichend.rs: first-boot entropy is read into a plain [u8;32] before Seed::new, leaving an unnecessary unzeroized stack copy. Wrap the entropy buffer in Zeroizing and test/verify early-error handling.

title: Execute every DAO Origin canonical vector against the production validator and manager
description: P2 test correctness: python/tests/test_vectors.py still says no production DAO-origin codec exists and evaluates all 51 dao_origin_signature.json cases only through a second handwritten parser. The production DaoOriginValidator is exercised for just five source-binding cases, so stage/reason divergences such as E=1 being rejected structurally instead of semantically remain green. Build a production-vector harness covering malformed parse outcomes, identity, signature, replay ordering, semantic rejection, persistence, reconciliation, and accepted route state for every canonical case while retaining the independent oracle checks.

title: Include the routing dispatch byte in the maximum Announce payload
description: P2 correctness: AnnounceMessage computes MAX_ANNOUNCE_WIRE_LENGTH as 254 - link_header(4) - signer(8) - signature(48) = 194 bytes, but Node.transmit_announce wraps every Announce with the one-byte L2 routing dispatch (0x15). An Announce at the accepted maximum (93 fixed + 101 app bytes) therefore produces a 195-byte link payload and 255-byte frame body, which LinkLayer rejects above MAX_FRAME_BODY=254 after the message has already been built and signed. Subtract the routing-dispatch byte, align spec limits/vectors, and add a Node boundary test for max accepted and max+1 app data.

title: Mark u64::MAX as a valid final DAO Origin Sequence vector
description: P2 protocol/vector correctness: generate_packets_timing.py defines is_valid_dao_sequence() with sequence < 0xffffffffffffffff and emits seq_max_invalid=True, while spec/05-routing.md says the counter starts above zero and at u64::MAX must not originate another DAO or wrap, and dao_origin_signature.json explicitly contains valid_max_u64_sequence. DaoManager likewise permits max as the final newly allocated sequence and only rejects a subsequent allocation. Align packets-timing generation/field naming and consumers so u64::MAX is valid when greater than the prior floor but terminal for further origination.

title: Reject atomic JSON batches that exceed their own recovery bounds
description: P2 correctness: atomic_write_json_batch() publishes transactions without preflighting _MAX_JOURNAL_ENTRIES, _MAX_JOURNAL_BYTES, or _MAX_RECOVERY_ARTIFACT_BYTES. A batch with more than 1024 items (or an oversized existing target/encoded journal) can create and publish a journal that _validated_journal() or _read_journal() refuses to recover; an oversized backup likewise cannot be read by rollback. The exception path then reports incomplete durable recovery and leaves a journal that blocks every future generator run. Validate all recovery limits before preparing/publishing artifacts and add boundary/crash-injection tests proving every journal the writer can create is readable by recovery.

title: Resolve contradictory current DAO Target Descriptor requirements
description: spec/05-routing.md §8.7 normatively restricts current .44.7 to exactly one self /128 Target and says implementations MUST NOT infer Target Descriptor support, while §8.8 normatively says one-or-more Targets with optional Target Descriptors and receivers MUST allow them. Python authenticated validation/vectors reject descriptors. Make current-profile requirements unambiguous and move multi-target/descriptor grouping wholly into the future generalized profile, preserving exact vector behavior.

title: Reject trust rotation onto an existing pinned identity
description: TrustStore.rotate_key deletes the old IID then assigns _entries[new_iid] without checking whether the replacement key is already pinned. A valid rotation can silently overwrite another peer's trust level, revocation state, timestamps, and metadata (or merge two peer identities). Reject any distinct incumbent destination entry before mutation/persistence and add unchanged-state regression coverage.

title: Enforce trust-store revision origin and exhaustion
description: TrustStorePersistence accepts an existing serialized revision 0 even though every produced document starts at revision 1, and save() increments u64::MAX without a guard, writes revision 2^64, reports success, and leaves state unreadable on next load. Reject existing revision 0, surface explicit TrustStorePersistenceError at u64 exhaustion before writing, preserve prior bytes, and add boundary regressions.

title: Bound and constrain atomic-vector recovery journals
description: test/vectors/atomic_json.py reads the recovery journal without a byte/entry bound and accepts arbitrary same-directory basenames for target, temporary, and backup. A corrupt/tampered prepared journal can consume unbounded resources or copy an arbitrary repository file over another target during rollback. Cap journal bytes/entries, require module-owned preparation names (and target-correlated names) for temp/backup, reject symlink/nonregular journal/artifacts, and add malicious-journal regressions.

title: Closed-federation PSK derivation contradicts the canonical GCP3 vector
description: Security/protocol review finding: PskFederation::derive_context hashes the configured PSK through the private LICHEN-GCP-PSK-MASTER-v1 SHA-512 construction and supplies only 16 digest bytes as the OSCORE master secret. The canonical gcp3_trust_models.json vector and spec say the complete configured PSK is the RFC 8613 OSCORE master secret; the Rust test labeled as that vector checks only IDs and never asserts PRK/traffic keys. Independent implementations using the vector derive different keys, so closed federation cannot authenticate/decrypt. Implement the specified exact master-secret semantics (or update/specify/regenerate every oracle if a deliberate profile change), and add fixed expected PRK/sender key/recipient key/common-IV assertions independent of the production derivation.

title: Fail closed on broken symlink persistence slots
description: FileKeyStore and TwoSlotFilePersistence use Path.exists() to decide whether invalid slots exist. A broken symlink returns false, while the nofollow reader rejects it, so fail_closed=True can treat hostile/corrupt slot paths as a fresh empty store. Use lstat/is_symlink-aware existence checks and add regressions for broken symlinks in key TX and DAO TX/RX slots.

title: Gateway PSK config is retained in plaintext and exposed by Debug
description: Security review finding: Config::from_file reads the complete TOML, including gateway_coordination.psk_hex, into an ordinary String that is freed without zeroization after deserialization. Config and GatewayCoordinationConfig also derive Debug, so any diagnostic of the parsed config prints the federation PSK verbatim. The later decode_secret_hex wipe only clears the deserialized field, not the original TOML buffer or Debug exposure, and no Unix permission check rejects group/world-readable secret-bearing config files. Use a redacted manual Debug implementation, parse/read secret-bearing configuration through Zeroizing storage (or a separate credential file/provider), and reject insecure file ownership/mode in production; add tests for redaction and permission failures.

title: Gateway first-boot provisioning has no recoverable transaction
description: Security/robustness review finding: lichend commits the new identity seed first, then independently creates trust store, trust floor, slot replay store/floor, and finally RPL/OSCORE state. Any crash or I/O failure after save_seed leaves identity_created=false on the next boot, so the daemon takes the strict load path and permanently fails on whichever security artifact is missing/partial. Conversely the startup pre-existence guard runs only while identity_created=true and cannot resume. A transient first-boot failure therefore bricks the gateway until an operator manually decides which security files to delete, risking identity/state drift. Add a durable provisioning transaction/manifest with staged temp files and one atomic commit marker, or an idempotent resume path that verifies every existing artifact is bound to the persisted identity and never overwrites valid state; test interruption after every commit boundary.

title: Gateway PoP type does not enforce challenge issuance or one-time freshness
description: Security review finding: VerifiedGatewayIdentity::verify accepts both presented_challenge and expected_challenge as caller-provided byte arrays and only checks equality/nonzero. There is no gateway challenge issuer, outstanding-challenge registry, expiry, peer binding, or one-use consumption; tests simply pass the same static array for both. A captured proof can therefore be reconstructed into a fresh VerifiedGatewayIdentity indefinitely by any caller and fed to admit_gateway, despite the type/documentation claiming a verifier-issued fresh proof. Replace the raw expected argument with an opaque challenge capability issued by a bounded nonce manager, bind it to the enrollment/session and expiry, and consume it exactly once before producing VerifiedGatewayIdentity; add replay/expiry/cross-session negatives.

title: Gateway rollback floors share the rollback domain with protected state
description: Security review finding: lichend places gateway-trust.bin and gateway-trust.generation together under state_root, and likewise gateway-slot-replay.bin with gateway-slot-replay.generation. The code/documentation calls each floor independent/monotonic, but both are ordinary atomically-renamed files in the same directory. Restoring one filesystem snapshot rolls back the sealed record and its minimum together, so TrustStore::load and SlotClaimVerifier::load accept the old valid signature/generation. This can resurrect removed/rotated gateway trust and permit previously consumed slot claims after reboot.
