Store floors in a genuinely non-rollbackable authority (TPM/NV counter, platform monotonic storage, or an append-only externally anchored log), or explicitly fail deployment when unavailable; test rollback of both paired files, not only one side.

title: Handoff OSCORE master secrets survive in unzeroized CBOR buffers
description: Security review finding: OscoreState derives ZeroizeOnDrop, but OscoreState::to_cbor_entries clones master_secret/master_salt into ciborium::Value::Bytes, and HandoffResponse::encode serializes those secrets into a plain Vec<u8>. GatewayCoordinator wraps that plain Vec in CoapResponse and Gateway::dispatch_runtime_gcp retains it through OSCORE protection; neither the intermediate Value allocations nor the encoded plaintext payload are zeroized on drop. Successful and failed handoff response paths therefore leave node OSCORE key material in reusable heap memory despite the advertised secret lifecycle. Encode into Zeroizing buffers/secret-aware response ownership, avoid unnecessary clones, and ensure all intermediate plaintext CBOR allocations are wiped after protection or on every error; test drop/error paths with an instrumented allocator or explicit owned buffer hooks.

title: Gateway identity-proof transcript duplicates its domain separator
description: Security review finding: rust/lichen-gateway/src/trust.rs build_identity_proof_transcript() reserves capacity for DOMAIN||IID||challenge but appends IDENTITY_PROOF_DOMAIN twice. Internal tests pass only because signer and verifier share the same defective helper; independent GCP implementations following the documented canonical transcript will sign DOMAIN||IID||challenge and fail authentication against Rust. Correct the transcript to append the domain exactly once and add a fixed literal/vector oracle that does not call the production builder for expected bytes/signature.

title: Reject Announce rx_channel values outside CCP-9 range
description: P2 exact-input/security consistency: python/src/lichen/announce/messages.py accepts rx_channel 0..15 in construction and parsing, while spec/05-routing.md 9.2, AnnounceSchedulerConfig, and the canonical CCP-9 profile require 0..7. A signed or relayed channel 8..15 can enter Node peer rendezvous state and select a channel the supported radio plan does not advertise. Restrict the wire/model boundary to 0..7, add construction/parser/vector regressions, and keep spec/vector oracle exact.

title: Gateway persistent constructor exceeds clippy API arity limit
description: Gateway::new_persistent takes eight positional arguments (identity, epoch, trust, coordinator, storage, provision flag, state root, sealing seed), failing clippy -D warnings and making security-sensitive path/seed/creation-mode arguments easy to transpose. Group the persistence settings into a typed configuration value and update production/tests.

title: Revoke outstanding sender-control authorities at SCHC terminal transition
description: Security review of the manager-issued raw SCHC egress fix found that _finish_unlocked drops outstanding data-fragment authorities but not previously issued sender ACK-REQ/control authorities. A timeout/repair ACK request issued just before a complete ACK, abort, cancel, policy invalidation, or expiry can therefore remain target-bound but signable for up to 60 seconds after its sender session is terminal. Bind sender-originated control authorities to the exact FragmentSender, revoke them on every terminal transition, preserve only a newly issued terminal Sender-Abort, and add a stale-control-after-success regression.

title: SCHC adaptation vector fixture fields are parsed but never asserted
description: rust/lichen-schc/tests/adaptation_vectors.rs includes five raw-fragment transition-oracle fields in AdaptationVector for every feature set, but reads them only when raw-fragment-codec+test-utils compiles the production-path duplicate transition. Clippy -D warnings fails reduced feature gates. Compile those fields under the same feature condition; in the full feature gate they remain consumed and asserted by the duplicate transition test.

title: Classify issued SCHC ACK authorities from immutable bytes
description: During correctness review of project-LICHEN-worker6-8j2e, LinkLayer._send_locked checks Ack.from_bytes(payload) while payload is the private _IssuedFragmentWire bytes subclass. Ack.from_bytes intentionally requires exact built-in bytes, so ordinary manager-issued ACK responses (for example C=1 0x7840) are misclassified as data and can bypass the mandatory Priority.ACK gate. Snapshot the issued authority to exact bytes for structural classification before consumption/signing, retain one-use/target binding, and add a non-compressed ACK wrong-priority regression.

title: Runtime GCP OSCORE responses omit Content-Format
description: rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs dispatch_runtime_gcp converts CoapResponse into SecureResponseData with options=&[], discarding response.content_format. Decrypted clients receive CBOR/SenML-CBOR/error payloads without the CoAP Content-Format option. Encode canonical Class E option 12 into the OSCORE plaintext and assert it after decrypting the runtime response.

title: Domain-separate and version the Announce origin signature transcript
description: P2 security/interoperability: AnnounceMessage.signed_data() signs raw IID||pubkey||seq||rx_channel||app_data with no protocol/domain/version prefix, unlike Link and DAO Schnorr-48 transcripts. Reusing the node identity key across protocol roles leaves Announce signatures without cryptographic context binding and makes future transcript evolution ambiguous. Define a fixed LICHEN-ANNOUNCE-vN domain (with unambiguous delimiter/length framing), update the normative spec and all implementations/vectors together, and add cross-domain negative KATs proving Link/DAO/SOS material is rejected as Announce authority.

title: Secure request API exceeds clippy argument limit
description: rust/lichen-node/src/secure.rs send_secure_request and its internal helper take eight arguments, failing the required cargo clippy -D warnings gate. Encapsulate request method/path/payload metadata in a request descriptor or otherwise reduce API arity without weakening checked payload sizing or persistence semantics.

title: Stop deriving packets-timing expected vectors from production timing code
description: P2 test-oracle integrity: packets_timing_vectors() imports production airtime, Trickle, DAO, CSMA, SFN, time-sync, DIO/IPv6/ICMP/SCHC/frame and other helpers, executes them, and publishes their return values as canonical expected JSON. Tests and --check can therefore self-confirm regressions by regenerating the oracle from the same implementation under test. Convert normative outputs to literal/spec-formula reference calculations isolated from lichen.*, add fixed external KATs for security wire material, and have separate tests compare production to those immutable values.

title: Make authenticated DIO vector wire bytes independent of production codecs
description: P2 test-oracle integrity: generate_authenticated_schc_dio.py builds canonical wire_hex/dio_hex/ipv6_hex/link_payload_hex with production LichenFrame, IPv6Header, Icmpv6Message, and encode_rule255. The expected verdicts and Schnorr signature are independent, but the exact protocol bytes are not: a shared production encoding bug can regenerate a new canonical vector that Python accepts and all other implementations are forced to copy. Replace packet/frame/SCHC construction with a small literal spec encoder (including checksum and all DIO base Flags/Reserved octets), pin fixed KAT bytes, and keep production decoders only in consumer tests.

title: Rust CCP beacon vector consumer assumes hash fields on every slot-selection case
description: rust/lichen-node/tests/ccp_beacon_format.rs iterates every type=slot_selection vector and unwraps output.hash_32, but canonical EMA/timing slot-selection cases legitimately omit EUI/hash metadata. This panics after vector regeneration. Filter production slot-hash assertions to cases with the required eui64/slot fields and only assert hash_32 when the vector supplies that oracle; require at least one consumed canonical case.

title: Update SCHC property tests for validated IPv6 and Rule 255 registry
description: The full Python gate has two deterministic failures in python/tests/test_hypothesis.py after the Version 3 SCHC contract changed: test_schc_packet_roundtrip still feeds arbitrary 0..1280-byte blobs to compress_packet, which now correctly accepts only validated complete IPv6 packets, and test_rule_id_validity still asserts Rule 255 is absent even though the immutable operational registry now intentionally contains the empty UNCOMPRESSED_RULE marker. Replace the arbitrary-blob roundtrip with independently generated valid IPv6 packets plus invalid-input rejection properties, and assert Rule 255's marker invariants instead of absence.

title: Provide true all-or-nothing DAO replay-floor batch commits
description: P2 security/correctness: DaoPersistence.store_rx_floors_batch() promises atomic all-or-none commits and DaoManager relies on that contract before route mutation, but both the abstract default and TwoSlotFilePersistence commit independent floors sequentially. The concrete doc even admits successful earlier floors remain after a later failure. A write fault can therefore advance only part of the replay state while the in-memory DAO transaction is rejected, causing durable inconsistent replay decisions/DoS on retry. Implement a transactional manifest/journal or reject multi-floor batches on this backend; add injected-failure/crash recovery tests at every commit boundary.

title: Keep joined RPL state unchanged on malformed authenticated DIO
description: Full lichen-node gate exposes stale multicast_dio_and_dis_are_received assertions that expect every malformed authenticated DIO option set to unjoin the leaf and erase neighbors. Production parsing rejects these packets before router mutation, which is the fail-closed/DoS-resistant behavior: malformed input must not tear down a valid parent. Update the regression to assert RplRejected with joined/neighbor state unchanged and preserve subsequent valid DIO handling.

title: Reject malformed raw SCHC fragmentation wires on send
description: LinkLayer._send_locked reserves raw payload prefixes 0x78/0x79 for SCHC fragmentation, but an unissued value that is neither a valid control nor a parseable Fragment falls through and is signed/transmitted as ordinary bulk data. For example b'\x78' or a malformed/padded fragment bypasses create_fragment_sender and control validation. The raw fragmentation dispatch should accept only one-use _IssuedFragmentWire values or fully validated directional controls at ACK priority; reject every other 0x78/0x79 payload and add malformed/truncated/padding regression cases.

title: Reject secure request payload length overflow before OSCORE reservation
description: Robustness review of SecureStack::send_secure_request found the new protected length expression 1 + class_e_len + payload.len() + TAG_LEN can overflow usize for an adversarially large caller slice before bounded frame preflight. Compute the length with checked arithmetic and return CoapEncode before reserving sender state; add a regression test if practical.

title: Node.send local delivery leaks SCHC validation exceptions
description: Node.send documents a boolean success result and catches SCHC policy errors on the forwarding path, but its DELIVER_LOCAL branch calls compress_packet(ipv6_bytes) without handling SchcError/ValueError/TypeError. IPv6Packet.from_bytes(strict=True) does not validate UDP checksums, while the newly hardened compress_packet does, so a locally addressed IPv6/UDP packet with a zero or bad checksum raises out of Node.send instead of returning False. Apply the same bounded failure handling as the forwarding path and add local-destination invalid-transport regression coverage.

title: Bound and recover orphaned atomic-vector preparation files
description: ROBUSTNESS/RESOURCE SECURITY: test/vectors/atomic_json.py can leak same-directory backup/temp files created before an entry is appended and before the journal is published. In particular, if backup _prepare succeeds and the following new-content _prepare fails/crashes, the backup is not in entries and the exception cleanup cannot remove it; a process crash anywhere before journal publication similarly leaves all prepared files forever. _recover_transaction only cleans names recorded in a journal. Repeated failures can exhaust the vector filesystem. Track each artifact immediately and clean it on exceptions, and add a safe bounded orphan-recovery scheme tied to the lock/transaction identity with crash-injection tests.

title: Serialize FileKeyStore writers and handle generation exhaustion
description: SECURITY/ROBUSTNESS: FileKeyStore.store_seed reads both slot generations and then writes a predictable per-slot .tmp without any inter-process lock/CAS. Concurrent rotations can select the same slot/generation, race the same temp path, lose an acknowledged seed update, or raise after another writer renames it. At generation 0xffffffff, max+1 also fails struct.pack rather than entering an explicit safe terminal state. Add process-safe serialization/unique temp handling, define u32 generation exhaustion/rollback semantics, and stress concurrent/crash boundary tests.

title: Make trust-store persistence durable, private, and concurrency-safe
description: SECURITY/ROBUSTNESS: TrustStorePersistence.save writes a predictable shared .tmp without locking or O_EXCL, does not set the directory/file to 0700/0600, and renames without fsyncing the directory. Concurrent writers can interleave/replace each other's temporary file or lose updates, process umask may expose peer metadata, and a reported successful save can disappear after crash. Use a locked single-writer or generation/CAS protocol, unique same-directory temp with restrictive mode at creation, fsync file and directory, and tests for concurrent saves, symlink/temp collisions, permissions, and crash recovery.

title: DAO vectors falsely identify production Schnorr as their signature oracle
description: generate_dao_origin_signature.py now correctly imports test/vectors/reference_schnorr48.py, but emitted oracle_provenance.signature_generation still says python/src/lichen/crypto/schnorr48.py. This false metadata defeats the purpose of the independent-oracle audit and misleads cross-implementation consumers. Point provenance to the independent PyNaCl-backed reference module, regenerate deterministically, and coordinate the metadata-only hash change.

title: Restore independent FNV oracle in shared vector generator
description: test/vectors/generate.py advertises independent CCP hash oracles but imports hash_32 from lichen.sim.tdma (which reexports production timing code) for hop/channel vector generation. A production hash regression can therefore regenerate matching incorrect expected outputs. Replace the import with a literal local FNV-1a32 oracle, pin it against published constants, and regenerate only affected CCP families deterministically.

title: Fail closed for unrecognized simulator TDMA vectors
description: python/src/lichen/sim/tdma.py::validate_vector returns True for unknown/empty vector shapes and defaults missing expected fields to computed values, so malformed or newly renamed vector cases can pass without asserting an oracle. Return False for unsupported shapes and require explicit expected outputs for each recognized branch; add negative tests.

title: Update authenticated fragmented-DIO reassembly mock with Rule 255 provenance
description: python/tests/test_node.py::test_link_issues_authenticated_dio_from_verified_reassembly monkeypatches the SCHC reassembly manager to return (ReceiverResult, raw_ipv6), so LinkLayer assigns sentinel rule_id=-1 and the new authenticated-DIO Rule 255 provenance check rejects it. Update the mock to the current return contract including literal Rule 255 and retain an assertion that non-255 provenance is rejected.

title: Simulator accepts out-of-range explicit TDMA beacon assignments
description: Post-fix correctness review of python/src/lichen/sim/tdma.py found TDMAScheduler.sync_from_beacon accepts any assigned value >=0 without exact type or assigned<num_slots validation, then marks the node SYNCED. A malformed or impossible slot assignment can therefore place the simulated node outside the advertised superframe instead of rejecting the beacon. Validate exact u32 SFN, non-negative exact receive time, positive exact num_slots, and assigned=-1 or 0..num_slots-1 before mutating scheduler state; add failure-atomic boundary tests.

title: CCP beacon-format vector encodes obsolete reserved layout and endianness
description: While aligning the canonical TDMA slot formula, test/vectors/ccp_beacon_format.json was found to define the 24-byte beacon header as epoch/num_slots/SFN/timestamp/flags plus 10 reserved bytes, label the multibyte example fields little-endian, truncate a microsecond timestamp to zeros, and say the codec is unimplemented. Normative spec/02a-coordinated-capacity.md section 2a.2 instead defines unsigned big-endian epoch, SFN, and timestamp followed by rx_chains, setup_window, occupied_time, 50 ms guard, and channel_mask; current implementations/vectors should use that contract. Replace the placeholder metadata and example with an exact independently decoded 24-byte header and add executable Python field/byte assertions.

title: Remove unconditional ULA routing from the Rust gateway native mesh profile
description: P2 protocol correctness: resolved LICHEN addressing permits link-local fe80::/64 and native 0200::/8 key-derived /128 addresses; ULA is explicitly not used. rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs is_local_mesh nevertheless treats every fd00::/8 destination as local and mesh_to_mesh forwards/compresses it without any RPL route lookup. This can misroute arbitrary ULA traffic onto the LoRa mesh and bypass the native-address/DAO admission invariant. Restrict local forwarding to link-local control and admitted native /128 RPL routes (plus any separately specified profile), and replace ULA-positive end-to-end tests with canonical native address vectors.

title: Reject zero TDMA slot counts instead of panicking
description: P2 correctness/API invariant: rust/lichen-node/src/tdma_scheduler.rs TdmaScheduler::slot_for computes modulo num_slots as u32 without validating num_slots. The public API accepts u16, so slot_for(..., 0) panics from division by zero in production/no_std callers. Change the API to return a validation error (or enforce a NonZeroU16/validated configuration), update all callers, and add zero/boundary/vector tests. Also replace stale integration helpers in ccp_beacon_format.rs and sfn_wrap_vectors.rs with calls to the production TdmaScheduler so canonical FNV1a32(EUI64)+u32(SFN) modulo N vectors actually test the implementation.

title: Keep ReceiptClock logical and millisecond timelines from being mixed
description: rust/lichen-link/src/evidence.rs uses one last_ticks value for observe/observe_millis and next_logical, so a LinkLayer caller can mix receive_frame and receive_frame_at in one clock domain. Logical packet counts then become comparable to milliseconds, can induce false regressions, and elapsed_since may return meaningless durations across modes. Make the receipt clock mode explicit/fail closed on mixing or maintain distinct domains, and test both call orders.

title: Canonicalize and validate DIS as link-local control traffic
description: rust/lichen-node/src/rpl_stack/transmit.rs send_dis emits the caller-provided unicast IPv6 destination unchanged, unlike send_dio, so a native or arbitrary same-IID prefix goes on wire despite the profile requiring link-local RPL control. receive-side dio_dis_destination_is_allowed accepts any non-multicast prefix sharing the local IID, and the raw DIS parser checks only the source IID suffix rather than canonical fe80::/64. Normalize unicast DIS destinations to canonical link-local, require canonical link-local source/destination (or ff02::1a where allowed), and add negative arbitrary-prefix tests.

title: Use timestamped link receipts in RplStack ingress
description: rust/lichen-node/src/rpl_stack/receive.rs accepts now_ms but calls LinkLayer::receive_frame for both normal and border ingress (including bootstrap retry), producing logical ReceiptEvidence with monotonic_millis=None. Authenticated SCHC fragmentation requires monotonic_millis and therefore cannot consume frames admitted through the production RPL receive path; the supplied reception time is also discarded. Call receive_frame_at with the normalized now_ms on every attempt and add ingress tests proving duration-capable evidence and nondecreasing behavior.

title: SCHC timer guards allow post-construction clock substitution
description: python/src/lichen/schc/fragment.py:SchcSessionManager and python/src/lichen/schc/reassembly.py:_AuthenticatedReassemblyManager wrap lambda: self._clock() in _ValidatedSchcClock, so the guarded callback identity stays constant while the actual self._clock field remains freely replaceable. Replacing _clock with a non-regressing attacker-controlled callable is undetected: a large jump can prematurely expire active sessions/hold-downs and retire wire capabilities; a frozen value can retain them indefinitely. This undercuts the fail-stop clock design and differs from LinkLayer's immutable MonotonicClock binding. Bind an exact immutable clock capability/callback snapshot directly (and ideally share the LinkLayer clock), fail closed on reference/domain mutation, and add forward-jump/freeze/substitution tests for both managers.

title: DAO Schnorr vectors are regenerated by the crypto implementation under test
description: test/vectors/generate_dao_origin_signature.py imports derive_keypair/sign from python/src/lichen/crypto/schnorr48.py to generate the canonical DAO signatures. Its JSON provenance mentions a separate C cross-check command, but no repository test/CI invocation enforces that cross-check, and --check only compares output regenerated by the same production signer. A defect or domain/transcript regression in the Python signer can therefore be blessed into the language-neutral security vectors. Generate with test/vectors/reference_schnorr48.py (or another mandatory independent oracle), retain fixed known-answer assertions, and make CI verify the independent result before accepting regeneration.

title: DAO origin verification reconstructs instead of retaining exact received transcript bytes
description: spec/05-routing.md requires DAO Origin Signature verification and replay digesting over exact received DAO bytes with no decode/normalize/re-encode. python/src/lichen/rpl/dao_origin.py:extract_unsigned_dao_bytes rebuilds a new DAO from parsed fields/options and validate() computes the signed DAO digest with dao.to_bytes(); DAO.from_bytes does not retain the original wire. Current parsing happens to preserve common encodings, but the security API cannot prove exact-wire provenance, accepts caller-constructed/mutated objects, and will silently canonicalize any present or future parser normalization. Carry an immutable raw DAO envelope/span from bounds-safe parsing through validation and digesting, bind it to the parsed object, and add noncanonical/mutation/exact-retransmission tests.

title: Authenticated DIO admission omits canonical IPv6 envelope checks
description: spec/09-packets-timing.md §13.3 requires a canonical multicast DIO to use validated Rule 255, IPv6 destination ff02::1a, correct link-local scope, and Hop Limit 255 before routing mutation. python/src/lichen/rpl/authenticated_dio.py checks only Next Header, ICMP type/code/checksum and DIO scope fields; it accepts signed DIOs encoded under another SCHC rule or carried to arbitrary unicast/global destinations and with arbitrary Hop Limit. This also affects fragmented-DIO issuance. Reject non-Rule-255/non-ff02::1a/non-255 envelopes (or precisely document and implement any separately authorized unicast profile) and add direct and fragmented admission regressions.

title: DIO parser accepts the reserved G/MOP/Prf bit as a canonical control message
description: python/src/lichen/rpl/messages.py:DIO.from_bytes ignores bit 6 of the G/MOP/Prf octet: grounded reads bit7, MOP reads bits5..3 and preference bits2..0, so wire values differing only by reserved bit 0x40 parse to the same DIO and authenticated admission accepts them. DIO.to_bytes always clears that bit, creating parse/reserialize non-canonicality and cross-implementation ambiguity at a signed routing-control boundary. Reject gmop_prf & 0x40 before issuing AuthenticatedDio and add direct/fragmented/vector tests.

title: Packet-format DIO vectors are generated from the production helper they claim to oracle
description: Final correctness review: test/vectors/generate_packets_timing.py packets_formats_vectors() imports RPL_DIO_FIELDS and dio_packet_bytes from python/src/lichen/packets/formats.py to generate rpl_dio_skeleton and all dio_rank_* expected hex. python/tests/test_packets_timing.py then regenerates with the same helper and only independently checks length/tail, so corruption in the DIO base layout can update both implementation and vectors undetected. The metadata also omits the distinct RFC 6550 Flags octet: dio_packet_bytes emits two zero octets after DTSN but comments both as reserved, and RPL_DIO_FIELDS lists only Reserved. Replace generation with a literal independent 24-byte DIO base encoder (Instance, Version, Rank, G/MOP/Prf, DTSN, Flags, Reserved, DODAGID), independently pin every rank vector byte, and keep production comparison separate.
acceptance_criteria: DIO expected bytes and field metadata are spec-derived without importing the production packet-format helper; tests independently pin all base fields and edge ranks.

title: Reject oversized SCHC floor records before persistence hashing
description: Security/robustness review of wm48 found restore_receiver_floor only checks record.len()>48 and calls the link commitment hash before exact record decoding. A corrupt local store can force unbounded hashing of an oversized record. Define the canonical fixed record length and reject all non-exact lengths before hashing/signature work; test oversized/truncated non-mutation.
notes: Defined canonical fixed SCHC floor-record length and rejects truncated/oversized records before commitment hashing or signature work; non-mutation cases covered. SCHC tests/clippy pass.

title: Rejected SCHC replay advances persisted high-water against test contract
description: Deterministic gate: python/tests/link/test_link_security_persistence.py::test_malformed_first_fragment_rejection_survives_reboot. After restoring a rejected first-fragment tombstone with high_water=0, an authenticated repeated malformed first fragment at counter 1 returns no response, but export_persistence_state()[0]['high_water'] is 1 while the test requires 0. Determine whether rejected-session replay suppression must retain the original rejection counter or monotonically absorb authenticated repeats; update implementation/spec-aligned test and persistence round-trip consistently. Repro: UV_CACHE_DIR=/private/tmp/lichen-uv-review3 uv run --project python pytest -q python/tests/link/test_link_security_persistence.py::test_malformed_first_fragment_rejection_survives_reboot.

title: Malformed fragmented DIO can skip durable reassembly commit
description: In LinkLayer._accept_authenticated_schc_fragment, reassembly manager state is mutated before reassembled DIO parsing/evidence issuance. If the completed payload is DIO-shaped but fails checksum/scope/role/option parsing, issuance raises before _save_persisted_state(), so a reboot can restore the pre-completion session and repeat responses/admission work. Preserve the DIO rejection while durably committing the authenticated reassembly transition, with a regression test.

title: Bound restored Rust link trust records by configured peer capacity
description: Correctness review of wm48 found LinkLayer::restore_peer_trust_state validates conflicts but can insert a signed record when peers.len()==max_peers, exceeding the configured bounded trust/replay capacity. Reject restore at capacity before mutation; test that state remains unchanged.
notes: Fixed restore capacity: validates configured-peer and replay capacities before any mutation; non-mutation test added. Full link tests/clippy pass.

title: Issued SCHC fragment wires bypass session expiry and clock fail-stop
description: SchcSessionManager.consume_fragment_wire() checks record.active but never advances/validates the session clock or expires records. An initial/retransmission _IssuedFragmentWire retained past idle_expires_at can still be consumed and transmitted without any timer maintenance call; likewise a now-NaN/regressed clock is not observed on this authority path, undermining y4vw's fail-stop guarantee. Under the manager lock, validate the shared clock and expire due records before consuming the one-use capability; stale/expired wires must return false, clock failures must revoke/unpin through the terminal cleanup. Add exact expiry-boundary and invalid-clock wire-consumption regressions.

title: AnnounceScheduler RX-channel accessors use nonexistent state
description: python/src/lichen/announce/scheduler.py get_rx_channel()/set_rx_channel() read and write self.rx_channel, but the scheduler stores the signed rendezvous channel in config.rx_channel. get_rx_channel raises AttributeError and set_rx_channel does not affect built announces; it also silently maps invalid values to channel 0 instead of matching set_channel validation. Delegate these compatibility accessors to current_channel/set_channel and add regression tests.

title: DesyncFSM cannot execute normative recovery timeout transition
description: python/src/lichen/timing/sfn.py implements DESYNCED->RECOVERING and the three-valid-beacon transition, but has no timeout API/timer transition for the normative RECOVERING + timeout -> DESYNCED rule in spec/09-packets-timing.md section 14.7. TDMA_BEACON_TIMEOUT_SUPERFRAMES is defined but unused. Add an explicit bounded timeout/missed-superframe transition that resets consecutive_valid, and vector-driven tests for timeout at each recovery count.

title: Relayed announce stores origin RX channel under immediate sender
description: In Node._process_announce(), announce.rx_channel is signed by and describes announce.originator_iid, but line 1186 stores it as _peer_rx_channel[sender.iid]. For a relayed announce, sender is the immediate relay and differs from the originator, so origin-controlled data is misbound to the relay. _peer_has_live_state then treats that stale/misbound entry as permanent eviction protection, and entries have no expiry. Store rendezvous channel under the authenticated identity it actually describes (or do not use relayed origin data for immediate-hop channel selection) and expire/remove it consistently; test direct vs relayed announces.

title: Node peer removal bypasses live-state and cleanup invariants
description: Node.remove_peer() (python/src/lichen/node.py lines 548-550) blindly deletes peer_db while add_peer eviction deliberately protects LinkLayer TOFU pins, announce pins, active fragmentation, RX-channel state, and live routes. Removing an active peer can strand fragment sessions, channel entries, gradients/DODAG references, and LinkLayer trust while making signature lookup fail. Define a coherent remove/forget operation that either refuses live peers or retires all dependent state through public layer APIs; also prevent direct peer_db mutation from bypassing canonicality/capacity. Add tests for pinned, routing-live, and active-fragment peers.

title: Runtime announce interval updates do not reach scheduler
description: Node.set_config() mutates self.config.announce_interval_ms (python/src/lichen/node.py lines 1395-1411), but AnnounceScheduler owns a distinct SchedulerConfig copy created in __post_init__ (lines 380-387). Consequently /config reports the new interval while the active scheduler continues using the old one. Validate and atomically propagate runtime changes to the scheduler (including while running), with a behavioral timing/config test.

title: Rust secure_rpl_public fixtures use link-local address as native RPL origin
description: lichen-node/tests/secure_rpl_public.rs constructs RplStack::provision_leaf with SecureStack::local_addr(), which is the fe80:: control address. Production validate_origin correctly requires ygg_addr_from_pubkey as the native RPL/DAO origin, so both public integration tests fail InvalidOrigin. Update fixtures to derive the canonical native address from the identity public key while retaining link-local for control traffic, then run the full lichen-node suite.
notes: Fixed public Secure RPL tests to use key-derived native address for RPL origin/DODAG and retain fe80 control destination. Focused and full lichen-node suites pass.

title: SCHC session clocks can create immortal state or leak replay pins
description: SchcSessionManager and _AuthenticatedReassemblyManager accept an injected clock but use its raw result without validating numeric type, finiteness, non-negativity, or monotonic progression. NaN makes every now >= expires_at test false, so prepared senders, active sessions, tombstones, and receiver contexts can become immortal; regression arbitrarily extends hold-down. In activate_and_start(), replay state is pinned before the first clock call, so a raising clock callback exits without a session record and leaks a replay pin permanently. Add one validated monotonic clock wrapper/high-water policy for SCHC timer state, obtain time before irreversible pin/allocation transitions (or roll them back), fail closed on regression/reentry/non-finite results, and cover raise/NaN/infinity/regression at activation and expiry boundaries.

title: Node CoAP relay integration still seeds removed ULA addressing
description: python/tests/test_node_coap_integration.py::test_coap_get_via_relay constructs fd00:: ULA endpoints and gradient destinations after Node moved to the required key-derived 02xx native primary. The request cannot be delivered, times out, and teardown exposes CancelledError. Update the integration fixture to use yggdrasil_address(pubkey) consistently for NodeChannel URIs and gradient destinations while keeping link-local next hops; add/retain the full A-B-C request/response assertion and bounded teardown.

title: Stale SCHC expiry abort can terminate a newer T=0 transfer
description: _AuthenticatedReassemblyManager keeps the pending-expiry control for a key after an expired context's tombstone matures into a floor. If the caller does not drain expire_due() before a newer-counter opener arrives (possible through the public LinkLayer APIs after a paused maintenance loop), receive() admits the replacement transfer but leaves the old Receiver-Abort queued. A later expire_authenticated_schc_reassembly() then emits that stale abort for the same peer/Rule ID, and because T=0 has no session discriminator it can abort the new transfer. When newer authenticated state supersedes the floor, atomically retire any pending control for the old state (or require/drain it before admission), and add a clock-driven regression covering expiry -> undrained control -> newer opener -> drain.

title: Resolve DAO signer from bounded canonical pin snapshot on IID miss
description: dao_origin_signature vectors require a cryptographically identifiable pinned signer with a forged/noncanonical claimed source to be rejected as IidMismatch, while a genuinely unpinned signer remains UnknownKey. Keep exact indexed IID lookup first; on miss only, take a capacity-checked canonical snapshot of the bounded pin store, verify the DAO origin transcript against all candidates, accept exactly one signer, and fail closed on zero/multiple matches, capacity overflow, or corrupt key/IID entries. Preserve route/replay non-mutation assertions.
notes: Rust complete: exact claimed-IID pin lookup validates canonical key/IID; miss uses capacity-checked exhaustive canonical pin snapshot, verifies DAO transcript across all candidates, accepts exactly one and fails closed on zero/collision/corruption/overflow. DAO vectors return IidMismatch for source mutation and UnknownKey for unpinned signer; full node suite passes.

title: Authenticated forwarded data can poison passive gradients for spoofed IPv6 sources
description: Security review of python/src/lichen/node.py found the FORWARD path installs a DATA gradient for packet.header.src_addr via rx.sender without any source-identity or route-origin evidence. Link authentication proves only the immediate sender, so an admitted peer can send a packet claiming an arbitrary absent victim 02xx source and install a 60-second route toward itself; the update occurs even before next-hop identity/compression/transmission succeeds. This enables blackholing/interception until an explicit higher-priority route arrives. Define the authorization/evidence required for passive learning (or keep it quarantined from forwarding decisions), bind learning to successful forwarding and authenticated provenance, and add spoofed-source/non-forwarded-packet regressions.

title: Concurrent Node.stop can abort initial fragmentation yet transmit reports success
description: Security/lifecycle review of python/src/lichen/node.py found _transmit_peer_schc registers a session and awaits the initial radio batch before creating its driver, while stop/_cancel_fragment_sessions may cancel that same sender concurrently. If stop cancels during the final awaited link.send and it returns true, _transmit_peer_schc observes sender.status != active and returns True even though stop emitted Sender-Abort and no retransmission lifecycle remains. Serialize initial activation with shutdown or track an explicit cancellation outcome, prevent post-stop fragment sends, and add an interleaving regression proving the caller receives False and no driver/session survives.

title: Relay dedup entries never expire and permit authenticated preplay suppression
description: Security review of the rl7e fix in python/src/lichen/node.py found _relay_identity is collision-free over normalized IPv6 bytes, but _relay_seen has no time domain or expiry. Exact legitimate repeat datagrams remain suppressed until capacity eviction, and an authenticated peer can spoof/predict a victim's full IPv6 datagram, seed or refresh the LRU entry, and make the later genuine datagram disappear indefinitely. Define a bounded replay window/expiry based on a monotonic clock and an authenticated end-to-end packet identity or explicit packet nonce where available, without reintroducing hop/SCHC encoding instability; test stale-entry expiry, repeated legitimate datagrams, and adversarial preplay refresh.

title: Node add_peer silently overwrites a different key on IID collision
description: Security review of python/src/lichen/node.py found add_peer assigns peer_db[canonical.iid] unconditionally. A different public key with the same 64-bit derived IID can replace an out-of-band or previously announced identity before link pinning, or make the existing peer unverifiable after pinning, turning an IID collision into trust substitution or persistent denial of service. Detect distinct-key collisions atomically, preserve the incumbent binding, surface a key-change/collision event, and add pre-pin and post-pin collision regressions using controlled PeerIdentity fixtures.

title: Relayed announces can grow Node peer_db without bound
description: Security review of python/src/lichen/node.py found add_peer and constructor peer_db canonicalization have no capacity limit. _process_announce adds every valid relayed originator, so one admitted neighbor can relay arbitrarily many self-signed identities and drive unbounded Python memory plus O(n) native next-hop scans; peer_lookup_all then also exceeds LinkLayer's bounded candidate contract. Apply a deterministic bounded admission/eviction policy aligned with the link trust-store capacity, protect peers with live security/routing state, fail closed when no safe eviction exists, and test an authenticated announce flood.

title: Node receive timeout accepts values that defeat timer progress or spin the receive loop
description: Security review of python/src/lichen/node.py found Node.__post_init__ does not validate NodeConfig.receive_timeout_ms, while set_config coerces bool/float/string values with int() and imposes no upper bound. A zero/negative constructor value or a radio rejecting such a timeout makes _receive_loop catch and immediately retry forever, causing CPU/log DoS; an arbitrarily large value delays _send_expired_reassembly_aborts far beyond the 60-second SCHC inactivity transition. Enforce one exact positive bounded-integer contract both at construction and update, choose a maximum consistent with proactive reassembly expiry, reject bool/coercive values, and add receive-loop/expiry regressions.

title: SCHC session vector overstates unsupported local key-generation binding
description: test/vectors/schc_session_security.json declares both local_key_generation and remote_key_generation as state-key components, and the SCHC draft says their generation tokens, but Python _AuthenticatedReassemblyManager/SchcSessionManager bind local full public key plus only the remote trust-store generation token. LinkLayer has no live local-key rotation and persistence is restored across a new owner instance, so either the artifact/spec must precisely scope local generation as relevant only to implementations with live local rekey, or Python needs an explicit persisted local-generation model. Resolve the contract and add an assertion that the vector's listed components match executable ownership.

title: Durable SCHC floors permanently exhaust TOFU peer capacity
description: _AuthenticatedReassemblyManager.replacement_occupied() counts durable admission floors, and LinkLayer._peer_has_eviction_blocker_unlocked() therefore refuses to evict any peer that has ever fragmented. Floors never expire, so after enough otherwise-idle peers, every pin is permanently protected and all new authenticated peers fail admission. Active contexts and response hold-downs must remain blockers, but floor-only state may be retired atomically during TOFU eviction because ReplayProtector retains a conservative permanent per-signer counter floor; add a bounded-capacity regression proving floor-only peers are safely evictable while active/tombstoned peers are not.

title: Stopped Node can retain live SCHC fragmentation driver
description: Robustness review of pro2 implementation found Node.stop() returns immediately whenever state is STOPPED, while Node.send()/_transmit_peer_schc can create an outbound fragmentation driver without requiring start(). Calling stop() after such a send leaks the retry task and active LinkLayer session. Make stop() drain Node-owned fragmentation sessions even when the ordinary receive/scheduler lifecycle was never started; add a regression.
notes: Fixed Node.stop() to drain Node-owned fragmentation sessions even from STOPPED state; shutdown regression now uses public stop() and verifies Sender-Abort plus no retained session.

title: Node restarts SCHC retry timer before repair batch finishes
description: Correctness review of pro2 implementation found Node._process_received signals outbound session activity before transmitting a negative-ACK repair batch. The driver can therefore begin the next 10-second wait while potentially slow LoRa fragment/ACK-REQ transmissions are still in progress, shortening the required post-request retransmission interval. Signal/reset the timer only after the complete repair output batch is radio-accepted; preserve terminal ACK handling and radio-failure abort behavior.
notes: Fixed with explicit paused/deadline timer state: ACK stops the old timer immediately, and a fresh full interval begins only after repair batch radio acceptance. Regression blocks repair TX beyond timer and proves no premature timeout.

title: Timing barrier test exceeds bounded authenticated-DIO issuance capacity
description: python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py::test_network_clear_and_option_mismatch_advance_replay_barriers authenticates three DIO facades before elevating the first. The bounded LinkLayer authenticated-DIO issuance registry evicts authenticated1, so verifier.verify(authenticated1) deterministically raises 'authenticated DIO is not a live LinkLayer issuance'. Sequence the authenticate/elevate operations or explicitly configure/assert capacity without weakening the production bound.

title: Relay dedup keys use mutable hop-by-hop SCHC bytes and no longer suppress loops
description: Correctness review found Node._process_received stores delivery_payload (the received SCHC encoding) in _relay_seen, while forwarding now decompresses, decrements Hop Limit, and recompresses under the next peer's authenticated SCHC context. A looped copy therefore has a different Hop Limit and may also use a different peer-specific encoding, so it will not match the cached bytes; locally originated packets have the same problem. The cache comment still claims it prevents relay loops, but it now only catches byte-identical encodings and allows repeated LoRa forwarding until Hop Limit exhausts. Define a stable authenticated IPv6 datagram identity suitable for dedup (excluding mutable forwarding fields while retaining collision-safe packet identity), use it consistently for RX and local TX, and add multi-hop loop tests with hop-limit changes and different peer compression modes.
notes: Implemented full canonical IPv6 relay identity with Hop Limit normalized, shared RX/local-TX cache path, hit refresh, and loop tests across hop-limit and SCHC encoding changes. Awaiting 3x review; do not close yet.

title: Node cannot configure its LinkLayer short destination address
description: Correctness review found LinkLayer now correctly rejects SHORT frames unless local_short_addr is configured, but NodeConfig has no local_short_addr field and Node.__post_init__ never passes one. Every Node instance therefore returns NOT_FOR_US for all authenticated short-addressed frames, even though short addressing is normative and spec/09-packets-timing.md §13.1 uses a short-addressed border router example. Add a validated Node configuration/plumbing path for the assigned non-reserved short address (including DAD lifecycle semantics as applicable) and integration tests proving matching short frames are accepted while other short addresses are rejected.
notes: Implemented NodeConfig.local_short_addr post-DAD plumbing and exact matching/nonmatching authenticated SHORT frame tests; validation delegated to LinkLayer's non-reserved exact-int contract. Awaiting 3x review; do not close yet.

title: State that SIID never establishes signer identity before signature verification
description: Security review found contradictory identity wording in draft-lichen-link-01 §3.4: after correctly calling SIID an unauthenticated candidate-selection hint, it says the immediate link identity is established by the Signer Identifier 'and' subsequent signature verification. An 8-byte SIID is a collision-prone alias and must never establish any part of authenticated identity; only successful verification under a current full trust-store public key/generation does. Rewrite the sentence and examples so SIID solely selects a bounded candidate set, collision sets retain all candidates/fail closed on capacity, and no trust/routing/replay/fragmentation state is keyed or authorized by SIID.

title: Domain-separate link Schnorr signatures from other single-key profiles
description: Security review found that the canonical link transcript in spec/02-physical-link.md and draft-lichen-link-01 is LENGTH||LLSec||EPO||SEQ||DST_LEN||DST||SIID||PLD with no fixed application-domain tag or digest. LICHEN deliberately reuses one Ed25519/Schnorr key across link frames, announces, gateway coordination, key rotation, DAO origin, SOS, and persistence; several of those profiles sign different raw or CBOR transcripts. DST_LEN only delimits link fields and is described as domain separation, but it does not separate the link protocol from other Schnorr48 applications. This leaves a confused-deputy/cross-profile signature-reuse surface and makes the 128-bit EUF-CMA claim depend on all other signed-message languages remaining disjoint forever. Prefix a versioned fixed link domain (or sign a domain-separated digest), specify the exact bytes, regenerate all link/DIO/timing signatures, and add negative tests proving a valid signature from another Schnorr profile is rejected as a link MIC and vice versa. Coordinate the format change through the rule/protocol version.
notes: Rust complete: exact LICHEN-LINK-v1 NUL domain prefix is prepended to link Schnorr transcript; independent vector preimage and negative legacy/other-profile tests added. Full link vectors/tests pass.

title: One peer can evict every authenticated DIO issuance
description: Security codereview finding in python/src/lichen/link/link_layer.py: accept_authenticated_dio stores opaque fan-out capabilities in one global OrderedDict capped at MAX_AUTHENTICATED_DIO_ISSUANCES, then evicts oldest entries without a per-signer quota. Unlike verified receipts, a single authenticated peer can sequentially send and have 64 fresh DIOs admitted, consuming each receipt and evicting all still-live DIO evidence from other peers before routing/time/SCHC consumers elevate it. Add a bounded per-signer issuance quota/fair eviction (or supersede only that signer's older equivalent evidence) and regress that one-peer flooding cannot invalidate another peer's live issuance.

title: Define canonical signer EUI-64 derivation in link draft
description: Cross-document correctness review found draft-lichen-link-01 terminology still says EUI-64 is typically derived from LoRa hardware, then uses an undefined 'canonical EUI-64 of the signing node' for mandatory SIID. Main spec/02 §4.2 defines a key-derived local signer EUI-64 by toggling the U/L bit of the key-derived IID exactly once. Add that precise derivation and distinguish it from optional hardware identifiers/destination neighbor records so implementations do not put a radio serial address into SIID.

title: Use current Rule 3 size in link-draft DIO example
description: Correctness review found draft-lichen-link-01 §6.1 still assumes an approximately 22-byte SCHC RPL DIO. Rule Set Version 3 defines a 40-byte fixed Rule 3 header, mandatory parent-selectable DIOs add the verbatim 3-byte Rule Version option, and link PLD also needs dispatch 0x14: canonical minimal PLD is therefore 44 bytes, not ~22. Replace the placeholder with an explicit current Rule 3+option payload and recalculate LENGTH/total together with project-LICHEN-worker6-2wi1.

title: Node suppresses terminal LinkLayer receipt-clock failure
description: Security codereview finding across python/src/lichen/link/link_layer.py and python/src/lichen/node.py: LinkLayer._receipt_now permanently sets _receipt_clock_failed after monotonic regression/reentry and every later receive path raises RuntimeError, but Node._receive_loop catches generic Exception, logs it, and continues as though recoverable. The node remains RUNNING while authenticated ingress is permanently unavailable and may repeatedly poll/log forever. Introduce a distinct terminal link-security clock exception (or terminal LinkLayer failure state), surface it like LinkPersistenceError so Node startup/background-task monitoring observes failure, and test first regression plus subsequent receive-loop termination.

title: Make link-draft CoAP example a valid dispatched payload
description: Correctness review found draft-lichen-link-01 §6.2 shows PLD=<1 byte SCHC-compressed CoAP>, contradicting §3.1/LICHEN framing: authenticated PLD begins with dispatch 0x14 and the body begins with a SCHC Rule ID, so any defined SCHC payload is at least 2 bytes (and a real CoAP residue is larger). Replace the placeholder with an explicit dispatch+valid SCHC packet and recalculate LENGTH; coordinate with project-LICHEN-worker6-2wi1 rather than merely changing old 0x3D to the still-invalid 1-byte arithmetic.

title: Correct signed-frame lengths in link draft examples
description: Correctness review found spec/drafts/draft-lichen-link-01.md examples 6.1 and 6.2 added mandatory SIID fields/flags without adding their 8 bytes to LENGTH. Broadcast DIO with 22-byte PLD has body 1+1+2+8+22+48=82 (0x52), total 83, not 0x4A/75. Extended unicast with 1-byte PLD has body 1+1+2+8 DST+8 SIID+1+48=69 (0x45), not 0x3D. Correct arithmetic and add regression checks for example field sums so future wire-field additions cannot leave lengths stale.

title: Fix MIC-selector short-address vector byte layout
description: Correctness review found both selector_0_with_short_addr and selector_1_with_short_addr in test/vectors/mic_length_selector.json encode input_hex as 08 LLSEC 02 0012 34ab cd68, while their oracle says dst_addr_hex=abcd and the likely intended fields are seqnum=0x1234, dst=abcd, payload=68. Focused python/tests/test_vectors.py failures prove LichenFrame decodes dst=34ab. Correct both wire literals (and ensure the test explicitly preserves the intended sequence/payload fields) so selector 0/1 address-mode cases are real equivalent oracles. Run focused tests and 3x review after the fix.

title: Python exhaustive peer lookup can crash or exhaust link receive
description: LinkLayer._find_sender catches failures from peer_lookup but calls peer_lookup_all directly and iterates its mutable/unbounded result. Callback exceptions or malformed return values escape receive(), and oversized lists force unbounded candidate processing/signature work. Snapshot an exact list, fail closed on callback/type errors, enforce MAX_ENTRIES, and cover exception/malformed/oversized results.

title: Python sends peer-specific unfragmented SCHC as link broadcast
description: Security review: Node._transmit_peer_schc() accepts a concrete next-hop PeerIdentity, but for packets <= MAX_SINGLE_FRAME_SCHC_PACKET it calls link.send(wrap_schc_payload(schc)) with default AddrMode.NONE instead of the peer canonical EUI-64/Extended mode. Every neighbor therefore authenticates and processes a packet compressed under one peer policy; this leaks unicast traffic, consumes replay/receipt work on non-targets, and contradicts the fragmented path, which correctly uses Extended. Send all peer-policy traffic to iid_to_eui64(peer.iid) with AddrMode.EXTENDED and add an exact wire-destination test for both single-frame and fragmented branches.

title: Gateway slot APIs allow invalid dimensions and ordinals to panic or exhaust CPU
description: P2 security review finding. The newly exported rust/lichen-gateway/src/slot.rs exposes unchecked coordination/config dimensions. SuperframeConfig has public duration_s and slots_per_superframe fields; superframe_id()/current_slot() divide or modulo by them and panic when either is zero. The free timestamp helpers have the same divide/modulo-by-zero behavior. SlotAllocator::allocate_for_ordinal() documents ordinal < gateway_count but never enforces it; contiguous allocation loops 0..ordinal and performs unchecked u32 additions/range endpoints, so an untrusted very large ordinal can cause CPU exhaustion or overflow/panic. validate_interleaved_pattern likewise performs unchecked u32 multiplication/addition. Replace panicking constructors/raw public fields with validated fallible construction or explicit Result errors, reject zero dimensions and ordinal >= gateway_count, use checked arithmetic, and add hostile boundary tests.

title: Gateway OSCORE ID derivation permits empty and collision-prone truncated identities
description: P2 security review. PskFederation::derive_context accepts zero-length sender/recipient IDs and does not reject equal IDs. iid_to_sender_id/derive_gateway_ids publicly allow len=0 and arbitrary 1..7 byte prefix truncation; tests even promote 2-byte IDs. Different gateways with the same truncated prefix can therefore receive identical OSCORE identity labels/KIDs, causing context lookup ambiguity and nonce/key identity confusion in a shared-PSK federation. Enforce the federation's unique full 8-byte IID IDs (or maintain a collision-checked allocation registry), reject empty/equal/colliding pairs before Context creation, and add collision/zero-length tests.

title: Gateway TOFU store has no peer bound or admission backpressure
description: Security review P2. TrustStore::verify_tofu inserts every new valid key-derived IID into an unbounded std HashMap. An untrusted discovery source can cheaply generate unlimited key/IID pairs and grow memory indefinitely; there is no MAX_PEERS, eviction policy safe for live pins, admission rate limit, or explicit full error. Bound the trust store, require deliberate admission/backpressure at capacity, never evict active pins on attacker input, and add capacity/flood tests.

title: Gateway TOFU trust state is volatile and silently resets on restart
description: Security review P2. New rust/lichen-gateway/src/trust.rs TrustStore is only an in-memory HashMap with new/default; it has no durable open/provision/commit format, rollback detection, or fail-closed startup. After any gateway restart all pins and DANE/PKIX upgrades disappear, so every peer becomes first-contact TOFU again and trust can be downgraded/re-established under changed external state. Add crash-safe durable pin/trust-level/key-rotation state with scoped integrity and explicit missing/corrupt/rollback behavior; production startup must not silently replace an existing trust store with empty state; test restart, torn write, corrupt copy, and rollback.

title: Rust route lookup aliases any IPv6 prefix by IID and rewrites authenticated paths
description: Security review P2. The convergence change adds RoutingTable::lookup_host_by_iid and makes Router::lookup_route fall back to it whenever exact/prefix lookup fails. rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs then accepts a route whose last hop shares only dst[8..], overwrites that authenticated final hop with the caller-supplied full destination, and forwards it. Any noncanonical 02xx alias sharing a node IID is therefore treated as the node's route even though LICHEN has one exact key-derived primary address and the upper bytes are part of identity/routing authority. Remove prefix-agnostic IID fallback from routable address lookup; explicitly translate only between validated canonical link-local control and exact ygg_addr_from_pubkey identities; add negative alias/shadow-route tests.

title: Rust SCHC authenticated-DIO capability issuance omits local destination binding
description: Security review P2. PeerContextAuthority::issue_from_authenticated_dio and AuthenticatedPeerSchcContext::from_authenticated_dio_frame in rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs validate current link evidence, signer/source, checksum, DIO scope/role, and version, but never require the authenticated L2 destination to be this receiver nor validate the IPv6 destination as allowed local/multicast. These public capability constructors can therefore elevate a valid signed DIO addressed to a different node when used outside the node wrapper, and downstream fragmentation policy trusts the issued capability. Bind issuance to the authority/link receiver's local destination policy (and allowed RPL multicast), or make the unsafe constructor crate-private behind a destination-checked integration API; add cross-destination rejection tests.

title: Rust basic Stack delivers broadcast-link frames with foreign IPv6 unicast destinations
description: Security review P2. The newly added wire_is_for_local_stack in rust/lichen-node/src/stack.rs returns true unconditionally for AddrMode::None. receive() then authenticates/decompresses and returns ReceivedIpv6 without checking the reconstructed IPv6 destination. Consequently a signed L2 broadcast containing IPv6 unicast for another node is delivered to every Stack/application and can trigger handle_and_reply, creating destination confusion and unintended processing. After decompression, require destination to equal a configured local address or valid multicast for all L2 modes; add a multi-node test proving foreign IPv6 unicast over broadcast is ignored.

title: Rust LinkLayer accepts caller-forged peer IID aliases
description: Security review P2. rust/lichen-link/src/identity.rs exposes PeerIdentity.pubkey and .iid publicly, while LinkLayer::add_peer in link_layer.rs indexes and later returns that caller-supplied IID without verifying iid_from_pubkey(pubkey). A caller can register an inconsistent {pubkey, iid}; a valid frame signature under that public key is then elevated to AuthenticatedFrame whose sender IID is the forged alias, and upper layers consume it for source/routing authority. Make PeerIdentity construction invariant-preserving (private fields and/or validate in add_peer), reject inconsistent identities before state mutation, and add negative tests proving a valid signature cannot acquire a non-derived IID.

title: Time stratum 1 is simultaneously defined as mesh-derived and local-source quality
description: Correctness review: spec/09-packets-timing.md:303-312 defines wire stratum 1 Meaning=Mesh-derived, Source Class=Network(peer DIO). Lines 324-330 then require direct manual, initialized RTC, and non-gpsd Local-client samples to use stratum 1 while explicitly forbidding relabeling them as mesh provenance. packets-timing.json time_sync_stratum and generate_packets_timing.py:689-704 retain the name MESH_DERIVED while listing Network, Local-client, Manual/static, and Internal RTC. Although prose says stratum does not infer provenance, the normative Meaning and enum-style vector name do exactly that. Rename the quality level to provenance-neutral terminology and align the table/vector so implementations do not reject or misattribute valid local stratum-1 samples.

title: SCHC draft omits required terminal tombstone and late-fragment semantics
description: Correctness review: spec/03-adaptation.md:313-330 normatively requires a 60-second terminal/expiry tombstone retaining replay high-water, outcome, and cached final ACK where applicable, and restricts session restart. draft-lichen-schc-lora-00.md:369-371 instead says inactivity sends Receiver-Abort and releases state; lines 500-505 say abort releases retained packet/reassembly state, but the draft never defines tombstones/high-water/restart gates despite referring to terminal hold-down at line 360. An implementer following the I-D can free all key state and let late authenticated fragments create a new T=0 session. Mirror or normatively reference the complete tombstone rules in the draft and distinguish active-buffer release from tombstone retention.

title: Link replay exhaustion lifetime is off by roughly 140x
description: Correctness review: spec/02-physical-link.md:317-327 defines one finite 24-bit counter with 16,777,216 tuples and no wrap. Lines 413-415 claim that at 10 packets/sec the epoch wraps in about 7.5 years. The actual lifetime is 16,777,216/10 = 1,677,721.6 seconds = 19.42 days (about 194.18 days at 1 pkt/s). This materially misstates mandatory key-rotation/provisioning cadence. Correct the arithmetic and wording (the terminal counter exhausts; it does not wrap).

title: Link destination gate reads mutable local-address configuration
description: P2 security/TOCTOU: LinkLayer._wire_is_for_local runs before _security_lock and reads mutable public identity.iid/identity.ygg_addr/local_short_addr fields. Concurrent reassignment can validate against transient target configuration and then commit replay/TOFU/receipt state under immutable _local_pubkey. Bind canonical local IID/EUI64/Ygg/short snapshots during __post_init__, use only snapshots in the gate, and add mutation regression.

title: Rule 7 independent oracle does not require boundary cases or valid-case mode fields
description: test_protocol_vector_security.py accepts any >=12 Rule7 address vectors and only validates encoding fields when present. The corpus can silently lose the newly required scope-0/scope-14 or mixed fe90/fe80 cases, and a valid case can omit one/both shared-mode encoding expectations while the oracle stays green. Require the named security boundary set and require both encoding fields on every valid case before checking the one shared AddressMode.

title: Malformed authenticated ELIDED SCHC escapes Link receive target gate
description: P2 robustness: LinkLayer._wire_is_for_local catches TypeError/ValueError around derive_elided_destination, but canonical SCHC decompression raises SchcError (plain Exception). A correctly signed known-peer ELIDED frame with malformed SCHC can therefore escape LinkLayer.receive and kill Node._receive_loop before replay/TOFU mutation. Catch canonical decode/packet exceptions at the target boundary, return NOT_FOR_US without state mutation, and add regression.

title: Rule-version vector incorrectly assigns reserved IDs 0x7A and 0x7B to fragmentation
description: test/vectors/rule_versioning.json says fragmentation uses rules 120-123. The Version 3 registry and both implementations define only directional fragmentation Rules 0x78/0x79 (120/121); 0x7A-0xFE are reserved. This text could make a consumer accept reserved IDs when versions match. Restrict the vector description/provenance to 0x78 and 0x79.

title: Timing DIO vectors lack independent envelope and checksum validation
description: The packets-timing authenticated DIO corpus is security-sensitive, but its independent test checks signatures and source/signer binding only. It does not verify that the stored SCHC dispatch wraps the exact IPv6 bytes, that IPv6 lengths/fields are coherent, that ICMPv6 checksums are valid except for the intentional negative, or that the DIO Time option span identifies the exact option. Add no-production-import checks over the envelope and each signed network case.

title: Authenticated SCHC DIO provenance claims independent checksum and identity checks that are absent
description: authenticated_schc_dio.json provenance says independent consumers revalidate exact checksums, source/signer binding, root AddrForKey binding, and construction bytes. python/tests/test_protocol_vector_security.py currently checks only outer signatures for this family; production-backed tests cannot serve as the independent oracle. Add a no-production-import check that parses the stored IPv6/ICMP/DIO envelope, validates lengths and ICMPv6 checksum, verifies SCHC dispatch + Rule255 exact payload wrapping, checks source IID against signer (including mismatch case), and checks root key/DODAG binding cases.

title: Rule 7 security oracle validates address encodings independently instead of shared mode
description: python/tests/test_protocol_vector_security.py derives source_encoding and destination_encoding independently from each address prefix. Rule 7 has one shared AddressMode bit: IID mode is canonical only when both endpoints are fe80::/64; otherwise both fields are full. The oracle therefore rejects the correct mixed fe90/fe80 vector and could bless a mixed encoding. Derive the expected encoding once from the address pair and assert both fields agree.

title: Rule 7 mixed link-local vector encodes one endpoint as IID under full mode
description: schc_adaptation.json rule7_noncanonical_link_local_full_mode_valid uses source fe90:: and destination fe80::. Normative Rule 7 has one AddressMode bit: because both are not in canonical fe80::/64, AddressMode=1 and both 128-bit addresses must be full. The vector correctly labels the source full but incorrectly labels destination_encoding=link_local_iid, contradicting its name/provenance/spec and enabling asymmetric noncanonical consumers. Set both to full and make Python/Rust consumers assert the single shared mode.

title: Python malformed first fragment emits abort without terminal hold-down
description: _AuthenticatedReassemblyManager.receive returns Receiver-Abort when a context-free authenticated payload under Rule 0x78/0x79 fails Fragment.from_bytes, but it records no rejection/tombstone/high-water. The same pinned signer can send each fresh malformed frame and force an unbounded abort response, contrary to the spec's unrecoverable-error terminal hold-down and bounded response behavior. Record a bounded rejected/aborted tombstone before responding, advance high-water on later terminal requests as specified, suppress non-terminal repeats, persist it, and add malformed/churn/reboot tests.

title: Python TOFU eviction leaves unbounded stale SCHC peer contexts
description: When LinkLayer.receive admits a 65th pin, it removes only _pinned_keys[evicted_iid] and _key_generations[evicted_pubkey]. Any _schc_peer_contexts and _schc_peer_context_issuances for that signer remain. They become unusable but each later pin/DIO churn adds another entry, so authenticated peers can grow both registries without bound and leave session/reassembly policy state detached. Because eviction already chooses an unleased generation, retire the evicted signer atomically across DIO issuances/peer contexts/verified receipts/fragment sessions/reassembly and preserve permanent replay floor; add churn/capacity/persistence tests.

title: Endpoint-direction vector consumer does not execute mutation expectation
description: python/tests/test_vectors.py fragmentation_endpoint_direction branch only asserts vector['expect_state_mutation'] is vector['expect_accept']; it never drives Link/SchcSessionManager state or observes whether wrong-direction input mutated replay/session/tombstone state. This is tautological and cannot catch the fail-before-mutation requirement. Make Python and Rust vector consumers submit authenticated direction cases through the production admission owner and snapshot/assert state/high-water/session capacity before/after, or remove the semantic field and place an equivalent independently parameterized production test tied to each vector.

title: Security-critical authenticated vectors use production code as their claimed independent oracle
description: The SCHC draft claims canonical vectors are not derived from code under test, but authenticated/timing generators import production identity, Schnorr, IPv6, link, SCHC, RPL, and timing modules; root_signature.json names production root_signature.py and root_authorization.json calls lichen.crypto independent. Replace expected-value generation with independent primitives/reference construction or relabel provenance and add a truly independent verifier. Hidden signature-preimage drift demonstrates the present tautology.

title: Rule-version compatibility text and mismatch fallback vector permit downgrade ambiguity
description: spec/03 says Version 3 is the only operational registry and mismatch forbids DODAG admission/Rule255 inside it, yet also says old rules remain supported one release; the draft implies roots alone advertise while parent-selectable non-roots must propagate; rule_versioning.json marks mismatch fallback true without the mandatory outside-DODAG context. Make operational/legacy support scopes explicit, require every parent-selectable DIO to propagate authenticated version, and encode inside/outside DODAG fallback cases.

title: SCHC draft names generic legacy vectors as canonical and profile vector says Version 2
description: test/vectors/schc_fragmentation.json is the fixed-profile Rule 0x78/0x79 dataset but its description still says Rule Set Version 2. The SCHC draft instead names schc_fragment.json alone as the canonical ACK-on-Error oracle, although that legacy/generic dataset includes non-profile Rule 0x2a and toy tile/window parameters. Update the profile vector metadata to Version 3 and make draft/README references distinguish the generic codec vectors from the normative LICHEN fixed-profile fragmentation vectors; do not claim all implementations must accept non-profile parameters in production.

title: SCHC draft weakens reassembly context identity from full signer key to EUI-64
description: spec/drafts/draft-lichen-schc-lora-00.md Section 8.1 says the peer key is the ordered pair of local and peer EUI-64 identities, while normative spec/03-adaptation.md keys by local link-signing identity plus the remote full signer identity and Rule ID. EUI-64-only wording weakens key-rotation/collision isolation and conflicts with Python/Rust production authority. Align the draft with the full authenticated signer identity tuple; clarify that EUI-64 is only the exact link address derived from/selected by the verified trust record and cannot substitute for the full signer key in state ownership.
notes: Final security review independently confirmed the EUI-64/full-signer context conflict and lack of vectors for key-generation separation, authentication-before-allocation, tombstones, replay high-water, and rotation.

title: SCHC draft contradicts 23,562-byte profile ceiling with obsolete 12 KB limit
description: spec/drafts/draft-lichen-schc-lora-00.md Section 5.1 defines an optional encoding ceiling of 126*187=23,562 bytes and requires sender knowledge of receiver capacity, but Section 5.4 later says max practical IPv6 datagram ~12 KB and packets larger than that MUST be application-chunked. The conflicting normative MUST can make conforming implementations reject valid provisioned profile-capacity transfers and disagrees with spec/03-adaptation.md plus schc_fragmentation.json profile_capacity. Remove the obsolete 12 KB requirement or align it exactly with the 23,562-byte ceiling and 1,281-byte mandatory receiver minimum; add/retain cross-reference to capacity vectors.

title: Python TOFU saturation returns authenticated frame after evicting its new pin
description: During receive, LinkLayer inserts a new peer pin then evicts any unleased entry. If all 64 established pins are generation-leased, the newly inserted unleased sender is selected and removed, yet receive still constructs and returns RxFrame. Node can deliver raw payload from a sender that is no longer pinned/current; a repro returns RxFrame with the new peer absent from pins. Fail admission before returning unless a durable pin/current generation remains, or reject capacity without mutating existing trust. Add all-leased saturation, raw/SCHC/RPL delivery, lease release, and pin/generation consistency tests.

title: Python sender mistakes inbound ACK-REQ for outbound negative ACK
description: SchcSessionManager.record_verified_frame accepts ACK-REQ bytes 0x7800/0x7880 through Ack.from_bytes as C=0 ACKs. With simultaneous bidirectional T=0 transfers on the same Rule 0x78, Node sender-control dispatch consumes the peer's inbound-session ACK-REQ before reassembly, advances sender high-water, then drops on bitmap validation; the inbound session never receives its response. Classify ACK-REQ direction before generic ACK parsing and route it only to reassembly. Add simultaneous bidirectional same-rule/window tests including abort/ACK/ACK-REQ ambiguity.

title: Rust generic Stack receives unicast frames addressed to other nodes
description: LinkLayer authenticates and returns known-peer frames without destination admission; generic Stack::receive immediately decompresses/delivers them. RplStack has a separate wire_is_for_local precheck, demonstrating the generic path lacks parity. Enforce signed destination/address-mode/local IID admission before any upper-layer mutation for every production stack, with overheard unicast/broadcast/elided/multicast tests.

title: Rust ACK high-water advances for unrelated authenticated payload
description: FragmentSender.handle_ack_frame calls handle_ack_bytes, but even when wrong rule/status returns SenderOutput::None it still sets ack_high_counter. Passing a higher-counter authenticated non-ACK or wrong-rule frame to this public API suppresses a later legitimate lower-counter ACK. Advance the session control high-water only after a structurally valid, session-bound ACK/abort is consumed; test wrong rule/type/window/status and out-of-order legitimate controls.

title: Rust fragmentation policy never reclaims retired peer slots
description: FragmentationPolicy installs only into an existing signer or empty slot and exposes no retire/remove lifecycle. After MAX_PEERS distinct signers have ever been accepted, later authenticated peers fail PolicyFull forever even if Link/PeerContextAuthority retired all old peers. Wire atomic peer retirement/eviction into policy, invalidate sessions/tombstones safely, and add churn/current-session/slot-reuse tests.

title: Rust SCHC failure tracker never reclaims churned signer slots
description: RuleVersionFailureTracker fixed slots are cleared only by success from the same signer; link peer retirement/eviction is not wired to tracker retirement or bounded replacement. After MAX_SOURCES one-failure signers churn out, all later failing signers return FailureTrackerFull and lose parsing errors/notifications indefinitely. Add explicit retirement/current-peer-aware bounded eviction without evicting active failure runs, and preserve the original parse error while signaling capacity.

title: Rust generic SCHC selection mislabels plaintext as OSCORE
description: Rust OSCORE and plaintext rule descriptors are identical and OSCORE Rules5/6 precede Rules0/1, so SchcContext::select_rule chooses a security-significant OSCORE ID for plaintext fields. The updated rule_versioning consumer already fails left=5/right=0. Require trusted parsed OSCORE evidence or exclude OSCORE rules from generic selection; update vectors/tests for both plaintext and genuine OSCORE.

title: Rust DIO source binding accepts arbitrary prefix aliases
description: Authenticated DIO parsing compares only IPv6 source IID to signer IID and does not require the control-plane source to be link-local fe80::/64 (or another explicitly allowed canonical prefix). A signed Rule255 DIO can use arbitrary 64-bit prefixes with the signer-owned IID; Router keys neighbors/parents by the full address, enabling one signer to create bounded-table aliases. Enforce canonical source scope and add alias/capacity/root/peer vector tests.

title: Dropping Rust LinkLayer does not revoke retained authenticated evidence
description: AuthenticatedFrame liveness includes a receiving-link AtomicBool, but LinkLayer has no Drop implementation that sets it. Dropping/reprovisioning a receiver leaves retained AuthenticatedPeerSchcContext values current through frame.is_current(), so compress/decompress remain usable indefinitely without an owning LinkLayer. Revoke the receiver generation on Drop and test drop/recreate/address reuse plus all retained context/session operations.
notes: Robustness review independently confirmed no LinkLayer Drop sets the receiver retirement flag; retained contexts survive exact receiver destruction.

title: Rust no_std SCHC authority can mint caller-asserted trust
description: Public PeerContextAuthority::issue_verified accepts arbitrary signer/counter/version/receipt facts, while public LinkVerifiedFragment exposes freely constructible fields. Any downstream can construct its own authority, mint an authenticated peer, and drive authenticated sender/receiver APIs without signature, source, root, destination, or clock verification. Under std such contexts can also panic via authenticated_frame().
