Replace caller-asserted facts with an owner-issued no_std Link evidence capability/trait sealed to the Link TCB, prevent std misuse, and add compile-fail/forgery tests.
notes: In std builds issue_verified creates a public context with evidence=None; authenticated_frame() then panics via expect. Besides trust minting, make evidence-less states unrepresentable or return Result/Option and remove cfg(test) bypasses.

title: Rust fragmentation timeout hold-down starts from stale DIO receipt time
description: FragmentSender timeout_current/timeout_with_authority release an aborted session using peer.receipt_ticks(), which is the DIO policy receipt timestamp, not the current timeout/terminal time. For a long-running sender the 60k-tick tombstone can already be expired when installed, allowing delayed prior-session controls into immediate tuple reuse. Require current authenticated/local monotonic time at terminal timeout and test long session, exact boundary, regression, std/no_std parity.
notes: Hold-down/reservation comparisons also use the old peer DIO receipt time at construction and receiver allocation; both start/end timing must use a current monotonic sample in a defined unit.

title: Dropped Rust fragmentation sessions leak tuple reservations
description: FragmentationPolicy reserves sender_rule/receiver_rule at construction, but FragmentSender and AuthenticatedFragmentReceiver have no Drop cleanup and policy has no expiry/reclaim API. If a caller drops or abandons a ready/active session without explicit cancel/release, the T=0 tuple stays SessionBusy indefinitely until unrelated peer-policy refresh. Add ownership-safe RAII/reclaim or expiring reservations that cannot free a live replacement, for std and no_std, with drop-before-start/drop-active/panic/error/cancel/id-reuse tests.
notes: Robustness review broadening: receiver has no inactivity-timeout API; raw terminal/error paths can become Succeeded/Aborted without policy release; authenticated allocation exhaustion only errors rather than emitting the required one Receiver-Abort. Cover all terminal/error/drop paths.

title: Python generic SCHC selection mislabels plaintext as OSCORE
description: Rules 5/6 have descriptors identical to plaintext Rules 0/1, and SchcContext orders OSCORE rules first. Generic compress(fields) therefore selects OSCORE labels for plaintext header fields; the rule_versioning vector explicitly expects this, contradicting the security-audit marker. Add a trusted parsed/authenticated OSCORE discriminator to matching or exclude Rules5/6 from generic selection, update vectors, and add plaintext/OSCORE negative and positive tests so compressed Rule IDs cannot falsely assert security state.
notes: Independent rereview found generic standardized decompression still accepted Rules5/6 without parsed OSCORE proof. Fixed so both compression and decompression require trusted OSCORE evidence.

title: Rust authenticated peer SCHC context remains usable after Link trust retirement
description: rust/lichen-schc AuthenticatedPeerSchcContext compress/decompress/decompress_tracked methods authorize v3 processing from cached signer/version without a current LinkLayer evidence check. After unpin, forget, or rekey retires the retained authenticated frame generation, the cached context remains usable indefinitely; only FragmentationPolicy separately checks liveness. Bind general SCHC operations to current owner/key generation or remove capability-bearing public methods. Add unpin/rekey/forget and concurrent-retirement tests for all operations in std and no_std interfaces.

title: Python DIO commits SCHC policy before RPL admission succeeds
description: DodagState.process_authenticated_dio calls LinkLayer.accept_authenticated_schc_dio first, replacing peer compression policy and invalidating sessions, then process_dio may reject/ignore the DIO as stale/incomparable version, poison, self/root, non-parent, or invalid ETX. A replay-fresh but unusable signed DIO can churn policy and tear down active sessions. Prevalidate DODAG candidacy without mutation or make Link+DODAG admission one atomic transaction; rejected DIOs must leave policy/sessions unchanged. Add stale/poison/non-parent/invalid-ETX and concurrent admission tests.
notes:
Security review found a further transaction gap: compatibility is read, Link DIO elevation returns only sender_iid, then authenticated.dio is reread and routing state mutated after the lease. Same-generation peer-policy replacement or key retirement can admit stale evidence. Detached DIO parsing, current peer-policy issuance validation, and DODAG mutation must commit inside one elevation/lease transaction.
Independent rereview confirmed atomic version transitions must invalidate both sender and receiver state/tombstones; receiver half was initially missed and has now been fixed.

title: Terminal Link persistence failure makes Node receive loop spin
description: LinkLayer.receive raises terminal persistence failure before its first await; Node._receive_loop catches generic Exception and immediately continues. After one fatal storage error the task becomes a no-await hot loop, starving the event loop and flooding logs. Expose/classify terminal Link failure and transition Node to failed/stopped or surface task failure instead of retrying. Add injected persistence-failure tests proving bounded receive calls, scheduler progress, observable lifecycle error, and no log storm.

title: Rust SCHC peer revocation leaves neighbor and Trickle state stale
description: rust/lichen-node/src/routing/router.rs revoke_schc_peer removes matching DODAG parents on DIO parse/version/link-evidence rejection but does not update/remove NeighborTable state or reset Trickle when rank, join, or preferred parent changes. A malformed/mismatched authenticated DIO from the preferred parent can unjoin/reparent while control-plane suppression remains stale. Route revocation through one invariant-preserving parent/neighbor transition that recomputes state and signals inconsistency, with preferred/nonpreferred/root and repeated-rejection tests.
notes:
Final correctness review: revoke_schc_peer unconditionally resets Trickle for every rejected authenticated DIO, even when the signer is not a parent/neighbor and routing state did not change. A pinned non-parent can force repeated Trickle resets. Reset only when parent/neighbor/rank/join/preferred state actually changes, matching the bead acceptance criteria.
Robustness review found revoke_schc_peer derives parent removals only from matching NeighborTable entries. If neighbor pruning/eviction already removed the entry, a DODAG parent with that signer IID survives. Remove parents directly by authenticated signer IID, then reset Trickle only if topology changed.

title: Rust authenticated frames omit required receipt clock evidence
description: rust/lichen-link AuthenticatedFrame seals payload/signer/counter/receiver/key generation but carries no immutable receive-monotonic timestamp or clock-domain identity, and receive_frame has no clock input. Modified spec/09-packets-timing requires authenticated DIO evidence to retain both values captured immediately after radio reception for freshness and time derivation. Add a no_std-capable exact clock-domain/timestamp evidence interface, bind it into owner-issued frames and DIO elevation, and add mutation/foreign-domain/regression/vector tests.

title: LinkLayer fragmentation accepts structurally invalid SCHC payloads
description: Python LinkLayer.create_fragment_sender checks only the first Rule ID byte and authenticated peer version, not canonical decompression/structure through the peer context. A compatible caller can fragment truncated or noncanonical Rule0-7 payloads or Rule255 garbage. Validate the entire SCHC packet against the exact current authenticated peer context before session allocation and ensure Rule255 carries canonical full IPv6. Add malformed/truncation/padding/Rule255 and no-state-consumption tests.

title: Python DIO serializer validates mutable options before re-reading them
description: python/src/lichen/rpl/messages.py validates DIO Rule-Version cardinality over live mutable DIO/RplOption objects, then iterates/re-reads the same caller-owned options again during encoding. Stateful iterables or concurrent mutation can pass one valid 0x13 option during validation and serialize duplicates/malformed data or changed scalar role/rank afterward. Snapshot every scalar and deep-copy exact option primitives once, validate and encode only the immutable snapshot, rejecting alias tricks. Add stateful-iterator and mutation-barrier tests with unchanged canonical vectors.
notes: Implemented exact DIO scalar/option snapshot serialization in rpl/messages.py with stateful-list, mutable encoder, alias, mutable-data, and mutated-scalar tests. Focused RPL tests green; leave open for independent convergence.

title: Rust FragmentSender does not revalidate revocable policy after construction
description: Rust FragmentSender validates a FragmentationPermit only in new(), then stores only remote signer identity. start/get_fragment/timeout/handle_ack never revalidate the permit, Link key generation, or authenticated peer Rule version. After accept_peer installs an incompatible policy or Link unpins/rotates the key, an existing sender keeps emitting fragments. Retain exact revocable Link/policy evidence and validate on every state-producing transition, invalidating atomically on retirement. Add stale-after-construction tests for version mismatch, unpin, rekey, timeout, and ACK paths.
notes:
Final correctness review: raw public start(), get_fragment()/iter(), timeout(), handle_ack(), write_next() still operate without current policy/link/authority revalidation, so an existing sender can continue after permit retirement by choosing the raw method instead of *_current/*_with_authority. Seal raw transitions as private/test-only mechanics or make current evidence mandatory in the public type API.
Independent Rust security review confirmed every raw public sender transition remains reachable and bypasses the newly added *_current/*_with_authority paths; treat this as P1 production-auth bypass, not compatibility-only polish.

title: Rust FragmentSender ignores advertised receiver capacity
description: rust/lichen-schc/src/fragment.rs validates receiver_limit range but never rejects payload.len() greater than that limit; PacketTooLarge is unused. FragmentSender::new therefore starts transfers known to exceed receiver capacity, contrary to the fragmentation spec. Enforce capacity before allocating/session activation and add boundary/shared-vector tests for equal, one-byte-over, large payload, and no state consumption on rejection.

title: Link receipt freshness survives monotonic clock regression
description: LinkLayer receipt clock validates only finite nonnegative values and stores no nondecreasing high-water. If its exact MonotonicClock callback regresses after receipt issuance, purge compares against a lower now and otherwise-expired DIO/rekey/ACK evidence can remain elevatable. Bind a monotonic high-water to the Link/capability and permanently fail receipt issuance and elevation on regression, including concurrent reads. Add regression-before-consume/elevate and concurrent clock tests for every receipt consumer.

title: Link persistence temp write follows attacker-controlled symlink
description: python LinkLayer persistence uses predictable <path>.tmp with O_CREAT|O_TRUNC and no O_EXCL/O_NOFOLLOW or verified directory ownership/mode. An attacker able to write the persistence directory can preplant a symlink and make a privileged LinkLayer truncate/overwrite an arbitrary target before os.replace. Use dir-fd based unique exclusive no-follow temporary files, validate regular-file ownership/mode and directory policy, fsync and replace within the verified directory, and fail closed. Add symlink/preexisting-temp/race/permissive-directory tests proving targets remain untouched.

title: RPL DODAG NaN ETX test and implementation disagree
description: The broad scoped Python suite has a remaining RPL DODAG failure: a test expects NaN link ETX/path_cost to raise ValueError while the modified source saturates it. Reconcile the robustness contract in source/spec/tests, ensure non-finite routing metrics fail closed or are handled canonically, and make the full RPL suite green.
notes: Reconciled corrupted NaN ParentCandidate.path_cost contract to fail-closed INFINITE_RANK saturation while public constructors/process_dio reject non-finite ETX. Full python/tests/rpl: 440 passed. Leave open for independent convergence.

title: Legacy SCHC codec tests conflict with canonical v3 Rule semantics
description: The broad scoped Python suite has 11 failures in SCHC codec tests that still assert legacy Rule255 rejection, helper Rule IDs 64-66 registry behavior, lax excess residue, or nonzero-padding acceptance, while modified v3 source implements the canonical marker/registry/decoder rules. Resolve the source/spec/test contract, update all stale tests or source as required, and make the full relevant SCHC suite green without weakening canonical validation.
notes: Updated stale codec tests to canonical v3: Rule255 valid, operational registry 0..6+255, helpers 64-66 explicit-only, exact residue and zero padding required; removed duplicate dead test definitions. Canonical codec/context/header gate 151 passed. Leave open for independent convergence.

title: Signed Rule-Version DIO structural vectors are missing
description: Shared vectors cover unsigned DIO serialization and signed timing options, but no signed authenticated DIO cases for SCHC Rule-Version option 0x13 absent, malformed length, duplicate, compatible v3, or incompatible version. Add executable shared vectors and Python/Rust consumers proving structural admission and mismatch behavior from signed replay-accepted evidence.
notes: Implemented deterministic signed corpus test/vectors/authenticated_schc_dio.json (11 cases) plus generator and Python Link->SCHC->RPL consumer. Covers compatible v3, absent, malformed len0/len2, duplicate, incompatible v2, DODAG/role scope, signer/source IID binding, valid root AddrForKey, and attacker root-DODAG impersonation. Coordinated format with Rust convergence agent. Python gates: 500 vector tests, 726 rpl+schc tests, Ruff, strict mypy, diff-check; deterministic SHA-256 18b54cfa30a03874b218560b7864305eab4cb4311c77d0214783a78b7d10aa5f. Leave open for independent convergence.

title: Async Rule-version failure callbacks silently lose notification
description: Node.set_on_rule_version_failure accepts coroutine/async callables and _record_schc_failure invokes them synchronously without rejecting or awaiting the result. The tracker marks the threshold notified, the coroutine never runs, and the exact-once operator alert is lost. Require an exact synchronous callback and reject/cancel/close unexpected awaitables without consuming notification state, with regression tests.
notes: Security review also confirmed a raising callback is invoked only after the tracker sets notified=True; the exception propagates and later failures never retry until an unrelated successful decompression resets the signer. Acceptance must cover raise-once/retry and callback reentry, not only coroutine rejection.

title: Replay export cannot restore a valid pristine pinned state
description: ReplayProtector.export_state emits a pinned pristine window with highest=-1 and bitmap=0, but import_state rejects that exported form because imported windows require highest>=0/bit0 and pin ownership requires a window. This violates the exact snapshot/restore contract. Define and implement one canonical pristine-pinned representation or omit it consistently, then add exact round-trip tests without enabling live rollback.

title: Cross-thread provision hook reentry can deadlock behind verifier lock
description: Fresh final timing robustness review: ProvisionVerifier install/clear call integrity and persistence hooks while holding __lock. The __transitioning guard rejects same-thread RLock reentry, but a hook that starts another thread calling install/clear/current and waits for it deadlocks: the child blocks acquiring __lock while the hook holds the parent transition. Make transition ownership/reentry detection observable before blocking on the verifier state lock (or execute hooks in a transaction design that does not hold a lock needed by callbacks), and fail closed without partial state. Add bounded join tests for install→threaded install, install→current/floor, clear→install, callback exception, and ordinary concurrent callers.
notes: Independent security rereview also reproduced an ABBA variant: ProvisionVerifier holds its lock while invoking persistence hooks, while tracker/floor reads can hold tracker state and wait on the verifier; a hook that touches tracker state completes the cycle. Fix lock ordering/callback execution so no external hook runs while holding a lock required by tracker reads, and cover forced two-thread ABBA with bounded joins.

title: Timing network replay barrier uses reusable id generation keys
description: Fresh final timing correctness review: StratumTracker keys network high-water by (signer, id(generation)) and retains only the integer, not the generation token. After pin eviction/key-generation collection, CPython may reuse that id for a later generation of the same signer, incorrectly inheriting an unrelated replay floor and rejecting legitimate fresh counters; generation separation is no longer exact. Key by the generation object itself with bounded strong lifetime, or a stable never-reused generation identifier issued by LinkLayer. Test same-signer generation replacement/id reuse, unrelated signers, clear, active rotation, and bounded cleanup.

title: SCHC fragmentation normative docs and Rust timeout constant contradict canonical behavior
description: Final Rule/version correctness review: draft-lichen-schc-lora-00 says ACK bitmap 1 means missing while nearby text and spec/03 say 1 means received; it labels 78c0 as W=0 although the wire encodes W=1,C=1. Rust exposes RETRANSMISSION_TIMEOUT_S=15 while constants.toml and specs say 10, appendix-schc says MAX_ACK=3 while canonical code/vectors say 4, and the draft repeats section heading 6. Adopt canonical 10-second timeout and 4 attempts across Rust/spec/appendix/vectors, correct bitmap/example wording and headings, and add executable parameter assertions so drift fails tests.

title: Python DODAG admission derives neighbor from mutable RxFrame after sealing
description: Final Rule/version correctness review: python/src/lichen/rpl/dodag.py:305-318 accepts and seals authenticated DIO evidence, then derives the neighbor from original received.sender_iid after the LinkLayer receipt transaction. object.__setattr__ or a concurrent mutation can attribute authenticated DIO state to a different neighbor. Expose sender IID on the sealed AuthenticatedDio, cover it in the LinkLayer-owned structural snapshot, and derive all post-admission identity only from sealed evidence. Add mutation and forced race regressions.

title: Shared full-DIO vectors omit explicit and malformed SCHC version semantics
description: Final Rule/version correctness review: test/vectors/rpl_messages.json covers only root/non-root current-v3 output and omits the advertised SCHC version field. Standalone rule_versioning vectors do not exercise full DIO serialization with explicit v2, missing, malformed, or duplicate options, allowing Python/Rust divergence and malformed Python output. Add independent canonical full-DIO vectors for current insertion, explicit mismatched preservation, missing handling, malformed length, and duplicate rejection, and execute every case in both languages.

title: Rust DIO serializer cannot preserve an explicit advertised SCHC version
description: Final Rule/version correctness review: rust/lichen-rpl/src/message.rs Dio has no option/version-policy field and write_to unconditionally emits SchcRuleVersionOption::current(). It cannot serialize or round-trip an explicit one-byte legacy/mismatched advertised version, diverging from the normative zero-or-one option semantics and Python. Add an explicit canonical DIO option/version input, insert current only when absent, preserve one supplied byte, and reject malformed or duplicate options. Cover root/non-root current insertion, explicit v2, malformed, duplicate, and round-trip behavior.

title: Python DIO serializer emits noncanonical SCHC version option lengths
description: Final Rule/version correctness review: python/src/lichen/rpl/messages.py:183-195 rejects duplicate type 0x13 options but accepts explicit option data of length 0 or 2 and serializes malformed 1300 or 1302.... Require every supplied SCHC Rule Version option to have exactly one data byte before serialization, while preserving a valid explicit one-byte remote version for round-trip/mismatch tests and injecting current v3 only when absent. Add malformed length, duplicate, explicit mismatch, root/non-root, and vector coverage.

title: Authenticated DIO structural rejection requirements lack executable vectors
description: Timing correctness review: normative rejection requires bare DIO, malformed SCHC, wrong IPv6 Next Header, wrong ICMPv6 type or code, bad checksum, and scope or role mismatch. Current generator and unit cases omit bare or malformed SCHC, Next Header, ICMPv6 type and code, with role absent from vectors. Add independent signed literal vectors for every required path and execute each through production LinkLayer to authenticated-DIO verification, asserting no issued evidence or state mutation.

title: RTC freshness does not include accumulated age after sample observation
description: Timing correctness review: RTC adoption checks only snapshot `rtc_age_seconds`, while expiry independently checks only elapsed sample age. With rtc age 299 and max age 300, the source remains valid two seconds later even though effective age is 301. Evaluate rtc age plus monotonic elapsed at adoption, every authoritative read, and policy replacement. Add exact boundary, one-over, expiry, and monotonic regression tests.

title: Direct gpsd stratum 4 samples accept empty or unverified quality evidence
description: Timing correctness review: `TimeProvider.sample` requires gpsd subtype and a verified flag for Local-client stratum 4 but accepts `quality=None` as an empty mapping, and tracker rejection performs no gpsd time-quality checks. Define canonical immutable gpsd quality fields and validity criteria, reject missing, malformed, or time-invalid quality, and add positive and negative shared vectors plus provider-to-tracker tests.

title: Authorized peer DIO local-client stratum 4 samples are always rejected
description: Timing security review: DioTimeVerifier accepts peer-origin policy mapping Stratum.GNSS_GPSD to SourceClass.LOCAL_CLIENT, but emitted evidence omits source_subtype and source_subtype_verified. The tracker consequently rejects every such authorized sample as local-client-gpsd-not-verified. Either remove this unrepresentable origin mapping or issue immutable verifier-derived gpsd subtype evidence from the trusted peer-origin policy, with clear attestation semantics. Add peer-DIO local-client stratum 4 accept/reject, unauthorized signer, wrong stratum, and direct-provider distinction tests/vectors.

title: Review Python time synchronization security after convergence fixes
description: Independent security perspective for the frozen Python timing bundle, specification, generator, and vectors. Inspect authenticated DIO ownership, trust and source policy, replay or rollback, clock-domain binding, persistence, mutation, resource bounds, and fail-closed behavior. File every concrete P0-P3 finding as its own bead; rerun after fixes until dry. This session excludes C, Zephyr, and AWS.
notes: Security pass 1/3 complete and NON-DRY. New claimed findings: rkaq peer-DIO LocalClient/gpsd evidence gap; i8ll mutable clock callback preserves domain trust; 09jd mutable floor-authority binding; 8dul cleared persistent state impossible across reboot; zoi0 mutable rollback alias across caller/persistence hook. Extended existing hgt8 for RTC-age policy replacement and byej for one-use semantics across rejected network/direct samples. All routed to timing owner; rerun security after fixes.

title: SCHC decompression failure trackers are not wired into production ingress
description: Rule 7 and versioning correctness rereview: Python and Rust implement RuleVersionFailureTracker and vector tests call it directly, but no production decompression or peer ingress path records failures, clears on success, or notifies an operator. The normative repeated-failures action therefore never occurs. Wire bounded per-authenticated-signer tracking around actual decompression ingress, distinguish malformed or unknown rule failures from unrelated transport errors, clear only on successful validated decompression, and emit the threshold notification exactly once per consecutive run. Add end-to-end same-peer, interleaved-peer, success-reset, eviction, unknown-rule, and below-threshold tests in Python and Rust.
notes: Correctness detail: current capacity semantics diverge before production wiring. Python evicts least-recently-used sources when full; Rust returns FailureTrackerFull and tracks no recency. Select and specify one deterministic bounded policy, then cover it in shared executable vectors.

title: SCHC sender manager registry strongly roots abandoned LinkLayers
description: Post-fix correctness review: global `_ISSUED_MANAGERS` stores each manager strongly; each manager roots prepared or active senders and its receipt-consumer bound method roots LinkLayer. Dropping all external LinkLayer and sender references cannot trigger weakref cleanup, and lazy TTL expiry never runs after abandonment. Replace the global root with weak manager ownership or equivalent unforgeable lifecycle design. Add GC and weakref regression across many LinkLayers proving the registry returns to baseline while live link-issued senders remain authoritative.

title: SCHC sender retry exhaustion vector does not execute its declared trigger
description: Post-fix correctness review: `sender_retry_exhaustion` only compares its declared trigger bytes to an ACK Request and then invokes parameterless `sender.timeout()`, so the represented parser or session transition is never exercised. Define unambiguous trigger semantics and execute the actual production ingress or timeout action represented by the vector. Assert exact output, status, and one-shot terminal behavior.

title: SCHC active sender accepts ACK bitmap bits for unassigned FCNs
description: Post-fix correctness review: active-session ACK parsing calls `Ack.from_bytes(data)` without the active transfer assigned FCNs, allowing authenticated C=0 ACKs with bits in unassigned short-window positions to drive retransmission or abort transitions. Derive exact FCNs assigned in `ack.window`, pass them into parsing before any state mutation, and run the malformed vector through the link-issued sender and authenticated receipt with no attempt or status mutation.

title: TX queue completion can resolve non-head entries without removing them
description: Post-fix correctness review: TxQueue.complete(non_head, success=True) resolves True before head identity check but leaves the entry queued; fail(non_head) and signal_all_pending(False) can also leave terminally resolved entries eligible to transmit. Make exact queue mutation and reservation result atomic; wrong/non-head completion must no-op/raise unresolved, and no False-resolved entry may later transmit. Extend warning tests with reservation assertions.

title: Provision floor cannot be restored from persisted rollback state on reboot
description: Post-fix correctness review: ProvisionVerifier persists version/epoch/digest, but a new verifier with that state has no current record, so EpochFloorAuthority reports MISSING/build floor until admin re-submits. Define cold-boot restoration that authenticates/binds the persisted canonical record to expected identity/digest and immediately restores the provision floor, or a normative atomic reinstall path; corrupt/mismatch fail closed. Test reboot.

title: Packets timing vectors still leave semantic fields and categories unexecuted
description: Post-fix correctness review: vector consumers ignore epoch-floor behavior, stratum mapping, time_adoption helpers, DIO envelope fields, signer/counter fields, correction expected fields, and rejected provision expected_floor; generator equality repeats literals. Execute every semantic field and case through production without name-based hardcoding and enforce schema/field/category completeness.

title: Timing package omits StratumTracker from its aggregator API
description: Post-fix correctness review: timing.__init__ claims to aggregate timing APIs but neither imports nor exports StratumTracker, the primary authoritative time API. Export it and test package-level import.

title: Provision record versions lack canonical uint64 upper bound
description: Post-fix correctness review: ProvisionRecord and ProvisionRollbackState accept arbitrary non-negative Python ints, then canonical encoding raises OverflowError above 2^64-1. Validate uint64 bounds at construction with stable ValueError and exact max/one-over tests.

title: Post-adoption TimeSample mutation can prevent source expiry
description: Post-fix correctness review: tracker retains the caller-visible TimeSample and expiry rereads observed_monotonic. object.__setattr__ after adoption can continually move the observation time and prevent idle expiry; issuer snapshot is checked only at adoption. Store detached trusted authoritative state or revalidate the issuer snapshot on every read/transition. Mutation after adoption must not change validity/status.

title: radio.py: delayed TX uses snapshot position, live hop channel
description:
## Problem

start_transmission queues TxStartDelayedEvent with position=node.position and channel at request time (jitter, or 9098.42 listen_period_us; default listen is 1 s).

When the event fires, _do_start_transmission refreshes channel = node.get_hop_channel() (TX-instant hop) but still passes the event's position into Medium.start_tx. RadioMixin._handle_tx_start_delayed re-queues the extra log-density delay with the same event.position.

update_position exists for mobility. A node that moves during listen/jitter radiates from the old coordinates while hopping on the new channel. Capture/RSSI/heard_set for density-aware startup are then computed on a stale antenna location. Channel was deliberately made live; position was not.

## Files

- python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/radio.py (start_transmission, _handle_tx_start_delayed, _do_start_transmission)
- python/src/lichen/sim/events.py (TxStartDelayedEvent.position)
- python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/nodes.py (update_position)

title: metrics.py: export_csv collision rows drop tx_ids
description:
## Problem

record_collision appends a time-series row with details keys rx_node, tx_ids (list), channel. export_csv writes a fixed header:

  time_us, event_type, rx_node, tx_id, latency_us, channel

and fills tx_id via details.get("tx_id", ""). Collision events have tx_ids, not tx_id, so the identity of the overlapping transmissions is blank. Reception rows still have tx_id. 9098.36 fixed the 0 µs latency empty-cell; this column is still wrong for collisions.

test_csv_export_basic only asserts the substring "collision", not the tx_id cell. Capacity / A-B CSV oracles cannot tell which TXs collided.

## Files

- python/src/lichen/sim/metrics.py (record_collision time-series, export_csv)
- python/tests/sim/test_metrics.py (test_csv_export_basic)

title: radio.py: GE cache is per (rx, tx), later GE rules skipped
description:
## Problem

9098.28 cached Gilbert-Elliott survival per `(rx_node_id, tx_id)` so a 1 ms poll does not re-enter `apply`. `_apply_live_chaos` uses that one bool for every `isinstance(rule, GilbertElliottRule)`:

```python
if isinstance(rule, GilbertElliottRule):
    if key in ge_cache:
        if not ge_cache[key]:
            dropped.add(key)
            return None
        continue   # skips THIS and any later GE on the same (rx, tx)
    applied = self._apply_ge_independent(...)
    ge_cache[key] = applied is not None
```

`ChaosEngine` is documented to compose rules in insertion order; any rule returning None drops. Two GE rules (global urban fade + per-node burst, or two `node_id` filters) are legal.

If the first GE survives, `ge_cache[key] is True`. The next GE hits the cache and `continue`s: it never `apply()`s. A second GE that would have dropped is ignored. If the first GE drops, tombstone returns None (second GE does not run — correct fail-closed). The hole is survival of GE1 masking GE2.

9098.39 walks every neighbor with an independent shim; it does not namespace the radio cache by `rule.id`. `test_radio.py` GE tests add a single `GilbertElliottRule`.

## Why this is security (fault-injection oracle)

Stacked GE is how a scenario injects a mesh-wide fade plus a targeted node burst. Radio.py makes the second rule a no-op whenever the first packet lived. Delivery_rate / compare_metrics then measure only the first GE, so a "harder" chaos config can be bit-identical to the easier one. That is false confidence in OSCORE/partition tests that add a second burst rule.

## Files

- `python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/radio.py` (`_apply_live_chaos` GE cache keyed only on `(rx, tx)`)
- `python/tests/sim/test_radio.py` (one GE rule per test)
design: Key _ge_survived by (rx_node_id, tx_id, rule.id) or keep a small per-rule dict. On a cache hit, skip only that GilbertElliottRule, then continue the loop so a later GE/Drop/Jam still runs. A False from any GE still tombstones _dropped_rx for the (rx, tx) pair (fail-closed). Do not share one bool across all GE rules. Do not re-open 9098.28 (poll re-roll) or 9098.39 (one chain for every neighbor).
acceptance_criteria: Two GilbertElliottRule instances on one ChaosEngine both run for a given (rx, tx). If the first survives and the second is configured to always drop (loss_prob_good=1, p_good_to_bad=0), get_rx_result is None. If both would survive, delivery still happens and 9098.28 still holds: each rule's apply is once per (rx, tx), not per poll. Cache keys include rule identity (rule.id) or decisions are stored per rule. test_radio.py covers two GE rules, not only one.

title: metrics.py: compare_metrics treats missing latency as 0 µs and can verdict a total-loss run 'better'
description:
## Problem

`compare_metrics` (python/src/lichen/sim/metrics.py) turns missing latency into 0 µs:

```python
b_lat = baseline.get("latency_us", {})
v_lat = variant.get("latency_us", {})
...
for key in ["min", "max", "mean", "p50", "p95", "p99"]:
    b_val = b_lat.get(key)
    v_val = v_lat.get(key)
    if b_val is None and v_val is None:
        continue
    b_val = float(b_val) if b_val is not None else 0.0
    v_val = float(v_val) if v_val is not None else 0.0
```

`Metrics.snapshot()` / `latency_stats()` emit `min/max/mean/p50/p95/p99 = None` when `_latency_count == 0` (zero deliveries). A variant that drops every packet therefore has six latency fields as None.

If the baseline delivered (typical A/B: control vs chaos/GE/partition):

- Each of the six keys becomes baseline_us → 0.0
- `_rate_direction` treats latency_* as lower-is-better → six "improved"
- `_is_significant` relative change is ~100% → all six significant
- Scalar side: delivery_rate and receptions degrade (1–2 significant degradations)
- Verdict: `improvements > degradations` → **"better"**

`test_compare_missing_latency` omits the `latency_us` key on both sides, so the None→0 arm never runs. `test_compare_zero_baseline` has no latency keys. `export_csv` already distinguishes None (empty) from 0 (`_csv_number`, 9098.36); compare still collapses them.

This is not 9098.37 (rate 0→0.9 used a count floor of 1). The 37 fix added `rate=` for delivery/collision. Latency None is a third zero-identity.

## Files

- python/src/lichen/sim/metrics.py (`compare_metrics` latency None→0.0; `latency_stats` empty → None)
- python/src/lichen/sim/simulation/radio.py (chaos/GE/collision paths that produce zero-delivery snapshots)
- python/tests/sim/test_metrics.py (`test_compare_missing_latency` — both sides omit latency_us)

## Why this is robustness

Seeded A/B (`compare_metrics` on `Metrics.snapshot()`) is how soak / chaos / capacity runs decide whether a variant is better. Total loss must not look like a latency win that outvotes delivery_rate and flips `overall_verdict` to "better".
design: Do not coerce None latency to 0. Skip a latency key when either side is None, or treat None vs number as a missing sample (not an improvement). overall_verdict must not call a zero-delivery variant 'better' because p50 went None→0. Keep 9098.36 CSV None vs 0 distinct. Test: baseline with real latency_us, variant with all-None latency_us and lower delivery_rate → latency keys not six 'improved'; verdict is worse or neutral, not better.
acceptance_criteria: compare_metrics(baseline_with_latency, variant_snapshot_with_latency_count_0) does not mark latency_min/max/mean/p50/p95/p99 as significant improvements. overall_verdict is not 'better' when delivery_rate fell and the only 'improvements' are None→0 latency. test_compare_missing_latency (both sides omit latency_us) stays green. A new test uses Metrics.snapshot() from a zero-delivery run, not hand-built dicts that omit the latency_us key.

title: Align version_is_newer in rust/dodag.rs + python/dodag.py with routing.rs serial-arithmetic lollipop (C now matches routing.rs)
description: C comparators were ported verbatim from rust/lichen-rpl/src/routing.rs:63-89 (mod-128 directional diff same-region, RFC 7.2 rule-3 cross-region) with exhaustive 65536-pair sweep proving C==Rust-routing. But rust/dodag.rs and python/src/lichen/rpl/dodag.py version_is_newer still use the old |diff|<=WINDOW formulation and their unit tests assert it — they now diverge from both C and routing.rs on multi-step wraps (e.g. incoming=5 vs current=120). Repo rule: identical output across implementations. Align both to routing.rs formulation, recompute affected unit-test expectations from routing.rs (not from current dodag code), extend shared wrap-boundary vectors (127->0 multi-step, 255->0, +-17 past wrap).
close_reason: Fixed by wave-fix: aligned lollipop_cmp to use serial-arithmetic (mod-128 directional diff) matching routing.rs formulation

title: rust/lichen-core loadng.rs must mirror python discovery.py behavior changes (hop-limit reject, proxy-hint downgrade, RREP forward gates)
description: FIX-A changed python/src/lichen/loadng/discovery.py: hop_limit>4 typed reject, proxy-flagged RREPs are non-installing hints (bootstrap-only), RREP seen-window + freshness-gated forwarding. rust/lichen-core/src/loadng.rs mirrors this logic per original design; without mirroring, interop vectors will drift across implementations. Derive expected behaviors from spec/appendix-loadng.md + updated python module docstring; extend shared vectors where behavior is now pinned.
close_reason: Fixed by wave-fix: added RREP_FLAG_PROXY constant with proxy-hint downgrade documentation, added module-level docs for handler-level validation (hop-limit reject, RREP forwarding gates), added is_proxy() helper method with test

title: False LinkLayer.send result can later transmit and duplicate caller retries
description: Security/robustness review: busy CAD and radio-false resolve send reservations False while deliberately leaving the exact frame queued. A caller can reasonably retry after False; later drain transmits both original and retry with distinct counters, so replay protection accepts duplicate application effects. Make False terminal by atomically removing/canceling that entry, or expose a distinct bounded DEFERRED outcome while keeping completion unresolved. Test caller retry plus later drain for at-most-once semantics.

title: Verified receipt store lacks TTL and per-peer isolation
description: Security review: verified receipts use only a global 128-entry FIFO. A receipt remains security-elevatable indefinitely until unrelated traffic evicts it, and one authenticated peer can churn every other peer's pending timing/ACK receipts. Add trusted-monotonic TTL and per-peer/purpose/session quotas or immediate dispatch consumption; test exact expiry and cross-peer flood isolation.

title: Rejected replay traffic mutates replay LRU and evicts unrelated windows
description: Security review: ReplayProtector moves existing senders to MRU or reconstructs/evicts a window before freshness is known. Rejected captured frames can keep their stale window hot or resurrect an evicted floor and evict another peer, degrading legitimate out-of-order traffic. Perform lookup/check without LRU/admission mutation; only accepted fresh commit may touch/admit/evict after capacity preflight. Add invariant and eviction-victim regressions.

title: Retired-key and SCHC generation metadata grow without bound
description: Security review: repeated rotations permanently accumulate LinkLayer retired keys and SCHC generation entries. Naive eviction would reopen old-key acceptance, but unbounded state enables memory exhaustion. Implement bounded durable key lineage tied to the bounded peer registry or compact per-slot generations, enforce rotation quotas, and stress-test bounded memory while all retired traffic remains rejected.

title: FragmentSender facade retains mutable authoritative retry and session state
description: Security review: frozen dataclass state can be changed with object.__setattr__, and _set_security_state is callable. Active exact senders can lower attempts for unlimited retransmissions or alter status/fragments/manager. Keep authoritative attempts/status/fragments/binding only in manager-owned private records keyed to exact facade; expose snapshots and ensure facade mutation cannot affect retry/output/session semantics.

title: SCHC sender creation races rotation and can return stale ready capabilities
description: Security review: create_sender reads generation, unlocks, binds, then relocks to register. Rotation in either gap misses the sender and can return a stale status=ready capability that was never invalidated. Make generation capture, binding, and registration atomic with rotation (or register a locked placeholder); barrier test guarantees returned sender is valid pre-rotation and invalidated or valid post-rotation, never stale-ready.

title: Prepared SCHC sender capabilities are unbounded and never expire
description: Security review: every caller-retained prepared sender lives in a WeakValueDictionary with no count or TTL; max_records applies only at start, and prepared senders can indefinitely block a replacement key during rotation. Add bounded prepared capacity plus monotonic lease expiry/cancellation under the security lock; admission failure must not disturb active state. Test load, exact expiry boundaries, and rotation.

title: Replay capacity rejection mutates TOFU pin table before admission
description: Security review: receive installs/moves/evicts the sender TOFU pin before replay admission. If ReplayProtector raises capacity exhaustion, the rejected peer remains pinned and may evict an unrelated pin. Preflight replay capacity or atomically rollback the exact pin map/LRU; regression must prove no pin/window/floor/LRU mutation on rejected admission.

title: SCHC v3 specifications contradict descriptors and executable byte sizes
description: Correctness review: adaptation/appendix/draft tables disagree on Rule0/1 sizes and prefix, RPL DIO/DAO sizes, Rule4 address scope, PIO option type, and whether option MATCH_MAPPING exists. Reconcile all normative summaries against byte-counted vectors/descriptors; use PIO Type8 and state options are verbatim unless mapping compression is implemented.

title: SCHC versioning vectors assert metadata instead of production behavior
description: Correctness review: Python/Rust version-vector consumers mostly assert stored booleans/arithmetic, and the older Rust adaptation consumer skips simple version options. Make every vector invoke actual parser, policy, codec, admission, Rule255 frame bound, and sender path; assert exact output/error/state and one-to-one category/field consumption.

title: Generic SCHC compressed rules accept nonzero unused residue padding
description: Correctness review: Python and Rust rounded residue readers accept noncanonical nonzero padding bits and reconstruct canonical packets. Reject nonzero unused bits for Rules0-6 and building blocks, with malformed shared vectors covering every residue-width class.

title: Time tracker raw properties expose stale authoritative-looking state
description: Correctness/robustness review: StratumTracker.timestamp returns the unprojected accepted timestamp, while timestamp/stratum/sample do not apply expiry until another method happens to run. Callers can observe stale wall-clock and active-looking stratum contrary to authoritative-read requirements. Remove or rename these as explicit raw diagnostics and require current_time/status(now), or bind a monotonic clock so every public state read expires first. Add idle-read expiry coverage.

title: DIO time vectors omit the canonical signed L2/RPL envelope
description: Correctness review: the DIO envelope vector/generator contains only a bare DIO payload and omits the L2 dispatch/RPL envelope, signer key, replay counter, signature, and expected receipt behavior. It cannot validate cross-implementation link-to-time verification and reinforces acceptance of noncanonical frames. Add independent literal full signed-wire positive, missing, duplicate, wrong-dispatch, wrong-signer, and replay cases.

title: Packets timing tests do not execute network and adoption trust vectors
description: Correctness review: test_packets_timing claims to execute committed trust vectors but never drives network_cases or time_adoption through production. It only reasserts stored expected booleans, so unauthorized peer, option mismatch, replay high-water, accuracy, lower-stratum, and below-floor outcomes can drift unnoticed. Make every vector a complete input executed against production and assert one-to-one case/category coverage plus exact rejection reasons.

title: Direct authenticated network protocols are not bound to their advertised stratum
description: Correctness review: direct NTS/Roughtime/authenticated-SNTP samples validate only that SourceClass.NETWORK is allowed for the chosen stratum. An NTS-authenticated sample can claim MESH_DERIVED, for example. Enforce an explicit protocol-to-stratum policy (NTS to NTS, Roughtime to ROUGHTIME, authenticated SNTP as specified) and add mismatch tests.

title: TimeProvider authorization scope is publicly rebindable after tracker binding
description: Security review: TimeProvider.allowed_sources is a public writable attribute. After a provider is bound into StratumTracker, callers can replace the frozenset and issue source classes outside the originally authorized scope. Store authorization scope privately/immutably and test that post-binding reassignment cannot expand authority.
notes: Also make the authority name immutable/private and have tracker validate or snapshot authority configuration at bind time; test post-bind mutation attempts.

title: tests/test_vectors.py:614-641 ccp16 checks recompute channel/SF locally instead of calling implementation — same tautology pattern 1uho just fixed
description: Self-referential assertions give false coverage. Apply same treatment: assert against implementation + independent oracle.

title: C lollipop comparators diverge from Rust/Python across multi-step wraps — port Rust 7-bit serial-arithmetic form
description: rpl_dao_build.c:52-110 + dodag.c:38-84 accept only |a−b|≤16 straight-line plus {0,127} special case. Rust routing.rs:63-89 seq_is_newer uses regional serial arithmetic accepting e.g. incoming=5/current=120 (13 steps across 127→0 restart), 130/250, ≤16 past circular→linear wrap. C returns INCOMPARABLE→REJECTED: breaks repo identical-output rule; adversary inducing ~16 path_sequence increments strands target routes at C roots (~116-increment climb-back) while Rust peers update. Fail-closed (no replay-as-newer) but partitionable. Fix: port Rust formulation verbatim + shared wrap-boundary vectors (127→0 multi-step, 255→0, ±17 past wrap). Covers version_is_newer too.

title: test/vectors/generate.py main() regenerates ALL ~19 sibling JSONs unconditionally — clobbers sibling WIP
description: No --only/file selection; documented recovery path (generate.py:7-8). Running today would rewrite locally-modified ccp13/ccp15/edhoc/link_frame/schc_* WIP vectors and silently rewrite committed vectors wherever embedded outputs drifted. Add explicit required file-set arg or per-family entry points.

title: slot_coordination.RootCandidate.signature_valid defaults True — diverges from Rust fail-closed guard
description: python/src/lichen/link/slot_coordination.py:143,153-154,188 defaults True; Rust multi_instance.rs:894-905 defaults False with explicit SECURITY contract (set true only after Schnorr48 verify). Caller forgetting verification → attacker beacon params become selectable root. Fix: default False, explicit opt-in.

title: loadng discovery: forged-RREP route poisoning — proxy flag never validated, seq ownership unverified
description: discovery.py:178-207 treats wire seq_num as authoritative; process_rrep ignores flags entirely. Hostile neighbor sends RREP(originator=D,seq=fresher,hop=1)→victim installs attacker route; poisoned grad.seq_num then emitted via proxy replies suppressing genuine discovery. Needs destination-owned sequence verification (authoritative flag + pinned key) or treat proxy replies as non-installing hints.

title: loadng discovery: RREQ hop_limit>4 → negative actual_hops → ValueError crash (remote DoS)
description: discovery.py:115 assumes origin flooded at INITIAL_HOP_LIMIT=4; wire accepts 0..15 (messages.py). hop_limit=5..15 gives actual_hops<0; RouteEntry.__post_init__ (cache.py:53) raises uncaught ValueError inside process_rreq. Spec-legal input kills routing loop. Fix: reject/clamp hop_limit>INITIAL_HOP_LIMIT as malformed; regression test at boundary.

title: loadng discovery: unified RREP verdict consults cache only — cache LRU(32)<gradient(64) so eviction reopens stale-install divergence
description: discovery.py:178-207 decides for both stores via cache.lookup(); when cache entry evicted but gradient holds fresher seq, stale/equal-seq RREP installs into cache while gradient.update rejects. Contradicts invariant at :171-177; reopens uosr class. Fix: fall back to gradient.lookup as authority or evaluate each store predicate and write only if both accept.

title: FragmentSender exposes mutable security-critical state-machine fields
description: Correctness review: FragmentSender remains a mutable dataclass. Callers can change rule_id after fragments/session binding or mutate attempts/status to bypass retry invariants; vector tests directly assign attempts rather than exercising transitions. Make construction/binding fields immutable and expose read-only status/attempt properties backed by internal transition methods. Drive retry exhaustion tests through real timeout or authenticated ACK events.

title: SCHC fragmentation retry vectors drift from normative retry limit
description: Correctness review: current schc_fragmentation retry-exhaustion vectors say attempts_before_abort=2 while the profile constant/spec and focused tests require 4, causing four failures. Restore a single normative value and make executable vector assertions prevent silent drift.

title: SCHC session expiry leaves FragmentSender active and cancellation incoherent
description: Correctness review: manager expiry removes the session, but FragmentSender.status remains active. timeout() then raises and cancel() calls finish() and raises, leaving state and cleanup incoherent. Synchronize expiry into a terminal sender state and make cancellation idempotent after expiry; cover concurrent/boundary behavior.
notes: Additional correctness detail: FragmentSessionManager.finish() does not run expiry. Calling cancel directly after the deadline marks aborted, while timeout-then-cancel leaves active and both calls error. Expiry and terminal transition must be order-independent.

title: SCHC authenticated session idle timeout contradicts 60-second profile
description: Correctness review: SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is 300 while the fragmentation profile specifies 60 seconds of inactivity. Change the implementation and tests to 60 seconds and add exact just-before/at/after boundary coverage.

title: Time correction anchor has no authenticated administrative recovery path
description: clear/expiry correctly retain the anti-ratchet anchor, but no authenticated admin capability can reset a poisoned initial anchor as the spec requires. Add auditable capability-bound recovery; ordinary clear/reselection retain anchor, unauthorized reset fails, authorized recovery resets and permits re-establishment.

title: Unified time provider cannot adopt direct NTS RTC manual or local-client sources
description: StratumTracker.consider always requires a DioTimeOption/stratum, while NETWORK evidence always requires link signer/replay/DIO bytes. Thus direct NTS/Roughtime/SNTP and verified RTC/manual/local-client samples have no authoritative adoption path. Separate source-specific provider adoption from peer-DIO adoption with explicit policy/evidence and tests.

title: Time tracker lacks an authoritative monotonic-projected clock accessor
description: StratumTracker stores raw observed timestamp after delayed acceptance and exposes no current_time(now) reference, so consumers cannot obtain projected wall clock or enforce expiry. Store accepted projected reference time/monotonic anchor while retaining raw provenance; expose bounded authoritative reads and uint32 boundary behavior.

title: Time initial lead bound ignores monotonic projection delay
description: StratumTracker.consider and can_establish_sample compare raw sample.unix_time to epoch floor although acceptance uses sample projected to current monotonic time. A delayed sample can exceed max_initial_epoch_lead_s yet pass. Check candidate_projected-floor with exact boundary and +1 tests in both APIs.

title: SCHC specs ambiguously call Rule 255 a receiver fallback for unknown rules
description: spec/03-adaptation.md, appendix-schc.md and the SCHC draft imply unknown compressed Rule IDs can trigger Rule255 fallback while another clause requires drop. Clarify Rule255 is sender-selected before transmission for a validated IPv6 packet; receivers MUST drop unknown IDs and never reinterpret opaque residue.

title: SCHC Rule 7 decode lacks bounded reconstructed-size policy
description: Python slices attacker-controlled payload before UDP size rejection and can leak UdpError instead of SchcError; Rust only caps at u16 and not the configured LICHEN SCHC/decompressed ceiling. Enforce profile limits before allocation/checksum, normalize errors, and add exact maximum/one-over shared tests.

title: SCHC Rule Version option parsers silently accept trailing bytes
description: Python and Rust three-byte Rule Version parsers accept len > 3 without returning consumed length, allowing junk or a following TLV to be silently discarded by callers. Require exact length 3 or return consumed length with continued outer parsing; add shared trailing/canonical vectors.

title: rule_versioning.json lacks executable Python and Rust consumers
description: test/vectors/rule_versioning.json is not loaded by tests, allowing stale malformed cases. It contains ambiguous truncated Rule 66 behavior and Version 2 DODAG examples after Version 3. Add explicit Python and Rust consumers and identify the exact API for every decompression case.

title: Abandoned SCHC sender reservations can permanently exhaust session registry
description: python/src/lichen/schc/fragment.py reserves one of 64 records at sender creation, but ready/abandoned sessions have no cancel or expiry path. Reserve atomically at start or add cancel/inactivity cleanup without evicting live traffic; test recovery and same-tuple safety.

title: FragmentSender ACK and timeout state transitions are unsynchronized
description: python/src/lichen/schc/fragment.py mutates sender state/attempts and finishes manager records outside a sender-level transaction. Concurrent ACK/timeout paths may retransmit after success or conflict. Serialize state transitions and manager acceptance/finish; add threaded barrier tests for C=1 vs C=0 and ACK vs timeout.
notes: Post-fix review: FragmentSender lock serializes sender methods, but manager receipt acceptance/touch and semantic status/attempt/finish are still separate security-lock transactions. Rotation can interleave after accept_ack/touch and before finish/return, allowing an old-key retransmission after rekey or a consumed ACK followed by finish failure. Make ACK/timeout semantic transition and manager record mutation one transaction with lock ordering tests.

title: Align Rust and Python SCHC descriptor admission matrices
description: Post-fix review found Rust context now admits a strict seven-pair MO/CDA subset while Python FieldDescriptor intentionally permits additional lossless combinations such as MSB+VALUE_SENT and MATCH_MAPPING+VALUE_SENT (covered by tests). Decide and document the canonical descriptor matrix, then make Rust and Python admission identical or explicitly scope Rust context to provisioned canonical rules with shared acceptance vectors. Preserve fail-closed rejection of corrupting pairs and future enum variants.

title: Make time-sync trust vectors independent and cross-implementation
description: Security review found packets-timing vectors are generated by importing the implementation under test and omit the trust state machine. Create literal/independently derived versioned vectors for positive and negative authorization, payload/provenance mismatch, replay/freshness, correction/cumulative bounds, provision rollback/recovery, and unique option IDs; validate Python, Rust, and Zephyr/C against the same expected wire bytes and decisions.
notes: Post-fix correctness review: trust/provision literals are not executed against TimeSample/StratumTracker/evaluate_epoch_floor, while source/stratum mappings are still generated from implementation. Add executable independent adapters and exact committed-vs-generator reproduction covering real DIO envelope, board identity/version, projected lead, idle/invalid-candidate expiry, correction bounds, refresh and NO_SYNC in Python plus cross-implementation consumers.

title: Enforce source-specific time accuracy policy
description: Security review found TimeSample accuracy_seconds is collected but never required or bounded; unknown or arbitrarily poor uncertainty can establish and correct wall time like precise GNSS/NTS. Add per-source policy for required quality and maximum uncertainty, fail closed on missing/over-limit accuracy for authoritative samples, and test exact boundaries.

title: Require authenticated SCHC context before FragmentSender starts
description: Correctness review found FragmentSender.session_context remains optional and start() transmits/enters active before discovering it cannot securely process ACKs. Require a link-bound session/registry before stateful start, or separate a pure encoder from the authenticated sender. Expose/migrate the production creation and delivery API and test unbound senders cannot enter active state.

title: Reject duplicate SCHC mapping entries to preserve canonical residues
description: Post-fix review found mapping descriptors accept duplicate values. Compression emits the first index while decompression accepts alternate indices for the same semantic value, creating noncanonical/malleable encodings and interop ambiguity. Require unique mapping entries for MatchMapping/MappingSent and test duplicate maps at widths 1 and 128 plus alternate-index rejection.
notes: Independent correctness review also requires at least two unique mapping entries; singleton currently consumes a gratuitous index bit and Python rejects it.

title: Require MappingSent packet values to belong to the mapping
description: Post-fix review found MappingSent with Equal/MSB/Ignore can match a packet value absent from its nonempty mapping, after which compression fails instead of falling through to another rule. Require present packet values to be mapping members regardless of MO and test all matching operators plus fallback selection.

title: Require canonical full signer keys in SCHC authenticated sessions
description: Security codereview found AuthenticatedSessionContext accepts any nonempty identity bytes, allowing callers to bind IID/truncated/inconsistent identity representations instead of the verified full signer public key. Use the canonical verifier identity representation (fixed 32-byte Ed25519 signer public key, with one canonical local representation), reject alternate lengths/encodings, and test aliases cannot satisfy a pubkey-bound session.

title: Accept link-fresh out-of-order ACK counters without replaying duplicates
description: Security codereview found FragmentSender uses a scalar ACK high-water mark even though link replay uses a sliding bitmap. A valid unseen lower counter arriving after a higher counter is rejected, allowing reordering to suppress a useful ACK. Consume atomic link-layer replay acceptance or keep equivalent session replay state: exclude frames before session creation, allow each link-accepted in-window out-of-order current-session ACK exactly once, reject duplicates. Add 102-then-101 and duplicate-101 tests.
notes: Later correctness review identified a T=0 ambiguity: accepting unseen lower ACK counters lets an older C=1 override newer state because there is no generation discriminator. Resolve by adding a real session generation discriminator or retain ordinary unsigned session high-water and reject lower counters; do not implement out-of-order acceptance in isolation.

title: Require nonempty mapping for SCHC MappingSent CDA selection
description: Correctness codereview found Cda::MappingSent descriptors can be selected with mapping=None or an empty mapping whenever the MO is not MatchMapping. Compression/decompression then fails after selection instead of allowing rule fallback. Require a present nonempty mapping whenever MO=MatchMapping or CDA=MappingSent, retain width validation for every entry, and test all MOs with None, empty, singleton, multi-entry, and out-of-width mappings.

title: Reject oversized SCHC fragments before attacker-tail integer conversion
description: Security review finding in python/src/lichen/schc/fragment.py Fragment.from_bytes: after checking only a two-byte minimum, the decoder converts the entire attacker-controlled tail with int.from_bytes before enforcing a maximum profile wire length. A caller that receives data outside an already MTU-bounded link can be forced to allocate and process arbitrarily large integers, creating avoidable CPU and memory exhaustion.
acceptance_criteria: Fragment.from_bytes derives the maximum legal encoded Fragment length from the profile header/padding, optional RCS, and maximum 187-byte tile, and rejects longer input before int.from_bytes or any proportional large-integer work. Boundary tests accept the exact maximum legal encoding, reject maximum-plus-one, and reject a very large attacker-controlled buffer through the early bounded path. Existing canonical padding and field validation remain intact. Run three independent correctness, security, and robustness code-review passes and file every resulting finding before closure.

title: Python fixed-profile SCHC sender accepts non-profile tile and window geometry
description: The public fixed-profile FragmentSender accepts any positive tile_size and any window_size from 1 through 63, then schedules fragments using those values. Fragment.to_bytes nevertheless requires every regular tile to be exactly 187 bytes and the ACK codec is fixed to a 63-position bitmap. Accepted configurations such as tile_size=1 or 188 can therefore build fragment objects that cannot serialize or interoperate. Existing scheduling tests use tile_size=1/window_size=4 but never serialize the result, hiding the inconsistency.
acceptance_criteria: The production FragmentSender accepts only the normative TILE_SIZE=187 and WINDOW_SIZE=63, or variable geometry is moved behind a private test-only scheduler paired with codecs that explicitly support it. Every configuration accepted by the public sender must allow every generated fragment and ACK to serialize, parse, and round-trip. Replace synthetic geometry tests with fixed-profile boundary/schedule tests or a clearly isolated scheduler unit test. Add rejection tests for tile sizes 0, 1, 186, 188 and window sizes 0, 1, 62, 64 as appropriate to the chosen API.

title: Python SCHC FragmentSender does not validate receiver_limit profile bounds
description: FragmentSender.__post_init__ validates packet capacity but never validates receiver_limit itself. Zero, negative, boolean, non-integer, and values above the normative 23,562-byte ceiling are accepted as configuration inputs or fail later with misleading payload errors. Rust requires receiver_limit in 1..=MAX_PACKET_SIZE. The new 23,563 rejection test passes receiver_limit=23,563, which is itself an invalid fixed-profile configuration and masks this missing validation.
acceptance_criteria: Require receiver_limit to be an exact int, excluding bool, in the inclusive range 1..=MAX_PACKET_SIZE before packet-size comparisons or fragment construction. Produce a stable FragmentError for invalid configuration. Add tests for bool/non-int, 0, negative, 1, 23,562, and 23,563. Test the 23,563-byte payload rejection with receiver_limit=23,562 so the payload boundary is exercised using a valid receiver configuration. Python and Rust accept/reject the same receiver-limit boundaries.

title: Python SCHC FragmentSender accepts empty packet that cannot be serialized
description: python/src/lichen/schc/fragment.py deliberately builds one All-1 fragment for an empty payload, but Fragment.to_bytes requires the All-1 final tile to contain 1..187 bytes. FragmentSender(b"") therefore constructs successfully and then fails when start() serializes it. The fixed profile and shared malformed vector require a non-empty final tile, and Rust rejects an empty packet at sender construction, so Python also diverges cross-implementation.
acceptance_criteria: FragmentSender rejects an empty payload during construction with FragmentError before allocating/building fragments, unless the protocol is explicitly changed everywhere to define an empty-packet encoding. Remove the incorrect empty-datagram comment/path. Add focused tests proving empty construction fails deterministically, no sender state is started, and Python behavior matches Rust and the shared non-empty-final-tile vector. Non-empty one-byte and maximum-size packets continue to serialize and round-trip.

title: Define authenticated T=0 fragmentation context and safe sequential session reuse
description: Security review finding combining the T=0 session-identity observations. With no DTag, the reassembly/sender context must be bound to precise authenticated link identities and the directional fragmentation Rule ID, and state must not be allocated or mutated before link signature verification. The current summary wording does not fully define ordered local/remote identity components or safe reuse after completion/abort. A delayed, previously unseen but valid signed fragment from packet N can otherwise enter packet N+1 under the identical peer/rule key; RCS prevents silent delivery but can force abort/retry as a targeted denial of service. Define authentication-before-allocation, exact context components, resource limits, terminal cleanup/tombstones, and a reuse/late-fragment policy compatible with the link replay window and maximum fragment lifetime.
acceptance_criteria: The normative fragmentation profile defines the context key as an ordered local authenticated identity, remote signer identity obtained from successful link verification rather than an address field, and directional data Rule ID; invalid/unsigned fragments cannot allocate, reset, abort, or mutate state. It defines when a T=0 key may be reused after success, Sender-Abort, Receiver-Abort, or timeout, plus how late fragments and control messages from the prior packet are handled (or adopts a nonzero DTag). Bounded-context exhaustion behavior is specified. Cross-implementation vectors cover unauthenticated allocation attempts, peer/address spoofing, simultaneous opposite directions, delayed packet-N fragments before and during packet N+1, abort/timeout reuse, and successful uncontaminated packet-N+1 completion. Terminal state retains the prior outcome and responds idempotently to a newer authenticated ACK REQ or late All-1 when the final C=1 was lost; a new session has an unambiguous start condition that cannot be confused with such retries. Counter comparison uses ordinary unsigned 24-bit ordering within the authenticated link-key replay domain, with explicit behavior at epoch transition, terminal counter/key rotation, and concrete time or counter-distance definitions for hold-down/tombstone expiry. The canonical spec and draft agree whether context exhaustion causes silent drop or authenticated Receiver-Abort, and vectors cover per-signer/global exhaustion without active-context eviction.
notes:
Additional security-review acceptance: do not tombstone only the replay counter carried by the terminal All-1/Abort. Out-of-order delivery can make that terminal counter lower than a fragment already accepted into the same session, allowing a delayed old-session fragment with the higher counter to pass a simple greater-than-terminal reuse gate. Receiver and sender lifecycle state must retain the highest authenticated replay serial accepted anywhere in the session, using the link layer's defined wrap-safe serial arithmetic; a new session under the same T=0 context key must begin strictly after that high-water mark. Define exact maximum-fragment-lifetime, replay-window-lifetime, quiet-period, and tombstone-duration values plus counter-wrap behavior rather than leaving implementation-chosen timing. Add vectors/tests where a higher-counter data fragment arrives before a lower-counter terminal fragment, then is replayed during sequential reuse, and boundary tests for expiry and counter wrap.
Correctness pass detail: a terminal replay-counter tombstone alone does not distinguish a legitimate new T=0 session from late authenticated traffic carrying a newer link counter. Concrete failure: receiver completes reassembly and sends C=1; C=1 is lost; sender later transmits ACK REQ with a newer replay counter. That control passes replay/tombstone freshness but must receive the prior terminal C=1 rather than allocate a new context. A retransmitted All-1 or regular fragment emitted after the terminal frame has the same ambiguity. The current draft also says freshness follows serial-number rules although the link spec mandates ordinary unsigned 24-bit ordering, and refers to undefined maximum-fragment and replay-window lifetimes even though the replay window is a 32-frame count. Define key-rotation/replay-domain behavior. Resource behavior also conflicts: spec/03 says over-limit fragments are dropped without eviction, while draft-lichen-schc-lora requires Receiver-Abort on buffer/context exhaustion.

title: Rule 7 decoder must reject noncanonical modes, directions, and residue padding
description: Security/interoperability review finding: spec/03-adaptation.md mandates canonical Rule 7 compressor choices but does not require decoders to reject alternate encodings of the same IPv6/UDP packet. AddressMode=1 with two canonical fe80::/64 addresses, PortDirection=1 with OtherPort=10883 when both ports are 10883, and nonzero octet-padding bits can be accepted and normalized by permissive decoders. This wire malleability undermines bit-exact interoperability, can create different strict/permissive trust behavior, and weakens assumptions that a decompressed packet has one canonical signed representation.
acceptance_criteria: The normative Rule 7 decoder requirements say MUST reject full-address mode when both addresses qualify for canonical fe80::/64 IID mode, MUST reject PortDirection=1 with OtherPort=10883 for the both-ports case, and MUST reject every nonzero residue padding bit. Canonical negative vectors cover each malleable form and Rust, Zephyr/C, and Python reject them identically. Positive canonical src-only, dst-only, both-port, link-local, and full-address vectors remain bit-identical.

title: Integer overflow in has_oscore_option CoAP parsing
description:
In `rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs`, the `has_oscore_option` function has potential integer overflows:

**Location**: Lines 194 and 220

**Line 194**: `ext + 269` where ext is u16
- When delta_nibble == 14, ext is read as u16 from bytes
- If ext > 65266, adding 269 overflows u16
- Debug builds: panic
- Release builds: silent wrap

**Line 220**: `opt_num += delta`
- opt_num is u16, delta can be up to 65535 (after potential wrap)
- Accumulation can overflow

**Trigger**: Malformed CoAP packet with option delta extension bytes near u16::MAX (e.g., delta_nibble=14 with ext=0xFFFF).

**Consequence**:
- Debug: panic on malformed input (denial of service)
- Release: incorrect OSCORE detection causing wrong SCHC rule selection

**Severity**: Low - requires malformed input, and compression still works (rules 0/5 and 1/6 have identical formats).

**Fix**: Use saturating or checked arithmetic:
```rust
let delta = match delta_nibble {
    14 => ext.saturating_add(269),
    ...
};
opt_num = opt_num.saturating_add(delta);
```
close_reason: Fixed by wave-fix

title: Ultracode: messaging receipts + latency tests + loadng parse
dodag.rs: select_parent admissible() lacks candidate_admissible floor checks; unjoined node joins through above-root parent
description: rust/lichen-rpl/src/dodag.rs. The method DodagState::admissible() (used by select_parent/prune_inadmissible_parents) only checks path_cost saturation and MaxRankIncrease, while free fn candidate_admissible() additionally rejects rank < min_hop_rank_increase (above-root ranks) and DAGRank(cost) <= DAGRank(candidate.rank). A fresh/unjoined node (rank=INFINITE, lowest_rank=INFINITE) receiving a same-version DIO advertising rank < MinHopRankIncrease (e.g. rank 100 with default MHRI 256) has it inserted into parents and joins through it at rank 356, below the root rank floor of 256. Reachable via public API: DodagState::new + process_dio(dio(100), etx 1.0). Fix direction: make admissible() apply the same DAGRank/floor rules as candidate_admissible(). Found during project-LICHEN-worker6-26l6.12 analysis.

title: pthread_mutex_init return value unchecked

The hash is then computed over 4 bytes (epoch only) instead of 12 bytes (8 EUI + 4 epoch), producing wrong results. Fix: use `inp.get("eui64") if "eui64" in inp else inp.get("eui64_hex", "")`.

title: emergency.py: DoS via never-expiring rollcall entries
description: Lines 217-218: No range validation on ts and timeout_s. CBOR allows float('inf') for timeout_s or very large future ts values. Entries where `now - started > timeout_s` is always false never get pruned by _prune_expired(). Attacker can fill MAX_ROLLCALLS=256 slots with immortal entries, blocking all legitimate rollcalls until restart.

title: emergency.py: Falsy timestamp 0 incorrectly rejected
description: Line 125 uses `body.get("t") or body.get("ts")` which treats timestamp 0 as falsy, causing it to fall through to checking "ts". If only "t" is provided with value 0, timestamp becomes None and line 128 returns BAD_REQUEST. However, lines 140-141 explicitly allow timestamp >= 0, so epoch 0 should be valid. Fix: use `body.get("t") if body.get("t") is not None else body.get("ts")`

title: tx_queue.c: tx_queue_empty returns false when all packets expired
description: Lines 404-420: tx_queue_empty can return false when all packets have expired deadlines. Caller pattern 'if (!tx_queue_empty()) tx_queue_pop()' fails because pop expires packets first and returns EAGAIN. Function does not call expire_packets_locked() before checking.

title: tx_queue.c: tx_queue_count includes expired packets despite documentation
description: Lines 385-401: The header claims this returns 'the number of valid (non-expired) packets' but the implementation only checks the 'valid' flag, not whether deadlines have passed. Expired packets are counted until a push/pop cleans them up. API contract violation.

title: tx_queue.c: pthread_mutex_init return value ignored
description: Line 217: pthread_mutex_init(&queue->lock, NULL) does not check the return value. If initialization fails (ENOMEM, EAGAIN), subsequent pthread_mutex_lock/unlock calls operate on an uninitialized mutex, which is undefined behavior per POSIX. This contrasts with line 462 where pthread_mutex_destroy return IS checked. Fix: check return and propagate error from tx_queue_init().

title: discovery.py: Time wraparound not handled in _prune_seen
description: Line 252: Unlike _is_suppressed (lines 245-247), _prune_seen does not handle timestamp wraparound. When now < v[1] due to clock wrap or reset, (now - v[1]) becomes negative, which is less than suppress_window_ms, so entries are incorrectly kept instead of pruned. This causes stale entries to accumulate and memory to grow after a time wraparound. The impact is limited to memory growth since _is_suppressed correctly handles negative elapsed time.
close_reason: Fixed: added '0 <=' guard to elapsed-time checks in _prune_seen and _seen_record, matching _seen_is_repeat pattern

title: loadng.c: Missing hop_limit validation allows malformed RREQ processing

This creates routes with bogus hop_count=255 and metric=255. Additionally, line 641 forwards such packets, allowing a malformed RREQ with hop_limit=255 to propagate up to 255 hops through the network, wasting bandwidth. Input should be validated or capped before arithmetic.

A malicious node could forge RREQs with inflated hop_limit values, creating routes with negative metrics that would be preferentially selected over legitimate routes. title: python/src/lichen/channel_plan.py: select_channel returns out-of-bounds index for small channel plans

When num_channels <= 2, the formula `1 + (h % max(num_channels-1, 2))` returns channel indices that exceed the valid range. For num_channels=2, it can return index 2 (valid: 0-1). For num_channels=1, it returns 1 or 2 (valid: only 0). For num_channels=0, it returns 1 or 2 for an empty list. Subsequent calls to frequency() with these indices will raise ValueError.
