title: lichen_pubkey_to_iid() hardcodes 32-byte pubkey length without compile-time assertion
description:
In ipv6_addr.c:64, tc_sha256_update() is called with hardcoded length 32:
tc_sha256_update(&sha_state, pubkey, 32);

Location: firmware/bridge-zephyr/subsys/lichen/ipv6_addr.c:64

The header declares pubkey as 'const uint8_t *' without size information. If a caller passes a shorter buffer, this causes an out-of-bounds read. The function relies entirely on caller discipline.

Impact: If a future caller passes less than 32 bytes, out-of-bounds read occurs. Ed25519 public keys are 32 bytes, so this is correct for intended usage, but the interface provides no protection.

Recommendation: 
1. Add a compile-time static_assert or BUILD_ASSERT for Ed25519 key size
2. Document the 32-byte requirement prominently in the header
3. Consider passing length parameter for defensive coding

Lower priority as this is an API design issue rather than a bug in current code.
close_reason: Already fixed. Line 38 defines LICHEN_ED25519_PUBKEY_LEN=32, and line 101 uses it: lichen_sha256(pubkey, LICHEN_ED25519_PUBKEY_LEN, hash, sizeof(hash)). The original tc_sha256_update(..., pubkey, 32) call no longer exists.

title: SHA-256 state struct not zeroed after use in generate_eui64
description:
In lora_l2.c generate_eui64(), the hash output buffer is zeroed (line 119), but the tc_sha256_state_struct containing intermediate hash state is not zeroed.

Location: firmware/bridge-zephyr/subsys/lichen/lora_l2.c:98, 119

Code:
- Line 98: struct tc_sha256_state_struct sha_state; (on stack)
- Line 119: memset(hash, 0, sizeof(hash)); (zeroes output, not state)

What goes wrong: The sha_state structure contains intermediate hash values that could theoretically be used in a side-channel attack to recover information about the hardware ID. On embedded systems with limited memory protection, stack contents may persist and be observable.

This is defense-in-depth for cryptographic hygiene. The risk is low since hwid is not high-entropy secret material, but the pattern differs from ipv6_addr.c:lichen_pubkey_to_iid() which does zero its hash buffer.

Fix: Add memset(&sha_state, 0, sizeof(sha_state)) after tc_sha256_final().
close_reason: Already fixed. The generate_eui64() function now uses lichen_sha256() wrapper (lichen_util.c:15-38) which properly zeroes the tc_sha256_state_struct via secure_zero() at line 36 before returning. The bead references line 119 which does not exist in current code, indicating refactoring already addressed this.

title: net_pkt_read return value compared incorrectly

title: lichen_ipv6_addr_to_str does not detect truncation

- ipv6_addr.c:145-166 (lichen_ipv6_addr_to_str)

title: Back-to-back transmits from one node self-collide (no airtime enforcement)
description: In the SimRadio/node_server model, a node can start a second transmission while its first is still in flight (TxEndEvent not yet fired, sim time not advanced), so both transmissions are simultaneously active in the medium and collide at receivers. Repro: tests/sim/test_integration.py::TestChaosMonkeyOperations::test_partition_rule_blocks_cross_group — a1 transmits to a2 (received OK), then immediately transmits to b1; both a1 transmissions overlap at b1 -> collision -> b1 receives nothing. A real half-duplex radio cannot transmit twice at once. Likely fix: _handle_tx should advance sim time by the airtime (or block until the node's TxEndEvent) so a node is busy for its transmission duration. Separate from fgk (the RX-timeout deadlock, now fixed). CI deselects this one test pending the fix.
close_reason: Fixed via half-duplex enforcement: start_transmission() now ends a node's previous in-flight transmission before starting a new one, so a single radio never has two overlapping signals in the medium (which self-collided at receivers). _handle_tx_end made robust to the superseded transmission's stale TxEndEvent (only retires the node's current tx). test_partition_rule_blocks_cross_group passes; test_rapid_tx_causes_collision rewritten as test_back_to_back_tx_is_half_duplex (a node's new TX supersedes its own in-flight one — multi-node collisions still covered by test_multiple_transmitters_collision). title: SimulatorServer.get_app() creates new Starlette on each call
description:
**Bug / Code Quality**

In server.py:218-226:
```python
def get_app(self) -> Starlette | None:
    if self._api is None:
        return None
    return self._api.create_app()  # Creates new instance each time!
```

Each call to get_app() creates a fresh Starlette application instance via create_app(). This is:

2. Potentially buggy if caller expects the same instance
3. Inconsistent with start() which caches the app for uvicorn

title: Pending events not purged on node removal
description:
**Correctness Issue**

When Simulation.remove_node() is called, the node's pending events (TxEndEvent, RxTimeoutEvent) remain in the EventQueue. When those events fire, _handle_tx_end and _handle_rx_timeout check if the node exists and skip gracefully, but:

1. Events accumulate unnecessarily in the queue
2. Time advancement calculations consider these orphan events
3. In long-running simulations with churn, this is a memory leak

The fix is to either:
- Filter events when processing (currently done, but wasteful)
- Add EventQueue.remove_for_node(node_id) and call it in remove_node()
- Use soft references or a cancelled flag on events

Files: simulation.py:111-124, events.py
close_reason: Fix already implemented: EventQueue.remove_events_for_node() is called in NodeManagementMixin.remove_node(). Tests pass.

title: RX rule255 address-validation divergence: Python decode_rule255 rejects unspecified/multicast sources, Rust accepts (structure-only per TX/RX split)
description: Found by review pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-9j6r (P3, pre-existing). The canonical TX/RX split (spec/03-adaptation.md 'Endpoint address policy') says Rule255 DECODING validates structure+checksums only. Rust decode_rule255 follows this strictly: validate_full_ipv6_structure (rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs:1464) has NO address classification. Python decode_rule255 (python/src/lichen/schc/headers.py:204-215) routes through validate_full_ipv6 which still calls _validate_ipv6_addresses (headers.py:161, post-9j6r reorder) - rejecting unspecified/multicast sources and unspecified dst on RECEIPT. So a UDP packet with valid checksum + multicast source (or unspecified dst) is REJECTED by Python RX but ACCEPTED byte-preserving by Rust RX - same on-air bytes, opposite verdict, exactly the class of divergence k0r2 fixed on the TX side. Also C: the generic rule255 fallback currently does no validation at all (bead 5rvk will add structural validation - its outcome determines C's RX accept set). Fix direction: decide the RX contract for address classes - either (a) Python drops the address checks from validate_full_ipv6 and moves them wholly to the TX wrappers (aligning RX with Rust; note UdpDatagram.from_bytes ALSO rejects unspecified/multicast sources at udp.py:98 - that layer's policy would need the same treatment and its callers audited), or (b) spec is amended to make the unspecified/multicast-source rejection part of the RX structure contract and Rust gains it. Either way pin with shared rule255 vectors whose denial strings distinguish the classes. Coordinate with 5rvk (C fallback validation) so all three land the same contract; the emission-stage function _validate_rule255_emission_endpoints (headers.py:162-181) already holds the TX-only classes.

title: Python validate_full_ipv6 orders address checks before RH3/UDP structure checks; Rust/C report structure first for dual-defect packets
description: Found by robustness review pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-bb5u (P3, pre-existing, unpinned by any vector). python/src/lichen/schc/headers.py:138-159 validate_full_ipv6 calls _validate_ipv6_addresses (:150, rejects unspecified/multicast src and unspecified dst) BEFORE the routing-header (:151) and UDP length/checksum (:152-159) structure checks. Rust validate_full_ipv6 (rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs:363-366) runs validate_full_ipv6_structure (which includes the RH3/Fragment/UDP checks) before validate_address_policy; C now matches after bb5u. For dual-defect packets ({unspecified or multicast src, unspecified dst} x {bad checksum, UDP length mismatch, non-RH3 routing, Fragment header, payload-length mismatch}) Python raises the address error while Rust/C raise the structure error. Verdicts identical (all reject - fail-closed), error identity diverges. The parity gate is verdict-only so nothing breaks today. Fix if triple-implementation dual-defect identity is wanted: move _validate_ipv6_addresses after the routing/UDP checks in validate_full_ipv6 (or into the emission-stage function where the remaining address classes already live), then pin with dual-defect vectors in test/vectors/schc_compression.json (one per combination class) consumed by all three parity harnesses. Note: pure internal message/order parity - no wire impact.
close_reason: validate_full_ipv6 now runs _validate_ipv6_addresses AFTER the routing-header and UDP length/checksum checks (headers.py), so dual-defect packets report the structural error first - mirroring Rust validate_full_ipv6 (codec.rs:363-366) and the C compress gate order (bb5u). Pins added: (a) python unit test test_validate_full_ipv6_structure_precedes_address_checks - dual-defect packets (mcast-src and loopback-src x zero and corrupt checksums) surface structural messages ('checksum is zero'/'malformed source'/'checksum mismatch') and never the address message, across decode_rule255 and validate_full_ipv6; (b) two shared dual-defect malformed_input vectors in test/vectors/schc_compression.json (mcast-src+zero-checksum, loopback-src+bad-checksum; verdict-only in all three harnesses) with the header regenerated under the new freshness guard (--check clean). Verified on heft: python 2156 pass (schc + all vectors), C parity 59/59 vectors (clang+ASan/UBSan), rust lichen-schc --features std all green incl shared_vectors on the same JSON. 3x codereview: no P0-P2 on the delta; reviewers confirmed no caller depends on the old order and RX baseline accept-set is preserved. Affected sites (19): generate_packet_walkthrough.py:429-435, generate_authenticated_schc_dio.py:375-383, generate_tunnel_authorization.py:580-588, generate_ipv6_addresses.py:122-130, generate_ipv6_icmpv6.py:216-224, generate_packets_timing.py:1676-1686, plus the same copied pattern in generate.py family: asn_sfn, capability_announcements, dao_origin_signature, delegation_tokens, forwarding_buffer, gcp_handoff_cose_sign1, link_frame_signed_modes, relay_signer_chain, root_dio_signature, rpl_route_state, schc_tile_sizing, wire_format_v2, announce_signed_data. Fix: catch FileNotFoundError alone; let RuntimeError (or any guard failure) propagate or exit distinctly with the guard's own message (e.g. 'vector artifact unsafe: ...'); add one regression test asserting a 0775 parent yields the unsafe-directory diagnostic rather than out-of-date. Secondary risk if unfixed: phantom staleness verdicts train operators to regenerate on demand, eroding the freshness check's value as a real-drift alarm. Operator note until fixed: fresh checkout + chmod 755 test/vectors before any generator run (also in bd remember vector-generators-on-fresh-checkouts).

title: ICMPv6 computed-zero checksum convention diverges: C reconstructs 0xFFFF, Python/Rust keep 0x0000
description: P3, found during project-LICHEN-worker6-5b1y (the UDP sibling of this divergence). ICMPv6 computed-zero checksum reconstruct convention diverges across implementations: C icmpv6_checksum (lichen/subsys/lichen/schc/schc_checksum.c:100-106) maps computed-zero to 0xFFFF via finalize_checksum; python icmpv6_checksum (python/src/lichen/ipv6/icmpv6.py:79-88) keeps 0x0000 (raw complement, no or-0xFFFF); rust has TWO icmpv6 checksum helpers: codec.rs icmpv6_checksum_parts (rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs:650-655) routes through ones_complement_sum which maps zero->0xFFFF (so the LIVE decompress agrees with C), while headers.rs icmpv6_checksum (rust/lichen-schc/src/headers.rs:237-242) keeps 0x0000 (agrees with python). Correction over the initial description: rust codec.rs DOES map (verified by kimi correctness pass of 5b1y); the divergence is python-vs-C/rust-live on the wire, plus a rust-internal inconsistency between its two checksum helpers. For ICMPv6 a zero checksum is legal (the RFC 8200 8.1 zero-prohibition is UDP-specific) and both wire values verify as valid when the true checksum is zero, so there is no rejection asymmetry - but reconstructed byte streams differ (rule-2 echo round trip of a computed-zero packet: C and rust live path emit 0xFFFF, python emits 0x0000), failing byte-identical round-trip assertions for that packet class (~1/65536 per distinct packet; no existing corpus row hits it - checked: icmpv6 echo vectors have nonzero computed checksums). Fix needs a coordinated convention decision (map or not for ICMPv6 - RFC is silent) applied to C finalize_checksum, python icmpv6, AND BOTH rust helpers (headers.rs icmpv6_checksum plus a decision whether ones_complement_sum should grow a protocol-scoped variant), then pin with a shared rule-2 vector whose ICMPv6 checksum computes to zero. Do NOT scope-creep 5b1y's UDP fix: that one is protocol-correct as-is.

title: RPL/authenticated-DIO ingest never re-screens endpoint addresses after byte-preserving SCHC RX
description: Observation from security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-29bu (P3, uncertain - needs cross-impl verification before acting). With the spec 03 TX/RX split (29bu: decode_rule255 is byte-preserving, no endpoint address policy on RX; Rust already behaved this way), malformed-endpoint packets (multicast/unspecified/loopback source) now flow further upstream in Python: python/src/lichen/rpl/authenticated_dio.py:317 accepts DIOs without endpoint validation, and python/src/lichen/rpl/routing.py:336 checks src multicast only after DIO processing. If C/Zephyr and Rust ingest layers behave the same (likely - canon), this is consistent behavior and per-layer screening is a design question, not a divergence; the upstream link/authority layers may already reject multicast-source frames before SCHC decode. Verify: (1) whether a multicast-source authenticated DIO can reach authenticated_dio.py:317 in each impl (link-layer source addressing may make this impossible), (2) whether DIO authority/seal checks make endpoint screening redundant, (3) if a real gap, add a source-screening step at the RPL ingest layer in ALL THREE impls together (canon-first), or document the decision in spec/03-adaptation.md. Do not screen at SCHC RX - that would re-break the byte-preserving TX/RX split.

title: C generic schc_decompress Rule255 path lacks the global 22554 ingress ceiling Rust enforces
description: Found by security codereview pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-qn87 (P3, pre-existing; production-unreachable today). Rust decompress rejects data.len() > SCHC_FRAG_MAX_PACKET_SIZE for ALL rules including 255 (rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs:2270-2274) - the encoded-SCHC-packet profile ceiling is enforced at ingress. C generic dispatcher lichen/subsys/schc/schc.c schc_decompress rule255 branch (~:152-165, post-qn87 line numbers) checks only INT_MAX and out_len - a rule255 data blob up to INT_MAX is admitted if the buffer allows. The lichen rule decompressors DO cap (schc_decompress.c:22,104,203,284,339,370,456), so only the generic uncompressed path diverges. Unreachable in production today: lichen_link_rx.c:351 bounds schc_len <= LICHEN_FRAME_PAYLOAD_MAX (250); the SCHC reassembler's limit gate (subsys/schc/schc.c ~:679) is test/fuzz-only in this tree. Fix: mirror Rust - reject data_len > SCHC_FRAGMENT_MAX_PACKET_SIZE in the generic decompress dispatcher (or document the caller-side ceiling contract in schc.h if a profile may legitimately want larger). Also cosmetic: lichen/tests/schc/main.c test_uncompressed_length_exceeds_int now exercises the fallback-ceiling branch (post-qn87) rather than the int-overflow guard; consider renaming to test_fallback_output_profile_ceiling or splitting the INT_MAX case.
close_reason: Generic decompress dispatcher schc_decompress now rejects data_len > SCHC_FRAGMENT_MAX_PACKET_SIZE (22554) at ingress with SCHC_ERR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL, mirroring Rust decompress (codec.rs:2270, same strict > and same 22554 constant) - closing the rule255/uncompressed path that previously admitted blobs up to INT_MAX. Behavior-neutral for all six lichen per-rule decompressors (they already cap identically, verified at schc_decompress.c:22,104,203,284,370,456) and unreachable from production RX (lichen_link_rx schc_len <= 249 frame bound; reassembler caps at its own limit <= 22554 and delivers raw without calling the dispatcher) - pure defense-in-depth per the bead. New pin test_rule255_ingress_profile_ceiling: exactly-ceiling rule255 decodes (22553), ceiling+1 rejects with full-buffer atomicity (sentinel memcmp). Reviewers also caught that the ceiling made the payload_len > INT_MAX guard dead code - removed per no-dead-code rule (limits.h still needed by compress) - and added a comment documenting the deliberate C error-code choice (BUFFER_TOO_SMALL, matching the per-rule convention; Rust uses InvalidPacket at this site). Verified on heft: all 18 C host suites green (clang+ASan/UBSan; schc 17/17), cppcheck clean; three-impl ingress agreement confirmed (C schc.h:122, Rust constants.rs:28, Python fragment.py:39 all 22554). 3x codereview: no P0-P2 on the delta. Findings filed: 5rvk (P2 - C rule255 fallback skips payload structural validation that Rust/Python enforce; pre-existing divergence now test-pinned).

title: Missing Rust/Python counterpart for C relayed-own-source drop on the non-RH3 forward path
description: Security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-xyix: C drops relayed datagrams claiming the node's own IPv6 source (router.c:497-502). Rust forward branch (rust/lichen-node/src/rpl_stack/receive.rs:267-291) and Python forward branch (python/src/lichen/node.py) check only next-hop relations. Add the own-source drop to both forward paths with unit tests.

title: Python _relay_source_routed lacks preferred-parent/root provenance gating (parity with Rust process_source_route)
description: Robustness/security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-xyix: Rust process_source_route (rust/lichen-node/src/rpl_stack/receive.rs:327-339) additionally requires the sender to be the preferred parent and the packet source to be the DODAGID; C enforces equivalent downward-traffic provenance. Python _relay_source_routed (python/src/lichen/node.py) now checks outer-dst-is-self (fixed in xyix) but still relays from any authenticated neighbor without RPL provenance gating. Decide and implement the Python-side policy (incl. behavior when dodag is None).

title: TX-path error logging mislabels policy rejections as corruption: lichen_l2_tx crash_info_store(CRASH_STATE_CORRUPTION) for every negative lichen_link_tx return
description: Found by security codereview pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-wrxl (P3, pre-existing pattern; the new SCHC_ERR_INVALID_ENDPOINT=-15 from wrxl now flows through it). lichen/subsys/lichen/link/l2/lichen_l2_tx.c:154 calls crash_info_store(CRASH_STATE_CORRUPTION, __LINE__, (uint32_t)(-ret)) for EVERY negative return from lichen_link_tx, so a legitimate caller-input policy rejection (e.g. -15 emission-policy) is persisted to flash as 'corruption code 15' - conflating caller-address errors with memory corruption and costing flash wear if a node repeatedly tries to send policy-invalid datagrams. Inputs are node-local so no remote trigger today. Also lichen_util.h lichen_link_strerror has no SCHC-code cases (logs 'unknown error'). Fix: classify SCHC_ERR_* (and other caller-input rejections) distinctly from CRASH_STATE_CORRUPTION (e.g. a CRASH_STATE_REJECT that does not persist, or drop the crash_info call for -EINVAL-class codes), and consider teaching lichen_link_strerror the SCHC codes; keep fail-closed behavior unchanged (datagram still dropped).

title: SCHC compress validation-order divergence: C policy-then-structure vs Rust/Python structure-then-policy (error identity differs on dual-defect packets)
description: Found by correctness+robustness codereview passes of project-LICHEN-worker6-wrxl (P3, inert today). For a packet that violates BOTH the endpoint address policy and a structural rule: C lichen_schc_compress runs validate_ipv6_address_policy (schc.c:557) BEFORE validate_ipv6_transport_lengths (schc.c:562) so it returns SCHC_ERR_INVALID_ENDPOINT (-15); Rust validate_full_ipv6 (codec.rs:363-366) runs structure first then policy; Python validate_full_ipv6 likewise (headers.py:138-159 structure, :861 emission). Verdicts identical (both fail closed); error identity differs. No shared vector exercises doubly-invalid input and all three consumers assert rejection-only, so nothing breaks today - but future interop tests comparing error identity would diverge. Fix if/when error-identity parity is ever asserted: align order (structure first, matching Rust/Python, is the lower-churn direction) or pin the divergence explicitly in spec/03-adaptation.md.
close_reason: lichen_schc_compress now validates structure/checksums (validate_ipv6_transport_lengths) BEFORE the emission endpoint policy (validate_ipv6_address_policy), mirroring Rust validate_full_ipv6 (codec.rs:363-366 structure->policy) and Python's TX wrappers (encode_rule255 headers.py:188-189, compress_packet :860-861) - closing the dual-defect error-identity divergence (C returned INVALID_ENDPOINT where Rust returns the structure error; Python has a single SchcError class). Pure ordering swap: accept/reject set provably unchanged (both validators pure; policy still unconditional after structure), verdict matrix re-verified per class; TX-only invariant and fallback bypasses unchanged. No dual-defect fixtures exist anywhere (verified computationally across all 17 malformed/policy vectors), so no test flips; all 18 C host suites green + python test_vectors 776/776. 3x codereview (correctness/security/robustness, reviewer-model passes): no P0-P2 on the delta; own-comment imprecision (Python citation) fixed pre-commit. Findings: 9j6r (P3 pre-existing - Python's internal address-before-structure order inside validate_full_ipv6, filed with fix direction + vector plan); C-RX Rule255 unvalidated-memcpy finding already tracked as 5rvk. Commit hygiene: staged only schc.c.

title: schc_parity gen_vectors.py treats expect_error as presence-only; a false value silently inverts rejection semantics
description: P3 hardening, found by worker5 subagent robustness pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-hahk. lichen/tests/schc_parity/gen_vectors.py:176 generates the C table with 'true' if 'expect_error' in vector - presence-based, not value-based. Empirically probed: a corpus with expect_error: false generates C expecting REJECTION (inverted); Python's consumer is also value-agnostic (test_vectors.py:722-731 - malformed_input ignores the value entirely, size_boundary checks presence not truthiness). The two consumers are consistent with each other so no live divergence today, but a future expect_error: false silently inverts meaning instead of failing closed. Everything else in the generator is fail-closed (verified by probe: unknown category, missing/extra fields, missing expect_error, duplicate JSON keys, bad/empty hex all exit 1 -> CMake FATAL_ERROR; CMAKE_CONFIGURE_DEPENDS covers JSON + generator; C main.c default: result=1 treats unknown kinds as failure). Fix: require expect_error to be a nonempty string when present (sibling corpus ipv6_malformed.json uses string error enums) and reject otherwise, in both gen_vectors.py and the Python consumers.

title: link_schc.h lichen_link_compress contract doc omits newly-visible SCHC_ERR_NO_MATCHING_RULE
description: P3 doc fix, found by worker5 subagent robustness pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-hahk. lichen/subsys/lichen/link/include/lichen/link_schc.h:59-61 documents lichen_link_compress returning only SCHC_ERR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL. With the hahk gate, the wrapped lichen_schc_compress now also returns SCHC_ERR_NO_MATCHING_RULE for malformed packets - and that is now the most likely TX-side failure for callers of this wrapper. The wrapper currently has no callers (verified by grep), so doc-only. Fix: add SCHC_ERR_NO_MATCHING_RULE (malformed packet rejected by the compress gate) to the contract comment. Also noted in the same robustness pass (opinion, no bead): lichen_link_strerror (lichen_util.h:90-155) has no SCHC cases so -1 logs as unknown error, and lichen_l2_to_zephyr_errno passes -1 through so Zephyr callers see -EPERM; pre-existing mapping gap worth folding into any error-mapping bead.

title: lichen_l2 mislabels SCHC TX rejection (SCHC_ERR_NO_MATCHING_RULE) as CRASH_STATE_CORRUPTION in retained RAM
description: P3, found by worker5 subagent robustness pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-hahk. With the hahk gate active, lichen_schc_compress now returns SCHC_ERR_NO_MATCHING_RULE for malformed locally-originated IPv6 datagrams (app bug or forwarded packet). lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/lichen_l2_tx.c:154 and firmware/bridge-zephyr/subsys/lichen/lichen_l2.c:993 route every negative lichen_link_tx return into crash_info_store(CRASH_STATE_CORRUPTION, __LINE__, (uint32_t)(-ret)), stamping the retained-RAM record; next boot crash_info_check_and_clear() logs previous crash (reason=corruption). Before the gate this path was reachable only via genuine internal inconsistencies (buffer-too-small); now routine malformed-packet rejections pollute the field-debug trail with false corruption reports. No functional harm (no reboot, mutex unlocked on every path, nonce not consumed - next_tx at :189 is after compress at :134). Fix: distinguish validation rejects (SCHC_ERR_NO_MATCHING_RULE = malformed input, log + drop + counter) from corruption-class failures before calling crash_info_store, or narrow CRASH_STATE_CORRUPTION to the specific internal-inconsistency returns; add a host test asserting a malformed TX does not stamp the crash record.

title: validate_ipv6_transport_lengths relies on caller for version check; self-check packet[0]>>4 == 6
description: P3 hardening, found by worker5 subagent correctness pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-hahk. lichen/subsys/lichen/schc/schc_helpers.c:453-472 reads packet[4..5] and packet[6] without validating packet[0]>>4 == 6; correctness depends entirely on the single caller lichen_schc_compress short-circuiting at schc.c:542 (pkt_len < IPV6_HDR_LEN || ipv6_version(packet) != 6). Python (packet.py:116-117 IPv6Header.from_bytes) and Rust (codec.rs:275 validate_full_ipv6_structure) both validate version INSIDE the validator. The guard pkt_len >= IPV6_HDR_LEN exists (:465-467, closing bead nyx7's OOB) but the version check is missing. validate_ipv6_header_chain is static with one guarded call site today, so no live bug - contract hardening so the validator is self-defending like the references. Fix: add version != 6 -> SCHC_ERR_NO_MATCHING_RULE at the top of validate_ipv6_transport_lengths; cover with a direct-call unit test in lichen/tests/schc/main.c (which also discharges the missing-test part of bead project-LICHEN-worker6-nyx7 if folded there).
close_reason: Fixed and pinned. validate_ipv6_transport_lengths (lichen/subsys/lichen/schc/schc_helpers.c) is now self-defending: version != 6 -> SCHC_ERR_NO_MATCHING_RULE immediately after the pkt_len >= IPV6_HDR_LEN guard, mirroring the internal version checks of Rust validate_full_ipv6_structure (codec.rs:272-277) and Python IPv6Header.from_bytes (packet.py:107-115). Production behavior unchanged: the sole caller lichen_schc_compress pre-gates version at schc.c:542, so the new check is unreachable-false there and the check can only make the validator stricter. Pinned by a new direct-call unit test test_validator_direct_call_self_defense in lichen/tests/schc/main.c (includes schc_internal.h; the test target already links the private include dir): (a) 4-byte truncated buffer rejects without OOB - regression guard for the latent stack read tracked by nyx7; (b) 40-byte version-4 buffer with chain-terminating NH 59 rejects - a DISCRIMINATING fixture (pre-uylk code returned SCHC_OK via the non-UDP terminal path, so a revert of the self-check fails the test; both correctness and edge reviewer passes independently converged on this fixture requirement after my initial {0x45} fixture proved vacuous - the old fixture was rejected by the ext-header chain walk regardless of the version check); (c) minimal version-6 header {[0]=0x60,[6]=59} returns SCHC_OK - over-strictness guard; (d) valid 59-byte CoAP linklocal returns SCHC_OK. Gates on heft: C host schc suite 16/16 (clang, ASan/UBSan); C schc_parity 51 vectors PASS (parity outcomes unaffected - compress-side non-IPv6 vectors reject at the pre-existing schc.c gate before the validator runs); cppcheck clean. Codereview 3x per step 4 (reviewer model): correctness kimi-k3 - one finding (vacuous version4 fixture), fixed; edge-cases kimi-k3 - same finding via mutation analysis (mutant: delete the self-check, test still passes with the old fixture - survived; new fixture kills the mutant), no others; security: claude-opus-4-5 down (err_9d442af7 - 5th opus failure today) so kimi-k3 fallback per protocol - PASS (no OOB: packet[0] read only after the length guard; stricter-only; discriminating pin confirmed; positive controls verified with an independent RFC 1071 oracle). This also lands the direct-call coverage nyx7's close was waiting on; nyx7's own OOB guard has been in place at schc_helpers.c:465-467 since the njdx-era work.

title: lichen-node rpl_stack: no Rust test asserts survey_routing_headers rejection paths (C-only coverage)
description: Observation from the security codereview pass of the scgh fixture fix (kimi-k3 review, pass 2). RxError::InvalidSourceRoute appears only in implementation code (rpl_stack/util.rs survey_routing_headers / advance_rpl_source_route), never in a Rust assertion: the Rust suite pins only the ACCEPT path plus byte-restoration. The reject directions are pinned only on the C side (lichen/tests/rpl_srh/main.c:330-360 duplicate/multicast hops; routing_dispatch -EBADMSG cases). For P-R parity add Rust mirror tests covering the rejection matrix: grid address == unspecified/multicast/==outer-dst/==source, duplicate grid addresses, segments_left > address_count, segments_left >= hop_limit, NO_NEXT followed by bytes, more than one Routing header, non-RH3 routing type, Fragment in chain, and the sender-IID forwarding-loop check in advance (next hop == authenticated sender).

comments.author: opencode-worker-7
comments.text: Coverage now exists: commit 6008e4eed8 (beads-worker-7, from xyix) adds rust/lichen-node/src/rpl_stack/tests.rs::srh_admission_vectors_match_c_router_policy consuming test/vectors/srh_admission.json - 34 C-parity cases covering every survey_routing_headers rejection path (envelope, HBH placement/uniqueness, RH3 type/alignment/reserved/grid/SL-vs-count/SL-vs-hop-limit, chain bound, truncated transport) plus in-transit/consumed admission. Ready to close as done.

title: RH3 policy shared laxity: Reserved octets 6-7 and non-canonical Hdr Ext Len unchecked in C, Python, and Rust alike
description: P3, found by worker5 subagent correctness pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-hahk. RFC 6554 s3 reserves RH3 octets 6-7 (16 bits after CmprI/CmprE/Pad) but all three implementations check only octets 4-5: C schc_helpers.c:432 (packet[offset+4]==0 && packet[offset+5]==0), Python headers.py:128 (data[2],data[3] where data = packet[offset+2:]), Rust codec.rs:301-310. A packet with nonzero Reserved octets 6-7 is accepted everywhere; functionally harmless (addresses start at octet 8; upper_destination read end-16 unaffected). Related laxity: address count uses floor division ((ext_len-8)/16 in C :436, (len(data)-6)//16 in Python :131, same in Rust :311), so a non-canonical Hdr Ext Len (e.g. HEL=3, 1 address + 8 trailing octets) is accepted with upper_destination landing on address-low-half + trailing garbage; RFC 6554 requires HEL == 2n when CmprI=CmprE=Pad=0, so HEL=3 is not expressible. Sender/receiver stay checksum-consistent (both use last-16), so this is RFC-conformance laxity, not a parity divergence. Fix needs COORDINATED changes in all three implementations plus new vectors (reserved-octets-nonzero, hel-non-canonical); C matches the references exactly today so no cross-impl break - decide whether njdx's canonical policy intended full Reserved-zero and tighten everywhere or document the shared laxity.

title: SOS origin sequence tracker LRU eviction reopens the replay window (amplifier of 2m0f); pin the active alert's origin entry
description: Found by security codereview pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-r7hs (P3, amplifier of 2m0f - fold into 2m0f's fix scope or fix together). python/src/lichen/coap/resources/sos_origin.py OriginSequenceTracker (:191-204) is an OrderedDict max_origins=256 with popitem(last=False) eviction. Entries are insertable by UNAUTHENTICATED sources: an attacker generates a fresh keypair, picks from_hex = own IID (self-consistent, passes the :219-224 binding), signs a self-addressed activate, and the fresh source key has a fresh rate budget (per-source at :263) and no tracker entry (vacuous gate per 2m0f), so accept() at emergency.py:272 inserts. 256 such inserts evict the REAL active origin's high-water entry; then a single captured legitimate origin activate (broadcast, any overhearing node has it) replays through the vacuous last_seen()=None gate and re-animates a ghost SOS alert (false emergency display/relay). Attack cost: 256 cheap self-signed POSTs + one captured broadcast. Fix direction: when fixing 2m0f, do NOT simply reject unseen origins - that would strand the legit origin after eviction; instead pin the active alert's origin entry against eviction (refresh/LRU-touch on each accept or explicit pin while self._active), and consider unauthenticated-insert hardening (e.g. only tracker-accept after envelope validation succeeds, which accept already is - the issue is eviction, not insert). Pin with a test: flood 256 fresh origins while an alert is active, then replay the captured activate and assert 4.01.

title: SOS POST cancel path has no rate limiting; spec 18.4.1 rate table covers all SOS types
description: Found by security codereview pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-r7hs (P3). python/src/lichen/coap/resources/emergency.py _cancel_from_body (:277-308) calls neither evaluate_rate_limit nor _record_request, while the activate path does (evaluate :263, 4.29+retry_after :265-271, record :273). spec/12-apps.md:560-573 (18.4.1) defines the per-source SOS rate table (600s cooldown, 3/hour, burst 2) for SOS messages generally, and 18.4.2 (:597-619) classifies cancel as an SOS type - so cancel is currently a spec deviation. Mitigations verified: when idle the handler short-circuits 4.04 before any parsing (:283-284); when active, bounded CBOR decode (4096B/1024 items/depth 16) + envelope shape checks + _pubkey_to_iid sha512 all run BEFORE the Schnorr48 verify, so garbage floods are cheap and there is no unbounded-work or memory-growth path (cancel never touches _request_times; ikcx leak is activate-side). Residual impact: unthrottled response generation (one 4.01/4.04 per request) and spec non-compliance. Fix: either apply the same evaluate_rate_limit/_record_request pair keyed by the active origin's source_key (but keep legitimate cancel un-blockable - e.g. exempt the valid-originator cancel from the budget while still recording it), or add a cheap pre-filter counter; decide semantics, then mirror in render_delete (which is likewise unthrottled) and pin with a test asserting rate-budget neutrality for a valid cancel (overlaps snh1's neutrality assertion - coordinate).

title: announce_store: corrupt state records permanently consume durable capacity slots
description: Found by edge-cases codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-t8ox (P3). rust/lichen-node/src/announce_store.rs:425-443 (name filter at 438): count_durable_state_records is name-based, so a state record that fails seal verification or the length check (234, 251) still consumes a durable slot forever: load() -> Corrupt, accept() -> Corrupt (via load), and there is deliberately no removal API. 64 such files wedge the store Full for new pins permanently; recovery is only manual file deletion + reopen (recount). Conservative by design (never undercounts) but the recount skews above the number of SERVABLE records with no quarantine or self-heal path. Requires local filesystem write access to trigger (which also permits worse), so low severity. Fix direction when picked up: on load() Corrupt, either quarantine-rename the offending file (e.g. dot-prefix, excluded by the recount filter) or subtract a per-open tally of load-failed records from the capacity gate - quarantine is the simpler fail-safe (record is unforgeable-sealed garbage either way).

title: gateway oscore stores: corrupt (not missing) record permanently bricks the context - heal covers only missing records
description: Found by 3x codereview of the recipient-store heal (9liz), robustness pass. FileStorage::write is atomic (0600 exclusive temp, fsync, verify, rename, dir fsync - lichen-hal/src/storage.rs:536-558), so torn records are only reachable via external causes (bitrot, tampering, hand-planted files). A corrupt state or floor record makes read() return Err(Corrupt) (gateway.rs:361-362) which propagates out of load() before the match arms: the heal handles MISSING records (state without floor / floor lag), never corrupt ones. A context with a bitrotted floor is Err(Corrupt) on every call forever (fail-closed, no security issue; availability trade-off only). Decide the intended policy: keep fail-closed-by-design (document it) vs add a bounded recovery path (e.g. corrupt floor + valid state heals like the missing-floor arm, since the seal is unforgeable; corrupt state + valid floor stays fatal). If healing corrupt floors, the same-highest window-bit argument still requires copying the exact sealed state.

title: gateway oscore recipient store: deleting BOTH state and floor files resets the replay window (dual-FS compromise residual)
description: Found by 3x codereview of the recipient-store heal (9liz), security pass. gateway.rs:447-458: (None,None) is interpreted as 'never seen' and returns empty, so an attacker who deletes both recipient-<hex> (state FS) and recipient-<hex>-floor (floor FS) for a previously-initialized context resets the replay window; subsequent genuine captured ciphertexts are accepted in ascending PIV order (capture-history replay incl. re-executable GCP commands). Every PARTIAL attack fails closed (delete state only -> Corrupt; stale state vs floor -> Corrupt; swaps/forges/truncates -> Corrupt; heal cannot elevate trust). Production requires the floor root on a different filesystem (verify_independent_rollback_root dev() check, lichend.rs:1408-1425), so full reset needs compromise of two independent rollback domains - the inherent limit of software-only anti-rollback (no monotonic counter), RFC 8613 s7.5-class residual. Action: document the residual explicitly in the threat-model section of the gateway docs; consider optionally recording a 'context ever-initialized' tombstone on the floor FS so single-FS deletion plus independent-FS state deletion cannot recreate the (None,None) fresh appearance.

title: gateway recipient store: no test for the (newer state, stale floor) heal branch nor same-highest window-bit rollback
description: Found by 3x codereview of the recipient-store heal (9liz). Both gateway tests simulate the crash by DELETING the floor (gateway.rs:1996-2001, 2044), but with state-then-floor write ordering and atomic FileStorage writes, the realistic crash artifact for accept N>1 is a floor present but stale at N-1 - handled by the state != floor rewrite arm (~469-472), exercised by no gateway test. Same-highest/fewer-window-bit rollback detection (the reason the heal must copy the full 13-byte state, not just highest; precedes() third clause ~426-432) is also untested. The announce store pins exactly this (store_rejects_state_rollback_and_heals_floor_lag, announce_store.rs:666-686). Implementation appears correct by inspection; add the missing test to pin the contract. Mirror the announce store test.

title: Rust tunnel_auth claim-selection and last_now high-water semantics diverge from Python (P3 pair)
description: Found by 3x codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-0rep (P3 pair, same file). (1) Selection: rust/lichen-gateway/src/tunnel_auth.rs:385-399 authorize_decapsulation takes the FIRST matching entry in scan order; Python python/src/lichen/gateway/tunnel_auth.py:545 selects the longest-prefix match. With overlapping prefixes covering one inner source, both permit, but WHICH claim governs (and thus whose expiry is enforced) can differ between Rust and Python. Fix: mirror Python longest-prefix selection (tie-break deterministically, e.g. lexicographic route_hash), pin with a unit test with two overlapping-prefix claims where expiry differs. (2) High-water time: Python updates _last_now even when the subsequent check denies (tunnel_auth.py:413 - _observe_time runs before the policy checks and sets the high-water on every authenticated attempt); Rust sets last_now only on success (tunnel_auth.rs:361, :415). Under interleaved denied traffic the rollback-detection boundary diverges: Python treats a denied attempt at time T as advancing the high-water (a later attempt below T rolls back), Rust does not. Fix direction: decide the intended semantics (advancing high-water on denied attempts prevents rollback masked by expected-denial traffic; NOT advancing avoids letting unauthenticated-ish failed attempts DoS the clock), then align both implementations and pin with mirrored tests. Note (2) interacts with the rollback-wipes-floors bead; land that one first. Both are cross-impl parity violations per the identical-output rule.

title: announce_store: separate-root anti-rollback rationale unenforced; identical roots accepted
description: Found by security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-t8ox (P3). rust/lichen-node/src/announce_store.rs:157-158 (rationale) vs 169-173 (no validation): the doc justifies separate state/floor roots with 'a rollback snapshot cannot silently rewind both sides', but persistent() never rejects state_root == floor_root (even canonically equal paths) and does not name the same-snapshot-boundary residual risk. If both roots live on one filesystem (natural operator default), a whole-fs snapshot restore rewinds state and floor as a consistent sealed pair; load() sees no precedes() violation and serves the restored floor, silently reopening a replay window for every sequence in (restored_floor, last_seen] until origins advance. True anti-rollback needs a monotonic counter (out of scope here); minimum fix: reject canonically-equal roots in persistent() and document the same-snapshot-boundary residual risk in the module doc.

title: beads-loop driver robustness gaps (heft generation)
description: Residual findings from 3x codereview of .opencode/plugins/beads-loop.tsx (fleet debug-trace round, 2026-08-30; fixed inline: Bun.appendSync nonexistent -> node:fs appendFileSync; bd failure returned 0 -> false 'queue drained' success, now -1 + error report). NOT fixed, pre-existing driver design: (1) no retry timer on skip/fail paths — if a round fails or completes under MIN_ROUND_INTERVAL_MS, next session.idle hits the min-interval guard and the loop silently stalls until external stimulus (trace shows this); (2) no timeout on the Bun.spawn bd-ready subprocess — a hung bd wedges running=true forever; (3) OPENCODE_BEADS_LOOP=0 or negative parses to worker 1 / short delays instead of refusing to activate; (4) drained path has no latch, re-toasts 'queue drained' on every idle; (5) appendPrompt can concatenate onto a partially typed user draft if a worker TUI is driven interactively. Relevant for the heft migration relaunch of the driver (bead bywc plugin, launch-beads-workers.sh).
notes: Addendum from re-review round: (6) trace file path is $HOME/Developer/fleet-debug.log — silently no-ops (catch{}) when ~/Developer does not exist, e.g. generic Linux hosts; homedir() fallback added, but a tmpdir fallback or one-time 'tracing disabled' report remains open. Also: sequential stdout->stderr pipe drain is a latent deadlock pattern reviewers assessed as unreachable for bd-ready output sizes (left as-is).

title: Fix recipient store load() doc: scope heal to first-accept window and note state-record trust
description: Found by correctness+robustness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-9liz; both findings target the same doc comment on GatewayOscoreRecipientStore::load (rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:436-438). (1) Robustness P3: the doc says the missing-floor heal covers 'crash window between the state and floor writes' without the first-accept qualifier - for a non-first accept the prior floor is still on disk in that window, so a crash there yields (Some, Some) healed by the pre-existing lag arm; only the first accept (no prior floor) yields (Some, None). The sibling sender-store doc was already scoped to 'first-accept crash window' and the new test comment is correctly scoped; only the load() doc carries the residue. (2) Correctness P2 (residual-risk note on the accepted design, agreed dominated by pre-existing strictly-worse paths: delete-both gives an uninitialized state where every sequence replays): the heal trusts the sealed state record alone when the floor is absent - an actor who can write the state root and delete the floor file gets one older sealed state accepted as the new floor with no precedes check. Add one sentence to the doc noting the heal trusts the state record alone under the seal threat model, matching the announce_store/sender-store rationale wording.

title: Gateway sender-store exhausted-flag arms have zero test coverage
description: Found by correctness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-lynw. rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs: all sender-store test states use exhausted: false. The exhaustion-regression rejection in sender_state_precedes (state (exhausted: false, low seq) vs floor (MAX, exhausted: true) must be Err(Corrupt), :253) and the terminal heal (floor := (MAX, true)) are logically verified correct by review but exercised by no test. Review confirmed the dangerous incomparable input is unproducible with current callers (exhausted implies next_sequence == u64::MAX, oscore lib.rs:655-663, validated at context.rs:322-324), but the exhausted flag is load-bearing for floor ordering and deserves a small test per the repo test-vector discipline. Fix: add a test that (a) loads a floor (MAX, exhausted) against a restored non-exhausted lower-seq state record and asserts Err(Corrupt), and (b) exercises the heal arm with a terminal (MAX, exhausted) state.

title: Gateway sender-store crash-window test comment overstates the simulated scenario
description: Found by correctness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-lynw. rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:1845-1848 (test oscore_sender_store_heals_first_accept_crash_window): the comment says the test simulates the crash between the writes of the FIRST-ever accept, but the test actually performs two fully successful compare_exchange calls (:1881-1886) and then deletes the floor - the on-disk shape of a crash between the writes of the SECOND accept. Branch coverage is unaffected (the (Some, None) heal is value-independent), but the comment and test name overstate what is simulated. Fix: reword the comment to say it reproduces the (Some(state), None) crash artifact shape, or actually simulate the first-accept window (single CAS then floor delete).

title: Dead test helper write_record_raw in gateway tests; raw writes bypass 0600 helper
description: Found by correctness+robustness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-lynw. rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:1714-1721: write_record_raw (writes with 0600 like hardened FileStorage) has zero call sites and cargo check --tests emits a dead_code warning that fails a clippy -D warnings gate. The tamper/rollback tests and the new first-accept-crash test use bare std::fs::write (:1789, :1799, :1807, :1899, :1907); this only works because each write truncates a pre-existing 0600 file in place (mode preserved on the inode). A future raw write to a NEW path would create a 0644 file that FileStorage::read rejects with Err(Io) instead of the expected Err(Corrupt), silently changing asserted failure modes. The sibling announce_store.rs routes all raw record writes through its write_record_raw helper (announce_store.rs:360-367). Fix: either delete the helper or route all raw record writes through it, matching announce_store.

title: pinned_pubkeys_snapshot lacks the durable fallback; DAO signer fallback diverges from indexed pin lookup after restart
description: Found by robustness review of project-LICHEN-worker6-dowx. pinned_pubkey_for (announce.rs:287-302) now consults the durable store on memory miss, but pinned_pubkeys_snapshot (announce.rs:310-325) is still memory-only. node.rs resolve_dao_signer_from_bounded_snapshot (384-391) uses the indexed lookup first and the snapshot only when it misses; after restart or in-memory eviction a durably-pinned key is authoritative in the indexed view yet invisible to the snapshot, so a DAO that the fallback should resolve returns UnknownKey. Fails closed (no wrong accept) - consistency gap only. Either give the snapshot a bounded durable-scan path or document that fallback resolution is memory-only.

title: Persist-first announce commit burns a sequence number on relay failure for persistent stores
description: Found by correctness+robustness review of project-LICHEN-worker6-dowx. In rpl_stack/receive.rs process_announce (376-407) the staged clone shares the durable store via Rc<RefCell>; staged.process() commits pin+floor before relay (announce.rs persist-first block). If send_l2_payload_to fails, self.announces = staged is skipped but the durable floor is already at seq N; the originator's same-seq retry (the invariant enshrined by failed_announce_relay_can_retry_same_origin_sequence, rpl_stack/tests.rs:753) then hits !seq_gt(N,N) -> StaleSeqNum and receive.rs forget_peer. Ephemeral processors (AnnounceProcessor::new) keep the old retry contract because is_persistent() skips the store, so the tested behavior and persistent-gateway behavior silently diverge. Bounded (next periodic announce advances seq; matches GCP-6.5's 'surviving cached value forces the legitimate sender to increment') but on lossy LoRa relay failures are routine. Decide: document the divergence, or add equal-seq idempotent retransmission for the durable floor (requires replay-amplification analysis since hop_count is unsigned).

title: C validate_ipv6_transport_lengths reads packet[4..5] before any pkt_len >= 40 check (latent OOB, unreachable via public API)
description: Confirmed by ASan during the robustness codereview pass of project-LICHEN-worker6-njdx. lichen/subsys/lichen/schc/schc_helpers.c:440-441 reads the payload-length field via ipv6_payload_len (read_be16, schc_helpers.c:82/100) and computes pkt_len - IPV6_HDR_LEN before any pkt_len >= IPV6_HDR_LEN guard: a direct call with pkt_len=4 triggers a stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 1. Unreachable in production (the only caller lichen_schc_compress guards pkt_len < IPV6_HDR_LEN at schc.c:542), but the validator should be self-defending. Fix: add a pkt_len < IPV6_HDR_LEN guard at the top of validate_ipv6_transport_lengths; cover with a direct-call unit test in the host C suite.

title: SOS rate limiter leaks memory for one-shot sources
description: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/emergency.py:102-121/137/165-172 (pre-existing, found during r7hs review): _prune_old_requests only runs inside evaluate_rate_limit for the source currently being evaluated and deletes an entry only when that source's own timestamps age out AND it queries again. An attacker generating fresh keypairs (one activation each; first request always passes) grows _request_times/_period_start unboundedly on a long-lived node. Add global pruning (periodic sweep or size cap with LRU eviction).

title: Non-string or variant SOS type values fall through and activate
description: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/emergency.py:213-216: the cancel branch matches body['type'] == 'cancel' exactly. A bytes-typed CBOR type (b'cancel' != 'cancel', verified) or variant token ('Cancel') falls through the pass into the ACTIVATION path, so a properly-signed cancel with a mis-encoded type returns CREATED and activates. Security-neutral today (signature must verify over that exact core, so only the originator's own mis-encoding is affected; C parity: sos_alert.c:403-410 uses exact strcmp). Fix: strict-type the branch (isinstance str) and/or whitelist activation types {sos, medical, security, fire} and reject unknown types with 4.00 instead of silently reinterpreting.

title: POST-cancel tests pin only internals; wire state and observe notification unasserted
description: python/tests/coap/test_sos_resource.py:285-304 (test_post_cancel_cancels_sos): after POST-cancel the test only checks sos._active; it never GETs /sos to pin the wire state {active: false, from: null, t: null} nor checks an Observe notification. A regression in cancel() (emergency.py:184-190) that cleared _active but left stale _from/_t or skipped updated_state() would pass. Follow TestSosGet/TestSosObserve conventions.

title: SOS replay gate is vacuous when the active origin has no sequence-tracker entry
description: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/emergency.py:303-305 (_cancel_from_body) and the render_delete counterpart: a captured-but-undelivered valid cancel envelope replays successfully when last_seen(source_key) is None. That happens when the alert was activated via a direct activate() call (no seq recorded) or when the 256-entry LRU in OriginSequenceTracker (sos_origin.py:202-203) evicts the active origin under a flood of distinct-origin activations. Gate on the activation-time sequence being known, or record it at activate() time.

title: rx workqueue robustness residue: unbounded deinit flush on wedged handler, loopback deaf-window divergence, disarm -EINVAL noise
description: Residual P2/P3 findings from 3x codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-sb0b (main items fixed in bead; these deferred). (1) deinit() ABORTED path calls lora_l2_rx_stop() whose k_work_flush_delayable can block forever if a wedged lichen_l2_input holds rx_mutex (old code had a bounded thread join); consider k_work_cancel_delayable_sync with a timeout or bounded flush. (2) Loopback driver deliver-on-arm models a radio that listened while disarmed; a real disarmed radio receives nothing - burst-TX windows rely on this on loopback but diverge from production; once real drivers implement one-shot recv_async (0l5j) re-evaluate whether deliver-on-arm should stay test-only with a loud comment. (3) On sx12xx-style drivers lora_recv_async(dev,NULL) when not receiving returns -EINVAL -> spurious 'disarm failed' warning; the rx_armed flag in sb0b's lora_l2_rx.c skips the call when unarmed, but the log path should also distinguish not-armed from real failure once real drivers exist. (4) COAP_CLIENT_THREAD_PRIORITY=14 override in ping_l2/coap_client tests silently breaks if NUM_PREEMPT_PRIORITIES ever drops below 15 - assert-guarded only at boot.

title: Rename stale test store_fails_closed_when_exactly_one_side_is_present
description: Found by correctness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-s6ml. announce_store.rs:466: since the s6ml fix, the second half of this test (:488-494) asserts the OPPOSITE of fail-closed for (Some, None) - it asserts load heals the floor forward. Assertions are correct; only the name misdescribes the now-asymmetric contract (missing state fails closed, missing floor heals). Rename to reflect the asymmetric contract, e.g. store_fails_closed_on_missing_state_and_heals_missing_floor.

title: unique_roots does not clear stale test dirs; pid reuse can resurrect state
description: Found by robustness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-s6ml. announce_store.rs:347-357: unique_roots builds temp paths from a per-process counter plus pid but never clears pre-existing directories; a crashed prior run whose pid was reused can leave pre-populated records that spuriously fail tests like store_survives_restart_and_enforces_durable_floor (flaky failure, not a false pass). Panic-leaked dirs share the same root cause. Fix: remove_dir_all before create_dir_all in unique_roots, or add a random component to the path.

title: accept() partial floor-write failure leaves cache behind disk state
description: Found by robustness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-s6ml. Pre-existing, safe direction: if write(state) succeeds and write(floor) fails in accept (announce_store.rs:312-313), accept returns Err(Io) and the in-memory cache keeps the older floor while disk state advanced; a replay of the already-accepted announce can then be re-accepted in-process via the cache hit (:301-307) with the stale lower floor. Never permits durable rollback (disk heals forward on next load), but it is the one cache/disk divergence the heal design permits. Fix: document the divergence in the accept() doc comment, or on floor-write Io failure re-read disk and refresh the cache entry.

title: Add test for heal-failure Err(Io) retry idempotency in announce_store load
description: Found by robustness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-s6ml. The fix relies on a failed heal write (announce_store.rs:273) leaving (Some(state), None) on disk and the next load retrying the heal successfully, but no test covers this and FileStorage has no fault-injection seam (unlike MemStorage fail_after_writes at lichen-hal/src/storage.rs:443). The retry is byte-idempotent only because Schnorr48 signing is deterministic (schnorr.rs:3, determinism test at :637). Fix: add a fault-injection seam to FileStorage or simulate via a raw unwritable floor path, then assert first load returns Err(Io) with floor still absent and second load heals to Ok(Some(state)) with identical record bytes.

title: persistent() should reject state_root == floor_root to enforce separate-roots invariant
description: Found by security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-s6ml. AnnounceTrustStore::persistent (announce_store.rs:121-136) accepts identical or nested state_root/floor_root without complaint, while the anti-rollback story (module doc :10-13) and the heal safety rationale lean on the caller passing distinct roots; a single-snapshot rewind of a shared root loads fine today. The existing test at :683 even passes the same path twice. Hardening: in persistent(), reject state_root == floor_root (and ideally a prefix/nesting check) with Err(Io) or a new error variant, and fix the affected test to pass distinct roots.

title: Awaitable tests assume lazy task factory (single sleep(0) tick)
description: python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:750, 780: a single 'await asyncio.sleep(0)' makes task.cancelled() True deterministically under the default lazy task factory (mutant-verified on CPython 3.11/3.14), but silently breaks under loop.set_task_factory(asyncio.eager_task_factory) (3.12+ opt-in): probe shows cancelled()=False, ran=[1] — the body runs eagerly and cancellation lands differently. Use a bounded drain loop (e.g. up to 10 ticks until task.cancelled()) in both tests to absorb task-factory and multi-tick delivery assumptions at zero cost.

title: Future done-callbacks run after rejection — residual channel needs scoping decision
description: python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:709-710, 721-722 + python/src/lichen/_sync_callbacks.py:26-27: a hook may attach add_done_callback to a Future before returning it; Future.cancel() synchronously schedules those callbacks to run on the NEXT loop iteration, so attacker code can still execute after the rejection raises. reject_awaitable_result cannot prevent this for Futures. Neither the tests nor the bead threat model covers or documents this residual channel — file a scoping decision (document as accepted residual in the helper docstring, or restrict hook results to Task/coroutine/custom). Needs a human/spec decision, not a blind fix.

title: LICHEN_COAP_SERVER_OSCORE help names coap_oscore_unprotect_resource_request; rename reference when authorize_mutating lands
description: lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/Kconfig:91 MUTATING-REQUEST GATE paragraph names coap_oscore_unprotect_resource_request (the current low-level helper). Bead project-LICHEN-worker6-2z8e ports coap_oscore_authorize_mutating from draft 02a8ee28fd and siblings migrate handlers to it; once that lands the Kconfig header names the wrong function. Update the name (semantics text already matches the mandated preserved behavior: EUI-64 ctx lookup, admin fallback, 4.01) in the same series as 2z8e or as immediate follow-up.

comments.author: opencode-worker-4
comments.text: Blocked-by: project-LICHEN-worker6-2z8e (update the gate-function name in the same series that lands coap_oscore_authorize_mutating).

title: Kconfig security-doc accuracy: LICHEN_COAP_KEYS claims BLE admin but code enforces SLIP; LICHEN_COAP_CLIENT_OSCORE cites wrong spec section
description: Two pre-existing doc-accuracy defects in lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/Kconfig, found during 3x codereview of worker6-1jl1: (1) :252-253 LICHEN_COAP_KEYS SECURITY note says write ops require 'local admin access (loopback or BLE LCI interface)' but lichen_coap_is_local_admin (coap_keys.c:51-98) checks the SLIP LCI interface via slip_transport_iface_get(); the same file's depends-comment (:213-218) correctly says SLIP. (2) :42-44 LICHEN_COAP_CLIENT_OSCORE cites 'spec/06-security.md Section 8.7' for the OSCORE-for-all-traffic recommendation; 8.7 is Key Management - the recommendation is Section 15.6 (spec/06-security.md:1271-1274). The SERVER_OSCORE citation was fixed in worker6-1jl1; the client one remains.

title: Rust encode_rule255 reports profile-ceiling overflow as retryable-looking BufferTooSmall
description: Confirmed empirically (discovered-from project-LICHEN-worker6-xuc8, robustness pass). encode_rule255 (rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs:1415-1422) checks needed > single_frame_limit.min(SCHC_FRAG_MAX_PACKET_SIZE) before consulting out.len() and returns BufferTooSmall::new(needed, profile_limit). Probe: raw 22554-byte nonzero-TC packet -> BufferTooSmall{required:22555, provided:22554} regardless of actual out capacity, so a grow-and-retry caller loop never terminates. Python raises unambiguous SchcError 'Rule 255 raw IPv6 packet exceeds 22553 bytes' (python/src/lichen/schc/headers.py:146-147). Both fatal; only the error classification differs. Fix: return a terminal profile-limit SchcError::InvalidPacket (or dedicated variant) when needed exceeds the profile ceiling, reserving BufferTooSmall for genuinely too-small caller buffers.

title: Adopt shared coap_oscore_authorize_mutating helper from 6mij.2.4 draft
description: Child of worker6-l9hb decomposition. Port the shared authorize helper from draft commit 02a8ee28fd (coap_oscore.c: coap_oscore_send_protected + coap_oscore_authorize_mutating; header decls) onto the current diverged branch. Apply open review findings in the same change: worker6-fmee (plain_buf may be NULL per doc but is unconditionally dereferenced in unprotect path - either guard with a bounded static dummy or make doc/annotation require non-NULL and validate), worker6-2m4y (respond path uses 1KB+ stack buf[CONFIG_COAP_SERVER_MESSAGE_SIZE]; use static, matching project pattern). Preserve the draft's semantics: OSCORE verify by EUI64 ctx lookup (coap_oscore.c:54-84), admin fallback when unprotected or OSCORE disabled, 4.01/4.03 responds, payload publication. VERIFY: lichen/tests/coap_lci_auth + coap_oscore_fallback on native_sim (Linux-only; requires EC2 Zephyr builder per AGENTS.md - native_sim is unreliable on macOS). Do NOT migrate handlers in this bead; sibling children do.

title: Pin raw_sample_diagnostic read-only contract (eager-invalidation pin depends on it)
description: python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:958 + python/src/lichen/timing/stratum.py:422-424: the zzw5 eager-invalidation pin rests entirely on raw_sample_diagnostic()'s read-only contract, and that test is its ONLY consumer in the suite. A future regression that makes the diagnostic revalidate (lazy clear) would pass line 958 while eager invalidation is silently lost. Fix: add one assert that a raw read on a live tracker does not change last_rejection_reason or state (pins the contract directly).

title: Floor-raise tests never adopt a post-clear sample (over-broad invalidation undetected)
description: python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:943-960 (zzw5 strengthening): each loop iteration ends without adopting a sample issued AFTER the clear, so an over-broad invalidation passes: verified mutant _clear_locked (stratum.py:438-439) setting __issuance_high_water[authority] = 2**63 (bricking the authority forever) passes all assertions, since the pre-clear candidate (seq 2) is rejected with the pinned reason either way. Fix: end each iteration with 'assert state.adopt(gnss(authority, FLOOR + 30))' (fresh issuance, above new floor) is True.

title: Raw TxQueue mutators are publicly reachable, unsynchronized, and uncontracted
description: tx_queue.py:401-429 pop/confirm_transmitted, tx_queue.py:587-599 signal_all_pending, tx_queue.py:294/98 public push(return_reservation=True), and LinkLayer.tx_queue is a public field (link_layer.py:186). Any in-process component holding the link instance can (i) tx_queue.push(raw)+drain_tx_queue() to put unsigned frames on air bypassing signing; (ii) signal_all_pending(True) to fake on-air success while dropping every queued frame; (iii) pop()/confirm_transmitted() remove the head without resolving the attached reservation, hanging the awaiting send() caller forever; (iv) a directly-pushed reservation can strand if no later queue op runs (wait() has no timeout), and a drain cancelled mid-CAD-backoff (link_layer.py:1457) is the one exit that cleans only the caller's own reservation. No remote path reaches the queue (all LinkLayer-internal use is under _tx_lock); this is local-misuse hardening. Fix: privatize or owner-token-gate the raw mutators (mirror _replay_owner_token pattern), document the reservation-resolution contract, and clean unresolved reservations on the CAD-cancellation exit. Found by security+correctness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-9qpz.

title: clear()/signal_all_pending leave packet drops unaccounted in TxQueueStats
description: tx_queue.py:488-492: clear() -> signal_all_pending(False) removes N entries and resolves their reservations False but increments none of packets_dropped_deadline/preempt/full, so the CAD-terminal path (link_layer.py:1466), the radio-exception path (link_layer.py:1475), and the on_persistence_failure eviction (link_layer.py:2108) silently shrink the queue. The operator invariant packets_queued ~ transmitted + dropped no longer holds after any CAD-busy episode, masking loss when diagnosing congestion/failure modes. No hang or corruption - observability only. Fix: count removals in clear()/signal_all_pending under a dropped-other bucket (or reuse an existing counter deliberately). Distinct from project-LICHEN-worker6-m01y (silent-clear semantics) and project-LICHEN-lllg (stats += atomicity). Found by robustness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-9qpz.

title: TxQueue.complete() removes by value-equality instead of entry identity
description: tx_queue.py:523: self._entries.remove(entry) deletes the first value-equal TxQueueEntry (plain @dataclass __eq__), not necessarily the reserved object. fail() (567) and cancel_reservation() (579) already use identity; complete() is the one inconsistent site. Unreachable today (complete is only called on the reserved head while the queue cannot mutate under _tx_lock), but a byte-identical entry pushed to the head while a twin is in flight (lock-bypassing push, same-ms enqueue_time_ms) would remove the wrong object and leave the stale twin eligible to re-reserve -> duplicate transmission. Fix: identity scan (e.g. next(i for i,e in enumerate(self._entries) if e is entry)) mirroring fail()/cancel_reservation(). Related: project-LICHEN-worker6-gwpt. Found by correctness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-9qpz.

title: restore_state() bypasses _sequence_started rewind guard and can reuse a tuple
description: link_layer.py:2093-2095 -> 2024-2027: set_sequence() refuses to rewind after first use (_sequence_started guard, RuntimeError at 1927-1928), but _restore_security_state overwrites _epoch/_seqnum unconditionally, taking neither _tx_lock nor the guard. A mid-operation restore rewinds the counter so two legitimately signed frames share one (epoch, seqnum) with different payloads; peer replay windows accept at most one sighting and drop the other (availability loss, no forgery). Fix: apply the same _sequence_started refusal (and take _tx_lock) on the restore path, matching set_sequence(). Found by security codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-9qpz.

title: DIO repeated-verify test pins replay barrier only via rejection reason string
description: In python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py test_repeated_dio_time_verify_same_counter_rejected (~line 468), the boolean 'assert not state.consider(option, sample=second)' is satisfiable by an insecure implementation: the first consider() adopted a sample with the same observed_monotonic (both verifies read the same detached.received_monotonic, time_sync.py:444), so _adopt_claimed_locked's stale-or-duplicate check (stratum.py:678-679) rejects even if the entire network replay barrier were deleted. Only the exact 'network-replay-counter-not-new' reason assertion discriminates. Strengthen the pin (e.g. assert the reason, or make the second verify use a fresh receipt time).

title: Announce store cache left stale after partial accept write failure
description: announce_store.rs accept() inserts the cache entry only after BOTH writes succeed (state then floor). If the floor write fails after the state write succeeded, accept returns Err but durable state now holds next while the cache keeps the old value; for an already-cached originator subsequent load() calls short-circuit on the cache and never re-consult disk, so monotonicity is enforced against the lower cached floor until restart and a seq in (old, next) can overwrite durable state with a lower-but-still-forward value. No pin change, durable floor never drops below old floor (liveness/consistency-of-cache only). Fix: insert the cache entry immediately after the state write succeeds — state-first is the commit point. Found by correctness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-12zy.

title: lichend open federation mode (GCP-3.2) has no enrollment path
description: Found in 3x codereview of w0fp. Gateway::admit_gateway (rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:960-980) implements TOFU proof-of-poskey admission, but no lichend daemon config or runtime endpoint invokes it — only unit tests (gateway.rs:1951-1954). mode=open in TOML therefore unconditionally errors at startup (lichend.rs:511-514) with no way to ever enroll; deploy/lichend.toml.example documents this refusal. Implement a spec GCP-3.2 enrollment surface (daemon config trust anchors and/or a runtime CoAP enrollment resource behind existing authz), keeping the no-plaintext-fallback guarantee, and update the example docs once reachable.

title: lichend TOML config silently ignores unknown keys (no deny_unknown_fields)
description: Found in 3x codereview of w0fp (robustness pass). Config structs in rust/lichen-gateway/src/config.rs (Config:14-30, GatewayCoordinationConfig:43-61, SecurityConfig:33-40) use #[serde(default)] without deny_unknown_fields, so a typo'd key such as master_salt (instead of master_salt_hex) or rollback_floor is silently dropped. Worst case: mode=psk starts without the intended master salt, deriving different per-peer OSCORE contexts than every other federation member (silent interop outage, fail-open-ish); misspelled psk_hex/peer_public_keys do fail closed via EmptyPeers/missing-psk. Add #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] to the public config structs (verify no existing deployment TOMLs rely on extra keys) and add a regression test that an unknown key under [gateway_coordination]/[security] is rejected. Related docs already shipped in deploy/lichend.toml.example.

title: spec: Bound waypoint storage
description:
Waypoint/route resources have no storage limits.

Fix: Add to 12-apps.md Section 18.3:

Ref: worker6-h4pl

title: spec: Reserve capability table portion for egress nodes
description:
LRU eviction allows attacker to evict legitimate egress entries.

Fix: Add to 06-security.md Section 8.12:

Ref: worker6-h4pl

No rate limit on EDHOC handshake initiation.

Fix: Add to 06-security.md Section 8.9:
'Implementations SHOULD rate-limit EDHOC initiations to at most 3 concurrent per peer IID and 10 concurrent globally.'

Ref: worker6-h4pl
