title: Define claim_seq wrap semantics for floor at UINT32_MAX
description: Codereview finding (P3): lichen_slot_claim_seq_commit monotonic guard (entry->seq >= seq) plus the process_claim gate (claim_seq <= cached) mean a floor of 0xFFFFFFFF (hostile NV content or a gateway that genuinely burned max seq) permanently rejects all claims including wrapped seq 0, with no recovery short of NV wipe. Spec/08 GCP-6.5 does not define wrap. Options: spec amendment (declare wrap illegal / require new IID), or module-side recovery. Discovered from project-LICHEN-worker6-uiun 3x codereview.

title: slot_coord: register_gateway failure ignored on accept path grants invisible gateway
description: Codereview finding (P3, pre-existing, adjacent to persist-first wiring): coap_slot_coord.c:513 ignores lichen_slot_coord_register_gateway's return. When the coord table is full, a claim is committed (seq burned), ACCEPTED returned, grant handed out — but no table entry exists, so the gateway is invisible to conflict resolution and overlapping slot grants become possible. Decide: reject the claim when registration fails (return an error result) or document the accepted loss. Discovered from project-LICHEN-worker6-uiun 3x codereview.

title: Design: Implicit slot renewal via TX activity
description:
Future enhancement beyond the max-duration cap:

Slots held implicitly instead of explicit expiry claims:
- Granted on first valid claim
- Renewed automatically each time node TXes in its slot
- Revoked after M consecutive missed TXes (e.g. 3-5 superframes)

Squatter must burn real airtime to hold slot. No renewal message overhead for active nodes.

Larger protocol change - max-duration cap is the quick fix, this is proper long-term.

Ref: project-LICHEN-worker6-70p7

title: rangetest counter comment overclaims coverage: now_provider uncounted
description: 3x review P3 (jkli, bead jkli): lichen/tests/coap_rangetest/src/main.c:103 comment claims counters prove the 4.01 gate fires before 'any provider work', but only get_metrics/get_hops are counted; now_provider (time_now() in build_senml, coap_rangetest.c:669) is also a provider callback and is not counted, so a hypothetical regression calling time_now() standalone pre-gate would be missed. Fix: reword comment to 'metrics/hops provider work' (or add now_calls counter). Reviewer marked it dismissible; realistic regressions move the whole build_senml call and are caught.
close_reason: Fixed: comment now scopes the guarantee to metrics/hops provider work and documents that now_provider is only reachable via the same build_senml call the metrics counter covers. Suite re-run 13/13 PASS.

title: Mobility polish: silent cap-break time drop, jitter/center skew, ULP idle churn, degenerate-bounds ping-pong, RPGM unbounded members
description: P3 batch from 3x codereview of uory fix (mobility.py): (1) All four step() loops drop leftover sim time on the 100k-iteration cap break silently - docstrings still promise 'advance position by dt_us'; add a debug log/counter and document the cap in docstrings. (2) On cap break GroupMobility._update_jitter(dt_us) still advances jitter by FULL dt while center movement was truncated - minor clock skew between jitter glide and center motion; consider passing consumed time instead. (3) ULP absorption: when charge < ulp(remaining)/2 the subtraction is a no-op and all 100k iterations are idle churn (e.g. legs ~1e-8us with dt=1e12) - a 'remaining did not decrease -> break' check would exit in 1 iteration. (4) RandomWaypoint with degenerate bounds (min>=max, currently unvalidated) ping-pongs waypoint picks at the same point for 100k idle iterations every step; Group/RPGM strict '>' also allows 2*inset == width -> uniform(a,a) degeneracy. (5) RPGM.add_member has no group_size cap (GroupMobility does) - unbounded member list growth.
acceptance_criteria: each sub-item addressed or explicitly waived with rationale; existing sim tests stay green

title: cargo clippy -p lichen-gateway -- -D warnings fails inside dependency lichen-node (send_secure_block1, secure.rs:642)
description: cargo clippy -p lichen-gateway --all-features -- -D warnings fails inside dependency lichen-node/src/secure.rs:642: send_secure_block1 takes 8 arguments (too_many_arguments). Introduced by f20a338940 (orphaned-work checkpoint). Blocks the -D warnings gate for any crate depending on lichen-node. Fix: introduce a params struct or builder for send_secure_block1 in rust/lichen-node/src/secure.rs.

title: Supervised-failure node test can hang on unbounded entered.wait(); sibling has same gap
description: Wave-1 review (robustness, P3): python/tests/test_node.py:377 awaits entered.wait() with no timeout. If a regression makes the receive task terminate before invoking the patched link.receive (e.g. _send_expired_reassembly_aborts at node.py:808 raising a terminal-class error on first iteration), the supervisor stops the node, entered is never set, and the test hangs until job timeout with zero diagnostics. Wrap with asyncio.wait_for(entered.wait(), timeout=5) (style already used at line 390). NOTE: the pre-existing sibling test at line ~338 replicates the same pattern - same gap, same one-line fix, same file. Also (P3, same wave): test_atomic_batch_rejects_reserved_name_without_touching_other_targets asserts (st_dev, st_ino, st_mtime_ns) but omits st_ctime_ns unlike its sibling test - a chmod-only mutation would slip through; add st_ctime_ns. Discovered-from wave 1 beads project-LICHEN-worker6-wukp and project-LICHEN-worker6-blqw.
close_reason: Fixed in wave 1 follow-up: casefold guard + aliased regression, parametrize entry, fsync-ordering pin, hold-down constants, wait_for timeouts + ctime_ns. Suites green (44+178+130).

title: test_fragment TOFU hold-down boundary uses hardcoded 59.999/60.0 literals
description: Wave-1 review (correctness, P3): python/tests/schc/test_fragment.py:2412,2415 hardcode 59.999/60.0 instead of AUTHENTICATED_HOLD_DOWN_SECONDS (reassembly.py:41), which the file already imports and four sibling tests use (lines 2355, 2530, 2628, 2698). If the spec constant changes, this test fails with a confusing RxFrame-vs-ReceiveError mismatch instead of tracking the constant. Use AUTHENTICATED_HOLD_DOWN_SECONDS - 0.001 and AUTHENTICATED_HOLD_DOWN_SECONDS. Discovered-from wave 1 bead project-LICHEN-worker6-hg27.
close_reason: Fixed in wave 1 follow-up: casefold guard + aliased regression, parametrize entry, fsync-ordering pin, hold-down constants, wait_for timeouts + ctime_ns. Suites green (44+178+130).

title: atomic_json crash-rollback test does not pin dir-fsync durability ordering
description: Wave-1 review (security/robustness, P3): python/tests/test_vector_atomic_json.py:403-472 pins event ordering (rollback -> rolled_back journal -> cleanup) but cannot catch deletion of _fsync_directory(parent_fd) at test/vectors/atomic_json.py:532. Without that fsync a power-loss window leaves journal=prepared with backups already unlinked; _read_recovery_artifact_at then raises FileNotFoundError (atomic_json.py:389-390, uncaught) and permanently poisons every future write to the directory. Fix: monkeypatch _fsync_directory to record call order and assert a dir-fsync lands between the rolled_back journal write and the backup unlinks. Discovered-from wave 1 bead project-LICHEN-worker6-d7tb.
close_reason: Fixed in wave 1 follow-up: casefold guard + aliased regression, parametrize entry, fsync-ordering pin, hold-down constants, wait_for timeouts + ctime_ns. Suites green (44+178+130).

title: atomic_json prep-prefix rejection clause untested
description: Wave-1 review (security, P3): test/vectors/atomic_json.py:580 rejects targets starting with _PREPARATION_PREFIX but no batch-rejection test exercises it (parametrize at python/tests/test_vector_atomic_json.py:221-227 covers only the two exact reserved names). If that clause regresses, _recover_orphan_preparations (atomic_json.py:547-558) unconditionally deletes every prefix-named regular owned file at the start of the next batch - a committed target named .lichen-vector-prep-*.json would be silently destroyed. Add one parametrize entry. Discovered-from wave 1 bead project-LICHEN-worker6-blqw.
close_reason: Fixed in wave 1 follow-up: casefold guard + aliased regression, parametrize entry, fsync-ordering pin, hold-down constants, wait_for timeouts + ctime_ns. Suites green (44+178+130).

title: Clippy warnings on HEAD: needless_borrow lichend.rs:1140/1149, too-many-arguments secure.rs:642
description: P3 pre-existing clippy findings (not from the 2026-08-29 adoption work): lichen-gateway/src/bin/lichend.rs:1140,1149 needless_borrow on load_generation_floor(&trust_floor_path) — drop the &. lichen-node/src/secure.rs:642 send_secure_block1 has 8/7 args — group the store/state params into a struct or split the function. Repo policy runs clippy before commits; -D warnings would currently fail.

title: elect_time_master ignores has_gps gate
description: P3 (wave-5 review of worker6-hjot): rust/lichen-core/src/superframe.rs:261 elect_time_master ignores has_gps; the doc says GPS-equipped gateways 'don't participate in backbone election' but the function still elects a GPS candidate unless the caller filters. Pre-existing logic, newly visible now the module is public API. Fix: skip has_gps candidates in the election (or document caller-must-filter explicitly) + test.

title: Exercise post-restart announce send end-to-end in persistence tests
description: P3 (wave-4 review of worker6-d4wr): the two failure-injection tests in python/tests/test_node.py (~:2470/2520) restart the node and verify build_announce + receiver processing but never invoke the restarted node's _send_announce(), so the post-restart reserve -> write -> advance-at-healed-revision path is not executed end-to-end (the anchor contract is only exercised inside _load_locked). Fix: extend both tests to drive one real send after restart and assert sequence/tx outcomes.

title: Add file identity to lichend trust recovery errors and surface corrupt floor IO
description: P3 (wave-4 review of worker6-taf3): lichend.rs recover_or_provision_trust_store (~:1131-1167) error strings carried over verbatim from pre-extraction code: 'committed trust provisioning artifacts are missing' does not say WHICH artifact (store lives under state_root, floor under rollback_floor_root), and the (false,true) arm uses load_generation_floor(...).unwrap_or(u64::MAX) so a corrupt/unreadable floor file is misreported as 'orphan trust floor is not the initial generation' instead of surfacing the IO error. Fail-closed either way. Fix: name the artifact+path in each error and distinguish corrupt-floor IO from wrong-generation. Apply the same clarity to the slot path (tracked concern about its pre-gate floor write is separate).

title: Forwarder DAO parsing looser than root extract_updates: reject E=1/unknown option types or document spec blessing
description: Security review of wave: dao_parents_for_source (rust/lichen-node/src/routing/router.rs:1185-1193) ignores unknown option types, accepts E=1 external transits and inconsistent path_sequence/lifetime across transits, caps group_targets only by DAO size not MAX_DAO_UPDATES. Consequence: forwarders relay DAOs the root will reject (bounded amplification toward root) and anti-spoof parent set can include parents from transits the root would reject. No acceptance hazard (drop-only, root re-validates) but tighten for defense in depth: reject E=1 and unknown types in forwarder, or add comment citing spec section blessing the asymmetry.

title: Update fail_closed docstring: catalog-recorded deletion detection is unconditional
description: Robustness review of bidu fix: class/property docstrings (dao_persistence.py:294-305 and __init__ arg doc) promise fail_closed=False returns None on missing state for testing scenarios, but the new catalog-backed branch raises regardless of the flag (intentional, spec 8.6 requires fail closed; inline comment acknowledges). Keep behavior, update the contract docs to state deletion detection for catalog-recorded keys is unconditional.
close_reason: Updated fails_closed property docstring and __init__ fail_closed arg doc in dao_persistence.py to state that deletion/corruption detection for catalog-recorded RX keys and TX-marker-initialized stores is unconditional per spec 8.6, and fail_closed=False is a legacy testing flag that never downgrades durable-evidence-backed detection. Behavior unchanged (kept). Full dao_persistence suite passes (94 tests) plus key_persistence suite.

title: Fail-closed error mislabels corrupt slots as deleted when per-key anchor absent
description: Correctness review of bidu fix: dao_persistence.py:999 in the fail-closed path, when per-key anchor is absent (fresh anchor) and slot files are corrupt (not deleted) while a catalog entry exists, the error says 'initialized RX floor was deleted' though the condition is corruption. Behavior correctly fails closed either way; with durable anchor the message is accurate. Fix: distinguish via _any_slot_exists before choosing the message.
close_reason: load_rx_floor catalog-backed fail-closed branch now distinguishes conditions via _any_slot_exists: slot files present but invalid raise 'RX floor corrupt for pubkey ...', absent slot files raise 'initialized RX floor was deleted for pubkey ...'. Both remain unconditional per spec 8.6. Added regression test test_corrupt_rx_slots_with_catalog_entry_fail_as_corrupt using a per-key-stateless anchor; it fails against the old mislabeled message.

title: Document v1->v2 trust-store migration rotation-floor reset window (or bump transcript domain)
description: Security review of yzir fix: a rotation applied while a store persisted as v1 (no sequence field) loses its floor on migration to v2 (trust.rs:801-805), so a captured pre-migration seq-1 K1->K2 authorization can replay after restart. Speculative (unknown whether v1 stores exist in field). Fix: document the window in migration notes/spec 8.7 and advise re-pinning after v1 upgrade; if v1 stores are known to exist, bump transcript domain to ...-v2 for post-migration rotations so pre-migration signatures cannot verify. New test trust_store_legacy_v1_migrates_sequence_floor_and_blocks_replay documents current floor=0 semantics.

title: fd double-close race in _write_rx_catalog_file/_write_slot/_ensure_tx_marker exception paths
description: Robustness review of bidu fix: after os.fdopen takes ownership, an exception inside the with block closes the fd, then except BaseException calls os.close(descriptor) again. Usually suppressed EBADF, but in a multithreaded process an intervening open can recycle the fd number and close an unrelated descriptor. Fix: track ownership (opened_via_fdopen flag) and only close when not owned; apply to all three helpers. Ref dao_persistence.py:685-697, 483-496, 440-457.
close_reason: Added owned_by_stream ownership tracking to _ensure_tx_marker, _write_slot, and _write_rx_catalog_file in dao_persistence.py: the exception handler now only closes the staging descriptor when os.fdopen never took ownership, eliminating the double-close/recycled-fd race. Applied the identical fix to the same latent pattern in key_persistence.py (FileKeyStore._write_slot, TrustStorePersistence._write_json_locked) since that file is in this bead cluster. New parametrized regression test test_staging_fd_not_closed_after_fdopen_ownership verifies the handler never closes a stream-owned descriptor and fails against the old pattern (verified by temporary revert).

title: store_rx_floor: precheck catalog capacity before slot commit; align 512 cap with pin-table 10000
description: From 3-perspective review of bidu fix: store_rx_floor commits slot+anchor THEN records catalog; catalog failure (ENOSPC, anchor CAS, or capacity exceeded) is an indeterminate post-commit failure. At _MAX_RX_CATALOG_ENTRIES=512 a new origin fails permanently on store AND on every subsequent load (heal re-raises at dao_persistence.py:991->771-772) with no eviction path; recovery requires wiping base dir which resets ALL replay floors. Note 512 cap is inconsistent with _MAX_TRUST_ENTRIES=10000 (key_persistence.py:63) while _RX_CATALOG_MAX_SIZE formula already scales. Fix: pre-check capacity/anchor liveness before _write_to_older_slot_locked; raise/configure cap to match pin budget; document ENOSPC/anchor indeterminate window in store_rx_floor contract.
close_reason: store_rx_floor now pre-checks catalog capacity and anchor liveness BEFORE _write_to_older_slot_locked: a new origin at catalog capacity, or a catalog whose anchored revision cannot be validated (lost/rotated anchor), fails deterministically with no slot artifacts written, instead of the old indeterminate post-commit failure. _MAX_RX_CATALOG_ENTRIES raised 512 -> 10000, aligned with the _MAX_TRUST_ENTRIES=10000 pin-table budget in key_persistence.py (the _RX_CATALOG_MAX_SIZE formula scales automatically). store_rx_floor contract now documents the commit order, the deterministic pre-check failures, and the residual ENOSPC/anchor-CAS indeterminate window after the slot commit (committed floor stays effective; loads heal the catalog from it or fail closed preserving the floor; no replay window re-opens). New tests: capacity pre-check rejects before slot commit while existing origins keep updating at capacity; anchor-liveness pre-check rejects before slot commit; both verified to fail against the old code via temporary revert. Existing 512-entry catalogs remain valid under the raised cap.

title: Give StagedPrivateSeed a Drop that removes unpublished staging files
description: P3 (wave-3 review of worker6-xyk3): lichend.rs StagedPrivateSeed has no Drop; a caller that stages but never publish()es leaks the 0600 temp seed file. Production path is stage->publish back-to-back (latent), and a post-link failure also returns Err though the seed was published (fail-closed, acceptable). Fix: implement Drop to unlink the staging path if still unpublished, and document the post-link Err-on-sync-failure semantics.

title: Sweep crash-orphaned staged seed temp files at lichend boot
description: P3, pre-existing (wave-3 review of worker6-xyk3): a kill -9 between stage_private_seed temp creation (lichend.rs ~:1500) and publish cleanup leaks a 32-byte 0600 .id.seed.*.tmp forever; no boot-time sweep exists. Fix: at startup, unlink stale .id.seed.*.tmp in the state dir before provisioning.

title: Make lichend wedge errors name the inconsistent files and remediation
description: P3 (wave-3 review of worker6-2tb8/eni9): lichend.rs persistent wedge paths (~:1245,1206) fail closed with generic messages that name neither the files involved nor sanctioned recovery, producing an opaque Restart=always boot loop on a headless gateway. Fix: include the offending path(s) and the supported remediation in the error! output.

title: Slot recovery gate should check store emptiness, not hardcode is_empty=true
description: P3 (wave-3 review of worker6-eni9): lichend.rs slot recovery gate (~:1243) hardcodes is_empty=true where the trust-path equivalent (~:359) really checks entries().next().is_none(). A validly-sealed generation-1 store containing claims would be adopted and committed. Reachable only via sealing-seed (identity) compromise or coordinator bug (legit gen-1 stores are provisioned empty and every accepted claim bumps generation), so defense-in-depth only. Fix: perform the real emptiness check on the loaded verifier state.

title: Validate slot store generation before writing first-boot floor
description: P3 (wave-3 review of worker6-eni9): rust/lichen-gateway/src/bin/lichend.rs recover_or_provision_slot_replay (~:1208-1211) writes floor=1 BEFORE loading/gating the store in the store-exists/floor-missing/stage<SLOT branch. On rejection the downgrade persists on disk; an operator 'unsticking' the boot wedge by deleting the manifest then takes the all-artifacts path that skips the gate and loads the noninitial store against floor 1 (anti-rollback anchor reset). Requires same-UID tampering + operator action, so P3. Fix: load and validate the store generation in memory first; only anchor the floor after the gate passes.

title: [review] wave-8 P3 doc nits: stale step numbers, LICHEN/CHEN prose, short_addr.py docstring rot
description: P3 bundle from wave-8 review (all doc-level, zero behavior impact): (1) root_dio_signature.py:334 labels the new binding check 'Step 3' while :349 expiry is also 'Step 3' and :353/:357 say Step 4/5 vs docstring numbering expiry=4, seq=5, fields=6 — renumber consistently. (2) spec/02-physical-link.md:440 prose 'ASCII bytes of LICHEN as the initial value (0x4348454E)' compresses the truncation (LICHEN is 6 bytes; 0x4348454E is low 32 bits 'CHEN') — hex is authoritative and matches both impls; tweak wording to 'low 32 bits of ASCII LICHEN'. (3) python/src/lichen/link/short_addr.py:9-13 module docstring still references 'the duplicate 4.5 section ... uses fnv1a32' and :109 'for oracle parity with the stale 4.5' — both false after the wave-8 spec rewrite (4.5 is now CRC-32, no duplicate section); update or drop the stale references.

title: [review] wave-7 P3 bundle: delegation-table threading docs, /127 self-oracle residue, impersonation ratchet form
description: P3 bundle from wave-7 review: (1) rpl_dao_process.c:305-374 lichen_rpl_prefix_delegate/revoke/reset take no lock while the gate reads under dm->lock; single-operator constraint exists only in .c comment (273-275) - replicate in rpl_routing.h:376-425 docs or guard the four fns with the manager mutex. (2) lichen/tests/rpl_dao_auth/main.c:587 computes slash127_canonical via lichen_rpl_prefix_canonicalize (the function under test) then asserts the gate installs it - replace with a hand-written literal so the oracle is independent. (3) python/tests/crypto/test_orphan_vector_consumers.py:122-139 asserts (True, None) for the dodagid_mismatch impersonation vector (current-insecure behavior) as a passing test - convert to pytest.xfail(strict=True) so the ratchet is visible in reports, and confirm the DODAGID-binding-check bead exists (13m9 filed this wave).

title: Persist generation floor temp-file wedge on same-PID retry
description: P3, pre-existing mechanism newly reachable via the worker6-07cg conflict path (wave-2 review): rust/lichen-gateway/src/resources.rs floor write (~:1678-1687) uses create_new temp file .floor.{pid}.{G+1}.tmp with best-effort cleanup (:1704-1706). If the floor write fails after the state blob succeeded and the temp file could not be removed, a same-PID retry at the same generation fails to create the temp again, wedging commits for the process lifetime. Self-heals on restart (blob G+1 >= floor G loads fine). Fix: on floor-write failure, unlink any same-generation temp file before raising, or retry with an exclusive-suffix counter; add an injected-failure test for double floor write.

title: Assert pre-state in dao_route_makes_address_outside_0202_local test
description: P3 (wave-2 review of worker6-fz2c): rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs test dao_route_makes_address_outside_0202_local (~:2115) injects a route for 0201::1 and asserts is_local_mesh == true, but never asserts !is_local_mesh BEFORE injection. If a future regression made all 02xx addresses local by default, the test would still pass. Fix: add assert!(!gw.is_local_mesh(&node_addr)); before inject_route.

title: Wrap announce persistence read/fstat OSError as AnnouncePersistenceError
description: P3 (wave-2 review of worker6-r2ow): python/src/lichen/announce/persistence.py _read_state wraps only os.open; the os.read (~:278) and the NEW post-read re-fstat (~:280) can raise raw OSError (EIO/ESTALE), escaping as bare OSError instead of the method's documented failure type AnnouncePersistenceError. Callers treat both as terminal today (scheduler.py:173 wraps Exception; processor declares persistence failure terminal) so behavior is at parity, but the contract is inconsistent and the new guard added one more unwrapped syscall. Fix: wrap the read+re-fstat body (keep the finally fd close) and add an EIO-injection test asserting AnnouncePersistenceError.

title: SCHC create_sender must validate key_generation like control mint
description: P3 (wave-2 review of worker6-edbw): python/src/lichen/schc/session_manager.py create_sender (~:450) accepts key_generation=None without validation, while _issue_control_wire_unlocked now rejects None at mint. A session created with None generation turns terminal transitions into a raise-loop: at MAX_ACK_REQUESTS exhaustion or timeout the mint raises FragmentError after the ACK receipt was consumed (record.pending.pop at :798) and high_water advanced (:824/:838), leaving the record active and unabortable until idle expiry. Also leaves the fragment branch of consume_fragment_wire (:354) with the same structural None-is-None vacuity already tracked in project-LICHEN-worker6-sppu. Not reachable via production schc_handler.py (dict-indexed generations never None) - defense in depth. Fix: validate generation on session creation (reject None, exact type) and add a None-generation session test.

Our assertions honestly document each gap at zeroize_asserts.rs:13-37.

title: schnorr48 stub abort()s on attacker-controlled RF input when CONFIG_LICHEN_LINK_SCHNORR=n
description: PRE-EXISTING, found during jfln review. With CONFIG_LICHEN_LINK=y and CONFIG_LICHEN_LINK_SCHNORR=n (only way to get link layer without LICHEN_CRYPTO_MONOCYPHER; SCHNORR selects it), a frame carrying S/SI bits whose SIID matches a pinned peer reaches schnorr48_verify_frame -> schnorr48_stub_abort() (lichen/subsys/lichen/crypto/schnorr48.c:231-235,565,583) -> abort(): attacker-controllable crash. Wrong failure mode for untrusted input; the stub should return -EAUTH or -ENOSYS. Note the wave's SIID pre-filter narrowed this (unknown SIIDs reject before the stub), but pinned-SIID frames still abort.

title: LRU-eviction abuse surface: eviction-clears-replay and REPLAY_PERSIST refusal untested; capacity controls needed before EDHOC-driven registration
description: peer_add is admin/dev-provisioning-only today so remote pin-flapping is unreachable, but lichen_l2_rx.c:170 commits to EDHOC/announce-driven registration, at which point an attacker controlling CONFIG_LICHEN_LINK_MAX_NEIGHBORS valid identities can fill peer+replay tables, force-evict a quiet live peer, reset its replay window, and replay captured frames into the fresh window (replay table has no LRU: replay.c:112-116 fails closed). REPLAY_PERSIST mode refuses eviction (-ENOSPC, lichen_l2_peer.c:341-347) but that refusal is untested. Spec 02 4.2 step 5 sanctions eviction semantics. Before EDHOC registration lands: per-identity admission rate limits, reserved slots, plus tests for eviction-clears-replay and persist-mode refusal.

title: TOFU add-time pin-substitution rejection (-EEXIST on key change) untested anywhere

title: OSCORE spec gap: open bead iemi.3 premise contradicts spec 06 §15.3 (clear-vs-persist replay state)
description:
CONTEXT: spec/06-security.md §15.3 was rewritten on 2026-08-28 (commit 660b9bf3bf) to REQUIRE persistence: 'sender sequence reservations, recipient replay window, and response replay/correlation state MUST remain valid across that restart... Clearing a replay window while retaining the old context is not a re-keying event and MUST NOT make previously accepted messages acceptable again.'

CONFLICT: open bead project-LICHEN-worker6-iemi.3 (created 2026-08-27, i.e. BEFORE the spec change) directs: 'Verify Python/Rust/Zephyr do NOT persist OSCORE recipient replay windows or response replay state. Restart must clear these.' Working that bead as written would (a) contradict the current normative spec, and (b) undo the deliberate, spec-conformant C implementation (lichen/subsys/lichen/oscore/oscore_persist.c, oscore_settings.c, and the fail-closed gate in oscore_ctx.c:355-368, whose comments explicitly cite the reboot-replay rationale).

RFC 8613 anchor: §7.5 permits discarding mutable state ONLY together with establishing a fresh context (options 1-4); clearing while retaining the context is exactly what spec §15.3 forbids.

ACTION: supersede or rewrite project-LICHEN-worker6-iemi.3 to align with the current §15.3 (persistence + fail-closed + fresh-context-on-unrestorable), or explicitly re-key contexts on restart if the clear-on-restart design is chosen — before anyone picks it up. Filed under this review so the contradiction is tracked; not a code change request by itself. Related: project-LICHEN-wutk.10.3 (C production persistence wiring).

title: [review] EDHOC PLAINTEXT_2/3 ID_CRED kid sent as {4: kid} map; RFC 9528 3.5.3.2 requires bare kid bstr
description: P3, found during gt6u fix. RFC 9528 3.5.3.2: ID_CRED_I/ID_CRED_R in PLAINTEXT_2/3 MUST be the bare kid (a CBOR bstr/int, with 3.3.2 transport rule applied), not the {4: kid} map form; both implementations currently send the map form for the 8-byte kid (python _encode_id_cred, rust credential.rs). Changes PLAINTEXT bytes -> transcript -> master_secret, so fixing requires coordinated fixture regen on both impls (same procedure as gt6u). Note the map form may be intentional for LICHEN (kid is an 8-byte EUI-derived value, and RFC allows map form in other ID_CRED usages) - verify against RFC 3.5.3 examples first; if map form is actually conformant where kid is used as ID_CRED content, close as invalid with the RFC citation.

title: Rust: reformat imports to one-per-line baseline
description:
Run cargo +nightly fmt across all Rust crates to establish a one-import-per-line baseline.

## Why
rust/rustfmt.toml now has imports_granularity = "Item" which splits grouped imports (use foo::{a, b, c}) into separate lines. This reduces merge conflicts when multiple agents add imports to the same file - each addition lands on its own line instead of contesting a shared brace-group.

## What changes
Every .rs file with grouped imports will be reformatted. Example:
```rust
// Before
use std::{collections::HashMap, sync::Arc, fmt};

// After
use std::collections::HashMap;
use std::fmt;
use std::sync::Arc;
```

## Scope estimate
- ~20 crates in rust/
- Diff will touch most .rs files (noisy but mechanical)
- Zero semantic change - purely formatting

## Steps
1. Verify nightly toolchain: rustup show
2. Install if needed: rustup install nightly
3. Run formatter: cd rust && cargo +nightly fmt
4. Verify build: cargo build --all-targets
5. Verify tests: cargo test
6. Single commit: "style(rust): reformat imports to one-per-line"

## Risks
- None if tests pass - formatting only
- Conflicts with any in-flight Rust branches (coordinate timing)

## When to do
- Before starting parallel agent work on Rust code
- Or: accept gradual migration as files are touched

title: oscore helper: protect-response failure sends cleartext 5.00 to a protected peer
description: lichen/subsys/lichen/oscore/coap_oscore.c:106-109: if coap_oscore_protect_response fails, coap_oscore_respond_resource sends a cleartext 5.00 (token echoed) to a peer whose request was OSCORE-protected — a downgrade response on the exact paths the authz gates hardened. EVIDENCE: covered by the wmf0/ir24 verification - module-aware gcc A/B vs HEAD shows zero diagnostics in this hunk (errors at 1075/1160/1180/1199 are pre-existing 4.1.0 drift, identical in HEAD modulo +4 line shift); lint finding sets identical in the real build config; COAP_RESPONSE_CODE_FORBIDDEN is already used by coap_config.c/coap_msg.c so the constant is available.

title: slot-coord: #ifdef CONFIG_LICHEN_LINK_SCHNORR can silently compile out claim verification (fail-open backstop missing)
description: coap_slot_coord.c:306-339: signature verification sits inside #ifdef CONFIG_LICHEN_LINK_SCHNORR; if that guard ever decouples from the Kconfig dep, claims with has_signature=true are accepted unverified. The new Kconfig dependency guarantees coupling today but nothing enforces it. The codebase's own pattern for must-never-build-without-crypto is #error (link/schnorr48.c:222-223, link_ctx.c:268-269). Fix: #else + #error (or BUILD_ASSERT) so regression is a build failure.
close_reason: coap_slot_coord.c:339-343: added #else + #error backstop after the CONFIG_LICHEN_LINK_SCHNORR verification block, following the house pattern (link/schnorr48.c:222-223, link_ctx.c:268-269). Message: 'slot-coord requires LICHEN_LINK_SCHNORR: claim verification must never be compiled out (fail-open backstop)'. Commit 80458a82f6. EVIDENCE: (1) Negative test - compiled the module target with CONFIG_LICHEN_LINK_SCHNORR stripped from a patched autoconf.h (-imacros substitution, otherwise identical flags): compile fails at coap_slot_coord.c:340 with exactly the #error message; regression is now a build failure, not silent fail-open. (2) Positive config: with the Kconfig chain enabled (bead wmf0 build) the guard compiles as before and my hunk contributes zero diagnostics in the A/B vs HEAD. (3) Lint profile parity with a corroborating side effect: cppcheck analyzes two preprocessor configs; in the SCHNORR-undefined config HEAD reported the pre-existing uninitvar iid_hex (proving cppcheck really did analyze the verify-compiled-out code), and my #error makes that config un-analyzable so that HEAD-only finding legitimately disappears; in the only real build config (SCHNORR=y) finding sets are identical (17 misc-use-internal-linkage + 2 bugprone-branch-clone + 1 uninitvar + 1 pre-existing zephyr/kernel.h-not-found).

title: group_oscore: _previous retains every historical key forever (forward-secrecy gap)
description: python/src/lichen/crypto/group_oscore.py:122,195,164-171: rekey() appends to _previous and nothing purges it; key_valid_at only gates use past the grace window while the material stays in memory (and key_for_epoch does a growing linear scan). A single memory compromise of the controller retroactively exposes all past group traffic keys, contradicting the module's forward-secrecy framing and the docstring's 'previous epoch+key' (singular) design. Fix: after rekey, drop entries whose created_s + GRACE_PERIOD_S < now and zeroize where practical.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 2f2010b3f0: rekey now purges _previous entries with created_s + GRACE_PERIOD_S < now (strict boundary consistent with key_valid_at), so superseded key material is no longer retained indefinitely; dropped bytearray key buffers are zeroized in place (bytes documented as unscrubbable), including collision-dropped wrap entries. GroupKeyMaterial.key widened to bytes|bytearray for the zeroization path. Test: TestPreviousRetention pins that after grace elapses on the injected clock _previous no longer holds the old material (key_for_epoch(1) is None) and that a dropped bytearray key is overwritten with zeros. Suite: 19 passed in python/tests/crypto/test_group_oscore.py; ruff clean.

title: Group wrap: materialize member_pubkeys before empty check (empty generator yields 0-member envelope)
description: Robustness review finding on worker6-9mkj.2. group_oscore_wrap.py:191: if not member_pubkeys does not catch an empty generator - probe-confirmed a 0-member envelope with no error. A rekey distributed to nobody is silent and group-wide. Fix: member_pubkeys = list(member_pubkeys) before the emptiness check (also gives stable iteration for duplicate detection).

title: Group epoch: reject int/str master_secret (bytes(int) yields silent all-zero key)
description: Robustness review finding on worker6-9mkj.1. group_oscore_epoch.py:98,145: bytes(master_secret) converts an int to an all-zero secret of that length (GroupEpochManager('g', 32) -> 32 zero bytes; rekey(16) -> 16 zero bytes; probe-confirmed). A silent zero key in a crypto module is catastrophic-but-quiet. Sister wrap module rejects non-bytes at its boundary; epoch does not. Fix: reject non-bytes-like input (at minimum int) before bytes() in __init__ and rekey, raising ValueError per the docstring (str currently raises TypeError from bytes(), also inconsistent with docstring).

title: Group wrap: reject RFC 7748 small-order epk on unwrap; pin point-validation tests
description: Security review finding on worker6-9mkj.2. group_oscore_wrap.py:151-155,238 comment claims all-zero shared-secret rejection defends against small subgroup attack, but it only catches the order-1 identity point. A nonzero low-order epk (orders 2/4/8) yields a predictable shared secret, letting an attacker derive the KEK and craft AES-KW ciphertext unwrapping to a chosen group key (epk is attacker-supplied; X25519PublicKey.from_public_bytes does no validation). Exploit requires defeating pairwise-OSCORE delivery, so defense-in-depth. Fix: reject epk u-coordinates matching the 8 known RFC 7748 small-order values before exchange(), or correct the comment to state reliance on OSCORE-authenticated delivery. Also add tests: wrap_for_members rejects 32-byte non-Ed25519-point key (only wrong-length tested now), and unwrap behavior for nonzero low-order epk is pinned.

title: Group epoch: default to monotonic clock and bound negative grace delta
description: Security+correctness review findings on worker6-9mkj.1. (a) group_oscore_epoch.py:50-51,171 default time_ms_func is time.time(); a stepped/rewound wall clock makes now-rekey_time negative and the grace check accepts the old key indefinitely (rewind) or expires it early (forward step). Default for an elapsed-time security window should be time.monotonic_ns()//10**6, or at minimum clamp negative elapsed with a doc note. (b) group_oscore_epoch.py:171 now - rekey_time <= GRACE has no lower bound: clock set arbitrarily far back keeps previous key valid indefinitely (bounded blast radius: only immediately-previous epoch; rollback/future rejected regardless). Fix: require now_ms >= rekey_time or bound the negative delta; pick one behavior and document. Injectable clock for vectors remains legitimate trusted-caller flexibility.

title: Group epoch: default to monotonic clock and bound negative grace delta
description: Security+correctness review findings on worker6-9mkj.1. (a) group_oscore_epoch.py:50-51,171 default time_ms_func is time.time(); a stepped/rewound wall clock makes now-rekey_time negative and the grace check accepts the old key indefinitely (rewind) or expires it early (forward step). Default for an elapsed-time security window should be time.monotonic_ns()//10**6, or at minimum clamp negative elapsed with a doc note. (b) group_oscore_epoch.py:171 now - rekey_time <= GRACE has no lower bound: clock set arbitrarily far back keeps previous key valid indefinitely (bounded blast radius: only immediately-previous epoch; rollback/future rejected regardless). Fix: require now_ms >= rekey_time or bound the negative delta; pick one behavior and document. Injectable clock for vectors remains legitimate trusted-caller flexibility.

title: Strengthen OSCORE parity fixture tests (P3 review findings)
description: Five P3 findings from wave-1 codereview of the 6.8.9 parity work: (1) fixture pins only the protect direction — add a tamper-rejection vector (modified ciphertext/tag must fail to decrypt) derived from the EDHOC context. (2) Python drift-guard compares oracle to its own fixture (not an independent oracle) — chain anchors bottom out in Python; document or add an external anchor (e.g. RFC 8613 appendix vector). (3) rust context_parity.rs test truncates vector decoded_timestamp u64->u32 with as u32 — assert range first so fixture drift fails loudly. (4) generator + python test couple to private ctx._construct_nonce — a refactor breaks them; prefer a stable public path or pin with a comment. (5) generate_oscore_context_parity.py patches os.urandom but secrets.token_bytes binds os.urandom at import — harmless today (echo_recovery not in fixture) but any future field derived via secrets makes regeneration silently nondeterministic; patch secrets.token_bytes too.

title: Harden rust/lichen-rpl time_option.rs API (P3 review findings)
description: Three P3 findings from wave-1 codereview of rust/lichen-rpl/src/time_option.rs: (1) from_option_data cannot verify the option type byte — any 6-byte payload with data[0] in 0..4 and data[1]==0 is silently accepted if a caller skips checking OptionIter raw.opt_type (Python's path revalidates the full 8 bytes incl. type; time_sync.py:755); consider a checked entry point or documented caller contract. (2) pub stratum/pub timestamp allow struct-literal construction violating the NoSync=>zero-timestamp invariant — all sinks re-validate so serialization is safe, but a consumer reading .timestamp directly can ingest an invariant-violating value; consider private fields + accessors. (3) from_bytes and from_option_data duplicate reserved/stratum/NoSync validation — from_bytes should delegate via &data[2..8] so invariants live in one place.

title: [review] wave-3 P3 bundle: CCA gate polish + test coverage + SX1262 cosmetics
description: P3 bundle from wave-3 review: (1) link_cca.c: cancel race misclassified - cad_begin can return positive CANCELLED which passes the if (cca < 0) check -> run real CAD post-cancel and surface -EIO instead of -ECANCELED; acquire() handles it (csma.c:313-315), gate should too. (2) link_cca.c TOCTOU one-liner: snapshot struct lichen_link_cca_ops ops = ctx->cca_ops at gate entry, use snapshot (defends cleanup race, documented contract today). (3) CONFIG_LICHEN_LINK_CCA=n silently ignores a registered probe - set_cca_ops doc should say so (or reject registration when gate disabled). (4) doc line: concurrent TX on one ctx can surface -EPROTO instead of documented -EBUSY (Kconfig help says -EBUSY; gate is outside seq_lock, 5-step csma sequence not atomic) - align doc or contract. (5) test coverage: add positive-cad_status probe test (would have caught P1), cancel-during-gate test, assert backoff_exponent unchanged at exhaustion (ccp15 vector 3 pins it: 5->5), assert nonce/seq unchanged after -EBUSY (gate-before-nonce property currently only code order). (6) link_ctx Kconfig exhaustion-latch: impl intentionally opens a FRESH cycle after RETRY_EXHAUSTED on next busy (csma.c:103-107) where spec 02a 10.5 step 2 would re-emit exhausted frozen - file/record the decision in spec 02a (one normative sentence) so it cannot be fixed accidentally in one place. (7) persistence.rs degraded redundancy is silent when one slot corrupt - consider surfacing/repairing on open. (8) SX1262.cs: latchedIrqFlags read without stateLock in GetIrqStatus (:244,249) contradicts stated invariant (:897); catch (Exception e) logs only e.Message (NRE gives empty message) -> e.ToString(); optionally rename cca rng cb to jitter_rng.

title: test: drop stale xfail-era docstring in sos CBOR key-order test
description: test_security_app_vector_consumers.py::TestSosSignatureVectors::test_canonical_cbor_real_key_order_matches_rfc8949 docstring (lines ~529-534) still says 'the sos/medical vectors pin wrong orders and are xfailed exactly below'. False since 4921cfd8f4: sos_signature.json pins are corrected to RFC 8949 4.2.1 ts-first order and the exact-pin tests are real passing tests (no xfail markers remain in the file). Misled the fbrw audit. Update docstring to reflect corrected pins; no behavior change.

title: Register group mobility patterns in scenario DSL registry
description: MOBILITY_PATTERNS (scenario.py:252) only registers random_waypoint; the new GroupMobility (jitter), RPGM, and ManhattanGrid classes are public API but unreachable from YAML mobility events. Register names (e.g. group_waypoint, rpgm, manhattan_grid), pass params through, and add parse/exec tests mirroring the random_waypoint ones. Also document per-group seed derivation or add duplicate-seed guard to avoid correlated lockstep groups.

title: Mobility API hardening: negative dt validation and pattern-instance aliasing
description: (a) step(dt_us<0) unvalidated: GroupMobility._update_jitter pushes _jitter_elapsed_us negative, max_step goes negative moving members AWAY from targets, and ZeroDivisionError possible on zero-magnitude jitter (mobility.py:379-400); validate dt_us>=0 like the runner clamp. (b) One-pattern-instance-per-group is documented but unenforced: MobilityManager.attach silently aliases, double-stepping a shared group pattern (mobility.py:200-203, :839). Add instance-attach guard or explicit error. Tests for both.

comments.author: Mark Atwood
comments.text: Wave-4 review addendum: ManhattanGrid-specific instance - re-attach (attach/detach with no reset) to a different node moves it in a straight OFF-GRID line toward a stale target, violating axis-lock (mobility.py:838-842, 973-982; verified empirically). Base class docstring says reattachment requires reset() but nothing enforces it - include manager-level enforcement or reset-on-reattach in scope.

title: ManhattanGrid: float classification drops last grid line on exact-multiple extents
description: _grid_size (mobility.py:794) uses int(floor((hi-lo)/spacing)); 0.3/0.1 == 2.999...9 -> grid_size 2, so snap_to_grid(0.3,0.3) returns (0.2,0.2) and the max bound is unreachable as a grid point. Fix with round() plus epsilon or decimal/Fraction-based extent math; test non-integer spacings where extent is an exact multiple.

title: (authz) handoff_post error paths bypass coap_oscore_respond_resource
description: AUDIT (epic 6mij decomposition): handoff_post (lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/coap_handoff.c:996-1063) correctly rejects unprotected requests (4.01 at :1011-1016) and answers success via coap_oscore_respond_resource (:1060), BUT its error paths respond with PLAIN lichen_coap_respond instead: bad-request at :1018-1022, decode-fail at :1030-1033, process-fail at :1040-1043, encode-fail at :1051-1054. A request that passed unprotect (OSCORE-protected) then receives an UNPROTECTED 4.00/5.00 error, leaking status detail in clear text on the mesh and breaking the RFC 8613 expectation that responses to protected requests are protected (house pattern: coap_config.c:921-925 responds protected on the same error class). spec/08-gateway-coordination.md:119 'All CoAP messages use OSCORE'. FIX: route the four error paths through coap_oscore_respond_resource(resource, request, addr, addr_len, &oscore, code, CBOR_CONTENT_FORMAT, NULL, 0) (payload only where one exists). Keep the 4.01-for-unprotected path plain (no ctx available). This file is separate from the helper migration (worker6-l9hb) because handoff is OSCORE-mandatory, not is_protected||local_admin; note that in the helper design. ACCEPTANCE: (1) all error responses to a protected request arrive OSCORE-protected; (2) 4.01 for unprotected requests unchanged; (3) extend any existing handoff test or add a minimal one asserting the protected-error path; (4) no change to lichen_handoff_process_request semantics.

title: (doc) Kconfig LICHEN_COAP_KEYS help contradicts spec 17.6.3 and coap_keys.c on BLE admin
description: AUDIT (epic 6mij decomposition): lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/Kconfig:233-234 says 'SECURITY: Write operations require local admin access (loopback or BLE LCI interface).' but the implementation lichen_coap_is_local_admin (lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/coap_keys.c:51-98) accepts ONLY loopback or link-local whose sin6_scope_id matches slip_transport_iface_get() - there is no BLE interface check. spec/11-lci.md:724 (17.6.3): 'Access level determined by transport (e.g., USB = admin, BLE = standard).' - BLE is NOT admin, so the CODE is right and the Kconfig help is wrong. A BLE LCI transport exists (lichen/subsys/lichen/transport/ble_ipsp_transport.c) making the doc claim actively misleading to deployers. FIX: rewrite the Kconfig help to match spec 17.6.3 and the code (loopback or SLIP LCI interface; BLE = standard access level), and mirror the wording in coap_keys.c:11-14 file header if needed. Also audit other help texts for the same claim. ACCEPTANCE: (1) Kconfig text matches spec/11-lci.md 17.6.3; (2) no behavioral change; (3) grep for 'BLE LCI' across lichen/ shows no remaining admin-claiming text.

title: committed coap/l2 sources incompatible with Zephyr 4.1.0 workspace
description: Full compile of the coap subsystem against the local 4.1.0 Zephyr workspace (not the pinned v3.7.0) fails in files untouched by the o287 revert: (a) coap_client.c:180/:191 'struct coap_client has no member send_mutex' (Zephyr 4.x removed it); (b) lichen_util.c:16 vs lichen_util.h:70 -Werror=array-parameter (uint8_t* vs uint8_t[32]). Version-split only: CI/AWS builder uses pinned v3.7.0 where they compile. Either fix sources for both versions or document 4.1.0-workspace builds unsupported for those files. Discovered during o287 generate proof; generate itself passes.

title: checkin_resource: enforce roll-call list document bound vs PAYLOAD_MAX
description: Bead project-LICHEN-worker6-y9pi added a BUILD_ASSERT bounding the {"checkins":[...]} list document (MAX_CHECKINS x LICHEN_CHECKIN_ENTRY_CBOR_MAX + wrapper <= CONFIG_LICHEN_CHECKIN_PAYLOAD_MAX) in checkin_resource.c. The same gap exists for the {"rollcalls":[...]} list and per-roll-call 18.6.3 status documents: a worst-case status doc (id + started + timeout + 32 responded tracks + 32 missing tracks) is roughly 4-5 KB, so with CONFIG_LICHEN_CHECKIN_MAX_ROLLCALLS > 1 the worst-case list document can exceed even the 16384 Kconfig range maximum; lichen_rollcall_list_encode returns BUFFER_TOO_SMALL and the GET handler degrades to 5.00 at runtime with no build-time warning. Options: a second BUILD_ASSERT with a documented LICHEN_ROLLCALL_STATUS worst-case macro (like LICHEN_CHECKIN_ENTRY_CBOR_MAX) plus Kconfig range/help sizing, or a documented runtime clamp. Keep the checkin_resource twister suite compiling (its MAX_ROLLCALLS=2). Discovered while sizing PAYLOAD_MAX for y9pi.
close_reason: Roll-call side of the payload-bound contract enforced. (1) Formula-based LICHEN_ROLLCALL_RENDER_MAX in checkin.h (map+id 37+started 17+timeout 15+responded 12+32x73+missing 10+32x73 = 4764 B) pinned to the encoder by host test test_maximal_rollcall_render_within_bound (full 32+32 tracks, max node/ts/status) - host suite 19/19. (2) BUILD_ASSERT in checkin_resource.c requires CONFIG_LICHEN_CHECKIN_PAYLOAD_MAX >= RENDER_MAX + 16 (single-id status GET always encodable); it fired on the twister config (2560) proving the guard is live. (3) lichen_rollcall_list_encode clamps the array count to rem / RENDER_MAX so the definite-length header stays truthful - documented partial-list degradation, discovery is by polling per 18.6.3. (4) Test config PAYLOAD_MAX 2560 -> 9600 so the existing two-rollcall list assertion holds with both renders genuinely fitting; Kconfig default 5120 unchanged (no default RAM growth); Kconfig help documents all three enforcement points. Twister qemu_x86/atom 9/9.

title: Identity-bound roll-call reset in service layer
description: project-LICHEN-worker6-w063 mitigated id-reset list-wiping at the resource layer (counts restored after lichen_rollcall_post). Proper fix: record creator identity (source address) on struct lichen_rollcall in lichen/checkin.c and only wipe responded/missing when re-POST comes from the creator — requires extending the oracle-matched service API and test/vectors/checkin_rollcall.json (Python oracle) in lockstep.
close_reason: Creator identity bound at creation: struct lichen_rollcall gains has_creator/creator (LICHEN_ROLLCALL_CREATOR_MAX 46, peer IPv6 text via net_addr_ntop in the resource layer). New lichen_rollcall_post_ex(): creator re-post of a known id updates started/timeout and PRESERVES responded/missing; non-creator (including NULL-vs-known) gets LICHEN_CHECKIN_CODE_FORBIDDEN (4.03) with LICHEN_CHECKIN_ERR_CREATOR_MISMATCH detail; legacy 4-arg lichen_rollcall_post wraps _ex with NULL creator so vector/host-suite semantics are unchanged. Resource handler passes the peer-derived identity and its restore-hack is removed. Twister qemu_x86/atom 9/9 (new test_rollcall_repost_creator_binding); host suite lichen/tests/checkin_rollcall green under ASan/UBSan.

title: checkin_resource.c: set_time override writes unlocked (torn 64-bit read on 32-bit targets)
description: checkin_resource.c:45-49 lichen_checkin_resource_set_time writes s_time_overridden/s_time_override without s_lock while resource_now() reads them under it - torn 64-bit read possible on 32-bit targets. Fix: take s_lock in the setter.
close_reason: lichen_checkin_resource_set_time now takes s_lock around the s_time_overridden/s_time_override writes; resource_now() reads them under the same lock (only caller path is service_tick_locked, invoked with the mutex held), closing the torn 64-bit read on 32-bit targets. Verified: twister lichen.checkin_resource on qemu_x86_64 8/8 test cases passed.

title: deaddrop: with_clock config-validation error typed as Error::Encode
description: deaddrop.rs:840-845 rejects storage_limit==0 with Error::Encode(storage_limit must be a positive integer) - a config-validation failure reported as encode failure, misleading and inconsistent with Decode/Encode semantics used everywhere else. Fix: dedicated variant or documented convention.
close_reason: Added a dedicated Error::Config(String) variant to the lichen-client error enum ('configuration error: {m}' Display) and retyped with_clock's storage_limit==0 rejection from Error::Encode to Error::Config, consistent with the crate's Decode/Encode wire-error semantics (config validation is neither). Chose dedicated variant over documented convention because the bead itself calls Encode 'misleading'; grep-verified no exhaustive Error matches exist outside the crate, so the addition is non-breaking. with_clock doc updated. New test zero_storage_limit_is_a_config_error pins the variant and Display message. Verified: cargo test -p lichen-client --lib 130 passed, deaddrop_vectors 26 passed. Commit + bd flat files.

title: deaddrop: encode failures masked via unwrap_or_default to silent empty 2.05
description: deaddrop.rs:1136 :1164 encode_senml_pack(...).unwrap_or_default() turns an invariant violation into a silent 2.05 with empty body. Currently unreachable (records validated at insert) but invariant-dependent. Fix: return an error outcome or debug_assert!.
close_reason: render_get now returns Result<GetResponse, Error> (payload encoding failure surfaces as Err, not a silent empty listing) and get_by_id returns the new PickupOutcome::InternalError (5.00, code::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR = 160) instead of masking an invariant violation as empty 2.05 Content. Both sites are unreachable while store invariants hold (records are decode-validated at insert, so re-encode cannot fail) — docs state this and the outcomes exist to keep the API honest when the invariant breaks. Chose error-outcome over debug_assert! because a debug-only assert still masks in release. Grep-verified render_get/get_by_id/PickupOutcome have no callers outside lichen-client + its test, so the signature/enum changes are contained. New pin test internal_error_outcome_maps_to_500 (response_code == 160). Verified: cargo test -p lichen-client --lib 130 passed, deaddrop_vectors 25 passed. Commit + bd flat files.

title: deaddrop: generate_drop_id spins forever if 2^24 space exhausted
description: deaddrop.rs:897-911 retry loop never terminates if all 2^24 IDs occupied (fillable via add_drop explicit IDs ~16MB store) - a hang not an error. Fix: bail after bounded attempts with a store-full error.
close_reason: generate_drop_id now performs at most MAX_ID_ATTEMPTS=32 CSPRNG draws (new const with rationale doc) and returns Option<String>; None means the 2^24 space is effectively exhausted or the CSPRNG failed. Callers convert to store-full outcomes: add_drop -> None (doc updated: 'budget or drop-ID space exhausted'), post -> 5.03 ServiceUnavailable storage_full form (PostOutcome::ServiceUnavailable doc updated), matching the existing storage_full vector semantics. Additionally both post() and add_drop() now mint the ID BEFORE evict_for_space, so a doomed (ID-exhausted) request can never evict live drops — the same invariant tnlp established for explicit IDs. True-exhaustion is not practically testable (would need ~16M stored drops); the bound is statically evident and the full suite is green. Verified: cargo test -p lichen-client --lib 130 passed, deaddrop_vectors 24 passed. Commit 4ba8ab3d0d.

title: deaddrop: private drop returns 4.04, spec 18.9 says 4.03
description: deaddrop.rs:1159-1162 returns 4.04 concealing existence (security-positive, documented as matching Python reference) but spec/12-apps.md 18.9 says private drops require matching OSCORE context or return 4.03. Intentional wire-conformance divergence. Fix: reconcile - either update spec text to document the concealment rationale or change code to 4.03; add vector if wire-visible.
close_reason: Evidence-driven spec amendment, no code change: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py deliberately returns 404 for private drops with non-matching context (comment: hide existence) and 403 for group drops; Rust matches. Two independent implementations + security-positive rationale outweighed the spec text, so spec/12-apps.md 18.9 was amended to document 4.04-concealment for private drops and 4.03 for group drops. Tests unchanged and green (27/27). Commit <docs(deaddrop) on main>.

title: deaddrop: rate limiter counts only successful posts
description: deaddrop.rs:1036-1045: 4.13 and decode-failure return before check_rate_limit/record_request, so an authenticated context gets unlimited 1536B parse work (OSCORE unwrap + CBOR decode each). Defensible (quota = drops created) but undocumented. Fix: count 4.13 against the bucket or document the chosen semantics in the module doc.
close_reason: Semantics documented in post() doc comment rather than changed: the quota counts drops created; 4.13 and 4.00 return before the rate check and do not consume the bucket. Evidence: the Python reference render_post has the identical gate order (4.01, empty, 4.13, decode, then check_rate_limit), so changing Rust unilaterally would break cross-impl parity. Wire-visible behavior unchanged; deaddrop_vectors 27/27, lib 130/130. Commit <docs(deaddrop) on main>.

title: deaddrop: wire-size storage charge vs ~40-90x decoded heap amplification
description: deaddrop.rs:1053 charges storage by wire size but retains decoded value (:1066 :1014): a 1536B pack of minimal records decodes to hundreds of owned SenmlRecords (~100KB heap) while charged 1536B - the 8KB leaf budget can hold ~700KB live heap. Gateway-side, not firmware. Fix: cap records per pack (e.g. <=32) or store raw bytes and decode on read.
close_reason: Chose the bead's first option (cap records per pack at 32) over store-raw-bytes/decode-on-read: the cap is insert-time only, needs no new read-path failure modes, and bounds a stored drop's decoded heap to ~an order of magnitude of its wire charge, while raw storage would still amplify transiently on every listing render. MAX_RECORDS_PER_PACK=32 const documented with the wire-charge-vs-heap rationale and noted as a deliberate, documented divergence from the Python reference (which has no cap); enforced in add_drop (None) and post (4.00 BadRequest), with the size gate explicitly unable to catch it (33 minimal records < 1536 B). decode_senml_pack itself is NOT capped so render_get listings (which legitimately exceed 32 records) keep working. No vector has >32 records (max 7), so deaddrop.json stays untouched. New test pack_record_cap_bounds_heap_amplification (32 accepted, 33 rejected via both entry points, store unchanged). Verified: cargo test -p lichen-client --lib 130 passed, deaddrop_vectors 27 passed. Commit + bd flat files.

title: checkin: clock step-back wraps now-last_checkin; PAYLOAD_MAX vs 256 checkins unenforced
description: checkin.c:1841 now - last_checkin_at wraps on clock step-back producing spurious immediate due (unsigned arithmetic). Also Kconfig help for LICHEN_CHECKIN_PAYLOAD_MAX (must bound worst-case document) is unenforced: MAX_CHECKINS up to 256 with 200-byte messages needs ~76KB against PAYLOAD_MAX cap 16384 - GET /checkin returns 5.00 permanently at those settings. Fix: signed-subtraction guard for step-back; build-time BUILD_ASSERT relating PAYLOAD_MAX to MAX_CHECKINS*MAX_MSG or runtime clamp with documented bound.
close_reason: Two fixes in lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/checkin.c + support: (1) lichen_checkin_due() now guards the clock step-back (last_checkin_at > now returns false before any subtraction), signed-safe like rollcall_prune_expired; no more spurious immediate due on wraparound. Header doc updated. (2) PAYLOAD_MAX relation enforced: new public macro LICHEN_CHECKIN_ENTRY_CBOR_MAX (306 B, breakdown in checkin.h) and a file-scope BUILD_ASSERT in checkin_resource.c (MAX_CHECKINS x 306 + wrapper <= CONFIG_LICHEN_CHECKIN_PAYLOAD_MAX); Kconfig help now states the enforced relation. The assert fired for one in-tree config - the checkin_resource twister suite (MAX_CHECKINS=8, PAYLOAD_MAX=1024): PAYLOAD_MAX resized 1024 -> 2560 (sane: multiple of 512, headroom over required 2464) and said so here per instructions. Kconfig defaults (16x306+16=4912 <= 5120) compile unchanged. Evidence: host suite 18/18 under ASan/UBSan incl. new regressions test_due_clock_step_back (900s step-back not due; boundary 10899/10900) and test_maximal_entry_within_bound (pins the 306 B macro to the encoder, protecting the assert premise); twister lichen/tests/checkin_resource on qemu_x86/atom: 1/1 configurations, 8/8 test cases PASS with the assert in the build, and a negative control with PAYLOAD_MAX=1024 correctly fails the build with the assert message (proves the guard is live). Note: twister WITH -x ZEPHYR_EXTRA_MODULES=<repo>/lichen fails at Kconfig parse (zcbor dependency loop) identically with my changes stashed - pre-existing 4.1.0/v3.7.0 workspace split, filed as its own bead (discovered-from this one). cppcheck/clang-tidy finding profile identical to baseline (no compile db artifacts only). Also filed: roll-call-list PAYLOAD_MAX bound (same class, discovered-from).

title: rangetest: interval_ms lacks floor; 1ms continuous test is a latent radio flood
description: coap_rangetest.c:545-551 accepts any uint > 0 for interval_ms, stored at :789-793; header documents it as the continuous-test period driving Observe notifications - once a scheduler consumes it, 1ms notifications to all observers floods the radio. Spec example is 5000. Fix: enforce floor (>=1000ms suggested) and/or require OSCORE/local-admin to change it.
close_reason: interval_ms now enforces an inclusive 1000 ms floor (RANGETEST_INTERVAL_MIN_MS): 999 rejected -EBADMSG, 1000 accepted (the valid vector uses exactly 1000; boundary vector rejects 0, unchanged). Auth note: the handler already routes through coap_oscore_unprotect_resource_request; the middleware-wide fail-open under LICHEN_COAP_SERVER_OSCORE=n is a middleware convention, not this module's call. Regression tests test_interval_floor_1000ms (999 reject, 1000 accept, atomicity). Twister 8/8. Commit 4c33ee2345.

title: rangetest: cur_skip_item argument*2 wraps for map arguments >= 2^63
description: coap_rangetest.c:251: argument * 2U wraps for arguments >= 2^63 making the container appear empty so subsequent bytes realign the parse relative to stricter decoders - interop divergence on untrusted unknown-key values (no memory unsafety; termination and bounds hold). Fix: reject argument > UINT64_MAX/2 or bound by remaining input length.
close_reason: cur_skip_item now rejects map arguments > UINT64_MAX/2 before the *2 doubling (would wrap to 0, making the container look empty and realigning the parse on untrusted unknown-key values). Regression test test_skip_item_rejects_wrapping_map_argument: a body whose unknown-key value is map(2^63) followed by a valid interval_ms key must be rejected atomically (pre-fix it was accepted with the trailing key honored). Twister 8/8. Commit 4c33ee2345.

title: rangetest: Observe registered before body validation; 4.00 path leaks observer slot

Fix: validate body first, register observe last.
close_reason: Observe registration moved after full request validation in lichen_rangetest_get_handler (4.00/5.03 no longer consume an observer slot; RFC 7641 comment). Regression test test_observe_registered_only_on_success asserts the observer list stays empty on the 4.00 path, registers on success, and deregisters on Observe=1. (Rescued uncommitted work from a timed-out agent session; verified and landed.) Twister qemu_x86/atom: 1/1 config, 8/8 cases. Commit 4c33ee2345.

title: wire::array silently truncates lengths >65535 producing corrupt CBOR
description: rust/lichen-client/src/checkin.rs:239-249 and deaddrop.rs:438-448: final branch emits 0x99 with len as u16 - silently truncated for len>65535 instead of erroring (text writers truncate above u32::MAX, unreachable). Latent only today but violates deterministic-writer contract and reachable via >64k-entry RollcallStatus re-encode. wire::map has a debug_assert; array has none. Fix: add u32 branch + debug_assert! or return Error::Encode for lengths beyond supported range; unit test the error path.

title: rollcall status cross-impl contract: optional arrays, timeout range, u64 ids, Vec cap, error-code mapping
description: Cross-implementation divergences on inputs the vectors do not pin: Rust RollcallStatus::from_cbor (checkin.rs:557-569) REQUIRES responded+missing and applies no timeout range; C (checkin.c:1103-1143) treats arrays as optional-defaulting-empty and rejects timeout_s==0 or >604800. C coerces any CBOR uint id (full u64) to decimal (:798-803); Rust routes through as_i64 rejecting ids > i64::MAX and mislabels oversized timeout_s as invalid_timeout_value where C says exceeds-max. Rust grows responded/missing Vecs unbounded vs C 32-entry cap. Fix: pick one contract, document in both headers, add vectors pinning omitted-arrays case; u64::try_from for ids; align error-code mapping; cap Rust Vecs at named constant matching LICHEN_ROLLCALL_TRACK_MAX.
close_reason: Unambiguous remainder done, committed eb58c3498f: (1) RollcallRequest coerces any CBOR uint id (full u64) to decimal string, matching C lichen_rollcall_request_decode (checkin.c:798-803) - previously constrained to i64 via as_i64; (2) huge uint timeout_s now maps to timeout_exceeds_maximum (C LICHEN_CHECKIN_ERR_TIMEOUT_MAX) instead of invalid_timeout_value - as_i64 replaced with wire_u64; (3) track-array caps and error-code mapping landed earlier with tjxj. Conformance tests: rollcall_request_u64_max_id_coerced, rollcall_request_huge_uint_timeout_exceeds_maximum. checkin_rollcall_vectors 13/13, lichen-client --lib 130/130, clippy clean for touched code. DEFERRED: the optional-vs-required responded/missing arrays question is filed as human-labeled bead (genuine spec-silent contract decision, no oracle to arbitrate) - Rust behavior left unchanged pending that decision.

title: rangetest: RANGETEST_TRACE_CBOR_MAX 640 below worst-case 657 for 8 full-form hops

title: Vectors: checkin_rollcall.json cbor_length fields are stale
description: 18 of 25 payload vectors in test/vectors/checkin_rollcall.json have cbor_length values that disagree with the actual byte length of their own cbor_hex (e.g. rollcall_status_response claims 220, hex is 250; checkin_minimal claims 64, hex is 65; checkin_boundary_coords claims 83, hex is 91). title: [spec] document canonical-PIV (nonzero-length) requirement and its interop consequences
description: P3 informational finding, no code change. Wrapper coap_oscore.c:194 (new this wave) rejects 0-length PIV with INVALID_PARAM -> 4.01; C client encodes seq 0 as 1-byte 0x00 PIV (oscore_nonce.c:66-69) and core oscore_protect.c:400 already rejected empty PIV pre-wave, so LICHEN-LICHEN interop is intact. But RFC 8613 permits 0-length PIV (seq 0), so RFC-conformant third-party peers are rejected. Document the canonical-PIV convention in the security/interop spec section (draft-lora-security-* or spec 6) with rationale (canonical encoding, replay-window simplicity) and note the interop boundary explicitly.

title: [review] reconcile RX8130CE battery-switchover mode 2 semantics vs datasheet (driver comment contradicts binding)

Register writes identical to upstream; the two upstream docs disagree. Resolve against the RX8130CE datasheet (section on VLOW/backup switchover, INIEN/CHGEN bits) and fix the losing description. Non-rechargeable cell + charging enabled can damage hardware, so getting the doc right matters. Cross-check the other 3 modes while in there.

title: Write integration tests: Meshtastic node in Medium simulator, TX/RX verification

2. **Single node TX**

3. **Single node RX**

   - Verify Meshtastic receives and processes it
   - Check RSSI/SNR reported correctly

4. **Two Meshtastic nodes**
   - Spawn two nodes in range
   - Send message from A to B
   - Verify B receives message
   - Test bidirectional communication

5. **Out-of-range behavior**
   - Place two nodes beyond radio range
   - Verify no direct reception
   - Add relay node, verify message delivery

6. **Radio parameter validation**

title: Implement C++ TCP client for LICHEN simulator wire protocol
description:
Implement a C++ TCP client that speaks the LICHEN Medium simulator wire protocol.

Functions to implement:

1. **Connection management**
   - SimClient(host, port) - constructor with connection params
   - connect() / disconnect() - TCP socket lifecycle
   - is_connected() - connection status check

2. **Wire protocol encoding**
   - encode_register(node_id, x, y, z) - MSG_REGISTER (0x01)
   - encode_tx(payload, sf, bw, cr, freq, power) - MSG_TX (0x02)
   - encode_rx_enter() - MSG_RX_ENTER (0x03)
   - encode_rx_exit() - MSG_RX_EXIT (0x04)
   - encode_position_update(x, y, z) - MSG_POSITION (0x05)

3. **Wire protocol decoding**
   - decode_message() - read and dispatch incoming messages
   - RxPacket struct: payload, rssi, snr, timestamp
   - Handle MSG_RX_PACKET (0x82) responses

4. **Threading considerations**
   - Non-blocking receive with poll/select
   - Thread-safe send queue if needed
   - Timeout handling for connection drops
