title: Evaluate Zephyr 3.7 IPSP L2 removal and restoration path
description: Analyze why CONFIG_NET_L2_BT was removed from Zephyr v3.7.0, whether this was intentional deprecation or refactoring, and what path exists to restore IPSP network L2 support. Check Zephyr commit history, mailing list, and upstream issues. Document whether restoration requires backporting, upstreaming a patch, or if IPSP is being replaced by a different mechanism.

title: Write integration tests for bidirectional message flow
description: Write integration tests demonstrating bidirectional message flow between LICHEN and IRC. Tests should cover: LICHEN message appears in mapped IRC channel with correct provenance; IRC message reaches LICHEN recipient through native messaging; unauthorized IRC users are rejected; rate limits and queue bounds are enforced; duplicates are suppressed across reconnect; store-and-forward works across simulated outages; malformed content and oversized messages are rejected. Use the simulator with at least two LICHEN nodes and a mock IRC server. Document test scenarios and expected behavior.

title: Test Zephyr upstream ESP32-S3 IPSP sample build
description: Build the Zephyr upstream IPSP sample (samples/bluetooth/ipsp) targeting ESP32-S3 to establish whether the sample compiles and links. Document any missing Kconfig options, driver gaps, or L2 layer issues. This provides concrete evidence of ESP32-S3 IPSP support status in current Zephyr.

title: Add authentication layer mapping IRC nicks to LICHEN identities (or anonymous gateway mode)
description: Implement an authentication layer that maps IRC nicks/hostmasks to LICHEN identities. Support two modes: (1) Authenticated mode where IRC users are mapped to specific LICHEN /128 identities based on configuration, with cryptographic verification where possible. (2) Anonymous gateway mode where IRC messages are relayed with a gateway-sourced identity clearly marked as bridge-originated. In both modes, preserve verified LICHEN native /128 origin metadata in a stable displayed form. Do not allow impersonation of arbitrary IRC accounts or LICHEN identities.

title: Implement tunnel backend (WireGuard/VPN abstraction)
Implement cellular modem backend with PPP support
Implement IRC to LICHEN relay: listen on IRC channels, POST to /msg/inbox with sender identity
description: Implement the IRC-to-LICHEN direction of the bridge. Listen for messages on configured IRC channels. Check sender authorization against configured nick/hostmask allowlist. Convert authorized IRC messages into LICHEN /msg/inbox POST requests targeting the mapped group/realm. Include sender identity metadata without impersonating arbitrary IRC accounts. Apply message length limits and attachment handling policy. Reject unauthorized users, malformed content, oversized messages, and protocol-control attempts. Implement store-and-forward for LoRa outages.

title: Implement LICHEN to IRC relay: observe /msg/inbox, filter by group, format and send to IRC channels
description: Implement the LICHEN-to-IRC direction of the bridge. Observe the gateway /msg/inbox CoAP endpoint for incoming authenticated LICHEN messages. Filter messages by configured group/realm mappings. Format messages for IRC with origin provenance (native /128 address and timestamp) using IRCv3 message tags when negotiated, falling back to readable text prefix. Apply rate limiting, queue bounds, and UTF-8 validation. Sanitize IRC control codes and CTCP. Implement deduplication using persistent message IDs and bridge-instance IDs.

title: Define configuration schema for LICHEN group/realm to IRC channel mapping
description: Define a configuration schema that maps LICHEN groups/realms to IRC channels. The schema should support: IRC server connection details (host, port, TLS, nick, password), channel-to-group mappings (IRC channel -> LICHEN group/realm), authorization rules (which IRC nicks/hostmasks can send to LICHEN), rate limit parameters, queue bounds, and store-and-forward settings. Use Pydantic or similar for validation. Configuration should be loadable from YAML/JSON files with secrets kept in protected runtime config.

title: Add IRC client dependency (irc3 or pydle) and implement connection handler class
description: Add an async IRC client library (irc3 or pydle) to the Python package dependencies. Implement an IRCConnectionHandler class that manages TLS connections to configurable IRC servers, handles reconnection with exponential backoff, negotiates IRCv3 capabilities where available, and joins configured channels on connect. The handler should emit events for connection state changes and received messages.

title: TX queue C conformance: enforce exhaustive vector case coverage
description: Round-3 security review found scenario validation still covers selected cases/fields only. Cases such as expiry_multiple_packets, routing_never_starved_by_bulk, capacity_enforced_strictly, and some initial packet fields can drift without affecting generated output. Make supported case coverage explicit and exhaustive: either consume/generate every vector case or reject unknown/unconsumed cases and validate all behavior-defining fields.
acceptance_criteria: Every case name in the four TX queue vector documents is explicitly consumed/validated or explicitly declared metadata-only; unexpected cases/fields fail generation; representative generated scenarios drive C behavior; sanitizer-backed tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by host sanitizer suite plus review cycle; superseding round-4 findings are tracked separately

title: LoRa L2 init: reject aborted or deinitializing state
description: Round-3 security review found lichen_lora_l2_init() returns idempotent success for every state other than UNINIT, including LORA_ABORTED after a queue-destroy failure and LORA_DEINITING. This falsely reports initialization although the queue is not reinitialized and start will fail. Limit idempotent success to fully initialized stable states and return an explicit error for aborted/deinitializing states.
acceptance_criteria: Init returns an error in ABORTED and DEINITING states and remains idempotently successful only for valid initialized stable states; tests/builds pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by host sanitizer suite plus review cycle; superseding round-4 findings are tracked separately

title: LoRa L2: preserve queue-destroy retry teardown provenance
description: Round-3 correctness review found normal STOPPED deinit maps tx_queue_destroy failure to generic LORA_ABORTED. Retrying deinit then takes the abort-only RX join path even if RX was never started or was already joined by stop(), potentially failing before the queue destroy retry. Add a distinct queue-destroy-failed lifecycle state or equivalent provenance so retry skips already-completed worker teardown and safely retries only remaining cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: Queue-destroy failure during normal teardown remains non-reinitializable but a subsequent deinit retries destruction without abort-only RX-thread assumptions; abort-origin teardown remains correct; successful retry reaches UNINIT; lifecycle tests/builds pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by host sanitizer suite plus review cycle; superseding round-4 findings are tracked separately

title: TX queue C conformance: consume vector scenario inputs
description: Round-2 security review found behavioral validation pins selected expected labels but ignores the corresponding scenario inputs/operations. A vector can be internally contradictory (for example incoming BULK expected to preempt BULK) and still generate successfully. Validate all behavior-defining scenario paths and generate table-driven inputs/expectations for the C tests, including priority and expiry named cases.
acceptance_criteria: Generator rejects internally inconsistent scenario/expected pairs across bounded, expiry, priority, and implementation vectors; generated C data drives representative expiry, FIFO/alias, preemption, and backpressure operations; negative tests or explicit validation prove scenario mutations fail; sanitizer-backed suite passes.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by host sanitizer suite plus review cycle; superseding round-4 findings are tracked separately

title: TX queue: sample admission time while holding queue lock
description: Round-2 security review found get_now_ms() is sampled before acquiring queue->lock. A caller delayed on the mutex can have its absolute deadline pass yet still be admitted; if high priority, that stale packet can preempt valid traffic before later expiry. Default deadlines are likewise based on a stale pre-lock sample. Acquire the queue lock before sampling time, handle clock failure before queue mutation, compute relative defaults from the locked sample, and preserve expire-before-admission ordering.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit pushes delayed until their deadline are rejected without admission/preemption; default deadlines are based on the time sampled under the queue lock; clock failure occurs before mutation; deterministic race/seam tests and sanitizer-backed suite pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by host sanitizer suite plus review cycle; superseding round-4 findings are tracked separately

title: TX queue: document and enforce destroy quiescence contract
description: Round-2 correctness review found tx_queue_destroy() is not an atomic lifecycle transition: tx_queue_clear() unlocks before pool and mutex teardown, so a concurrent push can enter during destruction. The public type is described as thread-safe but destroy has no external-quiescence precondition. Document that callers must stop/join all queue users before destroy and ensure production L2 follows this ordering; add a lifecycle assertion/state guard if feasible without changing the per-context design.
acceptance_criteria: Public destroy documentation explicitly requires exclusive ownership/no concurrent operations; production teardown visibly quiesces workers before destroy; tests cover the supported lifecycle and no code claims concurrent destroy safety.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by host sanitizer suite plus review cycle; superseding round-4 findings are tracked separately

title: TX queue tests: prevent generated vector header shadowing
description: Security review found that main.c includes tx_queue_vectors.h with quotes, so a source-tree header of that name is searched before CMake's binary include directory and can silently shadow the generated canonical-vector artifact while the build still reports generation success. Force inclusion of a uniquely named binary-generated header using include-search semantics that cannot prefer the source directory.
acceptance_criteria: The test source cannot resolve a same-named source-tree header ahead of the generated build artifact; CMake has an explicit dependency on the generated header; normal and sanitizer-backed CTest pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by host sanitizer suite plus review cycle; superseding round-4 findings are tracked separately

title: TX queue: make clear/destroy retryable on frame-pool release failure
description: Security review found that tx_queue_clear() ignores lichen_frame_pool_release() failures and marks entries invalid, while POSIX tx_queue_destroy() destroys the mutex before frame-pool destruction. A release failure can lose the live handle and then return EBUSY after synchronization is irreversibly destroyed, making retry unsafe. Preserve entry validity on release failure, expose/propagate clear failure, and order destroy operations so a failed destroy leaves a retryable object. Update every caller and declaration.
acceptance_criteria: Clear returns and propagates frame release errors without discarding live handles; destroy does not destroy queue synchronization until the frame pool is successfully releasable/destroyed; failure-injection tests prove retry succeeds; all declarations/callers/stubs compile and sanitizer-backed tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by host sanitizer suite plus review cycle; superseding round-4 findings are tracked separately

title: TX queue: eliminate FIFO half-range sequence ambiguity
description: Security/robustness review found that uint32_t enqueue_order plus signed half-range comparison can reverse FIFO/preemption ordering when one long-lived low-priority entry remains queued while at least 2^31 higher-priority enqueue/pop operations advance the sequence. Explicit deadlines may remain live for INT32_MAX ms, so the current adjacency-only wrap test does not prove the API invariant. Use an ordering representation or renormalization that cannot become ambiguous for live entries and add a half-range-gap regression test.
acceptance_criteria: FIFO and oldest-lowest preemption remain correct across uint32 half-range/full-wrap gaps without relying on packet enqueue rates; regression tests exercise a synthetic gap >=2^31; sanitizer-backed host tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by host sanitizer suite plus review cycle; superseding round-4 findings are tracked separately

title: No-PIV sent_response commit precedes encryption permanently refusing identical retry after AEAD fault
description: oscore_protect.c:721 commits sent_response correlation before encrypt :742; encrypt-fail retry then REPLAY-refused. Judged safe/fails-closed (matches lost-response; real retransmissions refused earlier by replay_reserve_pending) but commit is infallible RAM op under held mutex: moving after successful encrypt eliminates residual preserving zero-caller-bytes. Recommendation-grade improvement.
close_reason: Moved the no-PIV sent_response correlation commit in protect_response (oscore_protect.c) from before the AEAD call to AFTER successful lichen_aes_ccm_encrypt. The commit is still an infallible RAM write under the same continuously-held mutex (the no-PIV path locks at identity binding and never releases until cleanup), and the acceptability gate still runs under that same hold, so no concurrent commit can interleave; the commit simply now cannot precede the last fallible step. Failure semantics preserved exactly: zero-caller-bytes guarantee untouched (encrypt remains the only caller-buffer writer; sentinel-prefill check proves ct/opt untouched on fault), and on OSCORE_ERR_ENCRYPT_FAILED the window is now left UNCHANGED so a genuine retry of the identical correlation succeeds - this is the intended improvement (previously permanently REPLAY-refused). Re-ran the response-replay bit-exact harness pattern from prior review (temp dir oscmargin-verify, REAL oscore TUs + vendored monocypher + tinycrypt AES-CCM linked under renamed symbols reached through fault-injectable forwarders, stub zephyr headers, ASan+UBSan). Output pasted: 1: no-PIV response OK (ct_len=9, opt_len=0) / 1: duplicate correlation refused REPLAY (committed once) / [fault] encrypt call #4 injected failure / 2: AEAD fault -> ENCRYPT_FAILED, zero caller bytes (ct/opt sentinels intact) / 3: genuine retry after fault OK (would be REPLAY pre-1o6h) / 3: retry ciphertext BIT-EXACT to never-faulted oracle (9 bytes) / 4: post-retry duplicate refused REPLAY (commit-after-encrypt holds) / 5: with_piv path still bit-exact across sibling contexts / RESPONSE-REPLAY HARNESS OK. The bit-exact oracle is an independent twin context with identical master/IDs that never faulted - retry output equals what the first attempt would have produced. SECURITY comment at the encrypt site updated to describe the new ordering; also folded in the w9fw fresh-PIV margin wording (rollback equality check self-disables after the margin advance, skipped sequences never reused). Syntax matrix clean across all 7 oscore TUs at PT_MAX 256/2048 x MAX_CONTEXTS 8/32.

title: Inconsistent NULL-options error code between unprotect_request and unprotect_response siblings
description: oscore_protect.c:508-511 unprotect_request returns OSCORE_ERR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL for options==NULL with opt_out_len>0; :979-981 unprotect_response returns OSCORE_ERR_INVALID_PARAM for identical condition; both dropped old size-query mode. Pick one code, document removed query mode in both headers.
close_reason: Unified on OSCORE_ERR_INVALID_PARAM for the NULL-options-with-content condition. Majority convention ruled: protect_response (all NULL outputs -> INVALID_PARAM) and unprotect_response (NULL options/payload with content -> INVALID_PARAM) already treat NULL buffers as caller-contract violations while reserving BUFFER_TOO_SMALL for insufficient capacity, so oscore_unprotect_request (oscore_protect.c) was the odd one out and is the single site changed: the previously merged condition was split so NULL options (opt_out_len>0) or NULL payload (pay_len>0) now return OSCORE_ERR_INVALID_PARAM while capacity shortfalls keep OSCORE_ERR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL, exactly mirroring the response sibling's structure. title: protect_response call-frame stack roughly doubled by ciphertext_tmp buffer
description: File: lichen/subsys/lichen/oscore/oscore_protect.c:531. Consolidated protect_response adds ciphertext_tmp[PT_MAX+TAG] atop plaintext/aad/snapshots (~340B->~620B default PT_MAX=256; ~4.3KB frame at Kconfig max 2048) on thread stacks provisioned for old profile incl. memory-constrained STM32WL baseline. Options: encrypt into caller buffer after full validation (restore publish-order w/ partial-output guarantee care), shared scratch between request/response paths, or Kconfig-documented static assertion of required headroom. Measure then choose smallest-change option.
close_reason: Eliminated ciphertext_tmp[PT_MAX+TAG] from protect_response() entirely (preferred direct approach; smallest-change fallbacks not needed). Mirrored the request-path lifecycle (oscore_protect_request encrypts straight into the caller buffer): every failure-prone step (capacity checks, context validation, NVM persist_ssn, slot-recycle re-validation under re-locked mutex, sent-response replay commit, AAD build, option_tmp assembly) now completes BEFORE the single lichen_aes_ccm_encrypt call, which writes directly into the caller-visible ciphertext as the final fallible action; fresh_reserved cleared and out-params published only after it. Partial-output guarantee preserved for every policy/validation/NVM failure: zero caller-visible bytes written. Residual, documented in a SECURITY comment at the encrypt site: if the AEAD primitive itself faults (hardware-error territory with pre-validated sizes), partial bytes may land in the caller buffer, and (a) fresh-PIV path keeps the already-persisted NVM SSN rolled forward (RAM-side rollback in cleanup still applies; sequence gap is safe per the two-class model), (b) no-PIV path leaves the sent-response window committed so an identical retry is REPLAY-refused, matching the existing lost-response behavior. Chosen over shared-static scratch (new global-state locking discipline, larger correctness risk) and over STATIC_ASSERT headroom documentation (documents cost instead of removing it). Stack delta measured against Kconfig: frame shrinks by PT_MAX+8 bytes; default PLAINTEXT_MAX=256: -264B (~620B to ~356B call frame, -43%); Kconfig max 2048: -2056B (~4.3KB to ~2.3KB, -48%), directly relieving provisioned STM32WL stacks. Verified: clang -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra on all 7 oscore TUs (protect/ctx/replay/option/nonce/cbor/hkdf) against the real repo headers via stub zephyr/tinycrypt sandbox, at both default and max Kconfig configs, clean; response-replay semantics preserved byte-for-byte on the reachable domain (gate -> nonce -> AAD -> commit -> encrypt ordering keeps AAD-failure paths commit-free as before); crypto_wipe of the removed buffer deleted with it.

description: File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py:171. Bare float(value) with 10**400 input crashes add_drop; suppress(OverflowError) blocks cover only int() paths. Not wire-reachable (codec finite check gives 4.00) but direct/mesh callers crash rather than MAX_TTL clamp. Wrap or clamp.
close_reason: float(huge-int expires) no longer raises OverflowError out of add_drop/render_post paths: _numeric_value converts int/Decimal through guarded float(), returning +/-math.inf beyond float range; _extract_ttl's existing suppressed int() conversion then clamps +huge to DEADDROP_MAX_TTL and -huge to immediate expiry. Added regressions: 10**400 expires clamps to MAX_TTL (not default), -10**400 expires immediate-expiry, and wire-path huge-int remains 4.00 via codec finiteness validation. tests/coap -k deaddrop: 71 passed.

title: Decimal-valued expires bypasses _numeric_value and resurrects expired drop at DEFAULT_TTL
description: File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py:148-152,174-180. Codec _validate_field_type accepts Decimal as num so hand-built/add_drop records legitimately carry it; isinstance(int,float) check misses -> falls to DEFAULT_TTL violating no-resurrection invariant this bead established. Wire path safe (CBOR tags rejected). Fix: accept Decimal in _numeric_value or reject Decimal expires explicitly.
close_reason: _numeric_value now accepts finite Decimal (codec-admitted num type), converting via float() and clamping beyond-float-range values to +/-inf; non-finite Decimals rejected to None like bools/non-numerics. Decimal past-expires drops can no longer resurrect at DEFAULT_TTL. Regression tests: decimal future-remaining, decimal past-no-resurrection (listing empty + storage count 0), NaN-Decimal -> default-ttl observation via raw CBOR oracle. Wire path unchanged (CBOR tags still rejected at _decode_single_cbor). tests/coap -k deaddrop: 71 passed.

title: sos_alert accepts NaN/Inf/out-of-range coordinates contradicting documented invariant
description: Files: lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/include/lichen/sos_alert.h:87-88,131 + sos_alert.c:362-367,238-311,537-546. Header documents lat[-90,90]/lon[-180,180]; decoder validates neither; f16 exp31/f32/f64 non-finite values decode and round-trip with has_location=true feeding SOS dispatch/blue-force consumers. Policy decision needed: reject non-finite and/or range-enforce, document chosen behavior; update vectors.
close_reason: sos_alert.c now rejects non-finite (f16 exp31 NaN/Inf incl signed qNaN, f32 inf/nan, f64 nan) and out-of-range finite coords with SOS_ALERT_ERR_INVALID_VALUE via coordinate_in_range() at lat/lon decode sites; header doc updated. Vectors: 6 negative entries added to test/vectors/sos_cbor.json per receipt_cbor.json precedent (no cbor_hex so python wire-contract consumer unaffected). Verified: all 5 canonical vectors decode+re-encode byte-identical; 7 reject classes return err 8; +-90/+-180 boundary accepted (ASan+UBSan driver over real sos_alert.c, exit=0). python pytest: test_vector_consumers_lci.py -k sos 20 passed; test_security_app_vector_consumers.py 94 passed; cppcheck exit=0.

description: File: lichen/subsys/lichen/oscore/oscore_ctx.c:348-366,332 + oscore_protect.c:124-142. free() wipes struct but not s_seq_initialized[idx]; protect_request checks only idx>=0+flag never active/identity, so stale pointer increments counter and encrypts under zeroed keys returning OK; recycled-slot reuse could encrypt under another peer key. Mirror fix b: clear flag in free() and/or revalidate active+identity in protect_request.

title: Stale/replayed sync frames can inflate advertised stratum label via -EALREADY path
description: File: lichen/subsys/lichen/link/time_sync.c:332-338. Accepted -EALREADY branch overwrites s_stratum even without fresh SFN advance; link-authenticated-but-stale upstream frames claim higher quality label gaining adoption preference. Impact bounded (range enforced 0..3, wall clock untouched, gated elsewhere) but fix belongs here: refresh stratum only when set_sfn returned 0 or never increase current.

Stale link-authenticated frames can no longer inflate or degrade the advertised label. Variant chosen: strict fresh-advance gate, consistent with set_sfn's strictly-advancing freshness model and simpler than monotonic-label tracking.

title: TDMA static latch can initialize before load_key freezing stale epoch-derived slot
description: File: lichen/subsys/lichen/link/lichen_link_tx.c:47-64 lazily initializes function-static tdma_ctx above has_key check capturing ctx->epoch at first TX; later load_key rotates epoch but tdma_init_done latch prevents slot recomputation -> node hashed onto stale slot indefinitely. Inert today (time source FIXME), live once wired. Violates AGENTS.md init graph ordering requirement. Fix: latch after successful key load or recompute on epoch change.
close_reason: lichen_link_tx.c TDMA gate moved below has_key/ENOKEY check so lazy tdma_init can no longer freeze an epoch-derived slot from a keyless context; static latch extended with tdma_epoch_seen and re-inits whenever ctx->epoch rotates after load_key (init-done flag respected; exactly-once init per epoch). Aligns with AGENTS.md init graph load_key->tdma_init. Verified by clang -fsyntax-only; tx-path EBUSY/ENOKEY ordering audited against test suite (no assertions depend on old order; slot-0 pass-through behavior at now=0 unchanged). FIXME time source left out of scope.

title: lichen_link_set_slot accepts sentinel slot_id==0xff when ctx==NULL
description: File: lichen/subsys/lichen/link/tdma.c:102. With auto-derive sentinel 0xff and ctx NULL the function proceeds, storing slot=0xff instead of returning -EINVAL; subsequent tdma_tx_allowed computes nonsense offsets. Carried over verbatim during dedup. Fix: return -EINVAL when slot_id==0xff && ctx==NULL before assignment.

title: TDMA u32 overflow in slot_start product; init passes epoch where spec wants SFN
description: File: lichen/subsys/lichen/link/tdma.c:117,29,103. superframe*n_slots*d wraps mod 2^32 for large SFN producing inverted/non-monotonic windows; lichen_tdma_init and lichen_link_set_slot pass ctx->epoch as SFN arg of lichen_tdma_compute_slot while spec/02a section 2a.4 defines Slot=(fnv1a32(EUI64)+u32(SFN)) mod n over beacon SFN. Pre-existing, elevated now tdma.c is canonical. Fix: 64-bit intermediates/frame-relative phase; wire real beacon SFN; wrap vectors.
close_reason: Fixed: (1) tdma_tx_allowed schedule product widened to u64 intermediates with explicit mod-2^32 reduction per spec/02a 2a.2 unsigned rule (exact homomorphic reduction, kyn9 modular contract preserved bit-for-bit); (2) lichen_tdma_init and set_slot sentinel path no longer substitute key-rotation ctx->epoch for beacon SFN - init uses SFN-0 baseline, sentinel derives from the sfn argument per 2a.2 Slot=(fnv1a32(EUI64)+u32(SFN)) mod n. Battery extended: Case D first-product-overflow SFN=2147484 (start mod 2^32 = 1954, window [1954,2104) hand-computed), Case E sentinel derivation pinned to ccp_sfn_wrap_slot_hash.json (sfn=1,n=16->14; sfn=FFFFFFFF,n=3->2). Verified: clang -fsyntax-only tdma.c OK; real tdma.c+link_ctx.c+tx_queue.c ASan/UBSan harness green incl. all kyn9 A-C cases; python TDMAScheduler/slot_for equivalence PASS (13 hash vectors + 24 timing probes, same-frame domain); cppcheck clean. Discovered-and-filed enyo: pre-existing (HEAD) main.c schnorr48 call-site arity breakage outside scope.

title: msg POST ignores Content-Format
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/messaging.py

Robustness: MessagesResource.render_post and MessageReceiptsResource.render_post decode request.payload as CBOR with no check of request.opt.content_format. Spec 18.1.2 / 18.1.3 examples and resource advertisements use Content-Format 60 (application/cbor). Sibling PresenceResource.render_put rejects a present non-CBOR Content-Format with 4.00.

Impact: a client that sends CF=0 (text/plain) or SenML 112 with CBOR-looking bytes is accepted and mutates inbox/sent/receipts. Wrong-format payloads that happen to be valid CBOR maps are stored as messages.

Not covered by l9dn (field types inside a CBOR map).
acceptance_criteria: POST /msg/inbox, POST /msg/sent, POST /messages, and POST /msg/ack with a present Content-Format other than 60 return 4.00 and do not mutate inbox, sent, receipts, or _next_id. Missing Content-Format MAY still be accepted as CBOR (RFC 7252 default) or rejected; pick one and test it. PresenceResource CF check is the local pattern.
close_reason: Closed

title: PresenceCacheResource.record does not treat addr as IPv6
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/presence.py PresenceCacheResource.record / evict / snapshot

Spec 18.5.2 cache entries use IPv6 addr (example 0200:...:1111). record() only validates via PresenceCacheEntry.from_mapping, and _require_addr accepts any non-empty string. The dict is keyed on that raw string.

Consequences:
- "0200::1111" and "0200:0:0:0:0:0:0:1111" (and case variants) are distinct peers; GET/Observe emit duplicates.
- evict() must be called with the exact recorded spelling or it is a no-op.
- Garbage or unbounded addr strings are stored and serialized to every observer.

Distinct from k208 (entry count / TTL) and 7gk6 (decoder nodes-array size). Fix belongs at record(): parse as IPv6 and store one canonical form.
acceptance_criteria: record() rejects non-IPv6 addr. Equivalent IPv6 spellings occupy one cache slot and evict() hits that slot. Tests cover compressed vs expanded form.
close_reason: Closed

title: DeadDrop rate-limit buckets never reap idle identities
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py
Perspective: robustness

Spec 18.9: 6 POSTs per hour per OSCORE context. _prune_old_requests(context_id) only walks that one key, and only when check_rate_limit/record runs for it (deaddrop.py ~261-271). Empty lists are deleted; idle keys with old timestamps stay until that same identity posts again.

ConfessionsResource explicitly reaps stale rate buckets. DeadDropResource does not.

Evidence: N distinct bound identities each POST once. _request_times holds N keys forever (until process restart), even after every timestamp is older than 3600s, because no later check_rate_limit(context_id) is invoked for those ids.

Impact: rate-limit state grows with the number of OSCORE peers (and with test-injected ids) rather than with the 1-hour window. On a long-lived node this is unbounded RAM versus the 8KB/32KB drop budget.

Oracle: spec window is 1 hour; idle buckets must be reclaimable. See confessions.py _reap_stale_rate_buckets.
acceptance_criteria: Idle per-context timestamp lists older than the 1-hour window are dropped without waiting for that context to POST again. A sequence of distinct OSCORE identities each posting once must not grow _request_times without bound. ConfessionsResource._reap_stale_rate_buckets is a template.
close_reason: Closed

title: group_multicast_from_id leaks UnicodeEncodeError
description:
## Problem

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py group_multicast_from_id() documents AddrError for bad group ids and already rejects non-str and empty. The 16-bit group field is SHA-256(UTF-8(id))[0:2].

A Python str with unpaired surrogates is type str and non-empty, so it passes the guard, then:

  group_id.encode('utf-8')  # UnicodeEncodeError: surrogates not allowed

Verified: group_multicast_from_id('\\ud800') raises UnicodeEncodeError, not AddrError. Every other public helper in this file maps stdlib value errors to AddrError (to_ipv6, make_link_local zone parse, native_address_from_pubkey).

## Why it matters

Callers (CoAP /groups) catch AddrError. A lone surrogate in a group name escapes that handler and becomes a 5.00 instead of 4.00.

## Where

python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py:254-268 group_multicast_from_id
python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_collection.py:121-123 mcast_from_id
design: Keep SHA-256(UTF-8(id)) as specified. Catch UnicodeEncodeError from group_id.encode('utf-8') and raise AddrError from it, same as to_ipv6 wrapping ValueError. Do not NFC-normalize unless the spec adds that; this issue is only the exception type at the public boundary. Empty/non-str already raise AddrError.
acceptance_criteria: group_multicast_from_id('\ud800') raises AddrError (not UnicodeEncodeError). group_multicast_from_id('team-alpha') still matches the pinned SHA-256 high-16 oracle 0x29c4. Existing empty/non-str tests still raise AddrError.
close_reason: Closed

title: POST /location returning 404 (test_sensors_location_no_post) conflicts with RFC 7252 + C cross-impl contract
description: python/tests/coap/test_lci_auth.py::TestObservableAuth::test_sensors_location_no_post asserts POST /location -> NOT_FOUND while GET /location on the same mounted SenMLLocationResource returns CONTENT. RFC 7252 mandates 4.05 Method Not Allowed for an existing resource that does not implement a method; 4.04 asserts the URI matches no resource. Cross-impl contract disagrees too: C coap_location.c sensors_location_post returns 401 (non-admin) / 201 (admin), never 404, and no vector in test/vectors/coap_lci_auth.json encodes a 404 location case; spec/appendix-senml.md defines /sensors/location as GET-only observable. Resolution needs either a test correction (expect 4.05) or an explicit spec decision to implement admin-gated POST semantics mirroring the C stack.

title: Couple atomic publication bound to rollback readability
description: Correctness review of icxb found atomic_write_json_batch enforces _MAX_OUTPUT_ARTIFACT_BYTES independently from _MAX_RECOVERY_ARTIFACT_BYTES. If configuration or tests lower the recovery bound without also lowering the output bound, the writer can publish a new artifact that its next transaction refuses to back up. Cap each encoded artifact by min(publication_limit, recovery_limit), retain aggregate enforcement, and adjust the exact-bound regression to prove the replacement remains recovery-readable.

title: Bound and no-follow all vector generator check reads
description: Modified generator --check paths in test/vectors/generate_authenticated_schc_dio.py, generate_packets_timing.py, generate_announce_signed_data.py, generate_ipv6_addresses.py, generate_dao_origin_signature.py and related generators use Path.read_bytes/read_text without O_NOFOLLOW, ownership/type checks, stable snapshot checks, or a byte limit. A symlink or oversized canonical artifact can make a read-only determinism check follow an unintended file or exhaust memory. Add one shared bounded no-follow exact snapshot reader in atomic_json.py, use it for every generator check, and test symlink, nonregular, concurrent growth/change, and oversized artifacts while preserving zero-write --check behavior.

title: Validate DaoManager resource and clock configuration exactly
description: python/src/lichen/rpl/dao_manager.py __post_init__ only compares capacities and timing values numerically. bools, floats, infinities, and NaN can pass: for example max_targets=float('nan') disables len > max_targets enforcement, and NaN lifetime_unit_seconds/freshness_retention_seconds or clock results create invalid deadlines that never expire. Validate all capacities as exact positive bounded ints, pcs/rpl IDs/sequences as exact bounded ints, timing configuration and every clock/now_seconds sample as finite non-negative values with the required monotonic policy before replay-floor persistence or route mutation. Add bool/float/NaN/infinity/huge-bound and failing-clock tests.

title: Make DAO vector --check enforce canonical bytes
description: test/vectors/generate_dao_origin_signature.py --check parses the existing JSON and compares Python objects, unlike the other hardened generators. Reordered keys, altered indentation, duplicate keys collapsed by json.loads, or other noncanonical byte changes pass while the command reports deterministic generation. Compare OUTPUT.read_bytes() against atomic_json.json_bytes(document) byte-for-byte with bounded safe reading, preserve read-only behavior, and add CLI tests for formatting, key-order, duplicate-key, missing, and oversized artifacts.

title: TrustStore accepts a no-op same-key rotation as a new key generation
description: CORRECTNESS: TrustStore._rotate_key validates the signed transcript and destination collision only when new_iid differs, but never requires new_pubkey != old_pubkey. A caller can sign a rotation from a key to itself, receive success, advance the persisted rotation sequence, and replace the entry/timestamps even though spec 06 defines this as a key change that accepts a new key. Downstream rotation consumers may also treat success as authority to create fresh replay state. Align with the link rotation invariant by rejecting identical old/new keys before mutation; cover durable and semantic APIs.
