Parse and reject arguments explicitly, implement byte-exact --check behavior through json_bytes(), and test that check mode performs no replacement or mtime change.

title: lichend leaves an unzeroized identity-seed copy in its long-lived main frame
description: Security review finding: lichend copies *seed.as_bytes() into a plain [u8;32] sealing_seed before constructing trust/slot/GatewayPersistence owners. The local remains in the async main state for the daemon lifetime and is never zeroized; GatewayPersistence also holds a plain array until new_persistent moves/copies it, including early-error paths. This defeats the Zeroizing fields added to the eventual owners and leaves an unnecessary private-key duplicate in stack/future memory. Carry the seed as Zeroizing<[u8;32]> end-to-end (including GatewayPersistence), minimize copies, and explicitly zeroize the caller's buffer immediately after all owners derive/move their protected material; exercise early returns.

title: Link replay vector fixture types are not feature-gated with their test
description: rust/lichen-link/tests/shared_vectors.rs gates test_replay_window_vectors on schnorr+std but leaves its three serde fixture structs unconditional. Clippy -D warnings for the supported schnorr without std feature set fails with dead_code. Apply the same cfg to the fixture types (or otherwise align their compilation with the test).

title: Rust native-address documentation still labels exact 0200 prefix as /7
description: Rust production code constructs and routes native addresses with byte 0 exactly 0x02, matching the resolved 0200::/8 profile, but lichen-core/src/addr.rs, lichen-gateway/src/config.rs, and gateway trust docs still describe 0200::/7 and /7 dispersion. This contradicts API invariants and can lead callers to admit 0x03 addresses. Update Rust documentation/comments to exact /8 terminology; do not alter canonical derivation bytes.

title: Remove the legacy EUI/ULA identity model from the canonical IPv6 API
description: P3 protocol correctness: python/src/lichen/ipv6/addr.py and its tests still present a node Identity derived from arbitrary EUI-64 plus mutable ULA/GUA prefix assignment, while the resolved architecture says one Ed25519 key derives the IID/link-local/native 0200::/8 address and ULA is not used. The duplicate Identity name and exported AddressManager/make_ula APIs let callers construct identities and scopes that cannot satisfy current trust/SCHC/routing bindings. Replace or clearly quarantine these generic helpers, expose the key-derived native scope in the canonical API, and update tests/docs so no supported Node identity path advertises ULA.

title: Enforce immutable exact primitive types in AnnounceMessage
description: P3 security/robustness: frozen AnnounceMessage validates only len/ranges, so bool sequences/channels, str values of matching length, and mutable bytearray/memoryview identity, signature, or app_data can pass construction (including from_bytes on non-bytes input) and later fail inconsistently or mutate after a trust check. Enforce exact int (not bool) and immutable bytes for every wire/security field, bound app data to the link-profile maximum, and add constructor/parser mutation/type tests.

title: Replace stale source-line anchors in SCHC specifications
description: The reviewed SCHC docs still make exact-behavior claims through mutable source line anchors: spec/appendix-schc.md cites schc.h:93, constants.toml:29-36, and option.rs:33; spec/03-adaptation.md cites rules.py:290; draft-lichen-schc-lora-00.md cites rules.rs:503 and :257. These anchors have already drifted (for example current Rule 7/specialized registry layout no longer corresponds to those numbers), so readers can be sent to unrelated definitions. Replace them with stable spec section/table names and file/module references while retaining independent normative text. Spec-only; no C/Zephyr work.

title: Cross-interop test executes stale hard-coded Rust frame parser
description: python/tests/sim/test_cross_impl_interop.py executes rust/target/release/frame-parser whenever that path merely exists. In the merged tree the checked build artifact predates SIID support and returns ReservedBitSet for every valid new signed vector, so the Python full gate fails even though rebuilt Rust source may be correct; the test also ignores CARGO_TARGET_DIR used by isolated gates. Make the harness build/use the current locked workspace artifact (or verify source/artifact freshness and skip with a precise reason), and cover the SIID vectors against that current binary.

title: Define DAO two-slot generation exhaustion behavior
description: P3 robustness/security: TwoSlotFilePersistence computes max(gen0, gen1)+1 and serializes as >I without handling 0xffffffff. At exhaustion every subsequent TX/RX replay-floor commit raises raw struct.error, permanently disabling DAO operation rather than a defined fail-closed persistence error or safe epoch transition. Validate generation arithmetic, surface DaoPersistenceError, and specify/test exhaustion recovery without permitting rollback.

title: Align receipt-clock tamper test with terminal security error
description: python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py::test_link_receipt_clock_requires_exact_immutable_capability expects the internal 'binding changed' RuntimeError to escape, but LinkLayer._receipt_now intentionally converts all terminal clock failures into LinkSecurityClockError with the internal RuntimeError as __cause__ after revoking authenticated state. The fully merged timing suite therefore fails. Update the test to assert LinkSecurityClockError, terminal disablement/revocation, and a binding-changed cause rather than requiring the internal message at the public boundary.

title: Packets/timing --check crashes when an output file is missing
description: generate_packets_timing.py --check calls Path.read_bytes in a comprehension without handling FileNotFoundError. A missing generated output is simply an out-of-date result and should be reported with exit status 1 while remaining read-only, not emit a traceback. Add a missing-output CLI regression.

title: Make standalone gateway current-slot helper honor slots-per-superframe
description: P3 correctness/API invariant: rust/lichen-gateway/src/slot.rs current_slot_from_timestamp(timestamp, duration_s, start) returns elapsed seconds modulo duration and has no slots_per_superframe parameter. It is only a slot index when every slot is exactly one second; the same module's validated SuperframeConfig supports arbitrary duration_s/slots_per_superframe and correctly scales . Calling the public standalone helper for e.g. 60 seconds/240 slots returns 0..59 instead of 0..239 and can schedule transmission in the wrong quarter of the superframe. Remove/deprecate the inconsistent helper or accept validated slot dimensions and share the SuperframeConfig calculation; add non-1-second-slot vectors and reject timestamps before the configured epoch rather than silently saturating if the protocol requires synchronized time.

title: Update Rust link wire documentation and signed-frame length regression test
description: rust/lichen-link/src/lib.rs still documents bit 7 as reserved and omits the mandatory 8-byte signer EUI-64 from the wire layout; LinkLayer docs also claim frames lack a sender hint and require O(n) verification although SI now provides indexed lookup. In rust/lichen-link/src/schnorr.rs si_frame_serialises_and_verifies computes signed LENGTH without signer_eui64.len(), so it signs a length different from the serialized wire and never verifies the parsed wire transcript. Update source docs and make the regression test derive/verify the exact serialized LENGTH.

title: packets/timing vector generator treats --check as a destructive regeneration
description: test/vectors/generate_packets_timing.py ignores argv and always rewrites both canonical JSON outputs. Unlike sibling generators, invoking it with --check still mutates packets-formats.json and packets-timing.json and reports Wrote, so CI/review commands intended only to detect drift can bless or clobber authoritative vectors. Parse arguments explicitly, implement a non-writing byte/JSON comparison for --check, reject unknown arguments, and regress output mtimes/content on check and usage errors.

title: Atomic JSON batch can leave mixed canonical vector generations
description: test/vectors/atomic_json.py:atomic_write_json_batch prepares files then calls os.replace sequentially with no transaction marker or inter-process lock. A process crash after the first replace bypasses Python rollback and leaves packets-formats.json and packets-timing.json from different generations; concurrent generators can also interleave replacements into a mixed pair. These JSON files are cross-implementation security/protocol oracles, so mixed publication can silently validate an incoherent contract. Add a lock plus recoverable manifest/generation commit protocol, or publish one versioned bundle and atomically switch a single pointer; add crash-point and concurrent-writer tests.

title: Implement diagnostics for Rust link persistent-state errors
description: Robustness review of wm48 found public LinkPersistentStateError lacks Display and std::error::Error, unlike existing public link errors. This prevents downstream persistence coordinators from preserving actionable error context. Add stable messages/source behavior and tests.
notes: Added stable Display and Error implementations for public LinkPersistentStateError plus diagnostic coverage. Link tests/clippy pass.

title: SCHC clock failure leaves stale issued-sender capabilities globally registered
description: The new y4vw fail-stop cleanup clears SchcSessionManager._prepared/_records but leaves each externally referenced FragmentSender in module-global _ISSUED_MANAGERS. A terminally disabled manager can therefore retain stale issuance entries until every user handle is garbage-collected, and repeated failed manager instances can grow the global registry despite per-manager bounds. On clock-failure cleanup, atomically remove issuance entries that still point to this exact manager/sender while preserving unrelated agents/managers; add regression proving a pre-failure sender no longer resolves through the issuance registry.

title: Gate Rust peer-generation allocator to its production owner features
description: lichen-link no-default build emits dead_code warnings because NEXT_PEER_KEY_GENERATION and PeerKeyGeneration::allocate exist without the schnorr+std-gated LinkLayer that owns generation allocation. Gate allocator state/method to the same features so no-default remains warning-free while the opaque token type remains available to no_std upper layers.
notes: Feature-gated runtime/durable generation allocators and replay persistence helpers to their std+schnorr owner; no-default build is warning-free and all-target clippy passes.

title: SFN helpers accept non-octet and non-integer protocol inputs
description: python/src/lichen/timing/sfn.py hash_32/slot_for only check len(eui64), so bytearray/list inputs and non-octet integer sequences can be hashed; sfn_delta performs bitwise arithmetic without exact-int validation and accepts booleans as counters. Protocol-facing helpers should require exact bytes for EUI-64 and exact integers for u32 counters/slot counts, normalize documented out-of-range SFNs only after type validation, and test bool/float/list/bytearray inputs.

title: Node timing and jitter config accepts coercive non-integer values
description: Node validates receive_timeout_ms exactly, but the rest of its timing configuration is inconsistent: SchedulerConfig comparisons accept bool/float values; Node.set_config coerces announce_interval_ms via int(), accepting True and truncating positive floats; scheduled_send passes unvalidated rreq_jitter_min_ms/max_ms or caller overrides to random.randint and permits negative delays/runtime TypeError. Enforce exact integer/range/order validation at Node construction and runtime update boundaries (preserving atomic updates), with bool/float/string, negative, min>max, and excessive-bound tests.

title: CoAP vector integration tests hard-code obsolete vector cardinalities
description: python/tests/test_node_coap_integration.py asserts deaddrop.json and confessions.json each contain exactly four vectors, but the canonical artifacts now contain 18 and 17 valid vectors. This fails before validating any payloads and makes normal vector growth a test break. Replace cardinality literals with semantic required-case/name/category coverage and iterate every current vector, retaining CoAP/SenML validation.

title: DAO vector generator can truncate its canonical JSON on interruption
description: test/vectors/generate_dao_origin_signature.py still writes dao_origin_signature.json with Path.write_text(), unlike the other modified vector generators' same-directory fsync-and-replace helper. A process interruption, disk-full error, or serializer/write failure after truncation can leave the checked-in canonical DAO vector empty or partial; --check then only reports a parse failure and cannot recover it. Serialize first and use the shared atomic JSON writer while preserving the existing deterministic --check behavior; add injected write/replace failure coverage proving the prior destination survives.

title: slot_for accepts non-integer num_slots and can return a float slot index
description: Correctness/type-contract review of python/src/lichen/timing/sfn.py found slot_for only checks num_slots <= 0. A value such as 2.5 passes validation and Python modulo returns a float, violating the declared int return and producing an invalid TDMA slot index; True is also accepted as one slot. Enforce an exact positive integer num_slots (excluding bool), document the chosen unsigned-32 SFN normalization contract, and add invalid-type boundary tests independent of the generator oracle.
notes: Implemented exact-int validation for num_slots and SFN, documented u32 normalization, added bool/float/string/None boundary tests. Awaiting 3x review; do not close yet.

title: LichenFrame serializer does not enforce its declared field types
description: Correctness/type-contract review of python/src/lichen/link/frame.py found _validate only exact-checks mic_length. Values such as epoch=True or seqnum=True are accepted as counters; floats can pass range checks and later raise AttributeError at to_bytes(); a non-AddrMode addr_mode fails through an incidental attribute error; and non-bool signature_present/encrypted values are treated by truthiness. This yields exceptions outside FrameError and permits noncanonical caller state despite a protocol serializer API. Validate exact AddrMode, bool flags, exact int epoch/seqnum excluding bool, and bytes fields before arithmetic/serialization; add exhaustive invalid-type tests and retain FrameError (or a clearly documented TypeError contract) consistently.

title: Label parser-only signed-frame fixture as cryptographically invalid
description: Security review found spec/test-vectors/frame.json names frame_with_signature a signed frame with a Schnorr-48 MIC, but its 48 bytes are a repeated 0x55 placeholder and the artifact supplies no public key/transcript or explicit parser-only validity marker. Python and Rust tests accept it as a structurally valid parsed frame and never verify the signature. Although test/vectors/link_frame.json contains real independent signatures, the spec-level fixture can be mistaken for an authentication-positive vector and normalize treating S=1 plus 48 bytes as authenticated. Mark this case explicitly structural/parser-only with authentication_expected=false (or replace it with an independently valid signature and key metadata), and make consumer tests assert that parsing is not authentication; retain independent negative verification coverage for invalid 48-byte MICs.

title: SCHC retransmissions silently evict other sessions' unsent wire capabilities
description: Security codereview finding in python/src/lichen/schc/fragment.py: _issue_fragment_wire_unlocked inserts each one-use _IssuedFragmentWire into a global OrderedDict and blindly popitem(last=False) above MAX_ISSUED_FRAGMENT_WIRES. The cap equals only the maximum initial output for 64 two-window sessions (64*126); any ACK-driven repair/retransmission while that legitimate capacity is outstanding evicts another live session's unsent authority. Its later LinkLayer.send fails as stale, so one receiver controlling negative ACK timing can cause cross-peer transfer failures. Never silently evict a live issued capability: reserve/budget per active session including maximum repair output, consume/revoke deterministically, or fail the requesting transition atomically without harming other sessions; add saturated multi-peer repair regression.

title: Broaden link-draft payload terminology to both dispatch namespaces
description: Correctness review found draft-lichen-link-01 §2 defines Payload solely as a SCHC-compressed IPv6 datagram, but §3.1/main spec also defines dispatch 0x15 for raw LICHEN routing/control bodies alongside dispatch 0x14 SCHC. Update terminology so PLD is the authenticated dispatch octet plus its selected body; do not imply all payloads are SCHC/IPv6.

title: Move normative TDMA initialization requirements out of AGENTS.md references
description: Correctness review found spec/09-packets-timing.md §14.8 declares the mutable contributor instruction file AGENTS.md and hard-coded source line numbers (AGENTS.md:179/:218, lichen_link_init():147, etc.) normative for protocol initialization/FSM behavior. These references are not stable specification anchors, line numbers already drift, and non-Zephyr implementations cannot conform to C symbol ordering as protocol semantics. State any genuinely normative dependency ordering directly in an appropriate spec section with stable section links; keep platform-specific implementation guidance non-normative. Spec-only fix; no C/Zephyr work is required in this session.

title: Rename misleading 64-bit MIC parsing vector
description: Correctness review found spec/test-vectors/frame.json still names a selector-1 unsigned case frame_with_64bit_mic and describes 'MicLength=64'. Current normative semantics say bits 2-4 values 0/1 are compatibility selectors and unsigned frames carry no MIC; there is no 64-bit MIC. Rename/reword the case to selector-1 compatibility terminology while preserving its bytes and empty MIC expectation, and update any name-based consumers.

title: Fix fragmentation parameter cross-reference in SCHC draft
description: Correctness review found draft-lichen-schc-lora-00 §5.4 says the fragmentation parameters cross-reference spec/03-adaptation.md Section 5.7, but 5.7 is Rule Versioning; the fixed fragmentation profile is Section 5.6. Correct the reference so implementers land on the normative M/N/tile/RCS limits.

title: Add independent literals for production-derived timing vectors
description: Correctness review found generate_packets_timing.py builds many canonical cross-language expected values directly from lichen.timing production (Trickle constants/FSM, DAO delays, CSMA constants/state, generic airtime rows, FNV slot/hash, startup and desync FSM), while test_packets_timing mostly compares the artifact to the same generator/production and only checks positivity/ranges for several categories. Independent arithmetic currently covers duty-cycle and TDMA max-airtime but not the rest. Add spec-derived literal/second-implementation checks for every production-derived category (or make the generator independent) so a Python regression cannot rewrite the shared Rust/Python oracle and pass its own consumer.

title: Decouple link-frame oracle from production address/MIC enums
description: Correctness review found generate.py labels _oracle_encode_frame independent but frame_vectors imports production AddrMode and MicLength and uses their integer values to construct the canonical fields/wire. If those enum discriminants drift from spec bits, regeneration and the main consumer test drift together, especially unsigned Extended/Elided and selector-1 cases. Use literal spec-defined oracle constants (or an independent local enum) for all canonical inputs and add direct bit-position assertions in the independent consumer.

title: Fix contradictory fixed-header definition in link draft
description: Correctness review found draft-lichen-link-01.md §3.1 says PLD length is LENGTH minus fixed_header_size and then defines fixed_header_size as 4 for '(LENGTH+LLSec+EPO+SEQ)'. Those named fields total 5 octets, while the correct four body octets are LLSec+EPO+SEQ because LENGTH is excluded from its own value. Rewrite the definition unambiguously and cover PLD-length arithmetic for SI/no-SI and destination modes.

title: Atomic vector writer permits non-standard NaN and Infinity JSON
description: atomic_write_json uses json.dumps defaults, where allow_nan=True emits NaN/Infinity tokens that are not valid RFC JSON and are rejected by strict/Rust consumers. Canonical cross-language vectors must reject non-finite values during pre-serialization before creating/replacing any output, with a preservation regression.

title: Modified vector generators can truncate canonical fixtures in place
description: test/vectors/generate.py, generate_authenticated_schc_dio.py, and generate_packets_timing.py write canonical JSON with Path.write_text. A crash/write error can leave a truncated fixture; the timing generator can also update one of its two outputs before failing on the second. Add a shared same-directory atomic JSON writer using fsync+replace, preserve existing mode, clean temporary files on failure, and test failure preserves the prior destination.

title: Node accepts noncanonical peer IID and targets the wrong EUI-64
description: Correctness review finding (P3) in the final SIID/Extended-destination path: PeerIdentity.__post_init__ validates only lengths, so callers can construct PeerIdentity(pubkey=valid_key, iid=arbitrary_8_bytes). Node.add_peer stores that unverified IID verbatim at python/src/lichen/node.py:301-308, _peer_for_next_hop indexes link-local routes by IID at lines 320-329, and _transmit_peer_schc converts peer.iid into the exact Extended wire EUI-64 at lines 610-615/622-625. The public out-of-band add_peer path can therefore make a canonical route unresolvable or transmit an authenticated SCHC packet to an EUI-64 unrelated to the peer pubkey/policy. Canonicalize an exact PeerIdentity.from_pubkey(peer.pubkey) (or reject any IID mismatch) on add and when accepting constructor-supplied peer_db state; add a regression covering link-local lookup and Extended targeting.

title: MicLength.mic_len contradicts the wire selector semantics
description: Correctness review finding (P3): python/src/lichen/link/frame.py:53-67 documents selector values 0 and 1 as compatibility-only and no MIC for unsigned frames, but the public MicLength.mic_len property returns 4 and 8. Signed frames always carry 48 bytes independently of the selector (frame.py:133-135; spec/02-physical-link.md:203,246; test/vectors/mic_length_selector.json). A caller using this property for sizing or slicing will compute a wire layout the serializer/parser never emits. Remove/replace the property with profile-correct semantics (likely context-sensitive or no byte-length property) and add a regression asserting unsigned=0 and signed=48 for both selectors.

title: Python dropped fragmentation senders retain prepared reservations until TTL
description: Security review: SchcSessionManager.create_sender stores a strong reference to each FragmentSender in _prepared, so dropping the returned handle cannot trigger the global weakref cleanup and does not call discard_prepared. Repeating create-and-drop fills MAX_PREPARED_SENDERS and blocks valid transfers for PREPARED_SENDER_TTL_SECONDS. Provide deterministic handle-drop/cancellation cleanup (or a lease API that cannot be abandoned), without unsafe destructor exceptions, and test capacity recovery after dropped never-started handles.
notes: The same ownership model retains active records after the caller drops its only handle; include active-session drop cleanup/terminal hold-down semantics in the fix and tests.

title: Rust SOS rate limiter fails open for public non-default limits
description: P3 security review finding in newly added rust/lichen-link/src/sos.rs (completed implementation project-LICHEN-worker6-l1qw.10.7.3.2). SosRateLimitConfig::new and public fields accept arbitrary max_per_hour and burst_allowance, but SosRateLimitState stores only [u64; 3]. If max_per_hour > 3, valid_count can never reach the configured threshold and the hourly limit is disabled; if max_per_hour == 0 with no stored entry, the >= check finds no oldest timestamp and then falls through to Allowed (especially with burst_remaining > 0). A burst_allowance up to 255 likewise defeats the stated burst cap. Make construction validated/fallible or size storage from an enforced maximum, reject zero/out-of-range normative settings, and add max=0, max=4, large-burst, and check-after-prune tests.

title: Gateway slot claims and allocation maps have no resource bounds
description: P3 security review finding. The newly exported slot coordination types accept caller-controlled Vec sizes without protocol caps: SlotClaim::new accepts arbitrary slots, overlap_with/resolve_conflict perform O(n*m) contains scans and allocate an overlap Vec, find_next_available performs repeated linear contains, SlotAllocationMap accepts unlimited gateways and arbitrary per-gateway slot vectors, and assign_ordinals clones/sorts an unbounded slice. When wired to coordination messages this permits memory/CPU exhaustion by an authenticated or newly-TOFU peer. Define hard maxima from slots_per_superframe/federation policy, reject duplicates and out-of-range slots at decode/admission, bound peer/map counts, and use bounded/linear-time set representations. Add maximum+1 and large-overlap rejection tests.

title: Gateway federation PSKs are clonable and not zeroized on drop
description: P3 security review. New PskFederation in rust/lichen-gateway/src/trust.rs stores the federation master secret in Vec<u8>, derives Clone, exposes it through psk(), and implements no Zeroize/ZeroizeOnDrop even though the gateway adds a zeroize dependency. Dropped/reallocated clones leave federation-wide authentication material in process memory, increasing disclosure impact. Store secrets in a zeroizing non-clonable wrapper, minimize raw secret access, zeroize temporary master_secret copies, and add compile/runtime coverage for secret lifecycle.

title: Authenticated SCHC fragmentation sessions leak reservations when handles are dropped
description: Security review P3. New FragmentSender and AuthenticatedFragmentReceiver constructors reserve policy tuples in rust/lichen-schc/src/fragment.rs, but the handles do not borrow/own a release guard and implement no Drop cleanup. Only successful terminal processing or explicit cancel/timeout releases. Dropping a live handle leaves SessionBusy until the 60s inactivity deadline; the next allocation merely converts it to another 60s tombstone and still fails, allowing error/cancellation paths to strand per-peer send/receive capacity for up to two minutes repeatedly. Make reservation ownership RAII-safe or expose a policy cleanup/maintenance path that releases abandoned handles without extending hold-down unexpectedly; add drop/early-return tests for sender and receiver.

title: Rule-Version Length=0 vector misclassifies a complete malformed TLV as truncated
description: Correctness review: rule_versioning.json dio_rule_version_parse_length_0 (around lines 116-124) uses wire 1300 and expect_error=truncated, claiming it needs 3+length bytes. In normal TLV arithmetic Type+Length+zero value is exactly two bytes and complete; it is invalid because the specialized option requires Length=1, i.e. wrong_length/malformed_length_0. authenticated_schc_dio.json uses malformed_rule_version_length_0 and rpl_messages.json uses invalid_schc_version_option, exposing the cross-artifact cause mismatch. Align the exact classification and add an independent structural assertion.

title: DAO vector claims DODAGID but encodes the no-DODAGID form
description: Correctness review: test/vectors/rpl_messages.json:122-132 names dao_base and describes Base RPL DAO with DODAGID, but encoded is only 00000005 (the 4-byte no-D form), flags are zero, and dodag_id is null. test/vectors/generate.py:2552-2557 has the same contradiction. A DAO with DODAGID must set D (kd_flags bit 6) and append 16 bytes (20-byte base), as spec/03-adaptation.md:102-105 states. Either rename/document this as the no-DODAGID fallback case or encode the claimed form.

title: Version 0 wording implies an operational uncompressed fallback registry
description: spec/03-adaptation.md labels Rule Set Version 0 as Reserved (uncompressed fallback), and rule_versioning.json says version 0 is reserved for uncompressed fallback. Current policy says Version 3 is the only operational registry and Rule 255 syntax is version-independent only under narrow out-of-DODAG policy. Clarify that version 0 is simply reserved and never activates a fallback registry; Rule 255 does not make v0 operational.

title: Independent link-addressing oracle ignores key-derived Extended EUI-64 vector
description: link-addressing.json now includes key_derived_extended_eui64 for the Python/Rust interoperability correction, but test_protocol_vector_security.py checks only the arbitrary extended_eui64 case. Independently derive the key IID with SHA-512, flip the RFC 4291 U/L bit exactly once for wire EUI-64, validate the encoded frame destination, and reconstruct the expected link-local address.

title: Rule 7 AddressMode table ambiguously permits noncanonical link-local IID mode
description: spec/03-adaptation.md Rule 7 residue table says AddressMode=0 when both addresses are link-local, but the normative prose and uniqueness rule require both addresses specifically in canonical fe80::/64. Implementers following the table could encode fe80::/10 addresses outside /64 in IID-only mode and create an ambiguous/noncanonical wire representation. Change the table wording to the exact fe80::/64 predicate and keep the full-mode rule explicit.

title: Rule 7 multicast scope oracle omits reserved scope 0 and valid upper boundary 14
description: The new Rule 7 policy normatively accepts multicast destination scopes 2..14 and rejects 0,1,15, but schc_adaptation address-policy vectors cover scope2 valid, scope1 invalid, and scope15 invalid only. Add ff00:: invalid and ff0e:: valid boundary cases so consumers cannot implement the predicate as scope!=1&&scope!=15 or otherwise miss the lower/upper inclusivity.

title: Python self-signed SCHC control can raise inside LinkLayer.receive
description: SchcSessionManager.record_verified_frame derives fragmentation direction for ACK/Receiver-Abort after LinkLayer has replay-accepted and stored the receipt. If authenticated sender identity equals the local signer, fragmentation_rule_for_sender raises FragmentError for the non-peer pair and the exception escapes LinkLayer.receive instead of leaving the frame for higher-layer rejection. Catch equal/invalid endpoint direction during opportunistic sender-control registration, preserve the normal authenticated receive contract, and add a self-signed ambiguous-control regression showing no sender/reassembly mutation.

title: RPL root vector metadata retains obsolete ULA and 02xx::/7 identity models
description: rpl_messages.json calls fd00::1 a LICHEN root DIO despite authenticated root AddrForKey binding, and root_signature.json describes Yggdrasil derivation as 02xx::/7 while current profile is 0200::/8. Correct metadata/examples, regenerate any derived expectations if needed, and add metadata/semantic assertions so consumers cannot treat ULA or the obsolete prefix rule as valid root identity.

title: Rule 7 invalid IPv6 address set is not normatively defined
description: spec/03 Rule 7 defines structural checks but not which IPv6 source/destination classes are invalid; appendix only says invalid addresses while vectors reject multicast source and unspecified destination. Define exact canonical source/destination validity, including unspecified, multicast, loopback, IPv4-mapped, and scoped cases as applicable, and add allow/deny vectors consumed by Python/Rust.
notes: Python implementation complete: shared validate_rule7_addresses policy is enforced on Rule 7 compression/decompression; schc_adaptation.json rule7_address_policy has a production-backed 12-vector consumer. Focused gates: 12 vector cases pass, 28 SCHC header tests pass, Ruff clean, strict mypy headers.py clean, diff-check clean. Independent 3x review pending parent orchestration. Child k3t1.1 tracks and fixes normative Rule 255 fallback behavior.

title: SCHC spec omits receiver ACK response exhaustion transition
description: schc_fragmentation.json and both Python/Rust receivers count emitted ACK responses and send Receiver-Abort instead of a fifth ACK, but draft Section 5.2 says the receiver responds to every All-1/ACK REQ and only defines MAX_ACK_REQUESTS for sender request emissions. spec/03-adaptation.md is likewise silent about receiver response exhaustion. Specify the receiver counter and fifth-request Receiver-Abort transition so the vectors and implementations are normative and interoperable; clarify terminal hold-down behavior after that abort.
notes: Final security review independently found the receiver retry vector contradicted the then-current normative state machine; spec text must explicitly make this receiver counter/abort behavior normative.

title: Rust SCHC exposes obsolete v2 and contradictory window-size constants
description: rust/lichen-schc/src/fragment.rs is a public module now implementing canonical Rule Set Version 3 fragmentation Rules 0x78/0x79, but its module doc still says Rule Set Version 2. It also publicly exports DEFAULT_WINDOW_SIZE=32 and MAX_WINDOW_SIZE=62 while the normative fixed WINDOW_SIZE is 63 tiles; MAX_WINDOW_SIZE is unused and Python exports 63 under the same name. Downstream users can select an invalid non-profile window or infer only 62 tiles. Remove/rename obsolete constants or make all public window-size APIs represent the fixed 63-tile profile, update module docs to version 3, and add a public-constant/profile consistency test.

title: Rust tests compile out peer-context liveness enforcement
description: AuthenticatedPeerSchcContext compress/decompress guard their InvalidPeerEvidence return with cfg(not(test)); stale/evidence-less contexts therefore succeed in unit tests even though production rejects them. No_std base methods are likewise exposed although retained evidence is always false. Remove test-only semantic divergence, test through properly issued evidence/authority, and make unusable base methods unavailable or consistently failing.

title: Rust authenticated DIO vector consumer ignores exact rejection reason
description: rust/lichen-schc/tests/authenticated_dio_vectors.rs asserts only Ok versus Err for negative signed security cases. A malformed vector can pass for an unrelated failure and fail to prove the intended source/root/version/scope guard. Add stable typed rejection categories or exact error tokens and assert every vector's declared expected result/cause.

title: Scoped vector test module fails Ruff after replay-vector edits
description: ruff check python/tests/test_vectors.py reports relevant post-edit failures: unused last_counter near line 2563, unused logical_counter import near 4013, and E501 near 4036. The same module also has B905 near 2499 and undefined GradientEntry near 2676 in concurrent work. Coordinate with current owners, resolve all lint failures without hiding them, and rerun Ruff plus the complete vector test module.
notes: Fixed all five current Ruff defects in python/tests/test_vectors.py without suppressions or semantic changes: zip(strict=True) after existing length equality assertion; removed unused last_counter; added TYPE_CHECKING GradientEntry import while preserving lazy runtime import; removed unused receiver-state logical_counter import; split overlong assertion string identically. Ruff clean. pytest test_vectors.py -k 'not schema': 498 passed, 74 deselected, one expected replay warning. git diff --check clean. schema.json remained untouched by this work and is concurrently modified. Leave open for independent convergence.

title: Async persistence revision anchors leak awaitables and fail opaquely
description: PersistenceRevisionAnchor is checked only for callable read/advance. LinkLayer._read_persistence_revision_anchor treats an awaitable result as an invalid revision without cancelling/closing it, while _advance_persistence_revision_anchor ignores an awaitable return entirely. Accidentally async anchors leak never-awaited coroutines and may report success after only scheduling side effects. Require synchronous functions/results using the shared awaitable rejection helper, with coroutine-function, hidden-awaitable, Task/Future, and cleanup-failure tests for read and advance.
notes: Security review broadened this boundary: anchor read/advance execute under LinkLayer._security_lock with no transition/reentry guard. Same-thread recursive save, a spawned thread joining on the Link lock, or callback state mutation can deadlock or split serialized/runtime state. Fix must move hooks outside internal locks under guarded snapshot/CAS semantics, reject reentry, and fail closed after ambiguous writes; add cross-thread join and mutation tests.

title: SCHC spec and rule-version vectors describe contradictory Rule7/helper semantics
description: spec/03-adaptation.md states canonical rules including Rule7 are implemented in python/schc/rules.py, but specialized Rule7 exists only in headers.py and is absent from RULES. Rule-version vectors call operational Rule7/64-66 absent while rejection text calls 64-66 defined wire building blocks and labels truncated Rule66 rather than unknown. Reconcile exact implementation/spec/oracle semantics and descriptions so cross-implementation consumers test one unambiguous contract.
notes: Clarified spec/03-adaptation.md: generic descriptor registry Rules 0-6/255, canonical specialized wire Rule7 in Python headers.py/Rust codec.rs, and Python helper descriptors 64-66 are non-wire. Reconciled rule_versioning.json descriptions and changed stale Rule66 truncated expectation to unknown_rule_id; added explicit specialized/helper metadata. Relevant vector/SCHC/RPL tests, Ruff, mypy, diff-check pass. Leave open for independent convergence.

title: Unexpected awaitable cleanup stops after a throwing cancel hook
description: python/src/lichen/_sync_callbacks.py calls a custom awaitable's cancel() and then close() without guarding cleanup exceptions. If cancel raises, close is skipped and the cleanup exception escapes instead of the documented deterministic TypeError, potentially leaving a rejected callback result live. Make best-effort cancellation/closure exception-safe while preserving the primary rejection, avoid double side effects, and add custom awaitables whose cancel/close individually raise.

title: MonotonicClock accepts async callbacks and leaks unawaited coroutine objects
description: Fresh final timing robustness review: MonotonicClock validates only callable(callback). An async function is accepted; each clock read creates a coroutine, _mono rejects it, and the coroutine is never closed/awaited, producing resource warnings and possible captured-resource retention on every status/adopt path. Reject coroutine functions at construction and defensively close/reject any awaitable returned by a callable object, without changing domain identity or tracker state. Add async-function and awaitable-returning-object tests under warnings-as-errors.

title: SCHC retry vector provenance mislabels timeout ACK-REQ as fifth All-1
description: Final ACK correctness review: test/vectors/schc_fragmentation.json sender_retry_exhaustion provenance says timeout replaces a fifth All-1 attempt, but trigger_event is timeout and pre_exhaustion_message 7800 is an ACK REQ. All-1 is emitted only for initial or missing-final-tile batches. Correct provenance to fifth request / timeout ACK REQ, align draft step wording, and keep Python/Rust executable assertions on the exact sequence.

title: FragmentSender attempts documentation excludes ACK-REQ attempts
description: Final ACK correctness review: python/src/lichen/schc/fragment.py:744-748 describes attempts as the number of All-1 transmissions, but the state machine also increments it for ACK REQ emissions in timeout and missing-regular-fragment paths. Update the public contract to describe total All-1/ACK-REQ request attempts and distinguish generated output from confirmed radio transmission. Add assertions covering both increment paths so documentation and semantics cannot drift.

title: Unbounded correction-rate policy can raise OverflowError during adoption
description: Timing correctness review: SourcePrecedencePolicy accepts arbitrarily large non-negative `max_correction_rate_ppm`; `_anchor_rejection` multiplies it through floating point. A constructible value such as 10**400 raises OverflowError on a later adoption instead of returning a controlled decision. Impose a documented safe bound or use overflow-safe integer arithmetic so every accepted policy is total. Add maximum and over-maximum tests.

title: Rust RPL serializer hardcodes SCHC version option bytes outside registry owner
description: Rule 7 and versioning correctness rereview: rust lichen-rpl Dio defines SCHC_RULE_VERSION_OPTION as literal 13 01 03 instead of deriving it from lichen-schc SchcRuleVersionOption current and SCHC_RULE_VERSION_TYPE. A future registry increment can update codec compatibility while emitted DIOs silently remain version 3. Remove the duplicate constant, serialize through the canonical SCHC option API, and add a test that the DIO option equals current registry serialization rather than another literal.

title: TX queue invalid priority and deadline inputs mutate state before failure
description: Post-fix correctness review: `TxQueue.push(..., priority=1)` inserts an entry and increments stats before raising while evaluating `priority.name`; malformed deadlines can enqueue entries that later break expiry comparisons. Validate and normalize priority, data, deadline, channel, and reservation flags before any expiry, stats, order, LRU, entry, or reservation mutation. Add int, bool, NaN, and string boundary tests that prove invalid calls are atomic no-ops.

title: LinkLayer reads rekeyed peer registry outside security lock
description: Security review: _find_sender snapshots _rekeyed_peers.values() without the security lock while rotation mutates the dict from another thread. Concurrent receive/rekey can raise iteration errors or observe incoherent candidates. Snapshot candidate identities under _security_lock without awaiting, retain final retired-key check, and add threaded receive/rotation stress for linearizable outcomes.

title: TimeEvidence quality metadata is only shallowly immutable
description: Correctness review: MappingProxyType(dict(quality)) protects only the top-level mapping and retains mutable nested lists/dicts/objects. Mutating a nested value after issuance changes accepted evidence despite spec requiring immutable provenance. Recursively freeze/copy an explicitly allowed immutable metadata schema and add post-issuance nested-mutation regressions.

title: tests/timing/test_time_sync.py collection error: ProvisionEpochMetadata.__init__ TypeError
description: Stale signature vs WIP changes. Fix constructor/callers per current design.

title: schema.json: add gateway_coordination_document branch covering GCP vector family
description: Draft7 validation fails identically for rpl_multi_instance.json, committed gateway_coordination.json, WIP gcp6_slot_coordination.json. Add branch so family validates.
notes:
Current schema.json edit is syntactically invalid: after root properties.vectors closes near lines 51-52, the enclosing properties object is missing its closing brace before allOf. json.loads fails at line 80 char 3571. Restore the baseline "        }\n      }," nesting while preserving GCP additions, then run JSON parse/schema tests.
Final artifact lane adds schema work tracked by q3yh after the GCP/syntax branch lands; do not omit new link/SCHC/replay/rule-version categories/fields when restoring strict schema validity.

title: Clippy warnings: lichen-core tdma_beacon.rs:185 manual RangeInclusive contains; lichen-schc codec.rs:33,163 dead code; lichen-node routing/neighbor.rs:131 map_or
description: Fix each properly (use .contains, remove dead code, use map_or); keep clippy clean delta zero-warning policy going forward.

title: vectors: add loadng_discovery.json cases for hop-boundary drop, cache-fresh/gradient-empty stale case, equal-seq superiority
description: Cross-implementation oracle lacks canonical coverage for behaviors just pinned by unit tests (1leg/uosr fixes). Extend generator + JSON following existing conventions.

title: test_channel_plan.py: empty vectors array passes silently; missing hash_32.json skips
description: Vector-driven loops lack non-empty assertion; pytest.skip on missing oracle file = silent pass on lost authoritative data — the exact failure mode these gates prevent. Assert non-empty in each loader; replace skip with hard requirement.

title: Host-test TU copy-declares enum lichen_rpl_sequence_relation instead of including header
description: rpl_dao_build.c:15-22 duplicates enum decl (deliberate: avoids zephyr/kernel.h) → silent desync between test expectations and shipped binary possible. Include real header in test build or compile-time consistency check.

title: process_dio_bytes retains prior gateway_centric when DODAG Config option absent (behavior flip)
description: Old code unconditionally reset flag per-DIO (removed at dodag.c:459-481 during k35h fix); now written only when config!=NULL (:369-371) so stale gateway_centric=true survives indefinitely on same-DODAG DIos lacking the option. Reset when config==NULL or document Rust/Python-parity rationale for retain semantics.

title: gateway_centric accepted from any authenticated neighbor's DIO config option — mode flapping
description: dodag.c:368-371: any joined peer's DODAG Configuration option flips d->gateway_centric which drives announce scheduling (announce.c:738-753); no validation against root authoritative config; single malicious joined node toggles neighbors' announce mode per-DIO. Accept config only from adopted root DIO (compare dodag_id/root key); persist last-known-good.

title: rpl_dao_build.c sequence counters advanced outside dm->lock — lost-update TOCTOU
description: build_dao_mut writes dao_sequence/path_sequence/last_dao_* (:260-265) and build_dao_copy_with_lifetime writes dao_sequence (:334) after caller released lock (snapshots :279-283/:298-301/:324-326). Two builders read seq N both write N+1 → lost increment reuses DAOSequence across transmissions degrading DAO↔ACK correlation (RFC 6550 §7.1). Move snapshot+build+advance inside held lock or locked advance_sequences helper.

title: C lollipop comments/macro names invert RFC 6550 §7.2 regions (behavior correct)
description: Comments say '0-127 linear restart; 128-255 circular', LOLLIPOP_CIRCULAR_BIT=128; RFC defines opposite (128+ linear, ≤127 circular). Code verified functionally correct (region-agnostic same-region branch; cross-region arithmetic matches RFC examples 240vs5, 250vs5; increment implements rule 2 exactly). Hazard: maintainer 'fixing' to match comments breaks interop. Rename LOLLIPOP_CIRCULAR_BIT→LOLLIPOP_LINEAR_BASE + correct comments; behavior untouched.

title: vectors: extend rpl_multi_instance.json with receive_from_peer guard outcomes (stale_timestamp,self_origin,origin_auth_mismatch,too_many_routes,peer_limit_reached,NaN)
description: Security-critical reject paths have zero canonical coverage while docstrings promise identical outcomes across impls — exactly where triple drift bites (cf F15). Extend generate_multi_instance_vectors with accept/reject per guard incl. NaN/future timestamps.

title: multi_instance.get_dodag_version/create_dodag_state read _dodag_version without self._lock
description: Writes happen under lock (:increment/set); reads at :223-225,:256 race federation increments → torn version stamped into root DODAG state. Take lock in both readers.

title: multi_instance.receive_from_peer raises TypeError/KeyError/ValueError on malformed backbone dict instead of (False,'malformed')
description: multi_instance.py:420-484 unchecked message['timestamp'] arithmetic, int() coercions, to_ipv6 on garbage escape as exceptions. Rust typing makes states unrepresentable; Python needs envelope validation up front mirroring Rust reason taxonomy. Latent (no production caller yet) but must land before wiring.

title: slot_coordination.add_candidate missing MAX_CANDIDATES=32 cap (unbounded growth)
description: python/src/lichen/link/slot_coordination.py:299-305 appends without cap; Rust MultiRootState::add_candidate rejects beyond 32 (DoS guard). Beacon flood grows list unbounded, compounded by F6 fail-open. Port cap identically.

title: loadng discovery: non-installing (stale) RREPs still forwarded — amplification vector
description: discovery.py:209-220 falls through to forward even when unified gate refused install; no RREP seen-window like RREQ _seen. Each injected stale packet burns one TX per reverse-path node. Fix: forward only when fresh enough to install, or add RREP suppression window.

title: Link-layer oversized-frame test contradicts 254-byte body limit
description: Python link-layer focused tests fail because test_oversized_send_rejects_before_signing_without_mutation expects an 'exceeds 255' error, while spec section 4.1 and frame.py correctly cap the one-byte Length field body at 254 bytes (255 bytes total including Length). Update the assertion to the normative 254-byte body limit and retain the pre-signing/no-state-mutation checks.

title: SCHC ACK tests omit distinct authenticated wrong-signer case
description: Correctness review: the test named wrong_peer never constructs a different remote signer, and signed-wire coverage checks only a wrong local receiver and a same-identity clone. Add a third known signer, receive its cryptographically valid ACK after session start, assert exact-sender rejection without consuming or advancing the target session, then prove the intended signer's ACK still succeeds.

title: SCHC public DEFAULT_WINDOW_SIZE contradicts fixed 63-tile profile
description: Correctness review: fragment.py still defines and schc.__init__ exports DEFAULT_WINDOW_SIZE=7, while the fixed profile requires WINDOW_SIZE=63 and FragmentSender rejects other values. Remove the obsolete public setting or alias it to the normative profile constant; add cross-module coverage preventing divergent public defaults.

title: Replay counter APIs accept booleans and inconsistently reject non-integers
description: Correctness review: replay logical_counter validates only numeric ranges, so bool is accepted as epoch/sequence and floats or other types can fail later with inconsistent shift/type errors. Enforce exact-int (excluding bool) validation before range checks and apply it consistently through ReplayWindow and ReplayProtector public methods. Add boundary tests for zero, maxima, bool, float, and string inputs across logical_counter, check, commit, and check_and_update.

title: RPL messages module fails strict host compilation on conversions and nullability
description: Activating a focused messages.c test exposes -Werror failures: DIO gmop and DAO kd expressions implicitly narrow int to uint8_t, and iterator data pointers lack explicit nullable/non-null annotations. Make conversions explicit and annotate iterator/raw option pointer contracts consistently; update the host shim cast and remove the old test warning suppression if applicable.
notes: Returned open/unclaimed because the user explicitly excluded C/Zephyr/AWS work from this session; no C changes from this finding remain.

title: Python SCHC custom profiles cannot disable reserved Rule 7 handling
description: compress_packet/decompress_packet always run/reserve the global MQTT-SN Rule 7 codec before the caller-supplied profiles tuple, so profiles=() does not mean no profiles. Incorporate Rule 7 into a common profile abstraction or document and test this reserved built-in behavior.

title: Add signed-wire end-to-end tests for authenticated SCHC ACK delivery
description: Correctness review found SCHC ACK unit/vector tests fabricate RxFrame and caller baselines, bypassing signature verification, replay commit, local binding, and authoritative baseline capture. Add an end-to-end test that signs wire frames, obtains the trusted envelope through LinkLayer.receive, feeds the production session API, and proves forgery/substitution/replay/wrong-local/prior-session rejection. Keep unsafe codec fixtures explicitly separate.

title: Make authenticated RxFrame data immutable for every consumer
description: Correctness review found frozen RxFrame only snapshots properties while retaining a mutable public LichenFrame; node and KISS consumers still read rx.frame.payload and can observe data different from rx.payload after mutation. Hide/freeze the inner frame or expose only immutable verified snapshots, migrate consumers, and test all covered fields remain identical for every consumer.

title: Reject extraneous SCHC descriptor metadata for cross-implementation parity
description: Correctness review found Rust accepts mo_arg metadata when neither MO=MSB nor CDA=LSB and mapping metadata when neither MO=MatchMapping nor CDA=MappingSent, while Python rejects those malformed descriptors. Enforce canonical metadata presence: mo_arg iff the supported MSB/LSB pair needs it, mapping iff the supported MatchMapping/MappingSent pair needs it. Add a cross-implementation descriptor acceptance matrix and ensure built-in rules remain valid.

title: Fail closed on unsupported future SCHC MO/CDA variants
description: Post-fix review found non-exhaustive matching-operator and CDA enums are not explicitly allowlisted during descriptor validation; future variants can bypass rejection, especially when a field is absent. Explicitly accept only supported known MO/CDA variants before field lookup and add/update coverage that forces deliberate handling when the dependency adds variants.

title: Harden SCHC ACK/control APIs against invalid runtime input types
description: Robustness codereview found public ACK/control parsing and serialization paths do not consistently enforce exact bytes/integer runtime types. Ack.from_bytes and FragmentSender.handle_ack_bytes can accept mutable bytes-like objects or raise raw TypeError for lists/strings; ack_request/Fragment/Ack window and related fields accept bool via equality. Make public wire APIs fail predictably with FragmentError, reject bool/type confusion, preserve canonical valid encodings, add focused regression tests, and run 3x post-fix review.
notes: Security review independently confirmed mutable bytearray/memoryview ACK buffers could cross the auth/parser boundary; current fix now rejects non-bytes before dispatch and Ack parsing.

title: Python malformed ACK test ignores every parametrized wire value
description: python/tests/schc/test_fragment.py parametrizes test_malformed_ack_vectors with 784000 and 78ff but never references the wire argument. The test instead repeats unrelated invalid FragmentSender construction checks, so neither malformed ACK reaches Ack.from_bytes and ACK parser regressions can pass unnoticed.
acceptance_criteria: Change the parametrized test to call Ack.from_bytes(wire) and assert FragmentError for each malformed encoding. Remove the unrelated sender assertions or move them to sender-parameter tests. Prove both C=1 with a trailing octet (784000) and incomplete malformed control (78ff) are rejected, and retain valid canonical C=1/Receiver-Abort coverage.

title: Define canonical NO_SYNC timestamp semantics on the DIO wire
description: Spec/interop review finding. DioTimeOption permits Stratum.NO_SYNC with any unsigned 32-bit Unix timestamp at python/src/lichen/timing/time_sync.py:120-167, and python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:115-118 explicitly tests both zero and 0xffffffff. StratumTracker rejects any adopted NO_SYNC timestamp at lines 182-188, while spec/09-packets-timing.md:201-223 defines stratum 0 as no sync with monotonic counters only and the option timestamp as Unix epoch seconds. The wire meaning of a nonzero timestamp at NO_SYNC is therefore contradictory and non-canonical across encoders, decoders, and state handling.
acceptance_criteria: Specify one canonical interoperable rule for the timestamp field when stratum is NO_SYNC. Prefer requiring zero and rejecting nonzero on construction and decode; if the WG instead permits arbitrary bits, state that receivers MUST ignore them and require encoders to emit one canonical value. Update normative spec, Python, Rust, Zephyr/C, and canonical vectors consistently. Add positive canonical encoding plus negative/non-canonical decode tests, verify NO_SYNC cannot establish wall clock or enter tracker state, and exercise mixed-implementation vector parity. Run focused tests and three code-review passes per modified source module.

title: Version or preserve compatibility for the SourceClass API change
description: API correctness review finding. The current diff changes SOURCE_CLASSES and SOURCE_CAN_ESTABLISH_WALL_CLOCK from string-based public data to SourceClass values and changes can_establish_wall_clock from accepting a source string to requiring SourceClass, raising TypeError at python/src/lichen/timing/time_sync.py:208-217. python/src/lichen/timing/__init__.py:37-47 and 55-93 newly re-export this API. Existing callers using documented values such as GNSS or Network may compare successfully in some StrEnum contexts but fail at the explicit runtime guard, producing an unversioned behavioral break. Tests at python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:78-93 only assert rejection of string configuration and do not cover compatibility/migration.
acceptance_criteria: Choose and document an API compatibility policy before release: either normalize the six canonical legacy strings to SourceClass with a tested deprecation path, or introduce a clearly versioned breaking API with migration notes and a deliberate major-version boundary. Unknown strings MUST still fail closed with a precise error. Ensure SOURCE_CLASSES, capability lookup, SourcePrecedencePolicy, direct time_sync imports, and lichen.timing re-exports behave consistently. Add tests for every legacy canonical string, enum callers, unknown/misspelled values, policy configuration, deprecation/version behavior, and public re-exports; run focused tests and three code-review passes per modified source module.

title: Apple clang -Werror: rpl_messages.h opt_iter pointers lack nullability
description: Host compile of any TU that includes lichen/rpl_messages.h with Apple clang 21 (clang-2100) -Wall -Wextra -Werror fails on -Wnullability-completeness for struct lichen_rpl_opt_iter.data and struct lichen_rpl_raw_opt.data (rpl_messages.h around lines 397 and 407). Triggered because rpl_dodag.h/rpl_messages.h use real _Nonnull/_Nullable when __has_feature(nullability). Out of scope for project-LICHEN-worker6-k35h (stay off messages.c). Fix: annotate those two fields _Nullable (opt_iter.data may be NULL after init with NULL data; raw_opt.data is only valid after a successful next). Do not change codec behavior.

title: lichen-rpl crate-wide pre-existing rustfmt debt
description: cargo fmt -p lichen-rpl --check reports ~35 hunks across dao_origin.rs, multi_instance.rs, routing.rs, tests/ccp_beacon_sig_gate.rs, tests/multi_instance_vectors.rs (pre-existing at HEAD; committed without fmt). dodag.rs was formatted by worker6-26l6. Note: running cargo fmt -p lichen-rpl now would produce a large mechanical diff across files other workers may own; schedule as its own cleanup pass.

title: schnorr::build_signable truncates dst_addr_len byte for dst_addr longer than 255 bytes
description: rust/lichen-link/src/schnorr.rs build_signable() does buf.push(dst_addr.len() as u8) with no range validation. sign_frame/verify_frame are public API taking arbitrary slices; a >255-byte dst_addr would encode a truncated DST_LEN while appending all address bytes, producing signed data that no conforming frame can reproduce and enabling TX/RX disagreement. Not reachable through LinkLayer::build_frame/receive_frame (AddrMode bounds addr len at 8 and rx_frame_length now validates), so latent public-API hazard only. Discovered from project-LICHEN-worker6-uka3.2; suggest validating dst_addr.len() <= 255 or returning an error from sign_frame/verify_frame.

title: clippy -D warnings fails on lichen-link tests/shared_vectors.rs dead-code fields
description: tests/shared_vectors.rs CryptoMetadata fields (seed, private_key, public_key, preimage, signature) and LinkFrameVector.crypto are never read; cargo clippy -p lichen-link --all-targets -- -D warnings fails with dead_code. Pre-existing at HEAD (not introduced by worker6 fixes) and file has concurrent uncommitted WIP from another workstream (appended replay-window test). Fix by reading the fields in assertions or removing/allowing them once that WIP lands.

title: latency_ms output always returns 0
description:
File: lichen/subsys/lichen/link/include/lichen/tx_queue.h
Line: 175

Line 175 documents latency_ms as 'time packet spent in queue' but the implementation (tx_queue.c:354-366) always sets *latency_ms = 0 with a comment admitting it's a placeholder. The documented functionality does not work.

title: max_latency_ms stat field is never populated
description:
File: lichen/subsys/lichen/link/include/lichen/tx_queue.h
Line: 97

Line 97 documents max_latency_ms as 'Worst-case queue time observed' but the implementation never updates this field - it remains 0 from initialization. The field is dead/misleading.

title: tx_queue_stats_get reads stats without lock despite header claiming thread-safety
description:
File: lichen/subsys/lichen/link/tx_queue.c
Line: 424

Header line 207-208 states 'Thread-safe atomic copy under lock (no longer non-atomic)' but implementation at line 424 reads queue->stats without holding the lock. The stats struct is 24 bytes which cannot be atomically read, causing potential torn reads. The implementation comment acknowledges this is acceptable for diagnostics. Fix: either add lock_queue/unlock_queue around the read, or update header documentation to match implementation.

title: epoch.to_bytes raises OverflowError for negative or large values
description:
epoch.to_bytes(4, 'little') raises OverflowError if epoch < 0 or epoch >= 2^32. No validation or documentation of valid range. Same issue at line 198. Unlikely in practice since epochs are typically unix timestamps within u32 range, but unhandled exception is unexpected behavior.

File: python/src/lichen/channel_plan.py
Line: 55
close_reason: Closed

title: Silent EU868 fallback for unknown plan IDs
description:
get_plan() and get_plan_by_name() return EU868 for unknown plan IDs without warning. This hides configuration errors that could cause devices to operate on wrong frequencies.

File: python/src/lichen/channel_plan.py
Line: 174
close_reason: Verified fixed: get_plan() and get_plan_by_name() now raise UnknownPlanError for unknown plan IDs/names rather than silently falling back to EU868. All 69 channel plan tests pass.

title: tx_queue_count uses const qualifier but casts it away to lock
description:
Signature uses 'const struct tx_queue*' but implementation casts to non-const (line 383 in .c) to acquire mutex. Technically UB if original object was const-qualified. Inconsistent with tx_queue_empty and tx_queue_stats_get which correctly use non-const.

File: lichen/subsys/lichen/link/include/lichen/tx_queue.h
Line: 192

title: tx_queue_stats_get non-atomic read on multi-word struct
description:
Header tx_queue.h line 207-208 claims 'Thread-safe atomic copy under lock (no longer non-atomic)' but implementation at lines 424-429 does NOT take the lock and explicitly comments 'This read is not atomic'. On architectures where struct tx_queue_stats (6x uint32_t = 24 bytes) is not atomically copyable, concurrent writes during stats collection could produce inconsistent diagnostic data.

File: lichen/subsys/lichen/link/tx_queue.c
Line: 424

title: sync_hop.c: Potential division by zero if CONFIG_LICHEN_SYNC_HOP_SUPERFRAME_MS is 0
description: Line 48: Division by superframe_ms has no guard against zero. If CONFIG_LICHEN_SYNC_HOP_SUPERFRAME_MS is misconfigured to 0, this causes undefined behavior. However, this requires compile-time misconfiguration rather than runtime input, so it is an unlikely edge case.

title: emergency.py: Falsy timestamp=0 silently uses fallback field
description: Lines 124-125: Uses `body.get("t") or body.get("ts")` pattern. If t=0 (valid per line 141 which only rejects <0), Python evaluates `0 or ts_value` as ts_value. Payload {"from": "...", "t": 0, "ts": 100} silently uses timestamp=100 instead of the explicitly provided 0.
close_reason: Duplicate of vtw7. Bug already fixed - uses 'body["t"] if "t" in body' pattern.

title: test_vectors.py: Incorrect fallback produces confusing error on malformed test data
description: Line 183: `doc.get("vectors", doc)` falls back to iterating over the dict itself if "vectors" key is missing. This causes `v["name"]` to raise `TypeError: string indices must be integers` because `v` becomes a dict key string (e.g., "format_version"), not a vector dict. Should use direct access `doc["vectors"]` like other similar functions (lines 128, 135, 153, etc.) for a clear `KeyError` on malformed files.
close_reason: Closed

title: loadng.c: Prune interval off-by-one
description: Line 424: The condition `atomic_dec(&prune_countdown) <= 1` triggers pruning when countdown reaches 1 (after 15 calls) rather than 0 (after 16 calls). With PRUNE_INTERVAL=16, the actual interval is 15. The condition should be `<= 0` or `== 0` to match the defined interval constant.

title: python/src/lichen/loadng/messages.py: Signature length not validated during serialization
description: Lines 81, 124, 162: The to_bytes() methods serialize self.signature directly without validating length (must be 0 or 48). from_bytes() correctly validates, but a local caller can construct messages with invalid signature lengths that serialize successfully but would be rejected by receivers. Minor issue since receivers validate correctly.
close_reason: Closed

title: python/src/lichen/ccp.py: slot_hash silently produces wrong hash for short eui64 inputs
description:
The zip() on line 306 truncates to the shorter of eui64 and sfn_bytes (8 bytes). If eui64 is less than 8 bytes, only the provided bytes are XORed, producing a different hash than expected. No validation ensures eui64 is exactly 8 bytes.

Fix suggestion: Add validation: `if len(eui64) != 8: raise ValueError('eui64 must be exactly 8 bytes')`
close_reason: Duplicate of dl1g - fixed by adding eui64 length validation to select_channel()

title: tx_queue/main.c: ASSERT_EQ macro double-evaluates on failure
description:
Lines 33-38: When assertion fails, the first argument is evaluated twice (once for comparison, once for printf). For side-effectful expressions like tx_queue_pop(), this could call the function twice and print a different value than what was compared.

title: evict_if_needed could infinite loop if peers.remove fails to reduce len
description:
**File:** rust/lichen-link/src/link_layer.rs
**Lines:** 358-371 (ReplayProtector), 526-542 (LinkLayer)

**Issue:** The while loop 'while self.peers.len() > self.max_peers' relies on peers.remove() successfully reducing the map size. If remove() ever returns None (e.g., due to a bug where oldest_iid is stale), the loop would spin forever.

The current code does break on 'if let Some(iid) = oldest_iid ... else { break; }' which protects against empty maps, but the inner remove could theoretically fail if the HashMap is modified between finding oldest and removing.

**Trigger:** Theoretical only - requires concurrent modification or HashMap implementation bug.

**Bad behavior:** CPU spin in infinite loop.

**Suggested fix:** Use 'while let Some(oldest) = self.peers.iter().min_by_key(...).map(|(k,_)| *k) && self.peers.len() > self.max_peers { self.peers.remove(&oldest); ... }' pattern, or add iteration bound.
close_reason: No bug exists. The infinite loop scenario is impossible due to HashMap semantics: (1) max_peers uses NonZeroUsize ensuring capacity >= 1, (2) min_by_key() on a non-empty map always returns Some, (3) the key from iteration is guaranteed to exist in the map for the subsequent remove() call since this is &mut self with no concurrent modification. The existing break on oldest.is_none() handles the only valid empty-map case. Tests at lines 2050, 2075, 2112, and 2149 verify eviction works correctly under various conditions including counter saturation.

title: Flags field not validated - reserved bits accepted
description:
File: rust/lichen-core/src/loadng.rs
Lines: 377, 443, 520

The `flags` field in RREQ/RREP/RERR is parsed as raw u8 without validation. If the protocol spec reserves certain flag bits for future use or defines invalid combinations, malformed input could pass through undetected.

No validation should be added.

title: MIC comparison uses timing-variant == operator
description:
File: rust/lichen-schc/src/fragment.rs
Line: 963

Issue: The MIC comparison uses == which is not constant-time:
  if compute_mic(&self.storage[..packet_len]) == self.all1_mic

Severity: Low (P3) - CRC-32 is not cryptographic, so timing attacks cannot be exploited for authentication bypass. However, this sets a bad pattern.

What goes wrong: If this pattern is copied to code using cryptographic MACs, it creates a timing side-channel vulnerability. The == operator short-circuits on first byte difference.

Suggested fix: Add a comment explaining why constant-time is not needed here:
  // NOTE: CRC-32 is not cryptographic; constant-time comparison unnecessary

Alternative: Mark as opinion/wontfix since CRC-32 timing is not exploitable. The real fix is the SECURITY comment on compute_mic clarifying CRC-32 is not for authentication.
close_reason: False positive: The SCHC MIC is a CRC-32 (not a cryptographic MAC) used for transmission error detection per RFC 8724. The value is transmitted in the clear in the All-1 fragment, no secrets are involved, and timing side channels cannot leak anything an attacker does not already know. The project correctly uses constant-time comparison (via subtle crate) for actual security-sensitive operations like Schnorr signature verification.

title: version_is_newer special case (0,127) duplicates lollipop_cmp logic
description: File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/dodag.rs Line 77-78. The special case (new_ver, old_ver) == (0, 127) handles the linear-to-circular transition but lollipop_cmp already handles this via wrap_distance calculation. For (0, 127): a=0 linear, b=127 linear, abs_diff=127 > 16, returns None. So the special case is necessary. However, this duplicates RFC 6550 Appendix A logic - the special case encodes one specific valid wraparound while lollipop_cmp uses SEQUENCE_WINDOW for others. Document why this special case exists alongside the general algorithm.
close_reason: The bead's premise is incorrect. The special case (0, 127) in version_is_newer is NOT duplicate logic - it is an intentional policy override. lollipop_cmp(0, 127) returns None (incomparable) because both values are in the same region (0-127) with a gap of 127 exceeding SEQUENCE_WINDOW (16). The wrap_distance logic only applies to cross-region comparisons. The explicit test at line 1117 confirms: assert_eq!(lollipop_cmp(0, 127), None) followed by assert!(version_is_newer(0, 127)). This is a DODAG-specific policy decision to treat the 127->0 restart as a valid version bump, not a duplication. No changes needed.

title: test_vectors.py: _epoch_counter lacks input validation (P3)
description:
**File:** python/tests/test_vectors.py
**Lines:** 1678-1680

**Issue:**
```python
def _epoch_counter(epoch: int, seqnum: int) -> int:
    """Compute 24-bit replay counter from epoch and seqnum (spec 4.4)."""
    return (epoch << 16) | seqnum
```

**Problem:** No validation that:
- `epoch` is 8-bit (0-255)
- `seqnum` is 16-bit (0-65535)

If out-of-range values are passed (e.g., from corrupted test vector), the function silently produces incorrect results larger than 24 bits.

In test context this is low risk since vectors are controlled, but adding validation would catch malformed test data earlier.

**Suggested fix:**
```python
def _epoch_counter(epoch: int, seqnum: int) -> int:
    """Compute 24-bit replay counter from epoch and seqnum (spec 4.4)."""
    if not (0 <= epoch <= 255):
        raise ValueError(f"epoch {epoch} out of range [0, 255]")
    if not (0 <= seqnum <= 65535):
        raise ValueError(f"seqnum {seqnum} out of range [0, 65535]")
    return (epoch << 16) | seqnum
```
close_reason: fixed

title: receive_frame() does not validate destination address matches local node
description:
Location: rust/lichen-link/src/link_layer.rs line 515

receive_frame() parses the frame's dst_addr field but does not verify it matches the local node's IID or is a broadcast address. The frame is accepted if signature and replay checks pass, regardless of intended recipient.

This is likely intentional behavior (promiscuous mode, relaying, broadcast handling), but should be documented with a SECURITY comment explaining:
1. Why destination filtering is not performed at link layer
2. Where callers should filter if needed (upper layer)

If unintentional, frames intended for other nodes could be processed, wasting resources.
close_reason: Destination address validation is already implemented at the stack layer, not the link layer - this is intentional architecture. wire_is_for_local_stack() in stack.rs (lines 715-743) filters frames by destination BEFORE calling receive_frame(). Additionally, AuthenticatedFrame::is_unicast_for() (link_layer.rs:368-371) is provided for callers needing to check destination. The separation allows: (1) filter-before-crypto efficiency, (2) different filtering policies (promiscuous mode, forwarding). No code change needed.

title: O(n) peer signature scan has observable timing variation
description:
Location: rust/lichen-link/src/link_layer.rs lines 531-547

receive_frame() scans all peers calling verify_frame() until one succeeds. The number of verification attempts before success/failure is observable via timing.

This is already documented in the comment on lines 305-314 and acknowledged as acceptable in the threat model (lib.rs lines 21-27: 'Remote timing attacks over a high-latency LoRa mesh are impractical'). However, for completeness:

1. An attacker could learn relative position of sender in HashMap iteration order
2. Distinguishes 'unknown sender' (all peers checked) from 'known sender' (early exit)

This is informational only. The threat model explicitly considers this acceptable. No code change recommended for LoRa use case.
close_reason: The described O(n) peer scan vulnerability does not exist in the current implementation. The receive_frame path (lines 1085-1223) uses O(1) HashMap lookup via self.peers.get(&signer_iid) based on the signer EUI-64 from the frame header, then performs exactly one signature verification. There is no iteration over peers. The timing is constant with respect to peer count.

title: RootCandidate comparison may behave unexpectedly with NaN RF metrics
description:
File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/multi_instance.rs
Lines: 762-768

The Ord implementation for RootCandidate compares combined_score() (f32) values:

```rust
.then_with(|| {
    other
        .combined_score()
        .partial_cmp(&self.combined_score())
        .unwrap_or(Ordering::Equal)
})
```

While unwrap_or(Equal) prevents panics on NaN comparison, it makes NaN-containing candidates compare Equal to all others, potentially selecting an invalid candidate if NaN propagates into rssi_ema or snr_ema.

Trigger: A sensor or parsing bug sets rssi_ema to f32::NAN. This candidate compares Equal on the RF metric axis, falling through to IID tiebreaker.

Bad behavior: A candidate with corrupted RF metrics could be selected over better candidates, or cause non-deterministic ordering.

Fix: Filter out candidates with non-finite RF metrics before comparison, or treat NaN as worst-case value (-Infinity).
close_reason: Already implemented. The RootCandidate comparison handles NaN RF metrics via: (1) input sanitization in with_rf_metrics/with_rssi_ema/with_snr_ema that replaces NaN with worst-case defaults, (2) total_cmp() at line 977 for Ord compliance, and (3) comprehensive tests at lines 2271-2300 verifying NaN sanitization and sorting behavior.

title: Hardware quirks model for Medium simulator
description:
Model real radio hardware imperfections:

1. **Warm-up time**: TX/RX mode switch takes 1-5ms, packets during transition are lost
2. **PLL lock failures**: Occasional frequency lock failure (0.1-1% of TX attempts), retry needed
3. **Crystal drift**: ±10-30ppm frequency offset, affects capture effect and collision detection
4. **RSSI accuracy**: Real RSSI has ±3dB error, add noise to reported values
5. **RX deaf time**: After TX, radio is deaf for ~100μs (TX/RX turnaround)
6. **CAD false positives/negatives**: Real CAD has ~5% error rate

Implementation: Optional RadioQuirks config on SimRadio, disabled by default for deterministic tests.
notes:
Design decision: Medium assigns quirks (option B), not radio declares.

API:
- medium.set_quirks_profile('moderate') — global default
- medium.set_quirks('node-7', QuirkProfile(...)) — per-node override
- medium.set_quirks('node-3', PRESETS['sx1276']) — named hardware preset

Named presets as data:
- PRESETS['ideal'] — no quirks (deterministic tests)
- PRESETS['moderate'] — typical real-world
- PRESETS['sx1276'] — specific chip characteristics
- PRESETS['garbage'] — stress testing

QuirkProfile fields: warmup_ms, pll_fail_rate, crystal_ppm, rssi_noise_db, cad_false_positive_rate, cad_false_negative_rate, rx_deaf_us
close_reason: Hardware quirks model already fully implemented in lora_medium package. QuirkProfile includes warmup_ms (TX/RX mode switch 1-5ms), pll_fail_rate (0.1-1% PLL lock failures), plus crystal_ppm, rssi_noise_db, cad_false_positive_rate, cad_false_negative_rate, rx_deaf_us. Named presets (ideal, moderate, sx1276, sx1262, garbage) available. Medium class has set_quirks/get_quirks/clear_quirks API. Comprehensive tests in python/tests/sim/test_quirks.py (315 lines).

description: In rust/lichen-schc/src/fragment.rs std_ext module, lines 1231/1249/1274 use self.rule_id.unwrap_or(0) when constructing ACK/NACK. While rule_id is always Some at these sites in correct usage, if a future bug left it as None, this would silently construct an ACK with rule_id=0 (invalid per check_rule) that only fails at wire serialization time with FragmentError::InvalidRuleId. Contrast with no_std FragmentReceiver line 1000 which uses self.rule_id? for proper error propagation. Fix: use self.rule_id.expect("rule_id must be set") or self.rule_id.unwrap() to expose invariant violations immediately.
