title: pynacl dependency unused - premature optimization
description:
**Dependencies / Bloat**

pyproject.toml includes `pynacl>=1.5` as a core dependency, but:
- No imports of nacl/pynacl anywhere in src/lichen/
- Link layer (which would use crypto) is a stub
- This adds a C extension dependency for no benefit

pynacl requires libsodium which:
- Increases install complexity
- May need compilation on some platforms
- Adds security surface area

Either:
- Remove pynacl until link layer is implemented
- Move to optional dependencies: `[crypto]`
- Add a comment explaining the intended use

Note: cbor2 is similarly unused currently (no CBOR encoding in simulator), but it's pure Python so less impactful.

Files: pyproject.toml
close_reason: pynacl is actively used throughout the codebase: schnorr48.py, identity.py, edhoc.py, group_oscore.py, and address_collision.py all import from nacl.bindings. The bead's premise is incorrect - the dependency is not unused.

title: oscore clone housekeeping: dead non-compiled sibling modules hold divergent pre-port API copies
description: Found by 3x codereview of the rust-oscore observe port (9liz unblock work). /home/mark/crates/oscore/src/ contains unprotect.rs, context.rs, protect.rs, crypto.rs, option.rs, types.rs, tests.rs, group.rs that are NOT declared in lib.rs (only error, seqnum, edhoc, tests are) and reference crate::context::/crate::types:: paths that do not exist - dead files from an abandoned modular refactor. They differ semantically from the live lib.rs (unprotect.rs checks response PIVs with is_replay at L199 and lacks the empty-payload rejection), so anyone auditing the observe API from the directory listing reads the wrong implementation, and anyone 'restoring' the modules while fixing ythw breaks the build. Action: delete or archive them in the clone when the observe work lands (clone is machine-local; the deletion does not touch the lichen workspace).

title: oscore observe profile: no-PIV notification rejection is stricter than RFC 8613 4.1.3.5 - document deliberate deviation
description: Found by 3x codereview of the rust-oscore observe port (9liz unblock work). begin_unprotect_observe_response rejects every notification without an explicit PIV (InvalidParam, /home/mark/crates/oscore/src/lib.rs:1292-1296). RFC 8613 s4.1.3.5 permits the FIRST response to an Observe registration to omit the Partial IV (nonce from the request), so a fully RFC-compliant server's first notification would be dropped. The stricter behavior is a deliberate fail-closed choice: with the request-PIV one-shot guard bypassed for notifications, allowing no-PIV notifications would alias the AEAD nonce across notifications. Action: record the deviation in the LICHEN observe profile / spec security section so the C implementation and interop vectors agree with it deliberately (C side must also always include a fresh PIV per notification).

title: oscore port: add notification-replay rejection test (would have caught ythw)
description: Found by 3x codereview of the rust-oscore observe port (9liz unblock work). observe_notifications_share_request_piv_and_require_fresh_piv (/home/mark/crates/oscore/src/lib.rs, ~2483-2556) pins fresh-PIV requirement, request-PIV sharing, and ordinary one-shot consumption, but never REPLAYS a committed notification - under project-LICHEN-worker6-ythw the replay is accepted, so that assertion is the single most valuable missing pin. Add it AFTER the ythw fix lands (it would fail today): begin+commit the first notification, re-present the same (option, ciphertext) to begin_unprotect_observe_response, assert Err(Replay).

title: gateway oscore load() performs heal FS writes inside the radio ingress path (latency under FS failure)
description: Found by 3x codereview of the recipient-store heal (9liz), robustness pass. is_replay()/load() are read-shaped APIs but can perform a heal write (fsync+rename, gateway.rs:463) synchronously inside packet dispatch (~1360-1380), and on persistent heal-write failure every packet for that context pays 2 file reads + 2 schnorr48 keypair derivations + 2 verifies + 1 failed sign. Bounded per call, no amplification, and fail-closed is correct - but under a degraded FS the radio loop stalls per packet. If gateway latency budgets tighten, move the heal write off the hot path (background repair or defer to accept()) without changing the fail-closed semantics pinned by the 9liz tests.

title: gateway oscore store tests leak temp dirs when an assert fails mid-test
description: Found by 3x codereview of the recipient-store heal (9liz), robustness pass. The persistent-store tests remove their temp dirs only at the end (remove_dir_all after the last assert, e.g. gateway.rs:2062-2084); an early assert failure leaks the dir in std::env::temp_dir. Acceptable for CI (next runs never collide thanks to pid+AtomicU64 naming), but a std::path::Path guard struct or a small drop-guard helper would clean up on failure. Low value; bundle with any future test work in this file.

title: gateway oscore stores: unreachable Full branch in accept() cache-miss path (dead defensive code)
description: Found by 3x codereview of the recipient-store heal (9liz), correctness pass. gateway.rs:537-541 (recipient) and the sender equivalent (~647-650): accept() first calls is_replay -> load(), which either inserts the cache entry or propagates an error, so the else-branch push (and its capacity check) can never execute. Harmless dead defensive code today; delete it or restructure when the eviction policy (project-LICHEN-worker6-2c2k) lands, so the capacity invariant has exactly one enforcement point.

title: gateway oscore seal key is the identity seed on the state FS: seal is tamper-evidence only
description: Found by 3x codereview of the recipient-store heal (9liz), security pass (informational, design-accepted). lichend.rs:202 derives the sealing seed from the node identity seed persisted on the state FS (lichend.rs:165-192). A disk-READ attacker can derive the schnorr48 seal keypair and forge state/floor records - but the same read already yields the Ed25519 identity, so this adds nothing beyond full compromise. The seal is tamper-EVIDENCE against write-only/lagging-replica attackers, not confidentiality against read+write attackers. Action: state this contract explicitly where the sealing seed is documented (gateway docs / spec security section) so a future refactor does not quietly assume more.

title: gateway: dev() rollback-root independence check lives only in lichend, not in Gateway::new_persistent
description: Found by 3x codereview of the recipient-store heal (9liz), security pass (informational). The anti-rollback design relies on the floor root being on a filesystem independent of the state root; the enforcement (dev() comparison) exists only in the lichend binary (rust/lichen-gateway/src/bin/lichend.rs:1408-1425). Gateway::new_persistent (rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs:915-928) checks only canonicalize/nesting, so another embedder of the library constructor silently skips the check, collapsing the mitigation to directory separation. Promote the dev() independence check into Gateway::new_persistent (return GatewayOpenError) or a new constructor, keep the binary call site.

title: RollcallResource.render_post returns 2.01 without Location-Path
description: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/emergency.py:452 (pre-existing, noted during zbn8 review): POST /rollcall returns 2.01 Created without Location-Path/Query, the same RFC 7252 §5.8.1 conformance point that motivated the /sos 2.01->2.04 fix. Unlike /sos, a rollcall POST does create a new rollcall entry, so 2.01 is defensible IF a Location-Path option is added (e.g. /rollcall/<id>); otherwise switch to 2.04. Decide and align the C checkin_resource.h documentation which documents 'POST /rollcall (18.6.2) -> 2.01 Created'.

title: New announce integration tests leak temp dirs when an assertion fails
description: Found by robustness review of project-LICHEN-worker6-dowx. remove_roots in announce.rs tests (unique_test_roots/remove_roots helpers, ~1074-1077) runs only at the end of each happy path; on assertion failure the pid-suffixed dirs under std::env::temp_dir() leak (<=2 dirs per test, <=6 total). Bounded and acceptable in the short term. Fix with a guard struct whose Drop removes the roots.

title: announce_store read/write leaves unzeroized sealing-seed copies on the stack
description: Found by security review of project-LICHEN-worker6-dowx (pre-existing in child-1 code, but now on the announce admission hot path). AnnounceTrustStore::read and write (announce_store.rs:200-201, 220-221) call derive_keypair(&Seed::new(*seed)) which copies the node persistence key material onto the stack on EVERY record read, not just writes. The durable copy is correctly Zeroizing and Debug is redacted, but each pinned_pubkey_for durable fallback and each admission check leaves a transient non-zeroized seed copy in stack memory. Hygiene inconsistency with the crate's own Zeroizing discipline; low exposure window, no logging path. Fix: keep a pre-derived keypair in the store at construction, or zeroize the transient copies.

title: SOS cancel docs and minor behavior divergences vs DELETE path
description: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/emergency.py: (1) class docstring (~line 51-59) still says only 'DELETE cancels.' — update for the new POST type=cancel surface (2.04 CHANGED). (2) Ordering divergence: render_post decodes payload BEFORE the idle check, so a malformed POST-cancel to an idle node returns 400 where DELETE-when-idle returns 404 (render_delete checks active first) — observable only in malformed+idle combos; align or document. (3) Cancel bodies without node/ts are accepted (parity with render_delete which accepts arbitrary signed cores; spec 18.4.2 defines cancel within the alert format that includes them) — tighten both paths if strict format compliance is wanted.

title: SOS cancel-path test gaps: stale-seq replay, rate-budget neutrality, routing discrimination
description: python/tests/coap/test_sos_resource.py TestSosPutDelete: (1) the replay/stale-sequence gate on the POST-cancel path (emergency.py:304) is untested — after a successful cancel the resource is idle so naive replay hits 404; needs re-activate-then-replay-cancel (expect UNAUTHORIZED). (2) No test that cancel does not consume the rate budget (activate -> POST-cancel -> immediate re-activate within burst should be CREATED). (3) test_post_cancel_by_non_originator_rejected passes with AND without the fix (activate path also rejects wrong-key bodies) — it cannot discriminate routing; acceptable, but note it in a comment or use a distinguishing observable.

title: Self-secure SOS sequence acceptance (check accept() return, order before cancel)
description: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/emergency.py:306-307 (_cancel_from_body) and pre-existing at render_post:272-274 / render_delete:354-355: the boolean return of self._sequences.accept() is discarded; safety depends on the adjacent last_seen pre-check with no await between them. Any refactor inserting an await between check and accept breaks it. Harden: 'if not self._sequences.accept(...): return UNAUTHORIZED' (accept returns False on non-advancing), and in _cancel_from_body swap accept() to precede... rather: call accept() only after cancel() succeeds, or check its return, so a raise in cancel() cannot leave a consumed sequence with the alert still active (verified unreachable with pinned aiocoap, defensive only).

title: SOS cancel path skips trust-store verify_or_pin (defense-in-depth parity)
description: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/emergency.py:285-301 (_cancel_from_body) mirrors render_delete in never consulting self._trust_store.verify_or_pin, which the activation path enforces (emergency.py:252-256). Cancel authorization rests on IID-derivation + signature; exploiting requires a second key colliding on the victim's 8-byte IID (~2^63), so this is defense-in-depth parity with DELETE, not an introduced gap. Either add the check for parity with activate or document the divergence deliberately.

title: Clarify which poison assert is load-bearing in persist-awaitable test
description: python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:752-758: the 'Poisoned fail-closed' comment sits above verifier.current() is None and verifier.minimum_record_version == 0, which pass under a no-poison mutant (they pin 'commit never happened', guaranteed by virgin state); only the evaluate_epoch_floor assert enforces the poison contract. A future reader could misattribute which assert is load-bearing — add a one-line comment separating the two (non-commitment vs poison-revocation).

title: reject_awaitable_result suppresses BaseException from cancel()/close()
description: python/src/lichen/_sync_callbacks.py:29-33: the contextlib.suppress(BaseException) around attacker-controlled cancel()/close() swallows KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit raised by a malicious hook — fail-closed is preserved (TypeError still raised, awaitable terminated best-effort), but suppressing BaseException is broader than needed. Consider suppressing Exception only, or suppressing BaseException but re-raising KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit. Needs a robustness pass; note cancel() of a cancelled Task can legitimately raise CancelledError (a BaseException), which is why the broad suppress exists — decide which contract is intended.

title: Sibling OSError test also lacks a poison pin (install-path)
description: python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:685 (pre-existing, mutant-verified): test_provision_persistence_failure_does_not_commit asserts current() is None and minimum_record_version == 0, both of which hold without _poison_after_persistence_failure on the install path (state was never committed). The whole suite pins install-path poison only via reentry tests (:1674, :2206), never via a persistence-hook-failure trigger. Add the same floor-channel PERSISTENCE_FAILED pin as the persist-awaitable tests.

title: Assert no stray durable writes in awaitable clear test (saved list unasserted)
description: python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:760, 770: the clear test's persist_rollback_state=saved.append capture is never asserted. Cheap pin that the rejected clear transition performed no stray durable writes beyond the one legitimate install: assert len(saved) == 1 after the rejection (and it documents that the capture is load-bearing rather than vestigial).

title: Document emergent sample-invalidated-or-replayed dependency in floor-raise test
description: python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:948 + stratum.py:438-439,609-610: the pinned 'sample-invalidated-or-replayed' reason for adopt/consider is emergent, not direct — the candidate is issued (seq 2, samples.py:341-342) before the call, and _clear_locked's eager invalidation bumps __issuance_high_water to _latest_issuance_sequence() (=2), so the reject fires at stratum.py:609-610 before _rejection's 'below-epoch-floor' (stratum.py:145). Deterministic, but the dependency chain is undocumented; add a one-line comment citing stratum.py:438-439 to prevent a future 'why is this the reason?' fix.

title: replace-policy leg cannot distinguish old-policy vs new-policy validation ordering
description: python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:954: the replace-policy iteration uses a replacement policy identical to the old one, so validation placed after self.__policy = self._copy_policy(...) (stratum.py:473) produces the identical observable reason 'below-live-epoch-floor:accepted'. Only a replacement policy that would itself reject the below-floor sample can distinguish the orderings. The bead's core requirement (clear happens inside replace_policy before any read) is still pinned; this is the remaining ordering nuance.

title: Document CPython >=3.11.3 floor: asyncio.Lock cancelled-after-grant wedge
description: pyproject requires-python '>=3.11' but a task cancelled at the exact moment asyncio.Lock.acquire is granted can leave the lock wedged (no owner, _locked=True) on CPython 3.11.0-3.11.2 (gh-90155, fixed in 3.11.3/3.12.0). send()/drain_tx_queue() would hang forever on affected interpreters. Window is microscopic and the project venv is 3.11.15; on patched interpreters the lock self-heals and no queue state exists to corrupt. Fix: bump requires-python to >=3.11.3 or document the interpreter floor caveat. Found by robustness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-9qpz.

title: QueueRadio.receive ignores timeout deadline (fixture fidelity gap)
description: python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:83-85 (pre-existing fixture): QueueRadio.receive discards _timeout_ms and returns None immediately. Tests using it cannot detect a future production change where LinkLayer.receive retries on None or applies timeout semantics internally. Consider a fixture that honors the deadline (e.g. returns None only after the timeout elapses).

title: Dead max_sample_age_s fixture in existing DIO tracker test
description: python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py:395-398 (pre-existing, in reviewed range): max_sample_age_s=30 and clock.set(100) are dead fixture values for the asserted outcome — the sample was already claimed by authorized.adopt(sample) at line 382, so verifier._claim returns None and _adopt_locked rejects 'sample-already-considered' (stratum.py:605-607) before any age check fires. The config misleads readers into thinking age rejection is covered there.

title: Pin network replay high-water LRU eviction (honest signer eviction)
description: python/src/lichen/timing/stratum.py:626-632: the MAX_NETWORK_REPLAY_GENERATIONS LRU cap (popitem(last=False)) can evict an honest signer's high-water entry when an attacker-controlled signer floods 256 key rotations, re-admitting that signer's already-consumed counter. No test pins eviction behavior. Exploitation is expensive (256 live generations plus defeating link replay and freshness policy) but the behavior is unpinned — add a test that documents/guards the eviction semantics.

title: Test re-issue from same AuthenticatedDio with fresh receipt time
description: Both new DIO replay tests (python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py ~438, 467) re-verify the SAME AuthenticatedDio object, so a regression keying time-sample dedupe on receipt time instead of the frame-derived counter (time_sync.py:433) would pass (identical received_monotonic). A re-issue with fresh receipt time (OTA retransmission path) is the untested defense-in-depth route; same-frame link replay is already covered at lines ~548-555.

title: Pin DioTimeVerifier replay_counter composition with nonzero epoch
description: python/tests/timing/test_time_sync.py new DIO tests (~lines 439, 448) assert replay_counter equality/equality-to-2 using epoch 0 counters 1 and 2. A broken (epoch << 16) | seqnum composition (time_sync.py:433) would still produce 1 and 2 and pass. Add an assertion with a nonzero-epoch frame (e.g. counter (1<<16)|5) or pin a literal == 1 on the first sample.

title: Announce store tests leak temp dirs on assertion failure
description: announce_store.rs tests call std::fs::remove_dir_all only on the success path; any assert failure leaves lichen-node-announce-* dirs (0600 sealed records derived from test key material) in std::env::temp_dir(). Disk litter only — pid+counter names are collision-free. Fix: drop-guard struct so cleanup runs on unwind. Mirrors existing gap in gateway and lichen-hal tests. Found by robustness codereview of project-LICHEN-worker6-12zy.

title: identity-probe-1788045271
identity-probe
Fix stale test-vector comment in superframe election test
description: P4 (wave-5 review of worker6-hjot): superframe.rs:458-461 comment in test_elect_time_master_from_test_vector still cites the known-wrong test-vector decimals that the sibling test (~:432-437) explicitly corrects. Cosmetic: reword the comment.

title: Fix inaccurate gate comment and state_path annotation in new tests
description: P4 cosmetics (wave-4 review): (1) lichend.rs first_boot_trust_partial_recovers_at_initial_generation comment says the committed-stage retry 'loads the durable state without the initial-generation gate' - the gate still executes but passes via the manifest_stage >= boundary_stage disjunct; reword. (2) python/tests/announce/test_admission_recovery.py state_path fixture is annotated object instead of Path. No behavior change.

title: Fix mechanism comment in node permit restore test
description: P4 (wave-3 review of worker6-k4n4): python/tests/test_node.py (~:2318-2324) final assertion comment says the 4th announce is rejected by a permit check; it is actually rejected via STALE_SEQNUM (permit absent -> reconciling False, processor.py:127-143). Test is non-vacuous; only the comment is wrong. Fix the comment wording.

title: Guard zeroize feature-unification against oscore crate major bump
description: rust/lichen-oscore/Cargo.toml:25-33 direct aes/hmac zeroize pins guarantee zeroization only while the oscore fork uses the same aes 0.8/hmac 0.13 majors. If oscore bumps majors, two copies coexist, unification silently breaks, and the compile-time asserts in zeroize_asserts.rs:61,68 keep passing against the now-unused versions while real cipher/HMAC state goes unzeroized. Add a cargo-deny duplicate-versions check (or CI cargo tree -d gate) or at minimum a warning comment on the assert module.

title: OSCORE spec gap: OSCORE+Observe interaction unimplemented in C; spec silent — decision needed
description:
SPEC STATUS: spec/06-security.md is silent on OSCORE Observe interaction. RFC 8613 makes Observe support optional (§4.1.3.5 MAY), but once OSCORE-protected notifications are used it is normative: server SHALL include a fresh Partial IV in responses to Observe registrations except the first (§4.1.3.5, §8.3.1), Inner+Outer Observe handling, Outer Code FETCH for registrations, and client-side Notification Number replay tracking (§4.1.3.5.2, §7.4.1).

IMPL (C): no OSCORE-protected Observe exists. coap_oscore.c always protects responses via oscore_protect_response (no-PIV/request-nonce mode; coap_oscore.c:280-286) — never oscore_protect_response_with_piv (oscore_protect.c:885, which exists for exactly the §8.4 fresh-PIV mode). The C CoAP client cannot send an OSCORE-protected Observe registration (protect path passes NULL inner options, coap_client.c:534-537; only the OSCORE option rides on the outer request). Server-side position Observe (lichen/subsys/lichen/coap/coap_location.c:385-410,880) sends cleartext notifications only, gated to privacy=PUBLIC. Rust side delegates to the external oscore crate and has observe_responses.rs tests.

IMPACT: none today because C never emits OSCORE-protected notifications; but spec/12-apps observable resources and private/group position modes imply protected streaming is expected eventually. If OSCORE-protected Observe is added to C naively through the existing coap_oscore_protect_response, notifications would reuse the registration request's nonce for every update and clients could not order/replay-check them (RFC 8613 §4.1.3.5.2 violations).

DECISION NEEDED (informational, P4): either (a) commit to OSCORE-protected Observe in C — wire the fresh-PIV path for notifications, Inner/Outer Observe, FETCH outer code, and client Notification Number tracking, or (b) document C as cleartext-Observe-only for public resources and keep protected resources non-observable. Filing so the choice is explicit rather than accidental.

title: Group OSCORE modules: input-validation consistency (shared secret validator, unwrap TypeError, docstring overclaim)
description: P4 review findings across worker6-9mkj.1/.2 modules. (a) epoch accepts any non-empty secret length (3-byte secret succeeds locally, fails only at distribution) while wrap enforces 16..128/multiple-of-8 - share one master-secret validator. (b) unwrap_group_key raises TypeError (not documented ValueError) when member_wrapped_keys is None/non-iterable - probe-confirmed; WrappedGroupKey arrives from deserialized wire payload; add isinstance(dict) guard raising ValueError. (c) epoch docstring at :163 overclaims: says use .value for vector reason string but PREVIOUS value is previous_in_grace while grace_period_1hr vector reason is within_grace_period; scope the claim to ROLLBACK/FUTURE/GRACE_EXPIRED.

title: TX queue vectors: reject duplicate JSON object keys
description: Round-4 security review found gen_vectors.py uses json.load's last-key-wins behavior. Duplicate keys can leave the parsed object and digest unchanged while another cross-implementation parser takes the first key or rejects the document. Load canonical vectors with duplicate-key rejection and reject non-finite JSON constants; add generator regression coverage.
close_reason: gen_vectors.py loader now rejects duplicate keys (object_pairs_hook, any nesting), NaN/Infinity/-Infinity (parse_constant), and 1e999->inf overflow (post-load finite scan). 13 tests in new python/tests/timing/test_tx_queue_gen_loader.py; canonical vectors byte-identical through strict loader; 60 python tests pass, ruff clean.

title: TX queue vector generator: compare nested JSON types strictly
description: Round-3 security review found expect_path's scalar type check does not recurse into lists/dicts, so Python equality still treats nested false equal to 0 and true equal to 1. Implement recursive strict-type equality for JSON objects/arrays/scalars and use it for every expected path.
acceptance_criteria: Nested boolean/integer substitutions fail validation with a clear path; canonical vector generation and lint pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by host sanitizer suite plus review cycle; superseding round-4 findings are tracked separately

title: TX queue destroy: prevent retry after failed rollback restoration
description: Round-2 security review found that if frame_pool_destroy succeeds, pthread_mutex_destroy fails, and fallible frame_pool reinitialization also fails, the object retains a queue mutex but an invalid pool mutex; retry enters invalid synchronization. Remove reliance on fallible rollback or mark the object terminal and make every later queue/destroy operation reject without touching destroyed synchronization.
acceptance_criteria: Every tx_queue_destroy failure either leaves a fully retryable object or a clearly terminal object whose later public operations fail safely without locking destroyed state; failure-path tests cover the supported behavior; host sanitizer suite passes.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by host sanitizer suite plus review cycle; superseding round-4 findings are tracked separately

title: TX queue vector generator: reject boolean integer lookalikes
description: Round-2 security review found expect_path uses Python equality, where false == 0 and true == 1. Malformed priority/deadline/capacity values represented as JSON booleans can therefore satisfy integer expectations. Require exact compatible types when comparing generated-vector expectations, excluding bool for integers.
acceptance_criteria: expect_path rejects bool when an integer is expected and reports a clear vector/case/path error; canonical generation and lint pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by host sanitizer suite plus review cycle; superseding round-4 findings are tracked separately

title: TX queue: renormalize FIFO sequence before uint64 wrap
description: Round-2 review found raw uint64_t enqueue ordering still fails at the theoretical UINT64_MAX to zero wrap, making newly enqueued entries appear oldest. Renormalize the at-most-four live entry orders before terminal wrap while preserving relative FIFO order, and add an actual UINT64_MAX regression test.
acceptance_criteria: Enqueue at next_enqueue_order UINT64_MAX renormalizes live orders and preserves FIFO/oldest-lowest preemption; no counter wrap can reverse ordering; sanitizer-backed tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified by host sanitizer suite plus review cycle; superseding round-4 findings are tracked separately

title: CoAP v3 compression rules do not gate on NH==UDP (MQTT-SN rule does)
description: compress_global_coap_v3/link_local_v3 validate 5680..5695 ports + UDP checksum but never check ipv6_next_header==IPV6_NH_UDP; compress_mqtt_sn does. TX-side misclassification needs crafted ports+checksum; decompress-side revalidation limits impact. Add NH==UDP to both v3 CoAP rule paths for consistency.
close_reason: compress_global_coap_v3 and compress_link_local_coap_v3 in lichen/subsys/lichen/schc/schc_compress.c now gate ipv6_next_header(packet) != IPV6_NH_UDP -> SCHC_ERR_NO_MATCHING_RULE, matching compress_mqtt_sn's pattern (:385). Verified: clang -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra clean; canonical CoAP vectors still accepted - schc_rule1_compress_test (global CoAP path) PASSED and schc_rule5_compress_test (link-local CoAP path) PASSED, run as host CMake ctest on the Mac (Apple clang 21, 100% tests passed); these host suites hardcode -std=c23 which the AWS gcc 11.5 cannot parse, so they are Mac-side by design. Link-side Zephyr builds of the same source pass on AWS (link_crypto build compiles the schc subsystem). Note: schc.c lichen_rule_compress_coap already gated NH at the rule-wrapper level; this fix closes the direct compress_coap entry point.

title: Shift-UB comment overstates: ILP32 uint32_t is unsigned int so old shift was defined-wrapping not UB
description: oscore_protect.c:95-99 wording: promotion-to-signed UB only where int covers all uint32 values; ILP32 Zephyr targets have uint32_t==unsigned int so old idiom was defined wrapping. uint64 fix bit-identical either way. Reword comment for precision.
close_reason: Reworded the shift comment in response_replay_update (oscore_protect.c) for ABI precision. New wording states: the shift is computed in uint64_t because the integer promotion of a uint32_t lvalue is ABI-dependent - on ILP32 targets (uint32_t == unsigned int, all current Zephyr targets here) (*window << shift) was already defined wrapping arithmetic, while on an ABI whose int is wider than 32 bits the promoted type is signed int and a shift count >= 32 would be UB; the uint64_t intermediate is defined wrapping on every ABI and produces identical bit patterns. This replaces the previous overstatement ('promotes to signed int, formally UB once bit 31 participates'), which was wrong for ILP32 where promotion is a no-op to unsigned int. Code unchanged (the uint64_t fix was already in place and bit-identical either way). Verified: clang -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra on all 7 oscore TUs at PT_MAX 256/2048 x MAX_CONTEXTS 8/32 clean; harness windows exercise shift<32 and >=32 branches (rr/margin harness, ASan+UBSan clean).

title: TDMA latch single-threaded guarantee exceeds code; document contract or take seq_lock
description: link_ctx.h:94-96 'latch pair guarantees at most one lichen_tdma_init per (context,epoch)' but tx.c:70-74 mutates latch/tdma without seq_lock while load_key/set_epoch/cleanup touch ctx->epoch under lock. Idempotent+fail-open racy writes, no worse than HEAD statics, but doc overpromises. Either document single-thread-per-context contract or serialize.
close_reason: link_ctx.h TDMA latch doc extended in place (doc-only; chose document-over-serialize since the racy window is idempotent and fail-open and nxwa offers either remedy): latch guarantee now explicitly holds per single-threaded context owner; the latch is checked/updated by lichen_link_tx() outside seq_lock, so concurrent TX vs lichen_link_load_key()/cleanup() on the SAME context is caller-error (cross-referenced lichen_link_cleanup() thread-safety warning, matching surrounding doc style); worst-case racy outcomes stated as a redundant lichen_tdma_init() or one ungated TX (fail-open, matching HEAD statics), not serialized. No code change; latch logic untouched. Verified: clang -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra exit 0 on link_ctx.c and tdma.c consuming the header.

title: Huge finite Decimal ttl yields DEFAULT_TTL while equally-huge int clamps MAX_TTL
description: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/deaddrop.py:171 area. float(Decimal('1e999')) returns inf WITHOUT OverflowError so suppress() blocks untouched, ttl stays None, falls to DEFAULT (24h) instead of MAX_TTL(7d) like huge-int path. Fail-safe direction (< requested retention), wire-unreachable (codec finiteness 400s). Align by treating inf/nan-after-conversion as >=MAX clamp per docstring claim.
close_reason: Fixed _extract_ttl post-conversion non-finite handling: +inf->MAX_TTL, -inf/nan->0 (deaddrop.py). Docstring updated. Note: premise corrected - huge int ttl ALSO collapsed to DEFAULT before; both now clamp at 7d in parity. sNaN gated by is_finite() pre-check (never reaches conversion; falls to default, no crash) - covered. 9 parametrized unit cases added; all 79 deaddrop module tests pass (isolation harness: concurrent worker's mid-save lichen/schc fragment/session_manager IndentationError+circular import blocks any tests/coap collection in shared tree; unrelated files untouched; ruff clean on both modified files).

title: Missing nullability annotations nvm registration write_cb/read_cb
description: include/lichen/oscore.h:274-275 clang -Wnullability-completeness flagged; every other public API annotated _Nonnull/_Nullable. Two-token completeness fix.
close_reason: Added _Nullable annotations to both callback params of oscore_nvm_register_callbacks() (include/lichen/oscore.h) matching sibling style: oscore_nvm_write_cb _Nullable write_cb, oscore_nvm_read_cb _Nullable read_cb (NULL disables, per the doc comment). Also annotated the matching definition signature in oscore_ctx.c so declaration and definition stay identical. Header's existing !__clang__/!__has_feature(nullability) empty-macro fallback (oscore.h:70-77) makes the annotations inert under GCC/Zephyr builds — expanded form is textually the pre-change signature. Verified: clang -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra -Wnullability-completeness clean on all 7 oscore TUs at default and max Kconfig configs; no PRIu64/format drift. Note: coap_oscore.c (another oscore.h consumer) could not be syntax-checked in this sandbox because it requires the full zephyr/net CoAP+net_ip headers not worth stubbing for this leaf scope; its exposure to this change is limited to the two headers, both validated tree-wide elsewhere (dead macro proven zero-ref; annotation placement identical to 20+ existing annotated declarations in the same header).

title: Stale RFC-conformance comment + dead OSCORE_NONCE_S_POS=6 constant document obsolete nonce layout
description: oscore_ctx.c:210-216 comment claims ID-length overlap handled incorrectly implying byte-6 S placement; compute_nonce now conformant S@byte0, ID right-aligned byte7, PIV 8..12 (RFC 8613 Sec5.2/Fig8, verified vs python/rust cross vectors). include/lichen/oscore.h:109 OSCORE_NONCE_S_POS(6) zero references, asserts obsolete layout. Remove/reword both to prevent restoration regression.
close_reason: oscore_ctx.c: stale nonce-overlap paragraph replaced with the conformant layout statement: S flag at byte 0, Sender/Recipient ID right-aligned into byte 7, PIV in bytes 8..12 per RFC 8613 Section 5.2/Figure 8, implemented by compute_nonce() and verified against Python/Rust cross-implementation vectors — prevents restoration of the obsolete byte-6-S mental model. The >7-byte ID rejection gate below the comment is preserved unchanged (zero behavior change). include/lichen/oscore.h: OSCORE_NONCE_S_POS (6) macro and its @deprecated doc block deleted after re-grep confirming zero references tree-wide outside .beads metadata and the definition itself. Verified: clang -fsyntax-only clean on all oscore TUs consuming the header (protect/ctx/replay/option/nonce/cbor/hkdf) at default and max Kconfig configs.

title: Signed-promotion left-shift UB idiom replicated in new response_replay_update helper
description: File: oscore_protect.c:95 (also pre-existing oscore_replay.c:161 pattern out-of-blast-radius note only). (*window << shift)|1 / |= 1U << diff shift uint32_t promoted to int; formally UB once bit31 set. New-from-this-round helper must use uint32_t/uint64_t math casts. In-scope hygiene; sibling legacy optional follow-up beaded separately if desired.
close_reason: Fixed both flagged shifts in response_replay_update() (oscore_protect.c) with explicit uint64_t intermediate arithmetic per modern style, comments added: (1) newest-seq branch: *window = shift >= 32 ? 1U : (uint32_t)(((uint64_t)*window << shift) | 1U) — the old (*window << shift) promoted uint32_t to signed int making bit-31 participation formal UB; uint64 math truncated back is bit-identical for every previously-defined input (shift < 32 guaranteed by the ternary, >= 32 collapses to 1 exactly as before). (2) in-window branch: *window |= diff >= 32 ? 0U : (uint32_t)((uint64_t)1 << diff) — old 1U << diff was defined only for diff < 32 (guaranteed by callers via response_replay_acceptable with REPLAY_WINDOW range 16..32, i.e. zero observable change on the reachable domain) but formally undefined otherwise; now defined everywhere. Legacy oscore_replay.c:161 pattern deliberately untouched (out-of-blast-radius per scope; verified unchanged in source). response_replay_acceptable() line 83 bare-1U shift left as-is: unsigned int shift by < 32 is fully defined, no promotion hazard. Verified: clang -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra -Wshift-count-overflow clean on oscore_protect.c at default and max Kconfig configs; no PRIu64/format-string drift (helper contains no format usage); token greps confirm old signed-promotion idiom absent and guard idiom present.

title: sos_alert_to_cbor encoder emits coordinates its own decoder rejects
description: sos_alert_set_location void/unvalidated (sos_alert.h:134-137 documents ranges); to_cbor no value validation (sos_alert.c:405-495): local NaN/91.0 serializes onto air where receivers drop. Validate in setter (return int err) mirroring decoder bounds/non-finite checks, or validate encode-time consistently documented.
close_reason: sos_alert_set_location changed void->int returning SOS_ALERT_ERR_INVALID_VALUE when !coordinate_in_range(lat,90) or !coordinate_in_range(lon,180), SOS_ALERT_OK otherwise; atomic on failure (previous location state retained so encoder can never emit coordinates its own decoder rejects); encode path to_cbor left simple per instruction. Header prototype and @return/range contract documented at include/lichen/sos_alert.h. Caller audit: repo-wide grep finds zero call sites outside header+impl, nothing needed migration. clang -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsyntax-only passes.

title: Test gate command substring filter excludes address_assignment_vectors integration suite
description: cargo test -p lichen-rpl address_assignment matches 13 lib unit tests but 0 of tests/address_assignment_vectors.rs whose names lack substring. Full suite requires --test address_assignment_vectors (26 passed combined, exit 0 verified). Update test-gate docs/CI invocation.
close_reason: Invocation string is documented nowhere outside .beads bookkeeping, so added module-level //! docs to tests/address_assignment_vectors.rs stating the required cargo test -p lichen-rpl --test address_assignment_vectors invocation and explaining that the substring filter skips the suite (verified: filter catches 13 lib tests + 0 of 13 vector tests; --test yields 13 passed).

title: unix_now panics pre-epoch where Python twin evicts-all divergent failure modes
description: File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/address_assignment.rs:1237 expect() panics constructor on pre-epoch clocks; Python python/src/lichen/link/address_assignment.py:477-485 returns negative epoch evicting ALL persisted leases wholesale. Panic more conservative; record intentional asymmetry in docs or saturate+log for parity.
close_reason: unix_now now carries a doc comment recording the intentional divergence from the Python twin and why panic is the conservative choice (frozen-zero would leave persisted leases under deadlines forever). Behavior unchanged, expect() kept. Note: Python's prune_expired gained a now>=0 ValueError guard earlier today (7e54571f16), so current Python fails fast too; doc states both refuse to run on pre-epoch clocks, differing only in failure mode. Docs-only.

title: Groups test coverage gaps: multi-rekey stacking, admin-demotion negative, concurrency hooks
description: test_groups_rekey.py covers single rotation + grace boundary + prune-to-empty; missing N sequential rekeys stacking retired_epochs, double-prune idempotency assertion, admin-removal negative case (masks removed-admin defect), interleaving hooks for invitation store. Structural atomicity fine under cooperative asyncio; evidentiary gap only. File under review-coverage sweep.
close_reason: Added the two dispatcher-scoped evidentiary tests to existing new-style test_groups_rekey.py: (1) test_sequential_rekeys_stack_retired_epochs_with_prune_boundaries - 3 sequential rekeys stacking retired epochs [1] -> [1,2] -> (prune-on-read drops 1 at exact strict-boundary t0+3600) [2] -> [2,3], with epoch_accepted False/True probes at every exact expiry boundary and full stack equality pinned each step; final prune-on-read empties stack while live epoch-4 material asserted intact. (2) test_double_prune_is_idempotent_and_concurrency_free - two-entry stack, first mutating pass drops exactly one (pre/post lengths and full literal survivor entry), second identical pass proven zero-drop by deep equality of state snapshot AND returned material; sequential-only under the mutation lock, no fake async, docstring states why cooperative asyncio makes that the concurrency-relevant contract. Oracles are hand-derived construction values: key_ids from the key-{gid}-{epoch:03d} format, expires = rekey stamp + REKEY_GRACE_S arithmetic done offline, secrets/salts captured once at creation/rotation time; zero runtime echoes. Bead's other items (admin-demotion negative, invitation-store interleave hooks) intentionally not attempted here - outside the dispatcher's scoping for this leaf and group_membership/groups_invite signing+ledger logic is owned by in-flight beads. Verification: pytest tests/coap -k group = 78 passed; ruff clean on both touched files.

title: key_expires field is write-only state; no record/key GC beyond read-time pruning
description: File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/groups_collection.py:231,271 zero consumers found. Grace expiry checked on reads (correct) but dead field invites false assumption. Remove or implement GC semantics.
close_reason: Premise stale after today's rework (commit 9a857b8ce3 + working tree): key_expires is NO LONGER write-only - groups_collection.py:570 consumes it, serving it as 'expires' in the live GET /groups/{id}/key metadata response. Deletion branch would regress a working endpoint to expires=None for zero benefit; GC branch is overkill: retired-key grace already prunes via per-entry expires (_live_retired), group deletion is explicit owner DELETE, and nothing keys a lifecycle off key_expires. Chose simplest correct option: keep the field and pin its sole consumer evidentially - added additive test_key_metadata_reports_advertised_key_expiry in test_groups_item.py asserting full hand-derived payloads (expires=t0+86400 at create; t0+100+86400 after rekey; algorithm/key_id exact; no secret/salt leak). grep confirms exactly 3 occurrences repo-wide (2 writes, 1 read).

title: Messages lack explicit body-size cap unlike deaddrop
description: File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/messaging.py:134-296. Exposure bounded (~1KiB max blockwise x100 entries) small; spec parity with firmware body caps may require DEADDROP-style max constant. Low urgency, decide once with firmware.
close_reason: Added MESSAGES_MAX_BODY_SIZE = 1024 mirroring DEADDROP_MAX_DROP_SIZE pattern including public export from lichen.coap.resources (__init__ import block + __all__). Enforced twice in MessagesResource.render_post: raw len(payload) > cap -> 4.13 REQUEST_ENTITY_TOO_LARGE before decode (deaddrop error style), and final expanded body string > cap -> 4.00 BAD_REQUEST before ANY state mutation (covers canned-catalog expansion inflation). Constant aligned with blockwise-observation note (1KiB), below deaddrop's 1536. Tests: oversize CBOR {'body':'x'*4096} and raw b'x'*1025 -> 4.13 with zero inbox/_sent/_next_id mutation; largest encodable under-cap body accepted using cbor2 encoder as independent oracle for exact boundary sizing; canned expansion over cap -> 4.00 no mutation. Intentional test adjustment (not weakening): moved the x*4096 case out of test_post_rejects_all_cbor_resource_limit_bypasses_without_mutation into the dedicated 4.13 test with stricter code assertion, and removed its 256-item payload because busting _CBOR_MAX_ITEMS needs >1024 encoded bytes which the new guard now short-circuits first; map-entry/array-entry decode limits remain covered in-list. ruff check+format clean; tests/coap/test_messages_resource.py 144 passed; tests/coap 1679 passed/1 skipped/3 xfailed; adjacent suites test_messaging_vectors+test_vector_consumers_lci+client/test_lci+test_lci_contract_docs green.

title: Early INVALID_PARAM return in oscore_ctx_get skips *ctx_out=NULL sentinel
description: File: lichen/subsys/lichen/oscore/oscore_ctx.c:697-701. The recipient_id NULL+len>0 check returns before setting sentinel; sibling get_by_eui64 sets after combined check. Move *ctx_out=NULL directly after ctx_out NULL check completing worker6-x3bc intent.
close_reason: oscore_ctx_get(): *ctx_out=NULL hoisted directly after ctx_out NULL check so the recipient_id INVALID_PARAM early return now leaves the sentinel set; mirrors get_by_eui64 ordering. Note: HEAD had no sentinel at all; a concurrent working-tree edit had added it after the second check which still skipped it on that path - completed as true hoist.

title: Unreachable final return in time_sync update_from_parent
description: File: lichen/subsys/lichen/link/time_sync.c:341. lichen_time_sync_set_sfn only returns 0/-EALREADY both handled; final return err unreachable. Remove or fold; revisit if set_sfn contract grows.
close_reason: Unreachable trailing return removed. Branch coverage over set_sfn contract provably complete: guard (-EINVAL), err!=0 propagation (-EALREADY covers full 0/-EALREADY contract via generic nonzero check, future-proof), assignment+return 0. No empty trailing block remains. clang -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra clean.

title: Require exact DAO builder scalar types
description: API correctness review finding in python/src/lichen/rpl/dao_manager.py lines 445-499: _build_dao checks only 0 <= path_lifetime <= 255, so bool values are accepted as lifetimes, floats pass the range check and later leak a raw bytes TypeError, and ack_requested is not required to be bool (DAO.to_bytes coerces arbitrary truthy values). Validate exact int/non-bool path_lifetime and exact bool ack_requested before constructing or signing a DAO; cover bool/float/truthy-object inputs.

title: Preserve persistence write failures when staging cleanup also fails
description: ROBUSTNESS review: exception handlers in FileKeyStore._write_slot, TrustStorePersistence._write_json_locked, TwoSlotFilePersistence._write_slot, and _ensure_tx_marker call Path.unlink during an active write/replace failure without suppressing cleanup errors. A concurrent removal, permissions fault, or injected unlink error can mask the actionable primary fsync/replace/chmod failure (and for trust obscure indeterminate transition classification). Make cleanup best-effort without replacing the original exception and add focused fault tests.

title: Preserve key and trust persistence body errors through locking
description: python/src/lichen/crypto/key_persistence.py _exclusive_file_lock wraps the yield inside its OSError handler, so OSError raised by FileKeyStore or TrustStorePersistence reads, writes, fsync, replace, or directory operations is relabeled as cannot lock persistence state. This destroys the promised distinction between lock acquisition and storage failure and can mask the actionable cause during fail-closed recovery. Restrict lock-error translation to open/fstat/flock acquisition, let body exceptions propagate unchanged, make unlock/close unable to mask them, and add injected body-OSError tests for key and trust operations.

title: Reject coercive or negative DAO retry counters
description: P4 robustness review: timing.dao_retry_delay accepts bool as tuple index and dao_retry_exhausted accepts bool/negative/non-integral counters inconsistently. These are retry state-machine counters, so require exact non-negative integers in both helpers and cover coercive and negative inputs without changing valid timing vectors.

title: Correct lichen-link build_frame output buffer contract
description: The public documentation for LinkLayer::build_frame in rust/lichen-link/src/link_layer.rs says the output buffer must be at least inner_payload.len() + 53 bytes. The encoded signed frame actually needs payload + destination length + 61 bytes (1 length byte + 4 fixed header bytes + 8 signer EUI-64 bytes + 48 signature bytes, in addition to destination and payload). Callers following the documented contract receive BufferTooSmall. Document the exact required size, ideally with a checked helper/test.

title: Correct AnnounceMessage originator IID documentation to key-derived identity
description: P4 protocol documentation correctness: python/src/lichen/announce/messages.py still documents originator_iid as EUI-64-derived, while the implemented and normative identity profile derives the IID from SHA-512(Ed25519 pubkey) with the U/L bit cleared and explicitly quarantines EUI helpers to link interoperability. Update the source API documentation so callers are not directed toward a noncanonical identity model.

title: Remove or implement TrustStore.verify_or_pin allow_upgrade
description: P4 API correctness: TrustStore.verify_or_pin() exposes and documents allow_upgrade, but the parameter is never read and the method has no requested trust level to apply. Passing allow_upgrade=True has exactly the same behavior as False, so callers can believe an upgrade was authorized when none occurred. Remove the no-op argument or define an explicit validated upgrade contract and add behavior tests.

title: Announce parser tests fail strict Clippy on indexed fill loops
description: lichen-core/src/announce.rs tests use needless index ranges to fill IID/pubkey/signature fields, causing cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings to fail. Replace with slice iteration without changing fixtures.

title: Remove duplicate FileKeyStore base directory assignment
description: P4 robustness: FileKeyStore.__init__ assigns self._base_dir = Path(base_dir) twice consecutively. Remove the duplicate during the current persistence hardening convergence pass and verify Ruff/mypy.

title: Gateway codec tests contain needless double references
description: Two gateway.rs round-trip tests pass &schc where schc is already a slice, failing the required clippy -D warnings all-target gate. Pass the slice directly.

title: SuperframeConfig documentation contradicts epoch-relative implementation
description: rust/lichen-gateway/src/slot.rs SuperframeConfig::superframe_id documents the GCP absolute unix/duration formula, but the type explicitly stores 'Unix timestamp of superframe 0 start' and implements saturating (timestamp-epoch)/duration. This conflates the canonical global helper with an epoch-relative schedule and invites using the wrong claim freshness domain. Correct the method documentation to state its epoch-relative semantics and point callers needing canonical GCP IDs to superframe_id_from_timestamp.

title: Align scheduled-send exception logging regression test
description: python/tests/loadng/test_rreq_jitter.py::test_link_send_exception_is_logged_and_re_raised fails because Node.scheduled_send now logs the more general 'scheduled send failed (delay=...)' while still preserving the exception and traceback; the test requires the obsolete literal 'scheduled_send: link.send failed'. Choose and document the public diagnostic contract, then update the implementation/test consistently without weakening the checks that the error is logged and re-raised.

title: Independent DAO vector generator is not strict-mypy clean
description: Strict mypy reports six errors in generate_dao_origin_signature.py: unparameterized dict returns/arguments around prior/vector/rejected/generate and untyped rejected **kwargs. The generator was materially changed to be the independent Schnorr oracle, so its public helpers should carry exact object value types and pass the same strict gate as the production consumers without changing emitted JSON. Add precise annotations and verify byte-identical output.

title: No DIS (DODAG Information Solicitation) support for network discovery
description:
File: lichen/subsys/lichen/rpl

RFC 6550 Section 6.2 defines DIS messages for soliciting DIO messages from neighbors. This is useful for:
1. Faster network joining when a node boots
2. Probing network state after connectivity loss
3. Requesting updated routing information

Current implementation:
- LICHEN_RPL_CODE_DIS is defined (value 0)
- No DIS message structure or codec exists
- No DIS handling in the DODAG state machine

Impact: Nodes must passively wait for periodic DIOs, which with Trickle's exponential backoff could mean long delays (up to Imax) before joining or recovering.

Suggested fix:
1. Define DIS message structure (minimal: flags + reserved, optional: solicited information option)
2. Add DIS transmit function to trigger DIO responses
3. Add DIS receive handler that triggers DIO transmission

title: peer_eui64_to_iid XOR operation not documented as IID derivation
TxQueue stats not thread-safe despite class docstring warning
description:
File: python/src/lichen/link/tx_queue.py:111-116, 143

The class docstring says:
    '''Thread safety: Not thread-safe. Use external synchronization if
    accessed from multiple async tasks.'''

But TxQueueStats is a plain dataclass with mutable integer fields:

    @dataclass
    class TxQueueStats:
        packets_queued: int = 0
        packets_dropped_deadline: int = 0
        ...

And stats are updated non-atomically:
    self.stats.packets_queued += 1

In Python, += on integers is not atomic. If multiple coroutines access the queue (even with await points between operations), race conditions are possible.

The docstring warning is good, but consider:
1. Using threading.Lock for stats updates
2. Using atomic counters (not available in stdlib, but could use queue)
3. Documenting which operations need external synchronization

P4 since docstring warns about this.

Why it matters: Malformed prefixes (wrong length, invalid chars, non-fd00::/8) cause runtime -EINVAL in lichen_make_ula() but silently compile. Users might set invalid values unaware. A Kconfig string cannot enforce prefix format, so lichen_make_ula() is the validator, but error is delayed until runtime. Consider: Add BUILD_ASSERT or early boot validation of configured prefix.

title: [lora_l2.c:689] deinit join timeout may miss thread in backoff sleep
description:
Final pass: Related to project-LICHEN-i1gk.103 but distinct issue.

Root cause: At line 689:
  int join_ret = k_thread_join(&rx_thread_data, K_MSEC(DEINIT_JOIN_TIMEOUT_MS));

DEINIT_JOIN_TIMEOUT_MS is defined as 10 at line 145:
  #define DEINIT_JOIN_TIMEOUT_MS 10

The comment at lines 140-145 explains this is for 'best-effort recovery' but misses a scenario: if the thread entered the 1-second backoff sleep (line 366) just before stop() was called, and stop() then transitioned to STOPPED, the thread will exit on the next loop iteration - but only after the 1-second sleep completes.

The stop() function handles this with its longer timeout, but deinit() assumes stop() already joined the thread successfully. If stop() timed out and aborted the thread (ABORTED state), deinit() is called for recovery. But deinit()'s 10ms join timeout is far shorter than the 1-second backoff sleep.

Since ABORTED state implies thread was already k_thread_abort()'d, the 10ms timeout should be sufficient for that case. But the comment at line 688 says 'in normal operation, stop() already joined the thread' - implying there are non-normal cases where it didn't. If stop() returned before the thread exited (impossible due to join semantics), deinit's 10ms would miss it.

Actually analyzing further - k_thread_abort() is synchronous and forces immediate thread termination. The join after abort at line 616 with K_FOREVER should be nearly instant. And deinit() can only be reached from STOPPED or ABORTED states, both of which require stop() to have completed.

This is marginal but worth documenting the assumption explicitly.
close_reason: After analysis, the assumptions in the code are correct - k_thread_abort is synchronous and the join timeout is appropriate

title: [lichen_l2.c:1344-1345 vs lora_l2.c:906-925] callback registration order: iface_init registers before start, enable re-registers before start
description: Cross-file analysis: In lichen_l2_iface_init() at line 1345, the RX callback is registered BEFORE lichen_lora_l2_start() is called (start happens later via Zephyr net_if_up -> lichen_l2_enable). In lichen_l2_enable() at line 981, callback is registered BEFORE start() at line 982. Both are correct because the RX thread only starts running after start() succeeds, so there's no race. However, lora_l2_set_rx_callback() at line 908-910 logs a warning if state is UNINIT but doesn't error. After iface_init(), state is STOPPED (init succeeded), so callback registration succeeds. But if iface_init() partially fails after lora_l2_init() but before setting callback, retry init could see state=STOPPED (from first init) and skip callback registration... no, retry is blocked by lichen_iface != NULL check. Pattern is safe. No bug found.

title: [ipv6_addr.h:68-91] struct in6_addr fallback detection misses some platforms
description:
Round 2 gap analysis: Missed because header detection logic is complex.

At lines 68-91, the fallback struct in6_addr detection cascade checks various guards. However:

1. Line 74-76 checks for several BSD/Linux guards but misses some:
   - __NetBSD__ platforms may use different guards
   - Cygwin/MinGW may have different conventions

2. The detection relies on preprocessor guards being defined BEFORE this header is included. If ipv6_addr.h is included first (before netinet/in.h), the fallback definition is used, then including netinet/in.h later causes 'redefinition of struct in6_addr'.

The header comment at lines 82-86 acknowledges this and suggests LICHEN_HAVE_IN6_ADDR override, which is the correct escape hatch.

Not a bug per se - the header is defensive and provides an override. But the detection could be more robust with additional platform checks.
close_reason: Fix already implemented in working directory (uncommitted). The detection strategy was completely refactored from checking platform-specific guards (_NETINET_IN_H, _NETINET_IN_H_, etc.) to using __has_include(<netinet/in.h>) and directly including the header. This eliminates both issues: (1) no longer needs to enumerate platform guards (NetBSD, Cygwin/MinGW now covered), (2) include ordering handled by system header's own guards. File: /Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/project-LICHEN/lichen/subsys/lichen/l2/ipv6_addr.h lines 65-91.

title: [ipv6_addr.c:72-127] lichen_pubkey_to_iid: missing pubkey length validation
description:
Contract violation: precondition

**Issue:** The function documents that pubkey must be 32 bytes (LICHEN_ED25519_PUBKEY_LEN) but only validates pubkey != NULL. If a caller passes a shorter buffer, the lichen_sha256() call will read beyond the buffer (undefined behavior).

**Header doc (ipv6_addr.h:126):**
```
 * @param pubkey Ed25519 public key (32 bytes)
```

**Implementation:**
```c
if (pubkey == NULL || iid == NULL) {
    return -EINVAL;
}
// No length validation - uses hardcoded LICHEN_ED25519_PUBKEY_LEN (32)
ret = lichen_sha256(pubkey, LICHEN_ED25519_PUBKEY_LEN, hash);
```

**Impact:** Buffer overread if caller passes a shorter buffer. This is a SECURITY issue (potential information leak or crash).

**Mitigation:** C cannot validate array lengths passed as pointers. The current approach (document the contract, use array[N] syntax in declaration) is the standard C pattern. Add a BUILD_ASSERT similar to lichen_l2.c lines 108-111 to validate the constant matches expected size.

**Fix:** Add comment documenting this is caller's responsibility, similar to the SECURITY comment in the header. The function is correctly implementing the C idiom - no code change needed but consider adding a note about buffer size contract.
close_reason: Fixed: Added SECURITY comment documenting caller buffer size contract

title: [lora_l2.c:379-387] lora_modem_config.tx=true has no effect for half-duplex radios
description:
Category not checked: Hardware abstraction correctness

Bug found: At line 386, the LoRa config sets .tx = true. Looking at the comment at line 383:
  .tx_power = CONFIG_LICHEN_LORA_TX_POWER,
  .tx = true,

The .tx field in struct lora_modem_config is documented in Zephyr as:
'Set to true for TX mode, false for RX mode. Some radios need this hint.'

For half-duplex LoRa radios (which is all of them - SX127x, SX126x), the radio is either in TX or RX mode, not both. Setting .tx = true during configuration doesn't enable simultaneous TX/RX; it just tells the radio 'prepare for TX'.

But immediately after lora_config(), we start the RX thread which calls lora_recv(). The radio will switch to RX mode for lora_recv(), making the .tx = true meaningless.

The .tx = true is harmless but misleading. Better would be to set .tx = false since we're primarily an RX listener, or omit it (defaults to false).

Impact: P4 - Misleading config, no functional impact.
close_reason: Fixed: Added documentation explaining .tx=true is effectively unused since RX thread calls lora_recv() first, which switches to RX mode. Kept for driver default behavior and PA/LNA initialization hints.

title: [lora_l2.h:70-71] LICHEN_LORA_FRAME_OVERHEAD includes signature but signature is conditional
description:
Category not checked: Protocol framing assumptions

Bug found: LICHEN_LORA_FRAME_OVERHEAD is defined as 55 bytes, which includes 48 bytes for Schnorr-48 signature. However, looking at the wire format:

From lichen_l2.c line 594-596:
  /* NULL dst_eui64 = broadcast (no destination address in frame header) */
  ret = lichen_link_tx(&link_ctx, tx_ipv6_buf, pkt_len, NULL,
                       tx_frame_buf, &frame_len);

The lichen_link_tx() function applies signature only if ctx->has_key is true. From link_ctx.h (external), has_key indicates whether the signing key is provisioned.

If no signing key is provisioned:
- Actual overhead = 5 (header) + 4 (MIC) = 9 bytes
- MTU could be 255 - 9 = 246 bytes, not 200

But LICHEN_LORA_MTU is defined as 200 regardless of signing key presence. This is conservative (safe) but wastes 46 bytes of payload capacity when no signing key is set.

The code always reserves space for signature even when not used.

Impact: P4 - 46 bytes of wasted MTU when signing is disabled (conservative, not a bug).
close_reason: Fixed: Added documentation explaining LICHEN_LORA_FRAME_OVERHEAD (55 bytes) is intentionally conservative, reserving space for signature even when not used. Static MTU simplifies buffer sizing.

title: [main.c:117-119] init_standalone_lora late failure doesn't clean up RX callback
description:
Category not checked: Cleanup completeness on error paths

Bug found: In init_standalone_lora():
1. Line 97: lichen_lora_l2_set_rx_callback(lora_rx_handler, NULL) - registers callback
2. Line 99-103: lichen_lora_l2_start() called
3. Line 106-109: if get_eui64 fails, calls lichen_lora_l2_stop() 

The issue: lichen_lora_l2_stop() clears the callback (lora_l2.c:434-435), so this is actually fine for the eui64 failure case.

But there's another path:
- Line 117-119: if lichen_log_link_local_from_eui64() fails, we return ret without stopping LoRa.

So after a late failure in IPv6 address logging, LoRa is still running with the RX callback registered. This is inconsistent with the eui64-failure path.

Impact: P4 - Inconsistent cleanup: LoRa continues running after IPv6 address logging failure.
close_reason: Fixed: Code already has goto cleanup label at line 118 that properly calls lichen_lora_l2_stop() and lichen_lora_l2_deinit(). Issue appears to reference an older version of the code.

title: [ipv6_addr.c:28-33] LOG macro fallbacks are no-ops, could hide errors
description:
Gap found: Logging abstraction in non-Zephyr builds not reviewed.

Why this was missed: Host test infrastructure not examined.

The actual bug: Lines 28-33 define LOG_ERR, LOG_WRN, LOG_INF, LOG_DBG as ((void)0) for non-Zephyr builds. This allows the module to compile for host-side unit tests.

The issue: if a host test triggers an error condition (e.g., NULL pointer), the LOG_ERR is silently discarded. Tests won't see the error message.

Solutions:
1. Use fprintf(stderr, ...) in non-Zephyr builds
2. Use assert() for critical errors in test builds
3. Provide a test hook to capture log messages

This is a test infrastructure quality issue, not a production bug. The production (Zephyr) code logs correctly.

Priority 4 - test infrastructure improvement.
close_reason: Fixed: Changed LOG_ERR/LOG_WRN fallbacks from no-ops to fprintf(stderr) for host test visibility

title: [lora_l2.c:398-409] k_thread_create cannot fail but k_thread_name_set can
description:
Gap found: Thread creation error handling not verified.

Why this was missed: Round 1 covered thread abort, not creation.

The actual bug: Lines 401-404 call k_thread_create() with comment 'k_thread_create() returns the thread pointer passed in (first arg). It cannot fail at runtime - thread/stack resources are sized at build time.'

This is correct - k_thread_create cannot fail because it uses statically allocated thread and stack.

Lines 406-409 check k_thread_name_set() return and log warning on failure. This is defensive coding since thread naming is optional.

However, the thread is created with priority RX_THREAD_PRIORITY (CONFIG value). If this priority is invalid for the kernel configuration, behavior is undefined. The Kconfig should validate the priority range.

Verified thread creation correct. Priority 4 - Kconfig validation note.
close_reason: Fixed: Added comment noting Kconfig range validation ensures valid thread priority at build time

title: [lora_l2] deinit acquires then immediately releases lora_mutex (pointless)
close_reason: Fixed: Removed unnecessary mutex lock/unlock in lichen_lora_l2_deinit(). The callback pointer assignments no longer acquire lora_mutex because: (1) RX thread was already joined, (2) DEINITING state blocks new operations. Simplified the comment to explain why no mutex is needed.

title: [lichen_l2.c:863-873] NET_DEVICE_INIT priority could race with other init
description:
Gap found: Device initialization order not reviewed.

Why this was missed: Zephyr initialization framework interaction not examined.

The actual bug: NET_DEVICE_INIT at lines 863-873 uses CONFIG_KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_DEFAULT for initialization priority. This determines when lichen_l2_iface_init() runs relative to other initializations.

Potential issues:
1. If LoRa driver (lora0) initializes at a later priority, lichen_lora_l2_init() could fail
2. If hwinfo driver initializes later, generate_eui64() could fail
3. If tinycrypt initializes later, lichen_sha256() could fail

Zephyr typically initializes drivers before application code, and CONFIG_KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_DEFAULT is correct for network interfaces. The code handles failures gracefully (sets iface_init_failed).

Verified correct ordering for standard Zephyr configurations. Priority 4 - platform-specific concern for custom boards.
close_reason: Fixed: Added documentation comment to NET_DEVICE_INIT explaining why CONFIG_KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_DEFAULT is correct for network interfaces, noting that Zephyr initializes hardware drivers at earlier priorities, and that the init function gracefully handles missing dependencies via iface_init_failed.

title: [main.c:159-167] LED blink loop shares pattern with fatal error loop
description:
Gap found: main.c LED patterns not reviewed.

Why this was missed: LED diagnostic code considered non-critical.

The actual bug: In main(), USB failure causes 3 rapid blinks (lines 159-167) and then continues. LoRa failure causes continuous 200ms blinks forever (lines 192-197). Both use the same led_set() function and similar patterns, but USB failure is non-fatal while LoRa failure is fatal.

The subtle issue: if someone observing the device sees 3 rapid blinks, they might think something is wrong and reset. But the device would continue. The LED patterns could be more distinct:
- USB failure: 3 slow blinks (500ms), or different count
- LoRa failure: continuous fast blinks (current 200ms)

This is a UX design question, not a bug. The current code is correct. Priority 4 - suggestion only.
close_reason: Fixed: Enhanced inline comments to document the distinct LED patterns - USB failure uses 3 rapid 100ms blinks then stops, LoRa failure uses continuous 200ms blink forever. The patterns were already distinct; improved documentation to make this clearer.
